units.la: LEANTHEN, PRINCEPS Illustriss. ac DOMINE Clementiss. dixisse ferunt, ςοῦ ἀπαιδευτος μόνη τῃ μορφῃ ἱ ἀνθρώπων ἀποφέρειν, Homines nullis ingenuarum artium documentis imbutos, sola forma à bestiis differre. Hoc equidem veritati minimè absonum esse, ab omnibus approbari existimo. Nam bruta animantia juxta ac homines sensibus tum externis, tum internis, si physicae scientiae peritis fidem adhibeamus, præditi sunt. Si igitur homines, initio non ad obscuram aliquam effigiem creati, effecti, formati: sed ad divinam imaginem à Deo Opt. Max. conditi, facti, fabricati: per lapsum autem nostrorum primorum parentum in extremas ignorantiarum tenebras conjecti, & præcipitati: nullis artium liberalium axiomatibus imbuantur, instituantur, ac erudiantur: plane inter bruta animantia sunt numerandi. Deus autem I E H O V A humanum genus ab istiusmodi mentis tenebris vindicaturus, pro sua immensa misericordia ac bonitate⁓ Patriarchas, & reliquos Vates insigni ac eximia intelligentia, sapientia ac eruditione⁓ ornavit, ut cæteros[?], ingenuas non callentes scientias, divina sapientia erudirent. Sic Josephus Genef.41. prædicatur à Pharaone omnium Sapientum sapientissimus, hisce verbis: Nunquid sapientiorem & consimilem tui invenire potero? Sic 3.lib. Regum cap.4. Dedit Deus sapientiam Salomoni, & prudentiam multam nimis, & latitudinem cordis, quasi arenam, quæ est in littore maris: Et præcessit sapientia Salomonis sapientiam omnium Orientalium & [?]Aegyptiorum.
units.tr: Leanthen, most illustrious Prince and most clement Lord, is said to have remarked that men untrained in the liberal arts differ from the beasts only in form [οὐ ἀπαιδευτος μόνῃ τῇ μορφῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀποφέρειν]. I think this is by no means at odds with the truth, and that everyone approves it. For brute animals, as much as men, are endowed with senses, both external and internal, if we trust those skilled in natural science. If, then, men were not created at first as some dim likeness, but were made, formed and fashioned by God the Best and Greatest in his divine image, yet through the fall of our first parents were cast down into the deepest darkness of ignorance, and are instructed in no precepts of the liberal arts, they must plainly be counted among the brute animals. But God Jehovah, about to rescue the human race from such darkness of mind, in his immense mercy and goodness, adorned the Patriarchs and the other prophets with remarkable and outstanding intelligence, wisdom and learning, so that they might teach others, who did not know the non-liberal sciences, with divine wisdom. Thus Joseph is proclaimed by Pharaoh as the wisest of all the wise, in Genef. 41, in these words: "Can I find anyone wiser and like you?" So in 3 Kings chapter 4: "God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart, like the sand that is on the shore of the sea. And the wisdom of Solomon surpassed the wisdom of all the Orientals and Egyptians."

units.la: Estinsigne ipsius Spiritus Sancti elogium, quo Salomon celebratur: Et profecto idem ille Deus IEHOVA, Salomonem sapientiæ laurea redimiens, etiam nostros Principes hoc seculo, laus viventi Deo, mira eruditione ac scientia insignivit. Daniel. cap.3. ipsemet inquit: Tibi Deus Patrum meorum confiteor, teq; laudo: quia sapientiam & fortitudinem dedisti mihi. Sic Deus inter suos quoq; hostes, videlicet Ethnicos, multos viros excitavit sapientissimos, qui non tantum suos in omnis generis scientiis ad bene beateq; vivendum erudiere[?]: sed etiam multa singularis eruditionis suæ monumenta posteritati reliquerunt. Nam quis non Ciceronis monumenta de natura Deorum, in quibus tam præclara de Deo scripsit encomia, ut sane (si Filiũ Dei vera cognovisset fide) beatus celebrandus esset, ad astra, ut loquuntur, tolleret, ferret, & elevaret? Erasmus Rotero damus in Præfatione, quam libris Tusculananarum quastionum Ciceronis præfixit, confitetur non admodum se adversum habituros illos, inferedis calculis, qui sperant Ciceronem apud Superos quietâ vitam agere.
units.tr: It is a distinguished testimony of the Holy Spirit himself by which Solomon is celebrated. And surely that same God Jehovah, crowning Solomon with the laurel of wisdom, has also in this age distinguished our princes with wonderful learning and knowledge, to the praise of the living God. In Daniel chap. 3 he himself says: "I confess to you, God of my fathers, and praise you, because you have given me wisdom and strength." Thus God also raised up among his enemies, namely the Gentiles, many most wise men, who not only taught their own people in all kinds of knowledge for living well and happily, but also left to posterity many monuments of their singular learning. For who does not exalt and lift up to the stars, as they say, the writings of Cicero on the nature of the gods, in which he wrote such splendid praises of God, that he would indeed deserve to be celebrated as blessed, if he had known the true faith of the Son of God? Erasmus of Rotterdam, in the preface he prefixed to Cicero's Tusculan Disputations, confesses that he would not much oppose those who, reckoning it up, hope that Cicero lives a quiet life among the gods above.

units.la: Et sane nisi mihi Redemptoris nostri Christi verbum obstaret, Johan.3. Qui incredulus est Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum; ego quoque ex humanæ rationis lumine Ciceronem beatum præ-dicarem. Sed tamen hoc verissimum est, & sacræ Scripturæ, Matth.11. consentaneum, Ciceroni remissius fore in die Judicij, quàm iis, qui veritatis viam agnoverunt, & eam non sunt ingressi.
units.tr: And indeed, were it not that the word of our Redeemer Christ stood in my way, John 3: "He who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him," I too would, from the light of human reason, pronounce Cicero blessed. Yet this is most true, and agrees with Holy Scripture, Matthew 11: that it will be more bearable for Cicero on the day of judgment than for those who have known the way of truth and have not entered it.

units.la: Deinde quis non Magni Aristotelis scripta maximi faceret? Quis non ejus artium informandarum leges divinas esse autumaret? Certè quoties trium Aristotelicarum legum de artibus sapienter disponendis vim, robur ac pondus examino, trutino, ac pondero, non possum non statuere divinos sapientiæ radios in illo viro luxisse.
units.tr: Next, who would not hold the writings of the great Aristotle in the highest esteem? Who would not declare that his laws for arranging the arts are divine? Certainly, as often as I weigh, test and measure with scales the force, strength and weight of the three Aristotelian laws for wisely arranging the arts, I cannot but conclude that divine rays of wisdom shone in that man.

units.la: Nam summus ille Philosophus Petrus Ramus, JEHOVAE clementia adjutus, tam splendens compendiariæ viæ, videlicet Methodi, lumen ex ⌣Aristotelis nactus est legibus, ut totus jam Christianus orbis divina Methodo dispositas artes satis mirari nequeat. Quis enim ante Petri Rami tempora artes tam breviter, ut nunc sunt, Methodo conscriptas vidit? nonne omnis artium tradendarum via vepribus, dumis, & rubis hirsutis ac densis obsita fuit? Verum enimvero PRINCEPS Illustriss. ut evenire solet, saepe inveterata consuetudo tantum habet ponderis ac roboris, ut etiam veritatem sua corruscatione⌣ aciem oculorum hominum offendentem opprimere posse videatur. Quocirca quum vidissem, quod multi prorsus Petri Rami artes aurea conscriptas Methodo, ob difficultatem, quam praetendebat, pro nihilo haberent: adductus sum artes liberales sic conscribere, ut ex iis Methodum Rami: praecepta vero plerag;[?] Domini Melanchthonis studiosi adolescentes percipere⌣ possent. Nam ut verum asseram, praecepta D. Philippi Melanchthonis nullo modo a studiosa sunt juventute floccifacienda: pia enim illa Melanchthonis anima; ita quoq; liberales artes, licet non Methodo usque quaque succin-
units.tr: For that most eminent philosopher Peter Ramus, aided by the clemency of Jehovah, obtained from the laws of Aristotle the light of such a splendid shorter way, namely of Method, so that the whole Christian world can scarcely wonder enough at arts arranged by divine Method. For who before the time of Peter Ramus saw the arts set out by Method so briefly as they now are? Was not every way of teaching the arts overgrown with brambles, thorns and dense, bristling briars? But truly, most illustrious Prince, as usually happens, long-established custom carries so much weight and strength that it seems able to overwhelm even the truth, which strikes men's eyes with its brilliance. Therefore, when I saw that many people, on account of the difficulty they alleged, regarded as worthless the arts of Peter Ramus written in golden Method, I was moved to write the liberal arts in such a way that from them one could learn the Method of Ramus, while the precepts of Master Melanchthon could be grasped by studious young men. For, to speak the truth, the precepts of Dr. Philip Melanchthon must by no means be held in contempt by studious youth; for that pious soul of Melanchthon, so too the liberal arts, although not in every respect succinct in Method-

units.la: EPISTOLA
units.tr: EPISTLE

units.la: [?]ita splendeant, conscripsit, ut eas nulla unquam oblivio sit obliteratura.
units.tr: [?]so that they shine, he wrote, in such a way that no oblivion will ever obliterate them.

units.la: Fateor igitur ingenuè me hoc Opusculum ex Petro Ramo, D. Philippo Melanchthone, & aliis praestantissimis Authoribus concinnasse: nihil enim tam praeclarè dici potest, quod non dictum sit prius. Etsi vero illud Aristotelicum experientia verum comprobatum est: τὸ πᾶσιν ἀρέσαι δυσχερέστατον[?] ἐστιν, omnibus placere difficillimum est: tamen spes me fovet pulcherrima, hunc meum laborem in studiosorum gratiam susceptum, bonis & candidis hominibus non improbatum iri: Quia cum in inclyta V. C. Academia Marpurgensi superiori anno Musis operam navarem: & celeberrimus D. D. Sixtinus, quem honoris ergò nomino, audiret, me liberales artes Methodo Philippo Ramea conscripsisse, suum Filium Guilielmum, adolescētem profectò miro ingenio ac memoria praeditum, qui cum laude eo tempore, decimumtertium annum agens, paedagogi labores exantlaverat, voluit à me artibus Philippo-Ramea Methodo dispositis, institui, imbui, ac erudiri.
units.tr: I frankly confess, then, that I have put together this little work from Peter Ramus, Philip Melanchthon and other most distinguished authors, for nothing can be said so splendidly that it has not been said before. Although that saying of Aristotle has been proven true by experience, τὸ πᾶσιν ἀρέσαι δυσχερέστατον ἐστιν [it is most difficult to please everyone], nevertheless a most beautiful hope cheers me that this my labour, undertaken for the sake of students, will not be disapproved by good and fair-minded people. For when I was devoting myself to the Muses last year at the renowned Academy of Marburg, the most celebrated Dr. Sixtinus, whom I name out of respect, heard that I had written up the liberal arts in the Philippo-Ramist method. He wished his son Wilhelm, a young man truly endowed with remarkable talent and memory, who at that time, in his thirteenth year, had already completed the labours of a tutor with distinction, to be instructed, trained and educated by me in the arts arranged according to the Philippo-Ramist method.

units.la: Et certè tantùm intra decem hebdomadas profecit, ut in præsentia Patris & aliorum quorundam Studiosorum, Rhetoricam, Dialecticam, Physicam, Arithmeticam, Ethicam & Politicam ad unguem memoriter recitare potuerit.
units.tr: And indeed, within only ten weeks he made such progress that, in the presence of his father and of certain other students, he was able to recite from memory, word for word, Rhetoric, Dialectic, Physics, Arithmetic, Ethics and Politics.

units.la: Unde, PRINCEPS Illustriss. perspexi me in rem Ecclesiæ ac Reipublicæ Studiosis rem gratissimam factum ire, si artes liberales à me collectas prælo subjiciendas curarem, atque ita omnibus ingenuarum artium studiosis communicarem.
units.tr: Hence, most illustrious PRINCE, I have perceived that I would be doing a most welcome service for the Church and the commonwealth, and for students, if I took care to have the liberal arts that I have collected submitted to the press, and so shared them with all students of the liberal arts.

units.la: Moris est in Scholis trivialibus, Authores ferè innumeros studiosæ juventuti edisce-ndos proponere: sed, ut verum fatear, istiusmodi ratio docendi summis displicet Doctoribus. Nam multi studiosi ad vigesimum, imò ad vigesimum quartum vel quintum annum ita multis Authoribus, quos provectioris ætatis majore cum judicio & fructu legere possent, macerantur, ut deinde cum hæ-reticis disputantes prorsus obmutescât, quippe quum Christianæ doctrinæ fundamentum ignorent, atque ita maculam & labem Christianæ aspergant doctrinæ maximam.
units.tr: It is customary in the common schools to set before studious youth almost countless authors to be learned by heart. But, to tell the truth, this method of teaching greatly displeases the most eminent teachers. For many students are so worn down by so many authors, which they could read with greater judgement and profit when older, until their twentieth, indeed their twenty-fourth or twenty-fifth year, that afterwards, when they dispute with heretics, they are altogether struck dumb, since they do not know the foundation of Christian doctrine, and so they cast the greatest stain and disgrace upon Christian teaching.

units.la: Quapropter, Illustriss. PRINCEPS, summi Doctores judicant, juventutem esse linguis & artibus breviter instituendam, & et Christianam doctrinam una cum lacte nutricis, ut R.D.D. David Chytraus, Praeceptor meus ante triennium Rostochy plurimum observandus, in Proœmio sua Catechefis loquitur, esse instillandam.
units.tr: Therefore, most illustrious PRINCE, the greatest teachers judge that youth should be briefly instructed in languages and arts, and that Christian doctrine should be instilled along with the mother's milk, as the Reverend Dr. David Chytraeus, my teacher, to be most highly honoured, who was at Rostock three years ago, says in the preface to his Catechism.

units.la: Et profecto ante, quàm summum illud hoc seculo Philosophorum lumen, Petrus Ramus, artes juxta leges Aristotelicas reformavit: vix Grammaticam & dialecticam ante vigesimum annum Studiosi absolvere in Scholis potuerunt. Nunc vero, laus Deo Opt. Max. puer quinque annorum, singulis diebus fideliter institutus, ante vigesimum annum liberales artes, Dei auxilio absolvere potest.
units.tr: And indeed, before that greatest light of philosophers of this age, Peter Ramus, reformed the arts according to Aristotle's laws, students could scarcely finish grammar and dialectic in the schools before their twentieth year. But now, thanks be to God the Best and Greatest, a boy of five years, faithfully taught day by day, can finish the liberal arts with God's help before his twentieth year.

units.la: Vestræ autem Celf. Illustr. PRINCEPS, hæc meas primitias tum propter eximiam V. Celf. erga liberalium artium propagatores pietatem, tum propter singularem erga τὰς ἀρετὰς ὀρεῳ ἀνδρὰς[?] clementiam dedicare volui, obnixè humiliterq; rogans, ut V. C. hoc dedicationis meæ consilium in bonam partem interpretetur: id quod si intellexero, V C.
units.tr: Your Most Illustrious PRINCE, I have wished to dedicate these first fruits of mine, both on account of your Excellency's outstanding piety towards the promoters of the liberal arts, and on account of your singular clemency towards τὰς ἀρετὰς ὀρεῳ ἀνδρὰς [men of virtue], earnestly and humbly asking that your Excellency take this purpose of my dedication in good part, which if I shall have understood, your Excellency.

units.la: DEDICATORIA.
units.tr: DEDICATION.

units.la: V. C. ita me inflammabit, ut plura, Deo annuente,in Ecclesiæ & Reipublicæ utilitatem studiosæ sim juventuti communicaturus.
units.tr: Your Most Illustrious Highness will thereby so inspire me that, God willing, I shall share more of these studies with the young, for the benefit of the Church and the commonwealth.

units.la: Faxit Deus Opt. Max. per vulnera sui dilectissimi Filij IESV Christi, ut V. C. diu incolumis subditos regat, & gubernet, Christianas Scholas ad divini nominis gloriam summo amore prosequatur, quo studiosos adolescentes V. C. Beneficio ac commendatione, linguis artibusq; ita instituere, imbuere, erudire possimus, ut septicollis Idoli Locustis,nuper in Germaniam missis, infirmas alas acuta forfice olim amputare queat. Amẽ.
units.tr: May God, the Best and Greatest, through the wounds of his most beloved Son Jesus Christ, grant that Your Highness may long rule and govern your subjects in safety, and may pursue the Christian schools with the highest love for the glory of the divine name. By your kindness and recommendation, may we be able to train, imbue and instruct studious young men in languages and arts, so that they may one day be able to clip with a sharp shears the weak wings of the locusts of the seven-hilled idol, lately sent into Germany. Amen.

units.la: AUTOSCHEDIASMA M. RUDOLPHI GOCLENII liberalium artium Professoris in inclyta Academia Marpurgensi, in Syntagma, seu Syno- psin ingenuarum artium, singulari studio & opera à doctrina & virtute praestanti viro, IOHANN. BILSTENIO, Oreadum alumno, concinnatam.
units.tr: AUTOSCHEDIASMA of M. Rudolph Goclenius, Professor of the Liberal Arts in the renowned Academy of Marburg, a Syntagma or Synopsis of the liberal arts, put together with singular zeal and labour by the learned and virtuous man Johann Bilstenius, a pupil of the Oreadum school.

units.la: AD STUDIOSOS.
units.tr: TO THE STUDENTS.

units.la: Confectum,ducente Deo, comitante labore, Illustris Methodi percelebrisq; via, Bilstenii Syntagma breve,atq; rotunda Synopsis, Doctrina ingenua fertile prodit opus.
units.tr: With God leading and labour accompanying, Bilstenius's brief Syntagma and round Synopsis, following the illustrious and much-celebrated Method, comes forth, a work fruitful in liberal learning.

units.la: Non factum doctis, quibus experientia rerum est, Hoc feret aetati commoda magna rudi.
units.tr: It is not made for the learned, who have experience of things; it will bring great advantage to an untrained age.

units.la: Lac pueris aptum: solidus cibus aptus adultis, Ventriculi haud omnes, omnia ferre queunt.
units.tr: Milk suits children, and solid food suits adults; not every stomach can bear everything.

units.la: Quid? quod & hic aliquid, quod discat gradior aetas, Inveniet: docta non sumus arte pares: Dicitur ipse Solon etiam tali ore locutus: Discenti assidue multa senecta venit.
units.tr: What more? The age that is advancing may find something here to learn as well; we are not equal in learned skill. Solon himself is said to have spoken in such words: old age comes to the one who is always learning.

units.la: Hoc opus ergo legens, pubes studiosa perennes, Authori grates officiosa refer.
units.tr: So, studious youth, reading this work again and again, render your dutiful thanks to the author.

units.la: Dilige doctrinam, docilis discendaq; disce, Defuge desidiam, dilige dona Dei. Dona Dei lingua, famula rationis, & artes Bilstenii hic labor est, his sine dulce nihil.
units.tr: Love learning, and be teachable and learn what is to be learned; flee idleness, love the gifts of God. The gifts of God are language, the handmaid of reason, and the arts; this is Bilstenius's labour, and without these nothing is sweet.

units.la: ALIUD EJUSDEM.
units.tr: ANOTHER BY THE SAME.

units.la: Sicut apis, saltus, hortosq; & olentia nata Pascua, per flores & thyma summa volat:
units.tr: As the bee flies over woods, gardens, and fragrant pastures, over the flowers and the finest thyme,

units.la: Actore[?] hinc carpit, summo tenus optima quaq; Et dulcis fingit nobile mellis opus:
units.tr: and from there gathers all the best things from the top and sweetly shapes the noble work of honey,

units.la: Sic per Musarum, Tempeq; & amœna vireta Bilstenius[?] volitans, optima quaq; legit.
units.tr: so Bilstenius, flying through the meadows of the Muses, of Tempe and the pleasant greenery, gathers all the best things.

units.la: Atq; hinc gignit opus, genitumq; exponit in auras, Forsitan hoc Solis lucida tela fugit?
units.tr: And from this he produces the work and sets the thing born out into the breezes; perhaps it flees the shining darts of the sun?

units.la: Nil minus: ingenua nam totum continet orbem Doctrina, & multis eruta sensa libris.
units.tr: Not at all: for liberal learning contains the whole world, and meanings dug out from many books.

units.la: Non in aperto igitur passim prostare veretur, Serviat ut studiis, Grex studiosa, tuis.
units.tr: So it need not fear to lie about everywhere in the open; let it serve your studies, studious flock.

units.la: Hoc lege, sed lectum, bene percipe, pectore conde: Hoc exprome usu, cum feret usus, opus.
units.tr: Read this, but once read it, grasp it well and store it in your breast; bring it out in practice when practice calls for the work.

units.la: Nec vero hoc satis est: plus ultra, Symbolon esto (Dum contacta tibi ex ultima meta) tuum.
units.tr: Nor is this enough: go further, and let it be your watchword until you touch the last goal.

units.la: Post ea quæ Sophiæ Proceres monumenta dedere, Illa leges oculis, illa teres manibus.
units.tr: After those monuments which the leaders of Wisdom have given, read these with your eyes and wear these down with your hands.

units.la: Virtutis sectare viam: comitabitur illam, Ingredere, labor: progrediaris, amor.
units.tr: Pursue the path of virtue: labour will accompany you as you enter it, and love will attend you as you advance.

units.la: Emenso continget honor, pulcerrima merces Ergo age, virtutis perfice gnauus iter.
units.tr: Honour will come once the course is finished, the finest reward. Therefore come, diligently complete the journey of virtue.

units.la: OCTOSTICHON
units.tr: OCTOSTICHON

units.la: JOAN. PISCATORIS, Scholæ Herbornensis Moderatoris, ad IOAN. BILSTENIUM.
units.tr: JOHANNES PISCATOR, Moderator of the School of Herborn, to JOHANNES BILSTENIUS.

units.la: Ingenuas (aiunt) didicisse fideliter artes, Emollit mores, nec sinit esse feros. At didicisse sacri divina oracula Verbi, Informat mores ad pietatis opus. Ingenuas igitur cognosce fideliter artes: Sed Verbi inprimis dogmata nosce sacri: Sic simul humanis ornabere moribus, & sic Divina mentem tu pietate coles.
units.tr: They say that having faithfully learned the liberal arts softens manners and does not let them be savage. But having learned the divine oracles of the holy Word shapes the manners for the work of piety. Therefore, learn the liberal arts faithfully, but above all know the doctrines of the holy Word. So you will be adorned at once with humane manners, and so you will cultivate your mind with divine piety.

units.la: EPIGRAMMA PHILIPPI à THULEN pro Syntagmatis huius commenda- tione ad Sophiæ Stu- diosos.
units.tr: EPIGRAM OF PHILIPP VON THULEN, commending this Syntagma to the students of Sophia.

units.la: Sunt equidem multi, vario distincta colore, Stamina, qui vigili composuēre manu. Sunt quoq; praestātes, glomerata volumina magna, Qui Methodo celebri disposuēre, viri. Attamen hos inter pauci (mihi crede) videntur Aetati imberbi consuluisse probè, Sed valdè implicitis Tyrones artibus omnes Pædeuta, dociles instruere suos.
units.tr: There are indeed many threads, marked with varied colours, which skilful hands have woven. There are also excellent men who have arranged great rolled volumes by a famous method. Yet among these, few (believe me) have looked well after tender youth; rather, teachers, all too entangled in intricate arts, struggle to instruct their docile pupils.

units.la: Ergo videns Author pubem vexarier arteProlixa, Sophia perbreve scripsit opus.
units.tr: So the author, seeing young people harassed by an overlong art, wrote this very brief work, Sophia.

units.la: Hic igitur merito celebrandus honore videtur, Cujus & Aonio splendida fama choro est.
units.tr: This man, therefore, seems rightly to be honoured with praise, whose splendid fame is also in the Aonian choir.

units.la: Non minus & textoris opus sudore paratumEximio cunctis debet honore coli.
units.tr: No less is the weaver's work, achieved with sweat, owed to be honoured by all with distinguished esteem.

units.la: Nam cuicunq; sacrum jus, musas discere cura est,Hinc scire exigua sedulitate potest.
units.tr: For whoever takes care to learn sacred law and the Muses can know it from here with little diligence.

units.la: Huc ergo juvenis cupidam tu flectito mentem, Si bene Musarum visere castra cupis.
units.tr: Here, then, young man, turn your eager mind, if you wish to visit the camps of the Muses well.

units.la: Huc properato citò, Musas qui discere flagrasTempore percelerì: tu properato: Vale.
units.tr: Hasten here quickly, you who burn to learn the Muses in a short time; hasten. Farewell.

units.la: PARAENESIS JOAN. PFEILSTICKERI ad studiosam pubem.
units.tr: An exhortation by Joan Pfeilsticker to the studious youth.

units.la: EN pubes studiosa diu vexata laboreImprobo, & innumeris usq; onerata libris.
units.tr: Behold, studious youth, long harassed by toilsome and unworthy labour, and burdened with countless books.

units.la: En Syntagma tibi parvum Bilsteinius offert: Parvum equidem, at magna est utilitatis opus.
units.tr: Here Bilsteinius offers you a little Syntagma. It is small indeed, yet its work is of great usefulness.

units.la: Ex quo florifero ceu campo Pallados alma, Promere Thespiadum munera cuncta potes.
units.tr: From it, as from a flowering meadow, O nurturing one of Pallas, you can gather all the gifts of the Thespiades.

units.la: Tamq; laboratu est opus hoc breve, tamq; probatu: Ceu dederit Musis ipsa Minerva suis.
units.tr: This short work is so well wrought and so well tested that Minerva herself might seem to have given it to her Muses.

units.la: Rami etenim est Method, verù documeta Philippi: Sic simul hic, doceat quicquid uterque, tenes.
units.tr: For it is of Ramus's method, yet it carries the teachings of Philip, so you hold here whatever each of them teaches.

units.la: Sic nunc Musarum (concedunt numina) fontes Nectare abundantes ambrosiaq; fluunt: Utq; breui spacio, facilíq; labore medullam, Cordaq; Pieridum tangere & ossa queas. Huc igitur Tyro docilis properato: benignæ Et citò, quæ Musæ dona dedêre, cape. Laus iam sit superis, laus Musis, lausq; perennis Authori, hoc fœlix qui benè scripsit opus. Revera is merito non est indignus honore. Quem benè de studiis tu meruisse vides. Vivat Bolstenius, duretq; ad Nestoris annos Hoc opus, & fructu numina sancta beent.
units.tr: Thus now the fountains of the Muses, overflowing with nectar and ambrosia, flow forth (the gods permit it), so that in a short space and with easy labour you may touch the marrow, the heart and the very bones of the Pierides. Therefore, docile student, come here quickly and take the gifts the kindly Muses have bestowed. Now let there be praise to the gods above, praise to the Muses, and everlasting praise to the author who has happily written this work well. Indeed, he is rightly not unworthy of honour, since you see that he has deserved well of learning. May Bilstenius live, may this work last to Nestor's years, and may the holy powers bless it with fruit.

units.la: SYNTAGMA PHILIPPORA- MEUM AR- tium Libera- lium.
units.tr: A Syntagma of the Liberal Arts, according to the method of Philip Ramus.

units.la: Quid est Philosophia?
units.tr: What is philosophy?

units.la: PHILOSOPHIA est artium o-mnium cognitio.
units.tr: Philosophy is the knowledge of all the arts.

units.la: Quid est ars?
units.tr: What is art?

units.la: Ars est comprehensio præceptorum, in rebus æternis propriorum, & ordine dispositorum, ad utilem vitæ finem spe-ctantium.
units.tr: Art is the grasping of precepts, which belong to eternal things, are arranged in order, and look to a useful end of life.

units.la: Quomodo dividuntur artes Liberales?
units.tr: How are the liberal arts divided?

units.la: In Exotericas & Acroamaticas. <bl>In schlechte unnd</bl> <bl>hohe künste.</bl>
units.tr: Into exoteric and acroamatic. Into the plain and the high arts.

units.la: Quot sunt artes Exotericæ?
units.tr: How many exoteric arts are there?

units.la: Quatuor: Grammatica, Rhetorica, Poëtica, Dia-lectica.
units.tr: Four: grammar, rhetoric, poetics, and dialectic.

units.la: Quot sunt artes Acroamaticæ?
units.tr: How many acroamatic arts are there?

units.la: Tres: Physica, Mathematica, Ethica. Physica circa rerum qualitatem versatur: Mathematica circa re-rum quantitatem: Ethica circa mores.
units.tr: Three: physics, mathematics, and ethics. Physics is concerned with the quality of things, mathematics with their quantity, and ethics with morals.

units.la: Quænam comprehenduntur sub Physica?
units.tr: What is included under physics?

units.la: Optica, Astronomia, Geographia, Medicina & Musica.
units.tr: Optics, astronomy, geography, medicine, and music.

units.la: Quænam comprehenduntur sub Mat- he-matica?
units.tr: What is included under mathematics?

units.la: Arithmetica, Geometria & Architectura.
units.tr: Arithmetic, geometry, and architecture.

units.la: Quænam comprehenduntur sub Ethica?
units.tr: What is included under ethics?

units.la: Politica, Oeconomica, Apodemica, Polemica, Historia, Jurisprudentia & Theologia, de qua vide libellum, quem inscripsimus Apodixin doctrinæ Ca-tholicæ.
units.tr: Politics, economics, apodemics, polemics, history, jurisprudence, and theology, on which see the little book we have entitled Apodixis of the Catholic Doctrine.

units.la: Hæc breviter dicta sunto ad quandam præcognitionem artium adipiscendam: Nunc Dei auxilio, ar-tes ipsas aggrediemur.
units.tr: Let these things be said briefly, to gain some preliminary acquaintance with the arts. Now, with God's help, we shall take up the arts themselves.

units.la: GRAMMATICA TEUTONICA.
units.tr: GRAMMAR OF THE GERMAN TONGUE.

units.la: Quid est Grammatica Teutonica?
units.tr: What is German grammar?

units.la: <bl>Was ist die Teutsche Sprachekunst?</bl>
units.tr: What is the art of German grammar?

units.la: GRammatica Teutonica est ars purè lo-quendi Teutonicè. <bl>Die Teutsche</bl> <bl>Sprache-kunst ist eine kunst seuberlich Teutsch zu sprechen.</bl>
units.tr: Grammatica Teutonica is the art of speaking German purely. The art of German grammar is an art of speaking German cleanly and correctly.

units.la: Quot sunt ejus partes?
units.tr: How many parts does it have?

units.la: Duæ: Etymologia & Syntaxis.
units.tr: Two: Etymology and Syntax.

units.la: Quid est Etymologia?
units.tr: What is Etymology?

units.la: Etymologia est prima pars Grammaticæ, in quo de singularum vocum proprietate agitur.
units.tr: Etymology is the first part of grammar, in which the particular properties of individual words are treated.

units.la: Quid est Vox?
units.tr: What is a word?

units.la: Vox est nota, qua unaquæq; res vocatur.
units.tr: A word is a sign by which each thing is called.

units.la: Unde fit Vox?
units.tr: How is a word formed?

units.la: E litera & syllaba.
units.tr: From a letter and a syllable.

units.la: Quot sunt literæ, quibus Teutonica lin- gua scribitur?
units.tr: How many letters are there with which the German language is written?

units.la: Sex & viginti: <bl>A/B/C/D/E/F/G/H/I/K/L/M/N/O/P/Q/R/S/T/U/W/X/Y/Z</bl> [?] <bl>Xi/Ypsilon/Zeta/Jod/Dau</bl> [?]
units.tr: Twenty-six: A/B/C/D/E/F/G/H/I/K/L/M/N/O/P/Q/R/S/T/U/W/X/Y/Z [?] Xi/Ypsilon/Zeta/Jod/Dau [?]

units.la: Quotuplex est Vox?
units.tr: How many kinds of word are there?

units.la: Duplex: Numeri aut sine Numero.
units.tr: Two: those with inflection (declinable or conjugable) or those without.

units.la: Quot sunt voces Numeri?
units.tr: How many parts of speech with inflection are there?

units.la: Duæ: Nomen & Verbum.
units.tr: Two: the noun and the verb.

units.la: DE NOMINE.
units.tr: ON THE NOUN.

units.la: Quid est Nomen?
units.tr: What is a noun?

units.la: NOmen est vox numeri cum genere, casu & declinatione.
units.tr: A noun is a word with number, gender, case and declension.

units.la: Quotuplex est Nomen?
units.tr: How many kinds of noun are there?

units.la: Duplex: Substantivum aut Adjectivum.
units.tr: Two: the substantive noun and the adjective noun.

units.la: Quid est Substantivum Nomen?
units.tr: What is a substantive noun?

units.la: Cujus significatio per se absq; altero addito intelligitur: ut, <bl>Der Mensch</bl>/Homo, <bl>Der Vatter</bl>/Pater.
units.tr: One whose meaning is understood by itself, without another word added: for example, Der Mensch (man, Homo), Der Vatter (father, Pater).

units.la: Quid est Adjectivum Nomen?
units.tr: What is an adjective noun?

units.la: Cujus significatio absque altero intelligi non potest: ut, <bl>weiß</bl>/albus, <bl>schwarz</bl>, niger.
units.tr: One whose meaning cannot be understood without another word: for example, weiß (white, albus), schwarz (black, niger).

units.la: Quot sunt comparationis gradus, qui nonnullis Adjectivis accidunt?
units.tr: How many degrees of comparison are there, which belong to some adjectives?

units.la: Post positivum duo gradus nominantur, Comparativus & Superlativus.
units.tr: After the positive, there are two degrees, the comparative and the superlative.

units.la: Unde Comparativus & Superlativus formantur?
units.tr: How are the comparative and superlative formed?

units.la: A positivo, cui addendum est er / pro comparativo, & ste vel este [?] pro superlativo: ut, flug/ fluger/ [?] klugste[?]/from[?]/frommer/frommeste. Vocales autem & Diphthongi positivi mutantur in Comparativo & Superlativo, videlicet a ine/ o inö/ u inü/ au in eu: ut, lang/lögus, lenger/lengste. Groß/magnus, größser/größte. Jung/juvenis, jünger/jüngste. Braun/ fuscus, breuner/breunste. Excipe gut/ besser/beste/ bonus, melior, optimus. Böß/erger/ergste/malus, peior, pessimus. Viel/mehr/meiste/multum, plus, plurimum.
units.tr: From the positive, to which -er is added for the comparative and -ste or -este for the superlative, as: flug / fluger / klugste; from / frommer / frommeste. The vowels and diphthongs of the positive change in the comparative and superlative, namely a into ä, o into ö, u into ü, and au into eu, as: lang / lenger / lengste (long); Groß / größer / größte (great, large); Jung / jünger / jüngste (young); Braun / breuner / breunste (brown). Note the exception gut / besser / beste (good; better, best); Böß / erger / ergste (bad; worse, worst); Viel / mehr / meiste (much; more, most).

units.la: Quot sunt genera Teutonicorum Nomi-minum?
units.tr: How many genders do German nouns have?

units.la: Quinque: Masculinum, Foemininum, Neutrum, Commune & Omne.
units.tr: Five: masculine, feminine, neuter, common, and all (omne).

units.la: Quid est Masculinum genus?
units.tr: What is the masculine gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus <bl>der</bl>: ut, <bl>der Mann</bl>/Vir.
units.tr: It is marked by the article der: for example, der Mann (man, vir).

units.la: Quae nomina sunt Masculini generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the masculine gender?

units.la: Primo, quae viro, aut rebus viri specie conceptis congruunt: ut, <bl>der Vatter</bl>/ Pater, <bl>der König</bl>/ Rex, <bl>der Jenner</bl>/Januarius, <bl>der Mey</bl>/Majus: Deinde desinentia in b/d/f/g/h/k/l/m/n/r/s/t/w/y/z: ut, <bl>der</bl> <bl>leib</bl>/ corpus, <bl>der sand</bl>/ arena, <bl>der schlaff</bl>/somnus, <bl>der</bl> <bl>tag</bl>/dies, <bl>der fisch</bl>/piscis, <bl>der speck</bl>/lardum, <bl>der stahl</bl>/ chalybs, <bl>der leim</bl>/gluten, <bl>der schrein</bl>[?]/cista, <bl>der in-</bl> <bl>gwer</bl>/zingiber, <bl>der flachs</bl>/linum, <bl>der mist</bl>/fimus, <bl>der taw</bl>/ros, <bl>der blitz</bl>/fulgur, <bl>der schatz</bl>/thesaurus. His adde <bl>der bien</bl>/puls & <bl>der Weihe</bl>/Milvus: ut, Alle reine vögel esset. Das sind sie aber die ihr nicht essen solt: <bl>der Adler</bl>/ <bl>der Habicht</bl> / <bl>der Fischar</bl>/ <bl>der Teucher</bl>/<bl>der Weihe</bl>. Sagt D. Luther in den Teutschen Biblien/im V. Buch Mose/am XIV. Cap.
units.tr: First, those that agree with a man, or with things conceived in the form of a man: for example, der Vatter (father, pater), der König (king, rex), der Jenner (January, Januarius), der Mey (May, Majus). Next, those ending in b, d, f, g, h, k, l, m, n, r, s, t, w, y, or z: for example, der leib (body, corpus), der sand (sand, arena), der schlaff (sleep, somnus), der tag (day, dies), der fisch (fish, piscis), der speck (bacon, lardum), der stahl (steel, chalybs), der leim (glue, gluten), der schrein [?] (chest, cista), der ingwer (ginger, zingiber), der flachs (flax, linum), der mist (dung, fimus), der taw (dew, ros), der blitz (lightning, fulgur), der schatz (treasure, thesaurus). To these add der bien (bee?, puls) and der Weihe (kite, milvus), as in: "All clean birds you may eat. But these are the ones you shall not eat: der Adler, der Habicht, der Fischar, der Teucher, der Weihe." Dr. Luther says this in the German Bible, in the Fifth Book of Moses, chapter 14.

units.la: Quid est Foemininum genus?
units.tr: What is the feminine gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus <bl>die</bl>: ut, <bl>die Frawe</bl>/foemina.
units.tr: It is marked by the article die: for example, die Frawe (woman, foemina).

units.la: Quae nomina sunt Foeminini generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the feminine gender?

units.la: Primo, quae mulieri, aut rebus mulieris specie cōceptis congruunt: ut, <bl>die Mutter</bl>/ mater, <bl>die</bl> <bl>Tochter</bl>/filia, <bl>die pappel</bl>/populus arbor. Deinde definentia in <bl>e/ung/heit/keit/ey/ac tet/on/</bl> ur a Latinis formata: ut, <bl>die taube</bl>/ columba, <bl>die wohnung</bl>/habitatio, <bl>die faulheit</bl> / ignavia, <bl>die Gottsäligkeit</bl> / pietas, <bl>die Cantzeley</bl> / Grammatophylacium, <bl>die dignitet</bl>/ dignitas, <bl>die lection</bl>/lectio, <bl>die figur</bl>/figura.
units.tr: First, those that agree with a woman, or with things conceived in the form of a woman: for example, die Mutter (mother, mater), die Tochter (daughter, filia), die pappel (poplar, populus, a tree). Next, those ending in e, ung, heit, keit, ey, and ac, tet, on, ur, formed from Latin: for example, die taube (dove, columba), die wohnung (dwelling, habitatio), die faulheit (laziness, ignavia), die Gottsäligkeit (piety, pietas), die Cantzeley (chancery, grammatophylacium), die dignitet (dignity, dignitas), die lection (lesson, lectio), die figur (figure, figura).

nadel</bl>/acus, <bl>die gabel</bl>/ furca, <bl>die schauffel</bl>/pala, <bl>die semmel</bl>/simila, <bl>die rot-</bl> <bl>dommel</bl>/onocrotalus [?], <bl>die Deichssel</bl>/temo, <bl>die geissel</bl>/ flagellum, <bl>die schüssel</bl>/patina, <bl>die scheitel</bl>/vertex, <bl>die</bl> <bl>fackel</bl>/fax, <bl>die handzwehl</bl>/mantile, <bl>die scham</bl>/pudor, <bl>die bahn</bl>/iter, <bl>die stirn</bl>/frons, <bl>die birn</bl>/pyrū, <bl>die pein</bl>/ tortura, <bl>die lehr</bl>/doctrina, <bl>die schar</bl>/turba, <bl>die</bl> <bl>gefahr</bl>/periculum, <bl>die klafter</bl>/ulna, <bl>die leber</bl>/jecur, <bl>die</bl> <bl>schulter</bl>/humerus, <bl>die seder</bl>/penna, <bl>die kammer</bl>/cubiculum, <bl>die klammer</bl>/fibula, <bl>die thür</bl>/janua, <bl>die für</bl>/ delectus, <bl>die spür</bl>/indagatio, <bl>die ruhr</bl>/dysenteria, <bl>die wildnis</bl>/erem°, <bl>die laus</bl>/pediculus, <bl>die mauß</bl>/mus, <bl>die Gans</bl>/anser, <bl>die nuß</bl>/nux, <bl>die that</bl>/factum, <bl>die</bl> <bl>nat</bl>/futura, <bl>die not</bl>/angustia, <bl>die brüt</bl>/ovorum exclusio, <bl>die flut</bl>/eluvio, <bl>die glut</bl>/flamma, <bl>die hut</bl>/custodia, <bl>die armut</bl>/paupertas, <bl>die demut</bl>/humilitas, <bl>die</bl> <bl>sanfftmut</bl>/mansuetudo, <bl>die haut</bl>/cutis, <bl>die braut</bl>/sponsa [?], <bl>die zeit</bl>/tempus, <bl>die And some others.

units.la: Quid est Neutrum genus?
units.tr: What is the neuter gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus <bl>das</bl>: ut, <bl>das Testament</bl>.
units.tr: Its mark is the article das, as in das Testament (the testament).

units.la: Quae nomina sunt Neutrius generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the neuter gender?

units.la: Primo, Nomina oppidorum, pagorum, literarum & syllabarum: ut, <bl>das Leipzig</bl> / Lipsia, <bl>das Basel</bl> / Basilea, <bl>das Ulm</bl> / <bl>das Ja</bl> / <bl>das Nein</bl>. Excipitur <bl>die Lippe</bl> / urbs Lippia, & alia quaedam. Deinde desinentia in ment, nis, len vel lin, & alia nonnulla: ut <bl>das Sacrament</bl> / Sacramentum, <bl>das Gezeugnis</bl> / testimonium, <bl>das Gefängnis</bl> / carcer, <bl>das Männlein</bl> / masculus, <bl>das Fräulein</bl> / mulierecula, <bl>das Grab</bl> / sepulchrum, <bl>das Weib</bl> / mulier, <bl>das Kalb</bl> / vitulus, <bl>das</bl> <bl>Lamb</bl> / agnus, <bl>das Bad</bl> / balneum, <bl>das Rad</bl> / rota, <bl>das</bl> <bl>Augenglied</bl> / gena, <bl>das Glied</bl> / membrum, <bl>das Lied</bl> / canticum, <bl>das Leid</bl> / luctus, <bl>das Wild</bl> / fera, <bl>das Bild</bl> / imago, <bl>das Gold</bl> / aurum, <bl>das Band</bl> / vinculum, <bl>das Land</bl> / regio, <bl>das Pfand</bl> / pignus, <bl>das Kind</bl> / infans, <bl>das Rind</bl> / bos, <bl>das End</bl> / finis, <bl>das Elend</bl> / miseria, <bl>das Pfund</bl> / libra, <bl>das Pferd</bl> / equus, <bl>das Felsen</bl>[?] / rus, <bl>das Schaf</bl> / ovis, <bl>das Schaff</bl> / vas, <bl>das Schiff</bl> / navis, <bl>das Dorff</bl> / pagus, <bl>das Ding</bl> / res, <bl>das Bedüng</bl> / conditio, <bl>das Dach</bl> / tectum, <bl>das Fach</bl> / interstitium, <bl>das Gemach</bl> / conclave, <bl>das Gelach</bl> / symposium, <bl>das Pech</bl> / pix, <bl>das Blech</bl> / lamina, <bl>das Loch</bl> / foramen, <bl>das Block</bl> / truncus, <bl>das Joch</bl> / jugum, <bl>das Fleisch</bl>
units.tr: First, names of towns, villages, letters and syllables: for example, das Leipzig (Leipzig, Latin Lipsia), das Basel (Basel, Latin Basilea), das Ulm, das Ja (the yes), das Nein (the no). Excepted is die Lippe (the city Lippia), and some others. Then nouns ending in -ment, -nis, -len or -lin, and some other nouns: for example, das Sacrament (sacrament), das Gezeugnis (testimony), das Gefängnis (prison), das Männlein (little man), das Fräulein (little woman), das Grab (grave), das Weib (woman), das Kalb (calf), das Lamb (lamb), das Bad (bath), das Rad (wheel), das Augenglied (eyelid), das Glied (limb), das Lied (song), das Leid (sorrow), das Wild (game), das Bild (image), das Gold (gold), das Band (band), das Land (land), das Pfand (pledge), das Kind (child), das Rind (ox), das End (end), das Elend (misery), das Pfund (pound), das Pferd (horse), das Felsen [?] (rock), das Schaf (sheep), das Schaff (vessel), das Schiff (ship), das Dorff (village), das Ding (thing), das Bedüng (condition), das Dach (roof), das Fach (compartment), das Gemach (chamber), das Gelach (feast), das Pech (pitch), das Blech (plate), das Loch (hole), das Block (block), das Joch (yoke), das Fleisch (flesh).

units.la: Compositis præponitur Genus finalis nominis, ut, <bl>der apffelbaum</bl>/pomus, <bl>d'birnbaum</bl>[?]/pyrus: quia dicimus <bl>der baum</bl>/arbor, <bl>das einhorn</bl>/unicornis, <bl>dz</bl>[?] <bl>Eichhorn</bl>/Sciurus: quia dicimus <bl>das horn</bl>/cornu.
units.tr: Compounds take the gender of their final noun, for example der Apfelbaum (apple tree), pomus, der Birnbaum [?] (pear tree), pyrus; because we say der Baum (tree), arbor. Das Einhorn (unicorn), unicornis; das Eichhorn (squirrel), sciurus; because we say das Horn (horn), cornu.

units.la: Quid est commune Genus?
units.tr: What is common gender?

units.la: Cujus notæ sunt duo articuli: ut, <bl>der ge-</bl> <bl>vatter/</bl> compater, & <bl>die gevatter/</bl> commater, pro quo nos Westphali dicimus, <bl>die</bl> <bl>vadderiche/ & die gemahl[?]/</bl> conjux, <bl>der & das theil/</bl> pars, <bl>der & das scepter/</bl> sceptrum, <bl>die & das e kentnis[?]/</bl> notitia, <bl>die & das gifft/</bl> venenum. Hęc communia vulgo appellantur Dubia.
units.tr: Its marks are two articles, for example der Gevatter (godfather), compater, and die Gevatter (godmother), commater, for which we Westphalians say die Vadderiche and die Gemahl [?] (spouse), conjux; der und das Theil (part), pars; der und das Scepter (sceptre), sceptrum; die und das Kentnis [?] (knowledge), notitia; die und das Gifft (poison), venenum. These words are commonly called Dubia (doubtful).

units.la: Quid est omne Genus?
units.tr: What are the genders?

units.la: Cujus notæ sunt articuli <bl>Der/Die/Das:</bl> ut, <bl>Der/Die/</bl> <bl>Das fromme.</bl>
units.tr: The articles Der/Die/Das are its marks, as in Der/Die/Das fromme.

units.la: Quæ Nomina sunt omnis generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of every gender?

units.la: Quædam Adjectiva habent tres terminationes: ut, <bl>ein kluer man/ein kluge frau/ ein kluges thier.</bl> Masculinum Genus definit in er/ fœmininum in e/ neutrum in es/ quando <bl>ein/</bl> vel <bl>mein/</bl> vel o Adjectivo præponitur. Dicimus <bl>ʒween</bl> / in masculino genere, <bl>ʒwo</bl> in fœminino, <bl>ʒwey[?]</bl> in neutro.
units.tr: Some adjectives have three endings: ein kluer man, ein kluge frau, ein kluges thier. The masculine gender ends in er, the feminine in e, and the neuter in es, when ein or mein, or some such word, is placed before the adjective. We say zween in the masculine, zwo in the feminine, and zwey in the neuter.

units.la: Quot sunt Casus?
units.tr: How many cases are there?

units.la: Sex: Nominativus, Genitivus, Dativus, Accusativus, Vocativus & Ablativus.
units.tr: Six: nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, vocative and ablative.

units.la: Quot sunt Declinationes apud Germanos?
units.tr: How many declensions are there among the Germans?

units.la: Duæ: prima & secunda.
units.tr: Two: the first and the second.

units.la: Quid est prima declinatio?
units.tr: What is the first declension?

units.la: Prima Declinatio est quæ complectitur nomina masculini vel neutrius generis. Quædam bifariam Nominativo casu efferuntur: ut, der frieD & friede[?]/ pax, das aug & auge/ oculus, das gesinD & gesinde/ familia, der garten & garte / hortus, der nammen & namme/nomen, der jamen & same[?]/semen, der huften & huste/tussis, der wagen & wage/currus, der kasten & kaste[?] / arca. Juxta priorem terminationem casus formantur: ut, des nammens/des samens[?].
units.tr: The first declension is the one that includes nouns of the masculine or neuter gender. Some are produced in the nominative case in two forms: for example, der frieD & friede / pax (peace), das aug & auge / oculus (eye), das gesinD & gesinde / familia (household), der garten & garte / hortus (garden), der nammen & namme / nomen (name), der jamen & same[?] / semen (seed), der huften & huste / tussis (cough), der wagen & wage / currus (cart), der kasten & kaste[?] / arca (chest). The cases are formed according to the first form: for example, des nammens / des samens[?].

units.la: Cedò paradigmata primæ Declinationis. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Come, the paradigms of the first declension. Singular number.

units.la: N. <bl>Der meister/</bl> magister, | <bl>Das land/</bl> regio. G. <bl>Des meisters/</bl> | <bl>Des landes.</bl> D. <bl>Dem meister/</bl> | <bl>Dem lande.</bl> A. <bl>Den meister/</bl> | <bl>Das land.</bl> V. <bl>O meister/</bl> | <bl>O land.</bl> A. <bl>Vom[?] meister/</bl> | <bl>Vom[?] lande.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. The master / The land. Gen. Of the master / Of the land. Dat. To the master / To the land. Acc. The master / The land. Voc. O master / O land. Abl. From the master / From the land.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.

units.la: N. <bl>Die meister/</bl> | <bl>Die länder.</bl> G. <bl>Der meister/</bl> | <bl>Der länder.</bl> D. <bl>Den meistern/</bl> | <bl>Den ländern.</bl> A. <bl>Die meister/</bl> | <bl>Die länder.</bl> V. <bl>O ihr meister/</bl> | <bl>O ihr länder.</bl> A. <bl>Von den meistern.</bl> | <bl>Von den ländern.</bl>
units.tr: Nominative: The masters / The lands. Genitive: Of the master / Of the land. Dative: To the masters / To the lands. Accusative: The masters / The lands. Vocative: O you masters / O you lands. Ablative: From the masters / From the lands.

units.la: Unde genitivus singularis formatur?
units.tr: From what is the genitive singular formed?

units.la: Unde Dativus singularis formatur?
units.tr: From what is the dative singular formed?

units.la: A Genitivo singulari, abiecta litera s: ut, <bl>Des</bl> <bl>bauchs/Dem bauch. Des stabs/Dem stabe.</bl>
units.tr: From the genitive singular, with the letter s dropped: des bauchs, dem bauch; des stabs, dem stabe.

units.la: Quae est pluralis Numeri formatio?
units.tr: How is the plural number formed?

units.la: Masculina desinentia in el/en/er vel e: nihil in plurali assumunt, nisi quod Dativo & Ablativo n addat: ut, <bl>Der Engel/Angelus, Die Engel/Den Engeln. Der stecken/fustis, Die</bl> <bl>stecken/Den stecken. Der meister/</bl> <bl>magister, Die meister/Den meistern.</bl>
units.tr: Masculine nouns ending in el, en, er or e take nothing in the plural, except that they add n in the dative and ablative: der Engel (angelus), die Engel, den Engeln; der stecken (fustis), die stecken, den stecken; der meister (magister), die meister, den meistern.

units.la: Exeuntia in reliquas masculinas terminationes assumunt in plurali e: Et quaed m in e/o in ö/u in ü/au in eu/mutant: ut, <bl>Der gesang/cantus, Die gesenge.</bl> <bl>Der rock/tunica, Die röcke. Der sprung/saltus, Die</bl> <bl>sprünge. Der baum/arbor, Die bäume. Der zaun/sepes[?],</bl> <bl>Die zeune.</bl> Quae consonam geminant assumunt er: ut, <bl>Der mann/vir, Die männer. Der Gott/Deus, Die</bl> <bl>Götter. Sic der geist/Spiritus, Die geister. Der wurm/ver-</bl> <bl>mis, Die würme</bl>: ut Spangenberg in sua postilla loquitur.
units.tr: Masculine nouns ending in other consonants take e in the plural, and those with a, o, u or au change these vowels to ä, ö, ü or äu: der gesang (song, cantus), die gesenge; der rock (tunic, tunica), die röcke; der sprung (leap, saltus), die sprünge; der baum (tree, arbor), die bäume; der zaun (hedge, sepes), die zeune. Those that double a consonant take er: der mann (man, vir), die männer; der Gott (God, Deus), die Götter; so der geist (spirit, spiritus), die geister; der wurm (worm, vermis), die würme, as Spangenberg says in his postil.

units.la: Neutra desinentia in f/g/t/l/n/r/nis/ assumunt e: ut, <bl>Das schaf/ovis, Die schafe. Das ding/res, Die dinge. Das geschenck/donum,</bl> <bl>Die geschencke. Das spiel/ludus, Die spiele. Das schwein/porcus, Die schweine.</bl> <bl>Das thier/animal, Die thiere. Das zeugnis/testimo-</bl> <bl>nium, Die zeugnisse. Sic Das pferd/equus, Die pferde.</bl> <bl>Das ross/caballus, Die rosse.</bl> Et pauca alia. Exeuntia in reliquas neutrales terminationes, mutatis vocalibus & diphthongis ut supra, assumunt er: ut, <bl>das</bl> <bl>grab</bl> / sepulchrum, <bl>die greber. das loch/</bl>foramen, <bl>die</bl> <bl>löcher. das büch/</bl>liber, <bl>die bücher. das schwerd/</bl>gladius, <bl>die schwerdter.</bl> Sic <bl>das volck/</bl> populus, <bl>die</bl> <bl>völcker. das maul/</bl>os, <bl>die meuler. das korn/</bl>granum, <bl>die</bl> <bl>körner. das horn/</bl>cornu, <bl>die hörner. das hun/</bl>gallina, <bl>die hüner. das wort /</bl> verbum, <bl>die wort & wörter.</bl> Diminutiva in lein vel lin nihil in plurali assumunt: ut, <bl>das men-nlin</bl> masculus, <bl>die mennlin.</bl>
units.tr: Neuter nouns ending in f, g, t, l, n, r, or -nis take -e in the plural, e.g. das Schaf/sheep, die Schafe; das Ding/thing, die Dinge; das Geschenck/gift, die Geschencke; das Spiel/game, die Spiele; das Schwein/pig, die Schweine; das Thier/animal, die Thiere; das Zeugnis/testimony, die Zeugnisse. Likewise das Pferd/horse, die Pferde; das Ross/steed, die Rosse. And a few others. Neuter nouns ending in other terminations, changing the vowels and diphthongs as above, take -er in the plural, e.g. das Grab/grave, die Greber; das Loch/hole, die Löcher; das Buch/book, die Bücher; das Schwerd/sword, die Schwerdter. Likewise das Volck/people, die Völcker; das Maul/mouth, die Meuler; das Korn/grain, die Körner; das Horn/horn, die Hörner; das Huhn/hen, die Hüner; das Wort/word, die Wort und Wörter. Diminutives in -lein or -lin do not change in the plural, e.g. das Männlin/male, die Männlin.

units.la: Quid est secunda Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the second declension?

units.la: Secunda Declinatio est, quae complectitur nomina foeminini vel omnis generis.
units.tr: The second declension comprises nouns of the feminine gender, or of every gender.

units.la: Cedo paradigmata secundae Declinationis. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Here are the paradigms of the second declension. Singular number.

units.la: N. <bl>Die lade/</bl> arca, <bl>der/ die/ das gute/</bl> bonus, na, num. G. <bl>Der laden/ des/ der/ des guten/</bl> & gu es/guter/ abjectis articulis: ut, <bl>gutes verstades/guter art.</bl> D. <bl>Der laden/dem/der/dem guten.</bl> A. <bl>Die lade/den guten/die gute/das gute.</bl> V. <bl>O lade/guter/gute/gutes.</bl> A. <bl>Von der laden/dem/der/dem guten.</bl>
units.tr: Nominative: the chest (feminine); the good (masculine, feminine, neuter). Genitive: of the chest; of the good (masculine, feminine, neuter), and with the article dropped, "guter" and "gutes", as in "gutes verstandes / guter art" (of good understanding, of good disposition). Dative: to the chest; to the good (masculine, feminine, neuter). Accusative: the chest; the good (masculine); the good (feminine); the good (neuter). Vocative: O chest; O good (masculine, feminine, neuter). Ablative: from the chest; from the good (masculine, feminine, neuter).

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.

units.la: N. <bl>Die laden / die guten / & gute/</bl> abjecto articulo: ut, <bl>gute vnnd fromme männer werden zu diser</bl> <bl>zeit verachtet:</bl> Boni & probi viri hoc seculo contemnuntur. G. <bl>Der laden / der guten/ & guter /</bl> abjecto articulo: ut, <bl>guter dinge sein.</bl> Hilari animo esse. D. <bl>Den laden/den guten.</bl> A. <bl>Die laden/die guten.</bl> V. O <bl>ihr laden/ o ihr guten.</bl> A. <bl>Von den laden/von den guten.</bl>
units.tr: Nominative: the chests; the good, and good (with the article dropped), as in "good and upright men are despised in this age" (Boni et probi viri hoc seculo contemnuntur). Genitive: of the chests; of the good, and of good (article dropped), as in "to be of good cheer" (Hilari animo esse). Dative: to the chests; to the good. Accusative: the chests; the good. Vocative: O you chests; O you good. Ablative: from the chests; from the good.

units.la: Horum flexionem sequuntur & alia quaedam masculina ac neutra: ut,<bl>der knab</bl> & <bl>knabe</bl>/puer, <bl>des knabe</bl>. <bl>der Herr</bl> & <bl>Herre</bl>/Dominus, <bl>des Herren</bl>. <bl>der Planet</bl>/ Planeta, <bl>des Planeten</bl>. <bl>das Herz</bl>/cor, <bl>des Herzen</bl>.
units.tr: Other masculine and neuter nouns follow this inflection: the boy (der Knab, also Knabe; puer), genitive of the boy (des Knaben); the lord (der Herr, also Herre; Dominus), genitive of the lord (des Herren); the planet (der Planet; planeta), genitive of the planet (des Planeten); the heart (das Herz; cor), genitive of the heart (des Herzen).

units.la: Observationes.
units.tr: Observations.

units.la: In e desinentia, si sint substantiæ, in singulari, Nominativum, Accusativum & Vocativum habent similes, in cæteris casibus, & in toto plurali assumunt n; Reliqua in e singulari numero sunt indeclinabilia: in plurali vero declinantur, sicut <bl>die laden</bl>. Fœminina in consonam desinentia, singulari numero sunt indeclinabilia: in plurali vero e assumunt, mutatis vocalibus ut supra, Dativo & Ablativo pluralibus n addunt: ut, <bl>die hand</bl>/ manus, <bl>die hende</bl>/ <bl>den henden</bl>. <bl>die brust</bl>/pectus: <bl>die brußte den brüsten</bl>. <bl>die Statt</bl>/ Urbs, <bl>die Stette</bl>/<bl>den Stetten</bl>.
units.tr: Nouns ending in e, if they are substantives, have the nominative, accusative and vocative alike in the singular; in the other cases, and throughout the plural, they take n. The rest of the nouns ending in e are indeclinable in the singular, but in the plural they are declined like "die laden". Feminine nouns ending in a consonant are indeclinable in the singular; in the plural they take e, with the vowels changed as above, and add n in the dative and ablative plural. For example: the hand (die Hand; manus), plural the hands (die Hende), dative to the hands (den Henden); the breast (die Brust; pectus), plural the breasts (die Brüste), dative to the breasts (den Brüsten); the city (die Statt; urbs), plural the cities (die Stette), dative to the cities (den Stetten).

units.la: Declina Adjectiva anomala, quæ Vulgò prono- mina appellantur.
units.tr: Decline the anomalous adjectives, which are commonly called pronouns.

units.la: N. Ich / ego. G. meiner / mei. D. mihi / mihi. A. mich / me. Abl. von mir / à me. Pluralis Num. N. wir/ nos. G. unser / nostrum vel nostri. D. uns/ nobis. A. uns/nos. Abl. von uns / à nobis. N. Du/ tu. G. deiner/ tui. D. dir/ tibi. A. dich/ te. V. o du/ô tu. Abl. von dir / à te. Plur. Num. N. ihr/ vos. G. ewer / vestrum vel vestri. D. euch/ vobis. A. euch/vos. Voc. o ihr/ô vos. Abl. von euch / à vobis. G. seiner/ihrer/seiner/sui. D. ihm/ihr/ihm/sibi. A. sich/se. Abl. von sich / à se. Plur. Num. G. ihrer/ sui. D. ihnen/sibi. A. sich/se. Abl. von sich/à se.
units.tr: Nom. I (ego). Gen. of me (mei). Dat. to me (mihi). Acc. me (me). Abl. from me (à me). Plural. Nom. we (nos). Gen. of us (nostrum or nostri). Dat. to us (nobis). Acc. us (nos). Abl. from us (à nobis). Nom. you (tu). Gen. of you (tui). Dat. to you (tibi). Acc. you (te). Voc. O you (ô tu). Abl. from you (à te). Plural. Nom. you (vos). Gen. of you (vestrum or vestri). Dat. to you (vobis). Acc. you (vos). Voc. O you (ô vos). Abl. from you (à vobis). Gen. of him, of her, of it, of them (sui). Dat. to him, to her, to it (sibi). Acc. himself, herself, itself (se). Abl. from himself (à se). Plural. Gen. of them (sui). Dat. to them (sibi). Acc. themselves (se). Abl. from themselves (à se).

units.la: Ex dictis pronominibus oriuntur hæc possessiva: <bl>Mein</bl>/<bl>Dein</bl>/<bl>Sein</bl>. N. <bl>Mein</bl>/<bl>meine</bl>/<bl>mein</bl>/meus,a,um. G. <bl>Meines</bl>/<bl>meiner</bl>/<bl>meines</bl>. D. <bl>Meinem</bl>/<bl>meiner</bl>/<bl>meinem</bl>. A. <bl>Meinen</bl>/<bl>meine</bl>/ <bl>mein</bl>. V. O <bl>mein/meine/mein.</bl> A. <bl>Von meinem/meiner/meinem.</bl> Plural. Num. N. <bl>Meine</bl>/mei,meæ,mea. G. <bl>Meiner</bl>/meorum,arum,orum. D. <bl>Meinen</bl>/meis. A. <bl>Meine</bl>/meos,meas,mea. V. O <bl>meine</bl>/mei,æ,a. A. <bl>Von meinen</bl>/à meis.
units.tr: From these pronouns come the possessives my, thy and his. Nominative: my (masculine), my (feminine), my (neuter); the Latin is meus, a, um. Genitive: of my (masculine), of my (feminine), of my (neuter). Dative: to my (masculine), to my (feminine), to my (neuter). Accusative: my (masculine), my (feminine), my (neuter). Vocative: O my (masculine), O my (feminine), O my (neuter). Ablative: from my (masculine), from my (feminine), from my (neuter). Plural nominative: my (in all genders; Latin mei, mea, mea). Genitive: of my (Latin meorum, arum, orum). Dative: to my (Latin meis). Accusative: my (Latin meos, meas, mea). Vocative: O my. Ablative: from my (Latin a meis).

units.la: Ad hunc modum declinabis: <bl>dein/deine/dein/</bl> tuus,a,uum: <bl>Sein/seine/sein</bl> / Latinè redditur ejus, non suus:ut,<bl>sein Vatter vnd sein Mutter seind gestor-</bl> <bl>ben</bl> / ejus pater & ejus mater sunt mortui: non, suus pater & sua mater,ut vulgus loquitur. Sic in Nominativo plurali, <bl>seine Eltern vnd seine Schwestern sind</bl> <bl>gestorben</bl> / redditur, ejus parentes & ejus sorores obierunt: Non,sui parentes & suæ sorores. In obliquis, Suus,locum obtinet: ut, <bl>Petrus hat seines Vatters</bl> <bl>vnd seiner Mutter bald vergessen</bl> / Petrus sui Patris & suæ Matris citò oblitus est: non, ejus patris & matris: Sic enim alterius parentes intelligerentur. N. <bl>Der/die/das</bl>/hic, hæc,hoc. G. <bl>Des/der/des.</bl> D. <bl>Dem/der/dem.</bl> A. <bl>Den/die/das.</bl> Abl. <bl>Von dem/</bl> <bl>der / dem.</bl> Plural. Num. N. <bl>Die</bl> / in omni genere. G. <bl>Der</bl>/vel <bl>derer.</bl> D. <bl>Den</bl> vel <bl>denen.</bl> A. <bl>Die.</bl> Abl. <bl>Von den</bl> vel <bl>denen.</bl> Sic <bl>diefer/ diese/ dieß/</bl> hic,hæc, hoc. G. <bl>Dieses/diefer/dieses/</bl>&c.
units.tr: Decline thy and his in the same way. Thy (masculine, feminine, neuter) is rendered by the Latin tuus, a, um. His is rendered in Latin by the non-reflexive possessive ejus, not suus: for example, "his father and his mother are dead" is rendered "ejus pater et ejus mater sunt mortui", not "suus pater et sua mater", as the common people say. Likewise in the nominative plural, "his parents and his sisters have died" is rendered "ejus parentes et ejus sorores obierunt", not "sui parentes et suae sorores". In the oblique cases the reflexive suus takes its place: "Peter soon forgot his father and mother" is rendered "Petrus sui patris et suae matris cito oblitus est", not "ejus patris et matris", since the latter would mean the parents of someone else. Nominative: the, this (masculine, feminine, neuter); Latin hic, haec, hoc. Genitive: of the, of this (masculine, feminine, neuter). Dative: to the, to this (masculine, feminine, neuter). Accusative: the, this (masculine, feminine, neuter). Ablative: from the, from this (masculine, feminine, neuter). Plural nominative: the (in all genders). Genitive: of the (or of those). Dative: to the (or to those). Accusative: the. Ablative: from the (or from those). Likewise "this" (diefer, diese, diess; Latin hic, haec, hoc): genitive of this, and so on.

units.la: Sæpe pronominibus,<bl>der/die/das/</bl>vox,<bl>selbige</bl> an-nectitur: ut, <bl>der selbige/die selbige/dasselbige/</bl>ille,illa,illud,seu,is,ea,id. G. <bl>desselbigen/der</bl> <bl>selbigen des-</bl> <bl>selbigen.</bl> Declina <bl>selbige/sicut der/die/das gute.</bl> N. <bl>Er/sie/das/</bl> is,ea,id. G. <bl>Seiner/</bl>fœm. <bl>ihrer/</bl> ejus. D. <bl>Ihm/ihr/ihm/</bl>ei. A. <bl>Ihn/sie/es</bl> vel s/ eum, eam,id.
units.tr: The word "selbige" (same) is often attached to the pronouns der, die, das: the same (masculine), the same (feminine), the same (neuter); Latin ille, illa, illud, or is, ea, id. Genitive: of the same (masculine), of the same (feminine), of the same (neuter). Decline "selbige" like "der, die, das gute". Nominative: he, she, it (Latin is, ea, id). Genitive: of him, of her, of it (Latin ejus). Dative: to him, to her, to it (Latin ei). Accusative: him, her, it (Latin eum, eam, id; or s).

units.la: Es vero & s affixa pronomina possunt appellari: quia semper verbis affiguntur: ut, <bl>ich habe</bl> es gethan/vel ich habs getħan/ego id feci. Es est etiam particula, quæ verbis tertiæ personæ præfigitur, quando post verbum Nominativus ponitur: ut, Es sagt Paulus daß böse geschwetze verderben gute sitte/ Dicit Paulus,quod prava colloquia corrumpant bonos mores. A. Von ihm/ ihr/ ihm/ ab eo, ea, eo, Plural.Num. N. Sie/in omni genere. G. Ihren. D. Ihnen. A. Sie. Abl. Von ihnen. N. Wer vel welcher / quis vel qui, fœm. welche. Neut. Was vel welches. G. Wes vel welches/ welcher/wes vel welches/cujus. D. Wem vel welchem/ welcher / wem vel welchem. A. Wen vel welchen/ welche / was vel welches. Abl. Von wem vel welchem/ welcher/ wem vel welchem. Plural.Num. N. Welche / in omni genere. G. Welcher. D. Welchen. A. Welche. Abl. Von welchen.
units.tr: The enclitic "es" and "s" may also be called affixed pronouns, since they are always attached to verbs: for example, "ich habe es gethan" or "ich habs gethan" (I have done it; ego id feci). "Es" is also a particle placed before verbs of the third person when a nominative follows the verb: for example, "Es sagt Paulus, daß böse Geschwätz gute Sitten verderben" (Paul says that evil talk corrupts good morals; Dicit Paulus, quod prava colloquia corrumpant bonos mores). Accusative: to him, to her, to it (von ihm, ihr, ihm; ab eo, ea, eo). Plural nominative: they (sie; in all genders). Genitive: of them (ihren). Dative: to them (ihnen). Accusative: them (sie). Ablative: from them (von ihnen). Nominative: who or which (wer, or welcher; Latin quis or qui); feminine, which (welche); neuter, what or which (was, or welches). Genitive: whose or of which (wes, or welches; Latin cujus). Dative: to whom or to which (wem, or welchem). Accusative: whom or which (wen, or welchen; feminine welche; neuter was, or welches). Ablative: from whom or which (von wem, or welchem). Plural nominative: which (welche; in all genders). Genitive: of which (welcher). Dative: to which (welchen). Accusative: which (welche). Ablative: from which (von welchen).

units.la: Quibusdam pronominibus particula, Selbs/annexti solet: ut, mich selbs/ memetipsum, dich selbs/ temetipsum,sich selbs/semetipsum,&c.
units.tr: To some pronouns the particle "selbs" (self) is usually added: for example, myself (mich selbs; memetipsum), thyself (dich selbs; temetipsum), himself (sich selbs; semetipsum), and so on.

units.la: DE VERBO.
units.tr: On the Verb.

units.la: Quid est Verbum?
units.tr: What is a verb?

units.la: VErbum est vox numeri cum forma, persona,tempore & conjugatione.
units.tr: A verb is a word inflected for number, with form, person, tense and conjugation.

units.la: Quotuplex est forma Verbi?
units.tr: How many kinds of form does a verb have?

units.la: Duplex: Prima aut Secunda.
units.tr: Two: the first and the second.

units.la: Quid est prima forma?
units.tr: What is the first form?

units.la: Prima forma est, quæ complectitur verba activa & neutra.
units.tr: The first form is the one that includes active and neuter verbs.

units.la: Conjuga verba formæ primæ, juxta quæ Tyrones reliqua formēt.
units.tr: Conjugate verbs of the first form, by which beginners form the rest.

units.la: Primum præsens tempus.
units.tr: The first present tense.

units.la: Ich liebe/ amo, du liebest/ er liebet/ wir lieben/ ihr liebe / sie lieben.
units.tr: <bl>Ich liebe</bl> / I love, <bl>du liebest</bl> / you love, <bl>er liebet</bl> / he loves, <bl>wir lieben</bl> / we love, <bl>ihr liebe</bl> / you love, <bl>sie lieben</bl> / they love.

units.la: Ich bin/ sum, du bist/ er ist/ wir sind oder sein/ ihr seid/ sie sind oder sein oder seind.
units.tr: I am / sum; you are; he is; we are, or be; you are; they are, or be, or are.

units.la: Secundum præsens tempus.
units.tr: The second present tense.

units.la: Auff daß ich liebe / ut amem, du liebest / er liebe/ wir lieben/ ihr liebet / sie lieben.
units.tr: So that I may love / ut amem; that you may love; that he may love; that we may love; that you may love; that they may love.

units.la: Auff daß ich sey/ ut sim,Du seiest/er sey/wir seien/ ihr seiet/ sie seien.
units.tr: So that I may be / ut sim; that you may be; that he may be; that we may be; that you may be; that they may be.

units.la: Primum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The first imperfect tense.

units.la: Ich liebete / & per syncopen, liebte / amabam, du liebetest / er liebete / wir liebeten / ihr liebetet / sie liebeten.
units.tr: <bl>Ich liebete</bl>, and by syncope <bl>liebte</bl> / I loved, <bl>du liebetest</bl> / you loved, <bl>er liebete</bl> / he loved, <bl>wir liebeten</bl> / we loved, <bl>ihr liebetet</bl> / you loved, <bl>sie liebeten</bl> / they loved.

units.la: Ich war oder was/ eram, du warest/ er war/ wir waren/ ihr waret/ sie waren.
units.tr: <bl>Ich war</bl> or <bl>was</bl> / I was, <bl>du warest</bl> / you were, <bl>er war</bl> / he was, <bl>wir waren</bl> / we were, <bl>ihr waret</bl> / you were, <bl>sie waren</bl> / they were.

units.la: Secundum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The second imperfect tense.

units.la: Wolt Gott oder daß ich liebete / utinam vel ut amarem, du liebetest / er liebete / wir liebeten/ ihr liebetet/ ie liebeten.
units.tr: <bl>Wolt Gott oder daß ich liebete</bl> / would that I loved, <bl>du liebetest</bl> / would that you loved, <bl>er liebete</bl> / would that he loved, <bl>wir liebeten</bl> / would that we loved, <bl>ihr liebetet</bl> / would that you loved, <bl>sie liebeten</bl> / would that they loved.

units.la: Wolt Gott oder daß ich wäre/ utinam vel ut essem, du wärest/ er wäre/ wir wären/ ihr wäret/ sie wären.
units.tr: <bl>Wolt Gott oder daß ich wäre</bl> / would that I were, <bl>du wärest</bl> / would that you were, <bl>er wäre</bl> / would that he were, <bl>wir wären</bl> / would that we were, <bl>ihr wäret</bl> / would that you were, <bl>sie wären</bl> / would that they were.

units.la: Secundi imperfecti verba irregularia formantur à primi imperfecti secunda persona, mutato a in e/ o in ö/ u in ü/ & st abjecto: ut, ich hatte/ du hattest. wolt Gott oder das ich hätte. Ich schob / du schobest. wolt Gott oder daß ich schöbe. Ich starb / du stür-best. wolt Gott oder daß ich stürbe.
units.tr: The second imperfect of irregular verbs is formed from the second person of the first imperfect, changing a to e, o to ö, u to ü, and dropping st: for example, <bl>ich hatte / du hattest</bl>, and <bl>wolt Gott oder das ich hätte</bl> (would that I had); <bl>ich schob / du schobest</bl>, and <bl>wolt Gott oder daß ich schöbe</bl> (would that I pushed); <bl>ich starb / du stürbest</bl>, and <bl>wolt Gott oder daß ich stürbe</bl> (would that I died).

units.la: Perfectum tempus.
units.tr: The perfect tense.

units.la: Ich habe geliebet / amavi, du hast geliebet / er hat geliebet / wir haben geliebet / ihr habet geliebet / sie haben geliebet.
units.tr: <bl>Ich habe geliebet</bl> / I have loved, <bl>du hast geliebet</bl> / you have loved, <bl>er hat geliebet</bl> / he has loved, <bl>wir haben geliebet</bl> / we have loved, <bl>ihr habet geliebet</bl> / you have loved, <bl>sie haben geliebet</bl> / they have loved.

units.la: Ich bin gewesen / fui, du bist / er ist / wir sind / ihr seid / sie sind. Adde gewesen.
units.tr: I have been / fui; you are; he is; we are; you are; they are. Add "gewesen" (been).

units.la: Plusquamperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The pluperfect tense.

units.la: Ich hatte geliebet/amaveram, du hattest/er hatte/ wir hatten/ihr hattet/sie hatten. Adde geliebet.
units.tr: I had loved / amaveram; you had; he had; we had; you had; they had. Add "geliebet" (loved).

units.la: Ich war gewesen/fueram, du warest/er war/wir waren/ihr waret/sie waren. Adde gewesen.
units.tr: I was (having been) / fueram; you were; he was; we were; you were; they were. Add "gewesen" (been).

units.la: Pri[?]num futurum tempus.
units.tr: The first future tense.

units.la: Ich werde lieben / amabo, du wirst / er wird / wir werden / ihr werdet / sie werden. Adde lieben.
units.tr: I shall love / amabo; you will; he will; we shall; you will; they will. Add "lieben" (to love).

units.la: Ich werde sein/ero, du wirst/er wird/&c.
units.tr: I shall be / ero; you will be; he will be, etc.

units.la: Secundum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The second future tense.

units.la: Liebe du/ama, er liebe/lasset uns lieben/liebet ihr/ sie lieben.
units.tr: <bl>Liebe du</bl> / love thou, <bl>er liebe</bl> / let him love, <bl>lasset uns lieben</bl> / let us love, <bl>liebet ihr</bl> / love ye, <bl>sie lieben</bl> / let them love.

units.la: Sey du / sis vel es, er sey/ lasset uns sein/ seid ihr/ sie seien.
units.tr: Be thou / sis vel es; let him be; let us be; be ye; let them be.

units.la: Infinita verba.
units.tr: Infinitive verbs.

units.la: Lieben / | Geliebet haben. Sein / | Gewesen sein.
units.tr: <bl>Lieben</bl> / to love; <bl>Geliebet haben</bl> / to have loved. <bl>Sein</bl> / to be; <bl>Gewesen sein</bl> / to have been.

units.la: Cedò Verba, quorum imperfecta & perfecta irregularia ferè sunt.
units.tr: Verbs of the type ‘cedo’, whose imperfect and perfect forms are for the most part irregular.

units.la: Ich hawe / cedo, du hawest / er hawet / wir hawen. Imperfectum, Ich hieb / du hiebest. Perfectum, Ich habe gehawen.
units.tr: I hew / cedo; you hew; he hews; we hew. Imperfect: I hewed; you hewedst. Perfect: I have hewn.

units.la: Ich schreie / clamo, du schreiest. Imperfectum, Ich schrey / du schreiest. Perfectum, Ich habe geschreien.
units.tr: I cry out / clamo; you cry out. Imperfect: I cried out; you cried out. Perfect: I have cried out.

units.la: Ich thue / facio, du thust / er thut / wir thun / ihr thut / sie thun. Imperfectum, Ich thät / du thätest / er thät / wir thäten / ihr thätet / sie thäten. Perfectum, Ich habe gethan.
units.tr: I do / facio; you do; he does; we do; you do; they do. Imperfect: I did; you didst; he did; we did; you did; they did. Perfect: I have done.

units.la: In Be.
units.tr: In Be.

units.la: Ich schreibe / scribo, du schreibest. Imperfectum, Ich schreib / du schreibest / er schreib / wir schrieben / ihr schriebet / sie schrieben. Perfectum, Ich habe geschrieben. Sic bleiben/manere,& reiben/terere. Ableiben perfectum, ich bin geblieben.
units.tr: I write / scribo; you write. Imperfect: I wrote; you wrote; he wrote; we wrote; you wrote; they wrote. Perfect: I have written. Likewise "to remain" / manere, and "to rub" / terere. The perfect of "to leave off" (ableiben) is "I have left off" (ich bin geblieben).

units.la: Ich schiebe/ panem in furnum immitto, vel globū mitto, du scheubest/er scheubet/wir schieben. Imperfectum, ich schob / du schobest. Perfectum, ich habe geschoben.
units.tr: I push / panem in furnum immitto, or globum mitto; you push; he pushes; we push. Imperfect: I pushed; you pushed. Perfect: I have pushed.

units.la: Es stiebet/pulvis aut farina spargitur. Imperfectum, Es stob. Perfectum, Es hat gestoben.
units.tr: It drifts / pulvis aut farina spargitur. Imperfect: it drifted. Perfect: it has drifted.

units.la: Ich grabe/ fodio, du grabest/er grabet. Imperfectum, ich grub/ du grubest. Perfectum, ich habe gegraben.
units.tr: I dig / fodio; you dig; he digs. Imperfect: I dug; you dug. Perfect: I have dug.

units.la: Ich habe/ habeo, du hast/ er hat. Imperfectum, ich hatte/du hattest. Perfectum, ich habe gehabt.
units.tr: I have / habeo; you have; he has. Imperfect: I had; you had. Perfect: I have had.

units.la: Ich gebe/ do, du gibst/er gibt/wir geben. Imperfectum, ich gab/du gabest/er gab. Perfectum, ich habe gegeben.
units.tr: I give / do; you give; he gives; we give. Imperfect: I gave; you gave; he gave. Perfect: I have given.

units.la: Ich sterbe/morior, du stirbest/er stirbet/wir sterben. Imperfectum, ich starb / du sturbest vel storbest. Perfectum, ich bin gestorben.
units.tr: I die / morior; you die; he dies; we die. Imperfect: I died; you died. Perfect: I have died.

units.la: Ich hebe/attollo, du hebest. Imperfectum, ich hub/du hubest. Perfectum, ich habe gehaben/a crasso.
units.tr: I lift / attollo; you lift. Imperfect: I lifted; you lifted. Perfect: I have lifted, in the crude sense (a crasso).

units.la: Ich schaube/trudo, du scheubest/er scheubet. Imperfectum, ich schob/du schobest. Perfectum, ich habe geschoben.
units.tr: I shove / trudo; you shove; he shoves. Imperfect: I shoved; you shoved. Perfect: I have shoved.

units.la: In Oe.
units.tr: Verbs in Oe.

units.la: Ich lade/ invito, vel onera plaustro impono, du lädst/er lädt/wir haben. Imperfectum, Ich lud / du ludest. Perfectum, Ich habe geladen.
units.tr: Ich lade (I invite, or I load a cart onto a wagon); du lädst, er lädt, wir laden. Imperfect: ich lud, du ludest. Perfect: ich habe geladen.

units.la: Ich schneide/ seco, du schneidest/er schneidet. Imperfectum, Ich schneid/du schnittest/er schneid. Perfectum, Ich habe geschnitten.
units.tr: I cut / seco; you cut, he cuts. Imperfect: I cut, you cut, he cut. Perfect: I have cut.

units.la: Ich leide/ patior, du leidest. Imperfectum, Ich leid/du liddest. Perfectum, Ich habe gelidden vel gelitten.
units.tr: I suffer / patior, you suffer. Imperfect: I suffered, you suffered. Perfect: I have suffered (the older forms are gelidden or gelitten).

units.la: Ich siede/ bullio, vel aliquid liquore feruenti coquo,du seudst/er seudt/wir sieden. Imperfectum,ich sod/du sottest. Perfect.ich habe gesotten.
units.tr: Ich siede (I boil, or I cook something in hot liquid); du siedest, er siedet, wir sieden. Imperfect: ich sott, du sottest. Perfect: ich habe gesotten.

units.la: Ich sende/mitto,du sendest. Imperfect. Ich sand-te/du sandtest. Perfect. ich habe gesandt.
units.tr: I send / mitto; you send. Imperfect: I sandte / you sandtest. Perfect: I have gesandt.

units.la: Ich wende/verto, du wendest/er wendet. Imperfectum, ich wandte/ du wandtest. Perfect. ich habe gewandt vel gewendet.
units.tr: I turn; you turn, he turns. Imperfect: I turned, you turned. Perfect: I have turned, or I have turned (gewendet).

units.la: Ich finde/invenio, du findest. Imperfect.ich fand/ du fundest/er fand. Perfectum,ich habe gefunden. Sic uberwinden/vincere: binden/vincire: verschwinden/ evanescere.
units.tr: I find / invenio (to find), you findest. Imperfect: I found, you foundest, he found. Perfect: I have found. Likewise überwinden (to overcome) / to conquer; binden (to bind) / to bind; verschwinden (to vanish) / to vanish.

units.la: Ich werde/fio,du wirst/er wird. Imper.ich ward/du wurdest vel woꝛdest. Perfect.ich bin geworden.
units.tr: I become/fio, you become/he becomes. Imperfect: I became/you wurdest or wordest. Perfect: I have become (ich bin geworden).

units.la: In se.
units.tr: Verbs in se.

units.la: Ich schlaffe/dormio,du schlessest. Imperfectū,ich schliest/du schliessest. Perfect.ich habe geschlaffen.
units.tr: Ich schlafe / I sleep: du schläfst. Imperfect: ich schlief / du schliefst. Perfect: ich habe geschlafen.

units.la: Ich schaffe/creo,du schaffest. Imperfect.ich schuff/du schuffest. Perfect.ich habe geschaffen.
units.tr: Ich schaffe / I create: du schaffst. Imperfect: ich schuf / du schufst. Perfect: ich habe geschaffen.

units.la: Ich treffe/tango,du trifst. Imperfect.ich traff/du traffst. Perfect.ich habe getroffen.
units.tr: Ich treffe / I touch: du triffst. Imperfect: ich traf / du trafst. Perfect: ich habe getroffen.

units.la: Ich ruffe/voco, du rüffst. Imperfectum, ich rieff/ du rieffst. Perfect. ich habe geruffen.
units.tr: Ich rufe / I call: du rufst. Imperfect: ich rief / du riefst. Perfect: ich habe gerufen.

units.la: Ich trieffe/stillo, du treuffst. Imperfectum, ich troff/du troffest. Perfect. ich habe getroffen.
units.tr: I drip / stillo; you drip (treuffst). Imperfect: I dripped (troff), you dripped (troffest). Perfect: I have dripped (getroffen).

units.la: Ich greiffe/palpo vel prehendo, du greiffst. Imperf. ich greiff/du grieffest. Perf. ich habe gegriffen. Sic schleiffen/acuere.
units.tr: Ich greife / I touch or I grasp: du greifst. Imperfect: ich griff / du griffest. Perfect: ich habe gegriffen. So likewise: schleifen / to whet.

units.la: Ich sauffe/potu me ingurgito, du seuffst. Imperfect.ich soff/du soffst. Perfect. ich habe gesoffen.
units.tr: Ich saufe / I drink, I gulp down: du säufst. Imperfect: ich soff / du soffst. Perfect: ich habe gesoffen.

units.la: Ich lauffe/curro,du leuffst. Imperfect.ich lieff/du lieffst. Perfect.ich habe vel bin gelauffen.
units.tr: Ich laufe / I run: du läufst. Imperfect: ich lief / du liefst. Perfect: ich habe or bin gelaufen.

units.la: Ich helffe/juvo,du hilffst. Imperfect. ich halff/du hulffest. Perfect. ich habe geholffen.
units.tr: Ich helfe / I help: du hilfst. Imperfect: ich half / du halfst. Perfect: ich habe geholfen.
