units.la: Ich werffe/jacio,du wirffst. Imperfect. ich warff/du wurffest vel woꝛffest. Perfect. ich habe geworffen.
units.tr: Ich werfe / I throw: du wirfst. Imperfect: ich warf / du wurfst or worfst. Perfect: ich habe geworfen.

units.la: Ich durff/audeo, du darffst. Imperf. ich durffte/ du durfftest. Perfect. ich habe gedurfft.
units.tr: Ich darf / I dare: du darfst. Imperfect: ich durfte / du durftest. Perfect: ich habe gedurft.

units.la: In Ge.
units.tr: Verbs in Ge.

units.la: Ich schlage/verbero, du schlegst/ er schleqt/ wir schlagen. Imperfect. ich schlug/du schlugest. Perfect. ich habe geschlagen.
units.tr: I strike (ich schlage; the Latin gloss means "I beat"), you strike (du schlegst), he strikes (er schleqt), we strike (wir schlagen). Imperfect: I struck (ich schlug), you struckest (du schlugest). Perfect: I have struck (ich habe geschlagen).

units.la: Ich trage / bajulo, du tregest/er treget / wir tragen. Imperfectum, ich trug/ du trugest. Perfectum, ich habe getragen.
units.tr: I carry (ich trage), you carry (du tregest), he carries (er treget), we carry (wir tragen). Imperfect: I carried (ich trug), you carriedst (du trugest). Perfect: I have carried (ich habe getragen).

units.la: Ich lige/cubo, du ligest/er ligt/wir ligen. Imperfectum, ich lag/du lagest. Perfect. ich habe gelegen.
units.tr: Ich liege / I lie down, I recline: du liegst / er liegt / wir liegen. Imperfect: ich lag / du lagst. Perfect: ich habe gelegen.

units.la: Ich liege/mentior, du leugest/ er leuget / wir liegen. Imperfectum, ich log/ du logest. Perfect. ich habe gelogen. Sic fliegen/volare, & betriegen/decipere.
units.tr: Ich lüge / I lie, I tell lies: du lügst / er lügt / wir lügen. Imperfect: ich log / du logst. Perfect: ich habe gelogen. So likewise: fliegen / to fly; betrügen / to deceive.

units.la: Ich sauge/fugo, du seugest. Imperfect. ich sog/ du sogest. Perfect. ich habe gesogen.
units.tr: Ich sauge / I suck: du saugst. Imperfect: ich sog / du sogst. Perfect: ich habe gesogen.

units.la: Ich steige/scando, du steigest. Imperfectum, ich steig/du stiegest. Perfectum, ich habe gestiegen. Sic schweigen/tacere.
units.tr: Ich steige / I climb: du steigst. Imperfect: ich stieg / du stiegst. Perfect: ich habe gestiegen. So likewise: schweigen / to be silent.

units.la: Ich singe/cano, du singest. Imperfectum, ich sang/ du sungest/er sang. Perfectum, ich habe gejungen. Sic klingen/tinnire, zwingen / cogere, ringen / luctari, springen/salire, & pauca similia.
units.tr: Ich singe / I sing: du singst. Imperfect: ich sang / du sangst / er sang. Perfect: ich habe gesungen. So likewise: klingen / to ring; zwingen / to compel; ringen / to wrestle; springen / to leap; and a few similar verbs.

units.la: Ich bringe/Adfero, du bringest/er bringet. Imperfectum, ich brachte/du brachtest. Perfectum, ich habe gebracht.
units.tr: I bring [Ich bringe]; you bring, he brings [du bringest, er bringet]. Imperfect: I brought, you brought [ich brachte, du brachtest]. Perfect: I have brought [ich habe gebracht].

units.la: Ich fange/capio, du fengest. Imperfect. ich fieng/ du fiengest. Perfectu, ich habe gefangen. Sic hangen/ pendere.
units.tr: Ich fange / I catch, I take: du fängst. Imperfect: ich fing / du fingst. Perfect: ich habe gefangen. So likewise: hangen / to hang.

units.la: Ich verberge/abscondo, du verbirgest/er verbirget. Imperfectum, ich verbarg/du verbargest. Perfectum, ich habe verborgen.
units.tr: Ich verberge / I hide: du verbirgst / er verbirgt. Imperfect: ich verbarg / du verbargst. Perfect: ich habe verborgen.

units.la: In Ie.
units.tr: Verbs in Ie.

units.la: <bl>Ich fahe</bl>/capio, <bl>du fehest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich fieng/</bl> <bl>du fiengest. Ich habe gefangen.</bl>
units.tr: Ich fahe / I catch, I take: du fehest. Imperfect: ich fing / du fingst. Perfect: ich habe gefangen.

units.la: <bl>Ich sehe</bl>/video, <bl>du siehest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich sah vel sahe. Ich habe gesehen.</bl>
units.tr: <bl>I see</bl>, <bl>you see.</bl> Imperfect: <bl>I saw or sawe. I have seen.</bl>

units.la: <bl>Ich gehe</bl>/eo, <bl>du gehest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich gieng/</bl> <bl>du giengest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe</bl> & <bl>bin gegangen.</bl>
units.tr: Ich gehe / I go: du gehst. Imperfect: ich ging / du gingst. Perfect: ich habe or bin gegangen.

units.la: <bl>Ich stehe</bl>/sto, <bl>du stehest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich stund/ du stundest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe gestanden.</bl>
units.tr: Ich stehe / I stand: du stehst. Imperfect: ich stand / du standst. Perfect: ich habe gestanden.

units.la: <bl>Ich ziehe</bl> / traho vel proficiscor, <bl>du zeuchst / er zeucht</bl> <bl>/ wir ziehen.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich zog/du zogest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe</bl> vel <bl>bin gezogen.</bl>
units.tr: I draw, or I set out (traho vel proficiscor); you draw, he draws, we draw. Imperfect: I drew, you drewest. Perfect: I have drawn, or I have set out (I am gone).

units.la: <bl>Ich fliehe</bl>/fugio, <bl>du fleuchst.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich floh</bl> <bl>vel flohe/du flohest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich bin geflohen.</bl>
units.tr: I flee / fugio, you flee. Imperfect: I fled, or I fled / you fledst. Perfect: I have fled.

units.la: <bl>Ich breche</bl> / frango, <bl>du brichst.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich brach / du brachest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe gebrochen.</bl> Sic <bl>stechen</bl>/pungere, <bl>sprechen</bl>/loqui.
units.tr: <bl>Ich breche</bl> / to break, <bl>du brichst</bl> (you break). Imperfect, <bl>ich brach / du brachest</bl> (I broke / you brokest). Perfect, <bl>ich habe gebrochen</bl> (I have broken). Likewise <bl>stechen</bl> (to prick) / to prick, <bl>sprechen</bl> (to speak) / to speak.

units.la: <bl>Ich schleiche</bl>/ serpo, <bl>du schleichest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich schleich/du schliehest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich bin geschlichen.</bl> Sic <bl>weichen</bl>/cedere.
units.tr: Ich schleiche / I creep: du schleichst. Imperfect: ich schlich / du schlichst. Perfect: ich bin geschlichen. So likewise: weichen / to yield.

units.la: <bl>Ich riecke</bl>/odoror, <bl>du reuchst/er reucht/ wir</bl> <bl>riechen.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich roch/du rochest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich</bl> <bl>habe gerochen.</bl>
units.tr: Ich rieche / I smell: du riechst / er riecht / wir riechen. Imperfect: ich roch / du rochst. Perfect: ich habe gerochen.

units.la: <bl>Ich leihe</bl> / mutuum do, <bl>du leihest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich leih/du liechest/er leih/wir liehen.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe</bl> <bl>geliehen.</bl> Sic <bl>verzeihen</bl>/ condonare.
units.tr: Ich leihe / I lend: du leihst. Imperfect: ich lieh / du liehst / er lieh / wir liehen. Perfect: ich habe geliehen. So likewise: verzeihen / to forgive.

units.la: <bl>Ich dresche</bl>/excutio tribula, <bl>du drischest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich drasch/ du draschest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe gedroschen.</bl>
units.tr: Ich dresche / I thresh, I beat out grain with a flail: du drischst. Imperfect: ich drosch / du drischst. Perfect: ich habe gedroschen.

units.la: <bl>Ich heische</bl>/postulo, <bl>du heischest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich hiesch/du hieschest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe geheischen.</bl>
units.tr: Ich heische / I demand: du heischst. Imperfect: ich heischte / du heischtest. Perfect: ich habe geheischt.

units.la: In Re.
units.tr: In Re.

units.la: <bl>Ich backe</bl>/ pinso, <bl>du beckest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich buch/</bl>[?] buch/du buchst. Perfect. ich habe gebacken.
units.tr: I bake (pinso), you bake (beckest). Imperfect: I baked (buck or buk), you baked (buchst). Perfect: I have baked (gebacken).

units.la: Ich trincke/ bibo, du trinckest[?]. Imperfectum, ich tranck/du truncke st[?]. Perfect. ich habe getruncken. Sic stincken/foetere, & pauca similia.
units.tr: I drink (ich trincke / bibo); you drink[?]. Imperfect: I drank (ich tranck), you drankest[?] (du truncke st[?]). Perfect: I have drunk (ich habe getruncken). Likewise stincken (to stink, foetere), and a few similar verbs.

units.la: In Le.
units.tr: In Le.

units.la: Ich stele/furor, du stilst/er stilt/wir stelen. Imperfectum, ich stal/du stolest. Perfect. ich habe gestolen.
units.tr: I steal/furor, you steal, he steals, we steal. Imperfect: I stole, you stolest. Perfect: I have stolen.

units.la: Ich male/ molo, du melest. Imperfect. ich mul/du mulest. Perfect. ich habe gemalen.
units.tr: I grind (male/molo), you grind (melest). Imperfect: I ground (mul), you grindest (mulest). Perfect: I have ground (gemalen).

units.la: Ich schwelle/tumesco, du schwillest. Imperfect. ich schwal/du schwollest. Perfect. ich bin geschwollen. Sic bellen/latrare, & quellen/scaturire.
units.tr: I swell / tumesco, you swell (du schwillest). Imperfect: I swelled (ich schwal / du schwollest). Perfect: I have swollen (ich bin geschwollen). So bark / latrare, and well up / scaturire.

units.la: Ich will/ volo, Ich sol/ debeo, du wilt/du solt/ er wil/ er sol/ wir wöllen/ söllen. Imperfect. ich wolte/ solte. Perfect. ich habe gewolt/gesolt.
units.tr: I will / I want (volo), I shall / I ought (debeo); you will / you shall, he will / he shall, we will / we shall. Imperfect: I wanted / I ought. Perfect: I have wanted / I have ought.

units.la: In Me.[?]
units.tr: In Me.[?]

units.la: Ich neme/accipio, du nimest/vel nimst/vel nimpst. Imperfectum , ich nam / du namest. Perfect. ich hab genomen.
units.tr: Ich neme (I take / accipio), du nimest, or nimst, or nimpst (thou takest). Imperfect: ich nam (I took), du namest (thou tookest). Perfect: ich hab genomen (I have taken).

units.la: Ich schwimme/nato, du schwimmest. Imperfect. ich schwam/du schwummest/er schwam. Perfect. ich habe vel bin geschwummen.
units.tr: I swim / nato; you swim. Imperfect: I swam / you swummest / he swam. Perfect: I have or am swum (geschwummen).

units.la: In Ne.
units.tr: In Ne.

units.la: Ich nenne/nuncupo, du nennest. Imperfectum, ich nennete & nandte. Perfectum , ich habe genennet & genandt. Sic rennen / cursitare, vel alite equo vehi: trennen/dissociare: brennen/urere.
units.tr: I name (ich nenne), you name (du nennest). Imperfect: I named (ich nennete and nandte). Perfect: I have named (ich habe genennet and genandt). Likewise rennen, to run about or to be carried on a winged horse; trennen, to separate; brennen, to burn.

units.la: Ich spinne/ neo, du spinnest. Imperfect. ich span/ du spunnest. Perfect. ich habe gespunnen. Sic zerzinnen/ effluere.
units.tr: I spin (neo), you spin. Imperfect: I span, you spunnest. Perfect: I have spun. Likewise, to run away, to flow away (zerrinnen).

units.la: Ich scheine/fulgeo, du scheinest. Imperfectum, ich schein/du schienest. Perfect. ich habe geschienen.
units.tr: I shine, you shinest. Imperfect: I shone, you shonest. Perfect: I have shone.

units.la: In Re.
units.tr: In Re.

units.la: Ich fahre/ curru vehor, du ferest. Imperfectum, ich fuhr / du fuhrest. Perfectum , ich habe vel bin gefaren.
units.tr: I drive (I am carried in a cart), you drive. Imperfect: I drove, you drove. Perfect: I have driven or I am driven.

units.la: Ich schwere/juro, du schwerest. Imperfectum, ich schwur/du schwurest. Perfect. ich habe geschworen.
units.tr: I swear (juro), thou swearest. Imperfect: I swore, thou swarest. Perfect: I have sworn.

units.la: Ich gebere/ pario, du geberest. Imperfectum, ich gebar. Perfectum, ich habe geboren.
units.tr: I bear / pario, thou bearest. Imperfect, I bore. Perfect, I have borne.

units.la: Ich verliere/amitto, du verleurest. Imperfectum, ich verlor/du verlorest. Perfect. ich habe verloren. Sic friere n/algere.
units.tr: I lose [amitto], you lose. Imperfect: I lost, you lost. Perfect: I have lost. So too: to freeze / to be cold [algere].

units.la: In Se.
units.tr: In Se.

units.la: Ich blase/flo, du blesest/er bleset/wir blasen. Imperfectum, ich blies/du bliefest. Perfectum, ich habe geblasen.
units.tr: I blow (Latin flo), you blow, he blows, we blow. Imperfect: I blew, you blewest. Perfect: I have blown.

units.la: Ich lese/lego, du lisest. Imperfectum, ich las/du lasest. Perfect.ich habe gelefen.
units.tr: I read/lego; you read (lisest). Imperfect: I read (las)/you read (lasest). Perfect: I have read (gelefen).

units.la: Ich wachse/crefco, du wechsest. Imperfectum,ich wuchs/du wuchsest. Perfectum , ich habe vel bin gewachsen.
units.tr: I grow [crefco], you growest. Imperfect: I grew, you grewest. Perfect: I have or am grown.

units.la: Ich weis/ scio, du weissest / er weis/ wir wissen. Imperf.ich wuste/ du wustest. Perf. ich habe gewust.
units.tr: I know; thou knowest; he knows; we know. Imperfect: I knew, thou knewest. Perfect: I have known.

units.la: <bl>Ich reisse/</bl> lacero vel rumpo, <bl>du reissest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich reiß/du reissest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe gerissen.</bl> Sic <bl>schmeissen</bl> / verberare: <bl>scheissen</bl> / pedere: <bl>befleissen/</bl> diligentiam adhibere : <bl>schleissen</bl> / terere : <bl>beissen/</bl> mordere.
units.tr: I tear, you tear (reissen): to tear or break. Imperfect: I tore, you tore. Perfect: I have torn. So too schmeissen: to hurl or beat; scheissen: to break wind; befleissen: to apply oneself diligently; schleissen: to wear down or wear out; beissen: to bite.

units.la: <bl>Ich giesse/</bl> fundo, <bl>du geussest/er geusset/wir gies-</bl> <bl>sen.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich gos/du gossest.</bl> Perfectum, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>habe gegossen.</bl> Sic <bl>fliessen/</bl> fluere : <bl>schliessen/</bl> claudere: <bl>geniessen</bl> / frui: <bl>entspriessen</bl> / originem sumere: <bl>schiessen/</bl> jaculari: <bl>verbriessen/</bl> male habere aliquem.
units.tr: I pour, you pour (du geussest), he pours (er geusset), we pour (wir giessen). Imperfect: I poured, you poured (du gossest). Perfect: I have poured. Likewise: to flow; to shut; to enjoy; to spring forth, to take origin; to shoot, to throw; to vex, to trouble someone.

units.la: In Te.
units.tr: In Te.

units.la: <bl>Ich brate[?]/</bl> asso, vel cibū ad ignem torreo, <bl>du</bl> <bl>briest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>briet/du brietest.</bl> Perfectū, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>habe gebraten.</bl> Sic <bl>rathen</bl> / consulere, vel conjicere, cum compositis.
units.tr: Ich brate [?] / I roast, or I scorch food over the fire, du briest. Imperfect: ich briet / du brietest. Perfect: ich habe gebraten. So also rathen / to advise, or to guess, with compounds.

units.la: <bl>Ich streite/</bl> pugno, <bl>du streitest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>streit/du streitest.</bl> Perfect. <bl>ich habe gestritten.</bl> Sic <bl>be-</bl> <bl>streiten/</bl> oppugnare: <bl>reiten/</bl> equitare: <bl>überschreiten/</bl> transgredi.
units.tr: I fight, pugno, you fight. Imperfect: I fought, you fought. Perfect: I have fought. So also: to attack, oppugnare; to ride, equitare; to transgress, transgredi.

units.la: <bl>Ich schelte</bl> / famae alicujus detraho, vel increpo, objurgo, <bl>du schiltest.</bl> Imperfect. <bl>ich schalt/du schol-</bl> <bl>test.</bl> Perfectū, <bl>ich habe geschotten.</bl> Sic <bl>gelten/</bl> valere, cum compositis.
units.tr: Ich schelte / I disparage someone's reputation, or I rebuke and chide, du schiltest. Imperfect: ich schalt / du scholtest. Perfect: ich habe geschotten. So also gelten / to be worth, with compounds.

units.la: <bl>Ich trette</bl> / calco, <bl>du trittest.</bl> Imperfectum, <bl>ich</bl>
units.tr: Ich trette / calco (I tread), du trittest. Imperfectum: ich

units.la: Note: the signature "b 4" stands below the last line. trat/du trattest Perfectum, ich habe getretten.
units.tr: trat, du trattest. Perfectum: ich habe getretten.

units.la: Ich bitte/rogo vel obiecro,du bittest. Imperfect, ich bat/du batst[?]. Perfect, ich habe gebeten.
units.tr: I ask or beseech, you ask. Imperfect: I bat / you batst[?]. Perfect: I have gebeten.

units.la: Ich flechte/ pleƈto, du flichst/er flicht. Imperfect., ich flocht/du floch est[?]. Perfect. ich hab geflochten. Sic fechten/ digladiari.
units.tr: I plait (pleto); you plait, he plaits. Imperfect: I plaited, you plaitedst [?]. Perfect: I have plaited. Likewise "fechten" (to fight with swords): digladiari.

units.la: In Se.
units.tr: In Itself.

units.la: Ich sitze/ sedeo,du sitzest. Imperfectum, ich saß/du saßst. Perfect, ich habe gesessen.
units.tr: I sit (sedeo), you sit. Imperfect: ich saß / du saßst. Perfect: ich habe gesessen.

units.la: Ich schmelze/ liquefco instar ceræ, vel metalli,vel pinguedinis,du schmelzest. Imperfect. Ich schmalz/du schmolzest. Perfect ich bin geschmolzen.
units.tr: I melt, like wax, or metal, or fat; thou meltest. Imperfect: I melted; thou meltedst. Perfect: I have melted.

units.la: Hæc enumerata verba in imperfecto & perfecto variantur: Reliqua omnia ad superiorem formam quadrant: ut, ich see/femino,du seest. Imperfectum, ich seete/du seetst[?]. Perfect. ich habe geseet.
units.tr: These verbs listed here vary in the imperfect and perfect; all the rest follow the former pattern, as: I sow, thou sowest. Imperfect: I sowed; thou sowedst [?]. Perfect: I have sown.

units.la: Ich kleibe/limo obstruo,du kleibest. Imperfectum, ich kleibete/du kleibe est. Perfectum, ich habe gekleibet. At bekleiben/radices agere, habet in Imperfecto bekleib.
units.tr: I daub, stop up, obstruct; thou daubest. Imperfect: I daubed; thou daubedst. Perfect: I have daubed. But bekleiben, to take root, has bekleib in the imperfect.

units.la: Ich schmelze/ liquefacio,du schmelzest. Imperfectum,ich schmelzete/du schmelzetest. Perfect.ich habe geschmelzet. Sic alia quàm plurima. Observandum verba regularia formare adjectiva participialia in t: irregularia verò in n: ut, Ich liebe/geliebet/Ich habe/gehawen.
units.tr: I melt (liquefacio): ich schmelze, du schmelzest. Imperfect: ich schmelzete / du schmelzetest. Perfect: ich habe geschmelzet. So with very many others. It should be noted that regular verbs form participial adjectives in -t, but irregular verbs in -n, for example: ich liebe / geliebet; ich habe / gehawen.

units.la: Quid est secunda forma Verbi?
units.tr: What is the second form of the verb?

units.la: Secunda forma est, quæ verba passiva cōplectitur.
units.tr: The second form is the one that comprises passive verbs.

units.la: Conjuga verbum secundæ formæ, juxta quod reliqua formentur.
units.tr: Conjugate a verb of the second form, by which the others are formed.

units.la: Primum præsens tempus.
units.tr: The first present tense.

units.la: Ich werde geliebet / amor, du wirst / er wird/ wir werden/ihr werdet / sie werden. Adde singulis personis geliebet.
units.tr: I become loved; thou becomest, he becomes, we become, you become, they become. Add geliebet to each person.

units.la: Secundum præsens tempus.
units.tr: The second present tense.

units.la: Auff das ich werde geliebet/ut amer,du werdest/ er werde/wir werden/ihr werdet/sie werden. Adde singulis personis geliebet.
units.tr: That I may become loved; that thou mayest become, he may become, we may become, you may become, they may become. Add geliebet to each person.

units.la: Primum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The first imperfect tense.

units.la: Ich ward geliebet/amabar, du wurdest/er ward/wir wurden/ihr wurdet/sie wurden. Adde geliebet.
units.tr: I became loved, I was loved; thou becamest, he became, we became, you became, they became. Add geliebet.

units.la: Secundum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The second imperfect tense.

units.la: Wolt Gott/oder das; ich würde geliebet / utinam vel ut amarer, du würdest/er würde/wir würden/ihr würdet/sie würden. Adde geliebet.
units.tr: Would God, or that; I would become loved, or that I might be loved; thou wouldest become, he would become, we would become, you would become, they would become. Add geliebet.

units.la: Perfectum tempus.
units.tr: The perfect tense.

units.la: Ich bin geliebet worden / amatus sum vel fui, du bist/er ist/wir sind/ihr seid/sie sind. Adde geliebet worden.
units.tr: I have been loved; thou hast been, he has been, we have been, you have been, they have been. Add geliebet worden.

units.la: Plusquamperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The pluperfect tense.

units.la: Ich war geliebet worden / amatus eram vel fuerā, du warst/er war/wir waren/ihr waret/sie waren. Adde geliebet worden.
units.tr: I had been loved; thou hadst been, he had been, we had been, you had been, they had been. Add geliebet worden.

units.la: Primum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The first future tense.

units.la: Ich werde geliebet werden / amabor, du wirst/er wird/wir werden/ihr werdet/sie werden. Adde ge-liebet werden.
units.tr: I shall become loved; thou wilt become, he will become, we shall become, you will become, they will become. Add geliebet werden.

units.la: Secundum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The second future tense.

units.la: Werde du geliebet / amaretu, er werde geliebet/ lasset uns werden geliebet / werdet ihr geliebet / sie werden geliebet.
units.tr: Become thou loved; let him become loved; let us become loved; become ye loved; let them become loved.

units.la: Infinitum.
units.tr: Infinitive.

units.la: Werden geliebet werden.
units.tr: To be loved: werden geliebet werden.

units.la: Hactenus dictum est de vocibus numeri, videlicet de Nomine & Verbo: sequuntur voces sine Numero, nempe Adverbium & Conjunctio.
units.tr: So far has been said about the words that have number, namely the noun and the verb. There follow the words without number, namely the adverb and the conjunction.

units.la: DE ADVERBIO.
units.tr: ON THE ADVERB.

units.la: Quid est Adverbium?
units.tr: What is an Adverb?

units.la: ADverbium est vox sine numero, quae alicui voci adjuncta circunstantiam ejus una voce effert: ut <bl>hie/</bl> hic, <bl>hieher/</bl> huc, <bl>von hinnen/</bl> hinc, <bl>heute/</bl> hodie, <bl>einmal/</bl> semel, <bl>ja/</bl> ita, <bl>warlich/</bl> nae, <bl>nein/</bl> non, <bl>sihe/</bl> en [?], <bl>wolt Gott/</bl> utinam, <bl>ey lieber/</bl> obsecro, <bl>warumb?</bl> cur? <bl>hoscha/</bl> heus, <bl>vielleicht/</bl> forsitan, <bl>zugleich/</bl> simul, <bl>bes-</bl> <bl>onders/</bl> seorsum, <bl>viel mehr/</bl> multo magis, <bl>es sey so/</bl> sit ita, <bl>weniger/</bl> minus, <bl>gleich wie/</bl> velut, <bl>ohn gefehr/</bl> forte, <bl>allzuviel/</bl> [?] nimiū, <bl>sehr: offentlich/</bl> [?] per litteras, <bl>mund-</bl> <bl>lich/</bl> coram, <bl>sehr/</bl> valde <bl>schier/</bl> fere, <bl>weh/</bl> vae.
units.tr: An adverb is an indeclinable word which, when added to some other word, expresses its circumstance in a single word. Examples: <bl>here</bl> (here), <bl>hither</bl> (hither), <bl>from hence</bl> (hence), <bl>today</bl> (today), <bl>once</bl> (once), <bl>yes</bl> (so), <bl>truly</bl> (truly), <bl>no</bl> (not), <bl>behold</bl> (behold), <bl>would to God</bl> (would that), <bl>I beg you, my dear</bl> (I beg), <bl>why?</bl> (why?), <bl>hey there</bl> (hey), <bl>perhaps</bl> (perhaps), <bl>together</bl> (together), <bl>separately</bl> (apart), <bl>much more</bl> (much more), <bl>so be it</bl> (let it be so), <bl>less</bl> (less), <bl>just as</bl> (just as), <bl>by chance</bl> (by chance), <bl>too much</bl> ([?] too much), <bl>very publicly</bl> ([?] by letter), <bl>orally</bl> (in person), <bl>very</bl> (very), <bl>nearly</bl> (almost), <bl>woe</bl> (woe).

units.la: DE CONIUNCTIONE.
units.tr: DE CONIUNCTIONE.

units.la: Quid est Coniunctio?
units.tr: What is a Conjunction?

units.la: Coniunctio est vox sine numero, quae superiori sententiae aut parti subinde aliam annectit: ut, <bl>und/</bl> &, <bl>auch/</bl> quoq;, <bl>darzu/</bl> etiam, <bl>wiewol/</bl> etsi, <bl>ob-</bl> <bl>wol/</bl> quanquam, <bl>obschon/</bl> quamvis, <bl>entweder/</bl> aut, <bl>oder/</bl> aut, <bl>dann/</bl> quàm, <bl>denn/</bl> nam, <bl>weil/</bl> cùm, <bl>sinemal/</bl> [?] siquidè, <bl>derhalben/</bl> ergo, <bl>derwegē/</bl> quapropter.
units.tr: A conjunction is an indeclinable word which subsequently attaches another clause or part to the preceding sentence. For example: and (und/&), also (auch/quoque), moreover (darzu/etiam), although (wiewol/etsi), although (obwol/quanquam), although (obschon/quamvis), either (entweder/aut), or (oder/aut), than (dann/quam), for (denn/nam), since (weil/cum), since (sintemal/siquidem), therefore (derhalben/ergo), wherefore (derwegen/quapropter).

units.la: DE SYNTAXI.
units.tr: ON SYNTAX.

units.la: Quid est Syntaxis?
units.tr: What is Syntax?

units.la: Syntaxis est secunda pars Grammaticae, in qua de vocum structura agitur.
units.tr: Syntax is the second part of grammar, which deals with the construction of words.

units.la: Quae est prima regula de vocibus con- struendis?
units.tr: What is the first rule for construing words?

units.la: Substantivum regit substantivum in Genitivo: ut, <bl>das wort des Herren bleibt ewiglich/</bl> verbum Domini manet in æternum, die forcht des <bl>Herren ist der</bl> <bl>weisheit anfang</bl>/timor Domini est sapientiæ initiu. Substantivum regit etiam infinitum cum Adverbio <bl>zu</bl>: ut, <bl>zeit zusagen</bl>/ tempus dicendi, <bl>fursatz recht zu</bl> <bl>thun</bl>/propositum recte faciendi.
units.tr: A noun governs a noun in the genitive: for example, "the word of the Lord endureth for ever" (verbum Domini manet in aeternum), and "the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom" (timor Domini est sapientiae initium). A noun also governs an infinitive with the adverb "zu": for example, "time to speak" (tempus dicendi), and "a purpose of doing right" (propositum recte faciendi).

units.la: Quæ est Secunda?
units.tr: What is the second?

units.la: Substantivum regit Substantivum in Genitivo cū adjectivo descriptionis: ut, <bl>ein weib schöner gestalt</bl>/ fœmina speciosi vultus. Interdum additur <bl>uon</bl>[?]: ut, <bl>ein knab von guter art</bl>/ puer bonæ indolis.
units.tr: A noun governs a noun in the genitive together with a descriptive adjective: for example, "a woman of beautiful appearance" (fœmina speciosi vultus). Sometimes "von" is added: "a boy of good disposition" (puer bonae indolis).

units.la: Quæ est Tertia?
units.tr: What is the third?

units.la: Adjectivum & Substantivum eodem numero, genere & casu cohærent: ut, <bl>ein frommer mann</bl>/ probus vir, <bl>ein fromme frawe</bl>/ proba fœmina.
units.tr: An adjective and a noun agree in number, gender and case: for example, "a pious man" (probus vir), "a pious woman" (proba fœmina).

units.la: Nomen <bl>Gott</bl>/ Deus, nomen proprium viri, mulieris, urbis, & nomen ejus rei, quæ terra nascitur,& quæ mensuratur ac ponderatur, Substantivum post Genitivum, & pronomina, absq; Articulis fere usur-pantur.
units.tr: The word "God" (Deus), a proper name of a man, a woman or a city, and the name of a thing that grows out of the earth or is measured and weighed, are used as nouns after a genitive and after pronouns, and are almost always used without articles.

units.la: Relativum cum antecedente Substantivo necesse est numero & genere consentire: ut, <bl>der bötte/</bl> <bl>welchen du zu mir gesandt hast/ ist auff der reise vmb-</bl> <bl>bracht</bl>/ Tabellarius, quem ad me misisti, est in itinere interfectus. Relativi loco est particula so vel <bl>da</bl> <bl>von</bl>: ut, <bl>alle/ so in Christum glauben/ werden nit</bl> <bl>zu schanden</bl>/omnes, qui in Christum credunt, non confunduntur. <bl>Ich sende dir das buch/ da von du mir</bl> <bl>schreibest</bl>/ mitto tibi librum, de quo mihi scribebas.
units.tr: A relative pronoun must agree in number and gender with its antecedent noun: for example, "the messenger whom you sent to me has been killed on the journey" (Tabellarius, quem ad me misisti, est in itinere interfectus). The particle "so" or "da von" serves in place of a relative: "all who believe in Christ shall not be put to shame" (omnes, qui in Christum credunt, non confunduntur); "I send you the book about which you wrote to me" (mitto tibi librum, de quo mihi scribebas).

units.la: Quæ est Quarta?
units.tr: What is the fourth?

units.la: Adjectivum partitivum regit Genitivum pluralem: ut, <bl>der bürger einer</bl>/civium unus.
units.tr: A partitive adjective governs the plural genitive: for example, "one of the citizens" (civium unus).

units.la: Quæ est Quinta?
units.tr: What is the fifth?

units.la: Adjectivum copiæ, inopiæ, vel memoriæ regit Genitivum: ut, <bl>sie sind vol süsses weins</bl>/ sunt pleni musti. <bl>Ich wil deiner eingedenck sein/</bl> ero tui memor.
units.tr: An adjective of plenty, want or remembrance governs the genitive: for example, "they are full of sweet wine" (sunt pleni musti); "I will be mindful of you" (ero tui memor).

units.la: Quae est Sexta?
units.tr: What is the sixth?

units.la: Comparativo subjicitur <bl>dann</bl> vel <bl>als</bl>: ut, <bl>gold ist</bl> <bl>besser dann/</bl> vel <bl>als/ silber/</bl> aurum est melius argento.
units.tr: A comparative is followed by "dann" or "als": for example, "gold is better than silver" (aurum est melius argento).

units.la: Quae est Septima?
units.tr: What is the seventh?

units.la: Superlativo subjicitur <bl>vnter/</bl> vel <bl>vber</bl> / vel <bl>in</bl>: ut, <bl>der beste vnter allen/</bl> optimus omnium. <bl>der fürtreff-</bl> <bl>lichste vber alle/</bl> praestantissimus omnium. <bl>Der reich-</bl> <bl>ste in der Statt/</bl> ditissimus in urbe.
units.tr: A superlative is followed by "unter", "vber" or "in": for example, "the best of all" (optimus omnium); "the most excellent above all" (praestantissimus omnium); "the richest in the city" (ditissimus in urbe).

units.la: Quae est Octava?
units.tr: What is the eighth?

units.la: Nominativus praecedit verbum finitum, simili numero & persona: ut, <bl>ich liebe/</bl> amo, <bl>du schreibest/</bl> tu scribis, <bl>er saget</bl>, ipse dicit.
units.tr: A nominative precedes a finite verb, agreeing in number and person: for example, "I love" (amo), "you write" (tu scribis), "he says" (ipse dicit).

units.la: Infinitum, aut tota oratio infinita, est Nominativi loco: ut, <bl>borgen macht sorgen</bl> / mutuam pecuniam sumere vel dare parit curas: Alteri enim incumbit necessitas solvendi & reddendi, alter timet, ne suum perdat.
units.tr: An infinitive, or a whole infinitive clause, stands in place of a nominative: for example, "borrowing brings worries" (mutuam pecuniam sumere vel dare parit curas). For the one lies under the necessity of paying and repaying, and the other fears lest he lose what is his.

units.la: Duo singularia postulat verbum plurale: ut, <bl>mein</bl> <bl>Vatter vnd Bruder sind kommen</bl> / pater meus & frater venerunt.
units.tr: Two singular nouns take a plural verb: for example, "my father and brother have come" (pater meus et frater venerunt).

units.la: Quae est Nona?
units.tr: What is the ninth?

units.la: Verbum Activum regit Accusativum: ut, <bl>Nun lo-</bl> <bl>be mein seel den Herren</bl> / lauda mea anima Dominum.
units.tr: A transitive (active) verb governs the accusative: for example, "Now let my soul praise the Lord" (lauda mea anima Dominum).

units.la: Quae est Decima?
units.tr: What is the tenth?

units.la: Verbum Passivum regit Ablativum cum Adverbio <bl>von</bl>: ut, <bl>Himmel vnnd Erde sind von Gott ge-</bl> <bl>schaffen/</bl> coelum & terra sunt à Deo creata.
units.tr: A passive verb governs the ablative with the preposition "von": for example, "heaven and earth were created by God" (coelum et terra sunt a Deo creata).

units.la: Quae est Undecima?
units.tr: What is the eleventh?

units.la: Verbum fruendi, abstinendi, egendi, privandi, admirandi, insimulandi, regit genitivum: ut, <bl>Ich ge-</bl> <bl>niesse des/</bl> fruor hac re. <bl>Enthalt dich des/</bl> abstine ab hoc. <bl>Der Herr bedarff ihr[?]/</bl> Dominus his opus habet. <bl>Einen seines guts berauben/</bl> aliquem suis bonis spoliare. Ich verwunder mich des/ miror hoc. Er wird eines Diebstals beschuldiget/ ipse furti insimulatur.
units.tr: Verbs of enjoying, abstaining, needing, depriving, wondering and accusing govern the genitive: for example, "I enjoy this thing" (fruor hac re); "abstain from this" (abstine ab hoc); "the Lord has need of them" (Dominus his opus habet); "to rob someone of his goods" (aliquem suis bonis spoliare); "I wonder at this" (miror hoc); "he is accused of theft" (ipse furti insimulatur).

units.la: Quæ est Duodecima?
units.tr: What is the twelfth?

units.la: Verbum utendi, memoriæ, oblivionis, regit Genitivum vel Accusativum: ut, Ich wil Deines raths/vel Deinen rath gebrauchen/ tuo consilio utar. Gedencke meiner/ memento mei. Ich wil das gedencken / ero hujus memor. Dicimus etiam, gedenck an mich/ recordare mei. Hastu des vel das vergessen? oblitus es hoc?
units.tr: Verbs of using, remembering and forgetting govern the genitive or the accusative: for example, "I will use your counsel" (tuo consilio utar), or "your counsel" in the accusative; "remember me" (memento mei); "I will remember this" (ero hujus memor); we also say "think of me" (recordare mei); "have you forgotten this?" (oblitus es hoc?).

units.la: Quæ est Decimatertia?
units.tr: What is the thirteenth?

units.la: Verbum attribuendi, adimendi, sequendi, regit Dativum: ut, Ich gebe dir / do tibi. Folge mir / sequere me.
units.tr: Verbs of giving, taking away and following govern the dative: for example, "I give to you" (do tibi); "follow me" (sequere me).

units.la: Quæ est Decimaquarta?
units.tr: What is the fourteenth?

units.la: Verbum significans voluntatem, sensum, aut facultatem, regit infinitum: ut, Ich wil gehen / volo ire. Ich höre[?] singen / audio cani. Ich sol unnd muß die warheit sagen / cogor veritatem dicere. Interdum additur zu: ut, Ich begere zuwissen/ cupio scire.
units.tr: A verb signifying will, perception or ability governs the infinitive: for example, "I want to go" (volo ire); "I hear someone sing" (audio cani); "I must and ought to tell the truth" (cogor veritatem dicere). Sometimes "zu" is added: "I desire to know" (cupio scire).

units.la: Quæ est Decimaquinta?
units.tr: What is the Fifteenth?

units.la: Verbum motus ad locum regit Infinitivum cum Adverbio zu: ut, Ich komme zusehen / venio visum, vel ad videndum. Ich komme ihn anzusprechen / venio ipsum compellatum, vel ad compellandum ipsum.
units.tr: A verb of motion to a place governs the infinitive with the adverb "zu": for example, "Ich komme zusehen" (I come to see), "Ich komme ihn anzusprechen" (I come to speak to him).

units.la: Quæ est Decimasexta?
units.tr: What is the Sixteenth?

units.la: Quædam ex impersonalibus, quibus es præponitur, regūt Dativum, quædam Accusativum, quædam casum habent nullū: ut, Es hat mir getrewmet / ego somniavi. Es widerfehret mir / contingit mihi. Es reuwet mich / pœnitet me. Es regnet / pluit. Es schneiet / ningit. Es hagelt / grandinat. Es donnert / tonat. Es blitzget / fulgurat.
units.tr: Some impersonal verbs, which take "es" in front of them, govern the dative, some the accusative, and some have no case: for example, "Es hat mir getrewmet" (I dreamed); "Es widerfehret mir" (it happens to me); "Es reuwet mich" (I regret it); "Es regnet" (it rains); "Es schneiet" (it snows); "Es hagelt" (it hails); "Es donnert" (it thunders); "Es blitzget" (it lightens).

units.la: Quæ est Decimaseptima?
units.tr: What is the Seventeenth?

units.la: <bl>Adverbia</bl>, <bl>diesseit</bl> / <bl>jenseit</bl> / <bl>laut</bl> / <bl>trafft</bl> / <bl>vermöge</bl> / <bl>halben</bl>/<bl>von wegen</bl>/ <bl>umb willen</bl> / regunt Genitivum: ut, <bl>diesseit des wassers</bl>/cis flumen. <bl>Jenseit des Jor-</bl> <bl>dans</bl>/trans Jordanem. <bl>Laut seiner wort</bl>/ut sonant verba ejus. <bl>Krafft seiner wort</bl> / vi verborum ipsius. <bl>Vermöge des befehls</bl> / juxta sententiam mandati. <bl>Deines Iohns halben</bl> / filij tui caussa. <bl>Meinet</bl> <bl>halben</bl>/mea caussa. <bl>Von jeinet[?] wegen</bl>/ipsius nomine. <bl>Umb meinet willen</bl>/propter me. Genitivi pronominum primitivorum definunt in t ob additas particulas. Interdum reperitur <bl>jenseit dem Jordan</bl>.
units.tr: The adverbs "diesseit", "jenseit", "laut", "trafft", "vermöge", "halben", "von wegen" and "umb willen" govern the genitive: for example, "diesseit des wassers" (on this side of the water); "jenseit des Jordans" (beyond the Jordan); "laut seiner wort" (according to his words); "krafft seiner wort" (by virtue of his words); "vermöge des befehls" (in accordance with the command); "deines Iohns halben" (for the sake of your son); "meinet halben" (for my sake); "von jeinet wegen" (on his account); "umb meinet willen" (for my sake). The genitives of the primitive pronouns end in "t" because of the particles added. Sometimes "jenseit dem Jordan" is also found.

units.la: Quæ est Decimaoctava?
units.tr: What is the Eighteenth?

units.la: <bl>Adverbia</bl>, <bl>durch</bl>/per: <bl>ohn</bl>/sine: <bl>umb</bl>/circum: <bl>wi-</bl> <bl>der</bl>/contra: <bl>gen</bl>/& <bl>auff zu</bl>/ versus vel ad, regunt Accusativum: <bl>auß</bl>/ex: <bl>bey</bl>/apud: <bl>mit</bl>/cum: <bl>nach</bl>/post: <bl>von</bl>/a: <bl>vor</bl>/coram: <bl>zu</bl>/ad, regunt Ablativum.
units.tr: The prepositions "durch" (through), "ohn" (without), "umb" (around), "wider" (against), "gen" and "auff zu" (towards) govern the accusative; "auß" (out of), "bey" (at), "mit" (with), "nach" (after), "von" (from), "vor" (before) and "zu" (to) govern the dative.

units.la: Quæ est Decimanona?
units.tr: What is the Nineteenth?

units.la: <bl>Adverbia</bl>, <bl>an</bl>/ad vel de: <bl>auff</bl>/ super: <bl>für</bl>/ pro: <bl>geg-</bl> <bl>en</bl>/contra: <bl>hinder</bl>/ post: <bl>in</bl> in: <bl>neben</bl>/ juxta: <bl>über</bl>/ supra: <bl>unter</bl> / subter: <bl>zwischen</bl> / inter, regunt cum Verbo motus Accusativum, cum Verbo quietis Ablativum.
units.tr: The prepositions "an" (at or to), "auff" (upon), "für" (before), "gegen" (against), "hinder" (behind), "in" (in), "neben" (beside), "über" (over), "unter" (under) and "zwischen" (between) govern the accusative with a verb of motion, and the dative with a verb of rest.

units.la: Quæ est Vicesima Regula?
units.tr: What is the Twentieth Rule?

units.la: Lecturus præcepta prolixiora, videat Teutonicam Grammaticam Johannis Claji Hirtzbergensis, Lipsiæ à Johanne Rhamba excusam. Qui autem insignes Teutonicas phrases in Grammatophylacijs usitas[?] scire cupit, is diligenter non solum Jurisconsultorum Germanicos libros, sed etiam Reverendissimi Domini Doctoris Martini Lutheri teutonica Biblia legat.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to read longer rules should consult the German Grammar of Johannes Clajus of Hirtzberg, printed at Leipzig by Johannes Rhamba. But whoever wishes to know the distinguished German idioms in use in the grammar schools should diligently read not only the German books of the lawyers, but also the German Bible of the Reverend Lord Doctor Martin Luther.

units.la: Welcher lesen wil, weitlauffiger gebotte / der besehe die Teutsche Sprachekunst Johannis Clajs Hirtzbergensis / zu Leipzig von Johanne Rhamba getruckt. Wer aber herrliche Teutsche weisen zure-den / auff Canzelen gebräuchlich / zu wissen begeret / der muß fleissig nicht allein der Rechtsgelerten Teutsche bücher / sondern auch des Ehr-würdigen Herrn Doc. Martini Luthers Biblien lesen.
units.tr: Whoever wishes to read longer rules should consult the German Grammar of Johannes Clajus of Hirtzberg, printed at Leipzig by Johannes Rhamba. But whoever wishes to know the splendid German turns of phrase used in the pulpit should diligently read not only the German books of the lawyers, but also the Bible of the Reverend Lord Doctor Martin Luther.

units.la: GRAMMATICA LATINA.
units.tr: LATIN GRAMMAR.

units.la: Quid est Grammatica Latina?
units.tr: What is Latin grammar?

units.la: GRAMMATICA Latina est ars pure loquendi Latinè. <bl>Die Lateinische</bl> <bl>Sprachkunst ist eine küst[?] seuberlich Lateinisch zu sprächen.</bl>
units.tr: Latin grammar is the art of speaking Latin correctly. (The German gloss: the art of grammar teaches one to speak Latin cleanly and properly.)

units.la: Quot sunt ejus partes?
units.tr: How many parts does it have?

units.la: Duæ: Etymologia & Syntaxis Zwey: <bl>Die stimmer-klärung vnd die stumsetzung[?].</bl>
units.tr: Two: Etymology and Syntax. (The German gloss: the explanation of words and the putting together of sentences.)

units.la: Quid est Etymologia?
units.tr: What is etymology?

units.la: Etymologia est prima pars Grammaticæ, in qua de singularum vocū proprietate agitur. <bl>Die stimmer-</bl> <bl>klärung ist das erste theil der Sprachekunst/ in dem</bl> <bl>von d' einzigen stimmen eigenschafft gehandlet wird.</bl>
units.tr: Etymology is the first part of grammar, in which the properties of individual words are treated. (The German gloss: the explanation of words is the first part of grammar, in which the properties of single words are treated.)

units.la: Quid est Vox?
units.tr: What is a word?

units.la: Vox est nota, qua unaquæq; res vocatur. <bl>Die stim</bl> <bl>ist ein zeichen/ damit ein jedes ding genennet wird.</bl>
units.tr: A word is a sign by which each thing is named. (The German gloss: a word is a sign by which every thing is named.)

units.la: Unde fit Vox?
units.tr: How is a word formed?

units.la: E litera & syllaba. <bl>Auß dē buchstab vnd der sylben.</bl>
units.tr: From letters and syllables. (The German gloss: from letters and syllables.)

units.la: Quid est Litera?
units.tr: What is a letter?

units.la: Litera est individui soni comprehensio. <bl>Der buchstab</bl> <bl>ist eines vnzertheiligen gelauts begreiffung.</bl>
units.tr: A letter is the grasp of a single, indivisible sound. (The German gloss: a letter is the grasping of an undivided sound.)

units.la: Quot sunt literæ apud Latinos?
units.tr: How many letters are there in Latin?

units.la: Quatuor & viginti, sequentibus figuris scriptæ: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff, Gg, Hh, Ii, Ll, Mm, Nn, Oo, Pp, Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt, Uu, Xx, Yy, Zz, Jod, Vau.
units.tr: Twenty-four, written with the following characters: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff, Gg, Hh, Ii, Ll, Mm, Nn, Oo, Pp, Qq, Rr, Ss, Tt, Uu, Xx, Yy, Zz, J, V.

units.la: Quotuplex est Litera?
units.tr: How many kinds of letter are there?

units.la: Duplex: Vocalis aut Consona. <bl>Zwenfaltig/ der</bl> <bl>lautende oder mitlautende.</bl>
units.tr: Two: vowels or consonants. (The German gloss: twofold, the sounding and the co-sounding letters.)

units.la: Quid est Vocalis?
units.tr: What is a vowel?

units.la: Vocalis est litera, quæ per se syllabam potest efficere: ut,a,e,i,o,u,y.
units.tr: A vowel is a letter that can form a syllable by itself, as a, e, i, o, u, y.

units.la: Quid est Consona?
units.tr: What is a consonant?

units.la: Consona est litera, quæ tantùm cum vocali syllabâ potest efficere,ut literæ omnes,præter sex vocales.
units.tr: A consonant is a letter that can form a syllable only together with a vowel, as all the letters except the six vowels.

units.la: Quomodo dividitur Consona?
units.tr: How is a consonant divided?

units.la: In mutam, liquidam, & duplicem. Octo consonæ sunt mutæ: ut,b,c,d,f,g,p,q,t. Quatuor sunt liquidæ: ut,l,m,n,r. Tres sunt duplices: ut,x,z, & jod, quoties inter duas vocales ponitur: ut,pejor,major.
units.tr: Into mute, liquid and double. Eight consonants are mute: b, c, d, f, g, p, q, t. Four are liquid: l, m, n, r. Three are double: x, z, and j, whenever it is placed between two vowels, as in pejor and major.

units.la: Observatio.
units.tr: Observation.

units.la: Etsi scribimus Cneus & Cajus; tamen Gneus & Gajus secundùm Grammaticos pronuntiamus.
units.tr: Although we write Cneus and Cajus, nevertheless, according to the grammarians, we pronounce them Gneus and Gajus.

units.la: Quid est Syllaba?
units.tr: What is a syllable?

units.la: Syllaba est unius litera, aut multarum comprehensio, uno eodemq; spiritu ac tono proferenda: ut,a,e, i,o,u,y, æ,œ,au,eu,ei,ab,ars,mars,stans,stirps. Duarum vocalium in unam syllabam comprehensus sonus Diphthongus appellatur. Veteres Diphthogum ei, ufurparunt in pluralibus masculinis & fœmininis Accusativis nominum, quæ ium habent in genitivo plurali: ut,acreis,omneis,salubreis,parteis,arteis.
units.tr: A syllable is a single letter or a combination of several letters, to be uttered with one breath and one tone, as a, e, i, o, u, y, ae, oe, au, eu, ei, ab, ars, mars, stans, stirps. A sound formed by two vowels combined in one syllable is called a diphthong. The old writers used the diphthong ei in the plural masculine and feminine accusatives of nouns that have ium in the genitive plural, as acreis, omneis, salubreis, parteis, arteis.

units.la: Hactenus de litera & syllaba dictum est: sequuntur affectiones omnibus vocibus communes, videlicet Species & Figura.
units.tr: So much has been said about letters and syllables; there follow the attributes common to all words, namely species and figure.

units.la: Quid est Species Vocis?
units.tr: What is the species of a word?

units.la: Species vocis est,qua disquiritur,utrùm vox sit Primitiva,an Derivativa. Primitiva est, quæ à nulla alia descendit: ut,Equus,ein pferd/Aper,ein wilde schwein. Derivativa est,quæ ab alia voce originem trahit: ut, Equuleus, ein Füllen/Aprugnus, vo wilden schwein.
units.tr: The species of a word is that by which it is examined whether the word is primitive or derivative. A primitive word is one that descends from no other, as equus, a horse; aper, a wild boar. A derivative word is one that takes its origin from another word, as equuleus, a foal; aprugnus, of a wild boar.

units.la: Quid est Figura Vocis?
units.tr: What is the figure of a word?

units.la: Figura vocis est qua disquiritur utrū vox simplex, an composita sit. Simplex: ut Doctus, <bl>gelehrt/</bl>amo, <bl>ich liebe</bl>. Composita: ut, perdoctus, <bl>wolgelehrt/</bl> redamo, <bl>ich liebe widerumb</bl>.
units.tr: The figure of a word is that by which it is examined whether the word is simple or compound. Simple: as doctus, learned; amo, I love. Compound: as perdoctus, very learned; redamo, I love in return.

units.la: Quotuplex est Vox?
units.tr: How many kinds of word are there?

units.la: Duplex: Numeri aut sine Numero.
units.tr: Two: those with number and those without number.

units.la: Quid est vox Numeri?
units.tr: What is a word of number?

units.la: Vox numeri est, quæ numerum adsignificat. <bl>Die</bl> <bl>stim der zal ist/ so einen zaal neben andeutet.</bl> Numerus est duplex: Singularis, aut Pluralis. Singularis numerus est, quo res singularis exprimi potest: ut, Doctus, Legit. Pluralis, quo res plures exprimi possunt: ut, Docti, Legunt.
units.tr: A word of number is one that also signifies a number. (The German gloss: the word of number is one that also indicates a number.) Number is twofold: singular or plural. The singular number is that by which a single thing can be expressed, as doctus, learned; legit, he reads. The plural number is that by which several things can be expressed, as docti, learned (plural); legunt, they read.

units.la: Quot sunt voces Numeri?
units.tr: How many words of number are there?

units.la: Duæ: Nomen & Verbum, <bl>zwo: der name und das wort.</bl>
units.tr: Two: the noun and the verb. (The German gloss: two: the noun and the verb.)

units.la: DE NOMINE.
units.tr: ON THE NOUN.

units.la: Quid est Nomen?
units.tr: What is a noun?

units.la: Nomen est vox numeri cum genere, casu & declinatione. <bl>Der name ist ein stim der zal mit dem</bl> <bl>geschlechte/ falle und der biegung.</bl>
units.tr: A noun is a word that carries number, with gender, case and declension. (German: The name is a word that carries number, with gender, case and inflection.)

units.la: Quotuplex est Nomen?
units.tr: How many kinds of noun are there?

units.la: Duplex: Substantivum aut Adjectivum. <bl>zweyfältig: der bestehende oder zugewoertene.</bl>
units.tr: Two: the substantive or the adjective. (German: Twofold: the standing-alone name or the added name.)

units.la: Quid est Substantivum Nomen?
units.tr: What is a substantive noun?

units.la: Cujus significatio per se absq; altero addito intelligitur. <bl>welchers bedeutung ohn anderem zugethan</bl> <bl>verstanden wirdt:</bl> ut Homo, <bl>ein Mensch/</bl> Equus, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>Pferd.</bl> Substantivum est aut Appellativum, aut Proprium. Appellativum, quod multis commune est, <bl>der</bl> <bl>gemeine name ist/ welcher vielen gemein ist:</bl> ut, urbs, <bl>ein Statt</bl> / fluvius, <bl>ein fliessend wasser</bl>. Proprium, quod uni rei soli convenit, <bl>der eigen name ist /</bl> <bl>welcher einem dinge allein sich zu fuget</bl>: ut, Roma, <bl>die</bl> <bl>Statt Rom</bl>, Rhenus, <bl>der Rhein</bl>. Propriorum nominum quatuor sunt species: praenomen, quod honoris aut differentiae causa praeponitur: Nomen quod cuiq; est proprium: Cognomen, quod quis ex familia & cognatione habet: Agnomen, quod ab eventu alicui imponitur. Proprium autem nomen semper majore litera notatur: ut Cicero, Maro, Horatius.
units.tr: A substantive is one whose meaning is understood by itself, without any other word added: for example, man (Homo), horse (Equus). A substantive is either common (appellative) or proper. A common noun is one that belongs to many things: for example, city (urbs), river (fluvius). A proper noun is one that belongs to one thing alone: for example, Rome (Roma), the Rhine (Rhenus). There are four kinds of proper noun: the praenomen, which is placed before the name for honour or to distinguish; the nomen, which is each person's own; the cognomen, which a person has from family and kinship; and the agnomen, which is given to someone from an event. A proper noun is always marked with a capital letter: for example, Cicero, Maro, Horace.

units.la: Quid est Adjectivum Nomen?
units.tr: What is an adjective?

units.la: Cujus significatio absque altero aliquo intelligi non potest, <bl>welcheres bedeutung ohn einem anderen</bl> <bl>nicht mag verstanden werden</bl>: ut albus, <bl>weiß</bl> / niger, <bl>schwarz</bl>: Nihil enim certi percipias, nisi substantivum, paries, capillus, vel simile intelligatur, <bl>dann</bl> <bl>du kanst nicht gewisses vernemmen / wo nicht</bl> <bl>ein bestehender namme / die wand / das haupthaar / oder</bl> <bl>ein gleicher verstanden wird</bl>. Estq; triplex: Nominale, ut bonus: participiale, ut amatus: pronominale, ut meus.
units.tr: An adjective is one whose meaning cannot be understood without some other word: for example, white (albus), black (niger). For you can grasp nothing certain unless a substantive is understood, such as wall (paries), hair (capillus), or something similar; (German: for you cannot know anything definite unless an existing name is understood, the wall, the hair, or something like that). There are three kinds: the nominal, as good (bonus); the participial, as loved (amatus); and the pronominal, as mine (meus).

units.la: Quid accidit nonnullis Adjectivis nominibus?
units.tr: What happens to some adjectives?

units.la: Comparatio, cujus gradus vulgò tres dicuntur. Positivus, Comparativus, & Superlativus. Positivus est prima vox Adjectivi: ut Doctus. Comparativus est, qui per positivum cum Magis explicatur: ut, Doctior, id est, magis Doctus. Superlativus est, qui per positivum cum valde vel maximè explicatur: ut, Doctissimꝰ, id est, valdè vel maximè Doctus, <bl>sehr gelehrt</bl>.
units.tr: Comparison, whose degrees are commonly said to be three: the positive, the comparative and the superlative. The positive is the basic form of the adjective, as learned (doctus). The comparative is that which is explained by the positive with "more": as more learned (doctior), that is, more learned. The superlative is that which is explained by the positive with "very" or "most": as most learned (doctissimus), that is, very or most learned, very learned.

units.la: Unde Comparativus & Superlativus formantur?
units.tr: How are the comparative and superlative formed?

units.la: Si positivus fuerit fecundæ declinationis, à Genitivo: si tertiæ vel imparisyllabæ declinationis à Dativo. Comparativus autem, addito or, pro communi genere, & us, pro neutro: ut, à Docti, <bl>gelehrt</bl> / Doctior, Doctius, à tenui, <bl>dünn</bl> / tenuior, tenuius, à felici, <bl>glückselig</bl> / felicior, felicius. Superlativus, addito issimus, pro masculino, issima pro foemino, issimum pro neutro: ut, doctissimus, doctissima, doctissimum. Si tamen positivus desinat in er, superlativus masculinus fit, addito rimus, foemininus addito rima, neuter rimum: ut niger, <bl>schwarz</bl> / nigerrimus, nigerrima, nigerrimum. Quidam positivi formant Superlativos in limus: ut facilis, <bl>leicht</bl> / facilimus. Agilis, <bl>schnel und fertig</bl> / agilimus. Gracilis, <bl>dünn und</bl> <bl>mager</bl> / gracilimus. Humilis, <bl>niederträchtig und de-</bl> <bl>mütig</bl> / humilimus. Similis, <bl>gleich</bl> / similimus.
units.tr: If the positive belongs to the second declension, from the genitive; if to the third, or to the imparisyllabic declension, from the dative. The comparative adds -or for the common gender and -us for the neuter: thus from doctus, learned, comes doctior, doctius; from tenuis, thin, tenuior, tenuius; from felix, happy, felicior, felicius. The superlative adds -issimus for the masculine, -issima for the feminine, -issimum for the neuter: thus doctissimus, doctissima, doctissimum. If however the positive ends in -er, the masculine superlative is formed by adding -rimus, the feminine -rima, the neuter -rimum: thus niger, black, nigerrimus, nigerrima, nigerrimum. Some positives form their superlatives in -limus: thus facilis, easy, facilimus; agilis, quick and nimble, agilimus; gracilis, thin and lean, gracilimus; humilis, lowly and humble, humilimus; similis, like, similimus.

units.la: Quae comparantur irregulariter?
units.tr: Which words are compared irregularly?

units.la: <bl>Bonus, gut</bl> / melior, <bl>besser</bl> / optimus, <bl>der beste</bl>. <bl>Malus, böß</bl> / pejor, <bl>erger</bl> / pessimus, <bl>der ergste</bl>. <bl>Magnus, groß</bl> / major, <bl>größer</bl> / maximus, <bl>der größte</bl>. <bl>Parvus, klein</bl> / minor, <bl>kleiner</bl> / minimus, <bl>der</bl> <bl>kleinste</bl>. Et parvissimus, Lucretio. Multus, | plurimus. Multa, | plurima. Multum, <bl>viel</bl> / plus, <bl>mehr</bl> / plurimum, <bl>das meiste</bl>. Vetus, <bl>alt</bl> / veterior, <bl>elter</bl> / veterrimus, <bl>der elteste</bl>. Sacer, <bl>heilig</bl> / magis sacer, sacerrimus. Frugi, <bl>hänßlich</bl> / frugalior, frugalissimus. Pius, <bl>Gottsfürchtig</bl> / magis pius, maxime pius.
units.tr: Bonus, good; melior, better; optimus, best. Malus, bad; pejor, worse; pessimus, worst. Magnus, great; major, greater; maximus, greatest. Parvus, small; minor, smaller; minimus, smallest; and parvissimus, in Lucretius. Multus, much (masc.), plurimus; multa, plurima; multum, much (neut.), plus, more, plurimum, most. Vetus, old; veterior, older; veterrimus, oldest. Sacer, holy; magis sacer, sacerrimus. Frugi, thrifty; frugalior, frugalissimus. Pius, godly; magis pius, maxime pius.

units.la: Piissimus apud Diomedem, Senecam & Cuttium reperitur: Et apud quosdam alios pientissimus.
units.tr: Piissimus is found in Diomedes, Seneca and Curtius; and in some others, pientissimus.

units.la: Reliqua omnia, vocalem ante us vel is habentia per magis & maxime describuntur: praeter tenuis, tenuior, & strenuus, strenuior. Dexter, <bl>recht</bl> / <bl>oder glückhafftig</bl> / dexterior, dextimus. Nequam, <bl>schalckhafft</bl> / nequior, nequissimus. Maturus, <bl>zeitig oder reiffe</bl> / maturior, maturrimus & maturissimus.
units.tr: All the remaining words that have a vowel before -us or -is are compared with magis and maxime, except tenuis, tenuior, and strenuus, strenuior. Dexter, right or fortunate; dexterior, dextimus. Nequam, roguish; nequior, nequissimus. Maturus, timely or ripe; maturior, maturrimus and maturissimus.

units.la: Maledicus, <bl>lasterzedig/</bl> maledicentior, maledicentissimus.
units.tr: Maledicus, slanderous; maledicentior, maledicentissimus.

units.la: Magniloquus, <bl>großredig/</bl> magniloquentior, magniloquentissimus.
units.tr: Magniloquus, big-talking; magniloquentior, magniloquentissimus.

units.la: Magnificus, <bl>großthätig/</bl> magnificentior, magnificentissimus. (tissimus.
units.tr: Magnificus, magnificent in deeds; magnificentior, magnificentissimus.

units.la: Benevolus, <bl>gutwillig/</bl> benevolentior, benevolentissimus.
units.tr: Benevolus, well-disposed; benevolentior, benevolentissimus.

units.la: Sinister, <bl>linck oder unglücckhafftig/</bl> finisterior, finistimus. Positivo carent: (ftimus.
units.tr: Sinister, left, or unlucky; sinisterior, sinistimus. They lack the positive.

units.la: Anterior, <bl>vorder.</bl> Citerior, <bl>näher zu uns/</bl> citimus. Exterior, <bl>auffer/</bl> extimus & extremus. Inferior, <bl>und/</bl> infimus. Interior <bl>inner/</bl> intimus. Posterior, <bl>nachfolgend/</bl> postremus. Propior, <bl>näher/</bl> proximus, unde proximior. Superior, <bl>ober/</bl> supremus, & summus. Ulterior, <bl>ferner/</bl> ultimus, & novissimus, <bl>der letst.</bl> Prior, <bl>vorderer/</bl> primus, <bl>der erste.</bl> Ocyor, <bl>schnäller/</bl> ocyssimus. Potior, <bl>besser oder lieber/</bl> potissimus. Habitior, <bl>feisster oder besser bey leibe.</bl> Deterior, <bl>böser.</bl>
units.tr: Anterior, front. Citerior, nearer to us; citimus. Exterior, outer; extimus and extremus. Inferior, lower; infimus. Interior, inner; intimus. Posterior, following; postremus. Propior, nearer; proximus, whence proximior. Superior, upper; supremus and summus. Ulterior, farther; ultimus and novissimus, the last. Prior, former; primus, the first. Ocyor, swifter; ocyssimus. Potior, better or preferable; potissimus. Habitior, fatter, or better in body. Deterior, worse.

units.la: Superlativo carent:
units.tr: They lack the superlative:

units.la: Adolescens, <bl>jung/</bl> adolescentior. Ingens, <bl>groß/</bl> ingentior. Infinitus, <bl>unendtlich/</bl> infinitior. Satur, <bl>geset-</bl> <bl>tiget/</bl> saturior. Senex, <bl>alt/</bl> senior. Juvenis, <bl>jung/</bl> junior. Dives, <bl>reich/</bl> divitior & ditior.
units.tr: Adolescent, young: more adolescent. Huge, great: huger. Infinite, unending: more infinite. Sated, satisfied: more sated. Old, aged: older. Young, juvenile: younger. Rich: richer, and (in the shorter form) ditior.

units.la: Quid est Genus?
units.tr: What is Gender?

units.la: Genus est differentia Nominis secundum sexum.
units.tr: Gender is the difference of a noun according to sex.

units.la: Quot sunt Genera?
units.tr: How many genders are there?

units.la: Quinque: Masculinum, Foemininum, Neutrum, Commune & Omne.
units.tr: Five: masculine, feminine, neuter, common, and of all genders.

units.la: Quid est Masculinum Genus?
units.tr: What is the masculine gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus, hic.
units.tr: Its mark is the article hic.

units.la: • Quæ nomina sunt masculini Generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the masculine gender?

units.la: Quæ viro, aut rebus viri specie conceptis cōgruunt, <bl>die einem manne / oder dingen unter mannes gestalt</bl> <bl>verstandē / sich zufügen:</bl> ut, Jupiter, <bl>der oberste</bl> <bl>Heidnische Gott.</bl> Michael, <bl>der Engel also genandt.</bl> Marcus,ein <bl>eigener namme.</bl> Consul,ein <bl>Burgermeister.</bl> Catilina, ein <bl>Verhåter zu Rom.</bl> Pistor, ein <bl>frucht-</bl> <bl>stosser oder brotbecke[?].</bl> Boreas,der <bl>wind von mitter-</bl> <bl>nacht.</bl> Aprilis,der <bl>Monat Aprill.</bl> Visurgis,die <bl>weser.</bl> Vel, Deorum, Angelorum, Virorum, officiorum Virilium, Mensium, Ventorü, & fluviorum nomina sunt generis masculini. Silicernium, ein <bl>steinaltermann/</bl> & Mancipium, ein <bl>leibeigner /</bl> neutrius generis sunt, Styx,stygis, ein <bl>Hellischer fluß / wie die Poeten</bl> <bl>dichten/</bl> & Lethe, Lethes, ein <bl>Hellischer fluß/ welcher aller</bl> <bl>dinge vergessenheit bringet dem so daraus trinc-</bl> <bl>ket /</bl> sunt foeminini generis. Nar, ein <bl>fluß /</bl> masculini & neutrius generis est. Albula pota figuratè dicitur.
units.tr: Those which belong to a man, or to things conceived under the form of a man: e.g. Jupiter, the chief pagan god; Michael, the angel so named; Marcus, a proper name; consul, a burgomaster; Catiline, a traitor at Rome; pistor, a grain-pounder or baker; Boreas, the north wind; Aprilis, the month of April; Visurgis, the river Weser. Also the names of gods, angels, men, men's offices, months, winds and rivers are of masculine gender. Silicernium, a stone-old man, and mancipium, a slave, are neuter. Styx, Stygis, a hellish river as the poets describe it, and Lethe, Lethes, a hellish river which brings forgetfulness of all things to whoever drinks from it, are feminine. Nar, a river, is masculine and neuter. Albula is used figuratively when it is drunk.

units.la: Quid est Fœminimum Genus?
units.tr: What is the feminine gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus,Hæc.
units.tr: Its mark is the article hæc.

units.la: Quæ nomina sunt Fœminini Generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the feminine gender?

units.la: Quæ mulieri, aut rebus mulieris specie conceptis cōgruunt: ut, Pallas, <bl>die Göttin der künste vñ weiß-</bl> <bl>heit/</bl> aus <bl>des</bl> Jovis <bl>haupt geboren.</bl> Tullia, ein <bl>tochter</bl> Ciceronis. Glycerium, ein <bl>hulerin beim</bl> Terentio. Obstetrix, ein <bl>Hebamme.</bl> Aegyptus, <bl>Egyptenland.</bl> Peloponesus,ein <bl>landtschafft</bl> Græcię. Samus,ein <bl>Jnsel im Meer</bl> Ægeo. Roma, <bl>die statt</bl> Rom Carthago, ein <bl>Hauptstatt in</bl> Aphrica. Cerafus, ein <bl>Kirschbaum.</bl> Pyrus,ein <bl>Birnbaum.</bl> Buxus, ein <bl>Buchssbaum.</bl> Vel, Dearum,mulierum, muliebriū,officiorum,Regionū Infularū,Urbium,& arborū nomina sunt generis fœminini. Excipe,hoc scortū : hoc prostibulū, ein <bl>Hůr.</bl> Deinde urbiū nomina in*um[?] vel ur vel ir quæ neutra sunt,& pluralia in i,quæ masculina sunt:ut,hoc Marpurgū,<bl>Marpurg in Hessen.</bl> Tybur, ein <bl>statt Italie/</bl> <bl>nit weit von Rom.</bl> Gadir, ein <bl>statt in Hispanien.</bl> Hi Gabij,ein <bl>statt welschlādes.</bl> Philippi,ein <bl>statt</bl> Macedoniæ. Hoc Argos,ein <bl>statt in Griechenland.</bl> Hi Argi. Hic Sulmo,Ovidij patria. Hæc arborum nomina: Oleaster, ein wilder Ölbaum / rubus, ein busch oder brombeerstaud/dumus,ein Dornheck/styrax,ein baum von welchem wolriechig gummi fleuft / masculina sunt, Acer,ein ahornbaum/ robur, ein harteeych/ suber, pantoffelholz / siler, ein baum von weiden geschlecht/neutra sunt.
units.tr: Those which belong to a woman, or to things conceived under the form of a woman: e.g. Pallas, the goddess of the arts and wisdom, born from the head of Jupiter; Tullia, a daughter of Cicero; Glycerium, a courtesan in Terence; obstetrix, a midwife; Aegyptus, Egypt; Peloponnesus, a region of Greece; Samus, an island in the Aegean Sea; Roma, the city of Rome; Carthago, a chief city in Africa; cerasus, a cherry tree; pyrus, a pear tree; buxus, a box tree. Also the names of goddesses, women, women's offices, regions, islands, cities and trees are of feminine gender. Make an exception for hoc scortum and hoc prostibulum, a whore. Next, the names of cities ending in -um, -ur or -ir are neuter, and plurals in -i are masculine: e.g. hoc Marpurgum, Marburg in Hesse; Tibur, a city of Italy not far from Rome; Gadir, a city in Spain; hi Gabii, a city of Latium; Philippi, a city of Macedonia; hoc Argos, a city in Greece, hi Argi; hic Sulmo, Ovid's homeland. These are the names of trees: oleaster, a wild olive; rubus, a bush or bramble; dumus, a thorn hedge; styrax, a tree from which fragrant gum flows, are masculine. Acer, a maple tree; robur, hard oak; suber, cork-wood; siler, a tree of the willow family, are neuter.

units.la: Quid est Neutrum Genus?
units.tr: What is the neuter gender?

units.la: Cujus nota est articulus hoc.
units.tr: Its mark is the article hoc.

units.la: Quæ nomina sunt neutrius generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the neuter gender?

units.la: Nomina literarum, syllabarum, & quæ materialiter, id est, pro fe, non pro significatu suo sumuntur: ut. A magnum. Stirps est longum. Cæsar est disyllabum. In Bus correptam figuratè à Donato dicitur.
units.tr: The names of letters and syllables, and words taken materially, that is, for their form and not for their meaning: e.g. A magnum; stirps est longum; Cæsar est disyllabum. Donatus calls In with the short bus a figurative use.

units.la: Quid est commune Genus?
units.tr: What is the common gender?

units.la: Cujus notæ sunt articuli hic & hæc.
units.tr: Its marks are the articles hic and hæc.

units.la: Quæ nomina sunt Communis Generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of the common gender?

units.la: Nomina, quæ apud bonos authores nunc in masculino, nunc in fœminino genere usurpata inveniutur: ut, hic & hæc Advena,ein fremdbling/Verna,der oder die leibeigen in unserm hauß geboren ist. Atomus, unzertheilig/ oder staub im Sonnen glantz. Alvus, der bauchbarm. Adeps, allerley feiste. Horum communium quædam Vulgo appellantur Dubia.
units.tr: Nouns which in good authors are found used sometimes in the masculine and sometimes in the feminine gender: e.g. hic and hæc advena, a stranger; verna, a man or woman slave born in our household; atomus, indivisible, or a mote of dust in the sunlight; alvus, the belly and bowels; adeps, all kinds of fat. Some of these common nouns are commonly called doubtful.

units.la: Quid est Omne Genus?
units.tr: What is the gender of all genders?

units.la: Cujus notæ sunt articuli hic,hæc & hoc.
units.tr: Its marks are the articles hic, hæc and hoc.

units.la: Quæ Nomina sunt omnis generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of all genders?

units.la: Adjectiva unius vocis omnis generis sunt: ut, hic, hæc,hoc Amans,liebend. Audies,hörend/Alcs,schnel/ geflügelt. Bicorpor,zweyleibig. Bicolor, von zweyen farben. Bipes,zweyfüßig. Cicur,zam/sanfftte. Deses, saul/der nichts thut. Degener,der auß dem geschlecht schlägt. Dives,reich. Docens,lehrend. Ego,ich Ferens, tragend. Fœlix, glückselig. Hebes, stumpff Legens, lesend. Par,gleich. Pauper,arm. Perpes,ewig Præpes,
units.tr: Adjectives with one form for all three genders: e.g. hic, hæc, hoc amans, loving; audiens, hearing; alacer, swift, winged; bicorpor, two-bodied; bicolor, of two colours; bipes, two-footed; cicur, tame, gentle; deses, idle, one who does nothing; degener, one who has degenerated from his stock; dives, rich; docens, teaching; ego, I; ferens, bearing; felix, happy; hebes, blunt; legens, reading; par, equal; pauper, poor; perpes, everlasting; præpes,

units.la: <bl>schnel</bl>. Sospes, <bl>gesund</bl>. Sui, <bl>seiner</bl>. Superstes, <bl>nechwbe-</bl> <bl>rig</bl> / <bl>oder bey läben</bl>. Teres, <bl>rund</bl> in <bl>die lenge</bl>. Tu, <bl>du</bl>. Vetus, <bl>alt</bl>. Huc refer indeclinabilia, Ejusmodi, <bl>solch</bl>. Hujusmodi, <bl>solcherlei</bl>. Frugi, <bl>ein nützlicher</bl>. Nauci, <bl>verächtlich</bl>. Nihili, <bl>ein nichtiger</bl>. Nequam, <bl>schalckhafft</bl>. Quatuor, <bl>vier</bl>. Quinque, <bl>fünff</bl>. Sex, <bl>sechs</bl>. Septem, <bl>sieben</bl>. Octo, <bl>acht</bl>. Novem, <bl>neun</bl>. Decem, <bl>zehen</bl>. Undecim, <bl>eylff</bl>. Duodecim, <bl>zwölff</bl>. Tredecim, <bl>dreyzehen</bl>. Quatuordecim, <bl>vierzehen</bl>. Quindecim, <bl>fünffzehen</bl>. Sedecim, <bl>sechzehen</bl>. Septendecim, <bl>siebenzehen</bl>. Octodecim vel duodeviginti, <bl>achtzehen</bl>. Novendecim vel undeviginti, <bl>neunzehen</bl>. Viginti, <bl>zwentzig</bl>. Triginta, <bl>dreis-</bl> <bl>sig</bl>. Quadraginta, <bl>vierzig</bl>. Quinquaginta, <bl>fünfftzig</bl>. Sexaginta, <bl>sechzig</bl>. Septuaginta, <bl>siebentzig</bl>. Octoginta, <bl>achtzig</bl>. Nonaginta, <bl>neuntzig</bl>. Centum, <bl>hundert</bl>. Mille, <bl>tausent</bl>. Tot, <bl>so viel</bl>. Quot, <bl>wievil</bl>. A viginti ad centū minor numerus cum copula præcedit, vel sine copula sequitur: ut, unus & viginti, vel viginti unus.
units.tr: swift; sospes, safe, sound; sui, of himself; superstes, surviving, or still alive; teres, round in length; tu, you; vetus, old. Add the indeclinables: ejusmodi, of such a kind; hujusmodi, of this sort; frugi, useful, thrifty; nauci, worthless; nihili, of no account; nequam, wicked; quatuor, four; quinque, five; sex, six; septem, seven; octo, eight; novem, nine; decem, ten; undecim, eleven; duodecim, twelve; tredecim, thirteen; quatuordecim, fourteen; quindecim, fifteen; sedecim, sixteen; septendecim, seventeen; octodecim or duodeviginti, eighteen; novendecim or undeviginti, nineteen; viginti, twenty; triginta, thirty; quadraginta, forty; quinquaginta, fifty; sexaginta, sixty; septuaginta, seventy; octoginta, eighty; nonaginta, ninety; centum, a hundred; mille, a thousand; tot, so many; quot, how many. A smaller number from twenty to a hundred either comes first with a conjunction or follows without one: e.g. unus et viginti or viginti unus.

units.la: Quædam Adjectiva sunt duarum vocum, quarum prior est generis communis, posterior generis neutrius: ut, hic, hæc fortis, hoc forte, <bl>starck</bl>. Hic, hæc doctior, hoc doctius, <bl>gelehrter</bl>.
units.tr: Some adjectives consist of two words, the first of the common gender and the second of the neuter: e.g. hic, hæc fortis, hoc forte, strong; hic, hæc doctior, hoc doctius, more learned.

units.la: Quædam Adjectiva sunt trium vocum, quarum prima est generis masculini. Secunda generis fœminini, tertia generis neutrius: ut, hic bonus, hæc bona, hoc bonum, <bl>gut</bl>. Hic amaturus, hæc amatura, hoc amaturum, <bl>der/die/das lieben wil</bl>. Hic amatus, hæc amata, hoc amatum, <bl>der/die/das geliebet ist</bl>. Hic amandus, hæc amanda, hoc amandum, <bl>der/die/das</bl> <bl>geliebet werden muß</bl>. Hic meus, hæc mea, hoc meum, <bl>mein</bl>. Hic noster, hæc nostra, hoc nostrum, <bl>unser</bl>. Hi ducenti, hæ ducentæ, hæc ducenta, <bl>zweyhundert</bl>. Trecenti, tæ, ta, <bl>dreyhundert</bl>. Quadringenti, tæ, ta, <bl>vierhundert</bl>. Quingenti, tæ, ta, <bl>fünffhundert</bl>. Sexcenti, tæ, ta, <bl>sechshundert</bl>. Septingenti, tæ, ta, <bl>siebenhundert</bl>. O<bl>ctingenti</bl>,tæ,ta, <bl>achthundert</bl>. Noningenti vel nongenti,tæ,ta,<bl>neu hundert</bl>.
units.tr: Some adjectives consist of three words, the first masculine, the second feminine and the third neuter: e.g. hic bonus, hæc bona, hoc bonum, good; hic amaturus, hæc amatura, hoc amaturum, he, she or it who is going to love; hic amatus, hæc amata, hoc amatum, he, she or it who has been loved; hic amandus, hæc amanda, hoc amandum, he, she or it who must be loved; hic meus, hæc mea, hoc meum, my; hic noster, hæc nostra, hoc nostrum, our; hi ducenti, hæ ducentæ, hæc ducenta, two hundred; trecenti, -æ, -a, three hundred; quadringenti, -æ, -a, four hundred; quingenti, -æ, -a, five hundred; sexcenti, -æ, -a, six hundred; septingenti, -æ, -a, seven hundred; octingenti, -æ, -a, eight hundred; noningenti or nongenti, -æ, -a, nine hundred.

units.la: Quædam Adjectiva sunt trium & duarum vocum: ut, hic exanimus, hæc exanima, hoc exanimum, & hic, hæc exanimis, hoc exanime, <bl>todt oder baßtodt</bl>. Hic celeber, hæc celebris, hoc celebre, & hic, hæc celebris, hoc celebre, <bl>berümpt</bl>. Sic Alacer, <bl>frisch vnnd</bl> <bl>frölich</bl>. Campester, <bl>feldechtig</bl>. Equester, <bl>Reuterisch</bl>. Pedester, <bl>zu fuß</bl>. Saluber, <bl>heilsam vnd gesund</bl>. Sylvester, <bl>wäldisch oder bawisch</bl>. Usum specta.
units.tr: Some adjectives have three forms and some two: e.g. hic exanimus, hæc exanima, hoc exanimum, and hic, hæc exanimis, hoc exanime, dead or stone dead; hic celeber, hæc celebris, hoc celebre, and hic, hæc celebris, hoc celebre, famous. So too alacer, lively and cheerful; campester, of the field; equester, of horsemen; pedester, on foot; saluber, healthful and wholesome; silvester, of the woods, or rustic. Observe the usage.

units.la: Unde formatur Adjectivum participia-le in ns?
units.tr: Whence is the participial adjective in -ns formed?

units.la: A primo imperfecto verbi activi, neutrius, vel Deponentis, mutato bam vel bar in ns: ut, ab amabam, cubabam, execrabar, amans, der/die/das liebet/cu- bans, ligt/execrans, verfluchet. Excipe iens, euntis, cum Compositis, Abiens, abeuntis, Periens, pereuntis, Ambiens, ambientis, &c.
units.tr: It is formed from the first imperfect of an active, neuter or deponent verb, changing bam or bar to ns: for example, from amabam, cubabam and execrabar come amans (loving, one who loves), cubans (lying, one who lies) and execrans (cursing, one who curses). Except iens, euntis, and the compounds abiens, abeuntis; periens, pereuntis; ambiens, ambientis, etc.

units.la: Unde formatur Adjectivum participia- le in rus?
units.tr: Whence is the participial adjective in -rus formed?

units.la: A supino in u Verbi activi, neutrius, vel Deponentis, addito rus: ut, ab amatu, potatu, execratu, amaturus, einer der begeret zu lieben/oder lieben wil oder wird / potaturus, einer der begeret zu sauffen / oder sauffen wil oder wird / execraturus, der verfluchen will. Excipe Arguiturus, einer der anzeigen oder straf- fen will. Pariturus, der gebären will. Oriturus, der entstehen will. Moriturus, der sterben will. Nasciturus, einer der da wird geboren werden. Et vetaturus, der verbieten will. Præstaturus, der leisten will. Cubaturus, der ligen will. Sonaturus, der klingen will. Crepaturus, der rauschen will. Secundum Vallam libro primo, capite secundo.
units.tr: It is formed from the supine in u of an active, neuter or deponent verb, with rus added: for example, from amatu, potatu and execratu come amaturus (one who wishes to love, or is going to love), potaturus (one who wishes to drink, or is going to drink) and execraturus (one who wants to curse). Except arguiturus (one who wishes to show or punish), pariturus (one who wants to give birth), oriturus (one who is about to arise), moriturus (one who is about to die), nasciturus (one who is about to be born), and also vetaturus (one who will forbid), praestaturus (one who will perform), cubaturus (one who will lie down), sonaturus (one who will sound) and crepaturus (one who will rattle). According to Valla, book 1, chapter 2.

units.la: Unde formatur Adjectivum participia-le in us?
units.tr: How is the participial adjective in -us formed?

units.la: A supino in u Verbi passivi vel Deponentis, addito s: ab amatu, execratu, Amatus, der geliebet ist/ ex-cratus, der verfluchet hat. Nonnulla participialia in us formantur a supino in u Verbi neutrius: ut, juratus, der geschworen hat. Exoletus, der verachtet ist. Aratus, gepflüget. Laboratus, mit fleiß gearbeitet. Usum Specta.
units.tr: It is formed from the supine in u of a passive or deponent verb, with s added: from amatu and execratu come amatus (loved, one who is loved) and execratus (having cursed). Some participial adjectives in -us are formed from the supine in u of a neuter verb: for example, juratus (having sworn), exoletus (despised, one who is held in contempt), aratus (ploughed), laboratus (laboured at with diligence). See usage.

units.la: Unde formatur Adjectivum participia- le in dus?
units.tr: How is the participial adjective in -dus formed?

units.la: A Gerundio Verbi passivi, mutato do in dus: ut, ab amando, docendo, amandus, einer der würdig ist/ daß er geliebet werde / oder der geliebet werde muß/ docendus, einer der würdig ist daß er gelehret werde / oder der gelehret werden muß. Nonnulla in dus a Gerundio Verbi neutrius vel Deponentis veniunt: ut, arandus, carendus, hortandus, tuendus, sequendus: Et id genus alia, poetis familiaria.
units.tr: It is formed from the gerund of a passive verb, changing do to dus: for example, from amando and docendo* come amandus (one who is worthy to be loved, or who must be loved) and docendus (one who is worthy to be taught, or who must be taught). Some in -dus come from the gerund of a neuter or deponent verb: for example arandus, carendus, hortandus, tuendus, sequendus, and others of this kind, familiar to the poets.

units.la: Ab impersonalibus hæc participialia fiunt: pœnitens, der einreuen hat/ libens, gern vnd willig/ decens, gebürlich/ pudens, schämig vnd züchtig/ pertæsus, der ein verdruß hat/ licitus, nachgelassen/ pœnitedus, gering zu achten/ pudēdus, deß man sich schämen muß/ pigendus, der zu bedauren ist/ A defectivo, odi, osum, osu, fit osus, exosus & perosus, der gehasset hat.
units.tr: These participial adjectives are formed from impersonal verbs: poenitens (repenting, one who has regret); libens (gladly and willingly); decens (becoming, proper); pudens (modest and chaste, one who feels shame); pertaesus (one who is weary of, has a distaste); licitus (permitted); poenitendus (to be regretted, of little account); pudendus (one of whom one must be ashamed); pigendus (one who is to be pitied). From the defective verb odi, osum, osu: fit osus, exosus and perosus (one who has hated).

units.la: Num in Adjectivis participialibus tempus proprium est?
units.tr: Is tense proper to participial adjectives?

units.la: Non: sed mutuantur tempus a Verbo, cui in contextu orationis subjiciuntur: ut Aristoteles disputabit inambulans. Hic Verbum, Disputabit, est futuri temporis, ita & inambulans: Et idem fere de omnibus Adjectivis participialibus, quæ omnino nihil differunt a reliquis Adjectivis, nisi quòd propc[?]modum significationem, & rectionem suorum verborum habeant, existimandum est. Excipe passivorum & Deponentium perfecta: ut, amatus sum, præratus[?] sum: <bl>Ich bin geliebet / Ich habe gestritten.</bl>
units.tr: No. Rather, they borrow their tense from the verb to which they are joined in the context of the sentence: for example, "Aristotle will dispute while walking about." Here the verb "will dispute" is in the future tense, and so is "walking about". The same is almost true of all participial adjectives, which differ in no way from other adjectives, except that they nearly have the meaning and government of their verbs; this should be borne in mind. The exceptions are the perfects of passives and deponents: for example, amatus sum (I am loved) and praeratus sum (I have fought).

units.la: Quid est Casus?
units.tr: What is a case?

units.la: Casus est specialis terminatio Nominis.
units.tr: A case is the particular ending of a noun.

units.la: Quot sunt Casus?
units.tr: How many cases are there?

units.la: Sex: Nominativus, Genitivus, Dativus, Accusativus, Vocativus & Ablativus. Nominativus & Vocativus appellantur casus recti: reliqui casus obliqui.
units.tr: Six: nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, vocative and ablative. The nominative and vocative are called the direct cases; the rest are the oblique cases.

units.la: Neutra habent tres similes casus in utroq; numero, Nominativum, Accusativum, & Vocativum, qui in plurali semper exeunt in a. Excipe ambo, duo, hoc, quid vel quod: Et Adjectiva omnis generis indeclinabilia: ut, hujusmodi, quatuor, decem, centum, &c.
units.tr: Neuter nouns have three similar cases in both numbers, the nominative, accusative and vocative, which in the plural always end in a. Except ambo, duo, hoc, quid or quod; and adjectives of every gender that are indeclinable, such as hujusmodi, quatuor, decem, centum, etc.

units.la: Quid est Declinatio?
units.tr: What is declension?

units.la: Declinatio est nominis secundum casus flexio. Nomen ex duobus Rectis compositum utrinq; declinatur: ut, Respublica, Reipublicæ, Rempublicam, &c. præter Alteruter posteriore tantum parte hodie flexum. Quod vero ex Obliquo & Recto componitur, in eo tantum Rectus declinatur: ut, Jurisperitus, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>Rechtsgelehrter</bl> / Jurisperiti, Jurisperito.
units.tr: Declension is the inflection of a noun according to its cases. A noun compounded of two nominatives is declined at both parts: for example, Respublica, Reipublicae, Rempublicam, etc.; except alteruter, which today is inflected only in its latter part. But a noun compounded of an oblique case and a nominative is declined only in its nominative part: for example, Jurisperitus (a lawyer), Jurisperiti, Jurisperito.

units.la: Quotuplex est Declinatio?
