units.tr: How many kinds of declension are there?

units.la: Duplex: Parisyllaba aut Imparisyllaba.
units.tr: Two: parisyllabic and imparisyllabic.

units.la: Quid est Declinatio Parisyllaba?
units.tr: What is parisyllabic declension?

units.la: Declinatio parisyllaba est cujus Genitivus singularis parisyllabus est Nominativo singulari: ut, Musæ, Musa, Magistri, Magister, Vetris[?], Venter, Estq; triplex: Prima, aut Secunda, aut Tertia.
units.tr: Parisyllabic declension is that in which the genitive singular has the same number of syllables as the nominative singular: for example, Musa, Musae; Magister, Magistri; Venter, Ventris. It is threefold: first, second or third.

units.la: Quid est Prima Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the first declension?

units.la: Prima Declinatio est, cujus Nominativus singularis definit in a, vel e, vel as, vel es, Genitivus in æ vel es, Dativus in æ. Quædam bifariam Nominativo cafu efferuntur : ut, hæc Grammatica & hæc Grammatice, <bl>Sprachekunst[?]</bl>. Hæc aranea, <bl>ein spinnweb</bl>/ hic araneus, <bl>die spinn</bl> / secundæ Declinationis. Hæc Amygdala vel Amygdalus, <bl>ein Mandelbaum</bl>/ hæc Amygdala vel Amygdalum, <bl>ein mandelkern</bl>. Hæc Buccina, hoc buccinum, <bl>ein Trommete oder Schalmey[?]</bl>. Hæc mulctra, hoc mulctrum, <bl>ein melckeymer</bl>. Hæc tribula, hoc tribulum, <bl>ein tröschwage[?]</bl>.
units.tr: The first declension is that whose nominative singular ends in a, e, as or es, whose genitive ends in ae or es, and whose dative ends in ae. Some are given in two forms in the nominative: for example, grammatica and grammatice (the art of language, German: Sprachkunst). Aranea (a spider's web), and araneus (a spider), which is of the second declension. Amygdala or amygdalus (an almond tree), and amygdala or amygdalum (an almond kernel). Buccina and buccinum (a trumpet or shawm). Mulctra and mulctrum (a milking pail). Tribula and tribulum (a threshing sledge).

units.la: Cedò primæ Declinationis paradigmata.
units.tr: Now the paradigms of the first declension.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Hæc Musa, <bl>der gesang oder die kunst</bl> / Hæc Epitome, <bl>die kurtze begreiffung.</bl> G. Hujus, Musæ, <bl>des gesanges/ Epitomes, der kur-</bl> <bl>tzen begreiffung.</bl> D. Huic Musæ, <bl>dem gesange</bl> / Epitomæ <bl>der kurtzen</bl> <bl>begreiffung.</bl> A. Hanc Musam, <bl>den gesang/</bl> Epitomen, <bl>die kurtze</bl> <bl>begreiffung.</bl> V. O Musa, <bl>o du gesang</bl> / Epitome, <bl>o du kurtze</bl> <bl>begreiffung.</bl> A. Ab hac Musa, <bl>von dem gesange/</bl> Epitome, <bl>von</bl> <bl>der kurtzen begreiffung.</bl>
units.tr: N. This Musa, "the song or the art"; this Epitome, "the short summary." G. Of this Musa, "of the song"; of this Epitome, "of the short summary." D. To this Musa, "to the song"; to this Epitome, "to the short summary." A. This Musam, "the song"; this Epitomen, "the short summary." V. O Musa, "O song"; O Epitome, "O short summary." Ab. From this Musa, "from the song"; from this Epitome, "from the short summary."

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. Hæ Musæ, <bl>die gesånge/</bl> Epitomæ, <bl>die kurtzen</bl> <bl>begreiffungen.</bl> G. Harum Musarum, <bl>der gesånge /</bl> Epitomarum, <bl>der kurtzen begreiffungen.</bl> D. His Musis, <bl>den gesången/</bl> Epitomis, <bl>den kurtzen</bl> <bl>begreiffungen.</bl> A. Has Musas, <bl>die gesånge /</bl> Epitomas, <bl>die kurtzen</bl> <bl>begreiffungen.</bl> V. O Musæ, <bl>o ihr gesånge /</bl> Epitomæ, <bl>o ihr</bl> <bl>kurtzen begreiffungen.</bl> A. Ab his Musis, <bl>von den gesången/</bl> Epitomis, <bl>von</bl> <bl>den kurtzen begreiffungen.</bl>
units.tr: N. These Musae, "the songs"; these Epitomae, "the short summaries." G. Of these Musarum, "of the songs"; of these Epitomarum, "of the short summaries." D. To these Musis, "to the songs"; to these Epitomis, "to the short summaries." A. These Musas, "the songs"; these Epitomas, "the short summaries." V. O Musae, "O you songs"; O Epitomae, "O you short summaries." Ab. From these Musis, "from the songs"; from these Epitomis, "from the short summaries."

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Hic Andreas, | <bl>Hic Ecclesiastes, der Prediger.</bl> G. Hujus Andreæ, | <bl>Ecclesiastæ, deß Predigers.</bl> D. Huic Andreæ, | <bl>Ecclesiastæ, dem Prediger.</bl> A. Hunc Andream, | <bl>Ecclesiasten, den Prediger.</bl> V. O Andrea, | <bl>Ecclesiaste, O du Prediger.</bl> A. Ab hoc Andrea. | <bl>Ecclesiaste, von dem Prediger.</bl>
units.tr: N. This Andreas, | This Ecclesiastes, "the preacher." G. Of this Andreae, | Ecclesiastae, "of the preacher." D. To this Andreae, | Ecclesiastae, "to the preacher." A. This Andream, | Ecclesiasten, "the preacher." V. O Andrea, | Ecclesiaste, "O you preacher." Ab. From this Andrea, | Ecclesiaste, "from the preacher."

units.la: Pluralis Numerus superiorem formam sequitur.
units.tr: The plural follows the form above.

units.la: Accusativus singularis à Græcis in as, habet an sæpius,quàm am: ut Hic Aeneas,hunc Aenean.
units.tr: The Greeks form the accusative singular of nouns in as, and use an more often than am: as, hic Aeneas, hunc Aenean.

units.la: Patronymica,hoc est,quæ à parentum Nominibus deducuntur,in e, declinantur ut Epitome: in des, ut Ecclesiastes. Adrastine, id est, filia Adrasti,<bl>ein tochter</bl> <bl>des Königes Der Griechen.</bl> Aeneades, id est, filius Aeneæ,<bl>ein sohn des gewaltigen Helden.</bl>
units.tr: Patronymics, that is, names derived from the names of parents, are declined in e like Epitome, or in des like Ecclesiastes. Adrastine, that is, daughter of Adrastus, "a daughter of the king of the Greeks." Aeneades, that is, son of Aeneas, "a son of the mighty hero."

units.la: Cujus generis sunt Nomina primæ Declinationis?
units.tr: What gender are the nouns of the first declension?

units.la: Nomina primæ Declinationis in a vel e-sunt generis fœminini,in as vel es generis masculini: ut,hæc pœna,<bl>ein fåder[?]/</bl> hæc Pentecoste,<bl>Pfingsten.</bl> Hic Esaias,<bl>der</bl> <bl>Prophet.</bl> Hic absinthites,<bl>Wermutwein.</bl> Figuratè dicitur: Amarum Absinthites. Intelligitur vinum.
units.tr: Nouns of the first declension ending in a or e are feminine; those ending in as or es are masculine: e.g. haec poena, "punishment"; haec Pentecoste, "Pentecost." Hic Esaias, "the prophet." Hic absinthites, "wormwood wine." It is used figuratively: Amarum Absinthites, understood as wine.

units.la: Quæ excipiuntur?
units.tr: What are the exceptions?

units.la: Nomina, quæ viro,aut rebus viri speciè conceptis congruunt,masculina sunt: ut,Hic Collega,<bl>der mit-</bl> <bl>gesell an eine ampt.</bl> Cometa,<bl>ein haarechtiger stern.</bl> Mammona,<bl>der Gott der reichtumb.</bl> Planeta,<bl>ein irr-</bl> <bl>ender stern.</bl> Poeta,<bl>ein Verßdichter.</bl> Rabula,<bl>ein un-</bl> <bl>gestümer[?] schwäßer.</bl> Et id gen° plura. Pascha, paschæ, vel paschatis,<bl>überschritt oder Ostern</bl> / & Manna indeclinabile,<bl>Himmelbrot oder Himmeltaw</bl> / sunt neutrius generis. Advena,<bl>ein Fremdling.</bl> Verna,<bl>der oder</bl> <bl>die in unserem hauß geboren ist leibeigen.</bl> Dama,<bl>ein wilder</bl> <bl>wider Rechbock</bl>. Talpa,<bl>ein Maulwerff</bl> / sunt communis generis.
units.tr: Nouns that agree with a man, or with things conceived as male, are masculine: e.g. hic Collega, "a colleague in an office"; Cometa, "a hairy star (comet)"; Mammona, "the god of riches"; Planeta, "a wandering star"; Poeta, "a poet"; Rabula, "a blustering, noisy babbler"; and many more of this kind. Pascha, paschae or paschatis, "Passover or Easter," and Manna, indeclinable, "heavenly bread or heavenly dew," are neuter. Advena, "a stranger"; Verna, "a home-born slave, male or female"; Dama, "a fallow buck"; Talpa, "a mole," are of common gender.

units.la: Dativus & Ablativus plurales quo- modo definunt?
units.tr: How do the dative and ablative plural end?

units.la: Perpetuò in is. Hæc autem Substantiva: Filia,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>Tochter</bl>. Nata,<bl>ein Tochter</bl>. Dea,<bl>ein Göttin</bl> Liberta, <bl>ein frengegebene magd</bl>. Equa, <bl>ein mutterpferd</bl>. Mula, <bl>ein Maulesel</bl> / formant Dativum & Ablativum pluralem in abus. Quidam addunt, Anima, animabus,Domina,dominabus.
units.tr: Always in is. However, these substantives: Filia, "a daughter"; Nata, "a daughter"; Dea, "a goddess"; Liberta, "a freedwoman"; Equa, "a mare"; Mula, "a she-mule," form the dative and ablative plural in abus. Some add Anima, animabus; Domina, dominabus.

units.la: Quænam sunt singularis numeri tantum?
units.tr: Which nouns are singular only?

units.la: Culpa, <bl>ein schuld</bl> / fama, <bl>das gerücht</bl> / fuga, <bl>die</bl> <bl>flucht</bl> / gaza,<bl>der schatz</bl> / gloria, <bl>die ehr</bl>: Et nomina virtutum ac vitiorum : ut amicitia, <bl>freundtschafft</bl> / eloquentia, <bl>wolredenheit</bl> / avaritia,<bl>geitzigkeit</bl>. Attamen Authores dicunt : glorias,iras,amicitias,inimicitias.
units.tr: Culpa, "guilt"; fama, "rumour"; fuga, "flight"; gaza, "treasure"; gloria, "glory." Also the names of virtues and vices: amicitia, "friendship"; eloquentia, "eloquence"; avaritia, "greed." Yet authors say: glorias, iras, amicitias, inimicitias.

units.la: Quænam sunt pluralis numeri tantum?
units.tr: Which nouns are plural only?

units.la: <bl>Antiæ,die vorderen haarlöck der weibern</bl>. Athenæ, <bl>ein Stat in Griechenland</bl>. Apinæ, <bl>nuß mit weichen</bl> <bl>schalen</bl>. Argutiæ,<bl>spitzfindigkeit</bl>. Blanditiæ,<bl>liebkosung</bl>. Bigæ, <bl>ein Karr</bl> / <bl>da zwey Rösse anziehen</bl>. Calendæ, <bl>der erste tag eines jeglichen Monats</bl>. Clitellæ, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>sattel</bl>/ <bl>darauff die Esel schwäre last tragen</bl>. Copiæ, <bl>ein hauffen Kriegsvolck</bl>. Cunæ,<bl>kindswiegen</bl>. Decimæ, <bl>der zehend von früchten oder anderem dinge</bl>. Diræ,<bl>verfluchung</bl>. Divitiæ,<bl>reichthumb</bl>. Exequiæ,<bl>leich-</bl> <bl>bestattung</bl>. Excubiæ,<bl>die wacht</bl>. Exuviæ,<bl>die abgez-</bl> <bl>ogenen kleider der feinde/ oder thieren heut</bl>. Facetiæ, <bl>schimpffred</bl>. Feriæ,<bl>feyertag</bl>. Genæ,<bl>die backen oder wägen</bl>. Habenæ,<bl>d' zügel am zaun</bl>. Illecebræ,<bl>anreitzung</bl>. Insidiæ, <bl>ein heimlich hinderhalt</bl>/ Inducieæ, <bl>anstand des kriegs</bl>. Literæ,<bl>brieff oder künste</bl>. Manubiæ, <bl>peute so man dem</bl> <bl>feinde abgetrungen hat</bl>. Minæ,<bl>trauwort</bl>. Minutiæ, <bl>gar</bl> <bl>kleine stücklin</bl>. Nonæ/ <bl>im merzen/ meyen/ howmonat vñ[?]</bl> <bl>Weinmonat</bl> der <bl>siebende</bl> tag / in den <bl>anderen</bl> der fünffte. Nugæ, <bl>vnnütze geschwätze</bl>. Nuptiæ, ein <bl>braut-</bl> <bl>lauff</bl> / <bl>hochzeit</bl>. Nundinæ, ein <bl>jarmarckt</bl>. Paleæ, <bl>Kornhülsen</bl>. Phalangæ, ein <bl>angrund holtz</bl> / <bl>darauff man</bl> <bl>etwas wirfft</bl>. Palpebræ, <bl>die haar der augdeckten</bl>. Phaleræ, <bl>Roßgeschmuck</bl>. Prestigiæ, <bl>verblendung des</bl> <bl>gesichts</bl> / <bl>gauckleren</bl>. Primitiæ, <bl>die ersten früchte</bl>. Quisquiliæ, <bl>hinwürffige dinge/oder außfegeten</bl>. Salebræ, <bl>vnebne wege/vnzierliche reden</bl>. Scalæ, ein <bl>leyter</bl>. Scandulæ, <bl>dünne bretter / damit man die häuser</bl> <bl>decke</bl>. Scopæ, ein <bl>bäsem</bl>. Syracusæ, ein <bl>Statt</bl> <bl>in Si-</bl> <bl>cilia</bl>. Tenebræ, <bl>finsternis</bl>. Thermæ, <bl>bäder von natur</bl> <bl>warm</bl>. Tricæ, <bl>das sich den hünern vmb die füsse wicklet/verhinderung/ vnnütze</bl> <bl>ding</bl>. Valvæ, <bl>thüre oder laden die zwifach auffeinander gehen</bl>. Vindicię, <bl>schirmung zum rechten / oder die gerechtigkeit zubesitzen</bl> <bl>ein ding/das im Jancke ist/biß zu außtrag der sachen</bl>.
units.tr: Antiae, "the front locks of women's hair"; Athenae, "a city in Greece"; Apinae, "nuts with soft shells"; Argutiae, "subtlety"; Blanditiae, "flattery"; Bigae, "a chariot drawn by two horses"; Calendae, "the first day of each month"; Clitellae, "a saddle on which asses carry heavy loads"; Copiae, "a band of soldiers"; Cunae, "a cradle"; Decimae, "a tithe of fruit or other things"; Dirae, "a curse"; Divitiae, "riches"; Exequiae, "a funeral"; Excubiae, "a watch"; Exuviae, "the cast-off clothes of enemies, or the hides of animals"; Facetiae, "jests"; Feriae, "a holiday"; Genae, "the cheeks or jaws"; Habenae, "the reins"; Illecebrae, "enticements"; Insidiae, "a secret ambush"; Induciae, "a truce in war"; Literae, "letters or learning"; Manubiae, "booty taken from the enemy"; Minae, "threats"; Minutiae, "very small pieces"; Nonae: in March, May, July and October the seventh day, in the other months the fifth; Nugae, "idle trifles"; Nuptiae, "a wedding, a bridal procession"; Nundinae, "a market fair"; Paleae, "chaff"; Phalangae, "a wooden roller on which something is thrown"; Palpebrae, "the eyelashes"; Phaleræ, "horse trappings"; Prestigiae, "deception of the sight, juggling"; Primitiae, "the first fruits"; Quisquiliae, "rubbish or sweepings"; Salebrae, "uneven roads, uncouth speech"; Scalae, "a ladder"; Scandulae, "thin boards with which houses are roofed"; Scopae, "a broom"; Syracusae, "a city in Sicily"; Tenebrae, "darkness"; Thermae, "baths naturally warm"; Tricae, "what wraps itself round a hen's feet; a hindrance; trifles"; Valvae, "doors or shutters that open in two leaves"; Vindiciae, "the protection of a right, or the right to hold a thing pending the outcome of a case."

units.la: Quæ variant pluralem numerum?
units.tr: Which nouns vary in the plural?

units.la: Græca artiū Nomina: ut, Grammatice, ces, Grammatica, corum. Rhetorice, ces, Rhetorica, corum. Quædam uno casu usurpantur: ut inferias, <bl>todten</bl> <bl>Opffer</bl>. Inficias, <bl>läugnung</bl>/ inficias eo, <bl>ich läugne</bl>: Quædam duobus: ut, harum repetundarum, his repetundis, <bl>gelt oder gut</bl> / <bl>das den vnderthanen in den</bl> <bl>Vogteyen von den Vögten vnbillicher weiß abge-</bl> <bl>nommen ist</bl> / <bl>welches die vnderthanen / zu Rom im</bl> <bl>gerichte haben wider heissen mögen</bl>. Hæ suppetiæ, <bl>has suppetias, Zuschub/beistand</bl>.
units.tr: Greek names of the arts: as Grammatice, ces, Grammatica, corum; Rhetorice, ces, Rhetorica, corum. Some are used in one case only: as inferias, sacrifices for the dead. Inficias, a denial; inficias eo, "I deny it." Some are used in two cases: as harum repetundarum or his repetundis, money or goods unjustly taken by bailiffs from the subjects in their districts, which the subjects may demand back at Rome in court. Hæ suppetiæ, has suppetias, help or assistance.

units.la: Quid est Secunda Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the Second Declension?

units.la: Secunda Declinatio est, cujus Nominativus singularis definit in er, vel ir, vel ur, vel us, vel eus, vel um, Genitivus in i, Dativus in o, Accusativus in um. Casus Græcus aliquando manet: ut, Samos, <bl>ein Insel im</bl> <bl>Meer Ægeo</bl> / Lesbos, <bl>auch ein Insel im Meer Æ-</bl> gen/ pro, Samus, Lesbus. Ilion, <bl>die statt Troja</bl>/pro Ilium.
units.tr: The Second Declension is the one whose nominative singular ends in er, ir, ur, us, eus, or um; its genitive ends in i, its dative in o, its accusative in um. Sometimes the Greek case remains: as Samos, an island in the Aegean Sea, and Lesbos, also an island in the Aegean Sea, instead of Samus and Lesbus. Ilion, the city of Troy, instead of Ilium.

units.la: Quædam bifariam Nominativo Casu efferuntur: ut, hic Acinus, hoc Acinum, <bl>ein korn als ein wein-</bl> <bl>trauben</bl>. Hic Baptismus, hoc baptismum & Baptismatis, <bl>der Tauff</bl>. Hic baculus, hoc baculum, <bl>ein stab</bl> <bl>oder stecf</bl>. Hic chirographus, hoc chirographum, <bl>ein handschrifft</bl>. Hic crocus, hoc crocum, <bl>saffran</bl>. Hic & hæc intybus, hoc intybum, <bl>ein kraut / Löwenzan</bl> <bl>genennt / etliche wöllen es sey Wegwart / etliche es</bl> <bl>sey endivien mit den blawen blumen</bl>. Hic punctus, hoc punctum, <bl>ein klein unteilbar ding / ein stimm/</bl> <bl>chür/ oder ein augenblick</bl>. Hic supparus, hoc supparum, <bl>ein überkleid/ schurtz oder sägelthuch</bl>. Hic syngraphus, hæc syngrapha, hoc syngraphum, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>handschrifft oder verschreibung</bl>. Hoc angiportum, hic angiportus, hujus angiportus, <bl>ein kleines enges gäß-</bl> <bl>lin</bl>. Hic commentarius, hoc commetarium, <bl>ein brieff</bl> <bl>darin aller beschceid eines dinges kurtz begriffen ist/</bl> <bl>ein gedächtnis buch / ein erklärung über and' bücher</bl>.
units.tr: Some nouns are used in two forms in the nominative: as hic Acinus, hoc Acinum, a grape-seed or a grape. Hic Baptismus, hoc baptismum and Baptismatis, baptism. Hic baculus, hoc baculum, a staff or stick. Hic chirographus, hoc chirographum, a handwritten document. Hic crocus, hoc crocum, saffron. Hic and hæc intybus, hoc intybum, a herb called lion's tooth; some hold it is wayfarer (chicory), others endive with blue flowers. Hic punctus, hoc punctum, a small indivisible thing, a note in music, or a moment. Hic supparus, hoc supparum, an overgarment, an apron, or a sheet of cloth. Hic syngraphus, hæc syngrapha, hoc syngraphum, a handwritten bond or contract. Hoc angiportum, hic angiportus, hujus angiportus, a small narrow alley. Hic commentarius, hoc commentarium, a letter in which the whole account of a matter is briefly comprised; a notebook; an explanation of other books.

units.la: Cedo paradigmata Secundæ Declinationis.
units.tr: Give me the paradigms of the Second Declension.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Hic Magister, <bl>der meister/</bl> hoc scamnū, <bl>die banck</bl>. G. Hujus magistri, <bl>des meisters/</bl> scamni, <bl>der banck</bl>. D. Huic magistro, <bl>dem meister</bl>/ scamno, <bl>der banck</bl>. A. Hunc magistrū, <bl>de meister</bl>/ hoc scamnū, <bl>die banck</bl>. V. O magister, <bl>O meister</bl>/ O scamnum, <bl>O banck</bl>. A. Ab hoc magistro, <bl>vo de meister</bl>/ scano, <bl>von d' bäck</bl>.
units.tr: Nom. Hic magister, the master; hoc scamnum, the bench. Gen. Hujus magistri, of the master; scamni, of the bench. Dat. Huic magistro, to the master; scamno, to the bench. Acc. Hunc magistrum, the master; hoc scamnum, the bench. Voc. O magister, O master; O scamnum, O bench. Abl. Ab hoc magistro, from the master; scamno, from the bench.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. Hi magistri, die meister/ hæc scamna, die bäncke. G. Horum magistrorum, der meister / scamnorum, der bäncke. D. His magistris, den meistern/ scamnis, den bäncken. A. Hos magistros, die meister/ hæc scäna, die bäncke, V.O magistri, O jh: meister / O scamna, O jh: bäncke.
units.tr: Nom. Hi magistri, the masters; hæc scamna, the benches. Gen. Horum magistrorum, of the masters; scamnorum, of the benches. Dat. His magistris, to the masters; scamnis, to the benches. Acc. Hos magistros, the masters; hæc scamna, the benches. Voc. O magistri, O masters; O scamna, O benches.

units.la: A. Ab his magistris, von den meistern / scamnis von den bäncken.
units.tr: Abl. Ab his magistris, from the masters; scamnis, from the benches.

units.la: Quædam Nomina Secundæ Declinationis crescūt Genitivo, nempe à Gero & Fero composita: ut, Armiger, armigeri, ein waffentrager. Signifer, signiferi, ein Fenderich. Sic asper, rauh/hart/vnmilt. Adulter, ein Ehebrecher. Exter, fremd/außländisch[?]. Socer, meiner Frawen Vatter. Liber, frey vnd ledig. Miser, leidehafft/ellend. Tener, zart/weich. Dexter, gerecht/an der rechten seiten. Gener, Tochtertmann. Gibber, hogerechtig. Puer, ein knab. Prosper, der glück vnnd wolfart bringet. Vir, ein mann. Satur, satt/gesettiget.
units.tr: Some nouns of the Second Declension grow by a syllable in the genitive, namely those compounded from gero and fero: as armiger, armigeri, a weapon-bearer; signifer, signiferi, a standard-bearer. So too asper, rough, harsh, ungenerous; adulter, an adulterer; exter, foreign or alien; socer, my wife's father; liber, free and unencumbered; miser, wretched, miserable; tener, tender, soft; dexter, right, on the right side; gener, a son-in-law; gibber, hunchbacked; puer, a boy; prosper, bringing good fortune and prosperity; vir, a man; satur, full, sated.

units.la: Quædam in Secunda & Imparisyllaba Declinatione flectūtur: ut Oedipus, Oedipi & Oedipodis, ein sohn Laji des Thebanischen Königs / welcher die frag Sphyngis aufgelöset hatt. Polypus, polypi & polypodis, ein Meerfisch mit viel fussen / Ein nasen geschwär. Laurus, lauri & hujus laurus, ein Lorbeerbaum. Quercus, ci & us, ein Eichbaum. Cornus, ni & nus, ein grosser hagendorn. Pinus, ni & nus, ein fiechtenbaum. Ficus, ci & cus, ein feigenbaum. Colus, li & lus, ein Runckel / ein spinwock.
units.tr: Some nouns are inflected both in the second and in the imparisyllabic declension: as Oedipus, Oedipi and Oedipodis, son of Laius, the king of Thebes, who solved the riddle of the Sphinx. Polypus, polypi and polypodis, a sea creature with many feet; a polyp in the nose. Laurus, lauri and hujus laurus, a laurel tree. Quercus, ci and us, an oak tree. Cornus, ni and nus, a large hawthorn. Pinus, ni and nus, a pine tree. Ficus, ci and cus, a fig tree. Colus, li and lus, a distaff or a skein of yarn.

units.la: Cujus generis sunt nomina secundæ Declinationis?
units.tr: Of what gender are the nouns of the Second Declension?

units.la: Nomina secundæ Declinationis in er, vel ir, vel ur, vel us, vel eus, sunt generis masculini, in um omnino generis neutrius, si modò non sint viri vel mulieris propria: ut, hic magister, der meister. Hic vir, der man. Hic satur, satt. Hic Dominus, ein Herr. Hic Orpheus, ein außbündiger Leirer / welcher die wälde vnd harte steine mit seiner Leiren bewogē hat. Hoc Marpurgü.
units.tr: Nouns of the Second Declension ending in er, ir, ur, us, or eus are masculine; those in um are wholly neuter, unless they are the proper names of a man or a woman: as hic magister, the master; hic vir, the man; hic satur, sated; hic Dominus, a lord; hic Orpheus, an outstanding lyre-player who by his lyre moved forests and hard stones; hoc Marpurgum.

units.la: Quæ excipiuntur?
units.tr: What are the exceptions?

units.la: Hæc fœminina in us: Acopus, ein stinckend kraut. Alopecurus, ein kraut/mattenflachs. Amethystus, ein edelgestein. Arctus, der Heerwagen am Himmel groß <bl>und klein</bl>. Abyssus,ein abgrund. Astragalus,ein würffelspiel. Costus,ein kraut/ das eine wolriechige wur-zel hatt. Balanus,ein eychel/ein kapfftlin zu stulgang. Biblus,ein bintz. Bupleurus,ein kraut. Byssus,köstcher leinwaht. Cheronesus vel chersonesus,ein halbinsel. Chrysolitus,ein goldfarbig edelgestein. Crystallus,ein Crystallstein. Diphthongus,ein zwenfaltiger thon. Dialectus,ein eigenschafft zu sprechē. Epirus,ein land das kein Insel ist. Exodus,ein außgang. Eremus,ein wüste. Ficus,ein feigen. Hyssopus,ὕσσωπος. Humus,das <bl>Erdtreich</bl> Methodus,ein fürtzer weg. Nardus,spica in der Apotek. Papyrus,ein Egyptisch bäumlin darauß man schreibblätter machte. Periodus,ein umbhang. Synodus,ein versamlung. Vannus,ein wann. Et gemmarum & fruticum nomina plæraq;. Neutra sunt,vulgus, dz gemeine volck. Pelagus, die tieffe des Meers. Virus,ein starcker geruch/gifft. Interdum vulgus in masculino genere reperitur. Communia sunt, Barbitus,ein grosse Leire oder Laute. Camelus,ein Camelthier? Carbasus, subtil leinwath/ darauß man schiff sägel macht. Colus,ein rückel / ein spinwocf. Cythisus,grosser Klee. Grossus, ein unzeitige feige. Pampinus,ein weinrebē blatt. Paradisus,ein lustgarten. Phaselus, ein lang schiff. A nominativo in eus,Accusativus definit in a: ut, Orpheus,Orphea.
units.tr: These are feminine in -us: Acopus, a stinking herb; Alopecurus, a grass, foxtail; Amethystus, a precious stone; Arctus, the Great and Little Bear in the sky; Abyssus, an abyss; Astragalus, a dice game; Costus, a herb with a fragrant root; Balanus, an acorn, or a small cap for a stool; Biblus, a papyrus; Bupleurus, a herb; Byssus, fine linen; Cheronesus or chersonesus, a peninsula; Chrysolitus, a gold-coloured precious stone; Crystallus, a crystal stone; Diphthongus, a double-sounded vowel; Dialectus, a manner of speaking; Epirus, a land that is not an island; Exodus, a going out; Eremus, a desert; Ficus, a fig; Hyssopus, hyssop [ὕσσωπος]; Humus, the earth; Methodus, a short way; Nardus, spikenard, a spike in the apothecary's shop; Papyrus, an Egyptian plant from which writing sheets were made; Periodus, a sentence, a period; Synodus, an assembly; Vannus, a winnowing fan. Also most names of gems and shrubs. Neuter: vulgus, the common people; pelagus, the depths of the sea; virus, a strong smell or poison. Sometimes vulgus is found in the masculine. Common gender: barbitus, a large lyre or lute; camelus, a camel; carbasus, fine linen from which ship's sails are made; colus, a distaff or a skein of yarn; cythisus, large clover; grossus, an unripe fig; pampinus, a grapevine leaf; paradisus, a pleasure garden; phaselus, a long ship. From a nominative in eus, the accusative ends in a: as Orpheus, Orphea.

units.la: Nomina in us quomodo habent in Vocativo?
units.tr: How do nouns in -us form the vocative?

units.la: Nomina Appellativa vel Propria secūdæ declinationis in us,habēt in Vocativo e: ut,Dominus,domine. Tabellarius,tabellarie. Fluvius,fluvie,& fluvius per Antiptosin. Sic Agnus, Chorus populus e & us habere creduntur.Tria appellativa definūt in i: ut,Filius, fili, ein sohn. Meus,mi,mein. Genius, genii,ein <bl>Gott</bl> oder <bl>Engel</bl> der natur. Deus, & Lucus,ein geweihter <bl>wald</bl>/Vocativo manent.At Oedipus,ōOedipu. Propria in ius vel jus abjiciunt in Vocativo us, jod mutato in i: ut Antonius, ō Antoni. Cajus, ō Cai. Pompeius, ō Pompei. In eus abjiciunt s: ut, Orpheus, ō Orphei.
units.tr: Appellative or proper nouns of the second declension ending in -us have -e in the vocative: for example, Dominus, domine; Tabellarius, tabellarie; Fluvius, fluvie, and also fluvius by antiptosis. Likewise Agnus, Chorus and Populus are believed to take either -e or -us. Three appellatives end in -i: Filius, fili (a son); Meus, mi (mine); Genius, genii (a god or angel of nature). Deus and Lucus (a consecrated wood) remain unchanged in the vocative. But Oedipus becomes ō Oedipu. Proper nouns in -ius or -jus drop -us in the vocative and change the i: Antonius, ō Antoni; Cajus, ō Cai; Pompeius, ō Pompei. Those in -eus drop the s: Orpheus, ō Orphei.

units.la: Quænam sunt singularis numeri tantum?
units.tr: What nouns are used only in the singular?

units.la: Ceftus, ein <bl>gürtel der liebe / allerley hüpsche band.</bl> Fimus, <bl>mist.</bl> Humus, <bl>dz erdrich.</bl> Limus, <bl>kath/schleim.</bl> Pontus, <bl>dz Meer.</bl> Vilcus, <bl>vogelleim.</bl> Album, <bl>ein jet-</bl> <bl>lich register.</bl> Aevum, <bl>ein lange</bl> <bl>zeit / ewigkeit.</bl> Barathrum, <bl>ein groß tieff loch/ ein schlemmer.</bl> Coenum, <bl>dreck.</bl> Fascinum, <bl>bezauberung.</bl> Lethum, <bl>der tod.</bl> Lutum, <bl>kaat/leymen.</bl> Macellum, <bl>ein speißmarckt.</bl> Nihilum & Nihil per Apocopen, <bl>nichts.</bl> Pedum, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>hirtenstäck.</bl> Pelagus, <bl>die tieffe des Meers.</bl> Salum, <bl>das Meer.</bl> Senium, <bl>das alter.</bl> Solium, <bl>ein königlicher</bl> <bl>stul.</bl> Justitium, <bl>die aufsschlahung des gerichtes.</bl> Vitrum, <bl>glaß.</bl> Vulgus, <bl>der gemeine mann.</bl> Virus, <bl>stanck</bl> <bl>oder gifft</bl> / indeclinabile est. Deinde Nomina unius rei propria: Item, metallorum, frumentorum, herbarum, liquidorum, & ponderatorum nomina sunt singularis numeri tantum: ut Rhenus, <bl>der Rhein.</bl> Corinthus, <bl>ein stat in Achaja gelegen.</bl> Aurum, <bl>gold.</bl> Argentum, <bl>silber.</bl> Hordeum, <bl>gerst.</bl> Triticum, <bl>wentze.</bl> Cordum, <bl>herbstthew.</bl> Oleum, <bl>oel.</bl> Mulsum, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>tranck aus wein vnd honig gemacht.</bl> Butyrum, <bl>butter/schmaltz</bl> & similia. Usus specßtandus: Is enim quibusdam recitatis nominibus Num. Plurale attribuit, cum Scipiones, Fabios, Metallos, hordea, vina, &c. dicut autores.
units.tr: Cestus (a girdle of love, or all kinds of pretty bands); Fimus (dung); Humus (the earth); Limus (mud, slime); Pontus (the sea); Viscus (birdlime); Album (a list of each kind, a register); Aevum (a long time, eternity); Barathrum (a great deep hole, a glutton); Coenum (mud, filth); Fascinum (bewitchment); Lethum (death); Lutum (clay, loam); Macellum (a meat market); Nihilum, and Nihil by apocope (nothing); Pedum (a shepherd's staff); Pelagus (the depth of the sea); Salum (the sea); Senium (old age); Solium (a royal throne); Justitium (the suspension of the courts); Vitrum (glass); Vulgus (the common people); Virus (a stench or poison; it is indeclinable). Next, the proper names of single things, and the names of metals, grains, herbs, liquids and things sold by weight, are singular only: for example, Rhenus (the Rhine); Corinthus (a city in Achaia); Aurum (gold); Argentum (silver); Hordeum (barley); Triticum (wheat); Cordum (autumn dew); Oleum (oil); Mulsum (a drink made of wine and honey); Butyrum (butter, lard), and similar words. Usage must be observed, for after citing some of these names, authors give them a plural, saying Scipiones, Fabii, metalla, hordea, vina and so on.

units.la: Quænam sunt pluralis numeri tantum?
units.tr: What nouns are used only in the plural?

units.la: Cancelli, <bl>gatter aus holtz oder eysen.</bl> Cani, <bl>graw</bl> <bl>haar.</bl> Fasti, <bl>tage daran man gerichte halten dorffte/</bl> <bl>oder ein Calender.</bl> Fori, <bl>die schiff bühne.</bl> Gemini, <bl>zwilling.</bl> Inferi, <bl>die hellischen.</bl> Liberi, <bl>kinder.</bl> Accusativus singularis, Liberum apud J. Consultos, & Vallam. Superi, <bl>die einwohner des Himmels.</bl> Arma, <bl>waffen</bl> <bl>ober werckzeug zu einem jetlichen dinge</bl>. Adversaria, <bl>ein hädtbuch</bl>. Bellaria, <bl>allerley speiß die man zu letst</bl> <bl>mit</bl> <bl>dem käß fürstellet</bl>. Biblia, <bl>die hochheiligen</bl> <bl>Gottes bücher</bl>. Castra, <bl>ein kriegslager</bl>. Compita, <bl>da sich</bl> <bl>viel wege theilen</bl>. Cunabula vel incunabula, <bl>dz beth-</bl> <bl>lin in kindswiegen/oder ein anfang</bl>. Crepundia, <bl>al-</bl> <bl>lerley ding so man den kindern gibt, sie zu schweigen/ als</bl> <bl>Corallen / Wolffsjän [?]</bl>. Chronica, <bl>ein geschichtbuch</bl>. Exta, <bl>das gehenck/leber/lung</bl>. Hyberna, <bl>winterl-</bl> <bl>ager</bl>. Magalia vel Mapalia, <bl>hütten/Hirten heuslin</bl>. Menstrua, <bl>der weiber vierwüchiger fluß</bl>. Munia, <bl>die</bl> <bl>pflicht oder ämpter</bl>. Præcordia, <bl>die theil des leibes</bl> <bl>die nahe bey den hertzen/oder zu beiden seiten zu nechst</bl> <bl>unter den rippen ligen</bl>. Repotia, <bl>die nach hochzeit</bl>. Rostra, <bl>ein erhöcht gestül/davon man redet</bl>. Stativa <bl>ein kriegslager</bl>. Tesqua, <bl>wilde/ vngeheure örte</bl>. Justa, <bl>bestattung der todten</bl>. Verenda, <bl>des menschen scham</bl>.
units.tr: Cancelli (lattice work of wood or iron); Cani (grey hair); Fasti (days on which courts might be held, or a calendar); Fori (the gangways of a ship); Gemini (twins); Inferi (the dwellers in hell); Liberi (children). The singular Liberum is used by the jurists and by Valla. Superi (the inhabitants of heaven); Arma (weapons, or the tools for any task); Adversaria (a notebook); Bellaria (all sorts of food served last, after the cheese); Biblia (the most holy books of God); Castra (a military camp); Compita (places where many roads meet); Cunabula or incunabula (a child's cradle, or a beginning); Crepundia (all sorts of things given to children to quiet them, such as coral and wolf's teeth [?]); Chronica (a history book); Exta (the entrails: heart, liver, lungs); Hiberna (winter quarters); Magalia or Mapalia (huts, shepherds' little houses); Menstrua (a woman's monthly flow); Munia (duties or offices); Praecordia (the parts of the body near the heart, lying on either side just below the ribs); Repotia (the feast after a wedding); Rostra (a raised platform from which one speaks); Stativa (a military camp); Tesqua (wild, monstrous places); Justa (the funeral rites of the dead); Verenda (a man's private parts).

units.la: Quænam pluralem numerum variant?
units.tr: Which nouns vary in their plural forms?

units.la: Hic balteus, hæc balthea, <bl>ein gürtel</bl> <bl>mit spangen</bl>. Hic, hæc carbasus, hæc carbasa, <bl>leinwath/schiffsägel</bl>. Hic cetus, hæc cete, <bl>wallfisch</bl>. Hic jocus, hi joci, & hæc joca, <bl>schimpff</bl>. Hic locus, hi loci & hæc loca, <bl>ein ort/</bl> <bl>plaz</bl>. Hic sibilus, hi sibili & hæc sibila, <bl>ein pfeifung</bl>. Hic tartarus, hæc tartara, <bl>ein finster ort/ ob die Helle [?]</bl>. Hoc cœlum, hi cœli, <bl>der Himmel</bl>. Hoc fraenum, hæc fræna & hi freni, <bl>ein zaum/ oder das gebiß am zaum</bl>. Hoc porrum, hi porri, <bl>lauch</bl>. Hoc raftrum, hi raftri, <bl>ein rechen oder ege</bl>. Hoc jugerum, hæc jugera, jugeribus, <bl>ein feld zweyhundert und vierzig schuch lang/</bl> <bl>ein hundert und zwenzig breit</bl>. Hoc delicium, hæ deliciæ, <bl>wollust / kurzweil</bl>. Hoc epulum, <bl>ein bancket/</bl> hæ epulæ, <bl>allerley speise</bl>. Hoc balneum, <bl>ein eigen bad-</bl> <bl>stube/</bl> hæ balneæ, <bl>gemeine badstube</bl>.
units.tr: Balteus, balthea (a belt with clasps); Carbasus, carbasa (linen cloth, a ship's sail); Cetus, cete (a whale); Jocus, joci and joca (a joke); Locus, loci and loca (a place); Sibilus, sibili and sibila (a whistling); Tartarus, tartara (a dark place, or hell [?]); Coelum, coeli (heaven); Fraenum, fraena and freni (a bridle, or the bit of a bridle); Porrum, porri (leek); Rastrum, rastri (a rake or harrow); Jugerum, jugera, jugeribus (a field two hundred and forty feet long and one hundred and twenty feet wide); Delicium, deliciae (delight, pastime); Epulum (a banquet), epulae (all sorts of food); Balneum (a private bathroom), balneae (a public bathhouse).

units.la: Macte singularis numeri, & Macti pluralis numeri, <bl>fürtreffenlich</bl> / apud probatos authores sunt Nominativi, Accusativi & Vocativi Casus. Vide Calepinum. Quaedam duobus casibus usurpantur: ut, Tantidem, <bl>eben so thewr</bl>/ est Genitivi Casus: Tantundem, <bl>eben so viel</bl>/ est Accusativi casus.
units.tr: Macte in the singular and Macti in the plural (excellently) are, among approved authors, nominative, accusative and vocative forms. See Calepinus. Some words are used in two cases: Tantidem (just as dear) is the genitive case; Tantundem (just as much) is the accusative case.

units.la: Declina Ambo, allebend / & Duo, zween . N. Ambo, ambæ, ambo. Duo, duæ, duo. G. Amborū, ambarum, amboruū. Duorum, duarū, duorum. D. Ambobus, ambabus, ambobus. Duobus, duabus, duobus. A. Ambos, ambas, ambo. Duos, duas, duo. A. Ambobus, ambabꝰ, ambobus. Duobꝰ, duabus, duobus.
units.tr: Decline Ambo (both) and Duo (two). Nominative: both (masc., fem., neut.); two (masc., fem., neut.). Genitive: of both; of two. Dative: to both; to two. Accusative: both; two. Ablative: from both; from two.

units.la: Declina Adjectiva Anomala, quæ a Domino Philippo Melanchthone, & aliis, pronomina appellantur.
units.tr: Decline the anomalous adjectives, which Lord Philip Melanchthon and others call pronouns.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Ego, <bl>ich</bl>. Tu, <bl>du</bl>. G. Mei vel mis, <bl>meiner</bl>. Tui vel tis, <bl>deiner</bl>. Sui, <bl>seiner</bl>. D. Mihi, <bl>mir</bl>. Tibi, <bl>dir</bl>. Sibi, <bl>ihm</bl>. A. Me, <bl>mich</bl>. Te, <bl>dich</bl>. Se, <bl>sich</bl>. V. O tu, <bl>O du</bl>. A. A me, <bl>von mir</bl>. A te, <bl>von dir</bl>. A se, <bl>von sich</bl>.
units.tr: Nom. I (ich). Thou (du). Gen. Of me, mine (meiner). Of thee, thine (deiner). Of himself, of herself, his (seiner). Dat. To me (mir). To thee (dir). To himself, to him (ihm). Acc. Me (mich). Thee (dich). Himself (sich). Voc. O thou (O du). Abl. From me (von mir). From thee (von dir). From himself (von sich).

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. Nos, <bl>wir</bl>. Vos, <bl>ihr</bl>. G. Nostrum vel nostri, <bl>vnser</bl>. Vestrum vel vestri, <bl>ewer</bl>. Sui, <bl>ihrer</bl>. D. Nobis, <bl>vns</bl>. Vobis, <bl>euch</bl>. Sibi, <bl>ihnen</bl>. A. Nos, <bl>vns</bl>. Vos, <bl>euch</bl>. Se, <bl>sich</bl>. V. O vos, <bl>O ihr</bl>. A. a nobis, <bl>von vns</bl> / a vobis, <bl>von euch</bl>. a se, <bl>von sich</bl>.
units.tr: Nom. We (wir). You (ihr). Gen. Of us, our (unser). Of you, your (euer). Of them, their (ihrer). Dat. To us, us (uns). To you, you (euch). To them (ihnen). Acc. Us (uns). You (euch). Themselves (sich). Voc. O you (O ihr). Abl. From us (von uns); from you (von euch); from themselves (von sich).

units.la: Ex hisce tribus oriuntur regularia: Meus, mea, meū, <bl>mein</bl>. Tuus, tua, tuum, <bl>dein</bl>. Noster, nostra, noftrū, <bl>vn-</bl> <bl>ser</bl>. Vester, vestra, vestrū, <bl>ewer</bl>. Hic & hæc nostras, nostratis, hoc nostrate, <bl>vnsers landes/glaubens/oder</bl> <bl>anhags</bl>. Hic & hæc vestras, vestratis, hoc vestrate, <bl>ewers</bl> <bl>landes/glaubens/oder anhags</bl>. Suus, sua, suum, <bl>sein</bl>.
units.tr: From these three come the regular forms: my, mine (mein); thy, thine (dein); our (unser); your (euer). Of our country, faith or sect (vnsers landes/glaubens/oder anhangs), and likewise of your country, faith or sect (ewers landes/glaubens/oder anhangs). His, her own (sein).

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Hic, hæc, hoc, <bl>der/die/das</bl>. G. Hujus, <bl>des/der/des</bl>. <bl>Des.</bl> D. Huic,<bl>dem/der/dem.</bl> A. Hunc,hanc,hoc,<bl>den/</bl> <bl>die/das.</bl>A.Ab hoc,hac,hoc,<bl>von dem/der/dem.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. This, masculine, feminine and neuter (der/die/das). Gen. Of this (des/der/des). Dat. To this (dem/der/dem). Acc. This (den/die/das). Abl. From this (von dem/der/dem).

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. Hi, hæ, hæc, <bl>die/ in allem geschlecht.</bl> G.Horum, harum,horum,<bl>derer.</bl> D.His,<bl>denen.</bl> A. Hos,has,hæc, <bl>die.</bl> A.Ab his,<bl>von denen.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. These, of every gender (die). Gen. Of these (derer). Dat. To these (denen). Acc. These (die). Abl. From these (von denen).

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Is, <bl>der oder er.</bl> Ea,<bl>die oder sie.</bl> Id,<bl>das.</bl> G.Ejus, <bl>des oder sein/der/des.</bl> D.Ei, <bl>dem oder im/der/dem.</bl> A. Eum,<bl>den oder jn.</bl> Eam,<bl>die oder sie.</bl> Id,<bl>das.</bl> A.Ab eo, <bl>von dem/oder jm.</bl> Ab ea,<bl>von der oder jr.</bl> Ab eo,<bl>von dem.</bl>
units.tr: Nominative: "the" or "he" (masculine); "the" or "she" (feminine); "that" or "the" (neuter). Genitive: "of that," "his," or "of the" (masculine, feminine and neuter alike). Dative: "to the," "in the," or "to him" (masculine); "to the" or "to her" (feminine); "to the" (neuter). Accusative: "the" or "him" (masculine); "the" or "her" (feminine); "that" or "the" (neuter). Ablative: "from him" or "from one" (masculine); "from her" (feminine); "from it" (neuter).

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N.Ei,vel ii,eæ,ea,<bl>die oder sie.</bl> G.Eorum,earum,eorum,<bl>derer.</bl> D.Eis vel iis,<bl>denen.</bl> A.Eos,eas,ea,<bl>die oder</bl> <bl>sie.</bl> A.Ab eis vel iis,<bl>von denen.</bl> Sic idem,eadem,idem, ejuldem,&c.
units.tr: Nom. They (die oder sie). Gen. Of them (derer). Dat. To them (denen). Acc. Them (die oder sie). Abl. From them (von denen). In the same way the word for "the same" declines.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. Quis,<bl>wer/</bl> qui,<bl>welcher.</bl> Quæ vel qua,<bl>welche/</bl> quid,<bl>was/</bl>.quod, <bl>welches.</bl> G. Cujus,<bl>welches oder wes/welcher/welches.</bl> D. Cui, <bl>welchem oder wem/welcher/welchem.</bl> A. Quem, <bl>welchen oder wen/quâ,</bl> <bl>welche</bl> / quid ,<bl>was/</bl> quod <bl>welches.</bl> A.aquo,<bl>von welchem oder wem</bl> / à qua , <bl>von welcher</bl> / a quo,<bl>von welchem.</bl> Aliquando Qui in omni genere.
units.tr: Nominative: "who" (masculine); "which" (masculine, as in qui, "which"); "which" or "what" (feminine); "what" (neuter, quid); "which" (neuter, quod). Genitive: "whose" or "of which" (masculine, feminine and neuter alike). Dative: "to which" or "to whom" (masculine); "to which" (feminine); "to which" (neuter). Accusative: "which" or "whom" (masculine); "which" or "by which" (feminine); "what" (neuter, quid); "which" (neuter, quod). Ablative: "from which" or "from whom" (masculine); "from which" (feminine); "from which" (neuter). Sometimes qui serves in every gender.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N Qui,quæ,quæ vel qua,welche. G. Quorum,quarum,quorum,welcher. D. Queis vel quibus, welche. A. Quos,quas, quæ vel qua,welche. A queis vel quibus,von welchen. Hinc nascuntur regularia: Cujus, cuja,cujum. welches/ cujas,cujatis, welches landes/ oder glaubens/oder anhangs. Quot sunt Adjectiva,quæ Genitivum singularem in us,Dativum in i formant? Tredecim : Alius,alia,aliud,ein anderer/alius,alij, Alter,altera,alterum,einer von zweyen / alterius, alteri. Sic iste, ista, istud, der/die/das. Ille, illa,illud. Ipse,ipsa,ipsum. Ullus,ulla,ullum,etwar einer. Nullus,nulla, nullum,keiner. Uter, utra, utrum, welcher von zweyen. Uterque,utraque,utrumque, der eine und der ander. Neuter,neutra,neutrum, keiner von zweyen. Solus,sola,solum,allein/verlassen. Totus,tota,totum, ganz. Unus,una,unum, einer. Quod licet singulare sit: in plurali tamen usurpatur,si quando conjungitur nominibus pluralis numeri tantùm: ut, unæ nuptiæ,ein hochzeit. Unis mœnibus urbs cincta, mit ei-ner ringmawer ist die statt vmbgeben.
units.tr: Nom. Which (welche). Gen. Of which (welcher). Dat. To which (welche). Acc. Which (welche). Abl. From which (von welchen). From these come the regular forms: whose (welches); of whose country, faith or sect (welches landes oder glaubens oder anhangs). How many adjectives form the genitive singular in -us and the dative in -i? Thirteen: another (ein anderer), the other of two (einer von zweyen), that (der/die/das), that one, the same, any one (etwar einer), no one (keiner), which of two (welcher von zweyen), each of two (der eine und der ander), neither of two (keiner von zweyen), alone (allein, verlassen), whole (ganz), one (einer). Although these are singular, they are used in the plural when they are joined only to nouns of the plural number, as in "one wedding" (ein hochzeit) and "a city surrounded by one wall" (mit einer ringmawer ist die statt vmbgeben).

units.la: Adjectiva Demonstrativa sunt: Ego,Tu,Hic,&Ille.
units.tr: The demonstrative adjectives are: I, thou, this, and that.

units.la: Relativa: Is,Qui, Ipse. Ille alias demonstrat alias remotius refert: ut, ignavia corpus hebetat,labor firmat: illa maturam senectutem, hic longam adolescentiam reddit.
units.tr: The relatives are: he, who, the same. That one points to one thing and refers to another more remotely, as: idleness dulls the body, labour strengthens it; the former brings a ripe old age, the latter a long youth.

units.la: Reciproca sunt: Sui & Suus.Sic dicta,quod ad eandem personam, quæ præcedit, se reflectant. Rogare jussit hera, si se ames, ut ad se venias,non ad eam. Nam sic alia, quàm hera, intelligeretur. Deus servat hominem propter suam bonitatem: Et non servat hominem propter ejus bonitatem,id est,hominis.
units.tr: The reflexives are: self and his own. They are so called because they refer back to the same person who precedes. The mistress ordered that, if you love yourself, you come to yourself and not to her, for otherwise it would be understood as someone other than the mistress. God preserves man for his own goodness; and he does not preserve man for his goodness, that is, the man's.

units.la: Interrogativa sunt: Quis, cujus, cuja, cujum, & cujas,cujatis,uter utrius.
units.tr: The interrogatives are: who, whose, of which, and whose country, and which of two.

units.la: Possessiva: Meus,Tuus,Noster,& Vester.
units.tr: The possessives are: my, thy, our, and your.

units.la: Gentilia: Nostras & Vestras, imparisyllabæ Declinationis.
units.tr: The gentile (national) adjectives are: ours and yours, of the imparisyllabic declension.

units.la: Quibusdam adjectivis Pronominalibus hæ voces: Met,te,ce,& pte,majoris significantiæ gratia adduntur: ut,Egomet,meimet,mihimet,&c. Tutemet, tuimet,tibimet,&c. Tute,tete. Hicce, hæcce,hocce, hujusce, hisce, hosce, hasce. Meapte, tuapte, suapte, nostrapte,vestrapte.
units.tr: To certain pronominal adjectives these particles are added for greater emphasis: -met, -te, -ce and -pte. For example: I myself, of myself, to myself, and so on; thou thyself, of thyself, to thyself, and so on; thou thyself (tute), thou thyself (tete). This one here, this here, this one here, of this one here, these here, these ones here, these ones here. Of my own, of thy own, of his own, of our own, of your own.

units.la: Ec & Ali,Adjectivo Quis, præponitur: Nam,quis, que,quam,piam,postponuntur. Qui, habet a tergo, dam,vis,cunq;, & liber.
units.tr: Ec and Ali are placed before the adjective quis. Nam, quis, que, quam and piam are placed after it. Qui takes after it -dam, -vis, -cunque and -libet.

units.la: Quaenam Adjectiva appellantur a Gram- maticis Cardinalia?
units.tr: What adjectives are called cardinal by the grammarians?

units.la: Unus, duo, tres, quatuor, quinq;, sex, septem, octo, novem, decem, &c. quae supra enumeravimus.
units.tr: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, and so on, which we listed above.

units.la: Quaenam appellantur ordinalia?
units.tr: Which are called ordinal?

units.la: Primus, <bl>der erst</bl>. Secundus, <bl>der ander</bl>. Tertius, <bl>der</bl> <bl>dritte</bl>. Quartus, <bl>der vierte</bl>. Quintus, <bl>der fünffte</bl>. Sextus, <bl>der sechste</bl>. Septimus, <bl>der siebende</bl>. Octavus, <bl>der</bl> <bl>achte</bl>. Nonus, <bl>der neunte</bl>. Decimus, <bl>der zehende</bl>. Undecimus. Duodecimus. Decimustertius vel tredecimus. Decimusquartus. Decimusquintus. Decimussextus. Decimusseptimus. Decimusoctavus, vel duodevicesimus. Decimusnonus, vel undevicesimus. Vigesimus vel vicesimus, <bl>der zwentzigste</bl>. Vicesimusprimus, secundus: ac deinceps. Trigesimus vel tricesimꝰ. Quadragesimus. Quinquagesimus. Sexagesimus. Septuagesimus. Octogesimus. Nonagesimus. Centesimus, <bl>der hūderste</bl>. Ducentesimus, <bl>der zweihundertste</bl>. Trecentesimus, <bl>der drenhunderste</bl>. Quadringentesimus. Quingentesimus. Sexcentesimus. Septingentesimus. Octingentesimus. Noningentesimus. Millesimus, <bl>der tausigeste</bl>.
units.tr: First (der erst). Second (der ander). Third (der dritte). Fourth (der vierte). Fifth (der fünffte). Sixth (der sechste). Seventh (der siebende). Eighth (der achte). Ninth (der neunte). Tenth (der zehende). Eleventh. Twelfth. Thirteenth, or tenth-third. Fourteenth. Fifteenth. Sixteenth. Seventeenth. Eighteenth, or the alternative form. Nineteenth, or the alternative form. Twentieth (der zwentzigste). Twenty-first, twenty-second, and so on. Thirtieth. Fortieth. Fiftieth. Sixtieth. Seventieth. Eightieth. Ninetieth. Hundredth (der hunderste). Two hundredth (der zweihundertste). Three hundredth (der drenhunderste). Four hundredth. Five hundredth. Six hundredth. Seven hundredth. Eight hundredth. Nine hundredth. Thousandth (der tausigeste).

units.la: Quaenam appellantur Distributiva?
units.tr: What are called Distributives?

units.la: <bl>Singuli</bl>, lae, la, <bl>jeder besonder</bl>. Bini, nae, na, <bl>je zween</bl>. Terni, <bl>je dreyn</bl>. Quaterni. Quini. Seni. Septeni. Octoni. Noveni, Deni. Undeni. Duodeni. Ternideni. Quaternideni. Quindeni. Senideni. Septenideni. Octonideni. Novenideni. Viceni vel vigeni, <bl>je zwentzig</bl>. Triceni vel trigeni. Quadrageni. Quinquageni. Sexageni. Septuageni. Octogeni. Nonageni. Centeni. Ducenteni vel duceni. Trecenteni vel treceni. Quadringenteni vel quadrigeni. Quingenteni vel quingeni. Sexcenteni vel fexceni. Septingenteni vel septingeni. Octingenteni vel octingeni. Noningenteni vel noningeni.Milleni.
units.tr: Single, each one separately. Double, two each. Triple, three each. Quadruple, four each. Five each. Six each. Seven each. Eight each. Nine each. Ten each. Eleven each. Twelve each. Thirteen each. Fourteen each. Fifteen each. Sixteen each. Seventeen each. Eighteen each. Nineteen each. Twenty each, or twenty each. Thirty each, or thirty each. Forty each. Fifty each. Sixty each. Seventy each. Eighty each. Ninety each. A hundred each. Two hundred each, or two hundred each. Three hundred each, or three hundred each. Four hundred each, or four hundred each. Five hundred each, or five hundred each. Six hundred each, or six hundred each. Seven hundred each, or seven hundred each. Eight hundred each, or eight hundred each. Nine hundred each, or nine hundred each. A thousand each.

units.la: Quando dicimus: Militibus sunt ducenti Taleri dati, significatur,tota cohorte non nisi ducentos Taleros accepisse. Quado vero dicimus: Militibus sunt ducenteni Taleri dati, tum significatur singulos milites ducentos Taleros accepisse. Interdum distributiva idem significare,quod Cardinalia,usus docet.
units.tr: When we say: "Two hundred thalers were given to the soldiers," it means that the whole company received only two hundred thalers. When, however, we say: "Two hundred thalers each were given to the soldiers," then it means that each soldier received two hundred thalers. Usage shows that sometimes distributives mean the same as cardinals.

units.la: Quaenam appellantur multiplicativa?
units.tr: What are called Multiplicatives?

units.la: Simplus, einfacht. Duplus, zweyfacht. Triplus, dreyfacht. Quadruplus. Quintuplus. Sextuplus. Septuplus. Octuplus. Noncuplus. Centuplus, hundertfacht. Millecuplus, tausentfacht.
units.tr: Simple, single-fold. Double, twofold. Triple, threefold. Quadruple, fourfold. Quintuple, fivefold. Sextuple, sixfold. Septuple, sevenfold. Octuple, eightfold. Nonuple, ninefold. Decuple, tenfold. Centuple, hundredfold. Millecuple, thousandfold.

units.la: Simplex, einfaltig. Duplex, zweyfaltig. Triplex, dreyfaltig. Quadruplex. Quintuplex vel quincuplex. Sexduplex. Septuplex. Octuplex. Noncuplex. Decuplex. Centuplex, hunderfaltig. Millecuplex, tausendfaltig. Haec in plex sunt Declinationis imparisyllabae.
units.tr: Simple, single-ply. Double, two-ply. Triple, three-ply. Quadruple, four-ply. Quintuple or quincuple, five-ply. Sexduple, six-ply. Septuple, seven-ply. Octuple, eight-ply. Nonuple, nine-ply. Decuple, ten-ply. Centuple, hundred-ply. Millecuple, thousand-ply. These are the imparisyllabic nouns of the declension.

units.la: Quid est Tertia Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the Third Declension?

units.la: Tertia Declinatio est, cujus Nominativus singularis definit in er,vel es,vel is, vel e, Genitivus Nominativo parisyllabus in is, Dativus in i. Si Tertia Declinatio ob imparisyllabum Dativum pluralem imparisyllaba appellanda est: sequitur praecedentes Declinationes etiam ob imparisyllabum Genitivum pluralem esse imparisyllabas appellandas. Atqui hae imparisyllabae non vocantur. Ergo nec illa.
units.tr: The Third Declension is that whose nominative singular ends in -er, -es, -is or -e, whose genitive has the same number of syllables as the nominative and ends in -is, and whose dative ends in -i. If the Third Declension is to be called imparisyllabic because of its dative plural, it follows that the preceding declensions must also be called imparisyllabic because of their genitive plural. But these are not called imparisyllabic. Therefore neither is that one.

units.la: Cedo paradigmata Tertiae Declinationis.
units.tr: Give me the paradigms of the Third Declension.

units.la: Singularis Numerus. N. Hic venter, der bauch/ Haec vulpes, der fuchs. G. Hujus ventris, des bauchs/ Vulpis, des fuchses. D. Huic ventri, dem bauch/ Vulpi, dem fuchse. A. Hunc vetrem, den bauch/ Hanc vulpem, den fuchs. V. O venter, O bauch/ O Vulpes, O fuchs. A. Ab hoc ventre, von dem bauch/ ab hac vulpe, von dem fuchs.
units.tr: Singular number. Nominative: this belly, the belly / this fox, the fox. Genitive: of this belly, of the belly / of this fox, of the fox. Dative: to this belly, to the belly / to this fox, to the fox. Accusative: this belly, the belly / this fox, the fox. Vocative: O belly, O belly / O fox, O fox. Ablative: from this belly, from the belly / from this fox, from the fox.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.

units.la: N. Hi ventres, die bauch/ Hæ vulpes, die fuchse. G. Horū ventriū, der bäuche/ Harū vulpiū, der fuchse. D. His vetribus, den bäuchen/ His vulpibus, den fuchsen. A. Hos ventres, die bäuche/ Has vulpes, die fuchse. V. O ventres, O ihr bäuche/ O vulpes, O ihr fuchse. A. Ab his ventribus, von den bäuchen / Ab his vulpibus, von den fuchsen.
units.tr: Nominative: these bellies, the bellies / these foxes, the foxes. Genitive: of these bellies, of the bellies / of these foxes, of the foxes. Dative: to these bellies, to the bellies / to these foxes, to the foxes. Accusative: these bellies, the bellies / these foxes, the foxes. Vocative: O bellies, O you bellies / O foxes, O you foxes. Ablative: from these bellies, from the bellies / from these foxes, from the foxes.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular number.

units.la: N. Hoc mantile, ein handzwehel. G. Hujus mantilis, der handzwehel. D. Huic mantili, der handzwehel. A. Hoc mantile, die handzwehel. V. O mätile, O handzwehel. A. Ab hoc mantili, von der handzwehel.
units.tr: Nominative: this napkin, a hand towel. Genitive: of this napkin, of a hand towel. Dative: to this napkin, to a hand towel. Accusative: this napkin, a hand towel. Vocative: O napkin, O hand towel. Ablative: from this napkin, from a hand towel.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.

units.la: N. Hęc mantilia, die handzwehelen. G. Horum mantilium, der handzwehelen. D. His mätilibus, den handzwehelen. A. Hæc mantilia, die handzwehelen. V. O mantilia, O ihr handzwehelen. A. Ab his mantilibus, von den handzwehelen.
units.tr: Nominative: these napkins, hand towels. Genitive: of these napkins, of hand towels. Dative: to these napkins, to hand towels. Accusative: these napkins, hand towels. Vocative: O napkins, O you hand towels. Ablative: from these napkins, from hand towels.

units.la: Mille, Substantivum, singulari numero est indeclinabile & generis neutrius: plurali vero sic declinatur; Millia, milliū, millibus, millia. Amplustre vel aplustre, schiffgesterd[?]/in plurali aplustria & aplustra.
units.tr: Mille, used as a noun, is indeclinable in the singular and of neuter gender; in the plural it is declined thus: thousands, of thousands, to thousands, thousands, thousands, from thousands. Amplustre or aplustre, a ship's stern ornament; in the plural, aplustria and aplustra.

units.la: Quædam nomina primæ Declinationis sunt etiam tertiæ: ut, Achates, Achatę & Achatis, ein fluß/ Sicilię, ein edelgestein/ vnnd ein gesell Aeneæ. Orestes, stæ & stis, ein sohn des Obersten Kriegshauptmanns vor Troja/ der seine Mutter Clytemnestrā getödet hat. Polites, tæ, & tis, ein sohn Priami des Königs zu Troja / von der Hecuba geboren / den Pyrrhus für dem angesicht des Vatters vmbgebracht hat. Thucydides, dæ & dis, ein Griechischer Historien schreiber von Athen bürtig.
units.tr: Some nouns of the First Declension are also of the Third: for example, Achates, Achatae and Achatis, a river; Sicilia, a precious stone; and a companion of Aeneas. Orestes, -stae and -stis, a son of the Greek commander-in-chief before Troy, who killed his mother Clytemnestra. Polites, -tae and -tis, a son of King Priam of Troy, born of Hecuba, whom Pyrrhus killed before his father's eyes. Thucydides, -dae and -dis, a Greek historian, a native of Athens.

units.la: Quædam nomina Tertiæ Declinationis in is, trifariam formant Genitivum singularem: ut, Genesis, hujus Genesis, Genesios & Genesceos, <bl>gebärung</bl> oder <bl>geburt</bl>. Dioœcesis, hujus dioœcesis, dioœcesios,& dioœcescos, <bl>herrschung</bl>.
units.tr: Some nouns of the Third Declension in -is form the genitive singular in three ways: Genesis, of this genesis, Genesios and Genesceos, birth or generation. Dioecesis, of this dioecesis, dioecesios and dioecescos, rule or government.

units.la: Cujus generis sunt nomina Tertiæ De- clinationis?
units.tr: What genders are the nouns of the Third Declension?

units.la: Nomina tertiæ Declinationis in er sunt masculini generis, in es vel is fœminini, in e neutrius: ut, Hic pater, hujus patris, <bl>ein Vatter</bl>. Hic imber, hujus imbris, <bl>ein platzregen</bl>. Hæc sepes, hujus sepis, <bl>ein zaun</bl>. Hæc carnis olim, hodie caro, hujus carnis, <bl>fleisch</bl>. Hęc strigilis, per Apocopen strigil, hujus strigilis, <bl>ein roß</bl> <bl>kamm[?]</bl>. Hoc mare, maris, <bl>das Meer</bl>. Hoc cubile, cubilis, <bl>ein beth oder schlaffkammer[?]</bl>. In i exeuntia Substantiva sunt neutra & indeclinabilia: ut, hoc gummi, <bl>bech/so</bl> <bl>auß den beumen fleußt</bl>. Hoc sinapi, <bl>jenff[?]</bl>. At gummis & sinapis fœminina sunt.
units.tr: Nouns of the Third Declension in -er are masculine, those in -es or -is feminine, and those in -e neuter; for example: this father, of this father, a father (masculine). This rain shower, of this rain shower, a downpour (masculine). This hedge, of this hedge, a fence (feminine). This flesh, formerly carnis, now caro, of this flesh, flesh (feminine). This currycomb, by apocope strigil, of this currycomb, a horse's comb (feminine). This sea, of this sea (neuter). This bed, of this bed, a bed or bedchamber (neuter). Nouns ending in -i are neuter and indeclinable, for example: this gum, resin that flows from trees; this mustard, mustard. But gum and mustard are feminine.

units.la: Quænam excipiuntur?
units.tr: Which are the exceptions?

units.la: Primo in er quædam: ut, hæc mater, <bl>ein Mutter</bl>. Hic & hæc linter, <bl>ein außgehölter baum / so man an</bl> <bl>statt eins schiffleins braucht</bl>.
units.tr: First, some in -er: this mother (feminine), a mother. Masculine and feminine alike: linter, a hollowed-out tree used in place of a small boat.

units.la: Deinde in es,& is quædam masculina: ut, hi annales, annalium, <bl>Chronicken / darin allerley jargeschicht</bl> <bl>fürtzlich verzeichnet werden</bl>. Hi antes, antium, <bl>stein</bl> <bl>oder seulen an den gebäwen / die herfür gehen</bl>. Hic Assis, & per Apocopen As, cum Compositis, <bl>das in</bl> <bl>zwölff theil mag zertheilet werden</bl>. Acinacis, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>schwerdt der Persier</bl>. Aqualis, <bl>ein hand oder wasser</bl> <bl>becken</bl>. Axis, <bl>ein achs am wagen / die lini mitten durch</bl> <bl>die welt</bl>. Amnis, <bl>ein fluß</bl>. Cenchris, <bl>ein geflecktes</bl> <bl>schlag</bl>. Crinis, <bl>haar</bl>. Colis, <bl>ein junger zweig am wein</bl> <bl>räben oder traute</bl>. Collis, <bl>ein niderberg/hügel</bl>. Callis, <bl>ein wolgebaneter weg</bl>. Cassis, <bl>ein Jäger garn</bl>. Caulis, ein krautstengel. Coraxis, ein berg vnd fluß in Asia. Ensis, ein schwerdt. Fascis,ein bürde holtzes oder anderer dinge/ ein büschlein ruten vmb ein Axt gebunden / so man vor zeiten zu Rom den Bürgern meistern vortrug/ ein gewalt oder herligkeit. Follis, ein blasbalg. Fustis,ein stäcken. Ignis,fewr. Lemures, lemurum,nacht gespenst. Manes,manium,der verstor benen seelen oder geister. Majalis,ein verschnitten schwein. Mensis,ein Monat. Mugilis, der fisch eines grossen kopffs. Natalis,ein geburts tag. Natales,natalium, stam oder geschlechte. Orbis, ein kreiß. Panis, brot. Pantices, seiste des bauches oder durchlauff. Penis,ein schwanz. Penates, penatium & penatum, die Hausgötter. Piscis,ein fisch. Postis,thürpfost. Pugillares,pugillarium,schreibtäfelein. Rivalis,ein mitbuler. Torris, ein fewriger brand. Unguis, ein nagel an den fingern. Unicornis,ein Einhorn. Vectis, ein stang/ ein rigel so man für die thür stost. Vermis, ein wurm. Verres, ein unverschnitten schwein. Vates,ein weissager. Hic Jovis olim,hodie Jupiter,hujus Jovis.
units.tr: Next, some masculine nouns in -es and -is: annales (annals), chronicles in which all kinds of histories are briefly recorded. Antes, stones or pillars on buildings that project forward. Assis, which by apocope becomes As in compounds: a whole that may be divided into twelve parts. Acinaces, a Persian sword. Aqualis, a hand basin or water basin. Axis, the axle of a wagon; the line running through the middle of the world. Amnis, a river. Cenchris, a spotted snake. Crinis, hair. Colis, a young shoot on a vine or a grapevine tendril. Collis, a low hill. Callis, a well-made path. Cassis, a hunter's net. Caulis, the stalk of a cabbage. Coraxis, a mountain and river in Asia. Ensis, a sword. Fascis, a bundle of sticks or other things, a bunch of rods bound around an axe, which in former times was carried before the magistrates at Rome; also power or dignity. Follis, a bellows. Fustis, a stick. Ignis, fire. Lemures, of lemures, night spirits. Manes, of manes, the souls or spirits of the departed. Majalis, a castrated pig. Mensis, a month. Mugilis, a fish with a large head. Natalis, a birthday. Natales, of natales, stock or lineage. Orbis, a circle. Panis, bread. Pantices, the colic or diarrhoea of the bowels. Penis, a tail. Penates, the household gods. Piscis, a fish. Postis, a doorpost. Pugillares, writing tablets. Rivalis, a rival. Torris, a burning brand. Unguis, a fingernail. Unicornis, a unicorn. Vectis, a pole or bar which is thrust across a door. Vermis, a worm. Verres, an uncastrated pig. Vates, a seer. Formerly this was written Jovis as the nominative; today it is Jupiter, with genitive Jovis.

units.la: Neutrum est: Panaces hujus panacis,ein kraut das alle kranckheiten soll heilen.
units.tr: Neuter: panaces, of panacis, a herb which is said to cure all diseases.

units.la: Communia sunt: Anguis, ein wasserschlang. Canalis ,ein außgehölt holtz/ darin man wasser leitet. Canis, ein hund. Civis, ein Bürger. Corbis, ein geflochtë korb. Clunis,ein hinderbug. Felis,ein katz. Finis, ein end. Funis,ein seyl oder schnur. Hostis, ein feind. Plumbes,ein bolzstauff. Retis,ein netz. Sentis,ein dorn. Torques vel torquis,ein halßkette oder band. Vepres, veprium,dornhecken.
units.tr: Common gender: anguis, a water snake. Canalis, a hollowed-out piece of wood through which water is led. Canis, a dog. Civis, a citizen. Corbis, a woven basket. Clunis, the buttocks. Felis, a cat. Finis, an end. Funis, a rope or cord. Hostis, an enemy. Plumbes, a lead weight. Retis, a net. Sentis, a thorn. Torques or torquis, a neck-chain or band. Vepres, of veprium, thorn hedges.

units.la: Quæ habent in Accusativo singulari im tantum?
units.tr: Which have im only in the accusative singular?

units.la: Aqualis,ein handbecken. Araris,das wasser Ar.Buris, die pflugstertz. Charybdis, ein wirbel im Meer. Pelvis,<bl>ein fußbecken</bl>. Magudaris vel magydaris,<bl>meisterwurz</bl>. Mephitis,<bl>ein starcker gestanck auß der er-</bl> <bl>den oder dem wasser</bl>. Ravis,<bl>h-</bl> <bl>enserkeit</bl>[?]. Sitis,<bl>der durst</bl>. Tussis,<bl>der husten</bl>[?]. Et Propria plæraq;: ut, Fabaris,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>fluß</bl>. Tyberis,<bl>ein fluß/fleußt durch Rom</bl>. Leucaspis,<bl>einer</bl> <bl>von den gejellt Aeneæ</bl>[?]. Opis,<bl>eine wassergöttin</bl>.
units.tr: Aqualis, a hand basin. Araris, the river Arar. Buris, the handle of a plough. Charybdis, a whirlpool in the sea. Pelvis, a foot basin. Magudaris or magydaris, masterwort. Mephitis, a strong stench rising from the earth or water. Ravis, hoarseness [?]. Sitis, thirst. Tussis, a cough [?]. And most proper names, for example: Fabaris, a river. Tyberis, a river which flows through Rome. Leucaspis, one of Aeneas's companions [?]. Opis, a water goddess.

units.la: Græca sæpe pro im capiunt in: ut, Syrtis,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>gefärlich ort im Meer</bl>/pro Syrtim,habet Syrtin.
units.tr: Greek words often take im in the accusative: Syrtis, a dangerous place in the sea; for the accusative Syrtim, the form Syrtin is also found.

units.la: Febris,<bl>das kalte vnd warme wehe</bl>. Navis,<bl>ein schiff</bl>. Puppis,<bl>das hinderteil des schiffs</bl>. Restis,<bl>ein seil</bl> <bl>oder strick</bl>. Securis,<bl>ein Axt</bl>. Turris,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>thurn/em</bl> vel im habent.
units.tr: Febris, the fever that alternates cold and heat. Navis, a ship. Puppis, the stern of a ship. Restis, a rope or cord. Securis, an axe. Turris, a tower; they have either em or im.

units.la: Quænam habent in Ablativo singulari i tantum?
units.tr: Which have i only in the ablative singular?

units.la: Primò, Adjectiva in er, aut is, quorum neutra in e desinunt: ut, Alacer, alacris, alacre, ab hoc alacri. Dulcis,dulce,ab hoc dulci.
units.tr: First, adjectives in -er or -is whose neuters end in e: alacer, alacris, alacre; ablative alacri. Dulcis, dulce; ablative dulci.

units.la: Secundò,Mensium nomina in er,aut is: ut,September,Septembri,<bl>im Herbstmonat</bl>. October,Octobri, <bl>im Weinmonat</bl>. November,Novembri,<bl>im Winter-</bl> <bl>monat</bl>. December,Decembri,<bl>im Christmonat</bl>. Aprilis, Aprili,<bl>im Aprilmonat</bl>[?]. Quintilis,Quintili,<bl>im</bl> <bl>Hornmonat</bl>. Sextilis,Sextili,<bl>im Augstmonat</bl>.
units.tr: Second, the names of months in -er or -is: September, in the autumn month. October, in the wine month. November, in the winter month. December, in the Christmas month. Aprilis, in the month of April. Quintilis, in the month of Horn [July]. Sextilis, in the month of August.

units.la: Tertiò, quæ Accusatiuum singularem in im,vel in tantum formant: ut, hunc Aqualim, ab hoc Aquali. Hanc Neapolin,hac Neapoli,<bl>von der Newstatt</bl>. Canalis,Mugilis,Natalis,Rivalis,Strigilis,habent etiam i tantum in Ablativo.
units.tr: Third, those which form the accusative singular in -im or in -em only: the accusative singular is aqualim, and the ablative is aquali. Neapolis: the accusative is Neapolin, and the ablative Neapoli, from the new city. Canalis, mugilis, natalis, rivalis, and strigilis also have only i in the ablative.

units.la: Anguis, Febris, Ignis, Imber,Navis,Puppis,Restis, Securis,Turris,Unguis,Vectis,habent e vel i.
units.tr: Anguis, febris, ignis, imber, navis, puppis, restis, securis, turris, unguis, and vectis have either e or i.

units.la: Quomodo definit Genitivus pluralis?
units.tr: How does the genitive plural end?

units.la: In ium: ut, Linter,lintrium. Collis,collium. Mensis,mensium. Auris,aurium. Excipe, Vates,vatum. Juvenis,juvenum. Canis,canum. Panis,panum. Volu-cris, eris,volucrum. Strigilis,strigilum. Mugilis,mugilu. Pater,patrum. Mater,matrum. Frater,fratrum. Sedes, <bl>ein stul/ sedium</bl> & sedum. Apes,<bl>ein Imme/</bl> apium,& apum. Vsus spectandus.
units.tr: In -ium: linter, of linters; collis, of hills; mensis, of months; auris, of ears. Exception: vates, of seers. Juvenis, of young men. Canis, of dogs. Panis, of loaves. Volucris, of birds. Strigilis, of scrapers. Mugilis, of mullets. Pater, of fathers. Mater, of mothers. Frater, of brothers. Sedes, a seat: genitive plural sedium and sedum. Apes, a bee: apium and apum. Usage must be observed.

units.la: Festorum nomina ium & orum habent: ut, Bacchanalia, <bl>die Faßnacht/</bl> bacchanalium & bacchanaliorum. Sic sponsalia, <bl>versprechung der Ehe zwischen</bl> <bl>Mann vnd Weib/</bl> sponsalium & sponsaliorum. Ancile, <bl>ein kleines rundes schildlin /</bl> ancilii & anciliorum.
units.tr: The names of feasts have -ium and -orum: bacchanalia, the carnival: bacchanalium and bacchanaliorum. So also sponsalia, the betrothal, a promise of marriage between a man and a woman: sponsalium and sponsaliorum. Ancile, a small round shield: ancilii and anciliorum.

units.la: Quænam sunt singularis numeri tantum?
units.tr: Which nouns are singular only?

units.la: Bilis,<bl>gall/ zorn.</bl> Fames,<bl>hunger/ thewerzeit.</bl> Indoles,<bl>ein anzeigung zukünfftiger frombkeit.</bl> Pestis,<bl>die</bl> <bl>Pestilenz.</bl> Proles,<bl>ein junge zucht.</bl> Pubes, <bl>haar an der</bl> <bl>scham.</bl> Soboles,<bl>heranwachsende kinder/</bl> <bl>fasel.</bl> Sitis, <bl>durst.</bl> Tabes,<bl>ein außdörrende sucht.</bl> Tussis,<bl>der hust.</bl> Sic gausape,<bl>ein winterdecke mit großen löcken/</bl> & caepe,<bl>zottel/ zipfeln</bl>/neutra indeclinabilia, sunt singularis numeri tantum.
units.tr: Bilis, bile, anger. Fames, hunger, famine. Indoles, a sign of future virtue. Pestis, the plague. Proles, young offspring. Pubes, the hair of the groin. Soboles, growing children, offspring. Sitis, thirst. Tabes, a wasting disease. Tussis, a cough. Likewise gausape, a winter blanket with large loops, and caepe, a tassel or fringe, are neuter indeclinables and singular only.

units.la: Quænam sunt pluralis numeri tantum?
units.tr: Which nouns are plural only?

units.la: Alpes,<bl>schneegebürg / so Welschland von Franckreich</bl> <bl>vnnd dem Schweitzerland absündert.</bl> Sordes, <bl>vnsauberkeit.</bl> Ilia,<bl>die Därm im bauch/ die seyten</bl> <bl>weiche.</bl> Paretalia,lium & orum,<bl>malzeit so man heit auff</bl> <bl>die begräbnis der verstorbenen freunden.</bl> Sponsalia, <bl>versprechung der Ehe.</bl> Palearia,<bl>die haute so de</bl> <bl>Ochsen an der kählen hangen.</bl> Moenia,<bl>ringmawren.</bl> Tempe,neutrum indeclinabile,<bl>lustige ort in Thessalia.</bl>
units.tr: Alpes, the snowy mountains which separate Italy from France and Switzerland. Sordes, filth. Ilia, the bowels in the belly, the flanks. Paretalia, -lium and -orum, a funeral feast held today for the burial of departed friends. Sponsalia, a betrothal. Palearia, the hide hanging from the necks of oxen. Moenia, city walls. Tempe, a neuter indeclinable, pleasant places in Thessaly.

units.la: Sequentia nomina quibusdam casibus declinantur: ut, ab hac Ambage, <bl>von der vmbschweiffenden</bl> <bl>red/</bl> hæ & has Ambages, his ambagibus. Hæ Grates, <bl>dancksagung/</bl> has & ô grates. Hæc Lues, <bl>ein</bl> <bl>gemeine sucht vnnd plage/</bl> hanc luem, à luc. Hæc Vis,<bl>gewalt/</bl> hanc vim, à vi, hæ vires, harum virium,viribus. Hanc vicem, <bl>streit / schaden / gefahr[?]</bl> ligkeit/ <bl>veränderung/ ampt oder statt/</bl> hac vice, ha vices,his vicibus,has vices.
units.tr: The following nouns are declined only in some cases: from this ambage, a roundabout way of speaking; plural ambages, with ablative ambagibus. Grates, thanksgiving: plural forms are these and grates for the vocative. Lues, a general disease and plague: accusative luem, ablative lue. Vis, force: accusative vim, ablative vi; plural vires, genitive virium, dative and ablative viribus. Vicis, a change, exchange, loss, danger, office, or place: ablative vice; plural vices, genitive vicum, dative and ablative vicibus, accusative vices.

units.tr: Decline Moses.

units.la: Quid est Declinatio Imparisyllaba?
units.tr: What is an imparisyllabic declension?

units.la: Declinatio imparisyllaba est, cujus Genitivus singularis imparisyllabus est Nominativo singulari: ut, Hujus Sacerdotis, hic Sacerdos. Hujus fructuis, hic fructus. Hujus speciei, hæc species.
units.tr: An imparisyllabic declension is one whose genitive singular has more syllables than its nominative singular, as: of this priest (hujus Sacerdotis), from hic Sacerdos; of this fruit (hujus fructuis), from hic fructus; of this kind (hujus speciei), from hæc species.

units.la: Cedò paradigmata Declinationis Impa- risyllabæ. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Give me the paradigms of the imparisyllabic declension. Singular number.

units.la: N. Hic Sacerdos, <bl>der Priester</bl>/ Hic fructus, <bl>die frucht.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. The priest (hic Sacerdos); the fruit (hic fructus).

units.la: G. Hujus Sacerdotis, <bl>des Priesters</bl> / Hujus fructus, olim fructuis, <bl>der frucht.</bl>
units.tr: Gen. Of the priest (hujus Sacerdotis); of the fruit (hujus fructus, formerly fructuis).

units.la: D. Huic Sacerdoti, <bl>dem Priester</bl> / Huic fructui, <bl>der frucht.</bl>
units.tr: Dat. To the priest (huic Sacerdoti); to the fruit (huic fructui).

units.la: A. Hunc Sacerdotem, <bl>den Priester</bl> / Hunc fructum, <bl>die frucht.</bl>
units.tr: Acc. The priest (hunc Sacerdotem); the fruit (hunc fructum).

units.la: V. O Sacerdos, <bl>O Priester</bl>/O fructus, <bl>O frucht</bl> / Græ-ca in s, abjiciunt s in Vocativo: ut, Pallas, ò Palla. Paris, ò Pari.
units.tr: Voc. O priest (O Sacerdos); O fruit (O fructus). Greek nouns in -s drop the s in the vocative, as: Pallas, O Palla; Paris, O Pari.

units.la: A. Ab hoc Sacerdote, <bl>von dem Priester</bl>/ Ab hoc fructu, <bl>von der frucht.</bl>
units.tr: Abl. From this priest (ab hoc Sacerdote); from this fruit (ab hoc fructu).

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.

units.la: N. Hi Sacerdotes, <bl>die Priester</bl>/ Hi fructus, <bl>die früchte.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. The priests (hi Sacerdotes); the fruits (hi fructus).

units.la: G. Horum sacerdotum, <bl>der Priester</bl> / Horum fructuum, <bl>der früchte.</bl> D. His Sacerdotibus, <bl>den Priestern</bl> / His fructibus, <bl>den früchten.</bl> A. Hos Sacerdotes, <bl>die Priester</bl> / Hos fructus, <bl>die</bl> <bl>früchte.</bl> V. O Sacerdotes, <bl>O ihr Priester</bl> / O fructus, <bl>O ihr früchte.</bl> A. Ab his Sacerdotibus, <bl>von den Priestern</bl> / Ab his fructibus, <bl>von den früchten.</bl> Sacerdos interdum est foeminini generis.
units.tr: Gen. Of the priests (horum sacerdotum); of the fruits (horum fructuum). Dat. To the priests (his Sacerdotibus); to the fruits (his fructibus). Acc. The priests (hos Sacerdotes); the fruits (hos fructus). Voc. O priests (O Sacerdotes); O fruits (O fructus). Abl. From the priests (ab his Sacerdotibus); from the fruits (ab his fructibus). Sacerdos is sometimes of the feminine gender.

units.la: Cujus generis sunt nomina Declinationis imparisyllabae?
units.tr: What genders do the nouns of the imparisyllabic declension have?

units.la: Nomina Declinationis imparisyllabae, quae declinantur sicut Sacerdos vel Fructus, sunt masculini generis: ut, Hic Augur, auguris, <bl>ein weissager auß den</bl> <bl>geberde oder gesang der vögel.</bl> Abax, Abacis, <bl>ein tisch</bl> <bl>oder banck / darauff man etwas leget / ein brett</bl> <bl>daran man allerlei geschirr heng / ein rechentisch.</bl> Adamas, Adamatis, <bl>ein hart edelgestein / der mit warmen</bl> <bl>bocks blut kan zerbrochen werden.</bl> Agger, Aggeris, <bl>ein zusammen hauffung des Erdreichs / ein waal /</bl> <bl>bollwerck.</bl> Amor, amoris, <bl>liebe.</bl> Apex, apicis, <bl>der ober-</bl> <bl>ste theil jedes dinges.</bl> Aquilex, aquilegis, <bl>ein brunnen</bl> <bl>sinder.</bl> Aries, arietis, <bl>ein schaffsbock / dem nicht außg-</bl> <bl>ehawen ist.</bl> Atlas, atlantis, <bl>ein hoher berg in Africa /</bl> <bl>oder ein Riß der den Himel auff den schultern tregt /</bl> <bl>nach der Poeten gedicht.</bl> Et reliqua in as, quae in Genitivo ntis habent. Attagen, attagenis, <bl>ein haselhun.</bl> Arctophylax, arctophylacis, <bl>das gestirn / so man nen-</bl> <bl>net den Wagenmann.</bl> Anthrax, anthracis, <bl>ein kolen /</bl> <bl>Sanct Antonius feur / ein edelgestein.</bl> Bidens, bidentis, <bl>ein haw mit zwen zänen.</bl> Bombyx, bombycis, <bl>ein seidenwurm.</bl> Caudex, caudicis, <bl>der stam eines</bl> <bl>baums.</bl> Chalybs, chalybis, <bl>stahel.</bl> Charax, characis, <bl>ein rähsteck oder schien.</bl> Calix, calicis, <bl>ein trinckge-</bl> schirʒ. Calyx, calycis, die haut einer frucht/ blumen deckel. Cardo, cardinis, ein eisenwerck vmb welches die thüren gewendet werden/ der thür angel. Cinis, cineris, asch. Cimex, cimicis, ein stinckend würmlein. Coccyx, coccygis, ein Gückgauch. Codex, codicis, ein buch. Colax, colacis, ein schmeichler. Confluens, confluetis, ein orht da zwei wasser zusamen fliessen. Corax, coracis, ein Rabe. Cornicen, cornicinis, ein hornblaser. Cucumis, cucumeris, ein kraut Cucumern. Cupido, Cupidinis, ein Gott der liebe. Delphin vel Delphis, delphinis, ein schnel Meerschwein. Des, dentis, ein zan. Dextans, dextantis, sehen pfenning. Et reliquae Assis partes in ns. Dropax, dropacis, ein salbe/die haar aufsfallen macht. Eryx, Erycis, ein berg in Sicilien. Esox, esocis, ein Lachs. Esurio, esurionis, ein hungriger. Fidicen, fidicinis, ein seytenschlaher. Flos, floris, ein blum. Fons, fontis, ein brunn. Fornix, fornicis, ein gewölb/ein schwibogen. Frutex, fruticis, ein staud/ein strunck. Furfur, furfuris, kleyen. Grex, gregis, ein schaar kleines viehes. Glis, gliris, ein schläferige rellmaus. Gurges, gurgitis, ein grosse tieffe in einem fluß. Gryps, gryphis, ein Greiff. Harpago, harpagonis, ein schiffhacke. Harpax, harpagis, agstein/ein spinnwirtel / ein instrument / so an die spille gethan wirdꝛdaß sie leichter vmblauffe. Hydrops, hydropis, die wassersucht. Et reliqua polysyllaba in ps. Hymen, hymenis, der hochzeit Gott. Ibix, ibicis, ein schneile wilde Ziege. Lapis, lapidis, ein stein. Latex, laticis, ein jede feuchtigkeit. Lepus, leporis, ein Hase. Lichen, schüpechtige schebigkeit im antliz. Lien, lienis, das milz. Ligo, ligonis, ein hauw/ein hacke. Meccenas, mecoenatis, ein beso[?]derer guter künstlen. Mons, montis, ein berg. Mucro, mucronis, die spitz an eim jetlichen gewehr. Mulciber, mulciberis, der hinckende Gott <bl>des fewis[?]</bl> / Vulcanus <bl>genandt.</bl> Mus , muris , <bl>ein</bl> <bl>Mauß.</bl> Murex,muricis, <bl>ein Meerschnecke/die pur-</bl> <bl>purfarbigen schweiß hatt / ein treispitzigs eisen / so</bl> <bl>man außspietet / daß die feinde darein tretten.</bl> Onyx,onychis,<bl>ein nagel an den fingern oder zehen/ein</bl> <bl>edelgestein.</bl> Oriens,orientis, <bl>der Sonnen auffgang.</bl> Oryx ,orygis , <bl>ein grosse wilde Ziege / so das haar</bl> <bl>vom schwanz gegen dem kopff fehet.</bl> Occidens, occidentis, <bl>der Sonnen nidergang.</bl> Panax,panacis,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>kraut das alle kranckheit heilen soll.</bl> Papilio,papilionis, <bl>ein sommer vogel / ein Kriegsjälte[?].</bl> Pecten, pectinis,<bl>ein kamm/ ein Weber blatt / ein schölle/ist</bl> <bl>ein fisch.</bl> Phoenix,phoenicis, <bl>der vogel Phenix in</bl> <bl>Arabia / welcher sechshundert Jar alt wird / vnd sich</bl> <bl>selber darnach verbrennet / so wird auß der aschen</bl> <bl>einer wider geboren.</bl> Pons,Pontis,<bl>ein brücke.</bl> Podex, podicis, <bl>der hinder.</bl> Pollis, pollinis , <bl>das beste mäl.</bl> Pollex, pollicis, <bl>der daum.</bl> Pulex, pulicis, <bl>ein floch.</bl> Praesul, praesulis , <bl>der fürnembst vnter den Priestern</bl> <bl>Martis.</bl> Proceres,procerum,<bl>die balcken an den ge-</bl> <bl>bäwen / so fürauß gehen / die fürnembsten im volck.</bl> Phryx,phrygis,<bl>einer auß Phrygia.</bl> Pugio, pugionis, <bl>ein Dolch.</bl> Ramex, ramicis, <bl>ein bruch der gemächten.</bl> Remex, remigis, <bl>ein Ruderknecht.</bl> Ren, renis, <bl>die nieren.</bl> Relex , relecis , <bl>ein weinrebengerten.</bl> Rex, regis, <bl>ein König.</bl> Sales, salium, <bl>schwencke/</bl> <bl>schimpfrede.</bl> Sanguis,sanguinis, <bl>blut.</bl> Sandyx,sandycis , <bl>bergrot / minien.</bl> Spadix, spadicis , <bl>ein ab-</bl> <bl>gerissen zweig vom Dattelbaum / oder braunrot.</bl> Scipio, scipionis, <bl>ein steck an dem alt oder schwach</bl> <bl>leute gehen.</bl> Scfcunx,sefcuncis, <bl>dien loth.</bl> Et omnes Assis partes in x. Seps, sepis, <bl>ein kleiner Schlang/</bl> <bl>welches bis faul machet.</bl> Splen, splenis , <bl>das milz/</bl>
units.tr: Nouns of the imparisyllabic declension that are declined like Sacerdos or Fructus are masculine, as: hic Augur, augoris, a soothsayer who foretells from the gestures or song of birds. Abax, Abacis, a table or bench on which one lays something, a board on which all kinds of vessels hang, a counting-table.
