Adamas, Adamantis, a hard precious stone that can be broken with the warm blood of a goat. Agger, Aggeris, a heap of earth, a rampart, a bulwark. Amor, amoris, love. Apex, apicis, the uppermost part of anything. Aquilex, aquilegis, a well-digger. Aries, arietis, a ram that has not been castrated. Atlas, Atlantis, a high mountain in Africa, or a giant who bears heaven on his shoulders, according to the poets' fiction. And the rest in -as that have -ntis in the genitive. Attagen, attagenis, a hazel grouse. Arctophylax, arctophylacis, the constellation called the Wagoner. Anthrax, anthracis, a coal; Saint Anthony's fire; a precious stone. Bidens, bidentis, a hoe with two prongs. Bombyx, bombycis, a silkworm. Caudex, caudicis, the trunk of a tree. Chalybs, chalybis, steel. Charax, characis, a stake or prop for vines. Calix, calicis, a drinking vessel. Calyx, calycis, the husk of a fruit, the cover of a flower. Cardo, cardinis, the iron fitting on which doors turn, the hinge of a door. Cinis, cineris, ash. Cimex, cimicis, a stinking little worm. Coccyx, coccygis, a cuckoo. Codex, codicis, a book. Colax, colacis, a flatterer. Confluens, confluentis, a place where two waters flow together. Corax, coracis, a raven. Cornicen, cornicinis, a horn-blower. Cucumis, cucumeris, the cucumber plant. Cupido, Cupidinis, the god of love. Delphin or Delphis, delphinis, a swift sea-pig (dolphin). Dens, dentis, a tooth. Dextans, dextantis, a tenth-part coin. And the other parts of the as in -ns. Dropax, dropacis, an ointment that makes the hair fall out. Eryx, Erycis, a mountain in Sicily. Esox, esocis, a salmon. Esurio, esurionis, a hungry man. Fidicen, fidicinis, a lute-player. Flos, floris, a flower. Fons, fontis, a spring. Fornix, fornicis, a vault, an arch. Frutex, fruticis, a shrub, a stump. Furfur, furfuris, bran. Grex, gregis, a flock of small cattle. Glis, gliris, a dormouse. Gurges, gurgitis, a great deep pool in a river. Gryps, gryphis, a griffin. Harpago, harpagonis, a grappling hook. Harpax, harpagis, amber; a spindle-whorl; an instrument put on the spindle so that it turns more easily. Hydrops, hydropis, dropsy. And the other polysyllables in -ps. Hymen, hymenis, the god of marriage. Ibix, ibicis, a swift wild goat. Lapis, lapidis, a stone. Latex, laticis, any moisture. Lepus, leporis, a hare. Lichen, a scaly roughness of the face. Lien, lienis, the spleen. Ligo, ligonis, a hoe, a pickaxe. Maecenas, Maecenatis, a particularly good patron of the arts. Mons, montis, a mountain. Mucro, mucronis, the point of any weapon. Mulciber, mulciberis, the lame god of fire, called Vulcan. Mus, muris, a mouse. Murex, muricis, a sea-snail that yields purple dye; a three-pointed iron spike thrown out so that the enemy treads on it. Onyx, onychis, a fingernail or toenail; a precious stone. Oriens, orientis, the rising of the sun. Oryx, orygis, a large wild goat whose hair grows from the tail towards the head. Occidens, occidentis, the setting of the sun. Panax, panacis, a herb said to heal every disease. Papilio, papilionis, a summer bird; a kind of butterfly. Pecten, pectinis, a comb, a weaver's reed, a shell; it is a fish. Phoenix, phoenicis, the phoenix bird in Arabia, which lives six hundred years and then burns itself, and from its ashes another is born. Pons, pontis, a bridge. Podex, podicis, the backside. Pollis, pollinis, the finest flour. Pollex, pollicis, the thumb. Pulex, pulicis, a flea. Praesul, praesulis, the chief among the priests of Mars. Proceres, procerum, the beams on buildings that project forward; the chief men among the people. Phryx, phrygis, a man from Phrygia. Pugio, pugionis, a dagger. Ramex, ramicis, a rupture of the genitals. Remex, remigis, a rower. Ren, renis, the kidneys. Relex, relecis, a vine-shoot. Rex, regis, a king. Sales, salium, jests, mockery. Sanguis, sanguinis, blood. Sandyx, sandycis, red earth, minium. Spadix, spadicis, a branch torn from a date palm, or dark red. Scipio, scipionis, a staff on which old or weak people walk. Sescunx, sescuncis, a pound and a half (the ounce unit). And all parts of the as in -x. Seps, sepis, a small snake which makes things rot. Splen, splenis, the spleen.

units.la: Senex, senicis olim, hodie senis, ein alter. Sorex, soricis, ein spitzmauß. Sol, solis, die <bl>Sonne</bl>. Tradux, traducis, ein <bl>weinrāben zweig</bl>, den man weit von einem ort an das ander <bl>leubet</bl> / eine <bl>aebāung</bl>. Tibicen, tibicinis, ein <bl>pfeiffer</bl>. Titio, titionis, ein <bl>außgelöschter</bl> <bl>brand</bl>. Thorax, thoracis, ein <bl>wammes</bl> / ein <bl>brustharnisch</bl>. Torrens, torrentis, ein <bl>bergwasser</bl> auß <bl>dem</bl> <bl>regen entstanden</bl>. Tridens, tridentis, <bl>ein dreyspitzig</bl> <bl>eisen</bl>. Thrips, thripis, ein <bl>holzwurm</bl>. Turtur, turturis, ein <bl>Turteltaub</bl>. Unio, unionis, ein <bl>pärlin</bl> / ein <bl>zwi-</bl> <bl>bel</bl>. Japyx, japigis, ein <bl>wind der wider den Ostwind</bl> <bl>wähet</bl>. Judex, judicis, ein <bl>Richter</bl>. Vas, vadis, ein <bl>bürg</bl> / der sich für einen andern in <bl>bürgschafft begibt</bl>. Vertex, verticis, vel vortex, vorticis, ein <bl>wirbel</bl> / ein <bl>scheitel</bl> / ein <bl>gipfel des berges</bl>. Vervex, vervecis, ein <bl>hammel</bl>. Vespertilio, vespertilionis, ein <bl>flädermauß</bl>. Volvox, volvocis, ein <bl>rädwürmlin</bl>. Vomis, vel vomer, vomeris, ein <bl>schaar</bl> / ein <bl>pflugeisen</bl>. Vultur, vulturis, ein <bl>Geir</bl> [?]. Gradus, hujus gradus, ein <bl>staffel</bl> / <bl>trappe</bl> / ein <bl>gang</bl>. Portus, hujus portus, ein <bl>Meerhaff</bl>. Vultus, hujus vultus, der <bl>wil und anmutung</bl> / so im <bl>an-</bl> <bl>gesicht erzeiget wird</bl>.
units.tr: Senex, senicis formerly, now senis, an old man. Sorex, soricis, a shrew-mouse. Sol, solis, the sun. Tradux, traducis, a vine-branch which one bends from one place to another so that it takes root; a layering. Tibicen, tibicinis, a piper. Titio, titionis, a burnt-out brand. Thorax, thoracis, a doublet; a breastplate. Torrens, torrentis, a mountain torrent formed from rain. Tridens, tridentis, a three-pronged iron. Thrips, thripis, a woodworm. Turtur, turturis, a turtle-dove. Unio, unionis, a pearl; a pair. Japyx, japigis, a wind that blows against the east wind. Judex, judicis, a judge. Vas, vadis, a surety; one who binds himself in suretyship for another. Vertex, verticis, or vortex, vorticis, a whirlpool; a crown of the head; the summit of a mountain. Vervex, vervecis, a wether (castrated ram). Vespertilio, vespertilionis, a bat. Volvox, volvocis, a little wheel-shaped worm. Vomis, or vomer, vomeris, a ploughshare; a plough-blade. Vultur, vulturis, a vulture. Gradus, hujus gradus, a step, a stair, a pace. Portus, hujus portus, a harbour. Vultus, hujus vultus, the expression and bearing shown in the face.

units.la: Reliqua Nomina Declinationis imparisyllabæ, quæ in sequentem primam exceptionem cadunt, sunt generis fœminini: in secundam, generis neutrius: in tertiam generis communis.
units.tr: The remaining nouns of the imparisyllabic declension that fall under the following first exception are feminine. Those under the second exception are neuter, and those under the third are of common gender.

units.la: Quæ est prima Exceptio.
units.tr: What is the first exception?

units.la: Nomina Declinationis imparisyllabæ in as, in do, vel go hyperdisyllaba, in io verbalia, in is, in ys, in s præcedente consona, in x, & finientia in us, quæ u in obliquis retinent, fœminina sunt: ut, Hæc pietas, pietatis, (<bl>Gottsfürchtigkeit</bl>). Cupido, cupidinis, ein <bl>gierd</bl> / ein <bl>begird</bl>. Imago, imaginis, ein <bl>bild</bl>. Unio, unionis, <bl>einigkeit</bl>. Callis, callidis, ein <bl>helm</bl> / ein <bl>eisenhut</bl>. Chlamys,chlamydis,<bl>ein Ritterkleid/ ein Neuter rock</bl>. Bidens,bidentis,<bl>ein zweyjärig schaf</bl>. Fornax, fornacis, <bl>ein ofen</bl>. Pecus,pecudis,<bl>allerley vieh vnder des</bl> <bl>menschen gewalt</bl>. Amathus,amathuntis,<bl>ein Statt</bl> <bl>in Cypern</bl>.
units.tr: Nouns of the imparisyllabic declension ending in -as, in -do or -go with more than two syllables, in -io when verbal, in -is, in -ys, in -s preceded by a consonant, in -x, and those ending in -us that keep u in the oblique cases, are feminine. For example: hæc pietas, pietatis (godliness). Cupido, cupidinis, a desire or longing. Imago, imaginis, an image. Unio, unionis, unity. Callis, callidis, a helmet or iron hat. Chlamys, chlamydis, a knight's garment or a kind of cloak. Bidens, bidentis, a two-year-old sheep. Fornax, fornacis, an oven. Pecus, pecudis, all kinds of livestock under human control. Amathus, amathuntis, a town in Cyprus.

units.la: Hisce addantur sequentia foeminina: Ales, alitis, <bl>ein vogel</bl>. Anus,hujus Anus,<bl>ein alt weib</bl>. Acus,hujus acus, <bl>ein nadel/ein natel</bl>. Arbor,arboris,<bl>ein baum</bl>. Argo, Argoos,<bl>ein schiff Jasonis</bl>. Communio,communionis,<bl>gemeinschafft/gesellschafft</bl>. Conditio,conditionis,<bl>ein bedingt/stand oder wesen</bl>. Cos,cotis,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>wetzstein</bl>. Compedes,compedum,<bl>fußbande</bl>. Ditio, ditionis,<bl>ein herschafft/gebiet</bl>. Dos,dotis,<bl>ein brautschatz</bl>. Eos,eois,<bl>morgenröte</bl>. Echo,hujus echus,<bl>wi-</bl> <bl>derschall</bl>. Fraus,fraudis,<bl>ein betrug</bl>. Glos,gloris,<bl>des</bl> <bl>manns schwester</bl>. Grando, gradinis,<bl>hagel</bl>. Halcyon, halcyonis,<bl>ein vogel der winters zeit im Meer ge-</bl> <bl>büret</bl>. Icon,iconis,<bl>ein bildnuß</bl>. Idus,iduum, & <bl>fünff zehende</bl> <bl>tag im Merz/Mey/Hewmonat vnd Weinm-</bl> <bl>onat/in den andern der dreyzehende</bl>. Lactes, lactium, <bl>zart eingeweid</bl>. Laus, laudis, <bl>lob/preis</bl>. Manus,hujus manus,<bl>ein hand</bl>. Merces,mercedis,<bl>ein be-</bl> <bl>lohnung</bl>. Merges,mergitis,<bl>ein fomgarb</bl>. Occasio,occasionis, <bl>ein gelegenheit</bl>. Opes,opum, <bl>reichtumb</bl>. Penus, hujus penus, <bl>allerley vorratb zu speis vnnd</bl> <bl>trancf</bl>. Porticus, hujus porticus, <bl>ein bedeckt ohrt zu</bl> <bl>spatzieren</bl>. Portio,portionis, <bl>ein theil/ein stuck</bl>. Quadrupes,quadrupedis, <bl>ein vierfüssig thier</bl>. Quies, quietis,<bl>ruh/der</bl> <bl>schlaff</bl>. Ratio,rationis,<bl>die vernunfft</bl>. Requies, requietis vel requiei, <bl>ruh/schlaff</bl>. Religio, religionis,<bl>Gottes verehrung</bl>. Seditio,seditionis,<bl>ein</bl> <bl>aufruhr</bl>. Seges, segetis,<bl>wachsend korn</bl>. Sindon,sindonis,<bl>subtil leinwath</bl>. Siren,Sirenis,<bl>oben ein</bl> <bl>Jungfraw/unten ein fisch</bl>. Tribus, hujus tribus, <bl>ein außt-</bl> <bl>heilung des volcks in besondere ordnung/ein zunfft</bl>. Teges, tegetis, ein <bl>Decke auß binzen gemacht</bl> / ein <bl>matte.</bl> Talio, talionis, <bl>gleiche beschädigung.</bl>
units.tr: To these add the following feminines: Ales, alitis, a bird. Anus, hujus anus, an old woman. Acus, hujus acus, a needle or pin. Arbor, arboris, a tree. Argo, Argus, the ship of Jason. Communio, communionis, fellowship or society. Conditio, conditionis, a condition, state or circumstance. Cos, cotis, a whetstone. Compedes, compedum, fetters. Ditio, ditionis, dominion or territory. Dos, dotis, a dowry. Eos, eois, the dawn. Echo, hujus echus, an echo. Fraus, fraudis, a deceit. Glos, gloris, a husband's sister. Grando, grandinis, hail. Halcyon, halcyonis, a bird born on the sea in winter. Icon, iconis, a likeness. Idus, iduum, the fifteenth day in March, May, July and October, and the thirteenth in the other months. Lactes, lactium, tender entrails. Laus, laudis, praise. Manus, hujus manus, a hand. Merces, mercedis, a reward. Merges, mergitis, a sheaf of grain. Occasio, occasionis, an opportunity. Opes, opum, riches. Penus, hujus penus, all kinds of provisions of food and drink. Porticus, hujus porticus, a covered place for walking. Portio, portionis, a part or portion. Quadrupes, quadrupedis, a four-footed animal. Quies, quietis, rest or sleep. Ratio, rationis, reason. Requies, requietis or requiei, rest or sleep. Religio, religionis, the worship of God. Seditio, seditionis, an uprising. Seges, segetis, standing corn. Sindon, sindonis, fine linen. Siren, Sirenis, a maiden above and a fish below. Tribus, hujus tribus, a division of the people into a special order, or a guild. Teges, tegetis, a covering made of rushes, or a mat. Talio, talionis, equal injury.

units.la: Et Nomina, quæ declinantur sicut Species, sunt fœminini generis: ut, hæc acies, aciei, <bl>ein schneide an</bl> <bl>einem eisen</bl>/ <bl>die scharpffe der augen</bl> / <bl>scharpffsinnig-</bl> <bl>keit</bl> / <bl>ein kriegs oder schlachtordnung.</bl> Facies, faciei, <bl>das antlitz/oder angesicht.</bl> Res, rei, <bl>ein ding.</bl> Hæc integra sunt: Reliqua plurali numero carent. Dies, singulari numero masculino & fœminino genere usurpatur, plurali, masculino tantum. Hujus Compositum Meridies, <bl>der Mittag/</bl> masculinum tantum est, & singulare.
units.tr: Nouns declined like Species are also feminine: for example, hæc acies, aciei, the edge of an iron blade, the sharpness of the eyes, keenness of wit, or a battle line. Facies, faciei, the face or countenance. Res, rei, a thing. These are whole nouns; the others lack the plural number. Dies is used in the singular in the masculine and feminine genders, but in the plural only in the masculine. Its compound Meridies, midday, is masculine only and singular.

units.la: Declina Species.
units.tr: Decline Species.

units.la: N. Hæc species, <bl>die gestalt.</bl> G. Hujus speciei, <bl>der ge-</bl> <bl>stalt.</bl> D. Huic speciei, <bl>der gestalt.</bl> A. Hanc speciem, <bl>die</bl> <bl>gestalt.</bl> V. O species, O <bl>gestalt.</bl> A. Ab hac specie, <bl>von</bl> <bl>der gestalt.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. hæc species, the shape. Gen. hujus speciei, of the shape. Dat. huic speciei, to the shape. Acc. hanc speciem, the shape. Voc. o species, O shape. Abl. ab hac specie, from the shape.

units.la: N. Hæ species, <bl>die gestalte.</bl> G. Harum specierum, <bl>der gestalten.</bl> D. His speciebus, <bl>den gestalten.</bl> A. Has species, <bl>die gestalten.</bl> V. O species, O <bl>ihr gestalten.</bl> A. Ab his speciebus, <bl>von den gestalten.</bl>
units.tr: Nom. hæ species, the shapes. Gen. harum specierum, of the shapes. Dat. his speciebus, to the shapes. Acc. has species, the shapes. Voc. o species, O shapes. Abl. ab his speciebus, from the shapes.

units.la: Quæ est secunda Exceptio?
units.tr: What is the second exception?

units.la: Nomina Declinationis imparisyllabæ in ma, u, c, t, al, el, en, ar, ver, ber, ur, & terminatia in us, quæ u in obliquis mutant, neutra sunt: ut, Hoc Epigramma, Epigrammatis, <bl>ein überschrifft.</bl> Sic zeugma, zeugmatis, quanvis urbis nomen. Hoc cornu, hujus cornu, singulari numero indeclinabile, <bl>ein horn.</bl> Lac, lactis, <bl>milch.</bl> Caput, capitis, <bl>ein haupt.</bl> Tribunal, tribunals, <bl>ein Richterstul.</bl> Sic Ispal, ispalis, quanvis urbis nomen. Mel, mellis, <bl>honig.</bl> Examen, examinis, <bl>ein Schwarm oder Wespen schwarm /</bl> <bl>das junglin in der wag/ eine erforschung mit fragen.</bl> Calcar, calcaris, <bl>ein sporn.</bl>
units.tr: Nouns of the imparisyllabic declension ending in -ma, -u, -c, -t, -al, -el, -en, -ar, -ver, -ber, -ur, and those ending in -us that change u in the oblique cases, are neuter. For example: hoc epigramma, epigrammatis, an inscription. So zeugma, zeugmatis, though it is the name of a city. Hoc cornu, hujus cornu, indeclinable in the singular, a horn. Lac, lactis, milk. Caput, capitis, a head. Tribunal, tribunalis, a judgement seat. So Ispal, ispalis, though it is the name of a city. Mel, mellis, honey. Examen, examinis, a swarm of bees or wasps, the tongue of a balance, or an inquiry by questions. Calcar, calcaris, a spur.

units.la: Cadaver, cadaveris, <bl>ein todter leichnam / ein Zerstö-</bl>[?] rete <bl>Statt</bl>. Tuber,tuberis,ein <bl>geschwulft</bl> / ein <bl>knor-</bl> <bl>re</bl>[?] an einem baum. Jecur, jecoris vel jecinoris,die <bl>lä-</bl> <bl>ber</bl>[?]. Pecus,pecoris,<bl>vieh</bl>. Foedus, foederis, ein <bl>bünd-</bl> <bl>nuß</bl> / ein <bl>verlobter fried</bl>. Hisce addantur sequentia neutra: Ador, adoris, quo Genitivo usus est Ausonius, rein <bl>vnnd sauber Lorn</bl>[?]. Aequor, aequoris, das <bl>Meer</bl> / <bl>ebne des felds</bl>. Aes,aeris,<bl>erʒ</bl>/<bl>kupffer</bl>. Accidens,accidentis,ein <bl>zufellig ding</bl>. Antecedens, antecedentis, das <bl>vorgehende</bl>. Cacoethes, cacoetheos, ein <bl>böse gewonheit</bl>. Chaos,chaeos, <bl>vermischung al-</bl> <bl>ler ding</bl>. Cicer,ciceris,<bl>kichern</bl>. Consequens,consequentis,die <bl>folgung</bl>. Cor,cordis,das <bl>herz</bl>. Crus,cruris, das <bl>theil am schenckel vnder dem knie</bl>. Pondo,ein <bl>pfund</bl>. Fas,<bl>göttlich billich vnnd recht</bl>/& Nefas, <bl>vnbillich</bl>/sunt neutra indeclinabilia. Hippomanes,hippomaneos, <bl>pferdsaamen</bl>. Iter,itineris,ein <bl>reiß oder</bl> <bl>weg/straß</bl>. Ir,iris,die <bl>höle der händ vnd füsse</bl>. Lacer, laceris,<bl>Teuffelsdreck</bl>/ein <bl>safft Laserpitij</bl>. Marmor, marmoris, ein <bl>marmelstein</bl>. Melos, meleos, ein <bl>gesang</bl>. Moly,molyos,ein <bl>kraut</bl>. Nepenthes,nepetheos, ein <bl>kraut</bl>. Os oris,ein <bl>mundt</bl>. Os ossis,ein <bl>bein/ kna-</bl> <bl>che</bl>. Piper, piperis, <bl>pfeffer</bl>. Pus, puris, <bl>eyter</bl>. Rus, ruris,ein <bl>feld</bl> <bl>oder gut</bl>. Sil,silis,ein <bl>leimächtig erdt-</bl> <bl>reich in erdgruben</bl>. Sifer, siferis, <bl>rot rüblin</bl>. Spinther, spintheris, ein <bl>armgeschmuck der weiber</bl>. Telos, teleos, ein <bl>ende</bl>. Thus, thuris, <bl>weyrauch</bl>. Jus, juris, das <bl>recht/ oder ein brühe</bl>. Vas,vasis, in plurali,vasa,vasorum,secundę Declinationis, ein <bl>geschirr/</bl> <bl>ein faß</bl>.
units.tr: Cadaver, cadaveris, a dead body, or a ruined city. Tuber, tuberis, a swelling, or a knot on a tree. Jecur, jecoris or jecinoris, the liver. Pecus, pecoris, cattle. Foedus, foederis, a covenant, or a betrothed peace. The following neuters are also added: Ador, adoris, which Ausonius used in the genitive, pure and clean spelt. Aequor, aequoris, the sea, or the level of a field. Aes, aeris, bronze or copper. Accidens, accidentis, an accidental thing. Antecedens, antecedentis, that which precedes. Cacoethes, cacoetheos, a bad habit. Chaos, chaeos, a mixture of all things. Cicer, ciceris, a chickpea. Consequens, consequentis, a consequence. Cor, cordis, the heart. Crus, cruris, the part of the leg below the knee. Pondo, a pound. Fas, what is divinely right and just, and Nefas, what is unjust, are neuter and indeclinable. Hippomanes, hippomaneos, horse-semen. Iter, itineris, a journey, a way or road. Ir, iris, the hollow of the hands and feet. Lacer, laceris, devil's dung, or a juice of laserpitium. Marmor, marmoris, marble. Melos, meleos, a song. Moly, molyos, a herb. Nepenthes, nepetheos, a herb. Os, oris, a mouth. Os, ossis, a bone. Piper, piperis, pepper. Pus, puris, pus. Rus, ruris, a field or estate. Sil, silis, a clayey, earthy soil found in pits. Sifer, siferis, a red radish. Spinther, spintheris, an arm ornament of women. Telos, teleos, an end. Thus, thuris, frankincense. Jus, juris, law, or a broth. Vas, vasis, in the plural vasa, vasorum, of the second declension, a vessel or a cask.

units.la: Animans, animantis, ein <bl>thier</bl> / in Foeminino & Neutro genere frequentius, quàm Masculino dicitur.
units.tr: Animans, animantis, an animal. It is used more often in the feminine and neuter genders than in the masculine.

units.la: Atriplex, atriplicis, <bl>miltenkraut</bl> / est foeminini & neutrius generis. Halec, halecis, ein <bl>Häring</bl>/ neutrius & foeminini generis est. Sal, salis, <bl>Salʒ</bl>/ est masculini & neutrius generis, pro sapientia & urbanitate masculini tantum.
units.tr: Atriplex, atriplicis, orache, is of feminine and neuter gender. Halec, halecis, a herring, is of neuter and feminine gender. Sal, salis, salt, is of masculine and neuter gender, but for wisdom and wit only masculine.

units.la: Laver, <bl>b.uumen peterlin / ein fraut</bl> / foeminino & neutro genere ufurpatur.
units.tr: Laver, a parsley-like herb, is used in the feminine and neuter genders.

units.la: Quæ est tertia Exceptio?
units.tr: Which is the third exception?

units.la: Communis generis sunt hæc sequentia: Author, authoris, ein aufenger. Adeps, adipis, allerley feist. Bos, bovis, ein Ochs oder Rind. Bubo, bubonis, ein <bl>Nachteul.</bl> Calx, calcis, die verse des fusses/ das end eines jetlichen dinges: für kalck foeminini tantum. Conjunx, sive conjux, conjugis, ein Gemahel. Cortex, corticis, ein rinde/ein schelle/schale. Culex, culicis, ein jeder wurm mit flügeln. Dux, ducis, ein führer/ein führerin. Exlex, exlegis, gesatzlos/ungehorsam. Exul, exulis, ein vertriebener auß seinem vatterlandt. Forceps, forcipis, ein zang. Grus, gruis, ein <bl>Kranich.</bl> Imbrex, imbricis, ein holer ziegel. Index, indicis, ein anzeiger/ein register/ein probierstein. Infans, infantis, ein unmündig kind. Limax, limacis, ein erdschnecke. Lynx, lyncis, ein scharpfsichtig thier. Margo, marginis, das bort/das eusserste an jetlichem dinge. Martyr, martyris, ein <bl>Zeug.</bl> Natrix, natricis, ein <bl>wasserschlang.</bl> Nefrens, nefrendis, ein fählein/ein kleines schwein. Obex, obicis, ein rigel/ein klincke an der thür/verhaltung. Onyx, onychis, ein salb büchse. Pumex, pumicis, ein stein voll löcher/so auff dem wasser schwimmet. Pulvis, pulveris, staub. Redux, reducis, der gesund wider heim kommen ist. Rudens, rudentis, ein groß schiff seyl. Scobs, scobis, sägspän. Sciobs, scrobis, ein grub. Specus, us, ein loch. Serpes, serpentis, ein schlang. Silex, silicis, ein feuerstein/ein fßling. Stirps, stirpis, der stamm an einem baum: für ein geschlecht/ Foemin. tantum. Sus, suis, ein saw. Varix, varicis, ein auffgeblasen ader. Jaspis, jaspidis, ein <bl>edelgestein.</bl>
units.tr: The following are of common gender: author, authoris, an originator. Adeps, adipis, fat of any kind. Bos, bovis, an ox or cow. Bubo, bubonis, a night owl. Calx, calcis, the heel of the foot, the end of anything; for lime, feminine only. Conjunx, or conjux, conjugis, a spouse. Cortex, corticis, a bark, a rind, a shell. Culex, culicis, any winged insect. Dux, ducis, a leader, male or female. Exlex, exlegis, lawless, disobedient. Exul, exulis, one exiled from his homeland. Forceps, forcipis, a pair of tongs. Grus, gruis, a crane. Imbrex, imbricis, a hollow roof tile. Index, indicis, an indicator, a register, a touchstone. Infans, infantis, a child not yet of age. Limax, limacis, a slug. Lynx, lyncis, an animal with sharp sight. Margo, marginis, the border, the outermost edge of anything. Martyr, martyris, a witness. Natrix, natricis, a water snake. Nefrens, nefrendis, a young pig, a little hog. Obex, obicis, a bolt, a door latch, an obstacle. Onyx, onychis, an ointment box. Pumex, pumicis, a porous stone that floats on water. Pulvis, pulveris, dust. Redux, reducis, one who has come safely home again. Rudens, rudentis, a large ship's rope. Scobs, scobis, sawdust. Scrobs, scrobis, a ditch. Specus, us, a hole. Serpes, serpentis, a serpent. Silex, silicis, a flint, a pebble. Stirps, stirpis, the trunk of a tree; for a lineage; feminine only. Sus, suis, a sow. Varix, varicis, a swollen vein. Jaspis, jaspidis, a jasper, a precious stone.

units.la: Quæ habent in Ablativo singulari i tantum?
units.tr: Which have i only in the ablative singular?

units.la: Neutra in al aut ar definentia: ut Vectigal, sol[?] ab hoc vectigali. Calcar, ein spor[?] ab hoc calcari. Præter, Sal, salʒ. Hepar, Die Läber. Far[?] Jubar, der schein vnd glantz eines feurigen dinges. Nectar, ein süß tranck der Heydnischen Götter: quæ e habent: ut, sale, hepate, farre, jubare, nectare.
units.tr: Neuters ending in al or ar: as vectigal, ablative vectigali. Calcar, a spur, ablative calcari. Sal, salt. Hepar, the liver. Far, Jubar, the radiance and brightness of a fiery thing. Nectar, the sweet drink of the pagan gods. These have e: as sale, hepate, farre, jubare, nectare.

units.la: Adjectiva unius terminationis e vel i habent: ut, amans, ab hoc amante vel amanti. Degener, degenere vel degeneri. Excipe, pauper, sopes[?] & alia nonnulla. Item & Comparativi e vel i habent: ut, Major, majore, vel majori.
units.tr: Adjectives of one termination have e or i: as amans, ablative amante or amanti. Degener, degenere or degeneri. Except pauper, and some others. Likewise comparatives have e or i: as major, majore or majori.

units.la: Quæ habent in Nominativo plurali ia?
units.tr: Which have ia in the nominative plural?

units.la: Neutra, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tantum, vel in e & i simul definit: ut, ab hoc vectigali, hæc vectigalia: ab hoc audace vel audaci, hæc audacia. Excipe, Vetus, vetera: Et Comparativos: ut Majora, plura Veteres plura & pluria dixere.
units.tr: Neuters whose ablative singular ends in i only, or in e and i both: as ab hoc vectigali, hæc vectigalia; from hoc audace or audaci, hæc audacia. Except vetus, vetera; and the comparatives, as majora, plura. The older writers said plura and pluria.

units.la: Quæ habent in Genitivo plurali ium?
units.tr: Which have ium in the genitive plural?

units.la: Nomina, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tatum, vel in e & i simul exit: ut, ab hoc animali horum animalium. Ab hoc, hac, hoc fœlice, vel fœlici, horum, harum, horum fœlicium. Deinde ium habent, quorum Nominativus singularis in duas consonas exit: ut, pars, partium, ein theil. Falx, falciu, ein sichel/ oder Trum[?] schneidmesser. Merx, mercium, Kauffmans wahr/ oder gut. Sapiens, sapientium vel sapientum, weisse. Parens, parentium vel parentum, die eltern. Tertio monosyllaba quædam: ut, Cor, cordium. Lis, litium. Mas, marium. Mus, murium. Os, ossium.
units.tr: Nouns whose ablative singular ends in i only, or in e and i both: as ab hoc animali, horum animalium. From hic, hac, hoc felix, or felici: horum, harum, horum felicium. Then those with ium whose nominative singular ends in two consonants: as pars, partium, a part. Falx, falcium, a sickle or cutting knife. Merx, mercium, merchandise or goods. Sapiens, sapientium or sapientum, wise. Parens, parentium or parentum, parents. Certain monosyllables likewise: as cor, cordium; lis, litium; mas, marium; mus, murium; os, ossium.

units.la: Quænam excipiuntur à dictis Regulis?
units.tr: Which are excepted from the said rules?

units.la: Primo, Comparativi: ut, Major, majorum. Melior, meliorum. Plus habet plurium. Deinde hæc sequentia: Vetus, veterum. Memor, memorum. Inops, inopum. Vigil, vigilum. Hyems, hyemum. Arabs, arabum. Princeps, principum: Et reliqua in bs vel ps definentia.
units.tr: First, comparatives: as major, majorum; melior, meliorum; plus has plurium. Then the following: vetus, veterum; memor, memorum; inops, inopum; vigil, vigilum; hyems, hyemum; Arabs, Arabum; princeps, principum; and the rest ending in bs or ps.

units.la: Quae habent in Dativo & Ablativo plu- rali ubus?
units.tr: Which have ubus in the dative and ablative plural?

units.la: Hæc sequentia: Acus, ein Nadel. Arcus, ein handbog/ein schwibogen/ein regenbogen. Artus, artuum, Gliedmassen. Ficus, ein Feigenbaum. Lacus, ein See/ ein Juber/ein balcke. Portus, ein Meerhaff. Partus, die geburt. Quercus, ein Eichbaum. Questus, ein Klag mit weinen. Specus, ein loch in dem erdreich. Tribus, ein zunfft. Veru, ein bratspieß. Bos, bovis, habet Genitivo plurali boum, Dativo & Ablativo bobus vel bubus.
units.tr: The following: acus, a needle. Arcus, a hand bow, an arch, a rainbow. Artus, artuum, limbs. Ficus, a fig tree. Lacus, a lake, a tub, a beam. Portus, a harbour. Partus, birth. Quercus, an oak tree. Questus, a complaint with weeping. Specus, a hole in the earth. Tribus, a tribe. Veru, a roasting spit. Bos, bovis, has boum in the genitive plural, and bobus or bubus in the dative and ablative.

units.la: Nomina in ma habent in Dativo & Ablativo plurali, is, & bus: ut, Epigramma, epigrammatis & epigrammatibus. Poema, poematis & poematibus, ein gedicht in Verß gestellet.
units.tr: Nouns in ma have is and bus in the dative and ablative plural: as epigramma, epigrammatis and epigrammatibus; poema, poematis and poematibus, a poem composed in verse.

units.la: Declina Jesus.
units.tr: Decline Jesus.

units.la: N. Hic Jesus, ein Seligmacher. G. Hujus Jesu, des Seligmachers. D. Huic Jesu, dem Seligmacher. A. Hunc Jesum, den Seligmacher. V. O Jesu, o Seligmacher. A. Ab hoc Jesu, von dem Seligmacher.
units.tr: Nom. This Jesus, a Saviour. Gen. Of this Jesus, of the Saviour. Dat. To this Jesus, to the Saviour. Acc. This Jesus, the Saviour. Voc. O Jesus, O Saviour. Abl. From this Jesus, from the Saviour.

units.la: Declina Domus?
units.tr: Decline domus?

units.la: N. Hæc domus, ein Hauß. G. Hujus domus, des Hauses. Domi, zu Hauß. Adverbium est. D. Huic domui, dem Hause. A. Hanc domum, das Hauß. V. O domus, o Hauß. A. Ab hac domo, von dem Hause. N. Hæc domus, die Heuser. G. Harum domuum & domorum, der Heuser. D. His domibus, den Heusern. A. Has domus & domos, die Heuser. V. O domus, o ihr Heuser. A. Ab his domibus, von den Heusern.
units.tr: Nominative: this house, a house. Genitive: of this house, of the house. Domi, at home; it is an adverb. Dative: to this house, to the house. Accusative: this house, the house. Vocative: O house. Ablative: from this house, from the house. Plural. Nominative: these houses, the houses. Genitive: of these houses, of the houses (harum domuum and domorum). Dative: to these houses, to the houses. Accusative: these houses, the houses. Vocative: O houses. Ablative: from these houses, from the houses.

units.la: Quaenam sunt singularis numeri tantum?
units.tr: Which nouns are singular only?

units.la: Aer, aeris, die weite zwischen der Erden vnnd dem Himmel. Aether,aetheris,der lufft / das element des fewrs/der Himmel. Fell, fellis, die gall. Lux,lucis, der Sonnen liecht/der tag. Mel,mellis,honig. Mors, mortis,der seelen und des leibes auffiösung. Paupertas,paupertatis, armut. Penus hujus penus, vorath[?] an speiß und tranck. Piper, piperis,pfeffer. Pix,picis, pech. Plebs,plebis,das gemeine volck. Ros,roris,der taw.Salus,salutis,heil/wolstand/wolfart. Senectus, senectutis,das alter. Sopor,soporis,der schlaff. Supellex,supellectilis,haußrath/ fahrende hab. Talio talionis, gleiche vergeltung. Tellus, telluris, ein Göttin des Erdreichs/ oder die Erde. Juventus, juventutis,die jugend. Jubar,jubaris,der glanz. Ver,veris,der frühling/der lentz.Vesper,vesperis,der abendstern/ der abend. Et alia. Usus spectandus. Nam,Et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella, apud Virgilium legitur.
units.tr: Aer, aeris: the air between the earth and the heaven. Aether, aetheris: the air, the element of fire, the heaven. Fell, fellis: gall. Lux, lucis: the light of the sun, the day. Mel, mellis: honey. Mors, mortis: the dissolution of soul and body, death. Paupertas, paupertatis: poverty. Penus, penus (genitive hujus penus): a store of food and drink. Piper, piperis: pepper. Pix, picis: pitch. Plebs, plebis: the common people. Ros, roris: dew. Salus, salutis: health, prosperity, well-being. Senectus, senectutis: old age. Sopor, soporis: sleep. Supellex, supellectilis: household goods, movable property. Talio, talionis: equal retaliation. Tellus, telluris: a goddess of the earth, or the earth. Juventus, juventutis: youth. Jubar, jubaris: brightness. Ver, veris: spring. Vesper, vesperis: the evening star, or evening. And others. Usage is to be observed. For "And hard oaks will sweat dewy honey" is read in Virgil.

units.la: Nominativo singulari carent:Dapis,herrliche speiß. Frugis, allerley frücht zu unserer aussenthalt dienstlich.Opis,hilffe/beystand/vermögens/macht. Precis, bitt/gebett: Et foeminini generis sunt.
units.tr: These lack a nominative singular: Dapis: a sumptuous feast. Frugis: all kinds of fruit useful for our sustenance. Opis: help, aid, resources, power. Precis: prayer, supplication. These are also of feminine gender.

units.la: Ablativi casus tantum sunt: jussu, auß geheiß. Injussu, ohn geheiß. Natu,von alter. Noctu, bey nacht. Permissu, auß nachlassung. Promptu, vorhanden. Sponte mea,von mir selbs/frewwillig.
units.tr: These occur only in the ablative case: jussu, by command. Injussu, without command. Natu, by birth, from age. Noctu, by night. Permissu, by permission. Promptu, at hand. Sponte mea, of my own accord.

units.la: Expes,ohn hoffnung/ est Nominativi casus tantum.
units.tr: Expes, without hope, occurs only in the nominative case.

units.la: Quid est As?
units.tr: What is an As?

units.la: As est numerus Duodenarius, qui ob divisionis commoditatem multis rebus accommodatur.
units.tr: As is the number twelve, which, because it divides conveniently, is applied to many things.

units.la: Quot sunt consideranda in Asse?
units.tr: What must be considered in an As?

units.la: Duo: Partes,& Res,quibus applicatur.
units.tr: Two things: its parts, and the things to which it is applied.

units.la: Quaenam sunt ejus partes?
units.tr: What are its parts?

units.la: Uncia,ein pfenning oder zwey loth. Sextans,zween pfenning / oder vier loth. Quadrans, <bl>drey pfenning/</bl> <bl>oder sechs loth.</bl> Triens, <bl>vier pfenning oder acht</bl> <bl>loth.</bl> Quincunx, <bl>fünff pfenning/oder zehen loth.</bl> Semissis, <bl>sechs pfenning/oder zwölff loth.</bl> Septunx, <bl>siben pfen-</bl> <bl>ning/ oder vierzehe loth.</bl> Bes vel bessis, <bl>acht pfenning</bl> <bl>oder sechs zehen loth.</bl> Dodrans, <bl>neun pfenning/oder</bl> <bl>achtzehe loth.</bl> Dextrans seu decunx, <bl>zehen pfenning/</bl> <bl>oder zwentzig loth.</bl> Deunx, <bl>eilff pfenning/ oder zwey</bl> <bl>vnd zweintzig loth.</bl> As vel assis, <bl>ein schilling oder vier</bl> <bl>vnd zwentzig loth.</bl>
units.tr: Uncia: one penny or two loth. Sextans: two pence or four loth. Quadrans: three pence or six loth. Triens: four pence or eight loth. Quincunx: five pence or ten loth. Semissis: six pence or twelve loth. Septunx: seven pence or fourteen loth. Bes or bessis: eight pence or sixteen loth. Dodrans: nine pence or eighteen loth. Dextans or decunx: ten pence or twenty loth. Deunx: eleven pence or twenty-two loth. As or assis: one shilling or twenty-four loth.

units.la: Quid est Semiuncia?
units.tr: What is a semiuncia?

units.la: Semiuncia vel semūcia est uncia dimidia, <bl>ein loth.</bl>
units.tr: A semiuncia or semuncia is half an uncia: one loth.

units.la: Quid est Sescunx?
units.tr: What is a sescunx?

units.la: Quot rebus attribuitur As?
units.tr: To how many things is the As applied?

units.la: Septem rebus: pecuniæ, libræ, pedi, zodiaco, jugero, hæreditati, usurae. Hæres ex asse, <bl>alles guts ein</bl> <bl>Erbe.</bl> Usura ex sextante est, cum centenarius binos parit, <bl>wen hundert zween wucher.</bl> Sic usura ex quadrante, triente, quincunce, semisse, &c. <bl>von hundert</bl> <bl>drey/vier/fünff/sechs/&c.</bl>
units.tr: To seven things: money, the pound, the foot, the zodiac, the acre, inheritance, and interest. An heir to the whole As is the sole heir to all the goods. Interest from the sextans is when a hundred yields two, that is, two in the hundred. So interest from the quadrans, triens, quincunx, semissis, and so on is three, four, five, six, and so on in the hundred.

units.la: Observatio notatu digna.
units.tr: A remark worth noting.

units.la: Sæpe à Regulis Generalibus Speciales in singulis Declinationibus traditæ impediuntur: ut, Propheta, etiamsi desinat in a, non tamen est generis fœminini, sed masculini: Quia Generalis Regula est, Quæ viro, aut rebus viri specie conceptis congruunt, sunt masculini generis. Sic Venus, Veneris, <bl>die Göttin der</bl> <bl>Buler</bl> / etiamsi desinat in us, & u in obliquis mutet, non tamen est generis neutrius, sed fœminini: Quia generalis regula est, Quæ mulieri, aut rebus mulieris specie conceptis congruunt, sunt fœminini generis.
units.tr: Often the special rules given under each declension hinder the general rules. Thus, propheta, although it ends in a, is not of feminine but of masculine gender, because the general rule is that words which agree with a man, or with things conceived in the form of a man, are of masculine gender. Likewise Venus, Veneris, "the goddess of lovers", although it ends in us and changes u in the oblique cases, is not of neuter but of feminine gender, because the general rule is that words which agree with a woman, or with things conceived in the form of a woman, are of feminine gender.

units.la: DE VERBO.
units.tr: ON THE VERB.

units.la: Quid est Verbum?
units.tr: What is a verb?

units.la: VErbum est vox numeri cum forma, persona, tempore & conjugatione.
units.tr: A verb is a word inflected for number, with form, person, tense and conjugation.

units.la: Quotuplex est forma Verbi?
units.tr: How many kinds of verb form are there?

units.la: Duplex: Prima, aut Secunda.
units.tr: Two: the first form and the second form.

units.la: Quid est prima forma?
units.tr: What is the first form?

units.la: Prima forma est, quando Thema definit in o: Ac si Latinè flecti possit in or, dicitur Verbum activum: ut, Amo, ich liebe / amor, ich werde geliebet. Si non possit Latinè flecti in or, dicitur Verbum neutrum: ut, Sedeo, ich sitze. Sum cum compositis etiam Neutrum dicitur. Vapulo, ich werde geschlagen / Ardeo, ich brenne / das ist / ich werde verbrandt / Liceo, ich werde geschetzet [?] / gefälset / Fio, ich werde / Veneo, ich werde verkaufft / Bene vel male audio, ich werde gelobet oder gelestert / habent significationem passivā.
units.tr: The first form is when the stem ends in o. If it can be turned into or in Latin, it is called an active verb, as amo, I love, and amor, I am loved. If it cannot be turned into or, it is called a neuter verb, as sedeo, I sit. Sum and its compounds are also called neuter. Vapulo, I am beaten; ardeo, I burn, that is, I am burnt; liceo, I am valued; fio, I become; veneo, I am sold; bene vel male audio, I am praised or I am slandered. These have a passive meaning.

units.la: Verba in sco habent in se passionem, & exponuntur per fio, ac Positivū vel Comparativum: ut, ægresco, id est, fio æger vel ægrior, ich werde kranck oder krencker. Crudesco, id est, fio crudus vel crudior, ich werde rohe oder roher. Multa sunt, inquit Valla lib. 1. cap 22. quæ pro suis primitivis accipiuntur: ut, Conticesco, ich schweige still. Adhæresco, ich hange an. Delitesco, ich bin verborgen. Concupisco, ich begere. Labasco, ich falle oder sincke. Obdormisco, ich entschlafe. Contremisco, ich erzittere. Expavesco, ich erschrecke. Et similia. Definentia autem in sco mutuatur primitivi praeteritum & supinum: ut, inveterasco, ich werde alt / inveteravi, inveteratum.
units.tr: Verbs in sco have the passive within themselves, and are explained by fio, with the positive or comparative: as aegresco, that is, I become sick or sicker; crudesco, that is, I become raw or rawer. Valla, book 1, chapter 22, says there are many which are taken for their primitives: as conticesco, I fall silent; adhaeresco, I cling to; delitesco, I lie hidden; concupisco, I desire; labasco, I fall or sink; obdormisco, I fall asleep; contremisco, I tremble; expavesco, I am terrified; and similar verbs. Verbs ending in sco borrow the perfect and supine of their primitive: as inveterasco, I grow old; inveteravi, inveteratum.

units.la: Verba in fio habent passionem extrinsecus allatā: ut, madefio, id est, humore aspergor, ich werde naß.
units.tr: Verbs in fio have a passion brought in from outside: as madefio, that is, I am sprinkled with moisture, I become wet.

units.la: Verba in to aut xo frequentem & vehementem actionem significant: ut, agito, <bl>ich thue fleissig /</bl> <bl>ich treibe.</bl> Nexo, <bl>ich knüpffe [?] embsich.</bl>
units.tr: Verbs in to or xo signify a frequent and vehement action: as agito, I busy myself diligently or I drive; nexo, I tie diligently or I knot busily.

units.la: Verba in rio, desiderium aut voluntatem significant: ut, parturio, id est, cupio vel volo parere, <bl>ich be-</bl> <bl>gere zu gebären.</bl> Praeter scaturio, <bl>ich quelle herfür / &</bl> <bl>scalpturio, ich trasse/scharre /</bl> quae idem cum primitivis significant. Usus spectandus.
units.tr: Verbs in rio signify desire or will: as parturio, that is, I desire or wish to bring forth, I long to give birth. Besides these there are scaturio, I gush forth, and scalpturio, I scrape or scratch, which mean the same as their primitives. Usage must be observed.

units.la: Quid est Persona?
units.tr: What is person?

units.la: Persona est specialis terminatio verbi. Estque triplex in utroq; numero: ut, singularis prima, Amo. Secunda, Amas. Tertia, Amat. Pluralis prima, Amamus. Secunda, Amatis, Tertia, amant.
units.tr: Person is the specific ending of a verb. It is threefold in each number: as singular, first, amo; second, amas; third, amat. Plural, first, amamus; second, amatis; third, amant.

units.la: Verbum, quod tres distinctas personas habet in utroq; numero, dicitur personale.
units.tr: A verb which has three distinct persons in each number is called personal.

units.la: Quid est Verbum impersonale?
units.tr: What is an impersonal verb?

units.la: Verbum impersonale est, quod in tertia tantum persona singulari conjugatur. Estq; Activae formae, aut Passivae. Activae: ut, Delectat, <bl>es belustiget / es</bl> <bl>erfrewet.</bl> Passivae: ut, Amatur, <bl>man liebet.</bl> Verbum impersonale in ur, etiamsi passivae formae sit, non tamen passionem significat, sed actionem: ut, pugnatur a nobis, id est, nos pugnamus.
units.tr: An impersonal verb is one conjugated only in the third person singular. It is of either the active or the passive form. Active: as delectat, it delights or pleases. Passive: as amatur, one loves. An impersonal verb in ur, although it is of the passive form, does not signify passion but action: as pugnatur a nobis, that is, we fight.

units.la: Verbum impersonale passivae formae un- de formatur?
units.tr: From what is an impersonal verb of the passive form formed?

units.la: A quolibet verbo Activo, & Neutro: ut, amatur, <bl>man liebet.</bl> Statur, <bl>man stehet.</bl> Docetur, <bl>man lehret.</bl> Fletur, <bl>man weinet / man greinet.</bl> Legitur, <bl>man liest.</bl> Curritur, <bl>man lauffet.</bl> Auditur, <bl>man höret.</bl> Dormitur, <bl>man schläffte.</bl> Horum Gerundia exeunt tantum in dum, & Supina in um: ut, Amandum est, <bl>man muß</bl> <bl>lieben.</bl> Standum est, <bl>man muß stehen.</bl> Amatum est vel fuit, <bl>man hat geliebet.</bl> Statum est vel fuit, <bl>man hat ge-</bl> <bl>standen.</bl> Conjuga verbum Sum per tertiam personanam, additis Gerundiis & Supinis.
units.tr: From any active or neuter verb: as amatur, one loves; statur, one stands; docetur, one teaches; fletur, one weeps or whines; legitur, one reads; curritur, one runs; auditur, one hears; dormitur, one sleeps. Their gerunds end only in dum, and their supines in um: as amandum est, one must love; standum est, one must stand; amatum est vel fuit, one has loved; statum est vel fuit, one has stood. Conjugate the verb sum in the third person, adding the gerunds and supines.

units.la: Quid est tempus?
units.tr: What is tense?

units.la: Tempus est differentia Verbi secundum praesens, praeteritum & futurum.
units.tr: Tense is the difference in a verb according to present, past and future.

units.la: Quot sunt tempora Verbi?
units.tr: How many tenses does a verb have?

units.la: Undecim : Primum praesens. Secundum praesens, Primum imperfectum, Secundum imperfectum, Primum perfectum, Secundum perfectu, Primum plusquam perfectum, Secundum plusquam perfectu, Primum futurum, Secundum futurum, Tertium futuru.
units.tr: Eleven: first present; second present; first imperfect; second imperfect; first perfect; second perfect; first pluperfect; second pluperfect; first future; second future; third future.

units.la: Quid est Conjugatio?
units.tr: What is conjugation?

units.la: Conjugatio est Verbi secundum personas & tempora flexio. Estq; quadruplex : Prima, Secunda, Tertia, Quarta.
units.tr: Conjugation is the inflection of a verb according to persons and tenses. It is fourfold: first, second, third and fourth.

units.la: Prima est, cujus prima persona pluralis primi praesentis temporis definit in amus vel amur : ut, Amo, amamus, Amor, amamur.
units.tr: The first is that whose first person plural of the first present tense ends in amus or amur: as amo, amamus; amor, amamur.

units.la: Secunda est, cujus prima persona pluralis primi praesentis temporis definit in emus vel emur: ut, Doceo, docemus, Doceor, docemur.
units.tr: The second is that whose first person plural of the first present tense ends in emus or emur: as doceo, docemus; doceor, docemur.

units.la: Tertia est, cujus prima persona pluralis primi praesentis temporis definit in imus vel imur penultima brevi: ut, Lego, legimus. Legor, legimur.
units.tr: The third is that whose first person plural of the first present tense ends in imus or imur with a short penultimate: as lego, legimus; legor, legimur.

units.la: Quarta est, cujus prima persona pluralis primi praesentis temporis definit in imus vel imur penultima longa: ut, audio, audimus, audior, audimur.
units.tr: The fourth is that whose first person plural of the first present tense ends in imus or imur with a long penultimate: as audio, audimus; audior, audimur.

units.la: Conjuga quædam verba formæ primæ, juxta quæ studiosi reliqua in o flectant. Primum praesens tempus.
units.tr: Conjugate some verbs of the first form, by which students may inflect the rest in o. First present tense.

units.la: Conjugatio Prima.
units.tr: First Conjugation.

units.la: Amo, ich <bl>liebe</bl> / amas, du <bl>liebest</bl> / amat, er <bl>liebet</bl> / amamus, wir <bl>lieben</bl> / amatis, ihr <bl>liebet</bl> / amant, sie <bl>lieben</bl>.
units.tr: Amo, I love / amas, you love / amat, he loves / amamus, we love / amatis, you love / amant, they love.

units.la: Coniugatio Secunda.
units.tr: Second Conjugation.

units.la: Doceo, ich lehre/ does, docet, docemus, docetis, docent.
units.tr: Doceo, I teach; the rest of the present conjugates through the persons.

units.la: Coniugatio Tertia.
units.tr: Third Conjugation.

units.la: Lego, ich lese/legis, legit, legimus, legitis, legunt.
units.tr: Lego, I read.

units.la: Coniugatio Quarta.
units.tr: Fourth Conjugation.

units.la: Audio, ich höre/ audis, audit, audimus, auditis, audiunt.
units.tr: Audio, I hear.

units.la: Coniugatio Anomala.
units.tr: Irregular Conjugation.

units.la: Fero, ich trage/ fers, fert, ferimus, fertis, ferunt.
units.tr: Fero, I carry.

units.la: Sum, ich bin/ es, est, sumus, estis, sunt.
units.tr: Sum, I am / es, est, sumus, estis, sunt.

units.la: Volo, ich will/ vis, vult, volumus, vultis, volunt.
units.tr: Volo, I will (I want).

units.la: Secundum praesens tempus.
units.tr: Second present tense.

units.la: Amem, ich kan oder mag oder soll lieben/ ames, du kanst oder magst oder solt lieben/ amet, er kan oder mag oder soll lieben/ amemus, lasset uns lieben/ oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen lieben/ ametis, ihr könnet oder möget oder sollet lieben/ ament, die können oder mögen oder sollen lieben.
units.tr: Amem, I can, may or should love / ames, you can, may or should love / amet, he can, may or should love / amemus, let us love, or we can, may or should love / ametis, you can, may or should love / ament, they can, may or should love.

units.la: Doceam, ich kan oder mag oder soll lehren/ doceas, doceat, doceamus, lasset uns lehren oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen lehren/ doceatis, ihr könnet oder möget oder sollet lehren/ doceant.
units.tr: Doceam, I can, may or should teach / doceas, doceat, doceamus, let us teach, or we can, may or should teach / doceatis, you can, may or should teach / doceant.

units.la: Legam, ich kan oder mag oder soll lesen/ legas, legat, legamus, lasset uns lesen oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen lesen/ legatis, legant.
units.tr: Legam, I can, may or should read / legas, legat, legamus, let us read, or we can, may or should read / legatis, legant.

units.la: Audiam, ich kan oder mag oder soll hören/ audias, audiat, audiamus, lasset uns hören oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen hören/ audiatis, audiant.
units.tr: Audiam, I can, may or should hear / audias, audiat, audiamus, let us hear, or we can, may or should hear / audiatis, audiant.

units.la: Feram, ich kan oder mag oder soll tragen/ feras, ferat, feramus, lasset uns tragen oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen tragen/ feratis, ferant.
units.tr: Feram, I can, may or should carry / feras, ferat, feramus, let us carry, or we can, may or should carry / feratis, ferant.

units.la: Sim, ich kan oder mag oder soll sein/ sis, sit, simus, lasset uns sein oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen sein/ sitis, sint.
units.tr: Sim, I can, may or shall be; let us be, or we can, may or shall be.

units.la: <bl>Velim, ich kan oder mag oder soll wöllen</bl>/ velis, velit, velimus, <bl>laßet uns wöllen oder wir können oder</bl> <bl>mögen oder sollen wöllen</bl>/ velitis, velint. Observandum, pro Germanicis vocibus, <bl>sol/ sölte/ sollen</bl>[?] interdum usurpari, <bl>muß/ müste/ müssen</bl>. Verba secundi praesentis temporis interdum sunt futuri temporis: ut, Faxit omnipotens Deus, ut Petrus cras amet, doceat, legat, &c. <bl>Der Allmechtige Gott gebe/ das</bl> <bl>Petrus morgen lieben/</bl> <bl>lehren/ lesen werde.</bl> Ramus in suis Scholis exempla ex Cicerone attulit.
units.tr: Velim, I can, may or should be willing / velis, velit, velimus, let us be willing, or we can, may or should be willing / velitis, velint. It should be observed that for the German words sol, sölte, sollen [?] are sometimes used, as well as muß, müste, müssen. Verbs of the second present tense are sometimes of the future tense, as: May almighty God grant that Peter love, teach, read tomorrow, etc. (Der Allmächtige Gott gebe, das Petrus morgen lieben, lehren, lesen werde.) Ramus in his Schools brought forward examples from Cicero.

units.la: Primum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: First imperfect tense.

units.la: Amabam, <bl>ich liebete/</bl> amabas,amabat,amabamus, amabatis,amabant.
units.tr: Amabam, I loved.

units.la: Docebam, <bl>ich lehrete</bl>/ docebas,docebat, docebamus,docebatis,docebant.
units.tr: Docebam, I taught.

units.la: Legebam, <bl>ich las</bl>/legebas,legebat,legebamus,legebatis,legebant.
units.tr: Legebam, I read.

units.la: Audiebam, <bl>ich hörete</bl>/ audiebas, audiebat, audiebamus,audiebatis,audiebant.
units.tr: Audiebam, I heard.

units.la: Ferebam, <bl>ich trug</bl>/ferebas, ferebat, ferebamus,ferebatis,ferebant.
units.tr: Ferebam, I carried.

units.la: Eram, <bl>ich war</bl>/ eras,erat, eramus,eratis,erant.
units.tr: Eram, I was.

units.la: Volebam,<bl>ich wolte</bl> / volebas,volebat,volebamus, volebatis,volebant.
units.tr: Volebam, I wanted.

units.la: Secundum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: Second imperfect tense.

units.la: Amarem, <bl>ich liebete oder ich köndte oder möchte</bl> <bl>oder wölte oder sölte lieben/</bl> amares, amaret, amaremus,amaretis,amarent.
units.tr: Amarem, I loved, or I could, might or would or should love / amares, amaret, amaremus, amaretis, amarent.

units.la: Docerem, <bl>ich lehrete oder ich köndte oder möchte</bl> <bl>oder wölte oder sölte lehren</bl> / doceres,doceret,doceremus,doceretis,docerent.
units.tr: Docerem, I taught, or I could, might or would or should teach / doceres, doceret, doceremus, doceretis, docerent.

units.la: Legerem, <bl>ich läse oder ich köndte oder möchte oder</bl> <bl>wölte oder sölte lesen</bl>/ legeres,legeret,legeremus,legeretis,legerent.
units.tr: Legerem, I read, or I could, might or would or should read / legeres, legeret, legeremus, legeretis, legerent.

units.la: Audirem, ich hörete oder ich köndte oder möchte oder wolte oder solte hören/ audires,audiret,audiremus,audiretis,audirent.
units.tr: Audirem, I heard, or I could, might or would or should hear / audires, audiret, audiremus, audiretis, audirent.

units.la: Forem, ich trüge oder ich köndte oder möchte oder wolte oder solte tragen / ferres, ferret, ferremus, ferretis,ferrent.
units.tr: Forem, I carried, or I could, might or would or should carry / ferres, ferret, ferremus, ferretis, ferrent.

units.la: Essem, ich were oder ich köndte oder möchte oder wolte oder solte sein / esses, esset,essemus,essetis, essent.
units.tr: Essem, I might, could, would or should be.

units.la: Vellem, ich wolte/oder ich köndte oder möchte oder solte wollen/ velles vellet,vellemus,velletis,vellent.
units.tr: Vellem, I wanted, or I could, might or would or should be willing / velles, vellet, vellemus, velletis, vellent.

units.la: Verba secundi imperfecti temporis sunt interdum praesentis temporis, interdum futuri: ut, Vellem adesset Antonius, Cicero, <bl>Ich wolte das jetz Antonius</bl> <bl>gegenwertig were.</bl> Si sciret paterfamilias qua hora fur venturus esset, vigilaret utiq; & non sineret perfodi domum suam. Matthæi 24. <bl>Wenn ein Hausva-</bl> <bl>ter wüste / welche stunde der Dieb kommen würde/so</bl> <bl>würde er freilich wachen / vnnd würde nit zulassen/</bl> <bl>daß sein hauß durchbrochen würde. Matth.24.</bl> Vide Scholas Rami. Adverbia: utinam,cum,& similia, quibus temporibus conveniant, in Syntaxi docetur.
units.tr: Verbs of the second imperfect tense are sometimes of the present tense, sometimes of the future: as, Vellem adesset Antonius, Cicero: I wish that Antonius were present now. Si sciret paterfamilias qua hora fur venturus esset, vigilaret utique, et non sineret perfodi domum suam (Matt. 24). If the householder knew at what hour the thief would come, he would surely keep watch and not allow his house to be broken into (Matt. 24). See the Schools of Ramus. The adverbs utinam, cum, and similar words, with which tenses they agree, is taught in the Syntax.

units.la: Primum perfectum tempus.
units.tr: First perfect tense.

units.la: Amavi, <bl>ich habe geliebet/</bl> amavisti, amavit, amavimus,amavistis,amaverunt vel amavere.
units.tr: Amavi, I have loved.

units.la: Docui ,<bl>ich habe gelehret /</bl> docuisti, docuit, docuimus,docuistis,docuerunt vel docuere.
units.tr: Docui, I have taught.

units.la: Legi,<bl>ich habe gelesen/</bl> legisti, legit, legimus, legistis,legerunt vel legere.
units.tr: Legi, I have read.

units.la: Audivi,<bl>ich habe gehöret /</bl> audivisti, audivit,audivimus,audivistis,audiverunt vel audivere.
units.tr: Audivi, I have heard.

units.la: Tuli, <bl>ich habe getragen /</bl> tulisti,tulit,tulimus,tulistis,tulerunt vel tulere.
units.tr: Tuli, I have carried.

units.la: Fui, <bl>ich bin gewesen/</bl> fuisti,fuit,fuimus,fuistis,fuerunt vel fuere.
units.tr: Fui, I have been.

units.la: Volui, ich habe gewolt/ voluisti, voluit, voluimus, voluistis, voluerunt vel voluere.
units.tr: Volui, I have wanted.

units.la: Perfectum primum producit tempora quinque: Rim, Ram, Sem, Ro, Se: formabit cætera præsens.
units.tr: The first perfect produces five tenses: Rim, Ram, Sem, Ro, Se; the present will form the rest.

units.la: Secundum perfectum tempus.
units.tr: The second perfect tense.

units.la: Amaverim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen lieben</bl>/ amaveris, amaverit, amaverimus, amaveritis, amaverint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to love (amaverim, amaveris, amaverit, amaverimus, amaveritis, amaverint).

units.la: Docuerim, <bl>ich habe kennen oder sollen lehren</bl> / docueris, docuerit, docuerimus, docueritis, docuerint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to know how to teach (docuerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Legerim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen lesen</bl>/ legeris, legerit, legerimus, legeritis, legerint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to read (legerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Audiverim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen hören</bl>/ audiveris, audiverit, audiverimus, audiveritis, audiverint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to hear (audiverim, and the following persons).

units.la: Tulerim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen tragen</bl>/ tuleris, tulerit, tulerimus, tuleritis, tulerint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to carry (tulerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Fuerim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen sein</bl> / fueris, fuerit, fuerimus, fueritis, fuerint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to be (fuerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Voluerim, <bl>ich habe können oder sollen wollen</bl>/ volueris, voluerit, voluerimus, volueritis, voluerint.
units.tr: I have been able or ought to be willing (voluerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Interdum hæc verba sic exponantur: <bl>ich habe</bl> <bl>geliebet / gelesen / gehöret / getragen / gewolt</bl>; in contextu scil. præsentibus Adverbiis.
units.tr: Sometimes these verbs may be explained thus: I have loved / read / heard / carried / wanted, namely where adverbs in the context so require.

units.la: Primum plusquam perfectum tempus.
units.tr: The first pluperfect tense.

units.la: Amaveram, <bl>ich hatte geliebet</bl>/ amaveras, amaverat, amaveramus, amaveratis, amaverant.
units.tr: I had loved (amaveram, and the following persons).

units.la: Docueram, <bl>ich hatte gelehret[?]</bl>/ docueras, docuerat, docueramus, docueratis, docuerant.
units.tr: I had taught (docueram, and the following persons).

units.la: Legeram, <bl>ich hatte gelesen</bl>/ legeras, legerat, legeramus, legeratis, legerant.
units.tr: I had read (legeram, and the following persons).

units.la: Audiveram, <bl>ich hatte gehöret</bl> / audiveras, audiverat, audiveramus, audiveratis, audiverant.
units.tr: I had heard (audiveram, and the following persons).

units.la: Tuleram, <bl>ich hatte getragen</bl>/ tuleras, tulerat, tuleramus, tuleratis, tulerant.
units.tr: I had carried (tuleram, and the following persons).

units.la: Fueram, <bl>ich war/oder was gewesen/oder gewest</bl>/ fueras, fuerat, fueramus, fueratis, fuerant.
units.tr: I had been, or I was, or I have been (fueram, and the following persons).

units.la: Volueram,ich hatte gewolt/volueras,voluerat,volueramus,voluératis,voluerant.
units.tr: I had wanted (volueram, and the following persons).

units.la: Secundum plusquam perfectum tempus.
units.tr: The second pluperfect tense.

units.la: Amavissem, ich hette geliebt / oder ich hette können oder sollen lieben / amavisses,amavisset,amavissemus,amavissetis,amavissent.
units.tr: I would have loved, or I would have been able or ought to love (amavissem, amavisses, amavisset, amavissemus, amavissetis, amavissent).

units.la: Docuissem,ich hette gelehret/oder ich hette können oder sollen lehren/ docuisses,docuisset,docuissemus, docuissetis,docuissent.
units.tr: I would have taught, or I would have been able or ought to teach (docuissem, and the following persons).

units.la: Legissem, ich hette gelesen / oder können oder sollen lesen/legisses,legisset,legissemus,legissetis,legissent.
units.tr: I would have read, or I would have been able or ought to read (legissem, and the following persons).

units.la: Audivissem,ich hette gehöret/oder können oder sollen hören/ audivisses, audivisset,audivissemus,audivissetis,audivissent.
units.tr: I would have heard, or I would have been able or ought to hear (audivissem, and the following persons).

units.la: Tulissem, ich hette getragen/oder ich hette können oder sollen tragen / tulisses, tulisset,tulissemus,tulissetis,tulissent.
units.tr: I would have carried, or I would have been able or ought to carry (tulissem, and the following persons).

units.la: Fuissem,ich were gewesen/ oder ich köndte oder solte gewesen sein / fuisses,fuisset,fuissemus,fuissetis, fuissent.
units.tr: I would have been, or I could or ought to have been (fuissem, and the following persons).

units.la: Voluissem, ich hette gewolt / voluisses, voluisset, voluissemus,voluissetis,voluissent. Exempla, inquit Linacer de emend. str.[?] lib 1. de modo, hujus temporis in potentiæ significatione rara invenio.
units.tr: I would have wanted (voluissem, and the following persons). Examples, says Linacre in his work on the emendation of structure, book 1, on mood: I find this tense rare in the sense of possibility.

units.la: Primum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The first future tense.

units.la: Amabo, ich wil oder werde oder soll lieben / amabis,amabit,amabimus,amabitis,amabunt.
units.tr: I will, or shall, or ought to love (amabo, amabis, amabit, amabimus, amabitis, amabunt).

units.la: Docebo , ich will oder werde oder soll lehren / docebis,docebit,docebimus,docebitis,docebunt.
units.tr: I will, or shall, or ought to teach (docebo, and the following persons).

units.la: Legam , ich will oder werde oder soll lesen / leges, leget,legemus,legetis,legent.
units.tr: I will, or shall, or ought to read (legam, and the following persons).

units.la: Audiam , ich will oder werde oder soll hören / audies,audiet,audiemus,audietis,audient.
units.tr: I will, or shall, or ought to hear (audiam, and the following persons).

units.la: Feram,ich will oder werde oder soll tragen/ feres, feret,feremus, feretis ferent.
units.tr: I will, or shall, or ought to carry (feram, and the following persons).

units.la: Ero, ich will oder werde oder soll sein/ eris,erit,erimus,eritis,erunt.
units.tr: Ero: I will, or shall, or ought to be.

units.la: Volam, ich werd oder soll wöllen/ voles,volet,volemus,voletis,volent.
units.tr: Volam: I will, or shall, or ought to be willing.

units.la: Secundum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The second future tense.

units.la: Amavero vel amaverim,ich will geliebet haben/ oder ich werde oder soll lieben/ amaveris,amaverit,amaverimus,amaveritis,amaverint.
units.tr: I will have loved, or I will, shall or ought to love (amavero or amaverim, and the following persons).

units.la: Docuero,vel docuerim,ich will gelehret haben/ oder ich werde oder soll lehren/docueris,docuerit,docuerimus,docueritis,docuerint.
units.tr: I will have taught, or I will, shall or ought to teach (docuero or docuerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Legero vel legerim, ich will gelesen haben / oder ich werde oder soll lesen / legeris, legerit, legerimus, legeritis,legerint.
units.tr: I will have read, or I will, shall or ought to read (legero or legerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Audivero vel audiverim, ich will gehöret haben/ oder ich werde oder soll hören / audiveris, audiverit, audiverimus,audiveritis,audiverint.
units.tr: I will have heard, or I will, shall or ought to hear (audivero or audiverim, and the following persons).

units.la: Tulero vel tulerim, ich will getragen haben/ oder ich werde oder soll tragen/tuleris,tulerit,tulerimus, tuleritis,tulerint.
units.tr: I will have carried, or I will, shall or ought to carry (tulero or tulerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Fuero vel fuerim, ich will gewesen sein / oder ich werde oder soll sein / fueris,fuerit,fuerimus,fueritis, fuerint.
units.tr: I will have been, or I will, shall or ought to be (fuero or fuerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Voluero vel voluerim, ich will gewolt haben/ oder ich werde oder soll wellen / volueris, voluerit, voluerimus,voluueritis,voluerint.
units.tr: I will have wanted, or I will, shall or ought to want (voluero or voluerim, and the following persons).

units.la: Intra horam meam lectionem didicero: innert halb eine stunde will ich meine lection gelehrnet haben. Nihil ignoveris, nihil gratiæ causâ feceris,apud Cicer.Du solt nichts nachlassen/nichts soltu dancks oder gnaden halben thun.
units.tr: Intra horam meam lectionem didicero: within half an hour I will have learned my lesson. Nihil ignoveris, nihil gratiae causa feceris: as Cicero has it, "You shall overlook nothing; you shall do nothing for the sake of thanks or favour."

units.la: Tertium futurum tempus.
units.tr: The third future tense.

units.la: Ama vel amato tu, liebe du/ amato ille, er liebe/amate vel amatote vos,liebet ihr/ amanto illi, sie liebe.
units.tr: Love (ama or amato) you, love; he shall love (amato ille); love (amate or amatote) you, you shall love; they shall love (amanto illi).

units.la: Doce,vel doceto tu, lehre du/ doceto ille, er lehre/ docete, vel docetote vos, <bl>lehret ihr</bl>[?] / docento illi, <bl>sie</bl> <bl>lehren.</bl>
units.tr: Teach (doce or doceto) you, teach; he shall teach (doceto ille); teach (docete or docetote) you, you shall teach; they shall teach (docento illi).

units.la: Lege vel legito tu, <bl>lese du</bl> / legito ille, <bl>er lese</bl> / legite vel legitote vos, <bl>leset ihr</bl> / legunto illi, <bl>sie lesen.</bl>
units.tr: Read (lege or legito) you, read; he shall read (legito ille); read (legite or legitote) you, you shall read; they shall read (legunto illi).

units.la: Audi vel audito tu, <bl>höre du</bl> / audito ille, <bl>er höre</bl> / audite vel auditote vos, <bl>höret ihr</bl> / audiunto illi, <bl>sie hören.</bl>
units.tr: Hear (audi or audito) you, hear; he shall hear (audito ille); hear (audite or auditote) you, you shall hear; they shall hear (audiunto illi).

units.la: Fer vel ferto tu, <bl>trage du</bl> / ferto ille, <bl>er trage</bl> / ferte vel fertote vos, <bl>traget ihr</bl> / ferunto illi, <bl>sie tragen.</bl>
units.tr: Carry (fer or ferto) you, carry; he shall carry (ferto ille); carry (ferte or fertote) you, you shall carry; they shall carry (ferunto illi).

units.la: Es vel esto tu, <bl>sey du</bl> / esto ille, <bl>er sey</bl> / este vel estote vos, <bl>seid ihr</bl> / sunto illi, <bl>sie seien.</bl> Interdum haec verba sic exponantur: <bl>Du solt</bl> / <bl>er soll</bl> / <bl>ihr sollet</bl> / <bl>sie sollen</bl> / <bl>lieben</bl> / <bl>lehren</bl> / <bl>lesen</bl> / <bl>hören</bl> / <bl>tragen.</bl>
units.tr: Be (es or esto) you, be; he shall be (esto ille); be (este or estote) you, you shall be; they shall be (sunto illi). Sometimes these forms may be explained thus: you shall / he shall / you (pl.) shall / they shall, with love / teach / read / hear / carry.

units.la: Verba tertij futuri in imperando & precando usurpantur frequentissimè: ut, Ne hominem occidito, Ne adulterato, falsum testimonium ne dicito. Vide Dialogos Castalionis, <bl>Du solt keinen menschen töd-ten, du solt nicht ehebrechen,</bl> <bl>du solt kein falsch zeugnis reden.</bl>
units.tr: The forms of the third future are used very frequently in commanding and in praying, as: "Do not kill anyone; do not commit adultery; do not give false testimony." See the Dialogues of Castellio: "You shall not kill anyone; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not speak false witness."

units.la: Verba mea auribus percipe Domine: Intellige clamorem meum: intende voci orationis meæ, Psal. 5. <bl>Meine wort vernim mit den ohren Herr: verstehe</bl> <bl>mein geschrey: merck auff die stim meines gebetts.</bl>[?]
units.tr: "Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry; hearken unto the voice of my prayer," Psalm 5. "Hear my words with your ears, Lord; understand my cry; attend to the voice of my prayer."

units.la: Modorum doctrina prorsus est ex Grammatica explodenda: quippe quum usu falsa esse deprehendatur. Nam hæc Terentij verba: Quid feci? quid commerui? aut peccavi pater? falsò dicuntur indicativi modi: quia non sunt verba indicatis, sed interrogantis.
units.tr: The doctrine of moods must be entirely discarded from grammar, since in use it is found to be false. For these words of Terence, "What have I done? What have I deserved? Or have I sinned, father?", are wrongly called indicative mood, because they are not words of asserting but of questioning.

units.la: Sic hæc Legis verba. Non occides. Non furtum facies; falsò creduntur esse indicativi modi: quia non sunt verba simpliciter indicantis, sed imperantis.
units.tr: Likewise these words of the Law, "You shall not kill. You shall not steal," are wrongly believed to be indicative, because they are not words of simply asserting but of commanding.

units.la: Sic hoc verbum Ciceronis pro Ligario: Ignosce pater; falsò dicitur imperativi modi: quia Cicero non imperat, sed precatur.
units.tr: Likewise this saying of Cicero in the Pro Ligario, "Forgive, father," is wrongly called imperative, because Cicero is not commanding but praying.

units.la: Sic hæc verba apud Ciceronem: Nihil ignoveris. Nihil feceris; falsò creduntur esse Subjunctivi modi: quia non sunt verba subjungentis, sed imperantis.
units.tr: Likewise these words in Cicero, "You shall overlook nothing; you shall do nothing," are wrongly believed to be subjunctive, because they are not words of subjoining but of commanding.

units.la: Hactenus finita verba, quæ certos numeros ac personas habent, conjugavimus: Infinita verba, quæ per se certos numeros ac personas nō habent, sequuntur.
units.tr: Thus far we have conjugated those verbs which have definite numbers and persons. The infinite verbs, which of themselves have no definite numbers and persons, follow.

units.la: Præsens & imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: Present and imperfect tense.

units.la: Amare, <bl>lieben</bl>. Docere, <bl>lehren</bl>. Legere, <bl>lesen</bl>. Audire, <bl>hören</bl>. Ferre, <bl>tragen</bl>. Esse, <bl>sein</bl>. Velle, <bl>wollen</bl>.
units.tr: Amare, to love. Docere, to teach. Legere, to read. Audire, to hear. Ferre, to bear. Esse, to be. Velle, to will.

units.la: Perfectum & plusquam perfectum tempus.
units.tr: Perfect and pluperfect tense.

units.la: Amavisse, <bl>geliebet haben</bl>. Docuisse, <bl>gelehret haben</bl>. Legisse, <bl>gelesen haben</bl>. Audivisse, <bl>gehöret haben</bl>. Tulisse, <bl>getragen haben</bl>. Fuisse, <bl>gewesen sein</bl>. Voluisse, <bl>gewolt haben</bl>.
units.tr: Amavisse, to have loved. Docuisse, to have taught. Legisse, to have read. Audivisse, to have heard. Tulisse, to have borne. Fuisse, to have been. Voluisse, to have willed.

units.la: Futurum tempus eleganter hoc pacto circunloquimur. Me, te, illum, Nos, vos, illos, Amatum [illegible, ~6 letters] Me, te, illum, amaturum esse. Doctum Nos, vos, illos, amaturos esse. Lectum Auditum Latum <bl>Das ich/du/er/ Wir/ihr/sie/</bl> <bl>Lieben</bl> <bl>Lehren</bl> <bl>Lesen</bl> <bl>Hören</bl> <bl>Tragen</bl> <bl>werden.</bl>
units.tr: We express the future tense elegantly in this way: Me, te, illum (that I, you, he) ... amaturum esse, to be going to love; Nos, vos, illos (that we, you, they) ... amaturos esse, to be going to love. Likewise with doctum, lectum, auditum, latum: that I, you, he, we, you, they will love, teach, read, hear, bear. In German: "that I/you/he/we/you/they will" with love, teach, read, hear, bear.

units.la: Jam finita & infinita verba cōjugavimus: Sequuntur Gerundia & Supina, quæ specie nominalis casus flectuntur.
units.tr: Having conjugated the finite and infinite verbs, there follow the gerunds and supines, which are inflected in the manner of nouns.

units.la: Gerundia : ut,
units.tr: Gerunds, for example:

units.la: Amandi, <bl>zu lieben</bl> / amandum, <bl>zu lieben</bl> / amando, <bl>mit lieben</bl>.
units.tr: Amandi, of loving / amandum, to love / amando, with loving.

units.la: Docendi, <bl>zu lehren</bl> / docendum, <bl>zu lehren</bl> / docendo, <bl>mit lehren</bl>. <bl>Legendi, zu lesen / legendum, zu lesen / legendo, mit lesen.</bl>
units.tr: Docendi, of teaching / docendum, to teach / docendo, with teaching. Legendi, of reading / legendum, to read / legendo, with reading.

units.la: Gerundium, quod ficut Legendi flectitur, nonnunquam e in u mutat: ut, pro faciendi, faciendum, faciendo, dicitur etiam faciundi, faciundum, faciundo. Sic Dividundi, dividundum, dividundo.
units.tr: The gerund, which is inflected like legendi, sometimes changes e into u: for faciendi, faciendum, faciendo, one also says faciundi, faciundum, faciundo. Likewise dividundi, dividundum, dividundo.

units.la: Audiendi, <bl>zu hören / audiendum, zu hören / audien-</bl> <bl>do, mit hören.</bl>
units.tr: Audiendi, of hearing / audiendum, to hear / audiendo, with hearing.

units.la: Ferendi, <bl>zu tragen / ferendum, zu tragen / ferendo,</bl> <bl>mit tragen.</bl>
units.tr: Ferendi, of bearing / ferendum, to bear / ferendo, with bearing.

units.la: Supina: ut,
units.tr: Supines, for example:

units.la: Amatum, <bl>zu lieben</bl> / amatu, <bl>vom lieben.</bl> Doctum, <bl>zu lehren</bl> / doctu, <bl>vom lehren.</bl> Lectum, <bl>zu lesen</bl> / lectu, <bl>vom lesen.</bl> Auditum, <bl>zu hören</bl> / auditu, <bl>vom hören.</bl> Latum, <bl>zu tragen</bl> / latu, <bl>vom tragen.</bl>
units.tr: Amatum, to love / amatu, from loving. Doctum, to teach / doctu, from teaching. Lectum, to read / lectu, from reading. Auditum, to hear / auditu, from hearing. Latum, to bear / latu, from bearing.

units.la: Recita Verba sicut Amo conjuganda, quæ perfecta & supina variant.
units.tr: Recite the verbs that are conjugated like Amo, and which vary in the perfect and supine.

units.la: Accubo, <bl>ich lige neben einem / ich lige bey</bl> / accubui, accubitum.
units.tr: Accubo, I lie beside someone / I lie at table; accubui, accubitum.

units.la: Coeno, <bl>ich halte abendmal</bl> / coenavi & coenat° [?] sum.
units.tr: Coeno, I hold the evening meal / I dine; coenavi & coenat[?] sum.

units.la: Consto, <bl>ich bin standhafftig / ich tosste</bl> / constiti, constitum.
units.tr: Consto, I am steadfast / I stand firm; constiti, constitum.

units.la: Crepo, <bl>ich thene [?] / ich rühme</bl> / crepui, crepitum.
units.tr: Crepo, I creak / I boast; crepui, crepitum.

units.la: Circundo, <bl>ich umgebe / ich umringe</bl> / circundedi, circundatum.
units.tr: Circundo, I surround / I encircle; circundedi, circundatum.

units.la: Discrepo, <bl>ich laute anders / ich bin ungleich</bl> / discrepavi & discrepui, discrepitum.
units.tr: Discrepo, I sound differently / I am unlike; discrepavi & discrepui, discrepitum.

units.la: Domo, <bl>ich mache jam / ich mache gehorsam</bl> / domui, domitum.
units.tr: Domo, I tame / I make obedient; domui, domitum.

units.la: Do, <bl>ich gebe</bl> / dedi, datum.
units.tr: Do, I give; dedi, datum.

units.la: Emico, <bl>ich gleuße herfür</bl> / emicui, absq; supino.
units.tr: Emico, I spurt forth / I gleam out; emicui, no supine.

units.la: Enecco, <bl>ich ertödte / ich bringe umb</bl> / enecui, enectū.
units.tr: Enecco, I kill / I do to death; enecui, enectum.

units.la: Explico, <bl>ich wickle auff / ich lege auß</bl> / explicavi &
units.tr: Explico, I unroll / I set out; explicavi &

units.la: explicai[?],explicatum & explicitum.
units.tr: explicai[?], explicatum & explicitum.

units.la: Exto,<bl>ich bin vorhanden/ich</bl>
units.tr: Exto, I am present / I

units.la: <bl>bin</bl>/extiti,extitum.
units.tr: am; extiti, extitum.

units.la: Frico,<bl>ich reibe/ich kratze</bl>/fricui,frictum.
units.tr: Frico, I rub / I scratch; fricui, frictum.

units.la: Increpo, <bl>ich rausche / ich schelte/ straffe</bl>/ increpui
units.tr: Increpo, I rattle / I scold / I rebuke; increpui

units.la: & increpavi,increpatum.
units.tr: & increpavi, increpatum.

units.la: Lavo,<bl>ich wasche/bade</bl>/lavi,lavatum & lotum.
units.tr: I wash / I bathe (the perfect and supine vary).

units.la: Mico,<bl>ich scheine/glitzere</bl>/micui,absq; supino.
units.tr: Mico, I shine / I glitter; micui, no supine.

units.la: Necco,<bl>ich tödte</bl>/necavi & necui,necatum.
units.tr: Necco, I kill; necavi & necui, necatum.

units.la: Pessundo, <bl>ich trette mit füssen /</bl> pessundedi, pef-
units.tr: Pessundo, I trample underfoot; pessundedi, pes-

units.la: sundatum.
units.tr: sundatum.

units.la: Præsto,<bl>ich übertreffe/ich leiste</bl>/præstiti,præstitū.
units.tr: Praesto, I surpass / I perform; praestiti, praestitum.

units.la: Poto, <bl>ich trincke / ich sauffe</bl> / potavi, potatum &
units.tr: Poto, I drink / I guzzle; potavi, potatum &

units.la: potum.
units.tr: potum.

units.la: Plico, <bl>ich falte/ich wickele</bl>/ plicavi,&plicui,plica-
units.tr: Plico, I fold / I wrap; plicavi, & plicui, plicatum & plicitum.

units.la: tum & plicitum.
units.tr: [see previous line; the text continues below]

units.la: Satisfdo[?], <bl>ich thue versicherung mit Bürgen</bl> / satis-
units.tr: Satisfdo[?], I give security with sureties; satis-

units.la: dedi,satisfatum.
units.tr: dedi, satisfatum.

units.la: Seco,<bl>ich schneide/ich hawe</bl>/secui,sectum.
units.tr: Seco, I cut / I hew; secui, sectum.

units.la: Sono,<bl>ich laute/ich klinge</bl>/sonui,sonitum.
units.tr: Sono, I sound / I ring; sonui, sonitum.

units.la: Sto,<bl>ich stehe/ich bin unbeweglich</bl>/steti,statum.
units.tr: Sto, I stand / I am immovable; steti, statum.

units.la: Tono,<bl>ich Dene fast/ich Donbere</bl>/tonui,tonitum.
units.tr: Tono, I thunder / I roar loudly; tonui, tonitum.

units.la: Juvo,<bl>ich helffe/ich leiste beystand</bl>/juvi,jutum.
units.tr: Juvo, I help / I give aid; juvi, jutum.

units.la: Veto,<bl>ich verbiete</bl>/vetui,vetitum.
units.tr: Veto, I forbid; vetui, vetitum.

units.la: Venundo,<bl>ich verkauffe</bl>/venundedi,venundatum.
units.tr: Venundo, I sell, venundedi, venundatum.

units.tr: Recite the verbs as you conjugate Doceo, which vary in the perfect

units.la: fecta & Supina variant.
units.tr: The perfect and supine vary.

units.la: Audeo,<bl>ich bin kün/ich darff</bl>/ aufus sum vel fui,
units.tr: I dare / I am bold / I may.

units.la: aufum.
units.tr: (The supine follows the same pattern.)

units.la: Augeo,<bl>ich mehre/ich mache grösser</bl>/auxi,auctum.
units.tr: I increase / I make greater.

units.la: Aboleo,<bl>ich tilge auß/ich mache zunichte</bl>/ abolevi,
units.tr: I wipe out / I bring to nothing.

units.la: abolctum & abolitum.
units.tr: (The supine forms vary.)

units.la: Adoleo, <bl>ich opffere mit fewr: auff/ich zünde an</bl>/a-
units.tr: I offer by fire / I kindle upon.

units.la: dolevi & adolui.
units.tr: dolevi & adolui.
