units.tr: Algeo, I suffer from cold / I am freezing: alsi, no supine. Ardeo, I burn / I suffer from heat: arsi, arsum. Attondeo, I shave / I shear off: attondi, attonsum. Careo, I lack: carui, cassum & caritum. Caveo, I beware: cavi, cautum. Censeo, I value / I think: censui, censum. Cieo, I move: civi, citum. Concieo, I summon together / I stir up: concivi, concitum. Conniveo, I blink / I overlook (look through my fingers): connixi, no supine. Debeo, I am obliged / I owe: debui, debitum. Demulceo, I stroke / I appease / I soothe: demulsi, demulsum. Dependeo, I hang down: dependi, no supine. Despondeo, I promise / I despair: despondi, desponsum. Deleo, I blot out / I wipe out: delevi, deletum. Faveo, I favour: favi, fautum. Ferveo, I seethe / I glow: ferbui, no supine. Foveo, I warm / I keep warm: fovi, fotum. Fleo, I weep / I whimper: flevi, fletum. (no.) Frigeo, I am chilled / I am cold: frixi, no supine. Fulgeo, I shine / I gleam: fulsi, no supine. Gaudeo, I rejoice / I take delight in a thing: gavisus sum, or fui gavisum. Habeo, I have: habui, habitum. Haereo, I hang / I cling: haesi, haesum. Impleo, I fill: implevi, impletum. Indulgeo, I indulge / I cherish: indulsi, indultum. Luceo, I shine / I give light: luxi, no supine. Lugeo, I wail / I mourn: luxi, luctum. Maneo, I remain: mansi, mansum. Mereo, I serve for pay: merui, meritum. Mœreo, I grieve / I lament: mœstus sum vel fui. Misceo, I confuse / I mix: miscui, mixtum & mistum. Moveo, I move / I drive out: movi, motum. Mordeo, I bite / I slander: momordi, morsum. Mulgeo, I milk out: mulsi, mulctum. Mulceo, I stroke / I soothe: mulsi, mulsum. Neo, I spin / I sew: nevi, netum. Noceo, I harm: nocui, nocitum. Oboleo, I stink / I perceive: obolevi & obolui, obolitum. Placeo, I please: placui, placitum. Paveo, I fear: pavi, no supine. Prandeo, I dine at midday: prandi & pransus sum. Polluceo, I offer or hold splendidly: polluxi, pollustum. Pendeo, I hang / I doubt: pependi, no supine. Redoleo, I smell of something: redolevi & redolui, no supine. Rideo, I laugh / I mock: risi, risum. Recenseo, I muster / I recount: recensui, recensum & recensitum. Suadeo, I advise / I urge: suasi, suasum. Sedeo, I sit: sedi, sessum. Soleo, I am accustomed: solitus sum vel fui. Sorbeo, I sip / I slurp: sorbui & sorpsi, sorptum. Strideo, I creak / I whistle: stridi, no supine. Spondeo, I promise / I pledge: spopondi, sponsum. Torreo, I parch / I roast: torrui, tostum. Teneo, I hold: tenui, tentum. Tondeo, I shear: totondi, tonsum. Torqueo, I twist / I torment: torsi, tortum. Turgeo, I am swollen / puffed up: tursi, no supine. Urgeo, I press / I compel: ursi, no supine. Jubeo, I bid / I command: jussi, jussum. Video, I see: vidi, visum. Vieo, I bind / I bend: vievi[?], vietum. Voveo, I vow / I make a vow: vovi, votum.

units.tr: Recite the verbs as I read them out, which vary in the perfect and supine: Agnosco, I recognise again, agnovi, agnitum. Abdo, I hide / I put away, abdidi, abditum. Abscondo, I hide, abscondi or abscondidi, absconditum. Accumbo, I sit down at table, accubui, accubitum; so the rest compounded from Cubo. Adolesco, I grow up / I become great, adolevi, adultum. Accendo, I kindle, accendi, accensum. Ascendo, I climb up / I go up, ascendi, ascensum. Affligo, I throw to the ground / I afflict, afflixi, afflictum. Ago, I do / I deal with, egi, actum. (ctum.) Alo, I nourish / I sustain, alui, alitum and altum. Adimo, I take away / I free from, ademi, ademptum. Accino, I sing to, accinui, accentum. Assero, I affirm / I assert, asserui, assertum. Accerso, I summon / I call for, accersivi, accersitum. Arcesso, I accuse / I summon, arcessivi, arcessitum. Aspicio, I look at, aspexi, aspectum. Arguo, I point out / I rebuke, argui, argutum. Bibo, I drink, bibi, bibitum. Cano, I sing / I play, cecini, cantum. Cado, I fall, cecidi, casum. Capio, I seize / I receive, cepi, captum. Capesso, I lay hold of, capessi, without supine. Carpo, I break off / I speak ill of, carpsi, carptum. Claudo, I shut / I conclude, clausi, clausum. Cedo, I yield / I go to / I fall to, cessi, cessum. Caedo, I strike / I cut down, cecidi, caesum. Credo, I believe / I trust, credidi, creditum. Cresco, I grow / I increase, crevi, cretum. Cingo, I gird / I surround, cinxi, cinctum. Clepo, I steal, clepsi, cleptum. Confuesco, I become accustomed, confuevi, confuetum. Confido, I rely on something, confidi and confisus sum. Cognosco, I know / I recognise, cognovi, cognitum. units.la: Recita verba, sicut Audio conjuganda, quæper- fecta & supina variant.
units.tr: Recite the verbs as they are conjugated, as with audio, whose perfects and supines vary.

units.la: Aperio, <bl>ich thu auff/ich öffne/</bl>aperui, apertum. Abeo, <bl>ich gehe hinweg/</bl>abivi, abitum. Amicio, <bl>ich bekleide/</bl>amicivi, amictum. Cio, <bl>ich bewege/</bl>civi, citum. Concio, <bl>ich bewege/ richte an / ich berüffe zusam-</bl> <bl>men /</bl> concivi, concitum, penultima longa: Concitum, penultima brevi, est à verbo Concieo. Confentio, <bl>ich bewillige/ ich hält es mit einem/</bl> confensi, confensum. Comperio, <bl>ich erfahre/</bl>comperi, compertum. Farcio, <bl>ich erfülle/ ich meste[?]/</bl>farsi, fartum. Fulcio, <bl>ich unterstütze/ vestige/</bl>fulsi, fultum. Haurio, <bl>ich ziehe heraus/</bl> hausi, haustum. Irraucio, <bl>ich bin heiser/</bl>irrausi, irrausum. Operio, <bl>ich bedecke/ ich beschliesse/</bl>operui, opertū. Reperio, <bl>ich finde ohn geferd / ich erlange / ich</bl> <bl>er-dencke/</bl>reperi, repertum. Sancio, <bl>ich ordene/ ich gebe ein gesetz/</bl>sancivi & sanxi, sancitum & sanctum. Salio, <bl>ich springe/</bl>salij & salui, saltum. Sarcio, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>flicke zusamen/ ich erstatte/</bl>sarsi[?], sartū. Sentio, <bl>ich empfinde/ mercke/ hatte[?]/</bl>sensi[?], sensum. Sepio, <bl>ich verzeuue[?]/ verhindere/</bl>sepsi, septum. Sepelio, <bl>ich begrabe/</bl>sepelivi, sepultum. Venio, <bl>ich komme/</bl>veni, ventum. Veneo, <bl>ich werde verkaufft/</bl>venivi, venum. Vincio, <bl>ich binde/</bl>vinxi, vinctum.
units.tr: Aperio, I open, aperui, apertum. Abeo, I go away, abivi, abitum. Amicio, I clothe, amicivi, amictum. Cio, I stir up, civi, citum. Concio, I stir up, arouse, or summon together, concivi, concitum, with the penultimate long; concitum with the penultimate short comes from the verb concieo. Confentio, I consent, or I side with someone, confensi, confensum. Comperio, I learn, comperi, compertum. Farcio, I stuff or fill, farsi, fartum. Fulcio, I support or prop up, fulsi, fultum. Haurio, I draw out, hausi, haustum. Irraucio, I am hoarse, irrausi, irrausum. Operio, I cover or close up, operui, opertum. Reperio, I find by chance, I obtain, or I devise, reperi, repertum. Sancio, I ordain or enact a law, sancivi and sanxi, sancitum and sanctum. Salio, I leap, salui and salii, saltum. Sarcio, I patch together or make good, sarsi, sartum. Sentio, I feel, perceive, or ..., sensi, sensum. Sepio, I fence in or hinder, sepsi, septum. Sepelio, I bury, sepelivi, sepultum. Venio, I come, veni, ventum. Veneo, I am sold, venivi, venum. Vincio, I bind, vinxi, vinctum.

units.la: In primo imperfecto verbi, Eo, dicimus ibam non iebam in primo futuro Eam & ibo in Gerudio, Eundi, eundum, eundo cum Compositis.
units.tr: In the first imperfect of the verb eo we say ibam, not iebam; in the first future, eam and ibo; in the gerund, eundi, eundum, eundo, and likewise with the compounds.

units.la: Hactenus de integris Verbis primæ formæ: sequutur Defectiva, quæ persona vel tempore deficiunt.
units.tr: So much for the complete verbs of the first form. There follow the defective verbs, which lack a person or a tense.

units.la: Conjuga Ajo.
units.tr: Conjugate ajo.

units.la: Primum præsens: Ajo, ich sage/ ais, du sagst/ ait, er sagt. Ajunt, sie sagen. Primum imperfectum: Ajebam, ich sagete/ ajebas, ajebat, &c.
units.tr: First present: ajo, I say; ais, you say; ait, he says. Ajunt, they say. First imperfect: ajebam, I was saying; ajebas, ajebat, etc.

units.la: Conjuga Salve, Ave, Vale.
units.tr: Conjugate salve, ave, vale.

units.la: Tertium futurum: Salve, sey gegriesset/ Ave, Gott grüß Dich/ Vale, Gott friste dich lange gesund. Salvete, avete, valete. Infinita: Salvere, avere, valere.
units.tr: Third future: salve, be greeted; ave, God greet you; vale, may God keep you long in health. Salvete, avete, valete. Infinitive: salvere, avere, valere.

units.la: Conjuga Ausim.
units.tr: Conjugate ausim.

units.la: Secundum præsens: Ausim, ich darff oder dörffte/ ausis, ausit. Pluraliter: Ausint.
units.tr: Second present: ausim, I dare or might dare; ausis, ausit. Plural: ausint.

units.la: Conjuga Faxim.
units.tr: Conjugate faxim.

units.la: Secundum præsens: Faxim, ich mache oder verschaffe/ faxis, faxit, faximus, faxitis, faxint. Primum, futurum: Faxo, ich werde machen/ faxis, faxit. Pluraliter: faxunt.
units.tr: Second present: faxim, I make or bring it about; faxis, faxit, faximus, faxitis, faxint. First future: faxo, I will make; faxis, faxit. Plural: faxunt.

units.la: Conjuga Forem.
units.tr: Conjugate forem.

units.la: Secundum imperfectũ: Forem, ich werde oder sölte sein/ fores, foret. Pluraliter: Forent. Infiniti futurum: Fore, sein werden.
units.tr: Second imperfect: forem, I would be or ought to be; fores, foret. Plural: forent. Future infinitive: fore, to be going to be.

units.la: Conjuga Fio.
units.tr: Conjugate fio.

units.la: Primum præsens: Fio, ich werde/ fis, fit. Pluraliter: Fiunt. Secundum præsens: Fiam, fias, fiat, fiamus, fiatis, fiant. Primum imperfectũ: Fiebam, fiebas, &c. Secundum imperfectum: Fierem, fieres, fieret, &c. Perfectum: Factus sum vel fui, &c. Infinitum: Fieri. Futurum: Factum iri. Adjeƈt. participial. faciendus.
units.tr: First present: fio, I become; fis, fit. Plural: fiunt. Second present: fiam, fias, fiat, fiamus, fiatis, fiant. First imperfect: fiebam, fiebas, etc. Second imperfect: fierem, fieres, fieret, etc. Perfect: factus sum or fui, etc. Infinitive: fieri. Future: factum iri. Participial adjective: faciendus.

units.la: Conjuga Inquio.
units.tr: Conjugate inquio.

units.la: Primum præsens: Inquio & inquam, ich sage/ inquis, inquit. Pluraliter: Inquiunt. Secundum præsens: Inquiat. Primum perfectum: Inquisti, inquit. Primum futurum: Inquies, inquiet. Tertium futurum: Inque, inquito.
units.tr: First present: inquio and inquam, I say; inquis, inquit. Plural: inquiunt. Second present: inquiat. First perfect: inquisti, inquit. First future: inquies, inquiet. Third future: inque, inquito.

units.la: Conjuga Veneo.
units.tr: Conjugate veneo.

units.la: Primum praesens : Veneo , <bl>ich werde verkaufft</bl>/venis,&c. Imperfectum: Venibam. Perfectum : Venivi & venij.Futurum: Venibo,venibis,&c.
units.tr: First present: veneo, I am sold; venis, etc. Imperfect: venibam. Perfect: venivi and venii. Future: venibo, venibis, etc.

units.la: Conjuga,Memini,Odi,Coepi,Novi, Consuevi.
units.tr: Conjugate memini, odi, coepi, novi, consuevi.

units.la: Primum praesens & primum perfectum : Memini, <bl>ich gedencke oder habe gedacht</bl>/ meministi , meminit.
units.tr: First present and first perfect: memini, I remember or have remembered; meministi, meminit.

units.la: Odi,<bl>ich hasse oder habe gehasset</bl>/odisti, odit,&c.

units.la: Coepi,<bl>ich hebe an/oder hab angefangē</bl>/coepisti,&c.

units.la: Consuevi, <bl>ich pflege/oder habe pflegen</bl>/cōsuevisti.

units.tr: Second future: meminero, odero, coepero, novero, consuevero.

units.la: Conjuga possum.
units.tr: Conjugate possum.

units.la: Primum praesens : Possum , <bl>ich kan[?]</bl> / potes, potest, possumus, potestis,possunt.Secundū praesens:possim, possis,possit,&c poteram, possem, potui, potuerim, potuerā,potuissem, potero,potuero,posse,potuisse.
units.tr: First present: I can, possum; (German: ich kan[?]) you can, he can, we can, you (plural) can, they can. Second present (subjunctive): I may be able, you may be able, he may be able, etc.; I was able (imperfect), I could be able (imperfect subjunctive), I was able (perfect), I may have been able (perfect subjunctive), I had been able (pluperfect), I might have been able (pluperfect subjunctive), I shall be able (future), I shall have been able (future perfect); to be able (infinitive present), to have been able (infinitive perfect).

units.la: Conjuga Malo,Nolo.
units.tr: Conjugate malo, nolo.

units.la: Primum praesens : Malo , <bl>ich will lieber</bl>/ mavis, <bl>du wilt lieber</bl>/mavult,malumus,mavultis, malunt.
units.tr: First present: malo, I would rather; mavis, you would rather; mavult, malumus, mavultis, malunt.

units.la: Nolo,<bl>ich will nit</bl>/non vis,<bl>du wilt nit</bl>/non vult,nolumus,non vultis,nolunt. Secundum præsens: Malim,malis,malit,&c. Nolim,nolis,nolit,nolimus,&c. Primù imperfectum: Malebā,malebas,Nolebā,&c. Secundum imperfectum Mallem,&c. Nollem,&c. Primù perfectū:Malui,maluisti,Nolui,noluisti,&c. Secundum perfectum: Malucerim,Noluerim,&c. Primù plusquàm perfectū:Malueram,Noluerā,&c. Secundù plusquâ perfectû : Maluisse,Noluisse,&c. Primum futurū : Malam,males,Nolam,noles,&c.
units.tr: Nolo, I do not want; non vis, you do not want; non vult, nolumus, non vultis, nolunt. Second present: malim, malis, malit, etc.; nolim, nolis, nolit, nolimus, etc. First imperfect: malebam, malebas, etc.; nolebam, etc. Second imperfect: mallem, etc.; nollem, etc. First perfect: malui, maluisti, etc.; nolui, noluisti, etc. Second perfect: malucerim, noluerim, etc. First pluperfect: malueram, nolueram, etc. Second pluperfect: maluisse, noluisse, etc. First future: malam, males, etc.; nolam, noles, etc.

units.la: Tertium futurum. Noli vel nolito, nolite vel nolitote,Cic.de Nat.Deor.
units.tr: Third future. Noli or nolito; nolite or nolitote. Cic. de Nat. Deor.

units.la: Infinita: Malle,Maluisse,Nolle,noluisse.
units.tr: Infinitives: malle, maluisse; nolle, noluisse.

units.la: Quid est secunda forma?
units.tr: What is the second form?

units.la: Secunda forma Verbi est, quando Thema definit in or. Ac si Latinè flecti possit in o,dicitur verbu passivum : ut, Amor, ich werde geliebet/ amo, ich liebe. Si non possit Latinè flecti in o,dicitur Verbum Deponens: ut Loquor,ich rede : Loquo non dicimus. Sunt autem hic admonendi studiosi,quædam Verba efferri pero & or, eadem significatione: ut, Assentio & assentior,ich stimme zu/ich halte es mit einem. Impertio & impertior, ich theile mit. Comperio & comperior, ich erfahre/ ich werde innen. Usus artium Magister spectandus.
units.tr: The second form of the verb is when the stem ends in -or. If it can be inflected in Latin into -o, the verb is called passive, as amor, I am loved, from amo, I love. If it cannot be inflected into -o, it is called a deponent verb, as loquor, I speak; we do not say loquo. Here, however, studious readers should be reminded that some verbs are used both with -o and -or in the same meaning, as assentio and assentior, I agree or side with someone; impertio and impertior, I share; comperio and comperior, I learn or come to know. The usage of skilled writers is the master to be consulted.

units.la: Conjuga vulgaria Verba formæ secundæ, juxta quæ studiosi reliqua in or flectant.
units.tr: Conjugate the common verbs of the second form, by which students conjugate the rest in -or.

units.la: Primum præsens tempus.
units.tr: The first present tense.

units.la: Conjugatio Prima.
units.tr: First conjugation.

units.la: Amor, ich werde geliebet / amaris vel amare, du wirst geliebet/amatur,er wirt geliebet/amamur, wir werden geliebet/amamini, ihr werdet geliebet/amantur, sie werden geliebet.
units.tr: Amor, I am being loved (German: ich werde geliebet); you are loved; he is loved; we are loved; you (plural) are loved; they are loved.

units.la: Conjugatio Secunda.
units.tr: Second conjugation.

units.la: Doceor,ich werde gelehret/ doceris vel docēre,docetur,docemur,docemini,docentur.
units.tr: Doceor, I am being taught (German: ich werde gelehret); you are taught; he is taught; we are taught; you (plural) are taught; they are taught.

units.la: Coniugatio Tertia.
units.tr: Third conjugation.

units.la: Legor, ich werde gelesen / legeris vel legere, legitur,legimur,legimini,leguntur.
units.tr: Legor, I am being read (German: ich werde gelesen); you are read; he is read; we are read; you (plural) are read; they are read.

units.la: Coniugatio Quarta.
units.tr: Fourth conjugation.

units.la: Audior, ich werde gehöret / audiris vel audire, auditur,audimur[?],audimini,audiuntur.
units.tr: Audior, I am being heard (German: ich werde gehöret); you are heard; he is heard; we are heard; you (plural) are heard; they are heard.

units.la: Coniugatio Anomala.
units.tr: Anomalous conjugation.

units.la: Feror, ich we[?]de getragen/ ferris vel ferre, fertur, ferimur,ferimini,feruntur.
units.tr: Feror, I am being carried (German: ich werde getragen); you are carried; he is carried; we are carried; you (plural) are carried; they are carried.

units.la: Secundum præsens tempus.
units.tr: Second present tense.

units.la: Amer, ich kan oder mag oder soll geliebet werden/ ameris vel amere ametur, amemur, lasset uns geliebet werden/ oder wir können oder mögen oder sollen geliebet werden/amemini,amentur.
units.tr: Amer, I can, may or should be loved (German: ich kan oder mag oder soll geliebet werden); you can, may or should be loved; he can, may or should be loved; let us be loved, or we can, may or should be loved; you (plural) can, may or should be loved; they can, may or should be loved.

units.la: Docear, ich kan oder mag oder soll gelehret werden/ docearis vel doceare, doceatur, doceamur, doceamini,doceantur.
units.tr: Docear, I can, may or should be taught (German: ich kan oder mag oder soll gelehret werden); you can, may or should be taught; he can, may or should be taught; we can, may or should be taught; you (plural) can, may or should be taught; they can, may or should be taught.

units.la: Legar,ich kan oder mag od' soll gelesen werden/legaris vel legare legatur, legamur, legamini,legatur.
units.tr: Legar, I can, may or should be read (German: ich kan oder mag oder soll gelesen werden); you can, may or should be read; he can, may or should be read; we can, may or should be read; you (plural) can, may or should be read; they can, may or should be read.

units.la: Audiar, ich kan oder mag oder soll gehöret werden/ audiaris vel audiare, audiatur,audiamur,audiamini, audiantur.
units.tr: Audiar, I can, may or should be heard (German: ich kan oder mag oder soll gehöret werden); you can, may or should be heard; he can, may or should be heard; we can, may or should be heard; you (plural) can, may or should be heard; they can, may or should be heard.

units.la: Ferar, ich kan oder mag oder soll getragen werdē/ feraris vel ferare, feratur,feramur,feramini,ferantur.
units.tr: Ferar, I can, may or should be carried (German: ich kan oder mag oder soll getragen werden); you can, may or should be carried; he can, may or should be carried; we can, may or should be carried; you (plural) can, may or should be carried; they can, may or should be carried.

units.la: Primum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: First imperfect tense.

units.la: Amabar, ich ward geliebet/ amabaris vel amabare, amabatur,amabamur,amabamini,amabantur.
units.tr: Amabar, I was being loved (German: ich ward geliebet); you were loved; he was loved; we were loved; you (plural) were loved; they were loved.

units.la: Docebar, ich ward gelehret / docebaris vel docebare, docebatur, docebamur, docebamini, docebantur.
units.tr: Docebar, I was being taught (German: ich ward gelehret); you were taught; he was taught; we were taught; you (plural) were taught; they were taught.

units.la: Legebar,ich ward gelesen/ legebaris vel legebare, legebatur,legebamur,legebamini,legebantur.
units.tr: Legebar, I was being read (German: ich ward gelesen); you were read; he was read; we were read; you (plural) were read; they were read.

units.la: Audiebar, ich ward gehöret/ audiebaris vel audiebare, audiebatur, audiebamur, audiebamini,audiebantur.
units.tr: Audiebar, I was being heard (German: ich ward gehöret); you were heard; he was heard; we were heard; you (plural) were heard; they were heard.

units.la: Ferebar, ich ward getragen / ferebaris vel ferebâre, ferebatur, ferebamur, ferebamini, ferebantur.
units.tr: Ferebar, I was being carried (German: ich ward getragen); you were carried; he was carried; we were carried; you (plural) were carried; they were carried.

units.la: Secundum imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: Second imperfect tense.

units.la: Amarer, ich könte oder möchte oder solte geliebet werden / amareris vel amarere, amaretur, amaremur, amaremini, amarentur.
units.tr: Amarer, I could, might or should be loved (German: ich könte oder möchte oder solte geliebet werden); you could, might or should be loved; he could, might or should be loved; we could, might or should be loved; you (plural) could, might or should be loved; they could, might or should be loved.

units.la: Docerer, ich könte oder möchte oder solte gelehr- ret werden / docereris vel docere, doceretur, doceremur, doceremini, docerentur.
units.tr: Docerer, I could, might or should be taught (German: ich könte oder möchte oder solte gelehret werden); you could, might or should be taught; he could, might or should be taught; we could, might or should be taught; you (plural) could, might or should be taught; they could, might or should be taught.

units.la: Legerer, ich könte oder möchte oder solte gelesen werden / legereris vel legere, legeretur, legeremur, legeremini, legerentur.
units.tr: Legerer, I could, might or should be read (German: ich könte oder möchte oder solte gelesen werden); you could, might or should be read; he could, might or should be read; we could, might or should be read; you (plural) could, might or should be read; they could, might or should be read.

units.la: Audirer, ich könte oder möchte oder solte gehöret werden / audireris vel audirere, audiretur, audiremur, audiremini, audirentur.
units.tr: Audirer, I could, might or should be heard (German: ich könte oder möchte oder solte gehöret werden); you could, might or should be heard; he could, might or should be heard; we could, might or should be heard; you (plural) could, might or should be heard; they could, might or should be heard.

units.la: Ferrer, ich könte oder möchte oder solte getragen werden / ferreris vel ferrere, ferretur, ferremur, ferremini, ferrentur.
units.tr: Ferrer, I could, might or should be carried (German: ich könte oder möchte oder solte getragen werden); you could, might or should be carried; he could, might or should be carried; we could, might or should be carried; you (plural) could, might or should be carried; they could, might or should be carried.

units.la: Interdum haec verba sic exponantur: <bl>Ich</bl> <bl>würde geliebet/ gelehret/ gelesen/ gehöret/ getragen werden.</bl>
units.tr: Sometimes these verbs are explained thus: I would be loved, taught, read, heard, carried.

units.la: Primum perfectum tempus.
units.tr: First perfect tense.

units.la: Amatus sum vel fui, ich bin geliebet / amatus es vel fuisti, amatus est vel fuit, amati sumus vel fuimus, amati estis vel fuistis, amati sunt, fuerunt vel fuere.
units.tr: Amatus sum or fui, I have been loved (German: ich bin geliebet); you have been loved; he has been loved; we have been loved; you (plural) have been loved; they have been loved.

units.la: Doctus sum vel fui, ich bin gelehret / es vel fuisti, est vel fuit, docti sumus vel fuimus, estis vel fuistis, sunt, fuerunt vel fuere. Sic lectus, auditus, latus sum vel fui, ich bin gelesen/gehöret/getragen / es vel fuisti, &c.
units.tr: Doctus sum or fui, I have been taught (German: ich bin gelehret); you have been taught; he has been taught; we have been taught; you (plural) have been taught; they have been taught. So too lectus, auditus, latus sum or fui, I have been read, heard, carried (German: ich bin gelesen, gehöret, getragen); and so on through the persons.

units.la: Secundum perfectum tempus.
units.tr: Second perfect tense.

units.la: Amatus sim vel fuerim, ich habe können oder sollen geliebet sein / amatus sis vel fueris, sit vel fuerit, amati simus vel fuerimus, sitis vel fueritis, sint vel fuerint.
units.tr: Amatus sim or fuerim, I may have been able or obliged to be loved (German: ich habe können oder sollen geliebet sein); you may have been loved; he may have been loved; we may have been loved; you (plural) may have been loved; they may have been loved.

units.la: Doctus sim vel fuerim, sis vel fueris, sit vel fuerit, docti simus vel fuerimus, sitis vel fueritis, sint vel fuerint.
units.tr: Doctus sim or fuerim, you may have been taught; he may have been taught; we may have been taught; you (plural) may have been taught; they may have been taught, and so on.

units.la: Sic Lectus. Auditus, Latus sim vel fuerim, sis vel fueris, sit vel fuerit, &c.
units.tr: So too lectus, auditus, latus sim or fuerim, and so on through the persons.

units.la: Primum plusquam perfectum tempus.
units.tr: First pluperfect tense.

units.la: Amatus eram vel fueram, ich was geliebet / eras, vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, amati eramus vel fueramus, eratis, vel fueratis, erant vel fuerant.
units.tr: Amatus eram or fueram, I had been loved (German: ich was geliebet); you had been loved; he had been loved; we had been loved; you (plural) had been loved; they had been loved.

units.la: Doctus eram vel fueram, ich was gelehret / eras vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, docti eramus vel fueramus, eratis vel fueratis, erant vel fuerant.
units.tr: Doctus eram or fueram, I had been taught (German: ich was gelehret); you had been taught; he had been taught; we had been taught; you (plural) had been taught; they had been taught.

units.la: Sic Lectus, Auditus, Latus eram vel fueram, eras vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, &c.
units.tr: So too lectus, auditus, latus eram or fueram, and so on through the persons.

units.la: Secundum plusquam perfectum tempus.
units.tr: Second pluperfect tense.

units.la: Amatus essem vel fuissem, ich were geliebet worden / esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, amati essemus vel fuissemus, essetis vel fuissetis, essent vel fuissent.
units.tr: Amatus essem or fuissem, I would have been loved (German: ich were geliebet worden); you would have been loved; he would have been loved; we would have been loved; you (plural) would have been loved; they would have been loved.

units.la: Doctus essem vel fuissem, ich were gelehret worden/esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, docti essemus vel fuissemus, essetis vel fuissetis, essent vel fuissent.
units.tr: Doctus essem or fuissem, I would have been taught (German: ich were gelehret worden); you would have been taught; he would have been taught; we would have been taught; you (plural) would have been taught; they would have been taught.

units.la: Sic Lectus, Auditus, Latus essem vel fuissem, esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, &c.
units.tr: So too lectus, auditus, latus essem or fuissem, and so on through the persons.

units.la: Scimus quidem perfectorum temporum periphrasin ad Syntaxin pertinere: tamen ne studiosi de Ramea Grammatices difficultate quererentur, voluimus circunloquendi formam subjicere.
units.tr: We indeed know that the periphrasis of the perfect tenses belongs to syntax; nevertheless, so that students might not complain of the difficulty of Ramus's grammar, we have chosen to add the periphrastic forms.

units.la: Primum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The first future tense.

units.la: Amabor, ich wil oder werde oder sol geliebet werden / amaberis vel amabere, amabitur, amabimur, amabimini, amabuntur.
units.tr: I shall be loved, I will, shall or ought to be loved; you will or shall be loved, he will be loved, we will be loved, you (plural) will be loved, they will be loved.

units.la: Docebor, doceberis vel docebere, docebitur, docebimur, docebimini, docebuntur.
units.tr: I shall be taught, you will or shall be taught, he will be taught, we will be taught, you (plural) will be taught, they will be taught.

units.la: Legar, legeris vel legere, legetur, legemur, legemini, legentur.
units.tr: I shall be read, you will or shall be read, he will be read, we will be read, you (plural) will be read, they will be read.

units.la: Audiar, audieris vel audiere, audietur, audiemur, audiemini, audientur.
units.tr: I shall be heard, you will or shall be heard, he will be heard, we will be heard, you (plural) will be heard, they will be heard.

units.la: Ferar, fereris vel ferere, feretur, feremur, feremini, ferentur.
units.tr: I shall be carried, you will or shall be carried, he will be carried, we will be carried, you (plural) will be carried, they will be carried.

units.la: Secundum futurum tempus.
units.tr: The second future tense.

units.la: Amatus, Doctus, Lectus, Auditus, Latus ero vel fuero, <bl>ich will oder werde / oder soll geliebet / geleh-</bl> <bl>ret/gelesen/gehöret/getragen werden/</bl>eris vel fueris, erit vel fuerit, Amati, docti, lecti, auditi, lati erimus vel fuerimus, eritis vel fueritis, erunt vel fuerint.
units.tr: Loved, taught, read, heard, carried: I will be or will have been; I will or shall be loved, taught, read, heard or carried; you will be or will have been; he will be or will have been; we, loved, taught, read, heard, carried, will be or will have been; you (plural) will be or will have been; they will be or will have been.

units.la: Tertium futurum tempus.
units.tr: The third future tense.

units.la: Amare vel amator tu, <bl>werde du geliebet oder du</bl> <bl>sollt geliebet werden</bl>/ amator ille, amamini vos, amantor illi.
units.tr: Be you loved, or you shall be loved; let him be loved; be you (plural) loved; let them be loved.

units.la: Docere vel docetor tu, docetor ille, docemini vos, docentor illi.
units.tr: Be you taught, or you shall be taught; let him be taught; be you (plural) taught; let them be taught.

units.la: Legere vel legitor tu, legitor ille, legimini vos, leguntor illi.
units.tr: Be you read, or you shall be read; let him be read; be you (plural) read; let them be read.

units.la: Audire vel auditor tu, auditor ille, audimini vos, audiuntor illi.
units.tr: Be you heard, or you shall be heard; let him be heard; be you (plural) heard; let them be heard.

units.la: Ferre vel fertor tu, fertor ille; ferimini vos, feruntor illi.
units.tr: Be you carried, or you shall be carried; let him be carried; be you (plural) carried; let them be carried.

units.la: DE VERBIS INFINITIS.
units.tr: ON VERBS IN THE INFINITIVE.

units.la: Præsens & imperfectum tempus.
units.tr: The present and imperfect tenses.

units.la: Amari, <bl>geliebet werden.</bl> Doceri, <bl>gelehret werden.</bl> Legi, <bl>gelesen werden.</bl> Audiri, <bl>gehöret werden.</bl> Ferri, <bl>getragen werden.</bl>
units.tr: To be loved (amari). To be taught (doceri). To be read (legi). To be heard (audiri). To be carried (ferri).

units.la: Futurum tempus eleganter hoc pacto circumloquimur. Me, te, illum, Nos, vos, illos, Amatum Doctum Lectum Auditum Latum ut Me, te, illum, amatum fore. Nos, vos, illos, a-matos fore.
units.tr: We express the future tense elegantly in this way: "that I, you, he will be loved" (me, te, illum amatum fore); "that we, you, they will be loved" (nos, vos, illos amatos fore).

units.la: Cicero inquit, Epistol.221. Quos spero brevitempore societate victoriæ tecum copulatos fore. <bl>Das ich/du/er</bl> <bl>Wir/ihr/die</bl> <bl>werden</bl> <bl>Geliebet</bl> <bl>Gelehret</bl> <bl>Gelesen</bl> <bl>Gehöret</bl> <bl>Getragen</bl> <bl>werden.</bl>
units.tr: Cicero says, Epist. 221: "Whom I hope will in a short time be joined with you in the fellowship of victory" (Quos spero brevi tempore societate victoriae tecum copulatos fore). German: "That I / you / he / we / you / they will be loved, taught, read, heard, carried, be."

units.la: <bl>Cicero sagt / welche ich hoffe daß sie in kurtzer zeit</bl> <bl>durch gesellschafft der uberwindung mit dir werden</bl> <bl>vereiniget werden.</bl>
units.tr: Cicero says, "Which I hope will in a short time through the fellowship of victory be united with you."

units.la: Gerundia.
units.tr: Gerunds.

units.la: Amando, <bl>wen er/ die/ das geliebet wird.</bl> Docendo, <bl>wen gelehret wird.</bl> Legendo, <bl>wen gelesen wird.</bl> Audiendo, <bl>wen gehöret wird.</bl> Ferendo, <bl>wen getra-gen wird.</bl>
units.tr: Amando, for him, her or it who is loved. Docendo, for whom one is taught. Legendo, for whom one reads. Audiendo, for whom one hears. Ferendo, for whom one is carried.

units.la: Supina.
units.tr: Supines.

units.la: <bl>Amatu, daß er/die/das geliebet werde. Doctu, daß gelehret werde. Lectu, daß gelesen werde. Auditu,</bl> <bl>daß gehöret werde. Latu, daß getragen werde.</bl>
units.tr: Amatu, that he or she may be loved. Doctu, that one may be taught. Lectu, that one may be read. Auditu, that one may be heard. Latu, that one may be carried.

units.la: Donatus passivorum Gerundia & Supina omisit, cum tamen apud Authores occurrant: ut, Alitur vitium, vivitq; tegendo, Virgilius, id est ut exponit Dominus Philippus Melanchthon, dum tegitur. Digna res auditu, hoc est, ut audiatur.
units.tr: Donatus omitted the passive gerunds and supines, although they occur in the authors, as in "Alitur vitium, vivitque tegendo" (Virgil), that is, as Dominus Philippus Melanchthon explains, "while it is covered." And "digna res auditu" means "a thing worthy to be heard."

units.la: Verba Deponentia utram formam imitantur?
units.tr: Which form do deponent verbs imitate?

units.la: Passivam imitantur formam, & significationem habent activam: ut, prælior, <bl>ich streite/nicht ich wer-</bl> <bl>de gestritten /</bl> præliaris vel præliare, præliatur, præliamur, præliamini, præliantur.
units.tr: They imitate the passive form but have an active meaning, as in prælior, "I fight" (German: "ich streite", not "ich werde gestritten"): praeliaris or praeliare, praeliatur, praeliamur, praeliamini, praeliantur.

units.la: Prælier, prælieris vel prælierē, prælietur, præliemur, præliemini, præliéntur.
units.tr: I am fighting (passive: I am fought/ I wage war), you fight, or you fight (as a deponent), he fights, we fight, you fight, they fight.

units.la: Præliabar, præliabaris vel præliabare, præliabatur,præliabamur,præliabamini,præliabantur. Præliarer, præliareris vel præliarere, præliaretur, præliaremur,præliaremini,præliarentur. Præliatus sum vel fui. Præliatus sim vel fuerim. Præliatus erā vel fuerā. Præliatus essem vel fuissem. Præliabor, præliaberis vel præliabere, præliabitur. præliabimur,præliabimini,præliabuntur. Præliare vel præliator tu, præliator ille, præliamini vos, præliantor illi. Infinitum : Præliari. Futurum,Gerundium & Supinum,ut in forma prima. Præliatum ire Præliandi,præliandum,præliando. Præliatum,præliatu.
units.tr: I was fighting; you were fighting, or you were fighting (variant form); he was fighting; we were fighting; you (plural) were fighting; they were fighting. That I might fight; that you might fight, or that you might fight (variant form); that he might fight; that we might fight; that you (plural) might fight; that they might fight. I have fought; I may have fought. I had fought; I might have fought. I had fought (pluperfect); I would have fought. I shall fight; you will fight, or you will fight (variant form); he will fight; we shall fight; you (plural) will fight; they will fight. Fight (you); let him fight; fight (you, plural); let them fight. Infinitive: to fight. Future infinitive, gerund and supine as in the first conjugation: about to fight; fighting; to fight; fight. Participles: fighting, having fought; to be fought; by fighting; fighting; to fight; by fighting.

units.la: Sic Luctor, <bl>ich fechte</bl> / <bl>ich vnderstehe</bl> mich einen zu bodem werffen / <bl>ich widerstrebe</bl>. Digladior, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>streite</bl> mit eine schwerdt/<bl>ich zancke</bl>. Jocor, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>schimpffe</bl> mit worten. Ratiocinor, <bl>ich schliesse</bl> etwas auß der vernunfft. Recordor, <bl>ich gedencke</bl>. Suffragor, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>gebe</bl> einem meine stimme / <bl>ich vnderscheibe</bl> eines meinung. Dominor, <bl>ich herrsche</bl>. Fœneror, <bl>ich leihe</bl> auff wucher auß / oder <bl>ich nimme</bl> auff wucher von einem anderen. Assentor, <bl>ich schmeichle</bl>. Adulor, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>liebkose</bl>. Gratulor, <bl>ich wünsche</bl> glück / <bl>ich frewe</bl> mich eines andern glücks / <bl>ich dancke</bl>. Patrocinor, <bl>ich beschütze</bl> einen im gericht. Palpor, <bl>ich rüre</bl> leiß an / <bl>ich schmeichle</bl>. Execror, <bl>ich verfluche</bl>. Abominor, <bl>ich hab</bl> ein grewel. Detestor, <bl>ich vermaledeie</bl>/<bl>ich hab</bl> ein abscheuhen. Opitulor, <bl>ich komme</bl> zu hülffe. Famulor, <bl>ich diene</bl>. Minor, <bl>ich drawe</bl>. Minitor, <bl>ich drawe</bl> heffitig. Auxilior, <bl>ich helffe</bl>. Adversor, <bl>ich widerstrebe</bl>. Insidior, <bl>ich stelle</bl> nach. Arbitror, <bl>ich meine</bl>. Prædor, <bl>ich</bl> <bl>raube</bl>. Percontor, <bl>ich erfrage</bl>. Precor, <bl>ich bitte</bl>. Deprecor, <bl>ich abbitte</bl> / <bl>ich bitte</bl> heffitig. Populor, Depopulor, Expopulor, <bl>ich verherge</bl>/<bl>verwüste</bl>. Meditor, <bl>ich</bl> betrachte.Dignor:ich achte wirdig. Aucupor,ich fange vogel / ich jage oder stelle geschwindiglich nach. Venor,ich jage wild. Furor,ich stäle. Aspernor,ich verschmehe. Scrutor, ich erforsche. Causor, ich wende entschuldigung für. Acmulor, ich folge nach/ ich vergönne.Præstolor,ich warte oder harre auff einen.Lucror,ich gewinne. Scifcitor, ich frage nach eine ding. Lætor,ich bin frölich. Stomachor,ich bin zornig. Tristor, ich bin traurig. Glorior, ich rühme. Crapulor, ich fresse vnd sauffe. Indignor, ich bin schellig. Piscor, ich fische. Altercor,ich zancke mit einem. Cacchinnor, ich lache bewerisch. Grassor, ich gehe vngestümiglich/ ich wüte. Lachrymor,ich weine. Scortor,ich lebe vnzüchtig. Castrametor, ich schlage dz Heerlager auff. Philosophor, ich rede von sachen der weissheit. Tumultuor, ich bin auffrühzisch. Nugor, ich plaudere vnnütze Ding. Conversor,ich habe gemeinschafft.Auguror,ich weissage. Spatior, ich spaziere. Rusticor, ich gehe mit feldwerck vmb.
units.tr: So luctor, "I wrestle" / "I undertake to throw someone to the ground" / "I resist". Digladior, "I fight with the sword" / "I quarrel". Jocor, "I jest with words". Ratiocinor, "I reason something out". Recordor, "I remember". Suffragor, "I give my vote to someone" / "I distinguish someone's opinion". Dominor, "I rule". Fœneror, "I lend at interest" or "I borrow at interest from another". Assentor, "I flatter". Adulor, "I fawn upon". Gratulor, "I wish good fortune" / "I rejoice in another's good fortune" / "I give thanks". Patrocinor, "I protect someone in court". Palpor, "I touch gently" / "I flatter". Execror, "I curse". Abominor, "I abhor". Detestor, "I curse" / "I detest". Opitulor, "I come to help". Famulor, "I serve". Minor, "I threaten". Minitor, "I threaten vehemently". Auxilior, "I help". Adversor, "I resist". Insidior, "I lie in wait for". Arbitror, "I think". Prædor, "I plunder". Percontor, "I inquire". Precor, "I beg". Deprecor, "I plead for pardon" / "I beg earnestly". Populor, Depopulor, Expopulor, "I lay waste" / "I devastate". Meditor, "I contemplate". Dignor, "I consider worthy". Aucupor, "I catch birds" / "I hunt or pursue swiftly". Venor, "I hunt game". Furor, "I steal". Aspernor, "I scorn". Scrutor, "I search out". Causor, "I make excuses for". Aemulor, "I emulate" / "I grudge". Præstolor, "I wait for or stay for someone". Lucror, "I gain". Sciscitor, "I ask about a thing". Lætor, "I rejoice". Stomachor, "I am angry". Tristor, "I am sad". Glorior, "I boast". Crapulor, "I gorge and drink to excess". Indignor, "I am indignant". Piscor, "I fish". Altercor, "I quarrel with someone". Cachinnor, "I laugh loudly". Grassor, "I go on violently" / "I rage". Lachrymor, "I weep". Scortor, "I live licentiously". Castrametor, "I pitch camp". Philosophor, "I speak about matters of wisdom". Tumultuor, "I stir up rebellion". Nugor, "I chatter about trifles". Conversor, "I have fellowship". Auguror, "I prophesy". Spatior, "I stroll". Rusticor, "I work in the fields."

units.la: Nonnulla Deponentia habent Activam & passivam significationem, quæ à Grammaticis Communia appellantur : ut, Ofculor , ich küsse oder werde geküsset. Dignor , ich achte wirdig/oder werde wirdig geachtet.Confolor,ich tröste oder werde getröstet.Adhortor, ich vermahne oder werde vermahnet. Frustror, ich betriege / halte auff/ oder werde betrogen / auffgehalten. Criminor, ich beschüldige/ oder werde beschuldiget. Stipulor, ich verheisse / ich begere ein zusag oder versprechung / ich frage oder werde gefraget. Usus spectandus.
units.tr: Some deponents have both an active and a passive meaning; the grammarians call these common verbs: as osculor, "I kiss" or "I am kissed"; dignor, "I consider worthy" or "I am considered worthy"; consolor, "I console" or "I am consoled"; adhortor, "I exhort" or "I am exhorted"; frustror, "I deceive / hold up" or "I am deceived / held up"; criminor, "I accuse" or "I am accused"; stipulor, "I promise / I demand a pledge or promise" or "I am asked or questioned." Usage should be observed.

units.la: Misereor,ich erbarme mich/misereris vel miserere, miseretur,miseremur,miseremini,miserentur.
units.tr: I have mercy (I pity myself); you have mercy, or have mercy (imperative form); he has mercy; we have mercy; you (plural) have mercy; they have mercy.

units.la: Miserear, miserearis vel misereare, misereatur,misereamur,misereamini,misereantur.
units.tr: That I may have mercy; that you may have mercy, or that you may have mercy (variant form); that he may have mercy; that we may have mercy; that you (plural) may have mercy; that they may have mercy.

units.la: Miserebar, miserebaris vel miserebare, miserebatur, miserebamur, miserebamini, miserebantur.
units.tr: I was having mercy; you were having mercy, or you were having mercy (variant form); he was having mercy; we were having mercy; you (plural) were having mercy; they were having mercy.

units.la: Miserer, misererreris vel misererere, misereretur, misereremur, misereremini, misererentur, &c.
units.tr: Imperfect subjunctive: miserer, misereris or miserere, misereretur, misereremur, misereremini, misererentur, etc.

units.la: Supinum, Misertum, misertu.
units.tr: Supine: misertum, misertu.

units.la: At Mereor, ich verdiene / beschulde / meritum, meritu.
units.tr: But mereor, "I deserve" / "I incur guilt": meritum, meritu.

units.la: Medeor, ich artzne/ ich heile/ich komme zuhülff/ abfq; supinis.
units.tr: Medeor, "I heal" / "I help": without supines.

units.la: Polliceor, ich verheisse / sage zu / pollicitum, pollicitu.
units.tr: Polliceor, "I promise" / "I pledge": pollicitum, pollicitu.

units.la: Fateor, ich bekenne / fatum, fatu.
units.tr: Fateor, "I confess": fatum, fatu.

units.la: Liceor, ich biete auff ein feil ding / licitum, licitu.
units.tr: Liceor, "I bid on an article for sale": licitum, licitu.

units.la: Reor, ich achte/ meine / ratum ratu.
units.tr: Reor, "I think" / "I suppose": ratum, ratu.

units.la: Tueor, ich beschirme / oder werde beschirmet / tuitum, tuitu.
units.tr: Tueor, "I protect" or "I am protected": tuitum, tuitu.

units.la: Proficiscor, ich reise / profecisceris vel proficisceris, proficiscitur, proficiscimur, proficiscimini, proficiscuntur.
units.tr: I set out (I travel); you set out, or you set out (variant form); he sets out; we set out; you (plural) set out; they set out.

units.la: Proficiscar, proficiscaris vel proficiscare, proficiscatur, proficiscamur, proficiscamini, proficiscantur.
units.tr: That I may set out; that you may set out, or that you may set out (variant form); that he may set out; that we may set out; that you (plural) may set out; that they may set out.

units.la: Proficiscebar, proficiscebaris vel proficiscebare, proficiscebatur, proficiscebamur, proficiscebamini, proficiscebantur.
units.tr: I was setting out; you were setting out, or you were setting out (variant form); he was setting out; we were setting out; you (plural) were setting out; they were setting out.

units.la: Proficiscerer, proficiscereris vel proficiscerere, proficisceretur, proficischeremur, proficischeremini, proficiscerentur, &c.
units.tr: That I might set out; that you might set out, or that you might set out (variant form); that he might set out; that we might set out; that you (plural) might set out; that they might set out; etc.

units.la: Supinum: Profectum, profectu.
units.tr: Supine: profectum, profectu.

units.la: At Gradior, graderis, ich gehe / gressum, gressu.
units.tr: But I walk (I go): you walk, or go; supine: walking, by walking.

units.la: Revertor, ich komme wider / reversum, reversu.
units.tr: Revertor, "I return": reversum, reversu.

units.la: Fungor, ich brauche / ich verwalte / functu, functu.
units.tr: Fungor, "I use" / "I manage" / "I perform": functu, functu.

units.la: Vescor, ich esse / niesse / abfq; supinis.
units.tr: Vescor, "I eat" / "I enjoy": without supines.

units.la: Fruor, ich nutze / niesse / brauche / fruitum, fruitu.
units.tr: Fruor, "I enjoy" / "I use" / "I make use of": fruitum, fruitu.

units.la: Utor, ich brauche / ich habe gemeinschafft / usum, usu.
units.tr: Utor, "I use" / "I have fellowship with": usum, usu.

units.la: Oblivisor, ich vergesse / oblitum, oblitu. .. (su.
units.tr: Oblivisor, "I forget": oblitum, oblitu.

units.la: Reminiscor, ich erinnere mich / abfq; supinis. Irascor,<bl>ich zörne[?]</bl>/iratum,iratu. Ulciscor, <bl>ich rache[?] oder wircke mich an einem</bl> / ultum,ultu. Sequor,<bl>ich folge nach</bl>/secutum,secutu. Loquor,<bl>ich rede</bl>/locutum,locutu. Nanciscor,<bl>ich überkomme/ ich kriege</bl>/nactū,nactu. Queror,<bl>ich klage</bl>/questum,questu. Morior,<bl>ich sterbe</bl>/mortuum,mortuu. Patior,<bl>ich dulde/leide</bl>/passum,passu. Adipiscor,<bl>ich erlange/ bringe zuwegen</bl>/adeptum, adeptu. Nascor,<bl>ich werde geboren</bl>/natum,natu. Labor,<bl>ich falle/nim ab/fähle[?]</bl>/lapsum,lapsu. Comminiscor,<bl>ich erdichte</bl>/commētum,cōmentu. Expergiscor, <bl>ich erwach se/ ich wache auff/</bl> experrectum,experrectu. Paciscor, <bl>ich werde eins mit einem / ich mache ein</bl> <bl>vertrag</bl>/pactum,pactu. Orior, oreris vel orere,oritur, <bl>ich entstehe/gehe</bl> <bl>auff.</bl> Infinitum: Oriri. Supinum: Ortum, ortu. Nitor, <bl>ich strebe / verstehe / ich erhalte mich/ich</bl> <bl>verlasse mich auff einen/</bl> nixum,nixu & nisum,nisu. Amplector,<bl>ich umbfahe/ oder werde umbfangen/</bl> amplexum,amplexu. Largior, <bl>ich schencke / gebe reichlich auß/</bl> largiris vel largire, largitur, largimur,largimini,largiuntur. Largiar, largiaris vel largiare, largiatur, largiamur, largiamini, largiantur, &c. Supinum: largitum,largitu. At Experior, experiris, <bl>ich erfahre</bl> / expertum, expertu. Metior,metiris, <bl>ich messe/ich achte/</bl> mesum,mesu. Adorior, adoriris, <bl>ich falle an / ich greiffe an /</bl> adortum,adortu. Ordior, ordiris, <bl>ich hebe an/ fahe an</bl>/orsum,orsu,
units.tr: Reminiscor, "I remember": without supines. Irascor, "I am angry" (?): iratum, iratu. Ulciscor, "I take revenge (?) or wreak vengeance on someone": ultum, ultu. Sequor, "I follow": secutum, secutu. Loquor, "I speak": locutum, locutu. Nanciscor, "I obtain / I get": nactum, nactu. Queror, "I complain": questum, questu. Morior, "I die": mortuum, mortuu. Patior, "I endure / suffer": passum, passu. Adipiscor, "I attain / bring about": adeptum, adeptu. Nascor, "I am born": natum, natu. Labor, "I fall / slip away / fail (?)": lapsum, lapsu. Comminiscor, "I invent": commentum, comentu. Expergiscor, "I wake up / I awake": experrectum, experrectu. Paciscor, "I come to terms with someone / I make a contract": pactum, pactu. Orior, oreris or orere, oritur, "I arise / rise up": infinitive oriri; supine ortum, ortu. Nitor, "I strive / I rely / I depend on someone": nixum, nixu and nisum, nisu. Amplector, "I embrace" or "I am embraced": amplexum, amplexu. Largior, "I bestow / give generously": largiris or largire, largitur, largimur, largimini, largiuntur. Present subjunctive: largiar, largiaris or largiare, largiatur, largiamur, largiamini, largiantur, etc. Supine: largitum, largitu. But experior, experiris, "I experience / try": expertum, expertu. Metior, metiris, "I measure / I esteem": mensum, mensu. Adorior, adoriris, "I attack / I assail": adortum, adortu. Ordior, ordiris, "I begin / I set about": orsum, orsu.

units.la: Opperior, ich warte eines [?] / oppertum, oppertu, & opperitum, opperitu.
units.tr: I wait for [?] / waited for, by waiting for, & waiting for, by waiting.

units.la: Posteriora supina deponentiū non sunt in crebro usu: ideo autem ea adjecimus: quia format à se adjectiva participialia in us, quibus, addito verbo Sum, perfecta circumscribimus.
units.tr: The later supines of deponent verbs are not in common use; nevertheless we have added them, because from them are formed the participial adjectives in -us, with which, by adding the verb sum, we express the perfect periphrastically.

units.la: Observatio.
units.tr: Observation.

units.la: Verba secundorum temporum, sine Adverbiis in oratione collocata, sunt per Possum, aut Debeo, aut simile quid exponenda: id quod Thomas Linacer de emendata structura Latini sermonis lib.1. de Modo: Et Petrus Ramus Scholarum Grammaticarum lib.14. De Verbi modis & temporibus, confirmant sequentibus testimonijs ex illustribus authoribus sumptis: Quis cladem illius noctis, quis funera fando Explicet, aut possit lachrymis aequaie dolores, Virgilius. Explicet, id est, possit explicare. Si quis novi quid instituerit, is non omnia, quae ante acta sunt, rata esse patiatur, Cicero, id est, non debet pati rata esse, ut Priscianus ipse interpretatur. Valebis, meaq; negotia videbis, neque Diis adjuvantibus ante brumam expectabis, Cicero pro Vale, Vide, Expecta, inquit Linacer de Emend. Struct. lib.6. de temporum Enallage. Quando autem Verbis secundorum temporum adduntur Adverbia: saepe possum, debeo, omittuntur: ut, utinam Amarem, docerem, legerem, audirem, ferrem: <bl>wolt Gott daß ich liebete/lehrete/</bl> <bl>läse [?]/hörete/trüge [?]</bl>. Cum amarem, docerem, legerem, audirem, ferrem: <bl>daß ich liebte / lehrte / läse [?] / hörte /</bl> <bl>trüge [?]</bl>. Sed hoc fidelibus praeceptoribus commissum esto.
units.tr: Verbs of the second tenses, when placed in a sentence without adverbs, are to be explained by "can" or "ought" or something similar. Thomas Linacer, in De emendata structura Latini sermonis, book 1, on the mood, and Petrus Ramus, in Scholarum Grammaticarum, book 14, on the modes and tenses of the verb, confirm this with the following testimonies taken from illustrious authors. Virgil: "Who could unfold the slaughter of that night, who the deaths in telling, or could match sorrows with tears?" Here "unfold" means "could unfold." Cicero: "If anyone has begun something new, he should not allow all that was done before to remain valid." That is, he ought not to allow them to remain valid, as Priscian himself explains. Cicero again: "You will be well, and you will see my affairs, and with the gods helping, you will not wait until the winter solstice." Here "be well," "see," and "wait" stand for "you ought to be well," "you ought to see," and "you ought to wait." Linacer says this in De emend. struct., book 6, on the enallage of tenses. When adverbs are added to verbs of the second tenses, the words "can" and "ought" are often left out, as in: "would God that I loved, taught, read, heard, bore," and "that I loved, taught, read, heard, bore." But let this be left to faithful teachers.

units.la: Hactenus dictum est de vocibus Numeri, videlicet de Nomine & Verbo: sequuntur voces sine Numero, quae nullum numerum, neq; singularem, neq; pluralem adsignificant, nempe Adverbium & Conjunctio.
units.tr: So far we have spoken of the words that have number, namely the noun and the verb. There follow the words without number, which signify neither singular nor plural, namely the adverb and the conjunction.

units.la: DE ADVERBIO.
units.tr: ON THE ADVERB.

units.la: Quid est Adverbium?
units.tr: What is an adverb?

units.la: ADVerbium est vox sine numero, quae alicui voci adjuncta, circumstantiam ejus una voce effert. Adverbium est multiplex:
units.tr: An adverb is a word without number which, joined to some other word, expresses its circumstance in a single word. The adverb is of many kinds:

units.la: 1. Aut Loci: ut, Hic <bl>hie</bl>. Illic, <bl>dort</bl>. Isthic, <bl>dafelbst</bl>. Ibi, <bl>da</bl>. Ubi, <bl>wo</bl>. Huc, <bl>hieher</bl>. Illuc, <bl>dorthin</bl>. Isthuc, <bl>dahin</bl>. Eo, <bl>dahin</bl>. Quo, <bl>wohin</bl>. Hinc, <bl>von hinnen</bl>. Illinc, <bl>dorther</bl>. Isthinc, <bl>von dannen</bl>. Inde, <bl>von dar</bl>. Unde, <bl>von</bl> <bl>wannen</bl>. Hac, <bl>hierauß</bl>. Illac, <bl>dorthinauß</bl>. Isthac, <bl>da</bl> <bl>hie-nauß</bl>. Nequà, <bl>daß nicht wo hinauß</bl>. Ad, <bl>zu/bey</bl>. Apud, <bl>bey</bl>. Ante, <bl>vor</bl>. Adversum, <bl>wider</bl>: Et reliqua Adverbia, vulgò praepositiones appellatae, quae etiam interdum Adverbia temporis & personae sunt.
units.tr: 1. Of place: e.g. Hic, "here". Illic, "yonder". Isthic, "there (near you)". Ibi, "there". Ubi, "where". Huc, "hither". Illuc, "thither". Isthuc, "thither (to you)". Eo, "thither". Quo, "whither". Hinc, "from here". Illinc, "from yonder". Isthinc, "from there". Inde, "from thence". Unde, "from whence". Hac, "this way out". Illac, "that way out". Isthac, "out that way". Nequà, "lest anywhere out". Ad, "to, at". Apud, "at, by". Ante, "before". Adversum, "against". And the remaining adverbs, commonly called prepositions, which are sometimes also adverbs of time and of person.

units.la: 2. Aut Temporis: ut, Hodie, <bl>heut</bl>. Heri, <bl>gestern</bl>. Nunc, <bl>jetzund</bl>. Nuper, <bl>neulich</bl>. Cras, <bl>morgen</bl>.
units.tr: 2. Of time: e.g. Hodie, "today". Heri, "yesterday". Nunc, "now". Nuper, "lately". Cras, "tomorrow".

units.la: 3. Aut Numeri: ut, Semel, <bl>einmal</bl>. Bis, <bl>zweymal</bl>. Ter, <bl>dreymal</bl>. Quater, <bl>viermal</bl>. Quinquies, <bl>fünffmal</bl>. Sexies, <bl>sechsmal</bl>. Septies, <bl>siebenmal</bl>. Octies, <bl>achtmal</bl>. Nonies, <bl>neunmal</bl>. Decies, <bl>zehenmal</bl>. Vicies, <bl>zwenzigmal</bl>. Tricies, <bl>dreyßigmal</bl>. Quadragies, <bl>vierzigmal</bl>. Quinquagies, <bl>fünfzigmal</bl>. Sexagies, <bl>sechzigmal</bl>. Septuagies, <bl>siebenzigmal</bl>. Octogies vel octuagies, <bl>achtzigmal</bl>. Nonagies, <bl>neunzigmal</bl>. Centies, <bl>hundertmal</bl>. Millies, <bl>tausentmal</bl>.
units.tr: 3. Of number: e.g. Semel, "once". Bis, "twice". Ter, "thrice". Quater, "four times". Quinquies, "five times". Sexies, "six times". Septies, "seven times". Octies, "eight times". Nonies, "nine times". Decies, "ten times". Vicies, "twenty times". Tricies, "thirty times". Quadragies, "forty times". Quinquagies, "fifty times". Sexagies, "sixty times". Septuagies, "seventy times". Octogies vel octuagies, "eighty times". Nonagies, "ninety times". Centies, "a hundred times". Millies, "a thousand times".

units.la: 4. Aut Negandi: ut, Non, <bl>nein</bl>. Haud, <bl>nicht</bl>. Neque, <bl>noch</bl>. Haud quaquam, <bl>in keinem wege</bl>. Minimè, <bl>mit</bl> <bl>nichten</bl>.
units.tr: 4. Of negation: e.g. Non, "no". Haud, "not". Neque, "nor". Haud quaquam, "in no way". Minimè, "by no means".

units.la: 5. Aut affirmandi: ut, Ita, <bl>ja</bl>. Etiam, <bl>ja</bl>. Quidni, <bl>warumb nicht</bl>. Certè, <bl>fürwar</bl>. Profectò, <bl>trawn</bl>.
units.tr: 5. Of affirmation: e.g. Ita, "yes". Etiam, "yes, indeed". Quidni, "why not". Certè, "certainly". Profectò, "truly".

units.la: 6. Aut Demonstrandi: ut, En, <bl>siehe</bl>. Ecce, <bl>siehe da</bl>.
units.tr: 6. Of demonstration: e.g. En, "see". Ecce, "behold".

units.la: 7. Aut Optandi: ut, utinam, <bl>wolt Gott</bl>. O si, <bl>wolt</bl> <bl>Gott</bl>.
units.tr: 7. Of wishing: e.g. Utinam, "would that". O si, "O that God would".

units.la: 8. Aut Hortandi: ut, Eia, <bl>wolan</bl>. Age,agite,agedum,<bl>wolan/hui Doch</bl>.
units.tr: 8. Of exhortation: e.g. Eia, "come on". Age, agite, agedum, "come, then, come now".

units.la: 9. Aut Ordinis: ut, Deinde, <bl>darnach</bl>. Deinceps, <bl>hinfort</bl>. Primo, <bl>jum ersten</bl>. Secundo, <bl>jum andern</bl>. Tertio, <bl>jum dritten</bl>.
units.tr: 9. Of order: e.g. Deinde, "afterwards". Deinceps, "henceforth". Primo, "first". Secundo, "second". Tertio, "third".

units.la: 10. Aut Interrogandi: ut, Cur ? <bl>warumb</bl> ? Quare? <bl>warumb</bl>? Quamobrem? <bl>weshalben</bl>? Quando? <bl>wan</bl>? Num? <bl>was</bl>? Nonne? <bl>nicht</bl>?
units.tr: 10. Of questioning: e.g. Cur? "why?" Quare? "wherefore?" Quamobrem? "for what reason?" Quando? "when?" Num? "surely not?" Nonne? "is it not so?"

units.la: 11. Aut similitudinis: ut, Quasi, <bl>gleich als</bl>. Ceu, <bl>gerad als</bl>. Sic, <bl>also</bl>. Sicut, <bl>wie</bl>. Ut, <bl>wie</bl>. Quemadmodum, <bl>als</bl>.
units.tr: 11. Of similarity: e.g. Quasi, "as if". Ceu, "just as". Sic, "thus". Sicut, "as". Ut, "as". Quemadmodum, "even as".

units.la: 12. Aut Qualitatis: ut, Doƈte, <bl>geschicklich/artlich</bl>. Pulchrè, <bl>fein</bl>. Civiliter, <bl>höfflich</bl>. Fortiter, <bl>dapffer</bl>.
units.tr: 12. Of quality: e.g. Doctè, "skilfully". Pulchrè, "finely". Civiliter, "courteously". Fortiter, "bravely".

units.la: 13. Aut Quantitatis: ut, multùm, <bl>viel</bl>. Parùm, <bl>wenig</bl>. Parumper, <bl>ein kleine weil</bl>.
units.tr: 13. Of quantity: e.g. Multùm, "much". Parùm, "little". Parumper, "for a little while".

units.la: 14. Aut Intendendi: ut, Valde, <bl>sehr</bl>. Prorsus, <bl>ganz</bl> <bl>und gar</bl>. Nimium, <bl>allzusehr</bl>. Admodum, <bl>trefflich</bl>.
units.tr: 14. Of intensity: e.g. Valde, "very". Prorsus, "altogether". Nimium, "too much". Admodum, "exceedingly".

units.la: 15. Aut remittendi: ut, sensim, <bl>allgemach</bl>. Paulatim, <bl>nach und nach</bl>. Pedetentim, <bl>fuß für</bl> <bl>fuß</bl> / <bl>gemächlich</bl>. Vix, <bl>kaum oder kaumet</bl>. Saltem, <bl>nuhr</bl> <bl>zum wenigsten</bl>.
units.tr: 15. Of diminishing: e.g. Sensim, "gradually". Paulatim, "little by little". Pedetentim, "step by step / slowly". Vix, "hardly". Saltem, "at least".

units.la: 16. Aut Dubitandi: ut, Forsan, forsitan, fortassis, fortasse, <bl>vielleicht</bl>.
units.tr: 16. Or of doubt: as, perhaps, perchance, perhaps, peradventure, perhaps (German: vielleicht).

units.la: 17. Aut Personæ: ut, mecum: <bl>mit mir</bl>. Tecum, <bl>mit</bl> <bl>dir</bl>. Secum, <bl>mit ihm selbs/mit sich</bl>. Nobiscum, <bl>mit uns</bl>. Vobiscum, <bl>mit euch</bl>.
units.tr: 17. Of person: e.g. Mecum, "with me". Tecum, "with you". Secum, "with himself / with themselves". Nobiscum, "with us". Vobiscum, "with you (plural)".

units.la: 18. Aut Vocandi: ut, Heus, <bl>hoscha</bl>. Eho, <bl>hola</bl>.
units.tr: 18. Of calling: e.g. Heus, "hey there". Eho, "hola".

units.la: 19. Aut Distribuendi: ut, Seorsim, <bl>besonders</bl>. Separatim, <bl>besonderlich</bl>. Privatim, <bl>daheim besonders</bl>. Bifariam, <bl>auff zweyerley weise</bl>. Trifariam, <bl>auff</bl> <bl>dreyerley weise</bl>.
units.tr: 19. Of distribution: e.g. Seorsim, "separately". Separatim, "apart". Privatim, "privately". Bifariam, "in two ways". Trifariam, "in three ways".

units.la: 20. Aut excludendi: ut, solù, tantù, duntaxat, <bl>allein</bl>.
units.tr: 20. Of exclusion: e.g. Solùm, tantùm, duntaxat, "only".

units.la: 21. Aut Jurandi: ut, Pol, <bl>bey dem Gott</bl>. Pollux.
units.tr: 21. Of swearing: e.g. Pol, "by God". Pollux.

units.la: 22. Aut Eligendi: ut, potiùs, <bl>lieber</bl>. Quàm, <bl>dann</bl>. Imò, <bl>ja viel mehr</bl>. Magis, <bl>mehr</bl>. Potissimù, <bl>am meisten</bl>.
units.tr: 22. Of choice: e.g. Potiùs, "rather". Quàm, "than". Imò, "nay, rather". Magis, "more". Potissimùm, "most of all".

units.la: 23. Aut congregandi: ut, simul, <bl>zu gleich.</bl> Una, <bl>mit e-</bl> <bl>inander</bl> Pariter, <bl>zu gleich.</bl> Collectim, <bl>jempt ich.</bl>
units.tr: 23. Of gathering together: e.g. Simul, "at the same time". Una, "together". Pariter, "alike". Collectim, "collectively".

units.la: 24. Aut admirandi: ut, papæ, <bl>bthü e Gott.</bl> Hui, <bl>boz.</bl> Vah, <bl>wanne</bl> Proh, <bl>hüff Gott.</bl>
units.tr: 24. Of admiration: e.g. Papae, "good heavens". Hui, "whoa". Vah, "ah". Proh, "God help us".

units.la: 25. Aut cominandi: ut, Væ, væ, <bl>weh/weh.</bl>
units.tr: 25. Of threatening: e.g. Væ, væ, "woe, woe".

units.la: 26. Aut dolendi: ut, Hei, Ah, <bl>ey/ ey/ jo einer seuff-</bl> <bl>zet.</bl> Heu, <bl>ach[?].</bl>
units.tr: 26. Of grief: e.g. Hei, Ah, "alas, ah, ay". Heu, "alas".

units.la: 27. Aut indignandi: ut, Hem, <bl>daß dich boz.</bl> Proh, <bl>ach/ ach</bl> Vah, <bl>pfau[?] ich an.</bl>
units.tr: 27. Of indignation: e.g. Hem, "fie upon you". Proh, "ah, ah". Vah, "shame on it".

units.la: 28. Aut exclamandi: ut, O, <bl>setter mordio.</bl>
units.tr: 28. Of exclaiming: e.g. O, "help, murder!"

units.la: 29. Aut exultandi: ut, Evax, <bl>jauch hoschaho.</bl>
units.tr: 29. Of exulting: e.g. Evax, "hurrah, hoschaho!"

units.la: Authorü lectio plures suppeditabit species, quas, cum in infinitum pateant, nihil attinet hic recenseri, inquit Dominus Philippus Melanchthon.
units.tr: The reading of authors will supply more kinds, which, since they extend to infinity, it is pointless to list here, says Lord Philip Melanchthon.

units.la: Nonnulla Adverbia comparantur: ut, fortiter, fortius, fortissime. Celeriter, celerius, celerrime. Parum, minus, minime. Saepe, saepius, saepissime. Nuper, nuperrime. Magis, maxime. Satis, quàg/ satius, <bl>be-</bl> <bl>ß/ ser.</bl> Virg. Nonne fuit satius, id est, melius.
units.tr: Some adverbs are compared: as fortiter, fortius, fortissime (bravely, more bravely, most bravely); celeriter, celerius, celerrime (quickly, more quickly, most quickly); parum, minus, minime (little, less, least); saepe, saepius, saepissime (often, more often, most often); nuper, nuperrime (recently, most recently); magis, maxime (more, most); satis, satius, (sufficiently, better; German: besser, better). Virgil: "Would it not have been better?" that is, more fitting (melius).

units.la: DE CONIUNCTIONE.
units.tr: ON THE CONJUNCTION.

units.la: Quid est Conjunctio?
units.tr: What is a conjunction?

units.la: CONjunctio est vox sine numero, quae superiori sententiæ aut parti subinde aliam annectit. Conjunctio est Sextuplex: Copulativa, qua tam sensus, quam voces copulantur: Et, Que, <bl>vnd/</bl> Quoq, <bl>auch.</bl> Ac, atq, <bl>vnd.</bl> Etiam, <bl>darzu.</bl> Simul, <bl>sampt.</bl> Cum, <bl>nicht</bl> <bl>allein.</bl> Tum, <bl>sondern auch.</bl>
units.tr: A conjunction is an indeclinable word which subsequently joins another clause or part to the preceding sentence. The conjunction is sixfold: Copulative, by which both sense and words are joined: And, que, and also (<bl>vnd/</bl>); also, <bl>auch</bl>. And, atque, <bl>und</bl>. Also, <bl>darzu</bl>. Together, <bl>sampt</bl>. Not only, <bl>nicht allein</bl>. Both... and, <bl>sondern auch</bl>.

units.la: Aut conditionalis, qua cum conditione sententia aut pars annectitur: ut, Cum, <bl>wenn.</bl> Dum, <bl>dieweil.</bl> Donec, <bl>so lange.</bl> Quatenus, <bl>so fern.</bl> Si, <bl>wann.</bl> Sin, <bl>wann</bl> <bl>aber.</bl> Nisi, <bl>wo nicht.</bl>
units.tr: Or conditional, by which a sentence or part is attached with a condition: as, when, <bl>wenn</bl>. While, <bl>dieweil</bl>. As long as, <bl>so lange</bl>. In so far as, <bl>so fern</bl>. If, <bl>wann</bl>. But if, <bl>wann aber</bl>. Unless, <bl>wo nicht</bl>.

units.la: Aut Diversativa, qua diversa sententia aut pars subjicitur : ut, At, Ast, Sed, Verùm, Verò, Atqui, <bl>aber</bl>. Tamen, je <bl>och</bl>. Quanquam, Quanvis, <bl>wiewol</bl>
units.tr: Or adversative (diversative), by which a different sentence or part is added: as, but, <bl>aber</bl>; but, <bl>aber</bl>; but, <bl>sed</bl>; but truly, <bl>verum</bl>; but indeed, <bl>vero</bl>; but yet, <bl>atqui</bl>, <bl>aber</bl>. Yet, <bl>je och</bl>. Although, <bl>wiewol</bl>.

units.la: Aut Adversativa, qua Adversa sententia aut pars adjungitur: ut, Ve, <bl>oder</bl>. Vel, <bl>oder</bl>. Aut, <bl>entweder</bl>. Sive, <bl>entweder /o</bl> er. Seu, <bl>oder</bl>.
units.tr: Or disjunctive (opposing), by which an opposed sentence or part is joined: as, or, <bl>oder</bl>. Or, <bl>oder</bl>. Either, <bl>entweder</bl>. Whether... or, <bl>entweder/oder</bl>. Or, <bl>oder</bl>.

units.la: Aut Causalis, qua alicujus rei causa subjicitur: ut, Nam, <bl>denn</bl>. Namque, Enim, Etenim, <bl>Denn</bl>. Quia, <bl>weil/daß</bl>. Quoniam, <bl>sintemal</bl>. Quando, Quandoquidem, <bl>dieweil</bl>.
units.tr: Or causal, by which the reason of some thing is added: as, for, <bl>denn</bl>. For, Namque; for, Enim; for, Etenim, <bl>denn</bl>. Because, <bl>weil/daß</bl>. Since, <bl>sintemal</bl>. Since, Quandoquidem, <bl>dieweil</bl>.

units.la: Aut Ratiocinativa, qua ex Antecedente consequens concluditur: ut, Ergo, <bl>derhalben</bl>. Ideo, <bl>darumb</bl> Igitur, <bl>derhalben</bl>. Idcirco, <bl>darumb</bl>. Quapropter, <bl>derwegen</bl> Proinde <bl>derhalben</bl>. Quamobrem, <bl>deshalben</bl>.
units.tr: Or inferential, by which the consequent is concluded from the antecedent: as, therefore, <bl>derhalben</bl>. For this reason, <bl>darumb</bl>. Therefore, Igitur, <bl>derhalben</bl>. For this cause, <bl>darumb</bl>. Wherefore, <bl>derwegen</bl>. Accordingly, Proinde, <bl>derhalben</bl>. Wherefore, Quamobrem, <bl>deshalben</bl>.

units.la: Observationes notatu dignæ.
units.tr: Observations worth noting.

units.la: Conjunctio, quæ nulla significationis necessitate, sed ornatus gratia orationi inseritur, vocatur à Grammaticis completiva.
units.tr: A conjunction which is inserted into the sentence for the sake of ornament, not from any necessity of meaning, is called by the grammarians "completive."

units.la: Conjunctio, quando alicui voci adjuncta, circumstantiam ejus una voce effert, potest esse Adverbium: Et contrà, Adverbium, quando superiori sententiæ aut parti subinde aliam annectit, potest esse Conjunctio.
units.tr: A conjunction, when attached to some word, expresses the circumstance of that word in a single word, may be an adverb: and conversely, an adverb, when it subsequently joins another clause or part to the preceding sentence, may be a conjunction.

units.la: DE SYNTAXI.
units.tr: ON SYNTAX.

units.la: Quid est Syntaxis?
units.tr: What is Syntax?

units.la: SYntaxis est secunda pars Grammaticæ, in qua de Vocum structura agitur.
units.tr: Syntax is the second part of grammar, in which the construction of words is treated.

units.la: Quæ est prima Regula de vocibus cons- truendis?
units.tr: What is the first rule for construing words?

units.la: Substantivum regit substantivum in Genitivo: ut, Crescit amor nummi, quantum ipsa pecunia crescit, Juvenalis.
units.tr: A substantive governs a substantive in the genitive: as, "The love of money grows as much as money itself grows," Juvenal.

units.la: Substantivum regit etiam Adjectivum, substantivè usurpatum, in Genitivo: ut, Voluptas esca malorum, Cicero. Arma illius, Virgil. Victus amore tui, Virgil. Ratio mei, nostri, Cicero. Domum ejus, Cic. Nostri causa,in Sacris legitur: Nostra causa in Cic.
units.tr: A substantive also governs an adjective used as a substantive, in the genitive: as, "Pleasure, the bait of evils," Cicero. "His arms," Virgil. "Overcome by love of you," Virgil. "The reason of me," "of us," Cicero. "His house" (domum ejus), Cicero. "For our sake" (nostri causa) is read in the Sacred writings; "our cause" is in Cicero.

units.la: Ergo, habet vim Nominis substantivi, accipiturq; pro causa sive gratia: ut,illius ergo venimus,Virgil.
units.tr: Therefore "ergo" has the force of a substantive noun and is taken to mean cause or sake: as, "We came for his sake," Virgil.

units.la: Substantivum regit Gerundium in Di: ut, mala & impia consuetudo est, contra Deos disputandi, sive ex animo id fit,sive simulatè,Cicero.
units.tr: A substantive governs a gerund in -di: as, "It is a bad and impure custom to dispute against the gods, whether this is done from conviction or in pretence," Cicero.

units.la: Adjectivum neutrius generis, substantivè usurpatum,regit Genitivum: ut, Quantum quisq; sua nummorum possider arca, Tantum habet & fidei, Juvenalis. Id negotij credidit sibi solum dari,Terentius.
units.tr: An adjective of the neuter gender, used as a substantive, governs the genitive: as, "However much money each man has in his chest, so much credit he has," Juvenal. "He believed this business had been given to him alone," Terence.

units.la: Genitivus saepe cum aliis vocibus praeponitur elegantèr regenti Substantivo: ut,literarum tuarum sum profecto admiratus elegantiam & venustatem. Multorum in nos perfidiam notabis,Cicero.
units.tr: The genitive is often placed elegantly before the governing substantive, with other words in between: as, "I have truly admired the elegance and charm of your letters." "You will note the treachery of many against us," Cicero.

units.la: Interdum Substantivum regit Verbum infinitum: ut, Tempus esset jam de ordine argumentorum aliquid dicere,Cicero. Sed haec phrasis & similes, Graecis relinquendae sunt.
units.tr: Sometimes a substantive governs an infinitive verb: as, "It was now time to say something about the order of the arguments," Cicero. But this phrase and similar ones are to be left to the Greeks.

units.la: Appositio est, cum substantiva eodem numero & casu absque Conjunctione de eadem re dicuntur: ut, Effodiuntur opes irritamenta malorum,Ovidius. In Appositione, Substantiva ponuntur in diverso numero, cum alterum plurale tantum & unius rei proprii, vel Nomen collectivum est: ut, Sum in urbe Athenis. Mortuus est in urbe Philippis. Anthropophagi, <bl>men-</bl> <bl>schenfresser</bl>[?] genus hominum ferox.
units.tr: Apposition is when substantives are predicated of the same thing, in the same number and case, without a conjunction: as, "Riches are dug up, the incitements of evils," Ovid. In apposition, substantives are placed in different numbers when the other is plural only and belongs to one thing, or is a collective noun: as, "I am in the city of Athens." "He died in the city of Philippi." Anthropophagi, a fierce race of men.

units.la: Quæ est secunda Regula?
units.tr: What is the second rule?

units.la: Substantivum regit Substantivum in Genitivo vel Ablativo cum Adjectivo descriptionis: ut, Accipies hospitem non multi cibi, sed multi joci, Cicero. Homo antiqua virtute & fide, Terentius.
units.tr: A substantive governs a substantive in the genitive or ablative together with an adjective of description: as, "You will receive a guest not of much food but of much jest," Cicero. "A man of ancient virtue and faith," Terence.

units.la: Quæ est tertia Regula?
units.tr: What is the third rule?

units.la: Opus, <bl>von nöten</bl> / substantivum indeclinabile, regit Ablativum sæpius, quàm Genitivum: ut, Non opus est verbis, ubi rerum testimonia adsunt, Cicero. Nunc animis opus est Aenea, nunc pectore firmo, Virgilius. Opus erit elegantioris alicujus, Cicero.
units.tr: Opus (need), an indeclinable substantive, governs the ablative more often than the genitive: as, "There is no need of words where the evidence of facts is present," Cicero. "Now there is need of the spirit of Aeneas, now of a firm breast," Virgil. "There will be need of something more elegant," Cicero.

units.la: Quando Nominativus præcedit: tum Opus significat Necessarium, <bl>notwendig</bl>: ut, Si quid erit istic opus, Cicero, id est, necessarium. Tu quæ istic opus erunt, administrari prospicies, Cicero, id est, quæ necessaria erunt.
units.tr: When a nominative precedes, opus means necessary: as, "If there is anything needful there," Cicero, that is, necessary. "You will see to it that those things which will be needful there are provided," Cicero, that is, which will be necessary.

units.la: Quæ est quarta Regula?
units.tr: What is the fourth rule?

units.la: Adjectivum & Substantivum eodem numero, genere & casu cohærent: ut, Amicus certus in re incerta cernitur, Cicero. Nullus ad amissas ibit amicus opes. Ovid. Tunc tua res agitur, paries cum proximus ardet, Horat. Cujus est sententia? Ciceronis. Cui dedisti literas? Tabellario. Cujus hic est liber? Meus, Tuus, Noster, Vester. Cujus est hæc penna? Mea, Tua, Nostra, Vestra. Cujus est hoc atramentarium? Meum, Tuum, Nostrum, Vestrum.
units.tr: An adjective and a substantive agree in number, gender and case: as, "A sure friend is seen in an uncertain matter," Cicero. "No friend will follow lost wealth," Ovid. "Then your own property is at stake when the neighbouring wall burns," Horace. "Whose is the opinion?" "Cicero's." "To whom did you give the letter?" "To the letter-carrier." "Whose book is this?" "Mine, yours, ours, yours (plural)." "Whose pen is this?" "Mine, yours, ours, yours." "Whose inkstand is this?" "Mine, yours, ours, yours."

units.la: Adjectivum participiale cum Nomine in Ablativo casu junctum, si consequentia designatur, per particulas, Cum, dum, quamvis, si, postquam, ubi, & similes, explicatur: ut, Imperante Maximiliano, Veneti graviter afflicti sunt, id est, cum vel dum imperaret Maximilianus. Oppressa libertate patriæ, nihil est quod amplius speremus, Cicero. Id est, postquam oppressa fuerit libertas.
units.tr: A participial adjective joined with a noun in the ablative, when a consequence is indicated, is explained by the particles cum, dum, quamvis, si, postquam, ubi, and similar ones: as, "Under Maximilian the Venetians were severely afflicted," that is, when or while Maximilian was ruling. "With the freedom of our country crushed, there is nothing further we may hope for," Cicero, that is, after freedom has been crushed.

units.la: Interdum Ablativus, Existente intelligitur: ut, Hæc fiunt te Rege, Duce, Consule, Auctore.
units.tr: Sometimes the ablative is understood as "existing": as, "These things are done with you as king, leader, consul, author."

units.la: Interdum solus Ablativus participialis, neutrius generis, usurpatur: ut, Cæsar, viso, audito, cognito, hostes discessisse, castra movit.
units.tr: Sometimes the participial ablative of the neuter gender is used alone: as, "Caesar, having seen, heard and learned that the enemy had withdrawn, moved the camp."

units.la: Adjectivum nominale sæpissimè substantivo præponitur: pronominale vero Adjectivum postponitur: ut, Natura tenacissimi fumus eorum, quæ rudibus annis percepimus, Quintilianus. Ampla domus dedecori Domino sæpe fit, Cicero. Divinum ingenium. Diuturnum silentium. Munus nostrum ornato verbis, quoad poteris, Terentius. Ingenium tuum. Pietas tua.
units.tr: A nominal adjective is very often placed before its substantive, but a pronominal adjective is placed after it: as, "The nature of those things which we have grasped in our untrained years is most tenacious," Quintilian. "A spacious house often becomes a disgrace to its master," Cicero. "Divine genius." "Long silence." "Adorn our gift with words as far as you can," Terence. "Your genius." "Your piety."

units.la: Inter Adjectivum & Substantivum nonnunquam una aut plures voces interponuntur: ut, sæpè rogabis, ut mea defunctæ molliter ossa cubent, Ovidius. De tuo ipsius studio conjecturam cœperis, Cicero. Qui adipisci veram justitiæ laudem volet, justitiæ fungatur officijs, Cicero. Desinant maledicere, malefacta ne noscant[?] tua, Terentius. Erat forma præter cæteras honesta & liberali. Terent.
units.tr: Sometimes one or more words are interposed between adjective and substantive: as, "You will often ask that my bones may lie softly once I am dead," Ovid. "You will have begun to form a conjecture from your own study," Cicero. "Whoever wishes to attain true praise for justice, let him perform the duties of justice," Cicero. "Let them cease to speak evil, lest they come to know your misdeeds," Terence. "She had a form honourable and more becoming than the others," Terence.

units.la: Interdum Adjectivum naturam Substantivi induit: ut, Fortunate senex, Virgilius. Rusticus ille tuus, Juvenalis.
units.tr: Sometimes an adjective takes on the nature of a substantive: as, "Fortunate old man," Virgil. "That rustic of yours," Juvenal.

units.la: Relativum cum Antecedente Substantivo necesse est numero & genere consentire: casu autem non semper convenit, nam is sequenti verbo respondet: ut, Quo semel est imbuta recens servabit odorem Testa diu. Horatius.
units.tr: A relative must agree with its antecedent substantive in number and gender, but not always in case, for it corresponds to the following verb: as, "Whatever the fresh jar was once steeped in, it will long keep the smell," Horace.

units.la: Relativum eleganter interdum Substantivo præponitur: ut, Quam mecum colis amicitiam, multi laudant. Quod habui summum pretium persolvi tibi, Terentius. pro, persolvi tibi summum pretium, quod habui.
units.tr: The relative is sometimes placed elegantly before its substantive: as, "The friendship which you cultivate with me, many praise." "What I had, I paid you as the highest price," Terence, that is, "I paid you the highest price, which I had."

units.la: Relativum Qui, Quæ, Quod, & Adjectivum participiale, appositum duobus Substantivis diversorum generum, sæpius cum Antecedente, quàm sequente, convenit: ut, Unus erat toto naturæ vultus in orbe, quem dixere chaos, Ovidius. Domicilia conjuncta, quas urbes dicimus, Cicero. Non omnis error stultitia dicenda est. Cicero, pro dicendus.
units.tr: The relatives qui, quae, quod, and a participial adjective, in apposition to two substantives of different genders, agree more often with the antecedent than with the following noun: as, "There was one countenance of nature in the whole world, which they called chaos," Ovid. "Joined dwellings, which we call cities," Cicero. "Not every error is to be called foolishness," Cicero, where dicendus would be expected.

units.la: Relativum interdum refert praecedentem orationem in neutro genere: ut, uxorem nunquam habui, quod isti fortunatum putant, Terentius.
units.tr: The relative sometimes refers to the preceding clause in the neuter gender: as, "I never had a wife, which those men think fortunate," Terence.

units.la: Adjectiva Distributiva conveniunt Substantivis pluralis numeri tantum: ut, Binas accepi abs te literas, Cicero.
units.tr: Distributive adjectives agree only with substantives of the plural number: as, "I received two letters from you," Cicero.

units.la: Prior Synthesis, <bl>die erste Zusammensetzung</bl> / Nominis, est cum Nomini multitudinis singulari, subjicitur Adjectivum plurale: ut, pars volucres factae, Ovid. Multitudinis nomina sunt: Gens, turba, populus, pars, quisq;, uterq;.
units.tr: The first synthesis of a noun is when a plural adjective is subjoined to a singular noun of multitude: as, "a part became birds," Ovid. Nouns of multitude are: gens, turba, populus, pars, quisque, uterque.

units.la: Posterior Synthesis Nominis est, cum qualicunq; Substantivo adjectivum diversi generis subjicitur, quod ad intellectum, non vocem refertur: ut, in Eunuchum suam, Terentius. Intelligitur, in suam fabulam Eunuchum. Albula pota Deo, Ovidius. Intelligitur, Aqua. Triste lupus stabulis, Virgilius. Intelligitur, Animal. Huc refer & illa: Samnitum caesi tria millia, Livius. Duo millia crucibus affixi, Cuitius.
units.tr: The second synthesis of a noun is when an adjective of a different gender is subjoined to any substantive, referring to the sense rather than the word: as, "into his own play, the Eunuch," Terence; understood, "into his own play, the Eunuchus."
