units.tr: Without an adverb, the dative of cause, of instrument, or of a similar circumstance is frequently joined to a noun or verb: for example, φθόνῳ τοῦτο ἐποίησεν [phthonō touto epoiesen], he did this out of envy. ἀπέκτεινεν τῇ ξίφει [apekteinen tē xiphei], he killed with the sword. πῶς τρόπῳ γράφεις; [pōs tropō graphheis], how do you write? (in what manner do you write?)

units.la: Quae est vicesimaquarta Regula?
units.tr: What is the twenty-fourth Rule?

units.la: Cum Adverbium πότε, quando, interrogandi, expresse vel tacite praecedit, nomen temporis in Genitivo ponitur: ut, νυκτὸς ἢ ἡμέρας ἀσκεῖ[?], noête dieque studet. Νηστεύω δὶς τῆς σαββάτου[?], Lucae 18. Iejuno bis in Sabbato.
units.tr: When the adverb πότε, when, used interrogatively, precedes either expressly or implicitly, a noun of time is put in the genitive: for example, νυκτὸς ἢ ἡμέρας ἀσκεῖ [nyktos ē hēmeras askei], he practises night and day. Νηστεύω δὶς τῆς σαββάτου [nēsteuō dis tēs sabbatou], Luke 18. I fast twice on the Sabbath.

units.la: Quae est vicesimaquinta Regula?
units.tr: What is the twenty-fifth Rule?

units.la: Cum Adverbium μέχρις οὗ[?], quamdiu, interrogandi, expresse vel tacite praecedit, nomen temporis in Dativo vel Accusativo ponitur: ut, εἴκοσιν ὅλοις ἔτεσιν ἀποδημήσας[?], viginti integris annis profectus est peregrè. ὅλῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἠργασάμην[?], tota die operatus sum.
units.tr: When the adverb μέχρις οὗ [mechris hou], how long, used interrogatively, precedes either expressly or implicitly, a noun of time is put in the dative or accusative: for example, εἴκοσιν ὅλοις ἔτεσιν ἀποδημήσας [eikosin holois etesin apodēmēsas], he went abroad for twenty whole years. ὅλῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἠργασάμην [holē tē hēmerā ērgasamēn], I worked the whole day.

units.la: Quae est vicesimasexta Regula?
units.tr: What is the twenty-sixth Rule?

units.la: Duę negationes apud Graecos vehementius negant: ut, χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν[?], Iohann. 15. Sine me non potestis facere quicquam. Apud Latinos duae negationes affirmant.
units.tr: Two negatives among the Greeks deny more emphatically: for example, χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν [chōris emou ou dynasthe poieinouden], John 15. Without me you can do nothing. Among the Latins, two negatives affirm.

units.la: Quæ est vicesimaseptima Regula?
units.tr: What is the twenty-seventh Rule?

units.la: Adverbia : ἕως, dum vel donec : πρὶν [?], priusquam: verbis finitis & infinitis adjunguntur.
units.tr: The adverbs ἕως, while or until, and πρὶν [prin], before, are joined to finite and infinite verbs.

units.la: Ἐπειδὰν [?], postquam, convenit verbis, quibus ἐὰν inter conjugandum praeponitur.
units.tr: Ἐπειδὰν [epeidan], after, agrees with verbs in which ἐὰν is placed before the verb in conjugation.

units.la: Quæ est vicesimaoctava Regula?
units.tr: What is the twenty-eighth Rule?

units.la: Conjunctiones : κἂν, quamvis : ὅτι [?], quòd : conveniunt verbis, quibus nihil praeponitur, aut quibus ἄν inter conjugandum praefigitur.
units.tr: The conjunctions κἂν, although, and ὅτι [hoti], that, agree with verbs to which nothing is prefixed, or to which ἄν is prefixed within the conjugation.

units.la: Κἂν, atq; si : ἵνα, ut: ὄφρα, donec dum: ὡς, ut: ὅπως, ut: ὅταν, quum : ὁπότ' ἐπεὶ [?], quandoquidem: conveniunt verbis, quibus ἐὰν inter conjugandum praeponitur. Diversa significatione aliis etiam verbis conveniunt.
units.tr: Κἂν, and if; ἵνα, that; ὄφρα, until, while; ὡς, as; ὅπως, that; ὅταν, when; ὁπότ', when; ἐπεὶ, since: these agree with verbs to which ἐὰν is placed before within the conjugation. With a different meaning they also agree with other verbs.

units.la: Notandum contra Iesuvitas, quòd ὅτι [?] aliquando est conjunctio collectiva seu rationalis, & significat ideo vel propterea: ut, ἀφέωνταί [?] σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησε πολύ, Lucae 2. Remissa sunt peccata ejus multa, ideo seu propterea dilexit multum. Sic 1. Regum 2.accipitur.
units.tr: It should be noted, against the Jesuits, that ὅτι [hoti] is sometimes a collective or rational conjunction and means therefore or for this reason: for example, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησε πολύ, Luke 7. Her many sins are forgiven her, therefore (for this reason) she loved much. So it is taken in 1 Kings 2.

units.la: Apud Græcos Colon notatur puncto, ad summum literæ posito, sic·
units.tr: Among the Greeks the colon is marked with a point placed at the top of the letter, thus·

units.la: Interrogationis signum hoc est;
units.tr: The sign of a question is this;

units.la: Comma & periodus notantur ut apud Latinos.
units.tr: The comma and the period are marked as among the Latins.

units.la: Lecturi præcepta prolixiora, videant Græcā Grammaticam Michaelis Neandri vel Clenardi Grámaticam à Frid.Sylburgio denuò recognitam, & Græcam Syntaxin Doctissimi viri Iohannis Posselij [?]. Qui autem omnium Græcarum vocum significationes scire volunt : diligenter infigne Lexicon Iohannis Scapulæ, Basileæ ab Episcopio excusum legunto.
units.tr: Those wishing for fuller precepts should see the Greek grammar of Michael Neander, or the Greek grammar of Clenardus, newly revised by Friedrich Sylburg, and the Greek syntax of the most learned man Johannes Posselius. Those who wish to know the meanings of all Greek words should diligently read the outstanding lexicon of Johannes Scapula, printed at Basel by Episcopius.

units.la: GRAMMATICA HEBRAICA.
units.tr: GRAMMATICA HEBRAICA.

units.la: Quid est Grammatica He- braica?
units.tr: What is Hebrew grammar?

units.la: Grammatica Hebraica est ars pure loquendi Hebraice. Die Hebreische sprächekunst ist eine kunst seuberlich Hebreisch zu sprechē.
units.tr: Hebrew grammar is the art of speaking Hebrew correctly. (The Hebrew speech-art is an art of speaking Hebrew properly.)

units.la: Quot sunt ejus Partes?
units.tr: How many parts does it have?

units.la: Duæ: Etymologia & Syntaxis.
units.tr: Two: Etymology and Syntax.

units.la: Quid est Etymologia?
units.tr: What is Etymology?

units.la: Etymologia est prima pars Grammaticæ, in qua de singularū vocum proprietate agitur.
units.tr: Etymology is the first part of grammar, in which the peculiar properties of individual words are treated.

units.la: Quid est Vox?
units.tr: What is a word?

units.la: Vox est nota, qua unaquæque res vocatur.
units.tr: A word is a sign by which each thing is called.

units.la: Unde fit Vox?
units.tr: Of what is a word made?

units.la: E literis.
units.tr: Of letters.

units.la: Quot sunt literæ apud He- bræos?
units.tr: How many letters are there among the Hebrews?

units.la: Triginta quinque, à dextra sinistram versus legendæ, quarum hæ sunt figuræ, nomina & potestates.
units.tr: Thirty-five, to be read from right to left. Their shapes, names and sounds are these.

units.la: אָא Aleph sonat prout habet additam vocalem: ut, א a, א e, א i, א o, א u. ֻ Camez vocalis longa est a. ָ Pathah, vocalis brevis, est a. ַ Hatephpathah, vocalis brevis, est a raptum. ֵ Zere, vocalis longa, est e. ֶ Segol, vocalis brevis, est e. ֵ Hatephsegol, vocalis brevis, est e raptum. ְ Scheua, vocalis brevis, est e raptum. ִ Hiric magnum, vocalis longa, est i. ִ Hiric parvum, vocalis brevis, est i. ֹ Holem, vocalis longa, est o. ֳ Hatephcamez, vocalis brevis, est o raptum. ׁ Schurec, vocalis longa, est u. ֻ Kybbuz, vocalis brevis, est y.
units.tr: Aleph [א] sounds according to the vowel added to it: thus א a, א e, א i, א o, א u. Qamets [ָ] is a long vowel, a. Patah [ַ] is a short vowel, a. Hatef-patah is a short vowel, a reduced a. Tsere [ֵ] is a long vowel, e. Segol [ֶ] is a short vowel, e. Hatef-segol is a short vowel, a reduced e. Sheva [ְ] is a short vowel, a reduced e. Hiriq gadol [ִ] is a long vowel, i. Hiriq qatan is a short vowel, i. Holem [ֹ] is a long vowel, o. Hatef-qamets is a short vowel, a reduced o. Shureq [ׁ] is a long vowel, u. Qibbuts [ֻ] is a short vowel, u.

units.la: בּ ב Beth cum Dages, id est, puncto in me= dio, ב profertur ut b durum: sine Dages ב ut b molle seu aspiratum.
units.tr: Beth [ב] with dages, that is, a point in the middle, is pronounced as a hard b; without dages, ב is pronounced as a soft or aspirated b.

units.la: ג Gimel cū Dages ג g: sine Dages ג gh.
units.tr: Gimel [ג] with dages is g; without dages it is gh.

units.la: ד Daleth cum Dages ד d: sine Dages ד dh.
units.tr: Daleth [ד] with dages is d; without dages it is dh.

units.la: ה He aspiratio lenis, h.
units.tr: He [ה] is a light aspiration, h.

units.la: ו Vau sonat fere ut f: sed nō ita aspiratur.
units.tr: Vav [ו] sounds almost like f, but it is not aspirated in this way.

units.la: ז Zain est ẓ lene vel dz.
units.tr: Zayin [ז] is a soft z or dz.

units.la: ח Heth aspiratio fortis h vel ch.
units.tr: Heth [ח] is a strong aspiration, h or ch.

units.la: ט Teth est t.
units.tr: Teth [ט] is t.

units.la: י Iod sonat sicut j in jehova.
units.tr: Yod [י] sounds like the j in Jehovah.

units.la: כ Caph cum Dages ך: sine Dages כ. In fine signatur sic ך.
units.tr: Kaph [כ] with dages, and [ך] at the end of a word; without dages it is [כ]. At the end it is written thus [ך].

units.la: ל Lamed est l.
units.tr: Lamed [ל] is l.

units.la: מ Mem est m. In fine signatur sic ם vel sic ם.
units.tr: Mem [מ] is m. At the end it is written thus [ם] or thus [ם].

units.la: נ Nun est n. In fine scribitur sic ן.
units.tr: Nun [נ] is n. At the end it is written thus [ן].

units.la: ס Samech est s.
units.tr: Samekh [ס] is s.

units.la: ע Ajin sonat prout habet additam vocalem. Iudæi efferunt gargarismo tanquam g.
units.tr: Ayin [ע] sounds according to the vowel added to it. The Jews pronounce it from the throat with a gargling sound, like g.

units.la: פּ Pe cum Dages ࣰ p: sine Dages ࣰ ph vel f. In fine signatur sic ף.
units.tr: Pe [פּ] with dages is p; without dages it is ph or f. At the end it is written thus [ף].

units.la: צ Zade est ץ forte vel tf. In fine scribitur sic ץ.
units.tr: Tsade [צ] is ts, strong or tf. At the end it is written thus [ץ].

units.la: ק Kuph est k vel q.
units.tr: Qof [ק] is k or q.

units.la: ר Resch est r.
units.tr: Resh [ר] is r.

units.la: ש Schin cum punêto in dextro cornu ש est sch: in sinistro cornu ש est s.
units.tr: Shin [ש] with a point on the right horn is sch; with the point on the left horn it is s.

units.la: ת Thau cu Dages ת t: sine Dages ת th.
units.tr: Tav [ת] with dages is t; without dages it is th.

units.la: Quotuplices sunt literæ?
units.tr: What kinds of letters are there?

units.la: Duplices: Vocales aut Consonæ.
units.tr: Two kinds: vowels or consonants.

units.la: Quid dicis de vocalibus?
units.tr: What do you say about the vowels?

units.la: Vocales sicut consonis subjiciuntur, præter holem, ֹ schurec, ita postillas pronunciantur, ut, בַ ba, בֵ be, לַ la, לֵ le.
units.tr: Vowels are placed under the consonants, except holem and shureq, and are pronounced after them, as בַ ba, בֵ be, לַ la, לֵ le.

units.la: Excipe - pathah, quod in fine vocis ante ה he, ח heth, ע ajin, profertur: ut, אֱלוֹהַּ eloah, non elōha: רוּחַ ruach, non rucha: דֵּעַ deag, non dega: Quod idem fit in voce quadrisyllaba ירוּשָׁלַם Ierusch alaim per diphthongum ai, non Ierusch alámi.
units.tr: Except that patah, when it comes at the end of a word before ה he, ח heth or ע ayin, is pronounced before it: as אֱלוֹהַּ eloah, not elōha; רוּחַ ruach, not rucha; דֵּעַ deag, not dega. The same happens in the four-syllable word ירוּשָׁלַם Ierusch alaim, pronounced with the diphthong ai, not Ierusch alámi.

units.la: Quid dicis de consonis?
units.tr: What do you say about the consonants?

units.la: Ex consonis quædam appellantur labiales, eò quòd adminiculo labiorum pronuntientur, ut sunt בּוּמָף bumâph.
units.tr: Some of the consonants are called labials, because they are pronounced with the help of the lips, such as בּוּמָף bumaph.

units.la: Quædam dentales, ut sunt זַסְשָׁרָץ zasscharáz.
units.tr: Some are dentals, such as זַסְשָׁרָץ zasscharaz.

units.la: Quædam linguales, ut sunt דַּטְלָנָת datlanáth.
units.tr: Some are linguals, such as דַּטְלָנָת datlanath.

units.la: Quædā palatales, ut sunt גִּיכָק gichák.
units.tr: Some are palatals, such as גִּיכָק gichak.

units.la: Quædā gutturales, ut sùt אַהְחָץ achág.
units.tr: Some are gutturals, such as אַהְחָץ achag.

units.la: Quædam vocantur אֶהְוִי ehevi, quiescentes, quòd scilicet quiescant, hoc est, puncto carentes post longas vocales, & duas breves - pathah & ֶ segol, non legantur: ut, קָרְאָת karátha. גְּלָה gelé: לוֹ ló: צָדֶה zadé: פְּלָא pélé. Attamen in fine, ו vau sæpe sonat tanquam u, & י jod post ־ came-pathah, ִ holem, ֵ schurec, sonat tanquam i & utrunq; coalescit cum precedente vocali in diphthongum: ut, שָׁלוֹ schaléu, פִּיו piu, קָו káu, צָו záu, פָּנַי panái,
units.tr: Some are called ehevi [אֶהְוִי], that is, quiescent letters, because they are silent: that is, they carry no point after long vowels and after the two short vowels patah and segol, and are not read. Thus קָרְאָת karatha; גְּלָה gelé; לוֹ ló; צָדֶה zadé; פְּלָא pelé. Yet at the end, ו vav often sounds like u, and י yod after qamets-patah, holem or shureq sounds like i, and each combines with the preceding vowel into a diphthong: thus שָׁלוֹ schaléu, פִּיו piu, קָו kau, צָו zau, פָּנַי panai,

units.la: אֵלִי elái, נוֹי goi, גָּלוּי galúi.
units.tr: אֵלִי elai, נוֹי goi, גָּלוּי galui.

units.la: Quæda appellantur radicales, eò quòd ad radicem, hoc est, thema seu originem vocis semper pertineant, vt sunt in his vocibus memoriæ caussa collectæ, גַּר זְחָט gadh zachat saáph zakár.
units.tr: Some are called radicals, because they always belong to the root, that is, the theme or origin of the word. They are found in these words, collected for the sake of memory: גַּר זְחָט gadh zachat saaph zakar.

units.la: Quædam servíles dicuntur, eò quòd servant vocibus ad aliquid constituendum vel significandum, vt sunt: אַב הוי כלם נשת abhói chyllám náscheth.
units.tr: Some are called servile, because they are added to words to form or signify something: they are אַב הוי כלם נשת abhoi chyllam nascheth.

units.la: א Aleph habet aut segol, aut pathah, & tantùm dictionem incipit, quádo Hebraicum est.
units.tr: Aleph [א] takes either segol or patah, and begins a word only when the word is Hebrew (native).

units.la: ב Beth servíens in principio nominis significat in, cum, inter, aliquando instrumentum & motû ad locum: Quando verò servit in principio verbi infiniti, per cum, addito verbo, vel duos Ablativos consequentiæ exponitur. Punctatur autem sic: primò ב habet subjectum scheva, sed ante literam schevatam, mutat suum
units.tr: Beth [ב], serving at the beginning of a noun, means "in", "with", "among", sometimes an instrument, and motion towards a place. But when it serves at the beginning of an infinitive verb, it is explained by "with" plus the verb, or by two ablatives of consequence. It is pointed as follows: first, ב has sheva under it; but before a letter with sheva, it changes its own

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] scheva in hiric, altero scheva manente. Idem faciunt כ ke ל le.
units.tr: [illegible, about six letters] sheva into hiric, the other sheva remaining. Kaph [כ] and lamed [ל] do the same.

units.la: Secundò ב beth mutat suum scheva & scheva sequentis jod, in unum hiric. Idem faciunt כ ke, ל le, ו ve. Sed ante יְהֹוָה Ie-hova mutat utrunque scheva in unum pathah.
units.tr: Second, beth changes its own sheva and the sheva of a following yod into one hiric. Kaph, lamed and vav do the same. But before יְהֹוָה Jehovah it changes both shevas into one patah.

units.la: Tertiò ב beth mutat suum scheva in pathah sequente -: hatephpathah, vel infegol, sequente ֓: hatephsegol. Idem faciunt כ ke, ל le, ו ve. Sed ante אֱלֹהִים Elohim, & ante verbum infinitum אָמַר emor, mutant in zere, ab א sequente, omnibus punctis rejectis.
units.tr: Third, beth changes its sheva into patah when a − follows; into hatef-patah, or into segol, when ֓ follows; into hatef-segol. Kaph, lamed and vav do the same. But before אֱלֹהִים Elohim, and before the infinitive verb אָמַר emor, they change into tsere, because of the following א, all the other points being removed.

units.la: Quartò ב beth usurpat puncta extrusi ה He articuli demonstrandi, nepe pathah, sequente dages forti. Sic ב ke, ל le, ו ve.
units.tr: Fourth, beth takes the point of the demonstrative article ה he, namely patah, with a strong dages following. Kaph, lamed and vav do the same.

units.la: ה He in principio serviens efficit articulum demonstrandi, ille, vel Genitivum. Punctatur autem sic: Primo ה He habet pathah, sequente dages, quod dages cum poni no potest in sequenti litera (nempe gutturali aliqua vel Resch ) mutatur pathah in camez.
units.tr: He [ה], serving at the beginning, makes the demonstrative article, "that", or the genitive. It is pointed as follows. First, ה has patah, with dages following; since the dages cannot be placed in a following letter (namely some guttural or resh), patah is changed into qamets.

units.la: Secundò ה He mutat suum pathah in segol sequente ה vel ח heth.
units.tr: Second, ה changes its patah into segol when a ה or ח heth follows.

units.la: ה He est etiam Adverbium interrogādi, & tunc habet -: hatephpathah, aut ante gutturalem & ante schevatam solum pathah, aut si gutturalis habeat camez, ה habet segol.
units.tr: ה is also the interrogative adverb, and then it has a hatef-patah, or only patah before a guttural and before a sheva; or, if the guttural has qamets, ה has segol.

units.la: ו Vau serviens in principio est Conjunctio copulativa. Punctatur autem sic: Primò ו vau habet subjectū scheva, quod sequente litera schevata aut labiali, mutatur in schurec.
units.tr: Vav [ו], serving at the beginning, is the copulative conjunction. It is pointed as follows. First, ו has a sheva under it, which, when a letter with sheva or a labial follows, is changed into shureq.

units.la: Secundò, ו vau quando parvas voces conjungit, mutat suum scheva in camez: ut וָךְ קח kach valech.
units.tr: Second, vav, when it joins short words, changes its sheva into qamets, as וָךְ קח kach valech.

units.la: Tertiò ו vau convertit praeteritū, quando nullū aliud praecedit, in futurū, & tunc punctatur cum scheva: quod cum mutandum est, mutatur juxta regulas traditas.
units.tr: Third, vav, which converts a preterite into a future when no other word precedes it, is pointed with sheva; and when this has to be changed, it is changed according to the rules given.

units.la: Quartò 1 convertens futurum in præteritum, punctatur cum pathah, posito dages in litera sequenti. Sed pathah, subsequente Aleph (quod Dages non recipit) mutatur in Camez. Schevato ˌ jod non imprimitur Dages a 1 va.
units.tr: Fourth, vav converting a future into a preterite is pointed with patah, with dages placed in the following letter. But patah, when an Aleph follows (which does not take dages), is changed into qamets. A dages is not impressed on the vav in the case of a sheva with yod.

units.la: ב Caph in principio est Adverbium similitudinis, sicut, ut, tanquam. Si præponatur numeralibus, significat circiter: sin verbo infinito præfigatur, efficit tempus, quod per duos Ablativos consequetiæ exponitur. Ejus punctum est scheva, quod mutatur sicut scheva in litera ב beth.
units.tr: Kaph [ך] at the beginning is an adverb of likeness: "as", "like", "as if". If it is placed before numerals, it means "about"; but if it is prefixed to an infinitive verb, it makes a tense, which is explained by two ablatives of consequence. Its point is sheva, which is changed just like the sheva of the letter beth.

units.la: ל Lamed in principio est Dativi casus nota, aut Genitivi cùm author vel possessor indicatur. Significat etiam tempus, & motum ad locum. Cum infinito efficit Gerundium in di, & dum, ac Supinum inum, vel ut causalem, addito verbo. Ejus punctum est scheva, quod mutatur sicut scheva in litera Beth. Ante monosyllaba longa, & dissyllaba accentum in penultima habentia, peculiariter habet camez.
units.tr: Lamed at the beginning is the sign of the dative case, or of the genitive when the author or possessor is indicated. It also signifies time and motion towards a place. With an infinitive it makes a gerund in -di, and dum (while), and a supine in -inum, or, with a verb added, a causal clause. Its point is shewa, which changes like the shewa in the letter Beth. Before monosyllables that are long, and dissyllables with the accent on the penult, it peculiarly takes qamets.

units.la: ם Mem serviens nomini significat a, ab, de, ex, præ, propter. Est autem desumptum ex voce integra מִן[?] min. Adjectivo postpositum efficit cōparativum, sequente substantivo. Cum verbo infinito exponitur per Ne, velut, non, addito verbo. Ejus punctum est hiric, sequente dages, quod cum poni non potest, sequente gutturali vel Resch, mutatur hiric in zere.
units.tr: Mem serving a noun signifies a, ab, de, ex, præ, propter (from, by, of, out of, before, on account of). It is derived from the whole word min. Placed after an adjective it makes a comparative, with the substantive following. With an infinitive verb it is rendered ne, velut, non (lest, as, not), with a verb added. Its point is hiriq when a dagesh follows, which cannot be placed; when a guttural or Resh follows, hiriq changes into tsere.

units.la: ש Schin in principio serviens efficit pronomen relativum utriusq; numeri & generis. Item Conjunctionem Quòd, ut, quia. Punctum ejus est segol, sequente dages, si modò poni potest, sin minus, habet segol solum, interdum etiam pathah.
units.tr: Shin at the beginning, serving, makes the relative pronoun of either number and gender. It is also the conjunction quod, ut, quia (that, as, because). Its point is segol when a dagesh follows, if indeed it can be placed; otherwise it has segol alone, sometimes also patah.

units.la: Ex servilibus quædā dicūtur האמנתי[?] heemánti, quarum adjectione ad frontem vel calcem alicujus radicis, Hebræi sua nomina verbalia formant.
units.tr: Some of the servile letters are called heemanti, and by adding them to the front or end of a root the Hebrews form their verbal nouns. ## What is Dages?

units.la: Quid est Dages?
Dages est punctum in ventre literæ, hoc modo, ב: Estq; forte aut lene.
units.tr: Dages is a point placed in the belly of a letter, thus ב. It is either forte or lene.

units.la: Quid est Dages forte?
units.tr: What is Dages forte?

units.la: Quod in medio vocis post vocalem brevem, consonam duplicat, hoc est, unam in geminam dividit, ut שִׁבֵּר schibbèr, ac si essent duo ב. Omnesq; consonæ illud admittunt, exceptis א aleph, ה he, ח heth, ע ajin, ר resch. Atttamen ה he habet in vetre punctum Mappik appellatum, quo indicatur consonam ה he proferendam esse, ut יָדָהּ jadach, manus ejus.
units.tr: It is the point that, in the middle of a word after a short vowel, doubles a consonant, that is, divides one letter into two, as in שִׁבֵּר [schibbèr], as if there were two ב. All consonants admit it except א [aleph], ה [he], ח [heth], ע [ajin] and ר [resch]. However, ה [he] has in its belly a point called Mappik, which indicates that the consonant ה [he] is to be pronounced, as in יָדָהּ [jadach], her hand.

units.la: Quid est Dages lene?
units.tr: What is Dages lene?

units.la: Quod in principio, & medio vocis post scheva quiescens consonam fortificat, sed non geminat, ut, בן filius : אשבר efchbór, frangam. Et locum habet in sex consonis בגדכפת beghadh kephath, quas intendit ac duras reddit. Nam lene nominatur respectu fortis tanquam durioris.
units.tr: It is the point that, at the beginning and in the middle of a word, after a quiescent sheva, strengthens a consonant without doubling it, as in בן [ben], son, and אשבר [efchbór], I will break. It occurs in the six consonants בגדכפת [beghadh kephath], which it tightens and makes hard. For lene is so called in relation to forte, as the harder of the two.

units.la: Quid est Scheva?
units.tr: What is Sheva?

units.la: Scheva est vocalis brevissima e, sub consona posita hoc modo, בְ. Et legitur aut quiescit.
units.tr: Shewa is the very short vowel e, placed under a consonant, thus בְ. It is either read or quiescent. ## Where is it read?

units.la: Ubi legitur?
In principio vocis, ut, דְבִיר debir, oraculum. Deinde in medio post vocales longas, ut פָּקְדוּ pakedú. שֹׁמְרִים schomerim.
units.tr: At the beginning of a word, as דְבִיר debir, oracle. Then in the middle, after long vowels, as פָּקְדוּ pakedú, שֹׁמְרִים schomerim.

units.la: Tertiò, sub consona Dagessata, ⁊[?] sub consona cujus similis sequitur, ut דִּבְּרוּ dibberú, locuti sunt: הַלְלוּ halelú, laudate.[?]
units.tr: Thirdly, under a consonant with dagesh, or under a consonant followed by a similar one, as דִּבְּרוּ dibberú, they spoke; הַלְלוּ halelú, praise ye.

units.la: Quartò, in medio vocis, scheva geminato, prius quiescit, posterius legitur, ut יִפְקְדוּ jiphkedú.
units.tr: Fourthly, in the middle of a word, when shewa is doubled, the first is quiescent and the second is read, as יִפְקְדוּ jiphkedú. ## Where is it quiescent?

units.la: Ubi quiescit?
Primò in medio vocis post vocales breves, ut פִּקְדוּ pikdú. nisi sequatur gutturalis: ut, מַלְאָךְ maleách.
units.tr: Firstly, in the middle of a word after short vowels, as פִּקְדוּ pikdú, unless a guttural follows, as מַלְאָךְ maleách.

units.la: Secundò, in fine vocis non solû simplex, sed etiam geminum scheva quiescit, licèt dages adfit, ut, שָׁלֵךְ fchalách, non fchala-che: שִׁלְכַת fchalacht, non fchalachete nec fchalachte.
units.tr: Secondly, at the end of a word, not only simple but also doubled shewa is quiescent, even though a dagesh is present: as שָׁלֵךְ fchalách, not fchala-che; שִׁלְכַת fchalacht, not fchalachete nor fchalachte.

units.la: Tertiò, fcheva fub penultima primi & fecúdi futuri in plurali fœminino in נָה na, quiefcit, ubi ḥolem fine vau plerunq; præcedit, ut, תִּפְקֹדְנָה tiphcódna, non tiphcodena: פְּקֹדְנָה pekódna, non pekodena.
units.tr: Thirdly, sheva under the penultima of the first and second future, in the feminine plural ending in נָה [na], is quiescent, where holem, usually without vau, precedes it, as in תִּפְקֹדְנָה [tiphcódna], not tiphcodena; פְּקֹדְנָה [pekódna], not pekodena.

units.la: I. Regula de Accentibus.
units.tr: I. Rule concerning accents.

units.la: Monofyllaba dicłio habet accentum, nifi cum fequente uno accentu efferatur: ut, בֵּן ben, filius, אָב ab, pater, בֶּן־דָּוִד benDavid, Filius David.
units.tr: A monosyllabic word has the accent, unless it is pronounced together with a following accented word, as in בֵּן [ben], son; אָב [ab], father; בֶּן־דָּוִד [benDavid], son of David.

units.la: II. Regula.
units.tr: II. Rule.

units.la: In diffyllabis & polyfyllabis, fi ultima fuerit longa, accentus eft in eadem: ut דָּבָר dabár, verbum, מָלֵא malé, implevit.
units.tr: In dissyllables and polysyllables, if the last syllable is long, the accent is on it: as דָּבָר dabár, word, מָלֵא malé, he filled.

units.la: Excipe בַּיִת bajith, domus. שָׁמַיִם fchamájim, cœli, & alia nonnulla.
units.tr: Except בַּיִת bajith, house, שָׁמַיִם fchamájim, heavens, and some others. ## III. Rule.

units.la: III. Regula.
Quando in fine crefcunt fyllabæ, accentus ad ultimam defcendit: ut, דְּבָרִים debarim, verba, מָלְאוּ maleú, impleuerút.
units.tr: When syllables are added at the end, the accent descends to the last: as דְּבָרִים debarim, words, מָלְאוּ maleú, they filled.

units.la: Excipe קָמוּ kámu, furrexerút, הִפְקִידָה hiphkída, vifitauit fœmina, יִפְקִידוּ japhkídu, vifitabunt, תִּפְקִידוּ taphkídu, vifitabitis, & hafce fyllabas, ה ha, נָה na, נה nna, תָּ ta, תֶּ te, תִּי ti, נִי ni, מוֹ mo, הוּ hu, נוּ nu, נּוּ nnu: Et ה cha vel ה ha, fi vel quiefcens præcesserit: Et ה locale vel paragogicum in nominibus, quæ relinquunt accentum in penultima: ut פְּקִדְתִּי pakádti, vifitavi, פְּקֻדְנָה pekódna, vifitate, פְּקֻדוּךְ pekaducha, vifitarút te, דְּבָרֵיהָ debaréha, verba ejus, אַרְצָה árʒa, in terram.
units.tr: Except קָמוּ kámu, they rose, הִפְקִידָה hiphkída, she visited, יִפְקִידוּ japhkídu, they will visit, תִּפְקִידוּ taphkídu, you will visit, and these syllables: ה ha, נָה na, נה nna, תָּ ta, תֶּ te, תִּי ti, נִי ni, מוֹ mo, הוּ hu, נוּ nu, נּוּ nnu. And ה cha or ה ha, if a vowel or a quiescent letter has preceded; and the locative or paragogic ה in nouns which leave the accent on the penult: as פְּקִדְתִּי pakádti, I visited, פְּקֻדְנָה pekódna, visit ye, פְּקֻדוּךְ pekaducha, they visited you, דְּבָרֵיהָ debaréha, her words, אַרְצָה árʒa, to the land. ## IV. Rule.

units.la: IV. Regula.
Si ultima habuerit ֶ segol, vel patah, loco segol, accentus est in penultima: ut, מֶלֶךְ mélech, rex, פּוֹקֵדֵת pokédeth, vifitans, שֹׁמֵעַת schomáath, audiens, נַעַר nâ-gar, puer.
units.tr: If the last syllable has ֶ segol, or patah instead of segol, the accent is on the penult: as מֶלֶךְ mélech, king, פּוֹקֵדֵת pokédeth, visiting, שֹׁמֵעַת schomáath, hearing, נַעַר nâ-gar, boy.

units.la: Excipe quando segol est in fine, sequente ה quiescente, vel ם servilibus, tum accentus est in ultima: ut, חֹזֶה hozé, videns, פְּקֻדָתֶם pekadtém, visitastis, דְּבַרְכֶן debarchen, verbum vestrum.
units.tr: Except when segol is at the end, followed by a quiescent ה, or by the servile ם, then the accent is on the last: as חֹזֶה hozé, seeing, פְּקֻדָתֶם pekadtém, you visited, דְּבַרְכֶן debarchen, your word.

units.la: Hasce Regulas ex Gramatica Schin deleri excerpsimus: Lecturi pleniorem tractatum de Accentibus, videant Grammaticam Avenarij.
units.tr: We have excerpted these rules from the Grammar of Schin, which are to be deleted. Those who want a fuller treatise on accents should see the Grammar of Avenarius.

units.la: Quid est Meteg?
units.tr: What is Meteg?

units.la: Est virgula recta descendens, apposita puncto vocali, cujus pronuntiationem instar fræni retinet aut remoratur in principio vocis, ut לָרָקִיעַ larakía. Interdum vocalis brevis pducitur virgula Meteg, atq; tuc scheua quiescēs legitur, ut וַיְהִי váiebi.
units.tr: It is a straight stroke descending, placed beside a vowel point, which holds back or delays the pronunciation at the start of the word, as larakía [לָרָקִיעַ]. Sometimes a short vowel is lengthened by the Meteg stroke, and then a silent shewa is read, as váiebi [וַיְהִי].

units.la: Quid est Maccaph?
units.tr: What is Maccaph?

units.la: Est virgula inter duas voces, copulans illas sub uno accentu, ut גַּם־אִישָׁה Gamischáh, etiam maritus ejus.
units.tr: It is a stroke between two words, joining them under one accent, as Gamischáh [גַּם־אִישָׁה], "even her husband."

units.la: Quotuplex est vox Hebraica?
units.tr: How many kinds of Hebrew word are there?

units.la: Duplex: Numeri aut sine Numero.
units.tr: Two: those with number and those without number.

units.la: Quot
units.tr: How many?

units.la: Duæ: Nomen & Verbum.
units.tr: Two: noun and verb.

units.la: DE NOMINE.
units.tr: ABOUT THE NOUN.

units.la: Quid est Nomen?
units.tr: What is a noun?

units.la: NOmen est vox numeri cum genere, casu & declinatione.
units.tr: A noun is a word that has number, together with gender, case and declension.

units.la: Quotuplex est Nomen?
units.tr: How many kinds of noun are there?

units.la: Duplex: Substantivu aut Adjectivu.
units.tr: Two: the substantive and the adjective.

units.la: Quid accidit Adjectivis Nominibus?
units.tr: What belongs to adjectival nouns?

units.la: Comparatio, cujus gradus tres dicūtur, Positivus, Comparativus & Superlativus.
units.tr: Comparison, whose degrees are said to be three: positive, comparative and superlative.

units.la: Quomodo Comparativus & Superlativus formantur?
units.tr: How are the comparative and superlative formed?

units.la: Si Positivo adjiciatur Adverbiū יותר jother, magis, fit Comparativus: sin מאד meod, valde, fit inde Superlativus, ut טוב tób, bonus, יותר טוב jother tób, magis bonus, id est, melior, מאד טוב meod tób, valde bonus, id est, optimus. Frequentius tamen Comparativus describitur per מן min adjectivo postpositum, sequente substantivo, ut supra in litera ם Mem dictum est.
units.tr: If the adverb יותר jother, more, is added to the positive, the comparative is formed; if מאד meod, very, is added, the superlative is formed from it. For example, טוב tób, good; יותר טוב jother tób, more good, that is, better; מאד טוב meod tób, very good, that is, best. More often, however, the comparative is expressed by מן min placed after the adjective, followed by the substantive, as was said above under the letter Mem.

units.la: Quot sunt genera Hebraicorum nominum?
units.tr: How many genders do Hebrew nouns have?

units.la: Duo: Masculinum & foemininum.
units.tr: Two: masculine and feminine.

units.la: Quae Nomina sunt Masculini generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of masculine gender?

units.la: Quae viro, aut rebus viri specie conceptis congruunt, ut דָּיִד[?] David: אָב ab, pater: כָּרַת[?] Peráth, fluvius Euphrates.
units.tr: Those which agree with a man, or with things conceived in the form of a man, as David [דָּוִיד], Ab [אָב], father, Perath [פְּרָת], the river Euphrates.

units.la: Deinde omne Adjectivum est masculi-ni generis, & movetur in foemininum, assumpta litera ה, quam semper praecedit ־ camez, ut, טוֹב tob, bonus, טוֹבָה tobah bona.
units.tr: Next, every adjective is of masculine gender, and is changed into the feminine by adding the letter ה [He], which is always preceded by qamets [־], as טוֹב tob [tob], good, and טוֹבָה tobah [tobah], good (feminine).

units.la: Adjectivum participiale movetur in foemininum, assumpta litera ה He, quam praecedit ־ camez, vel (in regimine) afsumpta litera ת tau, quam praecedit ֽ segol, ut, פּוֹקֵד pokéd, vir visitas, פּוֹקְדָה vel פּוֹקֵדֶת pokedáh vel pokédeth, foemina
units.tr: A participial adjective is changed into the feminine by adding the letter ה He, preceded by qamets, or (in the construct state) by adding the letter ת tau, preceded by segol [ֽ], as פּוֹקֵד pokéd [pokéd], a man visiting, and פּוֹקְדָה or פּוֹקֵדֶת pokedáh or pokédeth, a woman

units.la: viſitans, מפקד mephakkéd, מפקדה mephakkedáh vel מפקדת mephakkédeth.
units.tr: visiting; מפקד mephakkéd, מפקדה mephakkedáh or מפקדת mephakkédeth.

units.la: מפקיד maphkíd, מפקידה maphkiáh vel מפקדת maphkéleth. מתפקד mithpakkéd, מתפקדה mithpakkedáh vel מתפקדת muthpakkedeth, &c.
units.tr: maphkid (masc.), maphkidah or maphkeleth (fem.) [מפקיד, מפקידה, מפקדת]. mithpakked (masc.), mithpakkedah or muthpakkedeth (fem.) [מתפקד, מתפקדה, מתפקדת], etc.

units.la: Quæ Nomina sunt fœminini generis?
units.tr: Which nouns are of feminine gender?

units.la: Quæ mulieri aut rebus mulieris specie conceptis congruunt, ut, אם ém, mater: בבל bábel, Babylonia.
units.tr: Those which agree with a woman, or with things conceived in the form of a woman, as, אם ém, mother; בבל bábel, Babylonia.

units.la: Deinde, quæ natura dualitatem in animalis corpore habent, ut, עין ájin, oculus: יד jádh, manus. רגל réghel, pes.
units.tr: Secondly, those which by nature have duality in the animal body, as עין ájin, eye; יד jádh, hand; רגל réghel, foot.

units.la: Tertiò quæ desinunt in ה He, præcedente camez, in ת tau, præcedente segol, in ית ith, in ות uth, fœminini generis sunt. Hisce regulis cum sequentibus vocibus fœmininis, ארץ érez, terra, אש ésh, ignis, אבן ében, lapis, observatis, reliqua substantiva sunt masculini generis.
units.tr: Thirdly, those which end in ה He, preceded by camez, in ת tau, preceded by segol, in ית ith, in ות uth, are of feminine gender. With these rules observed, together with the following feminine words, ארץ érez, earth; אש ésh, fire; אבן ében, stone, all the remaining substantives are of masculine gender.

units.la: Quot sunt Casus?
units.tr: How many cases are there?

units.la: Apud Hebraeos nomina non variantur de casu in casum, sed mutantur duntaxat de singulari numero in pluralem. Nonnunquam tamen, sed non constanter & perpetuo, casus obliqui exprimuntur, praepositis quibusdam servilibus consonis, invariata Nominis terminatione, in hunc modum:
units.tr: Among the Hebrews, nouns do not vary from case to case, but change only from singular to plural number. Sometimes, however, though not consistently or always, oblique cases are expressed by placing certain servile consonants before the noun, the ending of the noun remaining unchanged, in this way:

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. דָּבָר dabár, verbum. G. הַדָּבָר haddabár, verbi. D. לְדָבָר ledabár, verbo. A. אֵת־דָּבָר eth dabár, verbum. V. הַדָּבָר haddabár, ô verbum. A. מִדָּבָר middabár, à verbo.
units.tr: Nom. דָּבָר dabár, word. Gen. הַדָּבָר haddabár, of the word. Dat. לְדָבָר ledabár, to the word. Acc. אֵת־דָּבָר eth dabár, the word. Voc. הַדָּבָר haddabár, O word. Abl. מִדָּבָר middabár, from the word.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. דְּבָרִים debarím, verba. G. הַדְּבָרִים haddebarím, verborū. D. לִדְבָרִים lidbarím, verbis. A. אֵת־דְּבָרִים eth debarim. verba.
units.tr: Nom. דְּבָרִים debarím, words. Gen. הַדְּבָרִים haddebarím, of words. Dat. לִדְבָרִים lidbarím, to words. Acc. אֵת־דְּבָרִים eth debarim, words.

units.la: V. הַדְּבָרִים haddebarim, ò verba. A. מִדִּבְרִים middebarim, à verbis.
units.tr: Voc. הַדְּבָרִים haddebarim, O words. Abl. מִדִּבְרִים middebarim, from words.

units.la: Quot sunt Declinationes apud Hebræos?
units.tr: How many declensions are there among the Hebrews?

units.la: Duæ. Prima & Secunda.
units.tr: Two: the first and the second.

units.la: Quid est prima Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the first declension?

units.la: Prima Declinatio est quæ completitur nomina masculini generis, quorum pluralis numerus definit in ים im, ut מֶלֶךְ melech. rex, מְלָכִים melachim, reges.
units.tr: The first declension comprises masculine nouns whose plural ends in ים im, as מֶלֶךְ melech, king; מְלָכִים melachim, kings.

units.la: Interdum masculina in plurali desinunt in ות oth, ut אָב ab, pater, אָבוֹת aboth patres.
units.tr: Sometimes masculines end in the plural in ות oth, as אָב ab, father; אָבוֹת aboth, fathers.

units.la: Nomina specierum animalium sæpe in singulari numero capiuntur pluraliter, ut בָּקָר bakár, bos & boues.
units.tr: Names of kinds of animals are often taken in the singular in a plural sense, as בָּקָר bakár, ox, and oxen.

units.la: Quid est secunda Declinatio?
units.tr: What is the second declension?

units.la: Secunda Declinatio est quæ completitur nomina fœminini generis, quorum pluralis numerus definit in ות oth, ut חֶרֶב chereb, gladius, חַרְבוֹת charaboth, gladij.
units.tr: The second declension comprises feminine nouns whose plural ends in ות oth, as חֶרֶב chereb, sword; חַרְבוֹת charaboth, swords.

units.la: Multa fœminina in plurali desinunt in ים im, ut נְמֵלָה nemelá, formica, נְמָלִים nemelím, formicæ.
units.tr: Many feminines end in the plural in ים im, as נְמֵלָה nemelá, ant; נְמָלִים nemelím, ants.

units.la: Quædam habent utranq; terminationem plurale, ut, שָׁנָה schaná, annus, שָׁנוֹת schánoth, & שָׁנִים schanim, anni.
units.tr: Some have both plural endings, as שָׁנָה schaná, year; שָׁנוֹת schánoth and שָׁנִים schanim, years.

units.la: Nomina dualitatem significantia faciunt dualem numerum in יִם im, præcedentē pathah, ut רֶגֶל règhel, pes, רַגְלַיִם raghlájim, ambo pedes.
units.tr: Nouns signifying duality form the dual number in יִם im, preceded by pathah, as רֶגֶל règhel, foot; רַגְלַיִם raghlájim, both feet.

units.la: Declina Adjectiva Anomala, quæ ab aliis pronomina ap- pellantur.
units.tr: Decline the anomalous adjectives, which others call pronouns.

units.la: Pronomen primæ personæ utriusq; generis. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: First person pronoun of both genders. Singular Number.

units.la: N. אֲנִי ani & אָנֹכִי anochi, ego. 'i & נִי ni, affixa pronomina dicuntur, eo quod nunquam inueniantur separatim, sed perpetuo fini vocis adhærescant. 'i cum nominibus significat, meus, mea, meum, ut, אָבִי abi, pater meus: נִי ni, cū verbis denotat, me, ut פָּקָדַנִי pekadáni, visitauit me. G. שלי schelli, mei. D. לי li, mihi. Ac. אתי othi, me. A. ממני mimmenni, & מני minni, à me.
units.tr: ani and anochi, I. 'i and [נִי] ni, are called affixed pronouns, because they are never found separately but always cling to the end of a word. 'i with nouns means, my, as [אָבִי] abi, my father: ni with verbs denotes, me, as [פָּקָדַנִי] pekadáni, he visited me. Gen. schelli [שלי], of me. Dat. li [לי], to me. Acc. othi [אתי], me. Abl. mimmenni [ממני] and minni [מני], from me.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. נחנו nachnu, et אנחנו anachnu, nos.
units.tr: Nom. נחנו nachnu, and אנחנו anachnu, we.

units.la: Affixum נו nu, cum nominibus, noster, no-stra, nostrū: cū verbis Nos Accusatiuus. G. שלנו schellanu, nostri. D. לנו lanu, nobis. Ac. אתנו othanu, nos. Ab. ממנו mimmennu, à nobis.
units.tr: The suffix נו nu, with nouns: our (noster, nostra, nostrum); with verbs: us. Acc.: us. Gen.: שלנו schellanu, of us. Dat.: לנו lanu, to us. Acc.: אתנו othanu, us. Abl.: ממנו mimmennu, from us.

units.la: Pronomen secunda persona mascu-lini generis. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Pronoun of the second person, masculine gender. Singular Number.

units.la: N. אתה attah, tu. G. שלך schellecha, tui. Affixu ך cha, cum nominibus tuus, tua, tuum: cum ver-bis Te. D. לך lecha, tibi. Ac. אתך othecha, te. Ab. מִמְּךָ mimmecha, à te.
units.tr: Nom. אתה attah, you. Gen. שלך schellecha, of you. The suffix ך cha, with nouns: your (tuus, tua, tuum); with verbs: you. Dat. לך lecha, to you. Acc. אתך othecha, you. Abl. מִמְּךָ mimmecha, from you.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. אַתֶּם attem, vos.
units.tr: Nom. אַתֶּם attem, you (plural).

units.la: G. שֶׁלָּכֶם schellachem, vestri. Affixum כֶם chem, cum nominibus Vester, a, um: cum verbis Vos.
units.tr: Gen. שֶׁלָּכֶם schellachem, of you. The suffix כֶם chem, with nouns: your (vester, a, um); with verbs: you (vos).

units.la: D. לָכֶם lachem, vobis.
units.tr: Dat. לָכֶם lachem, to you.

units.la: Ac. אֶתְכֶם ethchem. vos.
units.tr: Acc. אֶתְכֶם ethchem, you.

units.la: Ab. מִמְּכֶם mimmechem, à vobis.
units.tr: Abl. מִמְּכֶם mimmechem, from you.

units.la: Pronomen secundæ personæ fœminini generis.
units.tr: Pronoun of the second person, feminine gender.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. אַתְּ at, tu.
units.tr: Nom. אַתְּ at, you.

units.la: G. שֶׁלָּךְ schellach, tui. Affixum ךְ ch, cū nominibus Tuus, a, um: cū verbis Te.
units.tr: Gen. שֶׁלָּךְ schellach, of you. The suffix ךְ ch, with nouns: your (tuus, a, um); with verbs: you.

units.la: D. לָךְ lach, tibi.
units.tr: Dat. לָךְ lach, to you.

units.la: Ac. אֹתָךְ othach, te.
units.tr: Acc. אֹתָךְ othach, you.

units.la: Ab. מִמָּךְ mimmach, à te.
units.tr: Abl. מִמָּךְ mimmach, from you.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. אַתֵּן atten, vos.
units.tr: Nom. אַתֵּן atten, you (plural).

units.la: G. שֶׁלָּכֶן schellachen, vestri. Affixum כֶן chen, ךֵן[?] chen,cum nominibus vester,a,um:cum verbis Vos. D. לָכֶן lachen, vobis. Ac. אֶתְכֶן ethchen, vos. Ab. מִמְּכֶן mimmechen, à vobis.
units.tr: Gen. שֶׁלָּכֶן schellachen, of you. The suffix כֶן chen, and ךֵן[?] chen, with nouns: your (vester, a, um); with verbs: you (vos). Dat. לָכֶן lachen, to you. Acc. אֶתְכֶן ethchen, you. Abl. מִמְּכֶן mimmechen, from you.

units.la: Pronomen tertiæ personæ mascu- lini generis. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Pronoun of the third person, masculine gender. Singular Number.

units.la: N. הוּא hu,hic,is,ipse. G. שֶׁלּוֹ schellô,ipsius. Affixum } o cū nominibus Ejus, הוּ hu cum verbis Eum. D. לוֹ lo,ipsi. Ac. אֹתוֹ othó,ipsum. Ab. מִמֶּנּוּ mimménnu,ab ipso.
units.tr: Nom. הוּא hu: this, he, that, himself. Gen. שֶׁלּוֹ schellô: of him. The suffix o with nouns: his (ejus); הוּ hu with verbs: him (eum). Dat. לוֹ lo: to him. Acc. אֹתוֹ othó: him. Abl. מִמֶּנּוּ mimménnu: from him.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. הֵם hem & הֵמָּה hémma,ipsi. Af-fixum ם Mem cum nominibus Eorum: cum verbis Eos: Et הֵם hem,cum solis nominibus pluralibus Eorum. G. שֶׁלָּהֶם schellahém,ipsorum. D. לָהֶם lahém & לָמוֹ lámo,ipsis.
units.tr: Nom. הֵם hem and הֵמָּה hémma: they. The suffix ם Mem with nouns: their (eorum); with verbs: them (eos); and הֵם hem with plural nouns only: their (eorum). Gen. שֶׁלָּהֶם schellahém: of them. Dat. לָהֶם lahém and לָמוֹ lámo: to them.

units.la: Ac אֶתְהֶם ethbhem [?] e: אֹתָם otham, ipsos.
units.tr: Acc. אֶתְהֶם ethhem [אֶתְהֶם] [the text is unclear]: אֹתָם otham, them.

units.la: Ab. מֵהֶם mehem, ab ipsis.
units.tr: Abl. מֵהֶם mehem, from them.

units.la: Pronomen tertiæ personæ fæminini generis.
units.tr: Pronoun of the third person, feminine gender.

units.la: Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: Singular Number.

units.la: N. הִיא hi, hæc, ea, ipsa.
units.tr: Nom. הִיא hi: this, she, it, herself.

units.la: G. שֶׁלָּה schellah, ipsius. Affixū ה ha, vel ה cum Mappik, cum nominibus Ejus: cum verbis Eam.
units.tr: Gen. שֶׁלָּה schellah: of her. The suffix ה ha, or ה with Mappiq: her (ejus); with verbs: her (eam).

units.la: D. לָהּ lah, ipsi.
units.tr: Dat. לָהּ lah: to her.

units.la: Ac. אֹתָהּ othah, ipsam.
units.tr: Acc. אֹתָהּ othah: her.

units.la: Ab. מִמֶּנָּה mimmennah, ab ipsa.
units.tr: Abl. מִמֶּנָּה mimmennah: from her.

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural Number.

units.la: N. הֵנָּה henna & הֵן hen, ipsæ.
units.tr: Nom. הֵנָּה henna and הֵן hen: they (feminine).

units.la: G. שֶׁלָּהֵן schellahen, ipsarum. Affixū ] Nun cum nominibus Earum: cum verbis Eas: Et הֵן hen cum solis nominibus, pluralibus Earum.
units.tr: Gen. שֶׁלָּהֵן schellahen: of them (feminine). The suffix Nun with nouns: their (earum); with verbs: them (eas); and הֵן hen with plural nouns only: their (earum).

units.la: D. לָהֵן lahen, ipsis.
units.tr: Dat. לָהֵן lahen: to them.

units.la: Ac. אֹתָן othan & אֶתְהֵן ethhen, ipsas.
units.tr: Acc. אֹתָן othan and אֶתְהֵן ethhen: them (feminine).

units.la: Ab. מֵהֵן mehen, ab ipsis. Affixa tertiæ persona sæpè sunt reciproca, ut דבר debaró, verbum suum.
units.tr: Abl. מֵהֵן mehen: from them. The suffixes of the third person are often reflexive, as דבר debaró [דְּבָרוֹ]: his word.

units.la: Quæ Pronomina sunt indeclinabilia?
units.tr: Which pronouns are indeclinable?

units.la: זה ze, hic, iste: זאת zoth, ista: הוא hu, is qui, ISTI, ISTÆ: אלה elle, isti, istæ. מי mi, quis, quæ, de homine interrogat: מה meh & מה mah, quid? de quacunq; re alia interrogant: אשר ascher, relativum, qui, quæ, quod.
units.tr: זה ze: this, that; זאת zoth: this (feminine); הוא hu: he who, this one, THESE (masculine); אלה elle: these, those (masculine and feminine). מי mi: who, which, of a person, asks about a person; מה meh and מה mah: what? asks about any other thing; אשר ascher: relative pronoun, who, which, that.

units.la: Quando Dativus pronominis primitivi post אשר ascher, ponitur, fit inde pronomè possessivum, quod absolutè sine substantivo usurpatur: ut, אשר לי ascher li, meus, mea, meum: אשר לנו ascher lanú, noster, nostra, nostrum: אשר לך ascher lechá, tuus, a, tuum, &c.
units.tr: When the dative of a primitive pronoun is placed after אשר ascher, it becomes a possessive pronoun, used absolutely without a noun: thus, אשר לי ascher li: mine (meus, mea, meum); אשר לנו ascher lanú: ours (noster, nostra, nostrum); אשר לך ascher lechá: yours (tuus, tua, tuum), etc.

units.la: DE VERBO.
units.tr: ON THE VERB.

units.la: Quid est Verbum?
units.tr: What is a verb?

units.la: VErbum est vox numeri cum forma, persona, tempore & conjugatione.
units.tr: A verb is a word of number, together with form, person, tense and conjugation.

units.la: Quotuplex est forma Verbi? Duplex: Prima aut Secunda.
units.tr: How many kinds of form does a verb have? Two: the first and the second.

units.la: Quotuplex est Persona? Triplex, & unaquaeq; suo genere distinguitur: prima tamen quaelibet, & tertia pluralis praeteriti sunt communes.
units.tr: How many persons are there? Three, and each is distinguished by its own form. However, any first person and the third person plural of the past tense are common.

units.la: Quotuplex est tempus? Duplex: Praeteritum aut Futurum.
units.tr: How many tenses are there? Two: the past and the future.

units.la: Quotuplex est Praeteritum? Vnicum est pro omnibus praeteritis, ut פקד visitabat, visitavit, visitaverat.
units.tr: How many past tenses are there? One serves for all pasts, as פקד (visited), visited, had visited.

units.la: Quotuplex est Futurum? Duplex: Primum aut secundum. Cum praeteritum & futurum primum indefinitè sumuntur etiam praesens tempus comprehendunt.
units.tr: How many futures are there? Two: the first and the second. Since the past and the first future are used indefinitely, they also cover the present tense.

units.la: Conjuga verba formae primae.
units.tr: Conjugate the verbs of the first form.

units.la: Praeteritum tempus.
units.tr: The past tense.

units.la: PAAL SIVE CAL. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: PAAL OR KAL. Singular number.

units.la: 1.C. | 2.M. | 3.M. פקד פקדת פקדה פקדה
units.tr: 1st common | 2nd masc. | 3rd masc.: פקד פקדת פקדה פקדה
2nd fem. | 3rd fem.

units.la: פָּקְדָּה פָּקְדַת
units.tr: פָּקְדָּה פָּקְדַת

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.
1st common | 2nd masc. | 3rd common

units.la: פְּקָדוּ פְּקַדְתֶּם פְּקָדְנוּ
units.tr: פְּקָדוּ פְּקַדְתֶּם פְּקָדְנוּ
2nd fem.

units.la: פְּקַדְתֶּן
units.tr: פְּקַדְתֶּן

units.la: Pakád, ille vir, pakedá, illa fœmina vifitavit, pakádta, tu vir, pakádt, tu fœmina vifitasti, pakádti, ego vir vel fœmina vifitavi.
units.tr: Pakád, that man visited; pakedá, that woman visited; pakádta, you man; pakádt, you woman visited; pakádti, I, a man or a woman, visited.

units.la: Pakedú, illi viri vel fœminæ vifitarunt, pekadtèm, vos viri, pekadtén, vos fœminæ vifitastis, pakádnu, nos viri, vel fœminæ vifitavimus.
units.tr: Pakedú, those men or women visited; pekadtèm, you men; pekadtén, you women visited; pakádnu, we, men or women, visited.

units.la: Apud Hebræos tertia persona singularis masculina, est Thema. Verba igitur, quæ in tertia persona habent terminantes vocales, -pathah, -zere, i holem, conjugantur in Paal siue Kal: ut, שָׁמַר schamár, custodivit, חָפֵץ chaphéz, voluit, יָכוֹל jachól, potuit: Et sunt aut Activa seu Transitiva levius significantia, aut neutra seu absoluta, quæ Hebræi stantia appellant.
units.tr: Among the Hebrews the third person singular masculine is the theme. Verbs therefore which have the terminating vowels pathah, zere or holem in the third person are conjugated in Paal or Kal, as שָׁמַר schamár [shamar], he kept; חָפֵץ chaphéz [chafetz], he wished; יָכוֹל jachól [yakhol], he was able. They are either active or transitive, signifying somewhat lightly, or neuter or absolute, which the Hebrews call "standing".

units.la: Verba, quæ in tertia persona singulari masculina, sub prima * hiric, dages in secunda, & ˙˙ zere, vel interdum ˉ pathah, sub eadem habent, conjugantur in Piel: Et quæ in Cal actiua sunt, hic extendunt significationem, ut, [Hebrew: אָכַל] achál comedit, [Hebrew: אֶכֵּל] ikkél, immoderate comedit. Quæ autem in Kal sunt neutra, hic fiunt Activa, ut, הלך halach, ambulavit, הלך hillech, fecit ambulare, seu duxit.
units.tr: Verbs which in the third person singular masculine have hiric under the first letter, dages in the second, and zere, or sometimes pathah, under the same letter, are conjugated in Piel. Those which are active in Kal here extend their meaning: for example, אָכַל achál [akhal], he ate, and אֶכֵּל ikkél [ikkel], he ate immoderately. Those which are neuter in Kal become active here: for example, הלך halach [halakh], he walked, and הלך hillech [hilekh], he made to walk, or led.

units.la: Quæ vero in Kal non habentur, & hic extant, sunt transitiva, ut, תקן tikken, aptavit.
units.tr: Those which do not occur in Kal but are found here are transitive, as תקן tikken [tiken], he fitted or adjusted.

units.la: Verba, quæ in tertia persona singulari, ab ה hi, vel ה he, sequente gutturali, habente hatephsegol, incipiunt, conjugantur in Hiphil: Et quae in Paal sive Kal sunt neutra, hic fiunt transitiva, ut שָׁכַב schachab, jacuit, הַשְׁכִּיב hischkib, fecit jacere, seu posuit.
units.tr: Verbs which in the third person singular begin with ה hi or ה he, followed by a guttural having hatephsegol, are conjugated in Hiphil. Those which are neuter in Paal or Kal become transitive here, as שָׁכַב schachab [shakhav], he lay, and הַשְׁכִּיב hischkib [hishkiv], he made to lie, or laid down.

units.la: Quaedam tamen sunt neutra in Kal, & hic etiam, ut קָרַב karab, & הִקְרִיב hikrib, accessit. Quae in Kal transeunt ad duo, hic ad tria, ut אָכַל achal, comedit, puta panem, הַאֲכִיל heechil, fecit comedere te panem.
units.tr: Some verbs are neuter in Kal and here too, as קָרַב karab [qarav], he drew near, and הִקְרִיב hikrib [hiqriv], he brought near. Those which are transitive to two objects in Kal become transitive to three here, as אָכַל achal [akhal], he ate, that is, bread, and הַאֲכִיל heechil [he'akhil], he made you eat bread.

units.la: Quae in Kal non sunt, & hic extant, habent significationem Kal, ut, הִשְׁלִיךְ hischlich, projecit.
units.tr: Those which do not occur in Kal but are found here have the meaning of Kal, as הִשְׁלִיךְ hischlich [hishlikh], he threw forth.

units.tr: We have conjugated the finite verbs; the infinitives follow.

units.la: פָּקוֹד pakód, visitare, cum quatuor consonis seruilibus, quæ in vocem בְּכְלָם bachlam, collectæ sunt, sic:
units.tr: Pakod, to visit, with the four servile letters, which are gathered into the word bachlam, goes thus: biphkod, kiphkod, liphkod, miphkod.

units.la: בִּפְקוֹד כִּפְקוֹד לִפְקוֹד מִפְּקוֹד biphkód, cùm visitaret, vel visitauisset, kiphkód, liphkód, ad visitandum, vel, vt visitem, mip-pekód, vt non visitem, vel, ne visitem.
units.tr: Biphkod, when he visited or had visited; kiphkod; liphkod, to visit, or that I may visit; mippekod, that I may not visit, or lest I visit.

units.la: Prima infiniti absoluti habet camez, sed cùm literis Bachlam illud in scheva mutat.
units.tr: The first of the absolute infinitive has qamets, but with the letters bachlam it changes that into shewa.

units.tr: Pakked, with the letters bachlam: bephakked, kephakked, lephakked, mippakked.

units.tr: Passives, which receive their passion from some agent, are conjugated in Niphal, as saraph, he burned, nisraph, he was burned.

units.la: Interdum verba, quæ actiue significant, hic conjugantur, ut נִשְׁבַּע nischbâg, juravit, נִלְחָם nilchâm, præliatus est.
units.tr: Sometimes verbs which have an active meaning are conjugated here, as nishbag, he swore, nilcham, he fought.

units.la: Verba in Pyal sunt tantùm passiva, eorumq; usus est, ubi nomen agentis nō exprimitur. Hic prima radicalis signatur cum Kybuz, raro cum ֽ: hatephcamez, & media imprimitur dages. Quando vero Ajin non potest capere dages, conuertitur illud cum suo kybuz in holem & interdum in schurec.
units.tr: Verbs in Pual are only passive, and their use is where the name of the agent is not expressed. Here the first radical is marked with qibbuts, rarely with hataph qamets, and the middle letter receives a dagesh. When, however, ayin cannot take a dagesh, it is changed, together with its qibbuts, into holem, and sometimes into shureq.

units.tr: Singular number. 1st common: hithpakkadti | 2nd masc.: hithpakkadta | 3rd masc.: hithpakked [?]
2nd fem.: hithpakkadt | 3rd fem.: hithpakkeda [?]

units.la: Pluralis Numerus. I. C. 2. M. 3. M. הִתְפַּקְּדוּ | הִתְפַּקְּדְתֶּם | הִתְפַּקְּדְנוּ [?]
units.tr: Plural number. 1st common: hithpakkadnu | 2nd masc.: hithpakkadtem | 3rd masc.: hithpakkedu [?]
2nd fem.: hithpakkadten [?]

units.la: Hithpakked, hithpakkeda, hithpakkadta, hithpakkádt, hithpakkádti. Hithpakkedú, hithpakkadtém, hithpakkadtén, hithpakkádnu.
units.tr: Hithpakked, hithpakkeda, hithpakkadta, hithpakkadt, hithpakkadti. Hithpakkedu, hithpakkadtem, hithpakkadten, hithpakkadnu.

units.la: Verba in Hithpael sunt & actiua & passiua habetia sub una voce reciprocam significationem, ut, התקדש hithkaddesch, sanctificauit se, vel sanctificatus est à se.
units.tr: Verbs in Hithpael are both active and passive, having under one form a reciprocal meaning, as hithkaddesh, he sanctified himself, or he was sanctified by himself.

units.la: Primum futurum tempus. Singularis Numerus.
units.tr: First future tense. Singular number.
1st c. 2nd m. 3rd m.

units.la: יתפקד תתפקד אתפקד
units.tr: yitpaqqad, titpaqqad, 'itpaqqad
2nd f. 3rd f.

units.la: תתפקדי
units.tr: titpaqqedi

units.la: Pluralis Numerus.
units.tr: Plural number.
1st c. 2nd m. 3rd m.

units.la: יתפקדו תתפקדו יתפקדו
units.tr: yitpaqqedu, titpaqqedu, yitpaqqedu
2nd f. 3rd f.

units.la: תתפקדנה תתפקדנה
units.tr: titpaqqedna, titpaqqedna

units.la: Secundum futurum tempus. Plur.Num. Singul.Num.
units.tr: Second future tense. Plural number. Singular number.
2nd m. 2nd m.

units.la: התפקדו hithpakkedú. התפקד hithpakkéd
units.tr: hithpakkedú (plural); hithpakkéd (singular)
2nd f. 2nd f.

units.la: התפקדנה hithpakkédna. התפקדי hithpakkedí. התפקד hithpakkéd. Hîc literæ Bachlam ב be, כ ke, ל le, מ me, adduntur.
units.tr: hithpakkédna (plural); hithpakkedí (singular); hithpakkéd (singular). Here the letters Bachlam, be, ke, le, me, are added.

units.la: Hactenus dictum est de vocibus Numeri, videlicet de Nomine & Verbo: sequuntur voces sine numero, nempe Adverbium & Conjunctio.
units.tr: So far we have spoken of the words that have number, namely the noun and the verb. There follow the words without number, namely the adverb and the conjunction.

units.la: DE ADVERBIO.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ADVERB.

units.la: Quid est Adverbium.
units.tr: What an adverb is.

units.la: ADverbium est vox sine numero, quæ alicui voci adjuncta, circunstantiam ejus una voce effert, ut פּה po, vel פּא po, & בָּזֶה bazé, hîc שָׁם scham, ibi, illic, istic. הֵנָּה henna, & שָׁמָּה schámma, illuc, istuc. מָחָר machar & מָחֳרָת machoráth, cras. בֹּקֶר bóker, mane עֶרֶב ereb, vesperi, לֹא lo, vel אֵין en, אַיִן Ajin, בַּל bal, בְּלִי beli, בְּלֹא belo, בִּלְתִּי bilti, id est, non, nequaquam. בֹּא kó, ita. כֵּן ken & כַּךְ kach, & בְּכֵן bechen, sic. הֵא he & הֵן hen, en. הִנֵּה himné, ecce. לוּ lu vel לוּא lu, utinâ. אַחַר achár, postea.
units.tr: An adverb is a word without number which, added to some other word, expresses its circumstance in a single word: po or pa, here; bazeh, here; sham, there, yonder; henna, hither; shamma, thither; machar and machorath, tomorrow; boker, in the morning; ereb, in the evening; lo, or en, ajin, bal, beli, belo, bilti, that is, not, by no means; ko, so; ken and kach, and bechen, thus; he and hen, lo; himne, behold; lu or lu', would that; achar, afterwards.

units.la: לָמָּה lámma, quare? הֲלֹא halò, nonne?
units.tr: lamma, why? halo, is it not?

units.la: כִּדְמוּת kidmut, instar. כְּמוֹ kemò, quasi, tanquam. טוֹב tob, bene. רַע rag, male. רָב ráb וְ רַבָּה rabbá, וְ הָרְבָּה harbeh, multum. מְאֹד meód, valde עַד־וְעַד ad-veád, magis, magisq;. לְעַט leát, paulatim. אוּלַי ulái, forsan אָמֵן אָמֵן amén, amén, verissimè. אֶל el, ad. אֶצֶל ézel, apud, juxta. אֵת eth, cum. בֵּין ben, inter. בִּגְלַל bighlál, propter. בְּלֹא belò, absque. בְּעַד beád, pro, per. לְעֻמַּת leymmáth, contrà. לְבַד lebád, praeter. מוּל mul, versus, erga. מוֹל mol, adversus. מִמּוּל mimmúl, e regione. מִן min, á, ab, abs, de, ex, prae. בַּעֲבוּר baabúr, propter.
units.tr: kidmut, like; kemo, as, as if. tob, well. rag, badly. rab, rabba and harbeh, much. meod, very. ad-vead, more and more. leat, gradually. ulai, perhaps. amen amen, truly, most truly. el, to. ezel, with, near, beside. eth, with. ben, between. bighlal, on account of. belo, without. bead, for, through. leymmath, against. lebad, besides. mul, toward, with regard to. mol, against. mimmul, opposite. min, from, by, away from, out of, of, before.

units.la: הָלְאָה haleá, ultra. זוּלַת zulàth, praeter. חֶלֶף chéleph, pro, vice. חוּץ chuz, extra. מֵעִם meim, cum, de, inter. מֵעַל meál, desuper. נֶגֶד néghed, coram. נֹכַח nóchach, contra. סָבִיב sabíb, circū. עִם im, cum. עִמָּד immád, cum. עַל al, super. עֵבֶר éber, trans. תַּחַת tachath, pro, sub, subter. עַד ad, tenus, usq; ad, usq; in. אַח ach, ah. הֵאָח heach, ah, euge. אֲבוֹי aboi, vah, papæ.
units.tr: haleah, beyond. zulath, besides. cheleph, for, in place of. chuz, outside. meim, with, from, among. meal, above. neghed, before. nochach, against. sabib, around. im, with. immad, with. al, upon. eber, across. tachath, for, under, beneath. ad, as far as, up to, into. ach, ah. heach, ah, well done. aboi, alas, oh.

units.la: DE CONIUNCTIONE.
units.tr: ON THE CONJUNCTION.

units.la: Quid est Conjunctio.
units.tr: What a conjunction is.

units.la: Conjunctio est vox sine numero, quæ superiori sententiæ aut parti subinde aliam annectit, ut, ו ve, גַם gam, אַף aph, id est, etiam, &. אִם im, si. אַף עַל־פִּי aph alpi, quamvis. אַךְ ach, tamen. או o, aut, vel, sive. בִּי hi, quia, quoniam. עַל־כֵּן al ken, igitur, לָכֵן lachén, propterea.
units.tr: A conjunction is an indeclinable word which from time to time joins another thing to the preceding sentence or part of a sentence, as ve [ו], "and"; gam [גַם], "also"; aph [אַף], that is, "even" or "also"; im [אִם], "if"; aph alpi [אַף עַל־פִּי], "although"; ach [אַךְ], "yet" or "nevertheless"; o [או], "or", "either", "or else"; hi [בִּי], "because", "since"; al ken [עַל־כֵּן], "therefore"; lachén [לָכֵן], "for this reason".

units.la: DE SYNTAXI.
units.tr: ON SYNTAX.

units.la: Quid est Syntaxis?
units.tr: What is Syntax?

units.la: Syntaxis est secunda pars Grammaticæ, in qua de vocum structura agitur.
units.tr: Syntax is the second part of Grammar, in which the construction of words is treated.

units.la: Quæ est prima Regula de vocibus construendis?
units.tr: What is the first rule on the construction of words?

units.la: Substantivum regit substantivum nomen, quod per Genitiuum explicatur, ut <bl>דבר יהוה</bl> debar Iehová, verbum Domini.
units.tr: A substantive governs a substantive noun, which is explained by the genitive, as debar Iehová, "the word of the Lord" [דבר יהוה].

units.la: Cùm substantiuum, quod regitur, præcedit, substantiuo regenti affixum additur, ut <bl>יהוה כסאו</bl> <bl>בשמים</bl> Iehová kisseó baschschamájim, Domini sedes in cœlis, pro <bl>כסא יהוה בשמים</bl> kisse Iehová basch& shy;schamájim, sedes Dñi in cœlis, Psal. 10.
units.tr: When the governed substantive comes first, the suffix is attached to the governing substantive, as Iehová kisseó baschschamájim, "the Lord's throne is in the heavens" [יהוה כסאו בשמים], for kisse Iehová baschschamájim, "the throne of the Lord in the heavens" [כסא יהוה בשמים], Ps. 10.

units.la: Substantiuum materiæ, quod regitur, explicatur per Denominatiuum, quo He& shy;bræi carent, <bl>נר זהב</bl> ner zahab, candela& shy;brum auri, id est, candelabrum aureum, <bl>לב בשר</bl> leb basár, cor carnis, id est, cor carneum.
units.tr: A governed substantive of material is explained by a denominative, which the Hebrews lack: ner zahab, "a lampstand of gold" [נר זהב], that is, a golden lampstand; leb basár, "heart of flesh" [לב בשר], that is, a fleshly heart.

units.la: Substantivum regit etiam Infinitum, ut <bl>עת רקוד</bl> eth rekód, tempus saltare, id est, saltandi.
units.tr: A substantive also governs an infinitive, as eth rekód, "a time to dance" [עת רקוד], that is, a time of dancing.

units.la: Quæ est secunda Regula?
units.tr: What is the second rule?

units.la: Adje�even tivum & Substantivum eodem numero, genere, & casu cohærent, sed i& shy;ta, ut in contextu Adjeẽtivum sequatur, ut איש טוב ifch tób, vir bonus : si autem substantivum sequitur, subintelligenda est copula, ut יהוה רחום rachum Iehova, misericors (scilicet est) Dominus.
units.tr: An adjective and a substantive agree in number, gender and case, but the adjective normally follows, as ifch tób, "a good man" [איש טוב]. If the substantive comes first, the copula is to be understood, as rachum Iehova, "the Lord (is) merciful" [יהוה רחום].

units.la: Excipiuntur numeralia cardinalia, quæ post unum ad decem usque adduntur pluralibus, & præponuntur substantivis, ut שבע שנים scebag schanim, septem anni: post decem vero usq; ad centum junguntur cum singularibus, ut שלושים שנה chelofchim schaná, triginta anni.
units.tr: Cardinal numerals are excepted: from one up to ten they are added to plural nouns and placed before substantives, as scebag schanim, "seven years" [שבע שנים]; but from ten up to a hundred they are joined with singulars, as chelofchim schaná, "thirty years" [שלושים שנה].

units.la: Quæ est tertia Regula?
units.tr: What is the third rule?

units.la: Adjectivum significans copiam, desiderium, notitiam, memoriam, metum, aut contrá, regit Substantivum nomen, quod per Genitivum vel Ablativum explicatur, ut, שבע ימים sebagjamím. fatur dierum. חסר לב chasar leb, deficiens corde.
units.tr: An adjective signifying abundance, desire, knowledge, memory or fear, or their opposites, governs a substantive noun, which is explained by the genitive or ablative, as sebagjamím, "full of days" [שבע ימים]; chasar leb, "lacking in heart" [חסר לב].

units.la: Quæ est quarta Regula?
units.tr: What is the fourth rule?

units.la: Adjectivum, quod regit nomen plurale vel collectivum singulare, accipitur superlative, ut, קטן בניו keton banau, parvus filiorum ejus, hoc est, minimus. גדולם gedolám, magnus eorū, hoc est, maximus.
units.tr: An adjective which governs a plural noun, or a singular collective noun, is taken superlatively, as keton banau, "small of his sons" [קטן בניו], that is, the youngest; gedolám, "great of them" [גדולם], that is, the greatest.

units.la: Quae est quinta Regula?
units.tr: What is the fifth rule?

units.la: Nominativus praecedit verbum finitum, similinumero, genere, & persona, ut, למה רגשו גוים lamma ragefchú gojim, quare fremuerunt gentes? Excipiuntur quæ per Synthesin dicuntur.
units.tr: The nominative precedes a finite verb, agreeing with it in number, gender and person, as lamma ragefchú gojim, "why did the nations rage?" [למה רגשו גוים]. The exceptions are those said by synthesis.

units.la: Quae est sexta Regula?
units.tr: What is the sixth rule?

units.la: Verbum activum regit post se nomen cum particula את vel sine illa, ut, אהב את ehabeth Iehová, dilige Dominum. יהוה ירא יהוה jera Iehová, time Dominum.
units.tr: An active verb governs after it a noun, with or without the particle את, as ehabeth Iehová, "love the Lord" [אהב את יהוה]; jera Iehová, "fear the Lord" [ירא יהוה].

units.la: Particula את eth interdum cum Nominativo Emphaseos gratia jungitur.
units.tr: The particle את eth is sometimes joined to the nominative for the sake of emphasis.

units.la: Quae est septima Regula?
units.tr: What is the seventh rule?

units.la: Verbum substantivum inter duo nomina plerunq; dissimulatur, ut צדיק אתה zaddík attá Iehová, justus (scilicet es) tu Domine.
units.tr: The substantive verb is usually omitted between two nouns, as zaddík attá Iehová, "you (are) just, O Lord" [צדיק אתה יהוה].

units.la: Quæ est octava Regula?
units.tr: What is the eighth rule?

units.la: Sine Adverbio, nomen caussæ, instrumenti, vel similis circunstantiæ, nomini aut verbo frequenter apponitur, ut, שִׂמְחִי ṙʻ רַעְתִּי semeche raathi, læti malo meo. חֲלָלִי chalele chereb, vulnerati gladio.
units.tr: Without an adverb, a noun denoting cause, instrument or a similar circumstance is often added to a noun or verb, as semeche raathi, "glad at my evil" [שִׂמְחִי רַעְתִּי]; chalele chereb, "wounded by the sword" [חֲלָלֵי חֶרֶב].

units.la: Quomodo notatur soph pasuk, id est, finis versus seu periodi?
units.tr: How is soph pasuk, that is, the end of a verse or period, marked?

units.la: Signatur virgula Metheg sub ultima periodi voce posita, sequentibus duobus punctis intra lineam subalternatim collocatis, ut : יֵשֵׁב jaschab, sedit.
units.tr: It is marked by the sign Metheg placed under the last word of the period, with two points set alternately within the line after it, as jaschab, "he sat" [יֵשֵׁב].

units.la: Quomodo notatur Athnach, id est, Colon?
units.tr: How is Athnach, that is, the colon, marked?

units.la: Hoc signo ˆ sub litera posito, ut עָמַד amád, stetit.
units.tr: By this sign placed under a letter, as amád, "he stood" [עָמַד].

units.la: Quomodo notatur Revia, id est, Comma?
units.tr: How is Revia, that is, the comma, marked?

units.la: Puncto supra mediam literam posito, הָאִישׁ häisch, ille vir. Differt à puncto vo-r cali Holem, quód illud supra sinistrum latus literæ signetur: ut [illegible, ~1 letter] ho,re via vero supra mediam literam, ut [illegible, ~1 letter] ha.
units.tr: By a point placed above the middle letter, as häisch, "that man" [הָאִישׁ]. It differs from the vowel point Holem, which is marked above the left side of the letter; Revia is placed above the middle letter.

units.la: Lecturi praecepta prolixiora, videant Hebraicam Grammaticam Michaelis Neandri, Valentini Schindeleri, vel aliorum.
units.tr: Those who want fuller rules should consult the Hebrew grammars of Michael Neander, Valentin Schindeler, or others.

units.la: Hactenus artes purè Germanicè, Latinè, Græcè & Hebraicè loquendi, expositæ fuerunt: Agemus jam de Arte ornatè Germanicè, Latinè, Græcè vel Hebraicè dicendi, videlicet de Rhetorica.
units.tr: So far we have set out the arts of speaking purely in German, Latin, Greek and Hebrew. We shall now deal with the art of speaking ornately in German, Latin, Greek or Hebrew, namely Rhetoric.

units.la: DE RHETORICA.
units.tr: DE RHETORICA.

units.la: Quid est Rhetorica ?
units.tr: What is Rhetoric?

units.la: RHETORICA est ars ornatè dicendi: cujus partes duæ sunt: Elocutio & pronuntiatio. <bl>Die redekunst ist eine kunst</bl> <bl>zierlich zu rede: welcher zwey theile sein/</bl> <bl>die Rede zierung und die Rede außsagung.</bl>
units.tr: RHETORIC is the art of speaking ornately. It has two parts: elocution and delivery. The rhetoric art is an art of speaking gracefully, which has two parts: the adornment of speech and the utterance of speech.

units.la: Quid est Elocutio?
units.tr: What is Elocution?

units.la: Elocutio est prima pars Rhetoricæ, in qua oratio exornatur. Ejus partes duæ sunt: Tropus & Figura. <bl>Die rede zierung ist der erste theil der redekunst / in</bl> <bl>welchem die rede herrlich außgebutzet wird. Der theile</bl> <bl>sind zween: die verblümung und zierliche gestalt.</bl>
units.tr: Elocution is the first part of rhetoric, in which speech is adorned. It has two parts: trope and figure. The adornment of speech is the first part of rhetoric, in which speech is splendidly decked out. Its parts are two: the figurative turn of phrase and the graceful form.

units.la: Quid est Tropus?
units.tr: What is a Trope?

units.la: Tropus est elocutio, qua vox à propria significatione in aliâ concinnè immutatur. <bl>Die verblümung</bl> <bl>ist eine rede zierung/ damit eine stim von der eigent-</bl> <bl>lichen bedeutung in eine andere zierlich verändert</bl> <bl>wird.</bl> Sunt autem Tropi quatuor: Metonymia, Ironia, Metaphora, Synecdoche.
units.tr: A trope is an elocution by which a word is gracefully changed from its proper meaning into another. The figurative turn of phrase is an adornment of speech, whereby a word is gracefully changed from its proper meaning into another. There are four tropes: metonymy, irony, metaphor, and synecdoche.

units.la: Metonymia est sextuplex: causæ principalis, caufsæ instrumentalis, causæ materialis, effecti, subjecti, adjuncti.
units.tr: Metonymy is of six kinds: of principal cause, of instrumental cause, of material cause, of effect, of subject, and of adjunct.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia causæ principalis?
units.tr: What is metonymy of principal cause?

units.la: Metonymia causæ principalis, <bl>die Namm</bl> <bl>verblümung der vornemen ursach</bl> / est cùm author & scriptor usurpantur, & effectæ res, seu scripta opera intelliguntur: ut, Et ait illi (diviti) Abraham, habent Moysen & Prophetas: audiant illos. Luc.16. Id est, habent scripta Moysis ac Prophetarum.
units.tr: Metonymy of principal cause, the figurative naming of the chief cause, is when the author and writer are put for the things they have produced, that is, for their written works. For example: "And Abraham said to him (the rich man), they have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them." Luke 16. That is, they have the writings of Moses and the Prophets.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia causæ instru-mentalis?
units.tr: What is metonymy of instrumental cause?

units.la: <bl>Metonymia causæ instrumentalis, die Namm ver-</bl> <bl>blümung</bl> <bl>der werckzeugigen vrsach</bl> / est cum instrumentum usurpatur, & caussa principalis intelligitur: ut, Quod si noluèritis, & me ad iracundiam provocaveritis: gladius devorabit vos, quia os Domini locutum est. Esaiæ 1.[?] Id est, Hostis, caussa principalis gladio tanquam instrumento interficiet vos. Interdum instrumentum usurpatur, & effectum intelligitur: ut, lingua, pro sermone. Manus pro scriptura.
units.tr: Metonymy of instrumental cause, the figurative naming of the instrumental cause, is when the instrument is put and the principal cause is understood. For example: "But if you will not, and provoke me to anger, the sword shall devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." Isaiah 1. That is, the enemy, the principal cause, will kill you with the sword as its instrument. Sometimes the instrument is put and the effect is understood: for example, "tongue" for speech, "hand" for writing.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia caussæ materialis?
units.tr: What is metonymy of material cause?

units.la: Metonymia caussæ materialis, <bl>die Namm verblü-</bl> <bl>mung der materialischen vrsach</bl> / est cum materia usurpatur, & res, quæ ex materia fieri solet, intelligitur: ut, Et ecce mulier quæ erat in civitate, peccatrix, ut cognovit quòd Jesus accubuisset in domo Pharisæi, attulit alabastrum unguéti, Lucæ 7. Alabastrum, id est, vasculum ex alabastro factum. Acervus æris & auri non deducit febres. Horat. Id est, acervus nummorum æneorum & aureorum.
units.tr: Metonymy of material cause, the figurative naming of the material cause, is when the material is put and the thing usually made from that material is understood. For example: "And behold, a woman in the city, a sinner, when she knew that Jesus was reclining in the house of the Pharisee, brought an alabaster box of ointment." Luke 7. "Alabaster" means a little vessel made of alabaster. "A heap of bronze and gold does not drive away fevers." Horace. That is, a heap of bronze and gold coins.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia effectis?
units.tr: What is metonymy of effect?

units.la: Metonymia effecti, <bl>die Namm verblümung des</bl> <bl>werckes</bl> / est cum effectum usurpatur, & efficiens intelligitur: ut, Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue: si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude. Præmium enim bonum tibi thefaurizas in die necessitatis, quoniâ eleemosyna ab omni peccato, & à morte liberat, & non patietur animam ire in tenebras, Tob.3. Peccata tua eleemosynis redime, Daniel.4. Eleemosyna, <bl>die almusen/id</bl> est, vera fides Christum apprehendens, (unde promanat Deo placens Eleemosyna) ab omni peccato, & à morte liberat: Effectum ponitur, & efficiens intelligitur, nempe meritum Christi vera fide apprehensum. Sed Jesuvitæ ogganniunt, nos non admittimus Glossam vestram, quia scriptura proprie, quemadmodum verba sonant, intelligenda est. Hoc verum est, Jesuvitæ, nisi alia scriptura vel ratio inexpugnabilis evidenter convincat, tropum esse admittendum. Nunc autem alia scriptura clare ac perspicue ostendit, in dicto Tobiæ & Danielis tropū esse: Quia Christus inquit Lucæ 17. Nunquid gratiam habet servo illi, quia fecit quæ ei imperaverat? Non puto. Sic & vos cum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite, servi inutiles sumus, quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Ergo cum ex mandato Christi omnes pij nihil suis operibus tribuere debeat, sequitur necessario Tobiæ & Danielis dictum tropice esse intelligendum.
units.tr: Metonymy of effect, the figurative naming of the effect, is when the effect is put and the efficient cause is understood. For example: "If you have much, give generously; if you have little, take care to share even little willingly. For you will store up for yourself a good reward in the day of necessity, since almsgiving frees from every sin and from death, and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness." Tobit 4. "Redeem your sins with alms." Daniel 4. Here "almsgiving," that is, true faith laying hold of Christ (from which almsgiving pleasing to God springs), frees from every sin and from death. The effect is put and the efficient cause is understood, namely the merit of Christ grasped by true faith. But the Jesuits cry out that we do not admit your gloss, because Scripture must be understood properly, as the words sound. This is true, Jesuits, unless another passage of Scripture or an unassailable reason clearly convinces us that a trope must be admitted. Now, however, another passage of Scripture clearly and plainly shows that there is a trope in the saying of Tobit and of Daniel. For Christ says in Luke 17: "Does he thank that servant because he did what he was commanded? I think not. So you also, when you have done all that is commanded you, say: we are unprofitable servants; we have done what we ought to have done." Therefore, since by the command of Christ all the godly must ascribe nothing to their works, it necessarily follows that the saying of Tobit and of Daniel is to be understood tropically.

units.la: Est & alia Metonymia effecti Poetica magis quam Oratoria (vulgo Metalepsis) cum nomen effecti attribuitur causæ efficienti: ut, pallida mors æquo pulsat pede pauperum tabernas, Regumq; turres, Horat. Mors, est causa efficiens, reddit pallidum, est effectū, cujus effecti nomen attribuitur ipsi causæ, & appellatur pallida mors ab Horatio, non quod sit pallida, sed quod hominem mortuum pallidum reddat.
units.tr: There is also another metonymy of effect, more poetic than oratorical (commonly called metalepsis), when the name of the effect is given to the efficient cause. For example: "Pale death strikes with equal foot the huts of the poor and the towers of kings." Horace. Death is the efficient cause; it makes men pale, which is the effect. The name of the effect is given to the cause itself, and Horace calls death "pale," not because it is itself pale, but because it makes the dead man pale.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia subje- cti?
units.tr: What is metonymy of subject?

units.la: <bl>Die Namm verblümung des</bl> <bl>unterworffenen /</bl> est cum res subjecta usurpatur, & res adjuncta intelligitur: ut, Jerusalem, Jerusalē. quæ occidis prophetas, & lapidas eos qui ad te missi sunt, Matth. 23. Id est, vos homines in Jerusalem, qui occiditis prophetas. Invadunt urbem somno vinoq; sepultam, Virgil. Id est, invadunt Trojanos dormientes & ebrios. Sic scholæ Rami, id est, disputationes in scholis. Imperator cecidit aliquot millia Turcarum. Hic Imperator tanquam subjectum ponitur, & intelligitur Adjuncti, nempe imperatoris exercitus.
units.tr: The figurative naming of the subject is when the subject is put and the adjunct is understood. For example: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you." Matthew 23. That is, you people in Jerusalem who kill the prophets. "They attack the city buried in sleep and wine." Virgil. That is, they attack the Trojans sleeping and drunk. So "the schools of Ramus," that is, the disputations in the schools. "The emperor cut down some thousands of Turks." Here "emperor" is put as the subject, and the adjunct is understood, namely the emperor's army.

units.la: Quid est Metonymia adjuncti?
units.tr: What is metonymy of the adjunct?
