units.la: Cujus Propositio est negata generalis, & Assumptio ac Conclusio sunt speciales: ut, Christus non est spiritus. Argumentum tertium: quia ex carne & ossibus constat.
units.tr: Its major premise is a general negative, and its minor premise and conclusion are particular, for example: Christ is not a spirit. Middle term: because he consists of flesh and bones.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est: Spiritus ex carne & ossibus non constat. At Christus ex carne & ossibus constat. Lucæ 24. Ergo Christus non est Spiritus.
units.tr: The syllogism is this: A spirit does not consist of flesh and bones. But Christ consists of flesh and bones. Luke 24. Therefore Christ is not a spirit.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in Baroco quar- to modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the fourth mood of Baroco?

units.la: Cujus propositio est affirmata generalis, & assumptio ac conclusio sunt speciales: ut, Hi Pharisæi non sunt ex Deo. Argumentū tertium: quia non audiunt verbum Dei.
units.tr: Its major premise is a general affirmative, and its minor premise and conclusion are particular, for example: These Pharisees are not of God. Middle term: because they do not hear the Word of God.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est: Qui ex Deo sunt, audiunt verbum Dei. At hi Pharisæi non audiunt verbum Dei. Ergo hi Pharisæi non sunt ex Deo.
units.tr: The syllogism is this: Those who are of God hear the Word of God. But these Pharisees do not hear the Word of God. Therefore these Pharisees are not of God.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in quinto modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the fifth mood?

units.la: Cujus propositio est negata, & omnes partes sunt propriæ: ut, Johannes non est Christus. Argumentum tertium: quia Johannes est vox clamantis in deserto.
units.tr: Its major premise is negative and all its terms are proper, for example: John is not Christ. Middle term: because John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est: Christus non est vox clamantis in deserto. At Johannes est vox clamantis in deserto. Ergo Johannes non est Christus.
units.tr: The syllogism is this: Christ is not the voice of one crying in the wilderness. But John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness. Therefore John is not Christ.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in sexto modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the sixth mood?

units.la: Cujus propositio est affirmata, & omnes partes sunt propriæ: ut, Moyses non est Christus. Argumentum tertium: quia non vocatus est ad annuntiandum Euangelium.
units.tr: Its major premise is affirmative and all its terms are proper, for example: Moses is not Christ. Middle term: because he was not called to proclaim the Gospel.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Christus vocatus est ad annuntiandum Euangelium,
units.tr: Christ was called to proclaim the Gospel;

units.la: Moyses non vocatus est ad annuntiandum Euangelium.
units.tr: Moses was not called to proclaim the Gospel.

units.la: Ergo Moyses non est Christus.
units.tr: Therefore Moses is not Christ.

units.la: Quid est tertia Figura?
units.tr: What is the third figure?

units.la: EST, quando argumentum tertium in propositione consequentem partem quaestionis antecedit, in Assumptione antecedentem partem affirmatè sequitur. Tertia figura (quae Melanchthoni est prima[?]) habet etiam sex modos.
units.tr: It is the figure in which the middle term in the major premise precedes the consequent part of the question, and in the minor premise affirmatively follows the antecedent part. The third figure (which is the first according to Melanchthon[?]) also has six moods.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in Barbara pri- mo modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the first mood of Barbara?

units.la: Cujus omnes partes sunt affirmatae generales: ut, Fideles sunt beati. Argumentum tertium: quia persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam.
units.tr: All its terms are general affirmatives, for example: The faithful are blessed. Middle term: because they suffer persecution for righteousness.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, sunt beati,Matth.5.
units.tr: Those who suffer persecution for righteousness are blessed, Matt. 5.

units.la: At fideles persecutione patiuntur propter justitiā[?].
units.tr: But the faithful suffer persecution for righteousness[?].

units.la: Ergo fideles sunt beati.
units.tr: Therefore the faithful are blessed.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in Celarent se- cundo modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the second mood of Celarent?

units.la: Cujus Assumptio est tantum affirmata, & omnes partes sunt generales: ut, Verbi Dei contemptores non erunt salvi. Argumentum tertium: quia à Deo damnantur.
units.tr: Its minor premise is only affirmative and all its terms are general, for example: Despisers of the Word of God will not be saved. Middle term: because they are damned by God.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Qui à Deo damnantur,non erunt salvi.
units.tr: Those who are damned by God will not be saved.

units.la: At verbi Dei contemptores à Deo damnantur.
units.tr: But despisers of the Word of God are damned by God.

units.la: Ergo verbi Dei contemptores non erunt salvi.
units.tr: Therefore despisers of the Word of God will not be saved.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in Darij ter- tio modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the third mood of Darii?

units.la: Cujus omnes partes sunt affirmatæ. Assumptio & Conclusio tantum speciales: ut, Christi est justificationis nostræ laus propria. Argumentum tertium: quia solus auctor est.
units.tr: All its terms are affirmative, with only the minor premise and the conclusion particular, for example: The praise proper to Christ is the praise of our justification. Middle term: because he alone is its author.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Qui solus auctor est justificationis nostræ, cujus est laus propria.
units.tr: He who alone is the author of our justification, to whom the proper praise belongs.

units.la: At Christus justificationis nostræ solus auctor est.
units.tr: But Christ alone is the author of our justification.

units.la: ErgoChristi est justificationis nostræ laus propria.
units.tr: Therefore the proper praise of our justification belongs to Christ.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in Ferio quar- to modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the fourth mood of Ferio?

units.la: Cujus propositio est negata generalis, Assumptio & Conclusio sunt speciales: ut, Christus non est Davidis filius. Argumentum tertium: quia est Davidis Dominus.
units.tr: Its major premise is a general negative, and its minor premise and conclusion are particular, for example: Christ is not the son of David. Middle term: because he is the Lord of David.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Qui est alicujus Dominus, ejusdem non potest esse filius.
units.tr: He who is the lord of someone cannot be that person's son.

units.la: At Christus est Davidis Dominus.
units.tr: But Christ is the Lord of David.

units.la: Ergo Christus non est Davidis filius, quod ad Divinitatem attinet.
units.tr: Therefore Christ is not the son of David, as far as his divinity is concerned.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in quinto modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the fifth mood?

units.la: Cujus omnes partes sunt affirmatæ propriæ: ut, Christus est patris unigenitus filius. Argumentum tertium: quia est secunda persona Divinitatis.
units.tr: All its terms are affirmative and proper, for example: Christ is the only-begotten Son of the Father. Middle term: because he is the second person of the Godhead.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: This is the syllogism:

units.la: Secunda persona Divinitatis est patris unigenitus filius.
units.tr: The second person of the Godhead is the only-begotten Son of the Father.

units.la: At Christus est secunda persona Divinitatis.
units.tr: But Christ is the second person of the Godhead.

units.la: Ergo Christus est patris unigenitus filius.
units.tr: Therefore Christ is the only-begotten Son of the Father.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus in sexto modo?
units.tr: What is the syllogism in the sixth mode?

units.la: Cujus Assumptio est tantum affirmata, & omnes partes propriæ: ut, David non fuit Messias. Argumentum tertium: quia fuit pater Salomonis.
units.tr: Its assumption is affirmative only, and all its parts are proper: for example, David was not the Messiah. The third argument: because he was the father of Solomon.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: This is the syllogism:

units.la: Pater Salomonis non fuit Messias. At David fuit pater Salomonis. Ergo David non fuit Messias.
units.tr: The father of Solomon was not the Messiah. But David was the father of Solomon. Therefore David was not the Messiah.

units.la: Observatio.
units.tr: Observation.

units.la: Vulgò quidem dicitur: Ex negativis nihil concluditur; sed si Antecedens vel etiam Consequens propositionis habeat particulam, Non, concluditur semper necessariò: ut, Qui non crediderit in filium Dei, damnabitur. Atqui Turca non credit in filium Dei, Ergo Turca certissimè damnabitur. Qui non laborat, non manducet. Atqui Titius non laborat. Ergo Titius non manducet.
units.tr: It is commonly said that nothing follows from negatives. But if the antecedent or the consequent of a proposition contains the particle "not," the conclusion always follows necessarily. For example: He who does not believe in the Son of God will be damned. But the Turk does not believe in the Son of God. Therefore the Turk will most certainly be damned. He who does not work shall not eat. But Titius does not work. Therefore Titius shall not eat.

units.la: Qui hosce Syllogismos & similes ad modos tertiæ figuræ referre volunt, dicunt, per Antecedens Propositionis & Assumptionis quod habet particulam, Non, intelligendum esse affirmatum quiddam: ut, Qui non crediderit, id est, qui infidelis est. Qui non laborat, id est, qui fugit laborem.
units.tr: Those who wish to refer these syllogisms and similar ones to the modes of the third figure say that the antecedent of the proposition and of the assumption, which contains the particle "not," must be understood as something affirmative. For example, "he who does not believe" means "he who is unbelieving," and "he who does not work" means "he who shuns work."

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus Conditionalis seu Hypotheticus?
units.tr: What is the conditional or hypothetical syllogism?

units.la: SYllogismus Conditionalis est, cujus propositio est Enunciatum Conditionale: Estque duorum modorum.
units.tr: A conditional syllogism is one whose proposition is a conditional statement. It is of two modes.

units.la: Quis est primus modus?
units.tr: What is the first mode?

units.la: Qui assumit Antecedens, & Consequens concludit, Discipulis Christi esurientibus licuit vellere spicas die Sabbathi. Argumentum tertium: quia Davidi esurienti licuit vesci panibus sanctis.
units.tr: The mode that assumes the antecedent and concludes the consequent: The disciples of Christ, being hungry, were allowed to pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath day. The third argument: because David, being hungry, was allowed to eat the holy bread.

units.la: Syllogismus conditionalis hic est:
units.tr: The conditional syllogism is this:

units.la: Si Davidi esurienti licuit vesci panibus sanctis: etiam discipulis Christi esurientibus licuit vellere spicas die Sabbathi Matth.12.
units.tr: If David, being hungry, was allowed to eat the holy bread, then the disciples of Christ, being hungry, were also allowed to pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath day. Matth. 12.

units.la: At Davidi esurienti licuit vesci panibus sanctis. 1.Reg.21.
units.tr: But David, being hungry, was allowed to eat the holy bread. 1 Sam. 21.

units.la: Ergo etiam discipulis Christi esurientibus licuit vellere spicas die Sabbathi.
units.tr: Therefore the disciples of Christ, being hungry, were also allowed to pluck ears of corn on the Sabbath day.

units.la: Assumptionis & Conclusionis apud Authores quaedam compendia sunt: At illud, hoc igitur: At primum verum, secundum vel postremum igitur: Ante-cedens verum, verum igitur & Consequens.
units.tr: Among authors there are certain shorthand forms for the assumption and the conclusion. "But that" (at illud) or "this, therefore" (hoc igitur) stands for the assumption; "the first is true," "the second or last, therefore" (primum verum, secundum vel postremum igitur) stands for the conclusion; "the antecedent is true, therefore the consequent is true" (antecedens verum, verum igitur & consequens) stands for the whole.

units.la: Interdum hoc modo argumentamur:
units.tr: Sometimes we argue in this way:

units.la: Si Petrus non egisset poenitentiam: fuisset damna-
units.tr: If Peter had not repented, he would have been damn-

units.la: At Petrus egit poenitentiam.
units.tr: But Peter repented.

units.la: Ergo Petrus non est damnatus.
units.tr: Therefore Peter was not damned.

units.la: Interdum non assumitur idem, sed majus: ut,
units.tr: Sometimes the assumption is not the same as the premise but a greater one, for example:

units.la: Si te pius homo admoneret: pareres.
units.tr: If a pious man were to admonish you, you would obey.

units.la: At Deus ipse & verbo suo, & cruce te monet.
units.tr: But God himself admonishes you both by his word and by the cross.

units.la: Ergo multo magis parebis.
units.tr: Therefore you will obey all the more.

units.la: Quid est secundus modus?
units.tr: What is the second mode?

units.la: Qui tollit Consequens, ut tollat Antecedens. Per legem non est justitia. Argumentum tertium: Quia Christus non est gratis mortuus.
units.tr: The mode that removes the consequent in order to remove the antecedent: Through the law there is no justification. The third argument: because Christ did not die in vain.

units.la: Syllogismus hic est:
units.tr: The syllogism is this:

units.la: Si per legem est justitia: Christus gratis mortuus est Gal.2. Atqui Christus non est gratis mortuus.
units.tr: If through the law there is justification, then Christ died in vain. Gal. 2. But Christ did not die in vain.

units.la: Ergo per legem non est justitia.
units.tr: Therefore through the law there is no justification.

units.la: Compendia Assumptionis & Conclusionis sunt: Non autem hoc, nec illud igitur: Secundum falsum, primum igitur: Consequens falsum, Antecedens igitur.
units.tr: The shorthand forms of the assumption and the conclusion are: "But not this, nor that, therefore" (non autem hoc, nec illud igitur) stands for the removal; "the second is false, therefore the first" (secundum falsum, primum igitur) stands for the conclusion; "the consequent is false, therefore the antecedent" (consequens falsum, antecedens igitur) stands for the whole.

units.la: Interdum hoc modo argumentamur:
units.tr: Sometimes we argue in this way:

units.la: Si Pharao obtemperasset Moysi: non periisset,
units.tr: If Pharaoh had obeyed Moses, he would not have perished.

units.la: At Pharao periit.
units.tr: But Pharaoh perished.

units.la: Ergo non obtemperavit Moysi.
units.tr: Therefore he did not obey Moses.

units.la: Hactenus Syllogismus simplex & conditionalis suerunt explicati: sequitur Syllogismus adversus.
units.tr: So far the simple and the conditional syllogisms have been explained. There follows the adversative syllogism.

units.la: Quid est Syllogismus Adversus?
units.tr: What is the adversative syllogism?

units.la: SYllogismus Adversus est, cujus propositio est Enunciatum Adversum. Estq; duorum modorum.
units.tr: An adversative syllogism is one whose proposition is an adversative statement. It is of two modes.

units.la: Quis est primus modus?
units.tr: What is the first mode?

units.la: Qui [?]è propositione, partibus omnibus affirmata, assumit unum,& reliquum tollit.
units.tr: The mode which, from a proposition with all its parts affirmed, takes one part and removes the other.

units.la: Qui in Domino moriuntur non sunt damnati. Argumentum tertium: quia sunt beati.
units.tr: Those who die in the Lord are not damned. The third argument: because they are blessed.

units.la: Aut beati sunt, aut damnati, qui in Domino moriuntur. At sunt beati, Apocal. 14.
units.tr: Either those who die in the Lord are blessed or they are damned. But they are blessed. Apoc. 14.

units.la: Ergo non damnati.
units.tr: Therefore they are not damned.

units.la: Quid est secundus modus?
units.tr: What is the second mode?

units.la: Qui tollit unum, & reliquum concludit. Propter filium Dei recipimur in gratiam sola fide. Argumentum tertium: quia propter legem non recipimur.
units.tr: The mode that removes one part and concludes the other: We are received into grace by faith alone, on account of the Son of God. The third argument: because we are not received on account of the law.

units.la: Aut propter legem, aut propter Filium Dei mediatorem sola fide a Deo recipimur in gratiam.
units.tr: Either on account of the law or on account of the Son of God, the mediator, we are received into grace by God through faith alone.

units.la: At non propter legem. Scriptum est enim: Maledictus omnis qui non permanserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis, ut faciat ea, Galatas 3.
units.tr: But not on account of the law. For it is written: "Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of the law, to do them." Gal. 3.

units.la: Nunc autem nemo permanet in omnibus, quę scripta sunt in libro legis: quia, 1. Johann. scriptum est: Si dixerimus, quoniam peccatum non habemus: ipsi nos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est.
units.tr: Now no one continues in all the things written in the book of the law. For it is written in 1 John: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us."

units.la: Omnes igitur per legem sunt maledicti.
units.tr: Therefore all are cursed by the law.

units.la: Ergo hinc necessario consequitur, nos fideles sola fide, non propter ulla legis opera, sed propter filium Dei in gratiam recipi.
units.tr: Hence it necessarily follows that we, the faithful, are received into grace by faith alone, not on account of any works of the law, but on account of the Son of God.

units.la: Quid est Dilemma?
units.tr: What is a dilemma?

units.la: <bl>Dilemma, ein zwenschneidige schlußrede /</bl> est Syllogismus cornutus Adversarium veluti cornibus utrinque feriens: ut, Si homines legi Divinae satisfaciunt, aut electi illi satisfaciunt, aut reprobi. At neque electi implent legem Dei: quia sola fide propter Christum conservantur, juxta dictum: Quoniam autem in lege nemo justificatur apud Deum, manifestum est: quia justus ex fide vivet. Galatas 3. Neque reprobi legi satisfaciunt: quia damnantur. Ergo nulli homines implent legem Dei. Vide Guilielmum Rodingum in Dialecticam Rami.
units.tr: A dilemma, a two-edged argument, is a horned syllogism that strikes the adversary on both horns, as in: If men satisfy the divine law, then either the elect satisfy it or the reprobate do. But the elect do not fulfil God's law, since they are preserved by faith alone for Christ's sake, according to the saying: "Now that no one is justified before God by the law is evident, because the just shall live by faith." Gal. 3. Nor do the reprobate satisfy the law, since they are damned. Therefore no men fulfil the law of God. See Guilielmus Rodingus on Ramus's Dialectic.

units.la: Quare Petrus Ramus Elenchos, die betrie[?]- genden Schlußreden in arte non tradidit?
units.tr: Why did Peter Ramus not hand down the Elenchi, the deceptive conclusions, in the art?

units.la: Eò quòd ex doctrina virtutis & veritatis appareat doctrina vitij & falsitatis. Ne tamen studiosi Adolescentes, Aristotelicorum & Philippeorum disputationes legentes, prorsus fallaciarum rudes sint, earum exempla subjiciemus.
units.tr: Because from the teaching of virtue and truth there appears the teaching of vice and falsehood. Yet, so that diligent young students, reading the disputations of the Aristotelians and the Philippists, may not be wholly ignorant of fallacies, we will set out examples of them.

units.la: Cedò exemplum fallaciæ Æquivocationis.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of equivocation.

units.la: Brachium est corpus, ex carne, ossibus, sanguine, & venis compositum.
units.tr: A arm is a body composed of flesh, bones, blood and veins.

units.la: At Deus habet brachium. Ergo Deus est corporeus. Negatur consequentia: quia est fallacia Aequivocationis. In propositione Brachium proprie dicitur de brachio humano: in Assumptione Brachium significat potentiam seu robur.
units.tr: But God has an arm. Therefore God is corporeal. The inference is denied, because it is the fallacy of equivocation. In the major premise, "arm" is properly said of a human arm; in the minor premise, "arm" signifies power or strength.

units.la: Cedò exemplum fallaciæ Amphiboliæ.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of amphiboly.

units.la: Verba activa significant effectionem. Deus in Historia Pharaonis aliquoties inquit: Ego indurabò cor Pharaonis. Ergo Deus fecit impiam pertinaciam in Pharaone. Negatur Consequentia: quia error oritur ex phrasi. In lingua enim Hebræa verba activa valdè crebrò permissionem significant. Est igitur vox, indurabo, permissivè exponenda, sinam durescere, sinam Pharaonem ferri suo impetu cùm mihi contumaciter repugnet. Similis phrasis est: Ne nos inducas in tentationem, id est, ne sinas nos induci.
units.tr: Active verbs signify effecting. In the history of Pharaoh, God says several times: "I will harden the heart of Pharaoh." Therefore God produced impious obstinacy in Pharaoh. The inference is denied, because the error arises from the phrasing. In the Hebrew language, active verbs very often signify permission. The verb "I will harden" is therefore to be explained permissively: "I will let it harden, I will let Pharaoh be carried along by his own impulse, since he stubbornly resists me." A similar phrase is: "Lead us not into temptation," that is, "do not let us be led into it."

units.la: Cedò exemplum fallaciæ Compositionis & Divisionis.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of composition and division.

units.la: Johannis 17. scriptum est: Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum, & quem misisti Jesum Christum. Et in Symbolo Apostolorum dicitur: Credo in Deum patrem: Et in Jesum Christum: Et in Spiritum sanctum. Non additur: Credo in Deū Jesum Christum: Credo in Deum Spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: In John 17 it is written: "This is life eternal, that they may know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent." And in the Apostles' Creed it is said: "I believe in God the Father; and in Jesus Christ; and in the Holy Spirit." It is not added: "I believe in God Jesus Christ; I believe in God the Holy Spirit."

units.la: Ergo solus pater est unicus verus Deus, non Filius, nec Spiritus sanctus cum eo, ut Arrius docuit.
units.tr: Therefore the Father alone is the only true God, and not the Son, nor the Holy Spirit with him, as Arius taught.

units.la: Negatur consequentia: quia error oritur ex compositione & divisione. Nam membra in dicto Johannis hoc modo construenda sunt: Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te, patrem, & quem misisti Jesum Christum, esse solum verum Deum: quia Christus est in omnibus Deus laudandus in secula, ut Paulus inquit Romanos 9. In Symbolo nomen Deus, ponitur collectivè, & postea subjicitur, quis sit ille Deus, in quem credimus, nimirum Pater omnipotens, & Filius ejus unigenitus, & Spiritus S. Nam in hos tres credimus. Quapropter hi tres: Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, sunt unus verus Deus.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because the error arises from composition and division. For the members in the saying of John must be construed thus: "This is life eternal, that they may know you, the Father, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent, to be the only true God," since Christ is God to be praised for ever in all things, as Paul says in Romans 9. In the Creed the name God is placed collectively, and afterwards it is specified who that God is in whom we believe, namely the almighty Father, his only-begotten Son, and the Holy Spirit. For we believe in these three. Wherefore these three, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, are the one true God.

units.la: Cedò exemplum fallaciæ Dictionis[?]
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of the word (dictio).

units.la: Appellatio Dei, in sacris literis sæpè sumitur pro officio Divino, ut Psalm.8i. Ego dixi, Dij estis, & filij excelsi omnes. Ergo eodem modo apud Johannem intelligendum est vocabulum, Deus, de officio Divino, quod Christus gerit: Et per Consequens Dominus noster Jesus Christus non est natura Deus, sed à Patre creatus, ut Arrius blasphemavit.
units.tr: The appellation "God" in the sacred letters is often taken for the divine office, as in Psalm 82: "I have said, You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High." Therefore in the same way in John the word "God" is to be understood of the divine office, which Christ bears. And consequently our Lord Jesus Christ is not God by nature, but was created by the Father, as Arius blasphemed.

units.la: Negatur Consequentia: quia Johannes magno studio docet, Christū esse verè & natura Deum. Nam tribuit ipsi æternitatem, rerum omnium creationem, vivificationem, illuminationem, quæ omnia soli Divinæ naturæ conveniunt, inquit Reverendus Dominus Doctor Simon Pauli, in parte prima Methodorum.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because John teaches with great care that Christ is truly and by nature God. For he ascribes to him eternity, the creation of all things, quickening and illumination, all of which belong to the divine nature alone, says the Reverend Doctor Simon Pauli in the first part of the Methods.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Accentus.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of accent.

units.la: Christus dixit ad suos discipulos: Dormite jam & requiescite, Matth. 26. Ergo bene fecerunt.
units.tr: Christ said to his disciples: "Sleep on now, and take your rest," Matthew 26. Therefore they did well.

units.la: Negatur Consequentia: quia ex affirmativa pronuntiatione significatur negativa, quasi Christus diceret: Non dormite, nec requiescite. Vel ut Lucas scribit 22. Quid dormitis? surgite, orate, ne intretis in tentationem.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because a statement in the affirmative signifies a negative, as if Christ said: "Do not sleep, nor rest." Or as Luke writes in chapter 22: "Why do you sleep? Rise, pray, lest you enter into temptation."

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Accidentis.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of accident.

units.la: Lex auget peccatum, Roman. 7. fit supra modum peccans peccatum per mandatum.
units.tr: The law increases sin: Romans 7, "sin became exceedingly sinful through the commandment."

units.la: Ergo lex non est docenda in Ecclesia, ut Antinomij docent.
units.tr: Therefore the law is not to be taught in the Church, as the Antinomians teach.

units.la: Negatur Consequentia: quia est fallacia accidentis: Quod enim per legem peccatum augetur, non à lege, sed à corrupta & vitiosa hominis natura oritur.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because it is the fallacy of accident. For that sin is increased through the law arises not from the law, but from the corrupt and vicious nature of man.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ à dicto secun- dum quid ad dictum sim- pliciter.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of the argument from a saying qualified (secundum quid) to a saying unqualified (simpliciter).

units.la: Injustitia est damnata. In imperiis multa injusta fiunt. Ergo imperia sunt damnata.
units.tr: Injustice is condemned. Many unjust things are done in governments. Therefore governments are condemned.

units.la: Hæc ridicula Consequentia Anabaptistis negatur: quia ista multa injusta, quæ in imperiis fiunt, sunt damnata, non ipsa imperia Divinitus ordinata.
units.tr: This ridiculous inference is denied to the Anabaptists, because those many unjust things which are done in governments are condemned, not the governments themselves, which are ordained by God.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Secundùm non caussam ut caussam.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of taking a non-cause as a cause.

units.la: Paulus jubet cavere, ne per Philosophiam decipiâmur. Ergo Philosophia est mala.
units.tr: Paul bids us beware lest we be deceived through philosophy. Therefore philosophy is evil.

units.la: Negatur Consequentia : quia Paulus sua admonitione non reddit Philosophiam malam, sed hoc vult, ne per Sophisticum usum hujusmodi rei bonæ ab aliis fallamur.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because Paul by this admonition does not make philosophy evil, but wills that we not be deceived by others through the sophistical use of such a good thing.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Consequentis.
units.tr: Give me an example of the fallacy of the consequent.

units.la: In mundo fiunt bona ac infinita mala. Ergo necesse est alium Deum bonũ esse, à quo bona existant, alium Deum malum, pariter æternum & omnipotentem, à quo res malæ oriátur, ut Manichæi locuti sunt.
units.tr: In the world there are good things and countless evils. Therefore it is necessary that there be one good God, from whom good things exist, and another evil God, equally eternal and omnipotent, from whom evil things arise, as the Manichaeans have spoken.

units.la: Respondetur, est fallacia Consequentis. Nam bonæ actiones arguunt suam caussam, nempe Deum bonum: malæ vero actiones arguunt etiam suas causas, sed Diabolum, vel corruptam humanam naturam.
units.tr: It is answered that this is the fallacy of the consequent. For good actions indicate their cause, namely the good God; but evil actions also indicate their causes, namely the Devil or corrupted human nature.

units.la: Diabolus autem & homo initio boni sunt creati, & postea in peccatum sese præcipitârunt. Ergo Diabolus & Homo, cùm sint creaturæ, non sunt mali Dij æterni & omnipotentes.
units.tr: But the Devil and man were created good at the beginning, and afterwards they hurled themselves into sin. Therefore the Devil and man, since they are creatures, are not evil gods, eternal and omnipotent.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Secundùm plu- res interrogationes.
units.tr: Here is an example of the fallacy of many questions.

units.la: Jesuvitæ inter cætera falsa objiciunt, Disciplinam doctrina Euangelij laxari : Et propterea Euangelium non esse vulgo proponendum.
units.tr: Among other false charges, the Jesuits claim that the discipline of the gospel doctrine is relaxed, and that for this reason the gospel should not be set before the common people.

units.la: Negatur Consequentia : quia non dissimulandum est, veram Dei agnitionem & invocationem tàm Laicis, quàm Pastoribus esse necessariam.
units.tr: The inference is denied, because it must not be concealed that the true knowledge and invocation of God is necessary for laymen as much as for ministers.

units.la: Cedo exemplum fallaciæ Petitionis principij.
units.tr: Here is an example of the fallacy of begging the question.

units.la: Non errant, inquiunt Jesuvitæ, qui sanctos defunctos funétos invocant : quia magna multitudo fecit id longo tempore.
units.tr: The Jesuits say that those who invoke the departed saints are not in error, because a great multitude has done so for a long time.

units.la: Negatur Jesuvitis Consequentia : quia hoc ipsum disputatur, an recte fecerit illa multitudo. Hieronymus graviter dicit : Errantium multitudo non parit errori patrocinium.
units.tr: The inference is denied to the Jesuits, because this very point is in dispute: whether that multitude has acted rightly. Jerome says gravely: "The multitude of those who err does not lend protection to error."

units.la: Quid est ignoratio Elenchi?
units.tr: What is the ignorance of the refutation?

units.la: Est velut commune domicilium aliarum captionum : ut, cœlum tegit omnia. Ergo se quoque tegit. Negatur Consequentia : quia universalis particula restringenda est, ut cœlum tegit omnia, praeterquam se.
units.tr: It is, as it were, the common home of other sophisms, as: "The sky covers all things; therefore it also covers itself." The inference is denied, because the universal particle must be restricted, so that the sky covers all things except itself.

units.la: Hactenus de Syllogismis & Fallaciis dictum est: sequitur Methodus.
units.tr: So much has been said about syllogisms and fallacies; there follows method.

units.la: Quid est Methodus?
units.tr: What is method?

units.la: Methodus, <bl>ein richtiger weg</bl>, est dispositio variorum enuntiatorum, a generalibus ad specialia progrediens. Estq; duorum modorum.
units.tr: Method, "a right way," is the arrangement of various propositions, proceeding from general things to special ones. And it is of two kinds.

units.la: Quis est primus modus?
units.tr: What is the first kind?

units.la: Qui in materia artium & doctrinarum adhibetur, & a Definitione ad Distributionem, a Distributione ad reliqua artium praecepta procedit.
units.tr: It is the kind used in the matter of the arts and disciplines, and it proceeds from definition to division, and from division to the remaining precepts of the arts.

units.la: Quis est secundus modus?
units.tr: What is the second kind?

units.la: Qui in orationibus solutis vel ligatis usurpatur: Et solet plerunque septem partes habere: Exordium, Narrationem, Propositionem seu Distributionem, Confirmationem, Confutationem, Transitionem, Perorationem.
units.tr: It is the kind used in prose or verse compositions, and it usually has seven parts: the exordium, the narration, the proposition or division, the confirmation, the confutation, the transition, and the peroration.

units.la: Quid est Exordium?
units.tr: What is the exordium?

units.la: Est initium, quo praeparamus animos audientium ad reliquam orationem. Exordium sumitur a personis, rebus, tempore, moribus, praeclaris sententiis, votis, dubitationibus vel admirationibus.
units.tr: It is the beginning, by which we prepare the minds of the hearers for the rest of the discourse. The exordium is drawn from persons, things, time, manners, striking sentiments, wishes, doubts, or expressions of wonder.

units.la: In Exordio Auditores reddimus attentos, quando significamus nos esse de magnis, novis, necessariis, utilibus, difficilibus vel obscuris rebus, adeo breviter, dilucide ac perspicue dicturos, ut omnia ab omnibus in toto coetu intelligantur.
units.tr: In the exordium we make the hearers attentive when we indicate that we are going to speak about great, new, necessary, useful, difficult or obscure matters, and that we will speak so briefly, clearly and perspicuously that everything is understood by everyone in the whole assembly.

units.la: Quid est Narratio?
units.tr: What is the narration?

units.la: Est facti expositio, quae statim exordio subjicitur. Haec saepe omittitur in orationibus.
units.tr: It is the exposition of the matter of fact, which comes immediately after the exordium. It is often omitted in discourses.

units.la: Quid est Propositio seu Distributio?
units.tr: What is the proposition or division?

units.la: Est qua Thesin, id est, generalem Quaestionem, aut Hypothesin, id est, Quaestionem specialem nos tractatum ire proponimus: aut enumeramus quot partes tractaturi simus.
units.tr: It is that by which we set forth the thesis, that is, the general question, or the hypothesis, that is, the special question, which we intend to treat; or we enumerate how many parts we are going to treat.

units.la: Quid est Confirmatio?
units.tr: What is the confirmation?

units.la: Est qua Quaestiones aut partes dubias, argumentis ex locis inventionis sumptis, probamus.
units.tr: It is that by which we prove the questions or the doubtful parts, with arguments taken from the topics of invention.

units.la: Quid est Confutatio?
units.tr: What is the confutation?

units.la: Est argumentorum, quae objiciuntur, dissolutio. Homines saepe ad decipiendum falsa comminiscuntur argumenta, quae facile falsitatis insimulari queunt, si quis attente octo Inventionis locos inspicit, utrum allatae rationes simpliciter falsae an contingentes sint.
units.tr: It is the dissolution of the arguments that are brought against us. Men often invent false arguments in order to deceive, which can easily be shown to be false if anyone carefully examines the eight topics of invention, to see whether the reasons adduced are simply false or merely contingent.

units.la: Quid est Transitio?
units.tr: What is the transition?

units.la: Est Vinculum, quo ostendimus breviter, quid dictum sit, & proponimus brevi, quid sequatur.
units.tr: It is the link by which we briefly show what has been said, and set forth in a few words what follows.

units.la: Quid est Peroratio?
units.tr: What is the peroration?

units.la: Est conclusio, in qua principalia membra plerunque repetuntur.
units.tr: It is the conclusion, in which the principal members are usually repeated.

units.la: Quot sunt Genera secundi modi Me- thodi?
units.tr: How many kinds are there of the second kind of method?

units.la: Quatuor: Didascalicum seu Didacticum, Judiciale, Deliberativum, Demonstrativum.
units.tr: Four: the didascalic or didactic, the judicial, the deliberative, and the demonstrative.

units.la: Quid est Genus Didascalicum?
units.tr: What is the didascalic kind?

units.la: Est Methodus docendi sive explicandi quæstiones simplices vel conjunctas. Quæstio simplex est cùm de una voce quæritur, ut, quid sit Theologia, quid sit Jurisprudentia. Quæstio conjuncta est integrum Enuntiatum, quod est aut confirmandum aut consutandum.
units.tr: It is the method of teaching or explaining simple or compound questions. A simple question is when a single term is asked about, as, "What is theology?" or "What is jurisprudence?" A compound question is a whole proposition, which is either to be confirmed or to be refuted.

units.la: Quomodo tractatur Quæstio simplex?
units.tr: How is a simple question treated?

units.la: Primò dicendum, quid vocabulum significet. Secundò, | an sit res. Tertiò, | quid sit res. Quartò, | quæ sint rei partes. Quintò, | quæ sint species. Sextò, | quæ causæ. Septimò, | qui effectus. Octavò, | quæ adjacentia. Nonò, | quæ cognata, Decimò, | quæ pugnantia.
units.tr: First, one must say what the word signifies. Second, whether the thing exists. Third, what the thing is. Fourth, what are the parts of the thing. Fifth, what are its species. Sixth, what are its causes. Seventh, what are its effects. Eighth, what are its adjuncts. Ninth, what are its kindred things. Tenth, what are its opposites.

units.la: Hujusmodi Methodum est Reverendus D. Doctor Simon Pauli secutus in suis Methodis Doctrinæ Christianæ, quas studiosi adolescentes legere possunt.
units.tr: The Reverend Doctor Simon Pauli followed this method in his Methods of Christian Doctrine, which studious young men can read.

units.la: Quid est Genus Judiciale?
units.tr: What is the judicial kind?

units.la: Est Methodus tractandi controversias forenses. Hujus Methodi status sunt tres:
units.tr: It is the method of treating legal controversies. There are three states of this method:

units.la: Primus Conjecturalis, an sit factum, ubi Confirmatio sumitur ab impulsione, affectu, ira, odio, avaritia,spe commodorum, loco, tempore, viribus, signis.
units.tr: The first is the conjectural, whether the thing was done, where the confirmation is drawn from impulse, feeling, anger, hatred, greed, hope of advantage, place, time, strength, and signs.

units.la: Secundus Juridicialis, an jure sit factum, ubi Confirmatio sumitur à natura, lege, consuetudine,æquo, bono, judicato, pacto.
units.tr: The second is the juridical, whether it was done rightly, where the confirmation is drawn from nature, law, custom, equity, goodness, judicial decision, and agreement.

units.la: Tertius Legalis, in quo de vocum significatione, ambiguo, contrariis legibus, scriptis verbis, sententia scriptoris ambigitur.
units.tr: The third is the legal, in which the meaning of words, ambiguity, conflicting laws, written words, and the intention of the writer are in question.

units.la: Quid est Genus Deliberativum?
units.tr: What is the deliberative kind?

units.la: Est Methodus, quæ versatur in suadendo, dissuadendo, adhortando, dehortando, petendo, consolando & similibus negotiis.
units.tr: It is the method that deals with persuading, dissuading, exhorting, dissuading from, asking, consoling, and similar matters.

units.la: Confirmatio sumitur in suadendo à necessario, honesto, utili, facili: In dissuadendo à non necessario, inhonesto, inutili, difficili.
units.tr: In persuading, the confirmation is drawn from what is necessary, honourable, useful, and easy; in dissuading, from what is not necessary, dishonourable, useless, and difficult.

units.la: Quid est Genus Demonstrativum?
units.tr: What is the demonstrative kind?

units.la: Est Methodus, quæ versatur in laudandis vel vituperandis personis, aut factis, seu rebus.
units.tr: It is the method that deals with praising or blaming persons, deeds, or things.

units.la: Laudamus aut vituperamus personas à patria, sexu, natalibus, ingenio, educatione, disciplina, doctrina, rebus gestis, præmio rerum gestarum, ætate, vitæ exitu.
units.tr: We praise or blame persons from their country, sex, birth, talent, upbringing, discipline, learning, deeds done, the reward of deeds done, age, and the end of their life.

units.la: Laudamus vel vituperamus facta à causis efficientibus, ab honesto, utili, inutili, facili, difficili, possibili, impossibili, circumstantiis, ubi, quomodo, quando.
units.tr: We praise or blame deeds from their efficient causes, from what is honourable, useful, useless, easy, difficult, possible, impossible, and from circumstances: where, how, and when.

units.la: Hæc vulgò in Rhetorica traduntur, sed natura ad Dialecticam pertinent.
units.tr: These things are commonly taught in rhetoric, but by nature they belong to dialectic.

units.la: Nonnulli zoili fortasse vociferabuntur: quare tu Methodi fingis modos, quum Petrus Ramus eos omiserit? Illi boni viri sciant, me non tantùm Petri Rami præcepta Tyronibus proponere, sed etiam Domini Philippi Melanchthonis axiomata, haudquaquam repudianda, cognoscenda studiosæ juventuti præscribere.
units.tr: Perhaps some carping critics will cry out: why do you invent kinds of method, when Peter Ramus omitted them? Those good men should know that I propose to young students not only the precepts of Peter Ramus, but also to prescribe for studious youth the axioms of Master Philip Melanchthon, which are by no means to be rejected.

units.la: Dialectices præcepta lecturi prolixiora, videant Petrum Ramum, Aristotelem, Dominum Philippum Melanchthonem, Dom. Doctorem Scribonium, Dominum Johannem Piscatorem, Fredericum Beurhusium & alios.
units.tr: Those who wish to read the fuller precepts of dialectic should consult Peter Ramus, Aristotle, Master Philip Melanchthon, Doctor Scribonius, Master John Piscator, Frederick Beurhus, and others.

units.la: Hactenus de Dialectica: nunc sequitur Physica.
units.tr: So much for dialectic; now follows physics.

units.la: DE PHYSICA.
units.tr: On Physics.

units.la: Quid est Physica?
units.tr: What is Physics?

units.la: PHYSICA, die natursunst/est ars bene naturam cognoscendi. Ejus subjectum est natura ipsa.
units.tr: PHYSICS, or the knowledge of nature, is the art of knowing nature well. Its subject is nature itself.

units.la: Quænam considerantur in natura?
units.tr: What is considered in nature?

units.la: Substantia, Facultas, Qualitas.
units.tr: Substance, faculty, and quality.

units.la: Quid est Substantia?
units.tr: What is substance?

units.la: Substantia est subsistentia, à naturæ Conditore, summè bono (tantùm enim ex naturæ lumine de Deo cognosci potest) nempe ente entium creata. Estq; aut spiritualis aut corporea.
units.tr: Substance is that which subsists, created by the Author of nature, the highest good (for God can be known only by the light of nature), namely created out of the being of beings. It is either spiritual or corporeal.

units.la: Spiritualis substantia est immortalis, intelligentia ac voluntate prædita.
units.tr: Spiritual substance is immortal and endowed with understanding and will.

units.la: Intelligentia est facultas spirituum, qua pro suo captu omnia entia intelligunt.
units.tr: Understanding is the faculty of spirits by which, according to their capacity, they understand all beings.

units.la: Voluntas est facultas spirituum, qua liberrimè entia eligunt aut rejiciunt.
units.tr: Will is the faculty of spirits by which they most freely choose or reject beings.

units.la: Spiritualis est substantia Geniorum & Animarum hominum.
units.tr: Spiritual substance is the substance of the Genii and of human souls.

units.la: Genii sunt boni vel mali. Hoc ex naturæ lumine veteres perspexerunt: ideoq; unicuiq; duos assignârunt Genios, bonum & malum.
units.tr: Genii are either good or evil. The ancients perceived this from the light of nature, and therefore assigned to each person two Genii, a good one and an evil one.

units.la: Anima hominis est substantia spiritualis primùm à numine homini inspirata: Deinde ex propagatione naturali à parentibus in liberos tradùcta, & tanquam lumen de lumine accensa.
units.tr: The human soul is a spiritual substance, first breathed into man by the divinity, and then transmitted from parents to children by natural propagation, and kindled like a light from a light.

units.la: Judicium animæ vel simplex est vel compositum.
units.tr: The judgement of the soul is either simple or compound.

units.la: Simplex est, quo res ipsas vel rerum affectiones simpliciter perpendit.
units.tr: It is simple when it weighs things themselves, or their affections, singly.

units.la: Compositum judicium est, quo ex simplicibus rebus dispositis aliquid colligit.
units.tr: A compound judgement is one by which it draws a conclusion from simple things arranged together.

units.la: Quotuplex est substantia corporea?
units.tr: How many kinds of corporeal substance are there?

units.la: Triplex : aut inanimata simplex ; aut inanimata mixta , aut animata mixta. Inanimata simplex est cœlum.
units.tr: Three: either simple inanimate, or mixed inanimate, or mixed animate. The simple inanimate is the heavens.

units.la: Quid est Cœlum?
units.tr: What is heaven?

units.la: Cœlum est mundi pars superior. Estq; duplex:Empyreum aut Aethereum.
units.tr: Heaven is the upper part of the world. It is twofold: the Empyrean or the Ethereal.

units.la: Empyreum cœlum, <bl>der sewr lauter Himmel</bl> / est sedes Dei, bonorum Geniorum & piarum animarum. Vocatur etiam cœlum cœlorum & tertium cœlum.
units.tr: The Empyrean heaven, the pure heaven, is the seat of God, of good Genii, and of pious souls. It is also called the heaven of heavens and the third heaven.

units.la: Aethereum cœlum est sedes stellarum. Quod & firmamentum dicitur. De orbibus cœli vide Sphæricam disciplinam Doctoris Scribonii.
units.tr: The Ethereal heaven is the seat of the stars, and is also called the firmament. On the spheres of the heavens, see the Sphere-science of Doctor Scribonius.

units.la: Quid est Stella?
units.tr: What is a star?

units.la: Stella est substantia corporea lucida cœlo adhærens. Estq; sixa aut errans. Fixa à tarditate motionis dicitur. Nam quasi immobilis insensibiliter propemodum movetur.
units.tr: A star is a bright corporeal substance adhering to the heaven. It is either fixed or wandering. It is called fixed from the slowness of its motion, for, as if immobile, it moves almost imperceptibly.

units.la: Stella sixa aut est in zodiaco, aut ultra citraque zodiacum.
units.tr: A fixed star is either in the zodiac, or beyond or on this side of the zodiac.

units.la: In zodiaco stellæ sunt duodecim : Aries , Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo,Virgo, Libra,Scorpius,Sagittarius,Capricornus, Aquarius,Pisces.
units.tr: In the zodiac there are twelve constellations: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces.

units.la: Aries est primum zodiaci signum, tredecim stellis arietis imaginem repræsentantibus, constans.
units.tr: Aries is the first sign of the zodiac, consisting of thirteen stars representing the image of a ram.

units.la: Taurus secundum signum est triginta duabus stellis Tauri effigiem constituentibus exornatum.
units.tr: Taurus is the second sign, adorned with thirty-two stars forming the figure of a bull.

units.la: Gemini tertium signum est stellis potissimùm octodecim efformatum.
units.tr: Gemini is the third sign, formed chiefly of eighteen stars.

units.la: Cancer quartum signum est , novem stellis quodammodo obscurioribus constans. Leo est quintum signum, sydus lucidum, viginti septem stellis illustratum.
units.tr: Cancer is the fourth sign, consisting of nine stars that are somewhat dimmer. Leo is the fifth sign, a bright constellation illustrated with twenty-seven stars.

units.la: Virgo sextum signum viginti sex stellis conformatum.
units.tr: Virgo, the sixth sign, is shaped by twenty-six stars.

units.la: Libra septimum signum stellis octo exornatum.
units.tr: Libra, the seventh sign, is adorned with eight stars.

units.la: Scorpius octavum signum stellis viginti una conformatum.
units.tr: Scorpio, the eighth sign, is formed by twenty-one stars.

units.la: Sagittarius nonum signum stellis triginta una constans.
units.tr: Sagittarius, the ninth sign, consists of thirty-one stars.

units.la: Capricornus est decimum signum octodecim stellis depictum.
units.tr: Capricorn is the tenth sign, depicted with eighteen stars.

units.la: Aquarius est undecimum signum stellis viginti duabus, hominis aquam ex amphora effundentis effigiem referentibus, constans.
units.tr: Aquarius is the eleventh sign, consisting of twenty-two stars, which represent the figure of a man pouring water from a jar.

units.la: Pisces signum duodecimum est triginta quatuor stellis, pisces conjunctos exprimentibus, exornatum.
units.tr: Pisces, the twelfth sign, is adorned with thirty-four stars, which portray two fishes joined together.

units.la: Hactenus de stellis in zodiaco: sequuntur stellæ ultra citraq; zodiacum.
units.tr: So much for the stars in the zodiac; there follow the stars beyond and on this side of the zodiac.

units.la: Quotuplices sunt stellæ ultra citraq; zodiacum.
units.tr: How many kinds of stars are there beyond and on this side of the zodiac?

units.la: Duplices: Aquilonares vel Meridionales. Aquilonares sunt, quæ septentrionalibus hominibus conspiciuntur.
units.tr: Two kinds: northern or southern. The northern are those that are seen by people in the northern regions.

units.la: Ejusmodi numerantur viginti una: ut Cynosura, Helice, Draco, Bootes, Corona Ariadnes, Hercules, Cepheus, Lyra, Gallina, Cassiopeja, Perseus, Heniochus, Serpens, Serpentarius, Sagitta, Aquila, Delphinus, Pegasus, Equiculus, Andromeda, Triangulus.
units.tr: Twenty-one of this kind are counted: such as the Cynosure, Helice, the Dragon, Bootes, the Crown of Ariadne, Hercules, Cepheus, the Lyre, the Hen, Cassiopeia, Perseus, Auriga, the Serpent, the Serpent-bearer, the Arrow, the Eagle, the Dolphin, Pegasus, the Little Horse, Andromeda, and the Triangle.

units.la: Cynosura sive ursa minor est signum septem stellis, suo complexu figuram plaustro similem depingentibus, constans.
units.tr: The Cynosure, or Little Bear, is a constellation of seven stars which, by their arrangement, depict a figure similar to a wagon.

units.la: Helice signum est Aquilonare viginti septem stellis ursæ majoris effigiem referentibus conformatum.
units.tr: Helice is a northern sign of twenty-seven stars, representing the figure of the Great Bear.

units.la: Draco sive Anguis, inter ursas sinuoso flexu prostratus continet stellas triginta unam.
units.tr: The Dragon, or Serpent, stretched out between the bears in a winding curve, contains thirty-one stars.

units.la: Bootes est signum septentrionale, prope ursam utramque, viginti duabus potissimum stellis constans.
units.tr: Bootes is a northern sign near both bears, consisting chiefly of twenty-two stars.

units.la: Corona Ariadnes, imago est septentrionalis octo stellis instar semicirculi condecorata.
units.tr: The Crown of Ariadne is a northern image, adorned with eight stars in the form of a semicircle.

units.la: Hercules sydus est septentrionale, viginti octo stellis conformatum.
units.tr: The constellation Hercules is northern, formed of twenty-eight stars.

units.la: Cepheus imago quadantenus obscura, prope Cynosuram & Draconem stellis undecim constans.
units.tr: Cepheus is an image somewhat obscure, near the Cynosure and the Dragon, consisting of eleven stars.

units.la: Lyra, quæ etiam vulturis cadentis effigie notatur: sydus est in cœlis Septentrionale, decem stellis ornatum.
units.tr: The Lyre, which is also marked by the figure of a falling vulture, is a northern constellation in the heavens, adorned with ten stars.

units.la: Gallina, quæ etiam Cygni nomine dicitur, est sig-num stellis septendecim conspicuum.
units.tr: The Hen, which is also called by the name of the Swan, is a sign visible with seventeen stars.

units.la: Cassiopea imago decima, sedili refupinato incumbens capite & stellis conformata tredecim.
units.tr: Cassiopeia, the tenth image, leaning on a reclining chair with its head thrown back, is formed of thirteen stars.

units.la: Perseus imago est undecima, stellis novendecim condecorata.
units.tr: Perseus is the eleventh image, decorated with nineteen stars.

units.la: Heniochus Pegasi pedibus subjectus, imago est aurigæ in sinistro humero capram gestantis, tredecim stellis lucens.
units.tr: Auriga, placed beneath the feet of Pegasus, is the image of a charioteer carrying a goat on his left shoulder, shining with thirteen stars.

units.la: Serpentarius sive Ophiuchus est imago Aesculapii,suis manibus serpentem tenentis: viginti quatuor stellis conspicua.
units.tr: The Serpent-bearer, or Ophiuchus, is the image of Aesculapius holding a serpent in his hands, conspicuous with twenty-four stars.

units.la: Serpens ab Aesculapio dependens est ejusdem nominis animal octodecim stellis notatum.
units.tr: The Serpent, hanging from Aesculapius, is an animal of the same name, marked with eighteen stars.

units.la: Sagitta est imago telum referens: quinque stellis prope aquilam conspicua.
units.tr: The Arrow, representing a missile, is conspicuous with five stars near the Eagle.

units.la: Aquila signum est effigiem aquilæ avis repræsentans: sex stellis illustratum.
units.tr: The Eagle is a sign representing the figure of the eagle bird, illustrated with six stars.

units.la: Delphinus eodem in loco decem stellis configuratus apparet. Pegasus est signum viginti stellarum configuratione equi alati imaginem referens.
units.tr: The Dolphin appears in the same place, arranged with ten stars. Pegasus is a sign of twenty stars, by its arrangement representing the image of a winged horse.

units.la: Equiculus est imago minoris equi, quatuor stellis nubilosis expressa.
units.tr: The Little Horse is the image of a lesser horse, expressed by four cloudy stars.

units.la: Andromeda signum est viginti tribus stellis conspicuum.
units.tr: Andromeda is a sign conspicuous with twenty-three stars.

units.la: Triangulus est imago triangularis quatuor stellis notata.
units.tr: The Triangle is a triangular image marked with four stars.

units.la: Adhuc de stellis Aquilonaribus: sequun- tur Meridionales.
units.tr: Further on the northern stars; the southern stars follow.

units.la: Meridionales stellæ sunt, quæ in plaga mundi Austrina antipodibus nostris potissimum apparent.
units.tr: The southern stars are those that appear chiefly to our antipodes in the southern region of the world.

units.la: Ejusmodi numerantur quindecim: Cetus, Orion, Eridanus, Lepus, Sirius, Procyon, Argonavis, Hydra, Crater, Corvus, Centaurus, Lupus, Ara, Corona australis, & Piscis major.
units.tr: Fifteen of this kind are counted: Cetus, Orion, Eridanus, Lepus, Sirius, Procyon, Argonavis, Hydra, Crater, Corvus, Centaurus, Lupus, Ara, the Southern Crown, and the Greater Fish.

units.la: CETUS est signum Meridionale viginti duarum stellarum configuratione, ceti marini figuram ostendens.
units.tr: Cetus is a southern sign of twenty-two stars arranged in a configuration showing the figure of a sea monster.

units.la: Orion est imago triginta octo stellarum positu, virum in lumbis zona cinctum exprimens.
units.tr: Orion is a figure of thirty-eight stars in position, representing a man girded with a belt at the loins.

units.la: Eridanus figura est triginta quatuor stellarum instar fluvii ejusdem nominis, quem hodie Padum vocant, diffluens.
units.tr: Eridanus is a figure of thirty-four stars, spread out like a river of the same name, which today they call the Po.

units.la: Lepus signum est duodecim stellis clarum.
units.tr: Lepus is a sign bright with twelve stars.

units.la: Sirius est astrum stellis octodecim insignitum, canis majoris effigiem referens.
units.tr: Sirius is a star marked with eighteen stars, representing the likeness of the Greater Dog.

units.la: Procyon est imago Caniculam referens, duabus stellis ornata.
units.tr: Procyon is a figure representing the Little Dog, adorned with two stars.

units.la: Argonavis est signum quadraginta quinque stellis lucens.
units.tr: Argonavis is a sign shining with forty-five stars.

units.la: Hydra imago est stellis vigintiquinq; serpentem referens.
units.tr: Hydra is a figure of twenty-five stars, representing a serpent.

units.la: Crater est imago poculum bibendo idoneum referens, eaq; septem stellis expressa.
units.tr: Crater is a figure representing a cup suitable for drinking, marked out by seven stars.

units.la: Corvus est sydus septem quoque stellis lucidum.
units.tr: Corvus is a constellation, likewise bright with seven stars.

units.la: Centaurus Chiron est imago triginta septem stellis conspicua.
units.tr: Centaurus Chiron is a figure conspicuous with thirty-seven stars.

units.la: Lupus imago est stellis novendecim configurata.
units.tr: Lupus is a figure arranged with nineteen stars.

units.la: Ara sive Altare cœli, septem stellis exornata lucet.
units.tr: Ara, or the Altar of heaven, shines adorned with seven stars.

units.la: Corona australis, quæ Bacchi quoq; nomine dicitur est imago tredecim stellarum.
units.tr: The Southern Crown, which is also called by the name of Bacchus, is a figure of thirteen stars.

units.la: Pi cis[?] major est sydus postremum duodecim stellis condecoratum.
units.tr: The Greater Fish is the last constellation, adorned with twelve stars.

units.la: Hactenus[?] de stellis fixis sequuntur errantes, videlicet Planetæ.
units.tr: So far on the fixed stars; the wandering stars follow, namely the planets.

units.la: Quot sunt Planetæ?
units.tr: How many planets are there?

units.la: PLanetæ sunt stellæ errantes in citeriore cœlo, varium inter se motum conficientes. Suntque septem:Saturnus,Jupiter,Mars,Sol,Venus,Mercurius, Luna.
units.tr: Planets are wandering stars in the lower heaven, performing varied motions among themselves. There are seven: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon.

units.la: Saturnus est Planeta primus plumbei coloris, triginta annis cursum suum absolvens.
units.tr: Saturn is the first planet, of a lead colour, completing its course in thirty years.

units.la: Jupiter est Planeta secundus lucidus, duodecim annorum spatio circulum suum percurrens.
units.tr: Jupiter is the second planet, bright, running its circuit in the space of twelve years.

units.la: Mars est Planeta tertius, colore rutilus sive flammeus, duobus annis suum cursum conficiens.
units.tr: Mars is the third planet, ruddy or fiery in colour, completing its course in two years.

units.la: Sol est Planeta quartus omnium lucidissimus in dominium diei conditus trecentis sexaginta quinque diebus cursum suum absolvens, vocatur & luminare magnum.
units.tr: The Sun is the fourth planet, the brightest of all, set over the rule of the day, completing its course in 365 days; it is also called the great light.

units.la: Sol si in orbis sui apogæo, aut perigæo feratur, fit solstitium.
units.tr: If the sun is carried to the apogee or perigee of its orb, a solstice occurs.

units.la: Solstitium est vel æstivale, vel hybernum. Æstivale solstitium est solis altissimi, ideoque diei longissimi determinatio.
units.tr: A solstice is either summer or winter. The summer solstice marks the highest sun and therefore the longest day.

units.la: Contingit hoc nostris temporibus duodecimo vel decimoteitio[?] Junii,in principio cancri.
units.tr: In our times this happens on the twelfth or thirteenth of June, at the beginning of Cancer.

units.la: Hybernum est solis à nobis remotissimi, ideoque diei brevissimi terminus. Sol si in æquatore est, nox diei, & è contra dies noctis omninò æquatur.
units.tr: The winter solstice marks the sun at its greatest distance from us and therefore the shortest day. When the sun is on the equator, night is equal to day, and conversely day is wholly equal to night.

units.la: Sunt autem duo æquinoctia, vernale & autumnale.
units.tr: There are two equinoxes, vernal and autumnal.

units.la: Vernale contingit in principio Arietis, undecimo plærunq; vel duodecimo Martii, tempore veris.
units.tr: The vernal equinox occurs at the beginning of Aries, usually on the eleventh or twelfth of March, in the season of spring.

units.la: Autumnale est, quod in principio Libræ mense Septembri accidit, tempore autumni.
units.tr: The autumnal equinox is that which falls at the beginning of Libra, in September, in the season of autumn.

units.la: Venus est Planeta candidissimus, Solemque matutino tempore antecedit, & tum Lucifer dicitur: aut eum tempore vespertino occidentem subsequitur, & tum Hesperus, item Vesperugo appellatur.
units.tr: Venus is the brightest planet. It precedes the sun in the morning, and then is called Lucifer; or it follows the setting sun in the evening, and then it is called Hesperus, also named Vesperugo.

units.la: Mercurius est Planeta omnium minimus, parumper albicans.
units.tr: Mercury is the smallest of all the planets, slightly whitish.

units.la: Luna est Planeta in ordine infimus: viginti septem diebus, & horis septem metam constitutam attinges. Vocatur & luminare minus.
units.tr: The Moon is the lowest planet in order: you will reach its appointed goal in twenty-seven days and seven hours. It is also called the lesser light.

units.la: Quid est Cometa?
units.tr: What is a comet?

units.la: Cometa est stella errans, nunc infra, nunc supra alios planetas cōspicua, ideoq; etiam gravissima quæque prænuntiare solet.
units.tr: A comet is a wandering star, seen now below and now above the other planets, and so it is wont to portend the gravest things.

units.la: Quid est Eclipsis Solis?
units.tr: What is a solar eclipse?

units.la: Eclipsis Solis est radiorum Solis à terra exclusio, seu aversio.
units.tr: A solar eclipse is the exclusion or turning away of the sun's rays from the earth.

units.la: Accidit hæc ob interpositionem Lunæ, propter propinquitatem radios solares sua crassitie excludentis & avertentis.
units.tr: This happens through the interposition of the moon, which, by its nearness, excludes and turns away the solar rays with its thickness.

units.la: Quid est Eclipsis Lunæ?
units.tr: What is a lunar eclipse?

units.la: Eclipsis Lunæ est luminis Solaris in Luna privatio, ob interpositionem terræ inter Solem & Lunam ex diametro factam.
units.tr: A lunar eclipse is the privation of solar light in the moon, caused by the earth being interposed between sun and moon, in a straight line through the diameter.

units.la: Adhuc de substantiis corporeis inanimatis simplicibus: sequuntur substantiæ corporeæ inanimatæ mixtæ seu concretæ.
units.tr: So far on simple inanimate corporeal substances; there follow mixed or compound inanimate corporeal substances.

units.la: Quænam sunt substantiæ corporeæ inanimatæ mixtæ?
units.tr: What are the mixed inanimate corporeal substances?

units.la: Elementa,Meteora, Metalla, Gemmæ,Lapides minus pretiosi,& Metalla friabilia.
units.tr: The elements, meteors, metals, gems, less precious stones, and friable metals.

units.la: Elementa , quamvis simplicia primùm facta fuerint : ob mutuam tamen inter se conjunctionem, impuritatem quandam contraxerunt, quæ simplicitatem quodammodo repressit, ut confervandis corporibus aliis magis essent idonea.
units.tr: The elements, although at first they were made simple, nevertheless, through their mutual conjunction, have contracted a certain impurity, which has in some measure repressed their simplicity, so that they are better suited to preserving other bodies.

units.la: Elementa sunt quatuor:Ignis,aer,aqua,terra.
units.tr: There are four elements: fire, air, water, earth.

units.la: Elementum ignis nihil aliud est, quàm propter syderum cœli propinquitatem aer calidissimus.
units.tr: The element of fire is nothing other than air made very hot, on account of the nearness of the stars of heaven.

units.la: Ignis autem quo in focis nostris fruimur, est intentissima tatùm caliditas cum extrema siccitate in corporibus ustibilibus. Et flamma ignis illius est accensus solummodò aer: quare etiam ob aëream levitatem in altum semper ascendit.
units.tr: The fire we enjoy in our hearths, however, is only an intense heat together with extreme dryness in combustible bodies. The flame of that fire is only air set alight; for this reason, too, because of its airy lightness, it always rises upward.

units.la: Aer est elementum pellucidum , & ratione loci calidum,frigidum,humidum,purum vel impurum.
units.tr: Air is a transparent element, and, according to its place, hot or cold, moist, pure or impure.

units.la: Aqua est elementum minus pellucidum,humidum & sua natura frigidissimum, nisi ob calidorum corporum propinquitatem calorem contrahat : ut, Thermæ, <bl>warme wasser / die warm auß der erden</bl> <bl>quellen.</bl>
units.tr: Water is a less transparent element, moist and in its nature very cold, unless through the nearness of hot bodies it takes on warmth, as in thermal springs: warm water, which wells up warm out of the earth.

units.la: Terra est elementum crassum, frigidum & siccifsimum.
units.tr: Earth is a thick, cold and very dry element.

units.la: Tantum de Elementis: sequitur de Meteoris.
units.tr: Thus much concerning the Elements: it follows concerning Meteors.

units.la: METEORA sunt substantiæ corporeæ inanimatæ mixtæ, quæ cum admiratione quadam in sublimi præcipuè aëre apparent. Suntq; ignita vel aquea.
units.tr: Meteors are mixed, inanimate corporeal substances, which appear in the upper air, chiefly the air, with a certain wonder. And they are either fiery or watery.

units.la: Ignita sunt exhalationes ignis instar verè exardescentes : ut, ignis perpendicularis, bolis,candela accensa,splendor nocturnus, capra saltans, scintilla volans, stella cadens, ignis fatuus , tonitru, coruscatio, fulmen.
units.tr: The fiery ones are exhalations truly blazing like fire, such as: the upright fire, the bolis, the lit candle, the nocturnal splendour, the leaping goat, the flying spark, the falling star, the will-o'-the-wisp, thunder, lightning flash, and the thunderbolt.

units.la: Ignis perpendicularis est exhalatio inæqualiter crassa, in supremo aere, formam columnæ pyramidalis referens.
units.tr: The upright fire is an exhalation unevenly thick, in the highest air, resembling the form of a pyramidal column.

units.la: Bolis est exhalatio æqualiter crassa, sagittæ ardentis ab una parte in aliam transcurrentis figuram reddens.
units.tr: The bolis is an exhalation evenly thick, presenting the figure of a burning arrow passing from one side to the other.

units.la: Candela accensa est exhalatio rara & subtilis, quæ ex æquo dilatabilis continuè in parte superiore accenditur.
units.tr: The lit candle is a rare and subtle exhalation, which, being equally dilatable, is continually kindled in its upper part.

units.la: Splendor nocturnus est exhalatio rarissima, & tenuis in summo aere accensa.
units.tr: The nocturnal splendour is a very rare and thin exhalation, kindled in the highest air.

units.la: Capra saltans est exhalatio velut in duas partes divisa, longas quidem, sed latiores, quæ scintillatione sua quasi saltare videntur.
units.tr: The leaping goat is an exhalation as if divided into two parts, long indeed but broader, which seem, by their sparkling, to leap.

units.la: Scintilla volans est exhalatio in plures partes dispersa, singulis seorsim inflammatis.
units.tr: The flying spark is an exhalation dispersed into several parts, each one kindled separately.

units.la: Stella cadens est exhalatio superius inflammata, deorsum decurrens, ut cadere videatur.
units.tr: The falling star is an exhalation kindled higher up, running downwards, so that it seems to fall.

units.la: Ignis fatuus est exhalatio candelæ instar accensæ oblongior. Hæc ventis agitata decliviora loca potissimum petit: unde noctu iter facientes, si eam sequantur, in præcipitia feruntur.
units.tr: The will-o'-the-wisp is an exhalation somewhat longer than a lit candle. Driven by the winds, it seeks chiefly the lower, sloping places; so travellers at night who follow it are carried into precipices.

units.la: Tonitru est exhalatio accensa cum sono e nubibus erumpens.
units.tr: Thunder is an exhalation kindled and bursting forth from the clouds with a sound.

units.la: Coruscatio est accensum tonantis exhalationis lumen, altius super terram resplendens.
units.tr: Lightning flash is the light of the thundering exhalation kindled, shining more high above the earth.

units.la: Fulmen est exhalatio coruscationi spissior artiusque composita, vehementius, & prope terram magis inardescens. Estque subtile, fuliginosum vel urens.
units.tr: The thunderbolt is an exhalation thicker than lightning flash and more tightly compounded, more violent, and burning more fiercely near the earth. It is either subtle, sooty or burning.

units.la: Subtile, quod nullo signo relicto, tacta quælibet perforat.
units.tr: Subtle, which, leaving no mark, pierces whatever it touches.

units.la: Fuliginosum, quod corpora, quæ transit, fuligine quadam relicta obfuscat.
units.tr: Sooty, which, leaving a certain soot on the bodies it passes through, darkens them.

units.la: Fulmen urens, quod multum ignis relinquit. Idcoq; ustibilia corpora facile accendit.
units.tr: Burning, which leaves much fire behind. Hence it easily sets alight bodies that can be burnt.

units.la: Hæc de ignitis Meteoris: sequuntur aquea.
units.tr: These things concerning the fiery meteors: now follow the watery.

units.la: AQUEA Meteora sunt vapores plenius constricti[?] ut, nubes, parelios, parafelene, halo, iris, pluvia, nix, grando, ros, pruina, ventus.
units.tr: The watery meteors are vapours more fully condensed, such as: clouds, the parhelion, the paraselene, the halo, the rainbow, rain, snow, hail, dew, hoarfrost, wind.

units.la: Nubes est vapor extremo medii aeris frigore conjunctus.
units.tr: A cloud is a vapour joined together by the cold of the extreme middle air.

units.la: Parelios imago solis in nube splendida, ad latus ejus posita, a radiis refractis expressa. Unde sæpe duo, interdum plures Soles conspiciuntur.
units.tr: A parhelion is an image of the sun in a bright cloud, placed at its side, expressed by refracted rays. Hence often two, sometimes more, suns are seen.

units.la: Parafelene est imago Lunæ, sub ea apparens.
units.tr: A paraselene is an image of the moon, appearing beneath it.

units.la: Halo est circulus Solis vel Lunæ, sub iis in media aeris regione existens.
units.tr: A halo is a circle around the sun or moon, existing beneath them in the middle region of the air.

units.la: Iris est arcus varicolor in nube concava, rara & inæquali, e radiorum oppositi *Solis reflexione formatus.
units.tr: The rainbow is a many-coloured arch in a hollow, thin and uneven cloud, formed by the reflection of the rays of the opposite sun.

units.la: Pluvia est nubes liquefacta, & in aquam guttatim destillatam resoluta.
units.tr: Rain is a cloud liquefied and resolved into water distilled drop by drop.

units.la: Nix est pluvia in aere ventorum agitatione in flocos distracta.
units.tr: Snow is rain scattered into flakes in the air by the agitation of the winds.

units.la: Grando est pluvia ante descensum in glaciales globulos redacta.
units.tr: Hail is rain turned into icy globules before it falls.

units.la: Ros est vapor condensatus, & decidendo mox in aquam resolutus.
units.tr: Dew is condensed vapour, which, soon falling, is resolved into water.

units.la: Pruina est vapor congelatus.
units.tr: Hoarfrost is vapour frozen.

units.la: Ventus est fumus subtilis, qui supra terrā movetur.
units.tr: Wind is a subtle smoke which moves above the earth.

units.la: Si autem fumus in speluncis terræ contentus, exitum non invenit & vi erumpit, existit Terræmotus.
units.tr: But if the smoke, contained in the caves of the earth, finds no exit and bursts forth by force, an earthquake arises.

units.la: Tantum de Meteoris: sequitur de Metallis.
units.tr: Thus much concerning Meteors: it follows concerning Metals.

units.la: METALLA sunt substantiæ corporeæ inanimatæ mixtæ, in venis terrarum decoctæ: ut, Sulphur, Mercurius seu argentum vivum, Aurum, Argentum, Æs, Ferrum, Plumbum, Stannum.
units.tr: Metals are mixed, inanimate corporeal substances, cooked in the veins of the earth: such as sulphur, mercury or quicksilver, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin.

units.la: Sulphur est pinguedo terræ, igneo calore ad indurationem excocta.
units.tr: Sulphur is the fatness of the earth, baked to hardening by fiery heat.

units.la: Mercurius seu argentum vivum est metallum tenuissimum, frigidissimum & gravissimum.
units.tr: Mercury or quicksilver is a very thin, very cold and very heavy metal.

units.la: Aurum est metallum è sulphure rubeo subtilissimo purissimo[?]q; factum: cujus substantia nec terra, nec aqua, nec aëre corrumpitur: nec igni etiam comburitur: sed magis magisq; in eo perpurgatur.
units.tr: Gold is a metal made from the most subtle, purest red sulphur; its substance is corrupted neither by earth, water, nor air, nor is it burnt even by fire, but is more and more purged within it.

units.la: Argentum est metallum ex puro albo Mercurio, & sulphure similiter claro & albicante genitum.
units.tr: Silver is a metal produced from pure white mercury and sulphur likewise bright and whitish.

units.la: Aes est metallum è sulphure crasso rubeo & Mercurio paululum impuriore genitum: quod vulgo Cuprum dicitur à Cypro insula, ubi copiosissime effoditur, quasi Cyprium.
units.tr: Copper is a metal produced from thick red sulphur and mercury somewhat more impure; it is commonly called cuprum from the island of Cyprus, where it is dug up most abundantly, as if Cyprian.

units.la: Ferrum est metallum è Mercurio immodico & sulphure spissiore utroque impuro & aduicnte[?] genitum.
units.tr: Iron is a metal produced from excessive mercury and a thicker sulphur, both impure and adhering.

units.la: Plumbum est metallum impurius è Mercurio admodum impuro, crasso & fæculento, & sulphure similiter impuro genitum.
units.tr: Lead is a more impure metal, produced from mercury very impure, thick and dregs-laden, and likewise impure sulphur.

units.la: Stannum est metallum è Mercurio albo in superficie & rubeo intrinsecus, & sulphure non bene commixto natum.
units.tr: Tin is a metal born of mercury white on the surface and red within, and of sulphur not well mixed.

units.la: Hæc de Metallis: sequitur de Gemmis.
units.tr: These things concerning Metals: now follow concerning Gems.

units.la: GEMMAE sunt lapides ob materiam puriorem subtilioremque speciosi & elegantes: ut, Crystallus, Adamas, Sapphirus, Smaragdus, Sardonyx, Selenites, Carbunculus, Carchedonius, Rubinus, Topazius Hyacinthus, Corallium, Magnes, Galactites, Achates, Turcois, Corneolus, Chrysoprasus, Hæmatites.
units.tr: Gems are stones, beautiful and elegant on account of their purer and finer matter: such as crystal, adamant, sapphire, emerald, sardonyx, selenite, carbuncle, carchedony, ruby, topaz, hyacinth, coral, magnet, galactite, agate, turquoise, cornelian, chrysoprase, haematite.

units.la: Crystallus est gemma pellucidissima, è succo purissimo lapidescente genita.
units.tr: Crystal is the most transparent gem, produced from the purest juice turning to stone.

units.la: Adamas est gemma transparens, eaque durissima.
units.tr: Adamant is a transparent gem, and that the hardest.

units.la: Sapphirus est gemma pellucida, colorem cœruleum obtinens.
units.tr: Sapphire is a clear gem, holding a blue colour.

units.la: Smaragdus est gemma pellucida, viridi colore etiam vicinum aërem inficiens.
units.tr: Emerald is a clear gem, which tints even the neighbouring air with its green colour.

units.la: Sardonyx est gemma transparens, unguis alicujus digitorum humanorum colorem referens.
units.tr: Sardonyx is a transparent gem, resembling the colour of a human fingernail.

units.la: Selenites gemma est instar speculi seu vitri translucens.
units.tr: The selenite gem is translucent, like a mirror or glass.

units.la: Carbunculus est gemma instar ignis noctu lumen præbens.
units.tr: The carbuncle is a gem like fire, giving light at night.

units.la: Carchedonius est gemma subpurpurea, stellæ instar clarè refulgens.
units.tr: The carchedony is a gem somewhat purple, shining brightly like a star.

units.la: Rubinus est gemma rubea per tenebras in specie exiguæ scintillæ alicujus micans.
units.tr: The ruby is a red gem, glittering through the darkness in the appearance of a small spark.

units.la: Topazius est gemma coloris aurei, Soli exposita, tantùm radios de se spargens.
units.tr: The topaz is a gem of golden colour, which, exposed to the sun, only scatters rays from itself.

units.la: Hyacinthus gemma est aquei coloris, ob duritiem indissolubilis, in tenebris nebulosa, interdiu clara & pura.
units.tr: The hyacinth gem is of watery colour, indissoluble on account of its hardness, cloudy in darkness, clear and pure by day.

units.la: Corallium est gemma fruticis lapidescentis figuram repræsentans.
units.tr: Coral is a gem representing the shape of a petrifying shrub.

units.la: Magnes est lapis colore ad cœruleum vergente, ferrum attrahens.
units.tr: The magnet is a stone inclining to a blue colour, attracting iron.

units.la: Galactites lapis pretiosus est colore cinereo, lacteum humorem refudans.
units.tr: The galactite is a precious stone of ash colour, pouring out a milky liquid.

units.la: Achates est gemma varicolor, leoninæ potissimum pellis similis.
units.tr: The agate is a many-coloured gem, most like the skin of a lion.

units.la: Turcois gemma est obscurior, coloris cœrulei ex viridi relucentis.
units.tr: The turquoise is a darker gem, of blue colour shining through green.

units.la: Corneolus gemma est ex viridi colore aureis interstincta maculis, in tenebris tantum parumper lucens.
units.tr: The cornelian is a gem of green colour marked with golden spots, shining only a little in darkness.

units.la: Hæmatites gemma est ferrugineo colore venulis sanguinolentis mixta.
units.tr: The haematite is a gem of iron-rust colour mixed with bloody veins.

units.la: Tantum de Gemmis: sequitur de lapidibus minus pretiosis.
units.tr: That is enough on gems; there follows the less precious stones.

units.la: LAPIDES Minus pretiosi sunt Porphyrites, Alabastrum, Ophytes, & id genus alia.
