Therefore betrothals can be contracted even without a pledge (arrhae, a betrothal gift), but when a pledge has been given, the betrothal is said to be confirmed.

units.la: Denique constat & absenti absentem desponderi posse: & hoc quotidie fieri. l. 4. ff. eod. In sponsalibus contrahendis, aetas contrahentium definita non est, ut in matrimoniis. Quapropter etiam à primordio aetatis sponsalia effici possunt, modo id fieri ab utraque persona intelligatur, id est, si non sint minores, quàm septem annis. l. 14. ff. eod.
units.tr: Finally, it is agreed that one absent person may be betrothed to another absent person, and this happens every day. L. 4, ff. eod. In contracting betrothals, no age of the contracting parties is fixed, as there is for marriages. For this reason betrothals can be made even at the very beginning of life, provided it is understood that both parties consent, that is, provided they are not younger than seven years. L. 14, ff. eod.

units.la: Quot sunt Species Sponsaliorum?
units.tr: What are the kinds of betrothal?

units.la: Duae: Sponsalia de praesenti & sponsalia de futuro Secundùm jus Canonicum Sponsalia de præsenti sunt, quando quis virgini sine cōditione pure & simpliciter promittit Conjugium. Hujusmodi Sponsalia de jure civili verè sunt matrimonium: siquidem nuptias non concubitus, sed consensus facit l.Nuptias. 30.ff.de divers.Reg.Jur.
units.tr: There are two: betrothal in the present and betrothal in the future. According to the canon law, a betrothal in the present is when someone promises marriage to a virgin without condition, purely and simply. Such betrothals are, by civil law, truly marriage, since it is consent, not sexual intercourse, that makes a marriage. L. Nuptias 30, ff. de divers. reg. iur.

units.la: Sponsalia de futuro sunt tractatus de futuro matrimonio, ita quòd illa promissio futurarum nuptiarum non contineat in se purum aut absolutum consensum, sed cum quodam tractu futuri temporis,secundùm Schneidevvinum hic.
units.tr: Betrothals in the future are agreements about a future marriage, such that the promise of future marriage does not contain in itself a pure or absolute consent, but has in it a certain interval of future time, according to Schneidewin here.

units.la: Quæ est differentia inter sponsalia de præsenti, & sponsalia de futuro?
units.tr: What is the difference between betrothal in the present and betrothal in the future?

units.la: Sponsalia de præsenti mutuo dissensu non dissolvuntur, nec pœnitentia in hoc contractu locum habet, sed pœnitens potest compelli ad consummandum matrimonium. Imò si legitimus inter virum & mulierem interveniat consensus de præsenti, sive juramentum sit interpositum sive non, non licet alteri ad alia vota transfire, quod si fecerit, secundum matrimonium de facto contractum, etiamsi carnalis copula subsecuta sit, separari, & primum in sua firmitate manere debet, teste Schneidevvino, qui hanc sententiam ex jure Canonico defendit. Sponsalia de futuro non ita obligant, sed sicut consensu contrahuntur, ita dissensu dissolvuntur. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: A betrothal in the present is not dissolved by mutual dissent, and repentance has no place in this contract; rather, the one who repents can be compelled to complete the marriage. Indeed, if a lawful consent in the present takes place between a man and a woman, whether or not an oath has been added, it is not permitted for either to turn to other vows; and if one does so, the second marriage de facto contracted, even if carnal union has followed, must be separated, and the first must remain in its force, as Schneidewin attests, who defends this opinion from the canon law. Betrothals in the future do not bind in this way, but just as they are contracted by consent, so they are dissolved by dissent. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quæ est differentia inter Matrimonium & Conjugium?
units.tr: What is the difference between matrimonium and conjugium?

units.la: Matrimonium & Conjugium sunt Synonyma. Nuptiæ vero tripliciter accipiuntur: primò pro sponsalibus de præsenti absque concubitu: Secundò pro matrimonio consummato per concubitum secutum. Tertiò Tertió & quidem proprie, profestivitate & solennitate nuptialis diei & convivii.
units.tr: Matrimonium and conjugium are synonyms. The word nuptiae, however, is taken in three ways: first, for betrothals in the present without intercourse; second, for a marriage consummated by the intercourse that follows; third, and properly so, for the festivity and solemnity of the wedding day and feast.

units.la: Quinam justas nuptias contrahunt?
units.tr: Who contract lawful marriages?

units.la: Justas nuptias inter se cives Romani contrahunt, qui secundum præcepta legum coeunt, masculi quidem puberes, fœminæ autem viripotentes, sive patresfamiliarum sint, sive filiifamiliarum: dum tamen si filiifamiliarum sint, consensum habeant parentum, quorum in potestate sunt. In princ. instit. de Nuptiis.
units.tr: Lawful marriages are contracted between Roman citizens who come together according to the precepts of the laws: males who have reached puberty and females who are of marriageable strength, whether they are heads of households or still under paternal authority; provided, however, that if they are under paternal authority, they have the consent of the parents in whose power they are. In the beginning of the Institutes, on marriages.

units.la: Quæ requiritur ætas in matrimonis contrahendis?
units.tr: What age is required for contracting marriage?

units.la: Pubertas masculorum & fœminarum. Pubertatem autem, inquit Imperator, in princ. instit. Quibus modis tutel. finit. in masculis post decimum quartum annum completum illico initium accipere disposuimus. Antiquitatis normam in fœminis bene positam in suo ordine relinquentes, ut post duodecim annos completos viripotentes esse credantur.
units.tr: Puberty for males and females. As the Emperor says, in the beginning of the Institutes, on the ways in which guardianships are ended: "We have decreed that in males puberty begins immediately after the completed fourteenth year. Leaving in females the ancient rule, well laid down in its place, they are believed to be of marriageable strength after twelve years are completed."

units.la: Quæ dicuntur proprie nuptiæ nefariæ?
units.tr: What are properly called unlawful marriages?

units.la: Quæ inter ascendentes & descendentes contrahuntur usque in infinitum. §. ergo non omnes. inst. de nupt. Ita ut si Adam, mortua Eva, hodie superstes esset, & cum aliqua matrimonium contrahere vellet, committeret nefarium.
units.tr: Those contracted between ascendants and descendants, without limit. §. ergo non omnes, Inst. de nupt. So that if Adam, Eve having died, were still alive today and wished to contract marriage with someone, he would commit an unlawful act.

units.la: Quæ dicuntur nuptiæ incestæ?
units.tr: What are called incestuous marriages?

units.la: Quæ inter collaterales consanguineos in primo & secundo gradu, lineæ inæqualis contrahuntur, inquit Schneidevvinus.
units.tr: Those contracted between collateral blood relatives in the first and second degree of an unequal line, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Quæ dicuntur nuptiæ inutiles?
units.tr: What are called invalid marriages?

units.la: Quæ tantùm lege civili vel canonico jure prohibente, & non natura vel jure Divino repugnante, contrahuntur.
units.tr: Those contracted where only civil law or canon law forbids them, and which do not conflict with nature or divine law.

units.la: Inter quas personas nuptiæ contrahi non possunt?
units.tr: Between which persons can marriages not be contracted?

units.la: Inter eas personas quæ parentum liberorumque locum inter se obtinent, contrahi nuptiæ non possunt: veluti inter patrem & filiam, vel avum & neptē, vel matrem & filium, vel aviam & nepotem & usq; in infinitum, §. ergo non omnes. inst.de nuptiis.
units.tr: Marriages cannot be contracted between persons who stand to one another in the place of parents and children: for example, between father and daughter, or grandfather and granddaughter, or mother and son, or grandmother and grandson, and so on without limit. §. ergo non omnes, Inst. de nuptiis.

units.la: Suntne inter fratrem & sororem pro- hibitæ nuptiæ?
units.tr: Are marriages between brother and sister forbidden?

units.la: Sanè inter fratrem sororemque nuptiæ prohibitæ sunt sive ab eodem patre eademq; matre nati fuerint, sive ab altero eorum. §. inter eas.inst.eod.
units.tr: Certainly marriage between brother and sister is forbidden, whether they were born of the same father and the same mother, or of only one of them. §. inter eas, Inst. eod.

units.la: Licetne fratris vel sororis filiam vel ne- p-tem ducere?
units.tr: Is it lawful to marry the daughter or granddaughter of a brother or sister?

units.la: Fratris verò vel sororis filiam uxorem ducere non licet: sed nec neptem fratris vel sororis quis ducere potest.§. fratris verò.inst. eod.
units.tr: It is not lawful to marry the daughter of a brother or sister, and nor may anyone marry a brother's or sister's granddaughter.

units.la: Licetne sororis Adoptivæ filiam ducere?
units.tr: Is it lawful to marry the daughter of an adoptive sister?

units.la: Ejus mulieris, quam pater tuus adoptavit, filiam non videris impediri uxorem ducere, quia neque naturali, neque civili jure tibi conjungitur. §. fratris. in-stit.eod.
units.tr: You will not be seen as hindered from marrying the daughter of a woman whom your father adopted, since she is joined to you neither by natural nor by civil law.

units.la: Possuntne duorum fratrum vel sororum liberi contrahere?
units.tr: Can the children of two brothers or two sisters contract marriage?

units.la: Duorum fratrum vel sororum liberi, vel fratris & sororis conjungi possunt. §. duorum. inst. cod. Sed jus Canonicum hoc nequaquam concedit: quia duorum fratrum vel sororum liberi jure Canonico sunt in secundo gradu, qui omnino prohibitus est, sicut & tertius & quartus : quintus autem gradus permissus est. Vide S[?]hneidevvinum.
units.tr: The children of two brothers or two sisters, or of a brother and a sister, may be joined. But canon law by no means permits this, because the children of two brothers or two sisters are in the second degree under canon law, which is wholly forbidden, as is the third and fourth degree; the fifth degree, however, is permitted. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Licetne amitam vel materteram ducere?
units.tr: Is it lawful to marry a paternal aunt or a maternal aunt?

units.la: Item amitam, licet adoptivam, ducere uxorem non licet. Item nec materteram : quia parentum loco habentur.§.item amitam inst.eod.
units.tr: Likewise it is not lawful to marry a paternal aunt, even an adoptive one. Nor is a maternal aunt, since they are held in the place of parents.

units.la: A quibus affinitatis veneratione absti- nendum est?
units.tr: From which relations by marriage must one abstain?

units.la: Affinitatis quoque venerationc, à quarundam nuptiis abstinere necesse est, ut ecce privignam aut nurum uxorem ducere non licet: quia utraque filiae loco sunt.§.affinitatis.inst.eod.
units.tr: One must also abstain from marrying certain relations by marriage: for example, it is not lawful to marry a stepdaughter or a daughter-in-law, since both stand in the place of a daughter.

units.la: A quibus deinde?
units.tr: From which others?

units.la: Socrum quoque & novercam prohibitum est uxorem ducere : quia matris loco sunt.§. Socrum.instit. eod.
units.tr: It is also forbidden to marry a mother-in-law or a stepmother, since they stand in the place of a mother.

units.la: Possuntne mariti filius, ex alia uxore, & uxo- ris filia ex alio marito, vel contrà, contrahere?
units.tr: Can a husband's son by another wife, and a wife's daughter by another husband, or the reverse, contract marriage?

units.la: Mariti filius ex alia uxore, & uxoris filia ex alio marito, vel contrà, matrimonium rectè contrahunt.§. mariti.inst.eod.
units.tr: A husband's son by another wife, and a wife's daughter by another husband, or the reverse, contract marriage validly.

units.la: Nunquid serviles cognationes nuptiis im- pedimento sunt?
units.tr: Do servile kinships impede marriage?

units.la: Illud certum est serviles quoque cognationes nuptiis impedimentum esse: si forte pater, filia, aut frater & soror, manumissi fuerint.§ illud.inst. eod.
units.tr: It is certain that servile kinships also impede marriage, if perhaps a father and daughter, or a brother and sister, have been manumitted.

units.la: Si quis adversus Imperatoris dicta secer- it, quid juris?
units.tr: If anyone acts against the Emperor's words, what is the law?

units.la: Si adversus ea, inquit Imperator, quae diximus, aliqui coierint: nec vir, nec uxor, nec nuptiae, nec matrimonium, nec dos intelligitur.§. si adversus.inst.eod.
units.tr: If, the Emperor says, some have come together contrary to what we have said, then neither husband nor wife is recognised, nor marriage, nor matrimony, nor dowry.

units.la: Quid est Divortium, die Ehescheidung?
units.tr: What is divorce?

units.la: Est legitima separatio mariti & uxoris, cum causae cognitione apud competentem judicem, dictum à diversitate mentium, vel quia in diversas partes eunt, qui[?]distrahunt matrimonium. l. 2. ff. de divortiis.& l. inter divortium.ff.de verb.signif.
units.tr: It is a lawful separation of husband and wife, granted by a competent judge after examination of the cause. It is so called from the difference of minds, or because those who dissolve a marriage go in different directions. See the law 2, Digest, on divorces, and the law "inter divortium", Digest, on the meaning of words.

units.la: Quot sunt causæ Divortii præcipuæ?
units.tr: What are the chief causes of divorce?

units.la: Quatuor : Prima causa divortii est, quando alter conjugum alteri continuis insidiis mortem machinatur, vel quando sceleratus maritus in miseram fœminam supra modum sævit. Nam Imperator Theodosius eleganter inquit : Sicut sine justa causa dissolvi matrimonia justo limite prohibemus : ita adversa necessitate pressum vel pressam, quamvis infausto, attamen necessario auxilio cupimus liberari. l.consensu C.de repudiis. Notandum tamen quòd hoc casu tantùm fiat divortium, quoad mensam & thorum, <bl>zu tisch vnd bett[?]</bl>.
units.tr: There are four. The first cause of divorce is when one spouse continually plots the death of the other by treachery, or when a wicked husband rages beyond measure against a wretched wife. For the Emperor Theodosius says well: just as we forbid marriages to be dissolved without a just cause, so we wish a man or woman oppressed by adverse necessity to be freed, though by an unhappy yet necessary remedy. Note, however, that in this case the divorce is only as to table and bed (from table and bed).

units.la: Secunda causa divortii est, si alter ex conjugibus infidelis fuerit, & noluerit habitare cum fideli, sed discesserit, hoc casu fideli, etiam vivente infideli, permissum est contrahere matrimonium cum alio. 1. Corinth. 7.
units.tr: The second cause of divorce is when one of the spouses is an unbeliever and is unwilling to live with a believer but departs. In this case the believer, even while the unbeliever is still alive, is permitted to contract marriage with another. 1 Corinthians 7.

units.la: Tertia causa divortii est, impotentia naturalis & accidentalis perpetua, & conceditur personæ, quæ habet naturæ integras vires, ut etiam vivente altera impotente, possit contrahere cum alia. Vide Schneidevvinum, & Kling. in tractatu matrimonial. caufar.
units.tr: The third cause of divorce is natural or accidental impotence that is perpetual. It is granted to the person who has the full powers of nature, so that even while the other is impotent he or she may contract marriage with another. See Schneidewin, and Kling in the treatise on matrimonial causes.

units.la: Quarta causa est adulterium, propter quod tam de jure Divino, quam civili & canonico matrimonium dissolvitur. Et innocenti licitum esse ducere aliam, viventeadhuc adultera, probat Schneidevvinus.
units.tr: The fourth cause is adultery, on account of which a marriage is dissolved by divine law as well as by civil and canon law. And Schneidewin proves that it is lawful for an innocent party to take another spouse while the adulterer is still alive.

units.la: Quid est legitimatio, die Ehelichmachung .
units.tr: What is legitimation?

units.la: Est restitutio natalium, qua is, qui ex illicito coitu natus est, efficitur legitimus. Tribus autem modis quis legitimatur:
units.tr: It is the restoration of birth rights, by which one who was born from an unlawful union is made legitimate. A person is legitimated in three ways:

units.la: Primò per oblationem curiæ, quando filius illegitimè natus, datur vel Imperatori, vel civitati, ut illi serviens efficiatur legitimus : atque ita legitimatus patri mortuo succedit, tam ex testamento, quàm ab intestato, cum aliis liberis legitimis, non autem aliis ascendentibus vel collateralibus. Cap.3.Auth.quibus modis naturales efficiuntur sui.
units.tr: First, by presentation to the curia, when an illegitimately born son is given either to the Emperor or to the city, so that by serving it he becomes legitimate. Thus legitimated, he succeeds his deceased father, both by will and without a will, together with the other legitimate children, but not with other ascendants or collateral relatives. Cap. 3, Authentica, "By what means natural children become their own (heirs)".

units.la: Secundò per rescriptum principis, quando Imperator, vel alius ejus nomine, illegitimum naturali ingenuitati restituit, ut deinceps pro legitimo habeatur: atque ita legitimatus, tum demum succedit patri, quando non extant naturales & legitimi simul. Nam suis existentibus, deinde naturalibus procreatis, aut primitùs natis, nequaquam legitimorum jus eis adjicitur. cap.2.in fine Auth. quibus modis naturales efficiantur legitimi & sui.
units.tr: Second, by the rescript of a prince, when the Emperor, or another in his name, restores an illegitimate child to natural freeborn status, so that thereafter he is held as legitimate. Thus legitimated, he succeeds his father only when there are no natural and legitimate children together. For when legitimate children exist, and natural children are afterwards begotten or were born earlier, no right of legitimate children is added to them. Cap. 2, at the end of the Authentica, "By what means natural children become legitimate and their own (heirs)".

units.la: Tertiò per subsequens matrimonium, cùm quis ducit concubinam suam, etiam in extremo vitæ articulo constitutus: tum liberi antea nati, ob honorem matrimonii subsequentis legitimantur non tantùm quo ad quædam, sed quoad omnia, etiamsi nulla insuper copula carnalis accesserit: quia matrimonium omnia præcedentia purgat. Vide libellum, qui inscribitur Analysis Dialectica quatuor librorum. Institut. In quo dicitur quòd legitimatus per subsequens matrimonium possit eligi in Episcopum, & succedere patri defuncto in bonis allodialibus & feudalibus, <bl>daß</bl> <bl>er mag den verstorbenen[?] vatter erben / an erbfrey gü-</bl> <bl>tern/vndlehen gütern.</bl>
units.tr: Third, by a subsequent marriage, when a man takes his concubine as wife, even when he is at the point of death. Then the children born earlier are legitimated, on account of the honour of the later marriage, not only in some respects but in all, even if no carnal union has followed; for marriage cleanses everything that went before. See the little book entitled "Dialectical Analysis of the Four Books of the Institutes", in which it is said that one legitimated by a subsequent marriage may be elected bishop, and may inherit from his deceased father in allodial and feudal estates.

units.la: QUIS EST UNDECIMUS Titulus? De adoptionibus. Von Kindtschafften/oder annemmungen an kindes statt.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE ELEVENTH TITLE? On adoptions. On children's relationships, or adoptions in place of children.

units.la: Qui deinde sunt in potestate patris?
units.tr: Who are then in the power of the father?

units.la: NON solum naturales liberi, secundum ea quæ diximus, in potestate nostra sunt, verum etiam ii quos adoptamus. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Not only natural children, as we have said, are in our power, but also those whom we adopt.

units.la: Quot modis fit Adoptio?
units.tr: In how many ways is adoption made?

units.la: Adoptio duobus modis fit, aut principali rescripto, quæ dicitur arrogatio, aut imperio magistratus, quæ proprie est Adoptio. §.adoptio.inst.eod.
units.tr: Adoption is made in two ways: either by an imperial rescript, which is called arrogation, or by the command of the magistrate, which is properly adoption.

units.la: Súntne hodie adoptivi liberi in potestate patris adoptivi?
units.tr: Are adopted children today in the power of the adoptive father?

units.la: Hodie, inquit Imperator, ex nostra Constitutione, cùm filiusfamilias a patre naturali extraneæ personæ in adoptionem datur: jura patris naturalis minimè dissolvuntur, nec quicquam ad patrem adoptivum transit, nec in potestate ejus est, licet ab intestato jura successionis ei à nobis tributa sint: si verò pater naturalis non extraneo, sed avo & proavo filium suum dederit in adoptionem, manet stabile jus patris adoptivi. §.Sed hodie.inst.eod.
units.tr: Today, says the Emperor, under our constitution, when a son under paternal power is given in adoption by his natural father to a stranger, the rights of the natural father are by no means dissolved, nothing passes to the adoptive father, and the son is not in his power, although we have granted him rights of succession on intestacy. But if the natural father has given his son in adoption not to a stranger but to a grandfather or great-grandfather, the rights of the adoptive father remain firm.

units.la: Quid exquiritur si impubes arrogatur?
units.tr: What is inquired into if an impubescent child is adrogated?

units.la: Cùm impubes per principale rescriptum arrogatur, causa cognita, arrogatio fieri permittitur, & exquiritur causa adrogationis an honesta sit expediatq; pupillo. §. cùm autem. inst.eod.
units.tr: When a minor is adrogated by imperial rescript, adrogation is permitted only after the cause has been examined, and it is inquired whether the reason for the adrogation is honourable and advantageous to the ward.

units.la: Quot annis oportet patrem adoptantem, filium præcedere?
units.tr: How many years must the adopting father be ahead of the son?

units.la: Debet is, qui sibi filium per Adoptionem vel arrogationem facit, plena pubertate, id est, decem & octo annis præcedere. §.minorem.inst.eod.
units.tr: One who makes a son for himself by adoption or arrogation must precede him by full puberty, that is, by eighteen years.

units.la: In cujus locum adoptare possumus?
units.tr: In whose place may we adopt?

units.la: Licet in locum nepotis vel neptis, pronepotis vel proneptis, vel deinceps adoptare, quamvis filium quis non habeat. §.licet. inst.eod.
units.tr: One may adopt in place of a grandson or granddaughter, a great-grandson or great-granddaughter, or further down the line, even if one has no son.

units.la: Possúntne Spadones & Castrati adoptare?
units.tr: Can eunuchs (spadones) and castrati adopt?

units.la: Illud utriusque adoptionis commune est, quòd & ii, qui generare non possunt quales sunt Spadones, <bl>(Unfruchtbare)</bl> adoptare possunt: castrati autem, <bl>(Verschnittene)</bl> non possunt. §. sed & illud.inst.eod.
units.tr: It is common to both kinds of adoption that those who cannot beget children, such as spadones (the infertile), can adopt; castrati, however, cannot.

units.la: Quod
units.tr: That

units.la: Quot est proprium Arrogationis?
units.tr: What is peculiar to arrogation?

units.la: Is qui liberos in potestate habet, si se adrogandum dederit, non solum ipse potestati adrogatoris subjicitur, sed etiam liberi ejus in ejusdem fiunt potestate, tanquam nepotes. §. illud proprium. instit. cod.
units.tr: If a man who has children in his power gives himself to be adrogated, he himself is not only made subject to the power of the adrogator, but his children also fall under the same power, as grandchildren.

units.la: Possuntne & servi Adoptari?
units.tr: Can slaves also be adopted?

units.la: Quem Dominus filium suum nominaverit, liberum esse constituimus: licet hoc ad jus filii accipiendum non sufficiat, § final. instit. cod.
units.tr: We decree that whom a master has named as his son is free, although this does not suffice to receive the right of a son.

units.la: QUIS EST DUODECIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWELFTH TITLE?

units.la: Quibus modis jus patriæ potestatis solvitur. Auff was weise das Recht Vätterlicher gewalt auffgelö- set wird. Recita modos solvendæ patriæ potestatis.
units.tr: By what modes the right of paternal power is dissolved. (By what way the right of paternal power is dissolved.) Recite the modes of dissolving paternal power.

units.la: PRimò,hi qui in potestate patris sunt, mortuo eo sui juris fiunt. in princ. instit. cod.
units.tr: First, those who are in the power of a father become their own masters (sui juris) when he dies. Inst. 1.12 pr.

units.la: Secundò, cùm is qui ob aliquod maleficium in insulam deportatur, civitatem amittit: sequitur,ut qui eo modo ex numero civium Romanorum tollitur, perinde quasi eo mortuo, desinant liberi in potestate ejus esse. §. cum autem is. instit. cod.
units.tr: Second, when a person who is banished to an island for some crime loses citizenship, it follows that those who are removed in that way from the number of Roman citizens are treated just as if he had died, and their children cease to be in his power. Inst. 1.12 §. cum autem is.

units.la: Tertiò, poenæ servus effectus filios in potestate habere definit. Servi autem poenæ efficiuntur, qui in metallum damnantur, & qui bestiis subjiciuntur. §. poenæ servus. instit. cod.
units.tr: Third, a son ceases to be in his father's power when the father is made a slave as a punishment. Those become slaves as a punishment who are condemned to the mines and who are given over to the beasts. Inst. 1.12 §. poenae servus.

units.la: Quartò,summa patriciatus dignitas, <bl>die hohe wir-</bl> <bl>digkeit des standes Keyserlicher Rhäte</bl> / illicò Imperialibus codicillis præstitis, filium à patria potestate liberat. §. Sed ex Constitut. instit. cod. Quintò, Emancipatione quoque, <bl>durch loßgebung</bl> <bl>auß Väterlicher gewalt</bl>, desinunt liberi in potestate parentum esse. §. praeterea. inst. eod.
units.tr: Fourth, the highest dignity of patrician rank, once the imperial codicils have been granted, frees a son from paternal power at once (the dignity of the rank of the Imperial Councillors). Inst. 1.12 §. Sed ex Constitut. Fifth, children also cease to be in the power of their parents through emancipation (release from paternal power). Inst. 1.12 §. praeterea.

units.la: Sextò, si pater filium, quem in potestate habet, avo vel proavo naturali in adoptionem dederit, solvitur quidem jus potestatis patris naturalis: transit autem in hujusmodi patrem adoptivum. §. sed & si. inst. eod.
units.tr: Sixth, if a father gives a son who is in his power in adoption to a natural grandfather or great-grandfather, the right of power of the natural father is indeed dissolved, but it passes to such a father by adoption. Inst. 1.12 §. sed & si.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS tertius Titulus?
units.tr: What is the thirteenth title?

units.la: De tutelis. <bl>Von Vormundschafften.</bl>
units.tr: On guardianships. <bl>Of Vormundschafften.</bl>

units.la: Quæ est alia personarum divisio?
units.tr: What is the other division of persons?

units.la: EX his personis, quæ in potestate non sunt, quædam vel in tutela sunt, vel curatione, quædam neutro jure tenentur. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Of those persons who are not under power, some are either under guardianship or under curatorship, and some are held by neither right. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid est Tutela?
units.tr: What is guardianship?

units.la: Tutela est, ut Servius definivit, vis ac potestas in capite libero ad tuendum eum, qui propter ætatem se defendere nequit, jure civili data & permissa. §. est autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: Guardianship is, as Servius defined it, the power and authority over a free head, given and permitted by civil law, for protecting one who cannot defend himself because of his age. Institutes, same title, section "est autem".

units.la: Quinam sunt Tutores?
units.tr: Who are guardians?

units.la: Qui eam vim ac potestatem habent. §. tutores. instit. eod.
units.tr: Those who hold that power and authority. Institutes, same title, section "tutores".

units.la: Quinam possunt tutores in testamen- to dare?
units.tr: Who may appoint guardians by will?

units.la: Permissum est parentibus, liberis impuberibus, quos in potestate habent, testamento tutores dare §. permissum inst. eod.
units.tr: It is permitted for parents to appoint guardians by will for their children who are under age and whom they hold in power. Institutes, same title, section "permissum".

units.la: Possuntne parentes posthumis tuto- res dare?
units.tr: Can parents appoint guardians for posthumous children?

units.la: Placuit non minus posthumis, quàm jam natis testamento tutores dari posse. §. cum autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: It has been settled that guardians may be appointed by will for posthumous children no less than for those already born. Institutes, same title, section "cum autem".

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS quartus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the fourteenth title?

units.la: Qui testamento tutores dari possunt. <bl>Welche im Testament zu Vormündern</bl> <bl>mögen gesetzt werden.</bl>
units.tr: Which persons may be appointed guardians in a will.

units.la: Quis potest in testamento tutor dari?
units.tr: Who can be appointed guardian in a will?

units.la: DAri tutor potest testamento, non solum paterfamiliâs, sed etiam filiusfamiliâs. Sed & servus proprius cum libertate testamento rectè tutor dari potest. in princip.inst.eod.
units.tr: A guardian can be appointed by will, not only for a head of household but also for a son under his father's authority. But a slave who belongs to the testator can also validly be appointed guardian by will, together with his freedom. At the beginning of the same title in the Institutes.

units.la: Potestne servus alienus tutor dari?
units.tr: Can another person's slave be appointed guardian?

units.la: Servus alienus purè inutiliter testamento datur tutor: sed ita, cùm liber erit, utiliter datur. §. sed & servus. inst. eod.
units.tr: Another person's slave is appointed guardian by will to no effect if the appointment is unconditional, but if it is made on the condition that he will be free, it takes effect. In the paragraph "but also a slave," in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: Potestne furiosus & minor viginti quinq; annis tutor dari?
units.tr: Can a madman, or someone under twenty-five years old, be appointed guardian?

units.la: Furiosus vel minor viginti quinq; annis, tutor testamento datus, tutor tunc erit cùm compos mentis, aut major viginti quinque annis fuerit factus. §. furiosus. inst. eod
units.tr: A madman, or someone under twenty-five, appointed guardian by will, will be guardian only when he is of sound mind or has become twenty-five years old. In the paragraph "madman," in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: Qualiter tutor in testamento datur?
units.tr: In what manner is a guardian appointed in a will?

units.la: Ad certum tempus, vel ex certo tempore, vel sub conditione, vel ante hæredis institutionem, posse dari tutorem non dubitatur. Certæ autem rei vel causæ tutor dari non potest: quia personæ non causæ vel rei tutor datur. §. ad certum. inst. eod.
units.tr: It is not doubted that a guardian may be appointed for a certain time, from a certain time, under a condition, or before the institution of the heir. But a guardian cannot be appointed for a certain matter or cause, because a guardian is appointed for a person, not for a cause or matter. In the paragraph "for a certain time," in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS quintus Titulus?
units.tr: Which is the fifth title of the tenth book?

units.la: De legitima Agnatorum tutela. <bl>Von</bl> <bl>rechtmässiger vormundtschafft der</bl> <bl>schwertmagen.</bl>
units.tr: On the legitimate guardianship of agnates. Of legitimate guardianship by the sword-kin.

units.la: Qui dantur tutores, si in testamento nul- lus datus est?
units.tr: Who are appointed as guardians if no one has been appointed in a will?

units.la: QUibus testamento tutor datus non est: his ex lege duodecim tabularum Agnati sunt tutores, qui vocantur legitimi, in princ. inst.cod.
units.tr: Those for whom no guardian has been appointed in a will have, by the law of the Twelve Tables, agnates as their guardians; these are called legitimate guardians. Inst. cod., at the beginning.

units.la: Sunt autem Agnati cognati per virilis sexus cognationem conjuncti, qui idem gentilitatis nomen, eandem familiam, & easdē imagines seu insignia habēt. <bl>Die eines geschlechts nammen/ einerlei stam/vnd ei-</bl> <bl>nerlei schildt oder helm haben:</bl> Cognati, spilmagen/ sunt qui per fœminini sexus personas cognatione junguntur. §. sunt autem. inst.cod.
units.tr: Agnates, however, are cognates joined through kinship on the male side, who share the same name of the clan, the same family, and the same images or insignia: those of one family name, one stock, and one shield or helmet. Cognates, or spear-kin, are those joined by kinship through persons of the female sex. Inst. cod., §. sunt autem.

units.la: Quomodo agnati impediuntur, ne tutores esse possint?
units.tr: How are agnates prevented from being guardians?

units.la: Agnationis jus omnibus modis capitis Deminutione plærunque perimitur: Nam Agnatio juris civilis nomen est: Cognationis verò jus non omnibus modis commutatur. Unde, etsi lex civilis hoc agit, ut quis nomen & jus familiæ perdat, & ut non sit adgnatus: non tamen potest facere, ut non sit filius ejus ex quo naturaliter progenitus est: Quia civilis ratio civilia quidem jura corrumpere potest: naturalia verò non utiq;. §. final. inst. cod.
units.tr: The right of agnation is in nearly every case destroyed by a diminution of civil status, for agnation is a term of civil law, whereas the right of cognation is not altered in every way. Hence, although civil law brings it about that someone loses his name and his family right and ceases to be an agnate, it cannot make him not the son of the one by whom he was naturally begotten, because civil reason can indeed corrupt civil rights, but not natural ones. Inst. cod., §. final.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS sextus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the sixteenth title?

units.la: De capitis deminutione. Von ständes veränderung. Quid est Capitis deminutio?
units.tr: On diminution of status. What is capitis deminutio? On change of status.

units.la: CApitis Deminutio est status mutatio: Eaq; tribus modis accidit. Nam aut maxima est capitis Deminutio, aut Minor, quam quidam mediam vocant, aut minima. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: Diminution of status is a change of status, and it occurs in three ways. For it is either the greatest diminution, or a lesser one, which some call the middle diminution, or the least. in princ. inst. cod.

units.la: Quid est maxima capitis Deminutio?
units.tr: What is the greatest diminution of status?

units.la: Cùm aliquis simul & civitatem & libertatem amittit, quod accidit in his, qui servi poenæ efficiuntur atrocitate sententiæ.§.maxima.inst.eod.
units.tr: When someone loses both citizenship and liberty at once. This happens to those who become slaves of punishment through the severity of a sentence. §. maxima. inst. eod.

units.la: Quid est minor sive media capitis De- minutio?
units.tr: What is the lesser, or middle, diminution of status?

units.la: Cùm civitas quidem amittitur, libertas verò retinetur: quod accidit ei, cui aqua & igni interdictum fuerit, <bl>der in die acht gethan wirð</bl>: vel ei qui in Insulam deportatus est, <bl>der in ein Insel verweist ist</bl>. §. minor.ind.eod.
units.tr: When citizenship is lost but liberty is kept. This happens to one who has been placed under the ban of fire and water (who is put under the ban), or to one who has been deported to an island (who is banished to an island). §. minor. inst. eod.

units.la: Quid est minima capitis Deminutio?
units.tr: What is the least diminution of status?

units.la: Cùm civitas retinetur & libertas, sed status hominis commutatur: quod accidit in his, qui cùm sui juris fuerint, coeperunt alieno juri subjecti esse, vel contrà. Veluti si filiusfamilias à parte emancipatus fuerit, est capite deminutus.§ minima.inst.eod.
units.tr: When citizenship and liberty are kept, but the person's status is changed. This happens to those who, having been sui iuris, have begun to be subject to another's authority, or the reverse. For example, if a son under his father's authority is emancipated, he has suffered a diminution of status. §. minima. inst. eod.

units.la: Quomodo perit jus Cognationis?
units.tr: How is the right of kinship lost?

units.la: Si minima capitis Deminutio interveniat, manet cognatio: si maxima capitis Deminutio interveniat: jus cognationis perit, ut puta servitute alicujus cognati.§.quod autem.inst.eod.
units.tr: If the least diminution of status occurs, kinship remains; if the greatest diminution of status occurs, the right of kinship is lost, as for instance by the enslavement of a kinsman. §. quod autem. inst. eod.

units.la: Ad quos Agnatos tutela pertinet?
units.tr: To which agnates does guardianship belong?

units.la: Non simul ad omnes pertinet, sed ad eos tantùm qui sunt proximiores gradu: vel si plures ejusdem gradus sunt, ad omnes pertinet.§ final.inst.eod.
units.tr: It does not belong to all of them together, but only to those who are nearer in degree; or, if several are of the same degree, it belongs to all of them. §. final. inst. eod.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS s- eptimus Titulus? De legitima patronorum tutela. Von Rechtmässiger vormundtschaffe der schutzvätter.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TENTH, seventh Title? On the lawful guardianship of patrons. Of the lawful guardianship of the patron-fathers.

units.la: Quot sunt libertorum & libertarum tutores?
units.tr: How many guardians do freedmen and freedwomen have?

units.la: EX lege duodecim tabularum, libertorum & libertarum tutela ad patronos liberosque eorum pertinet, quae & ipsa legitima tutela vocatur: quia hereditates libertorum libertarumq; si intestati decesserint, jusserat lex ad patronos, liberosq; eorum pertinere. Quos igitur ad hereditatem Lex vocat, eosdem etiam tutores esse jussit: quia plærunq; ubi successionis est emolumentum, ibi & tutelae onus esse debet. §. eo enim. inst. cod.
units.tr: By the law of the Twelve Tables, the guardianship of freedmen and freedwomen belongs to their patrons and the patrons' children, and it is also called legitimate guardianship. The law had ordained that if freedmen and freedwomen died intestate, their estates pass to the patrons and their children. Therefore the law also ordained that those whom it calls to the inheritance should be their guardians, since generally where there is the advantage of succession, there the burden of guardianship ought to be as well. §. eo enim. inst. cod.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS octavus Titulus? De legitima parentum tutela. <bl>Von recht-</bl> <bl>mäßiger vormündtschafft der Eltern.</bl>
units.tr: What is the eighteenth title? On the lawful guardianship of parents.

units.la: Qui sunt Emancipatorum tutores?
units.tr: Who are the guardians of the emancipated?

units.la: SI quis filium aut filiam, aut nepotem aut neptem ex filio & deinceps, impuberes emancipaverit: legitimus eorum tutor est, inst.cod.
units.tr: If anyone has emancipated a son or daughter, or a grandson or granddaughter through a son or further down the line, while they are still below puberty, he is their legitimate guardian (inst.cod.).

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS nonus Titulus? De fiduciaria tutela. <bl>Von treuhelflicher[?] vormundtschafft.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE NINETEENTH TITLE? On fiduciary guardianship. <bl>On guardianship by a trustee[?] (treuhelflich).</bl>

units.la: Qui sunt Emancipatorum tutores, defun- ctis parentibus?
units.tr: Who are the guardians of emancipated persons once the parents have died?

units.la: SI pater filium vel filiam, nepotem vel neptem & deinceps, impuberes manumiserit: legitimam nanciscitur eorum tutelam: quo defuncto si liberi ejus virilis sexus exi-stant: fiduciarij tutores, vel fratris vel sororis efficiuntur. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: If a father has emancipated (manumitted) a son or daughter, a grandson or granddaughter, and so on down the line, who are below puberty, he acquires their legitimate guardianship. When he dies, if his children of male sex are still living, they become fiduciary guardians, either of the brother or of the sister. At the beginning of the Institutes, in the Code.

units.la: Qua ætate omnes tutores vel curatores vocentur?
units.tr: At what age are all guardians or curators to be called?

units.la: Qui ad tutelam vocantur, perfectæ sint ætatis, id est, majores viginti quinq; annis, quod nostra constitutio in omnibus tutelis & curationibus observari generaliter præcepit, inquit Imperator. §. final. institut.eod.
units.tr: Those who are called to guardianship must be of full age, that is, over twenty-five years old, which our constitution has generally commanded to be observed in all guardianships and curatorships, says the Emperor, at the final section of the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: What is the twentieth title?

units.la: De Attiliano tutore, & eo qui ex lege Iulia & Titia dabatur. <bl>Vom Vormünder der vom Attilio und</bl> <bl>dem gesetz Iulia und Titia gegeben ward.</bl>
units.tr: Concerning the guardian appointed by the Attilian law, and the one given under the Julian and Titian laws.

units.la: Si cui nullus tutor datus fuerat, quomodo ei consulebatur?
units.tr: If someone had been given no guardian, how was provision made for him?

units.la: Si cui nullus omninò tutor fuerat: ei dabatur in urbe quidem à prætore Urbano, & majore parte Tribunorum plebis tutor ex lege Attilia: in provinciis verò à præsidibus provinciarum ex lege Julia & Titia.in princ.instit.eod.
units.tr: If someone had no guardian at all, then in the city a guardian was given by the urban praetor and by the majority of the tribunes of the plebs under the Attilian law; but in the provinces, by the governors of the provinces under the Julian and Titian laws.

units.la: Si in testamento tutor sub conditione, aut purè aut ex die certo datus fuerat, unde interim tutor petebatur?
units.tr: If a guardian had been given in a will, either under a condition or outright, or from a certain day, whence was a guardian sought in the meantime?

units.la: Si in testamento tutor sub conditione, aut ex die certo datus fuerat: quam diu conditio aut dies pendebat, ex eisdem legibus tutor dari poterat. §. sed & si. inst. eod.
units.tr: If a guardian had been given in a will under a condition, or from a certain day, then for as long as the condition or the day was pending, a guardian could be given under the same laws.

units.la: Quando desiit id fieri?
units.tr: When did this cease to be done?

units.la: Ex his legibus tutores pupillis desierunt dari, posteaquam primo Consules pupillis utriusq; sexus tutores ex inquisitione dare coeperunt, deinde praetores ex constitutionibus. §. sed ex his. inst. cod.
units.tr: These laws ceased to give guardians to wards after the consuls first began to give guardians to wards of either sex after inquiry, and then the praetors began to do so by constitutions.

units.la: Quomodo hodie creantur tutores vel curatores?
units.tr: How are guardians or curators appointed today?

units.la: Nos disposuimus, inquit Imperator, si facultates pupilli vel adulti usq; ad quingetos solidos valeant, <bl>auff fünff hundert gülden sich erstrecken</bl>/ defensores civitatum, una cum ejusdem civitatis religiosissimo Antistite, vel alias publicas personas, id est, magistratus vel juridicum Alexandrinae civitatis, tutores vel curatores creare. §. Nos autem. inst. cod.
units.tr: "We have ordained," says the Emperor, "that if the property of a ward or minor amounts to as much as five hundred solidi, the defenders of the cities, together with the most religious bishop of the same city, or other public persons, that is, the magistrates or the judicial officer of the city of Alexandria, shall appoint guardians or curators."

units.la: Quando rationem reddunt tutores?
units.tr: When do guardians render account?

units.la: Quum pupillorum, pupillarumq; tutores negotia gerant: post pubertatem tutelae judicio rationem reddunt. §. final. inst. cod.
units.tr: Since guardians conduct the affairs of wards, male and female, they render account after puberty by the judgment of guardianship.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS primus Titulus? De authoritate Tutorum. <bl>Von der Vormündergewalt.</bl>
units.tr: Which is the twenty-first title? On the authority of guardians. <bl>On the power of guardians.</bl>

units.la: Quando Tutoris authoritas est necessaria?
units.tr: When is the guardian's authority necessary?

units.la: SI aliis promittant pupilli, necessaria est Tutoris authoritas. Namque placuit meliorem quidem conditionem licere eis facere, etiam sine Tutoris authoritate: deteriorem vero non aliter, quàm cum tutoris authoritate. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: If pupils make promises to others, the authority of the guardian is necessary. For it has been settled that they may do what is in their better interest even without the guardian's authority, but what is to their disadvantage they may do only with the guardian's authority.

units.la: Possúntne pupilli hæreditatem adire?
units.tr: Can pupils enter upon an inheritance?

units.la: Neq; hæreditatem adire, neq; bonorum possessionem petere, neq; hæreditatem ex fideicommisso suscipere aliter possunt, nisi tutoris authoritate, quanvis illis lucrosa sit, ne ullum damnum habeant.§.neque tamen.inst.cod.
units.tr: Pupils cannot enter upon an inheritance, seek possession of goods, or take up an inheritance by trust-bequest, except with the authority of the guardian, even though the transaction is profitable to them, so that they suffer no loss.

units.la: QVIS EST VICESIMVS secundus Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTY-SECOND TITLE?

units.la: Quibus modis tutela finitur. Auff was weise sich die vormündt-schafft endet. Recita modos tutelæ finiendæ.
units.tr: By what means guardianship is ended. Recite the ways in which guardianship is ended. (In what manner guardianship comes to an end.)

units.la: Primo, pupilli pupillæq; cum puberes esse coeperint, a tutela liberantur: masculi quidem post decimum quartum annum completum : fœminæ vero post duodecim annos completos. in princip.instit.eod.
units.tr: First, wards, both boys and girls, are released from guardianship once they have begun to reach puberty: boys after completing their fourteenth year, and girls after completing their twelfth year. In princip. Inst. eod.

units.la: Secundò, finitur tutela, si adrogati sint adhuc impuberes vel deportati.§.item.inst.eod.
units.tr: Second, guardianship ends if the ward is adrogated while still under puberty, or is deported. §. item. Inst. eod.

units.la: Tertiò, si in servitutem pupillus redigatur. dicto §.item.
units.tr: Third, if the ward is reduced into slavery. Said §. item.

units.la: Quartò, si ab hostibus captus fuerit. dict.§. item.
units.tr: Fourth, if the ward is taken captive by enemies. Said §. item.

units.la: Quintò, si usque ad certam conditionem datus sit tutor testamento: æque evenit, ut desinat esse tutor existente conditione.§.sed & si.inst.eod.
units.tr: Fifth, if a guardian has been appointed by will only until a certain condition: it likewise follows that he ceases to be guardian once the condition has occurred. §. sed & si. Inst. eod.

units.la: Sextò, finitur tutela morte vel pupillorum vel tutorum.§.simili.inst.eod.
units.tr: Sixth, guardianship ends by the death of either the wards or the guardians. §. simili. Inst. eod.

units.la: Septimò, capitis deminutione tutoris, per quam libertas vel civitas amittitur, omnis tutela perit.§. sed & capitis.inst.eod.
units.tr: Seventh, by the diminution of the guardian's status (capitis deminutio), through which liberty or citizenship is lost; every guardianship then perishes. §. sed & capitis. Inst. eod.

units.la: Octavo, pupilli & pupillæ capitis deminutio, licet minima sit, omnes tutelas tollit. d.§. sed &. instit.eod.
units.tr: Eighth, the diminution of status of a ward, male or female, however slight it may be, cancels all guardianships. Said §. sed &. Inst. eod.

units.la: Nonò, qui ad certum tempus testamento dantur tutores, finito eo deponunt tutelam.§. præterea. in-stit. eod. Decimò, desinunt tutores esse, qui removentur à tutela ob id, quod suspecti visi sunt. §. desinunt. instit.eod.
units.tr: Ninth, guardians who are appointed by will for a fixed time lay down the guardianship when that time has expired. §. præterea. Inst. eod. Tenth, those guardians cease to be guardians who are removed from guardianship because they have been regarded as suspect. §. desinunt. Inst. eod.

units.la: Undecimò, desinunt tutores esse, qui ex justa causa sese excusant, & onus administrandæ tutelæ deponunt. d. §. desinunt. inst. eod.
units.tr: Eleventh, guardians cease to be guardians who excuse themselves for a just cause and lay down the burden of administering the guardianship. Said §. desinunt. Inst. eod.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS tertius Titulus? De curatoribus. Von sorgtragern.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE twenty-third Title? Concerning curators. Of caretakers (curators).

units.la: Quinam accipiunt curatores?
units.tr: Who receive curators?

units.la: Masculi quidem puberes, & fœminæ viripotentes, usq; ad vicesimum quintum annum completum curatores accipiunt: quia licet puberes sint, adhuc tamen ejus ætatis sunt, ut sua negotia tueri non possint. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Boys who have reached puberty and girls who are capable of marriage receive curators until they have completed their twenty-fifth year. Although they are of puberty, they are still of an age at which they cannot look after their own affairs. In princ. Inst. eod.

units.la: Inviti adolescentes, curatores non accipiunt, præterquam in litem. §. item inviti. inst. eod.
units.tr: Unwilling adolescents do not receive curators, except in a lawsuit. §. item inviti. Inst. eod.

units.la: Furiosi quoque & prodigi, licèt majores viginti quinq; annis sint: tamen in curatione sunt agnatorum ex lege duodecim tabularum. §. furiosi inst. eod.
units.tr: Madmen and spendthrifts too, even if they are over twenty-five years old, are nonetheless under the curatorship of their agnates by the law of the Twelve Tables. §. furiosi. Inst. eod.

units.la: Et mente captis, surdis, & mutis, & qui perpetuò morbo laborant, quia rebus suis superesse non possunt, curatores dandi sunt. §. sed &. inst. eod.
units.tr: Those who are deprived of their mind, the deaf and the mute, and those who suffer from a constant sickness, must be given curators, because they cannot manage their own affairs. §. sed &. Inst. eod.

units.la: Interdum pupilli curatores accipiunt, ut puta si legitimus tutor non sit idoneus: quoniam habenti tutorem, tutor dari non potest. §. interdum. inst. eod.
units.tr: Sometimes wards receive curators, for instance if the lawful guardian is not fit; since a tutor cannot be given to someone who already has a guardian. §. interdum. Inst. eod.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS quartus Titulus? De satisdatione tutorum vel curatorum. Von bürgschafft der vormünder oder sorgtrager.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE twenty-fourth Title? Concerning the security given by guardians or curators. Concerning the surety of guardians or caretakers.

units.la: Nunquid tutores vel curatores satis- dare coguntur?
units.tr: Are guardians or curators compelled to give security?

units.la: NE pupillorum pupillarúmve negotia à curatoribus tutoribúsve consumantur vel diminuantur: curet prætor ut & tutores & curatores eo nomine satisdent. Sed hoc non est perpetuum: Nam tutores testamento dati, satisdare non coguntur. in prin. inst.eod.
units.tr: Lest the affairs of wards or minors be consumed or diminished by their curators or guardians, the praetor takes care that both guardians and curators give security for this purpose. But this is not universal: for guardians appointed by will are not compelled to give security. In prin. Inst. eod.

units.la: Si plures sint ex testamento vel inquisitio- ne dati, potestne unus administrare?
units.tr: If several have been appointed, by will or by inquiry, can one of them administer alone?

units.la: Si ex testamento vel inquisitione duo pluresve dati fuerint: potest unus offerre satisdationem de indemnitate pupilli vel adolescentis, & contutori suo vel concuratori præferri, ut solus administret: vel ut contutor aut concurator satisofferens præponatur ei, ut & ipse solus administret. §. sed si ex testamento. inst.eod.
units.tr: If two or more have been appointed by will or by inquiry, one of them may offer security for the indemnity of the ward or adolescent, and be preferred to his co-guardian or co-curator, so that he alone administers; or else a co-guardian or co-curator who offers security may be put before him, so that he alone administers. §. sed si ex testamento. Inst. eod.

units.la: Qui tenentur pupillis & adultis cæterisque personis ex administra- tione?
units.tr: Who are bound to wards, adults and other persons by administration?

units.la: Sciendum est, non solum tutores vel curatores pupillis vel adultis, cæterisque personis ex administratione rerum teneri: sed etiam in eos, qui satisdationem accipiunt, subsidiariam actionem esse, quæ ultimum eis præsidium possit adferre. §. sciendum. inst.eod.
units.tr: It must be known that not only guardians or curators are bound to wards, adults and other persons by the administration of property, but also that there is a subsidiary action against those who take the security, which can bring them a last resort. §. sciendum. Inst. eod.

units.la: Qui tenentur hac actione?
units.tr: Who are bound by this action?

units.la: Neq; præfectus urbi, neq; prætor, neq; præses provinciæ, neque quisquam alius, cui tutores dandi jus est, hac actione tenebitur: sed hi tantummodò, qui satisdationem exigere solent. §. final. instit. eod.
units.tr: Neither the prefect of the city, nor the praetor, nor the governor of a province, nor anyone else who has the right to appoint guardians, will be bound by this action; but only those who are accustomed to demand the security. §. final. Inst. eod.

units.la: QVIS EST VICESIMVS quintus Titulus? De excusationibus tutorum vel curato- rum. <bl>Von entschuldigung der</bl> <bl>vormünder und sorg-</bl> <bl>trager.</bl>
units.tr: The twenty-fifth title: On the excuses of guardians or curators. (On excusing guardians and curators.)

units.la: Ex quibus causis excusantur Tutores vel Curatores?
units.tr: From what causes are guardians or curators excused?

units.la: PRimò, propter liberos sive in potestate sint, sive emancipati. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: First, on account of children, whether they are under power or emancipated. Inst. at the beginning, same title.

units.la: Secundò, Divus Marcus in semestribus rescripsit, eum qui res fici[?] administrat, à tutela vel cura, quandiu administrat, excusari posse. §. ite divus. inst. eod.
units.tr: Second, the divine Marcus, in his semester rescripts, ruled that one who administers the property of the treasury may be excused from guardianship or curatorship for as long as he administers it. Inst., §"Ite divus", same title.

units.la: Tertiò, qui Reipublicæ causa absunt, à tutela vel cura excusantur. §. item qui. inst. eod.
units.tr: Third, those who are absent on the public business of the commonwealth are excused from guardianship or curatorship. Inst., §"Item qui", same title.

units.la: Quarto, qui potestatem aliquam habent (ut Consules & Prætores) se excusare possunt, sed susceptam tutelam deserere[?] non possunt. §. & qui. inst. eod.
units.tr: Fourth, those who hold some public office (such as consuls and praetors) may excuse themselves, but they cannot abandon a guardianship once they have undertaken it. Inst., §"Et qui", same title.

units.la: Quintò, propter litem, quam cum pupillo vel adulto tutor vel curator habet, excusari non potest: nisi forte de omnibus bonis vel hæreditate controversia sit. §. item propter. inst. eod.
units.tr: Fifth, a guardian or curator cannot be excused on account of a lawsuit he has with his ward, whether pupil or adult, unless perhaps the dispute concerns all the goods or the inheritance. Inst., §"Item propter", same title.

units.la: Sextò, tria onera tutelæ non adfectatæ, vel curæ, præstant vacationem, quandiu administrátur. §. item tria. inst. eod.
units.tr: Sixth, the three burdens of guardianship or curatorship, not sought after, confer exemption for as long as they are carried. Inst., §"Item tria", same title.

units.la: Septimò, propter paupertatem excusatio tribuitur. §. sed & inst. eod.
units.tr: Seventh, excuse is granted on account of poverty. Inst., §"Sed et", same title.

units.la: Octavò, propter adversam valetudinem excusatio locum habet. §. item propter. inst. eod.
units.tr: Eighth, excuse applies on account of ill health. Inst., §"Item propter", same title.

units.la: Nonò, eos qui literas nesciunt (hoc est, qui idiotæ ac blittei[?] sunt, <bl>so vnerfahren leuen vnd nårrisch sein</bl>) esse excusandos, Divus Pius rescripsit: quamvis & imperiti literarum (hoc est, qui neque legere, neque scribere sciunt, attamen sunt prudentes) possint ad administrationem negotiorum sufficere. §. similiter. inst. eod.
units.tr: Ninth, the divine Pius ruled that those who do not know letters (that is, who are idiots and fools, so unerfahren, leichtfertig und närrisch sein, i.e. inexperienced, frivolous and foolish) are to be excused; although those unskilled in letters (that is, who can neither read nor write, yet are prudent) may be sufficient for the management of affairs. Inst., §"Similiter", same title.

units.la: Decimò, si propter inimicitias, aliquem testamento tutorem pater dederit: hoc ipsum praestat ei excusationem. §. item si propter. inst. eod.
units.tr: Tenth, if a father, because of enmities, has appointed someone as guardian in his will, this very fact gives that man an excuse. Inst., §"Item si propter", same title.

units.la: Undecimò, inimicitiæ, quas quis cum patre pupillorum vel adultorum exercuit: si capitales fuerunt, nec reconciliatio intervenit, à tutela vel cura solent excusare. §. inimicitiæ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Eleventh, enmities which someone has had with the father of the pupils or adults, if they were capital and no reconciliation has taken place, usually excuse one from guardianship or curatorship. Inst., §"Inimicitiae", same title.

units.la: Duodecimò, is, qui status controversiam à pupillorum patre passus est (id est, quem pater pupillorum aliquando contendit esse servum) excusatur à tutela. §. item is. inst. eod.
units.tr: Twelfth, one who has suffered a challenge to his status from the father of the pupils (that is, whom the father of the pupils once claimed to be a slave) is excused from guardianship. Inst., §"Item is", same title.

units.la: Decimotertiò, major septuaginta annis à tutela & cura se potest excusare. §. item major. inst. eod.
units.tr: Thirteenth, one who is over seventy years old may excuse himself from guardianship and curatorship. Inst., §"Item major", same title.

units.la: Decimoquartò, in militæ observandum est ut nec volens ad tutelæ onus admittatur, §. idem & in. instit. eod.
units.tr: Fourteenth, in military service it is to be observed that a soldier is not admitted to the burden of guardianship even if he is willing. Inst., §"Idem et in", same title.

units.la: Decimoquintò, Romæ Grammatici, Rhetores, & Medici, & qui in patria sua has artes exercent, & intra numerum sunt (de quo vide l. si duas. §. est autem. ff. de excusationibus) à tutela & cura habent vacationem. §. item Romæ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Fifteenth, at Rome grammarians, rhetoricians and physicians, and those who practise these arts in their own homeland and are within the prescribed number (on which see the law "Si duas", §"Est autem", Digest, on excuses), have exemption from guardianship and curatorship. Inst., §"Item Romae", same title.

units.la: Decimosextò, Philosophi, Oratores, Grammatici, qui publicè juvenibus prosunt, excusantur à tutelis. d. l. si duas. ff. de excusationib.
units.tr: Sixteenth, philosophers, orators and grammarians who teach young people in public are excused from guardianships. Said law "Si duas", Digest, on excuses.

units.la: Quod est tempus excusationis?
units.tr: What is the time for excuse?

units.la: Qui excusare se volunt, non appellant: sed intra quinquaginta dies continuos, ex quo cognoverint se esse tutores vel curatores datos, se excusare debent. §. qui autem vult. inst. eod.
units.tr: Those who wish to excuse themselves do not appeal, but must make their excuse within fifty continuous days from the time they learned that they have been given as guardians or curators. Inst., §"Qui autem vult", same title.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS sextus Titulus? De suspectis tutoribus vel curatoribus. <bl>Von verdächtigen vormündern oder sorgträgern.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTY-SIXTH TITLE? On suspect guardians or curators. On suspect guardians or curators.

units.la: Cui datum est jus removendi tutores suspectos?
units.tr: To whom has the right to remove suspect guardians been given?

units.la: DAtum est jus removendi tutores suspectos Romæ prætori,& in provinciis præsidibus earum, & legato proconsulis.in princ.inst.cod.
units.tr: The right to remove suspect guardians was given at Rome to the praetor, and in the provinces to the governors, and to the proconsul's deputy.

units.la: Qui suspecti fieri possunt?
units.tr: Who can become suspect?

units.la: Possunt quidem omnes tutores fieri suspecti, sive sint testamentarij, sive non sint, sed alterius generis tutores.§.ostendimus.inst.eod.
units.tr: Indeed, all guardians can become suspect, whether they are testamentary guardians or not, but only guardians of the other kind.

units.la: Qui possunt suspectos postulare?
units.tr: Who can bring a charge against suspect guardians?

units.la: Sciendum est,quasi publicam esse hanc accusationem,hoc est,omnibus patere. Quinimò & mulieres admittuntur ex rescripto Divorum Severi & Antonini: sed eæ solæ, quæ pietatis necessitudine ductæ, ad hoc procedunt utputa mater, nutrix quoque & avia: potest & soror.§.consequens.inst.eod.
units.tr: It should be noted that this accusation is regarded as public, that is, open to everyone. Indeed, women are also admitted by rescript of the deified Severus and Antoninus, but only those who proceed to this out of a sense of duty, for example a mother, a nurse, or a grandmother; a sister may also do so.

units.la: Quis est suspectus?
units.tr: Who is suspect?

units.la: Suspectus est qui non ex fide tutelam gerit, licet solvendo sit.§. suspectus.inst.eod.
units.tr: A suspect person is one who administers the guardianship without good faith, even though he is able to pay.

units.la: Suntne removendi qui fraudulenter tute- lam administrant?
units.tr: Must those be removed who administer the guardianship fraudulently?

units.la: Sciendum est eos,qui fraudulenter tutelam administrant, etiamsi satis offerant, removendos esse à tutela: quia satisdatio tutoris propositum malevolum non mutat, sed diutius grassandi in re familiari facultatem præstat.§.novissime. inst.eod.
units.tr: It should be noted that those who administer the guardianship fraudulently must be removed from the guardianship, even if they offer sufficient security; for the giving of security by a guardian does not change his malicious purpose, but rather grants him the opportunity to go on longer plundering the estate.

units.la: Hactenus Tituli primi libri Institutionum breviter enarrati fuêre.
units.tr: So far the titles of the first book of the Institutes have been briefly explained.

units.la: QUOT SUNT TITULI IN secundo libro Institutionum?
units.tr: HOW MANY TITLES ARE THERE IN the second book of the Institutes?

units.la: Viginti quinq;.
units.tr: Twenty-five.

units.la: QUIS EST PRIMUS TITULUS? De rerum divisione & acquirendo ipsarum Dominio. <bl>Von[?] theilung der güter/</bl> <bl>vnnd von derselben eigen-</bl> <bl>thumb zu erlangen.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIRST TITLE? On the division of things and on acquiring ownership of them. On the division of goods, and on acquiring ownership of them.

units.la: Recita transitionem.
units.tr: Recite the transition.

units.la: SUperiori libro de iure personarum exposuimus: modò videamus de rebus, quæ vel in nostro patrimonio vel extra patrimonium nostrum habentur. in princ.inst.cod.
units.tr: In the earlier book we set out the law of persons; now let us see about things, which are held either in our patrimony or outside our patrimony.

units.la: Res in patrimonio nostro habentur, quæ Dominio nostro subjectæ sunt, ut res prophanæ, corporales: Extra patrimonium nostrum sunt, quæ nostro dominio non subjiciuntur, ut res sacræ, religiosæ & sanctę. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: Things are held in our patrimony when they are subject to our ownership, such as profane and corporeal things; things are outside our patrimony when they are not subject to our ownership, such as sacred, religious and holy things. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Deinde, quaedam naturali jure communia sunt omnium, quaedam publica, quaedã universitatis, quaedam nullius, plæraq; singulorũ.§. quaedam.inst.cod.
units.tr: Next, some things are common to all by natural law, some are public, some belong to a community, some belong to no one, and most belong to individuals.

units.la: Quae sunt communia?
units.tr: What things are common?

units.la: Naturali jure communia sunt omnium hæc: aer, aqua profluens, & mare, & per hoc littora maris. Nemo igitur[?] ad littus maris accedere prohibetur: dum tamen a villis, & monumentis & ædificiis abstineat. §.& quidem,inst.cod.
units.tr: By natural law the following are common to all: air, flowing water, and the sea, and through it the seashore. No one is therefore prohibited from approaching the seashore, provided that he refrains from villas, monuments and buildings.

units.la: Quae sunt publica?
units.tr: What things are public?

units.la: Flumina omnia, & portus publica sunt: ideoque jus piscandi omnibus commune est in portu fluminibusque. §. flumina. inst.cod. Hoc autem non procedit quando flumen est privatum sive proprium alicujus, quia tunc ei, cujus est, licet piscari, & non aliis, Nam Ulpianus inquit: In laçu, qui mei domini est, utique piscari aliquem prohibere possum. l. injuriarum in fine. ff. de injuriis & famof. libell.
units.tr: All rivers and harbours are public; therefore the right of fishing is common to all in harbours and rivers. This does not hold, however, when a river is private or belongs to someone, for then it is lawful for its owner to fish and for no one else. For Ulpian says: "In a lake which is mine, I can certainly forbid anyone to fish." Law of injuries, at the end, Digest, on injuries and defamatory libel.

units.la: Quæ sunt universitatis?
units.tr: What things belong to a community?

units.la: Quæ in civitatibus sunt, Theatra, stadia & fiqua alia lunt civitatum communia. §. universitatis. inft. cod.
units.tr: The theatres, stadiums and other things in cities which are common to the citizens belong to a community.

units.la: Quæ sunt nullius?
units.tr: What things belong to no one?

units.la: Nullius sunt res sacræ & religiosæ, & sanctæ: quod enim Divini juris est, id nullius in bonis est. §. nullius. inft. cod.
units.tr: Sacred, religious and holy things belong to no one; for what is of divine right is in no one's possession.

units.la: Quæ sunt res sacræ?
units.tr: What are sacred things?

units.la: Sacræ res sunt quæ ritè per pontifices Deo consecratæ sunt: veluti ædes sacræ, & donaria, quæ ritè ad ministerium Dei dedicata sunt: quæ etiam alienari & obligari prohibuit Imperator, excepta causa redemptionis captivorum. §. sacræ res. inft. cod.
units.tr: Sacred things are those duly consecrated to God by the pontiffs, such as sacred buildings and offerings which have been duly dedicated to the service of God; the Emperor also forbade these to be alienated or pledged, except for the purpose of ransoming captives.

units.la: Quis potest religiosum locum facere?
units.tr: Who can make a place religious?

units.la: Religiosum locum unusquisque sua voluntate facit, dum mortuum infert in locum suum. §. religiosum. inft. cod.
units.tr: Each person makes a place religious by his own will, when he buries a dead person in his own place.

units.la: Cujus sunt res sanctæ?
units.tr: Whose are holy things?

units.la: Sanctæ res veluti muri & portæ civitatis, quodammodo Divini juris sunt: & ideo nullius in bonis sunt. Ideo autem muros sanctos dicimus, quia pœna capitis constituta est in eos, qui aliquid in muros deliquerint. §. sanctæ quoq; inst. cod.
units.tr: Holy things, such as the walls and gates of a city, are in a sense of divine right, and therefore belong to no one. We call the walls holy because the penalty of death is laid down for those who have committed an offence against the walls.

units.la: Quot modis fiunt res singulorum?
units.tr: In how many ways do things become the property of individuals?

units.la: Singulorum hominum multis modis res fiunt: quarundam enim rerum dominiū nanciscimur jure naturali, quod sicut diximus appellatur jus gentiū: quarundam verò jure civili. §. singulorum. inst. cod.
units.tr: Things become the property of individuals in many ways: for we acquire ownership of some things by natural law, which, as we have said, is called the law of nations, and of others by civil law.

units.la: Quid est Dominium?
units.tr: What is ownership?

units.la: Dominium est jus de re corporali perfectè dispo-nendi nendi aut vendicandi, nisi legevel conventione quis prohibeatur, inquit Shneidevvinus.
units.tr: Ownership is the right to dispose of or claim a corporeal thing absolutely, unless someone is prohibited by law or agreement, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Quotuplex est Dominium?
units.tr: How many kinds of ownership are there?

units.la: Duplex:aliud est directum seu superius,aliud utile seu inferius.
units.tr: Two: one is direct or superior, the other useful or inferior.

units.la: Quid est directum Dominium?
units.tr: What is direct ownership?

units.la: Quod Dominus superior habet in rebus feudalibus & emphyteuticis, & est sine fructu, cū spe tamen consolidationis. <bl>Das der Grundherr hat in lehen gü-</bl> <bl>tern und erbzinß gütern/ und ist ohn frucht/ doch mit</bl> <bl>der hoffnung des heimfals.</bl>
units.tr: It is what the superior lord has in feudal and emphyteutic goods; it is without fruit, yet with the hope of consolidation. That the lord has in fief goods and hereditary-lease goods, and it is without fruit, yet with the hope of reversion.

units.la: Quid est utile Dominium?
units.tr: What is useful ownership?

units.la: Quod Vasallus habet in rebus Feudalibus, & Emphyteuta in bonis emphyteuticis <bl>daß der lehentrager</bl> <bl>hat in lehengütern / uñ[?] ein Meyer oder erbzinß-</bl> <bl>trager/ in et[?] bzinß gütern.</bl> Hinc Dominium duas partes habet, nudam scilicet proprietatem, & usumfructum, quae si fuerint conjuncta, dicitur plenum Dominium.Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: That which the vassal has in feudal property, and the emphyteuta in emphyteutic goods. Hence ownership has two parts, namely bare ownership and the usufruct, which, when joined together, are called full ownership. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quae acquiruntur jure naturali seu jure gentium secundario?
units.tr: What things are acquired by natural law, or secondarily by the law of nations?

units.la: Feræ bestiæ, & volucres, & pisces, & omnia animalia, quæ mari, cœlo, & terra nascuntur: simulatq; ab aliquo capta fuerint, jure gentium statim illius esse incipiunt: Quod enim ante nullius est, id naturali ratione occupanti conceditur. §. ferae. inst. eod. Verum hodie ferae bestiae & pisces plærunq; magistratus sunt. Occupanti igitur non conceduntur.
units.tr: Wild beasts, birds, fish, and all animals that are born in the sea, the sky, or the land: as soon as they have been caught by someone, they at once begin to belong to that person by the law of nations. For what belongs to no one before is granted to the one who seizes it by natural reason. Inst. eod., §. ferae. But today wild beasts and fish are for the most part the property of the magistrate, so they are not granted to whoever seizes them.

units.la: Suntne Apes occupantis?
units.tr: Are bees the property of the one who takes them?

units.la: Apium fera natura est. Itaque apes, quae in arbore tua consederint, antequam à te alveo includantur, non magis tuae intelligantur esse, quam volucres, quae in arbore tua nidum fecerint. §. apium. inst. eod. Sed in hac re quid ubiq; locorum consuetudinari jure observetur, attendi debet, inquit Schneidewin.
units.tr: Bees are wild by nature. Therefore, bees that have settled in your tree are not understood to be yours any more than birds that have built a nest in your tree, before they are enclosed by you in a hive. Inst. eod., §. apium. But in this matter, what is observed by customary law in each place must be considered, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Sùntne pavones, columbæ, & cervi cicu- res occupantis?
units.tr: Are peacocks, doves, and tame deer the property of the one who takes them?

units.la: In iis animalibus quæ ex consuetudine abire & redire solent, talis regula comprobata est: ut eousque tua esse intelligantur, donec animum revertendi habeant. Nam si revertendi animum habere desierint, etiam tua esse desinunt, & fiunt occupantium. §. pavonum. inst. cod.
units.tr: In those animals which are accustomed to go away and come back, this rule is approved: that they are understood to be yours for as long as they have the intention of returning. For if they cease to have the intention of returning, they also cease to be yours and become the property of whoever takes them. Inst. cod., §. pavonum.

units.la: Sùntne Gallinæ & Anseres domestici occupantis?
units.tr: Are domestic hens and geese the property of the one who takes them?

units.la: Si anseres tui aut gallinæ tuæ aliquo modo turbati turbatæve evolaverint: licet conspectum tuum effugerint, quocunq; tamen loco sint, tui tuæve esse intelliguntur: & qui lucrandi animo ea animalia detinet, furtum committere intelligitur. §. Gallinarum. inst. cod.
units.tr: If your geese or your hens have flown away, having been disturbed in some way, even though they have escaped your sight, wherever they are they are understood to be yours; and whoever keeps those animals with intent to profit is understood to commit theft. Inst. cod., §. Gallinarum.

units.la: Sùntne ea, quæ ex hostibus capiuntur, occupantis?
units.tr: Are things captured from enemies the property of the one who takes them?

units.la: Ea, quæ ex hostibus capimus, jure gentium statim nostra fiunt. §. item ea. inst. cod.
units.tr: Things that we capture from enemies become ours at once by the law of nations. Inst. cod., §. item ea.

units.la: Cujus sunt quæ in littore maris inveniuntur?
units.tr: Whose are the things found on the seashore?

units.la: Lapilli & gemmæ, & cætera quæ in littore maris inveniuntur, jure naturali statim inventoris fiunt. §. item lapilli. inst. cod.
units.tr: Pebbles, gems, and other things that are found on the seashore become at once the property of the finder by natural law. Inst. cod., §. item lapilli.

units.la: Cujus sunt, quæ ex animalibus nostris nascuntur?
units.tr: Whose are the things born from our animals?

units.la: Ea, quæ ex animalibus Dominio tuo subjectis nata sunt, naturali jure tibi acquiruntur. §. item ea. inst. cod.
units.tr: Those things which are born from animals subject to your dominion are acquired to you by natural law. Inst. cod., §. item ea.

units.la: Cujus est id quod per Alluvionem agro alicui adjicitur?
units.tr: Whose is that which is added to someone's field by alluvion?

units.la: Quod per alluvionem agro tuo flumen adjecit, jure gentium tibi acquiritur. Est autem Alluvio, incrementum latens. <bl>Der [?]Zuwurff ist ein verborgener</bl> <bl>Zuwachs.</bl> §. praeterea quod. inst. eod.
units.tr: What a river has added to your field by alluvion is acquired to you by the law of nations. Now alluvion is a hidden increase. Inst. eod., §. praeterea quod.

units.la: Cujus est pars fundi in uno impetu non la- tenter detracta?
units.tr: Whose is a part of an estate that has been torn away not secretly but in a single onslaught?

units.la: Si vis fluminis de tuo praedio partem aliquam detraxerit, & vicini praedio attulcrit[?], palàm est eam tuâ permanere. §. quod si vis. inst. cod.
units.tr: If the force of a river has torn away some part of your estate and carried it to the estate of a neighbour, it is plain that it remains yours. Inst. cod., §. quod si vis.

units.la: Cujus est Insula in mari nata?
units.tr: Whose is an island born in the sea?

units.la: Insula quae in mari nata est, quod raro accidit, occupantis fit: nullius enim esse creditur. §. Insula. instit.cod.
units.tr: An island that is born in the sea, which happens rarely, becomes the property of the one who occupies it, for it is believed to belong to no one. Inst. cod., §. Insula.

units.la: Cujus est Insula in flumine nata?
units.tr: Whose is an island born in a river?

units.la: Insula in flumine nata, quod frequenter accidit, si quidem mediam partem fluminis tenet: communis est eorum, qui ab utraq; parte fluminis prope ripam praedia possident, pro modo scilicet latitudinis cujusq; fundi, quae prope ripam sit. Quod si alteri parti proximior sit: eorum est tantum, qui ab ea parte prope ripam praedia possident. §. at insula. inst. cod.
units.tr: An island born in a river, which happens often, if it occupies the middle part of the river, belongs in common to those who hold estates on both banks near the shore, in proportion, of course, to the width of each estate that lies near the bank. But if it lies nearer to one side, it belongs only to those who hold estates near the bank on that side. Inst. cod., §. at insula.

units.la: Cujus est alveus ( ein wassergrab ) à flu- mine derelictus?
units.tr: Whose is the riverbed abandoned by a river?

units.la: Si flumen naturali alveo in universum derelicto, ad aliam partem fluere coeperit: prior quidem alveus eorum est, qui prope ripam ejus praedia possident: pro modo scilicet latitudinis cujusq; agri, quae (latitudo) prope ripam sit. Novus autem alveus ejus juris esse incipit, cujus & ipsum flumen est, id est, publicus. §. quod si naturali. inst. cod.
units.tr: If a river, having entirely abandoned its natural bed, has begun to flow in another direction, the former bed belongs to those who hold estates near its bank, of course in proportion to the width of each field that lies near the bank. But the new bed begins to fall under the law to which the river itself belongs, that is, it becomes public. Inst. cod., §. quod si naturali.

units.la: Cujus est species, quam quis ex aliena materia fecerit?
units.tr: Whose is a shaped thing that someone has made from another's material?
