units.la: Placuit sententia existimantiū, si ea species ad priorem & rudem materiam reduci possit: eum videri dominum esse, qui materiae Dominus fuerit: si non possit reduci: eum potius intelligi Dominum, qui fecerit. §. quum ex aliena. inst. cod.
units.tr: The opinion of those who hold that, if the new form can be reduced to the earlier and raw material, the one who was owner of the material is considered the owner, has been approved; but if it cannot be reduced, the one who made it is rather understood to be the owner. Inst. cod., §. quum ex aliena.

units.la: Si quis purpuram alienam vestimento suo intexuerit, quid juris?
units.tr: If someone has woven another's purple into his garment, what is the law?

units.la: Si alienam purpuram vestimento suo quis intexuerit: licet pretiosior sit purpura, tamen accessioni s vice cedit vestimento, & qui dominus fuit purpurae, adversus eum qui surripuit, habet furti actionem & condictionem: sive ipse sit, qui vestimentum fecit, sive alius. Nam extinctae res, licet vendicari non possint, condici tamen a furibus, & quibusq; aliis possessoribus possunt. <bl>Verbrachte Dinge / ob sie wol nicht</bl> <bl>mögen wider erlanget werden / so können sie doch</bl> <bl>von den Dieben und andern besitzern gefordert werden.</bl> §. si tamen. inst. cod.
units.tr: If someone has woven another's purple into his garment, then, although the purple is more valuable, it nevertheless yields to the garment as an accessory, and the one who was owner of the purple has an action for theft and a claim for recovery against the one who stole it, whether he himself made the garment or someone else did. For things that have been destroyed, although they cannot be claimed back, can nevertheless be demanded from thieves and from any other possessors. Inst. cod., §. si tamen.

units.la: Cujus est aedificium ex aliena materia extructum?
units.tr: Whose is a building constructed from another's material?

units.la: Cum in suo solo aliquis ex aliena materia aedificaverit, ipse intelligitur Dominus aedificii: quia omne, quod solo inaedificatur, solo cedit. <bl>Alles was</bl> <bl>auff einen grund gebawet wird / das gehöret dem</bl> <bl>grunde zu.</bl> Nec tamen ideo is, qui materiae Dominus fuerat, definit dominus ejus esse. §. cum in suo. inst. cod. Ex diverso, si quis in alieno solo ex sua materia domum aedificaverit, illius fit domus, cujus & solum est. §. ex diverso inst. cod.
units.tr: If someone builds on his own ground using another's material, he is understood to be the owner of the building, because whatever is built on the ground belongs to the ground. Yet the man who owned the material does not thereby cease to be its owner. Conversely, if someone builds a house on another's ground using his own material, the house belongs to the owner of the ground.

units.la: Cujus est planta seu arbor?
units.tr: Whose is a plant or tree?

units.la: Si Titius alienam plantam in solo suo posuerit, ipsius erit. Et ex diverso, si Titius suam plantam in Maevij solo posuerit, Maevij planta erit: si modo utroque casu radices egerit: ante enim quam radices egerit, ejus permanet cujus fuerat. §. si Titius. inst. cod.
units.tr: If Titius places another's plant in his own ground, it will be his. Conversely, if Titius places his own plant in Maevius's ground, it will be Maevius's plant, provided that in either case it has taken root; for before it has taken root, it remains the property of its former owner.

units.la: Cujus sunt literæ?
units.tr: Whose are the letters?

units.la: Literæ licèt aureæ sint, perinde chartis membranisve cedunt, ac solo cedere solent ea, quæ inædificantur aut inferuntur. Ideoq; si in chartis membranisve tuis carmē, vel historiam, vel orationem Titius scripserit hujus corporis non Titius, sed tu Dominus esse videris. §. literæ quoq;. inst. eod.
units.tr: Letters, even if they are golden, yield to the paper or parchment in the same way that things built or attached to the ground yield to the ground. Therefore, if Titius has written a poem, a history or a speech on your paper or parchment, it is not Titius but you who appear to be the owner of this physical material.

units.la: Cujus est tabula picta?
units.tr: Whose is a painted panel?

units.la: Si quis in aliena tabula pinxerit, quidam putant tabulam picturæ cedere, aliis videtur, picturam, qualiscunq; sit, tabulæ cedere: sed Imperatori videtur melius esse tabulam picturæ cedere. §. si quis in. inst. eod.
units.tr: If someone paints on another's panel, some think the panel yields to the painting; others think the painting, whatever its quality, yields to the panel. But the Emperor thinks it better that the panel yields to the painting.

units.la: Si quis à non Domino bona fide fundum emeret, quid juris?
units.tr: If someone in good faith buys land from a non-owner, what is the law?

units.la: Si quis à non Domino, quem Dominum esse crediderit, bona fide fundum emerit, vel ex donatione, aliáve qualibet justa causa: æquè[?] bona fide acceperit: naturali ratione placuit, fructus, quos percepit, ejus esse pro cultura & cura. §. si quis à non. inst. eod.
units.tr: If someone in good faith buys land from a non-owner whom he believed to be the owner, or receives it in good faith by gift or by some other lawful cause, natural reason has decided that the fruits he has gathered belong to him, in return for his cultivation and care.

units.la: Quando fructus fiunt usufructuarij?
units.tr: When do fruits become the property of the usufructuary?

units.la: Is, ad quem usufructus fundi pertinet, non aliter fructuum Dominus efficitur, quàm si ipse eos perceperit. Et ideò licèt maturis fructibus, nondum tamen perceptis, decesserit: ad hæredes ejus non pertinent, sed Domino proprietatis adquiruntur. §. is verò. inst. eod.
units.tr: The person to whom the usufruct of a piece of land belongs does not become owner of the fruits unless he has actually gathered them. Therefore, if he dies after the fruits have ripened but before they have been gathered, they do not pass to his heirs but are acquired by the owner of the property.

units.la: In pecudum fructu etiam fœtus est, sicuti lac, pilus & lana. Itaq; agni, hœdi, & vituli, & equuli, & suculi, statim naturali jure dominij fructuarij sunt. <bl>Nach natürlichem rechte des eigenthums / gehöret</bl> <bl>dem nießbraucher.</bl> §. in pecudum. inst. cod.
units.tr: In the produce of livestock the offspring also count, just as milk, hair and wool do. Thus lambs, kids, calves, foals and piglets belong at once, by natural law, to the usufructuary.

units.la: Cujus est Thesaurus, quem quis in suo fundo reperit?
units.tr: Whose is the treasure that someone finds on his own land?

units.la: Thesauros, quos quis in loco suo invenerit, Divus Hadrianus naturalem aequitatem secutus, ei concessit, qui eos invenerit. Idemque statuit, si quis in sacro aut religioso loco fortuito casu invenerit. At si quis in alieno loco, non data ad hoc opera, sed so[?] tuitò invenerit: dimidium Domino soli concessit, & dimidium inventori.§Thesauros.inst.cod.
units.tr: The Divine Hadrian, following natural equity, granted treasures that someone finds in his own place to the one who finds them. He decided the same if someone finds a treasure by chance in a sacred or religious place. But if someone finds one in another's place, not by work undertaken for that purpose but by chance, he granted half to the owner of the ground and half to the finder.

units.la: Quid est Thesaurus?
units.tr: What is a treasure?

units.la: Thesaurus est vetus depositio pecuniae, cujus non extat memoria, ut jam dominum non habeat: sic enim fit ejus qui invenerit, quòd nō alterius sit. Alioquin si quis aliquid vel lucri causa, vel metus vel custodiae condiderit sub terra, non est Thesaurus: cujus etiam furtum fit, inquit Jurisconsultus Paulus in l. nunquam. ff. de acquirend. rer domin.
units.tr: A treasure is an ancient deposit of money whose memory has perished, so that it no longer has an owner; for in this way it becomes the property of the finder, since it belongs to no one else. Otherwise, if someone has hidden something under the ground for the sake of profit, fear or safekeeping, it is not a treasure, and its removal is theft, as the jurist Paul says in the law "Nunquam", Digest, on the acquisition of ownership of things.

units.la: Ideo si quis vendit domum, & emptor reperiat pecuniam in muro, quae ab ipso venditore vel ejus parentibus recondita est, non pertinet ea pecunia ad emptorem, sed venditori restituenda est, per expressum textum in l. à tutore. ff. de rei vendicat.
units.tr: Therefore, if someone sells a house and the buyer finds money in a wall that was hidden there by the seller himself or by his parents, that money does not belong to the buyer but must be restored to the seller, by the express text of the law "A tutore", Digest, on the vindication of things.

units.la: Acquiruntur etiam res per traditionem?
units.tr: Are things also acquired by delivery?

units.la: Per traditionem quoque jure naturali res nobis adquiruntur: nihil enim tam conveniens est naturali aequitati, quàm voluntatem Domini volentis rem suam in alium transferre, ratam haberi. §. per traditionem. inst. cod.
units.tr: Things are also acquired by us through delivery, by natural law; for nothing is so consistent with natural equity as that the will of an owner who wishes to transfer his thing to another should be upheld.

units.la: Quomodo res venditae acquiruntur?
units.tr: How are sold things acquired?

units.la: Venditae res & traditae emptori non aliter acquiruntur, quàm si is venditori pretium solverit, vel alio modo ei satisfecerit. §. venditae. inst. cod.
units.tr: Things sold and delivered to a buyer are acquired by him only if he has paid the price to the seller or has otherwise satisfied him.

units.la: Quomodo in personam incertam transfer- tur rei proprietas?
units.tr: How is ownership of a thing transferred to an uncertain person?

units.la: Prætores & Consules cum missilia jactant in vulgus; <bl>wenn sie geben[?] werffen unter das volck/</bl> ignorant quid eorum quisq; sit excepturus: & tamē quia volunt, quod quisq; acceperit ejus esse, statim eum Dominum efficiunt. §. hoc amplius. inst. eod.[?]
units.tr: When praetors and consuls throw largesse among the crowd, they do not know which person will catch which item; yet because they wish whatever each person has received to be his, they at once make him its owner.

units.la: Cujus est res pro derelicto habita?
units.tr: Whose is a thing regarded as abandoned?

units.la: Si rem pro derelicto à domino habitam occupaverit quis, statim is dominus efficitur. Pro derelicto autem habetur quod Dominus ea mente abjecerit, ut id in numero rerum suarum esse nolit: ideoq; statim Dominus ejus esse desinit. §. qua ratione. institut.eod.[?]
units.tr: If someone takes possession of a thing that its owner has regarded as abandoned, he at once becomes its owner. A thing is regarded as abandoned when its owner has cast it away with the intention of not wishing it to remain among his possessions; therefore he at once ceases to be its owner.

units.la: QUIS EST SECUNDUS Titulus? De rebus corporalibus & incorporalibus. Von leiblichen und unleiblichen gütern.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SECOND Title? Concerning corporeal and incorporeal things. <bl>Von leiblichen</bl> <bl>und unleiblichen gütern.</bl>

units.la: Quæ sunt res corporales?
units.tr: What are corporeal things?

units.la: Quæ sui natura tangi possunt: veluti fundus, homo, vestis, aurum, argentum, & deniq; aliæ res innumerabiles §. corporales. inst. eod.[?]
units.tr: Those which can be touched by their own nature: for example, a farm, a man, a garment, gold, silver, and finally countless other things. Inst. same title, §. corporales.[?]

units.la: Quæ sunt res incorporales?
units.tr: What are incorporeal things?

units.la: Quæ tangi non possunt: qualia sunt ea, quæ in jure consistunt, sicut hæreditas, usufructus, usus & obligationes quoquo modo contractæ. §. incorporales. inst. eod.[?]
units.tr: Those which cannot be touched: such are those which consist in law, like an inheritance, usufruct, use, and obligations contracted in any way. Inst. same title, §. incorporales.[?]

units.la: Eodem numero sunt jura prædiorum urbanorū, & rusticorum, quæ etiam servitutes vocantur. §. final. inst. eod.[?]
units.tr: To the same class belong the rights of urban and rural estates, which are also called servitudes. Inst. same title, §. final.[?]

units.la: QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHICH IS THE THIRD TITLE?

units.la: De servitutibus praediorum. <bl>Von dienst-</bl> <bl>barkeiten der liegenden güter.</bl>
units.tr: On servitudes of rural and urban property. (German: On the easements of immovable goods.)

units.la: Quotuplex est Servitus?
units.tr: How many kinds of servitude are there?

units.la: Duplex : personalis aut realis. Personalis, quae à persona personae debetur, ut est in hominibus servilis conditionis, de qua supra dictum est: vel quae à persona rei debetur, ut quando persona cogitur certo cuidam loco assistere: Realis est, quae à re, rei debetur.
units.tr: There are two kinds: personal or real. A personal servitude is owed by a person to a person, as among men of servile condition, which was discussed above; or it is owed by a person to a thing, as when a person is compelled to attend a certain place. A real servitude is owed by a thing to a thing.

units.la: Quotuplex est Servitus realis?
units.tr: How many kinds of real servitude are there?

units.la: Duplex: Rustica aut urbana Rustica, quae rusticis praediis debetur: Urbana, q̄ urbanis prędiis debetur.
units.tr: There are two kinds: rural or urban. A rural servitude is owed to rural estates; an urban servitude is owed to urban estates.

units.la: Quae dicuntur rustica prędia?
units.tr: What are called rural estates?

units.la: Rustica prędia dicuntur ipsi agri vel fundi. Item ędificia, quae sunt structa[?] pro rebus rusticis, pecoribus & fructibus, sive sint in urbe, sive extra urbem.
units.tr: Rural estates are the fields or farms themselves. Likewise the buildings constructed for farm matters, for livestock and for produce, whether they stand in the town or outside it.

units.la: Quae dicuntur urbana prędia?
units.tr: What are called urban estates?

units.la: Urbana prędia dicuntur ędificia, inhabitādi gratia facta, & hominum usui & habitationi destinata, sive in urbe, sive extra urbem in rure vel villa posita sint. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: Urban estates are buildings made for the purpose of dwelling and intended for human use and habitation, whether they stand in the town or outside it, in the countryside or on a country estate. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Ad hoc autem ut cognoscatur an sit servitus rustica seu urbana, inspicitur qualitas prędii dominantis, cui servitus debetur: non prędii servientis, quod servitutem debet. Unde licet via sit servitus rustica, tamen si debetur pe fundum tuum domui meae, dicitur urbana servitus, secundum Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: To know whether a servitude is rural or urban, one looks at the nature of the dominant estate, to which the servitude is owed, not at the serving estate, which owes it. Hence, although a way is a rural servitude, if it is owed across your estate to my house, it is called an urban servitude, according to Schneidewin.

units.la: Quae sunt servitutes Rusticorum prędiorum?
units.tr: What are the servitudes of rural estates?

units.la: <bl>Iter, der fußpfad. Actus, der treibe weg. Via, der fahrweg.</bl>
units.tr: Iter, the footpath. Actus, the driveway for animals. Via, the carriage road.

units.la: <bl>fahrweg.</bl> Aquaeductus, <bl>Das wasser leiten.</bl>
units.tr: Carriage road. Aquaeductus, the leading of water.

units.la: Iter est jus eundi ambulandi hominis, non etiam jumentum agendi, vel vehiculum.
units.tr: Iter is the right of going and walking for a person, not also the right of driving a beast of burden or a vehicle.

units.la: Actus est jus agendi vel jumentum vel vehiculum: ita qui habet iter, actum non habet: qui actum habet & iter habet, eoque uti poterit etiam sine[?] jumento.
units.tr: Actus is the right of driving either a beast of burden or a vehicle. So one who has a footpath does not thereby have a driveway; but one who has a driveway also has a footpath, and may use it even without a beast of burden.

units.la: Via est jus eundi & agendi & ambulandi: Nam & iter & actum via in se continet.
units.tr: Via is the right of going, driving and walking; for via contains both iter and actus within itself.

units.la: Aquaeductus est jus aquae ducendae per fundum alienum. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Aquaeductus is the right of conducting water through another's land. At the beginning of the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: Inter rusticorum praediorum servitutes quidam computari recte putant aquae haustum, pecoris ad aquam adpulsum, jus pascendi, calcis coquendae, arenae fodiendae. §. inter. inst. eod.
units.tr: Some rightly think the following should be counted among the servitudes of rural estates: drawing water, driving livestock to water, the right of pasturing, of burning lime, and of digging sand. See the section inter in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: Quae sunt servitutes urbanorum praediorum?
units.tr: What are the servitudes of urban estates?

units.la: Quae aedificiis inhaerent: ut vicinus onera vicini sustineat; ut in parietem ejus liceat vicino tignum immittere; ut stillicidium vel flumen recipiat quis in aedes suas vel in arcam, vel in cloacam, ne altius quis tollat aedes suas, ne luminibus vicini officiat. §. praediorum inst. eod.
units.tr: Those that adhere to buildings: that a neighbour bear the burdens of his neighbour; that a neighbour may insert a beam into his wall; that someone receive rainwater or runoff into his house, into a cistern or into a drain; that someone not raise his house higher, so as not to obstruct his neighbour's light. See the section praediorum in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: Prima servitus urbana, est jus oneris ferendi, quando scilicet talis imponitur servitus aedibus vicini mei, ut columna, vel paries ejus perpetuo ferat onus meae domus, non quidem quod columna seu paries sit suturus perpetuus, sed si defecerit, vel collapsus fuerit, ut is reficiat, qui servitutem debet. l. eum. ff. de servitutib. urbanor. praed.
units.tr: The first urban servitude is the right of bearing a burden, namely when such a servitude is imposed on my neighbour's building that his column or wall shall perpetually carry the load of my house. This does not mean the column or wall will last forever; but if it gives way or collapses, the one who owes the servitude must rebuild it. See the law eum, Digest, on urban servitudes of estates.

units.la: Secunda servitus urbana, est jus immittendi tigni in parietem vicini. Vulgo tramrecht.
units.tr: The second urban servitude is the right of inserting a beam into a neighbour's wall. Commonly called tramrecht, the right of the beam.

units.la: Tertia servitus urbana est duplex: una affirmativa videlicet a[?]ertendi stillicidij, & altera negativa, licet non aveitendi stillicidij. Servitus affirmativa stillicidij avertendi dicitur, quando quis habet illud jus, ut à tecto suo possit avertere, seu derivare aquam pluvialem in aream vel tectum vicini. <bl>Daß der trauff auff des nachbarn tach</bl> <bl>oder hoff falle.</bl> l. urbanorum. ff. eod.
units.tr: The third urban servitude is twofold: one affirmative, namely the right of diverting rainwater, and the other negative, namely the right of not having it diverted. The affirmative servitude is called the right of diverting runoff, when someone has the right to divert or channel rainwater from his roof into his neighbour's yard or onto his neighbour's roof. (German: That the drip from the neighbour's roof or yard falls where it may.) See the law urbanorum, Digest, same title.

units.la: Servitus negativa nō avertēdi stillicidij est, quando is, cujus stillicidium cadit in meam aream, illud non potest avertere ad suam domum, ita ut nō cadat in meam aream. dict. l. urbanorum. ff. eod.
units.tr: The negative servitude of not diverting runoff exists when the one whose runoff falls into my yard cannot divert it to his own house so that it no longer falls into my yard. See the same law urbanorum, Digest, same title.

units.la: Quarta servitus urbana quoq; duplex est, affirmativa, ut altius tollendi, & negativa altius non tollendi. Servitus altius tollendi est, quando scilicet jure servitutis possum cogere vicinum, ut altius tollat ædes suas, quia ex eo sentio utilitatem, cùm prosit mihi ad arcendum impetum ventorum, vel ut præstet umbram eo loco, quo solem habere gratum non est, ut dicitur in l. si arborem. ff eod. Servitus altius non tollendi est, quando contra naturalem ædificandi libertatem constituitur hæc servitus, ut non liceat vicino invito vicino ædes suas altius ædificare: aliàs enim quilibet ad cœlum usq; ædificare potest, cùm altius ædificia tollere, si domus servitutem non debeat, Dominus ejus minimè prohibeatur. l. altius. C. de servitutib. & aqua.
units.tr: The fourth urban servitude is likewise twofold: affirmative, the right of raising higher, and negative, the right of not raising higher. The servitude of raising higher is when, by right of servitude, I can compel my neighbour to raise his house higher, since I gain advantage from it, as it serves to ward off the force of the winds, or to provide shade in a place where sunlight is unwelcome, as is said in the law si arborem, Digest, same title. The servitude of not raising higher is when this servitude is established against the natural freedom to build, so that it is not lawful for a neighbour, against his neighbour's will, to build his house higher. Otherwise anyone could build right up to the sky, since an owner is not forbidden to raise his buildings higher unless his house owes a servitude. See the law altius, Code, on servitudes and water.

units.la: Quinta servitus urbana dicitur: ne luminibus officiatur. <bl>Daß nicht deß nachbaurn liecht verbawet</bl> <bl>oder verhindert werde.</bl> Sciendum autem, quòd quilibet potest ædificando obscurare lumina vicini. l. cum eo. ff. eod. nisi servitus hæc imposita sit, ne vicinus obscuret lumina ædium vicini.
units.tr: The fifth urban servitude is called: that light not be obstructed. (German: That the neighbour's light not be built over or hindered.) It must be understood that anyone may, by building, darken his neighbour's lights; see the law cum eo, Digest, same title, unless this servitude has been imposed, that the neighbour not darken the lights of the house.

units.la: Quomodo servitutes constituuntur?
units.tr: How are servitudes constituted?

units.la: Pastionibus, & stipulationibus, & etiam testamento. §. si quis. inst. eod.
units.tr: By agreements, by stipulations, and also by testament. See the section si quis in the same title of the Institutes.

units.la: QUIS EST QUARTUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FOURTH TITLE?

units.la: De usufructu. Vom niessbrauch oder leibzucht. Quid est usufructus?
units.tr: On usufruct. Concerning the use-right or life-interest. What is usufruct?

units.la: USusfructus est jus alienis rebus utendi, fruendi, salva rerum substantia. Est autem jus in corpore, quo sublato & ipsû tolli necesse est. in prin.inst.eod.
units.tr: Usufruct is the right of using and enjoying the things of another, with the substance of the things preserved. It is a right in the thing itself, and if it is removed, the thing too must necessarily be removed. Inst. same title, at the beginning.

units.la: In quibus rebus constituitur usufructus?
units.tr: On what things is usufruct established?

units.la: Non tantum in fundo & aedibus, verum etiam in servis, & jumentis, & caeteris rebus: Exceptis iis, quae ipso usu consumuntur. §. constituitur. inst.eod.
units.tr: Not only on land and buildings, but also on slaves, beasts of burden, and other things, excepting those which are consumed by the very use. Inst. same title, the paragraph "constituitur."

units.la: Quando finitur usufructus?
units.tr: When does usufruct end?

units.la: Finitur usufructus morte usufructuarij, & duabus capitis deminutionibus, maxima & media, & nō utendo per modum & tempus. §. finitur. inst.eod.
units.tr: Usufruct ends by the death of the usufructuary, by two changes of status, the greatest and the middle, and by not using it within the prescribed manner and time. Inst. same title, the paragraph "finitur."

units.la: QUIS EST QUINTUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIFTH TITLE?

units.la: De usu & habitatione. Vom brauch vnd wohnung. Quibus modis constituitur & fini- tur usus?
units.tr: On use and habitation. How is use constituted and terminated?

units.la: Iisdem illis modis, quibus usufructus constituitur, etiam nudus usus constitui solet: iisdemq; illis modis finitur, quibus & usufructus definit, in princ.inst.eod.
units.tr: By the very same modes by which usufruct is constituted, bare use is also customarily constituted; and it is terminated by the same modes by which usufruct also ends, at the beginning of the title.

units.la: Quid interest inter usum & usum- fructum?
units.tr: What is the difference between use and usufruct?

units.la: Minus juris est in usu, quàm in usufructu. Nam is qui fundi nudum habet usum, nihil ulterius habere intelligitur, quàm ut oleribus, pomis, floribus, fœno, stramentis, & lignis ad usum quotidianum utatur: nec ulli alij jus quod habet, aut vendere, aut gratis concedere potest: quum is, qui usumfructum habet, possit hæc omnia facere. §. minus inst. eod.
units.tr: There is less right in use than in usufruct. For the one who has the bare use of a farm is understood to have nothing further than to make use, for his daily needs, of vegetables, fruit, flowers, hay, straw and wood; nor can he sell or grant gratuitously to anyone else the right that he has; whereas the one who has usufruct can do all these things. At the paragraph "minus", in the same title.

units.la: Quale jus habet qui ædium usum habet?
units.tr: What right does one who has the use of a house have?

units.la: Is qui ædium usum habet, hactenus jus habere intelligitur, ut ipse tantum inhabitet, nec hoc jus ad alium transferre potest. §. item is. inst. eod.
units.tr: The one who has the use of a house is understood to have a right only to this extent: that he himself alone may live in it, and he cannot transfer this right to another. At the paragraph "item is", in the same title.

units.la: Quale jus habent, qui servi vel jumenti aut pecorum usum habent?
units.tr: What rights do those have who have the use of a slave, a beast of burden, or livestock?

units.la: Is ad quem servi usus pertinet, ipse tantum opera atq; ministerio ejus uti potest. Idem scilicet juris est in jumento. Sed etsi pecorum, vel ovium usus legatus sit: neq; lacte, neq; agnis, neq; lana utetur usuarius: quia ea in fructu sunt. Plane ad stercorandum agrü suum pecoribus uti potest. §. item is ad quem, inst. eod.
units.tr: The one to whom the use of a slave belongs can make use only of his own labour and service. The same is clearly the law for a beast of burden. But even if the use of flocks or sheep has been bequeathed, the user will use neither the milk, nor the lambs, nor the wool, because these belong to the fruits. Plainly, he can use the animals to manure his own field. At the paragraph "item is ad quem", in the same title.

units.la: Quale jus habet qui habitationem habet?
units.tr: What right does one who has habitation have?

units.la: Habitationem habetibus permisit Imperator non solum in ea degere, sed etiam aliis locare. §. sed si. instit. eod.
units.tr: The Emperor allowed those who have habitation not only to dwell in the place, but also to let it to others. At the paragraph "sed si", in the same title.

units.la: Exposuimus summatim quibus modis jure gentium res adquiruntur: modò videamus quibus modis legitimo & civili jure adquiruntur. § .final.instit.eod.
units.tr: We have set out in summary the modes by which things are acquired by the law of nations; now let us see by what modes they are acquired by the legitimate and civil law. At the final paragraph, in the same title.

units.la: QUIS EST SEXTUS TITULUS? De usucapionibus & longi temporis pra- escriptionibus. <bl>Von nemmung in besitz vnnd</bl> <bl>langer zeit verjärung.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SIXTH TITLE? Concerning usucapions and prescriptions of long time. <bl>Of taking possession and</bl> <bl>prescription through long time.</bl>

units.la: Quae & quomodo adquiruntur res Jure Civili?
units.tr: What things are acquired by civil law, and how?

units.la: Constitutionem promulgavit Imperator, qua cautum est, ut res quidem mobiles per triennium: immobiles vero per longi temporis possessionem, id est, inter praesentes decennio, inter absentes viginti annis usucapiantur: Et his modis non solum in Italia, sed etiam in omni terra, quae Imperatoris imperio gubernatur, dominia rerum, justa causa possessionis praecedente, adquirantur. in princip. in stit.[?] eod.
units.tr: The Emperor promulgated a constitution by which it was provided that movable things are usucapted by three years' possession, but immovable things by possession of a long time, namely ten years between those who are present and twenty years between those who are absent; and by these modes ownership of things is acquired, with a just cause of possession preceding, not only in Italy but in every land governed by the Emperor's rule. Inst. at the beginning of the same title.

units.la: Quando non procedit usucapio?
units.tr: When does usucapion not take effect?

units.la: Si quis liberum hominem, vel rem sacram vel religiosam, vel servum fugitivum possideat. Furtivae quoq; res & quae vi possessae sunt, nec si praedicto longo tempore bona fide possessae fuerint, usucapi possunt.§.sed aliquando.& §.furtivae.inst.eod.
units.tr: If someone possesses a free man, or a sacred or religious thing, or a fugitive slave. Stolen things also, and those taken by force, cannot be usucapted, not even if they have been possessed in good faith for the aforesaid long time. Inst. same title, §. sed aliquando and §. furtivae.

units.la: Potestne aliquando res furtiva usucapi?
units.tr: Can a stolen thing ever be usucapted?

units.la: Aliquando furtiva vel vi possessa res usucapi potest: veluti si in Domini potestatem reversa fuerit: Tunc enim vitio rei purgato, procedit ejus usucapio.§.aliquando.inst.eod.
units.tr: Sometimes a stolen thing, or one taken by force, can be usucapted: for example, if it has returned into the power of the owner; for then, once the defect of the thing has been cleansed, its usucapion proceeds. Inst. same title, §. aliquando.

units.la: Potestne res fisci usucapi?
units.tr: Can the property of the treasury be usucapted?

units.la: Res fisci, <bl>das gut fürstliches schatzes</bl> / usucapi non potest.§.res fisci.inst.eod.
units.tr: The property of the treasury, <bl>the goods of the princely treasury</bl>, cannot be usucapted. Inst. same title, §. res fisci.

units.la: QUIS EST SEPTIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SEVENTH TITLE?

units.la: De donationibus. <bl>Von schencken</bl> <bl>vnd gaben.</bl>
units.tr: On donations. On gifts and presents.

units.la: Estne & aliud genus adquisitionis?
units.tr: Is there also another kind of acquisition?

units.la: EST & aliud genus adquisitionis, Donatio. Donationum autem duo sunt genera:Mortis causa, & non mort's causa. in principio eodem.
units.tr: There is also another kind of acquisition, donation. Donations are of two kinds: those made in view of death (mortis causa) and those not made in view of death. At the beginning of the same title.

units.la: Quid est mortis causa Donatio?
units.tr: What is a donation made in view of death?

units.la: Quæ fit propter mortis suspicionem: cùm quis ita donat, ut si quid humanitùs ei contigisset, haberet is, qui accepit: sin autem superuixisset[?], is qui donauit reciperet: vel si eum donationis pœnituisset: aut prior decesserit is, cui donatum sit. §. mortis causa. inst. eod.
units.tr: It is one made in expectation of death: when someone gives on the condition that, if something should happen to him from human causes, the recipient is to have it; but if he should survive, the donor is to get it back; or if he should regret the gift; or if the recipient should die first. Institutes, same title, §. mortis causa.

units.la: Quæ sunt donationes non mortis causa?
units.tr: What are donations not made in view of death?

units.la: Quæ sine ulla mortis cogitatione fiunt, quas inter vivos appellamus: quæ si iuerint perfectæ, temerè revocari non possunt. Perficiuntur autem, cùm donatoi suam voluntatem scriptis aut sine scriptis manifestauerit. §. aliæ autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: Those made without any thought of death, which we call inter vivos (between the living). Once these are completed they cannot be rashly revoked. They are completed when the giver has declared his will either in writing or without writing. Institutes, same title, §. aliae autem.

units.la: Quando opus est insinuatione?
units.tr: When is insinuation necessary?

units.la: Si summa donationis excesserit quingentos solidos, opus est insinuatione. <bl>wenn die summa der</bl> <bl>geschenckes ist über fünff hundert gülden/ so ist von nöten</bl> <bl>öffentlicher vertündigung beim Richter des versas-</bl> <bl>sers geschenckes in schrifft.</bl> d. §. aliæ autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: If the sum of the donation exceeds five hundred solidi, insinuation is necessary. If the sum of the gift is more than five hundred guilders, a public declaration of the gift in writing before the judge of the giver's place is necessary. Same passage as above, §. aliae autem, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Possuntne revocari Donationes?
units.tr: Can donations be revoked?

units.la: Etsi plenissimæ sint donationes: si tamen ingrati existant homines, in quos beneficium collatum est: Donatoribus per constitutionem licentiam præstitit imperator certis ex causis eas revocare. §. sciendum. inst. eod.
units.tr: Even if donations are made in full, yet if the people on whom the benefit was conferred prove ungrateful, the emperor by constitution granted donors license to revoke them for certain causes. Institutes, same title, §. sciendum.

units.la: Estne aliud genus Donationis inter vivos?
units.tr: Is there another kind of donation between the living?

units.la: Est & aliud genus inter vivos donationis, quod propter nuptias vocatur. §. final. inst. eod.
units.tr: There is also another kind of donation between the living, which is called donation on account of marriage. Institutes, same title, §. final.

units.la: Est autem notandum, quòd donatio propter nuptias ea est, quam maritus constituit uxori propter matrimonium, respectu dotis sibi datæ, in compensationem dotis. Sicut enim dos à muliere adfertur ad maritum, ita hæc donatio constituitur à marito uxori.l.cùm multæ. C.de donationib. ante nupt.
units.tr: It should be noted that a donation on account of marriage is that which a husband settles on his wife because of the marriage, in return for the dowry given to him, as compensation for the dowry. For just as the dowry is brought by the wife to the husband, so this donation is settled by the husband on the wife. Law "cum multae", Code, on donations before marriage.

units.la: Et hanc vulgò appellamus, <bl>ein gegenvermachung</bl> <bl>oder leibgedinge</bl>. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: And we commonly call this "a counter-bequest or life annuity" (ein gegenvermachung oder leibgedinge). See Schneidewin.

units.la: QVIS EST OCTAVVS Titulus? Quibus alienare licet vel non. Welchen gestattet wird ihre güter zu ent-frömbden oder nicht.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE EIGHTH TITLE? Which persons are permitted to alienate their goods or not.

units.la: Potestne is qui Dominus est, semper alienare?
units.tr: Can the one who is owner always alienate?

units.la: Accidit aliquando, ut qui Dominus sit, alienare non possit: Et contrà qui Dominus non sit, alienandæ rei potestatem habeat. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: It sometimes happens that the owner cannot alienate, and conversely that one who is not the owner has the power to alienate the thing. Beginning of the same title in the Institutes.

units.la: Potestne maritus dotale prædium alienare?
units.tr: Can a husband alienate dotal land?

units.la: Dotale prædium maritus invita muliere per legem Juliam prohibetur alienare: quamvis ipsius sit, dotis causa ei datum. Neque alienatio vel obligatio consentientibus mulieribus procedat, ne sexus muliebris fragilitas in perniciem substantiæ earum convertatur. §. cum enim. inst. cod.
units.tr: Under the Julian law a husband is forbidden to alienate dotal land against his wife's will, even though it is his own, given to him for the sake of the dowry. Nor does an alienation or obligation proceed with the women's consent, lest the frailty of the female sex be turned to the ruin of their property. Institutes, same title, §. cum enim.

units.la: Potestne creditor pignus alienare?
units.tr: Can a creditor alienate a pledge?

units.la: Creditor pignus ex pactione, quamvis ejus ea res non sit, alienare poterit. §. contrà autem. inst. cod.
units.tr: A creditor may alienate a pledge by agreement, even though the thing is not his own. Institutes, same title, §. contra autem.

units.la: Possuntne pupilli alienare?
units.tr: Can wards alienate?

units.la: Nunc admonendi sumus, neque pupillum, neque pupillam, ullam rem sine tutoris authoritate alienare posse. §. nunc admonendi. inst eod.
units.tr: Now we must be reminded that neither a male ward nor a female ward can alienate anything without the authority of the guardian. Institutes, same title, §. nunc admonendi.

units.la: QVIS EST NONVS TITVLVS? Per quas personas cuique adquiritur. Durch welche personen einem etwas erworben wird.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE NINTH TITLE? Through which persons anything is acquired for someone. Through which persons something is acquired for one.

units.la: Quæ sunt illæ personæ?
units.tr: What are those persons?

units.la: Adquiritur vobis, dicit Imperator, non solùm per vosmetipsos, sed etiam per eos, quos in potestate habetis. Item per servos, in quibus usumfructum habetis. Item per homines liberos, & per servos alienos, quos bona fide possidetis. in princ. instit.cod.
units.tr: Acquisition is made for you, says the emperor, not only through yourselves but also through those whom you have in your power. Likewise through slaves in whom you have usufruct. Likewise through free men, and through the slaves of others, whom you possess in good faith. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Cui adquiritur, si filius aliquid adquirit?
units.tr: To whom is it acquired, if a son acquires something?

units.la: Sancitum est ab Imperatore, ut si quid ex re patris ei obvenat, hoc secundùm antiquam observationem totum parenti adquiratur. Quod autem ex alia causa sibi filiusfamilias acquisivit: hujus usumfructum patri quidem adquirat: Dominium autem apud eum remaneat: ne quod ei suis laboribus, vel prospera fortuna accesserit, hoc in alium proveniens, luctuosum ei procedat. §. igitur inst.eod.
units.tr: The emperor has enacted that if anything comes to him from his father's property, according to the ancient practice the whole of it is acquired for the parent. But what the son under power has acquired from another cause, the father acquires the usufruct of it, while ownership remains with the son, lest whatever has come to him through his own labours or good fortune should, passing to another, turn out sorrowful for him. Institutes, same title, §. igitur.

units.la: Quantum pater emancipando filium, ex ejus rebus, quæ adquisitionem effugiebant, retinere potest?
units.tr: How much of the son's property, which escaped acquisition, can a father keep when he emancipates him?

units.la: Statuit Imperator, ut parens pro tertia parte Domini, quam retinere poterat, dimidiam non dominij rerum, sed usufructus retineat. §. hoc quoq;. instit.eod.
units.tr: The emperor has ordained that the parent, in place of the third part of ownership which he could retain, keeps not half the ownership of the things but only the usufruct. Institutes, same title, §. hoc quoque.

units.la: Quæ per servos possunt adquiri?
units.tr: What can be acquired through slaves?

units.la: Vobis adquiritur, inquit Imperator, quod servi vestri ex traditione nanciscuntur: sive quid stipulentur, sive ex donatione, vel ex legato, vel alia qualibet causa adquirant. §. item vobis. instit.eod.
units.tr: It is acquired for you, says the emperor, whatever your slaves obtain by delivery: whether they stipulate something, or acquire it by gift, by legacy, or by any other cause. Institutes, same title, §. item vobis.

units.la: Recita transitionem.
units.tr: Recite the transition.

units.la: Hactenus tantisper admonuisse sufficiat, quemadmodum singulæ res vobis adquirantur. Legatorum autem jus, quo & ipso singulæ res vobis adquiruntur: Item fideicommissorum, ubi singulæ res vobis relinquutur, opportunius inferiore loco referemus.
units.tr: It is enough to have advised thus far briefly how individual things are acquired for you. The right of legacies, by which individual things are also acquired for you, as well as fideicommissa, where individual things are left to you, we will treat more conveniently in a lower place.

units.la: Videamus itaque nunc quibus modis per vniversitatem ic-vo-is[?] adquirantur. Ac prius de hæred[?] tatibus dispiciamus: quarum duplex cōditio est Nam vel ex testamento (quæ testamentariæ nominantur) vel ab intestato (quæ proprie legitimæ dicuntur) ad vos pertinent.
units.tr: Let us therefore now see by what modes things are acquired for you by universal succession. And first let us examine inheritances, of which there is a double condition: for they belong to you either by testament (which are called testamentary) or without a will (which are properly called legitimate).

units.la: Et prius est ut de his dispiciamus, quæ ex testamento vobis obveniunt: qua in re necessarium est initiū de ordinandis testamentis exponere. §.final.inst.cod.
units.tr: And first we should consider those which come to you by testament; in this matter it is necessary to explain at the outset the ordering of wills. Institutes, same title, §. final.

units.la: QVIS EST DECIMVS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TENTH TITLE?

units.la: De testamentis ordinandis. <bl>Von testa-</bl> <bl>menten zumachen / oder letzten</bl> <bl>willen aufzurichten.</bl>
units.tr: On making wills, or drawing up a last testament.

units.la: Unde appellatur Testamentum?
units.tr: Whence is the testament so called?

units.la: TEstamentū ex eo appellatur, quòd testatio mentis fit. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: A testament is so called because the mind is testified (testatio mentis). Inst. Cod., beginning.

units.la: Quot genera testamentorum olim in usu fuerunt?
units.tr: What kinds of testaments were once in use?

units.la: Sciendum est, olim quidem duo genera testamentorum in usu fuisse: quorum altero in pace & otio utebantur, quod calatis comitiis appellabant: altero, cùm in prælium exituri essent, quod procinctum dicebatur. Accesit deinde tertium genus testamentorum, quod dicebatur per æs & libram (scil. quod per emancipationem, id est, imaginariam quandam venditionem agebatur, quinq; testibus & libripende, civibus Romanis puberibus p[?]ræsentibus[?], & eo qui familiæ emptor dicebatur. §.sed ut nihil. institut. cod.
units.tr: It should be known that formerly two kinds of testament were in use. One was used in peace and leisure, and was called the calate comitia. The other was used when men were about to go out to battle, and was called the procinctum. A third kind of testament was later added, which was made per aes et libram, that is, by a kind of imaginary sale called emancipation, carried out before five witnesses, a balance-holder, Roman citizens of full age being present, and the one called the buyer of the family. §. But as nothing... Inst. Cod.

units.la: Quot sunt hodie genera testamentorum?
units.tr: What kinds of testament are there today?

units.la: Duo: alterum paganicum, & alterum militare. Paganicum est quod domi fit extra militiam. <bl>Das zu</bl> <bl>hauß außerhalb dem Frieg[?] gemacht wird</bl>, cujus duæ sunt species: Aliud enim Testamentum solenne sive in scriptis appellatur: aliud testamentum nuncupativum dicitur, q℘[?] sine scriptis fit. Vide Schneidewin.
units.tr: There are two: the civil (pagan) testament and the military testament. The civil testament is made at home, outside military service, and it has two forms. One is called the solemn or written testament; the other is called the nuncupative testament, which is made without writing. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quomodo testamenta solennia ordinantur?
units.tr: How are solemn testaments drawn up?

units.la: Cùm paulatim tàm ex usu hominum, quàm ex constitutionum emendationibus cœpit in unam conlonantiam[?] jus civile & prætorium jungi: constitutum est, ut uno eodemq; tempore (quod jus civile quodammodo exigebat) septē testibus adhibitis, & subscriptione testium, quod ex constitutionibus inventum est, & ex edicto prætoris) signacula testamentis imponerentur: ita, ut hoc jus tripertitum esse videatur: Et testes quidem & eorum præsentia uno contextu testamenti celebrandi gratia, à jure civili descendunt: subscriptiones autem testatoris & testium, ex Sacrarum constitutionum observatione adhibeantur: signacula autem, & testium numerus, ex edicto prætoris. Sed his omnibus à Constitutione Imperatoris propter testamentorum sinceritatem, ut nulla fraus adhibeatur, hoc additum est: ut per manus testatoris vel testium nomen hæredis exprimatur, & omnia secundùm illius constitutionis tenorem procedant. § sed cum paulatim. inst. eod.
units.tr: When, little by little, both by the practice of men and by the amendments of the constitutions, civil law and praetorian law began to be joined into one harmony, it was established that at one and the same time (which civil law in a way required), seven witnesses being present, and with the subscription of the witnesses (which was found in the imperial constitutions) and by the edict of the praetor, seals should be set upon the testament. So this law appears to have three parts. The witnesses, and their presence for the sake of completing a single instrument of the testament, derive from civil law; the signatures of the testator and the witnesses are required by observance of the sacred constitutions; the seals and the number of witnesses come from the edict of the praetor. But to all these things the constitution of the Emperor added this, for the sake of the sincerity of testaments, so that no fraud may be employed: that the name of the heir be expressed by the hand of the testator or of the witnesses, and that everything proceed according to the tenor of that constitution. §. But since little by little... Inst. eod.

units.la: Possuntne testes uno annulo signare?
units.tr: Can witnesses sign with one ring?

units.la: Possunt omnes testes & uno annulo signare testamentum. Sed & alieno quoque annulo licet signare testamentum §. possunt. inst. eod.
units.tr: All the witnesses can sign the testament with one ring. Indeed, it is also permitted to sign a testament with another's ring. §. Possunt. Inst. eod.

units.la: Qui possunt esse testes in testamento?
units.tr: Who can be witnesses to a testament?

units.la: Testes adhiberi possunt ij, cum quibus testamenti factio est. Sed neq; mulier, neq; impubes, neq; servus, neq; furiosus,neq; mutus,neq; surdus,neq; is, cui bonis interdictum est, der in die acht <bl>ist gethan</bl>/ neq; ij, quos leges jubent improbos intestabiles q; esse, pos-sunt in numerum testium adhiberi. §.testes autem. instit.eod.
units.tr: Those may be admitted as witnesses who have the capacity to make a testament. But a woman, a minor below the age of puberty, a slave, a madman, a mute, a deaf person, one whose goods have been placed under interdiction, one who has been put under the ban, nor those whom the laws order to be infamous and incapable of giving testimony, can be counted among the witnesses. §. Testes autem. Inst. eod.

units.la: Possúntne pater & duo fratres testes esse?
units.tr: Can a father and two brothers be witnesses?

units.la: Pater,nec nō is,qui in potestate ejus est. Item duo fratres,qui in ejusdem patris potestate[?] lunt, utiq; testes in uno testamento fieri possunt: quia nihil nocet, ex una domo plures testes alieno negotio adhiberi.§.pater.inst.eod.
units.tr: A father, and likewise the one who is in his power, may be witnesses. Likewise two brothers who are in the power of the same father can certainly be witnesses to one testament, because it does no harm for several witnesses from one household to be called to another's business. §. Pater. Inst. eod.

units.la: Possúntne hæres, & qui ei conjunctì sunt in testamento testes esse?
units.tr: Can the heir, and those joined to him, be witnesses in a testament?

units.la: Neq; hæres scriptus, neq; is, qui in potestate ejus est,neq; pater ejus,qui eum habet in potestate,neque fratres, qui in ejusdem patris potestate sunt,testes adhiberi possunt.§.sed neq;.inst.eod.
units.tr: Neither a written heir, nor the one who is in his power, nor his father who has him in power, nor brothers who are in the power of the same father, may be admitted as witnesses. §. Sed neque. Inst. eod.

units.la: Legatarijs autem & fideicommissarijs, quia non juris successores sunt,& aliis personis eis conjunctis testimonium non denegat Imperator.§. legatariis. instit.eo.
units.tr: But the Emperor does not deny testimony to legatees and fideicommissary beneficiaries, because they are not successors in law, nor to other persons joined to them. §. Legatariis. Inst. eod.

units.la: In qua materia potest scribi testamentum?
units.tr: On what material may a testament be written?

units.la: Nihil interest, testamentum in tabulis, an in chartis, membranisve vel in alia materia fiat.§. nihil autem.inst.eod.
units.tr: It makes no difference whether the testament is made on tablets, on paper, on parchment, or on some other material. §. Nihil autem. Inst. eod.

units.la: Potéstne quis plura testamenti sui exem- plaria scribere?
units.tr: Can someone make several copies of his testament?

units.la: Unum testamentum pluribus codicibus conficere quis potest.§.sed & unum.inst.eod.
units.tr: One testament may be drawn up in several copies. §. Sed et unum. Inst. eod.

units.la: Sufficiúntne hæc de scriptis testamentis?
units.tr: Are these things sufficient concerning written testaments?

units.la: Hæc quidem de testamentis, quæ scriptis conficiuntur, sufficiunt: si quis autem sine scriptis voluerit ordinare jure civili testamentum: septem testibus adhibitis, & sua voluntate coram eis nücupata, sciat hoc perfectissimum testamentum jure civili, firmumq; constitutum. §. final. inst. cod.
units.tr: These things concerning testaments that are made in writing are enough. But if anyone wishes to make a testament under civil law without writing, let him know that, with seven witnesses admitted and his will declared before them by word of mouth, this is held to be the most perfect testament under civil law and firmly established. §. Final. Inst. cod.

units.la: QUIS EST UNDECIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE ELEVENTH TITLE?

units.la: De militari testamento. Von der Kriegsleut[?] testament. Estne supra dicta diligens observatio in ordinandis testamentis, militibus propter nimiam imperi- tiam eorum constitutionibus prin- cipalibus remissa?
units.tr: On the military testament. Von der Kriegsleut[?] testament. Is the careful observance above mentioned in ordering testaments remitted to soldiers, by imperial constitutions, on account of their great inexperience?

units.la: EST, nam quanvis ij neq; legitimum numerum testium adhibuerint, neq; aliam testamentorum solennitatem observaverint, <bl>Der testamenten Sier-</bl> <bl>ligkeit halten</bl>: rectè nihilominus testantur, videlicet cum in expeditionibus occupati sunt. in princip. institut.cod.
units.tr: It is. For although they have neither employed the lawful number of witnesses nor observed any other solemnity of testaments (Der testamenten Sierligkeit halten), nevertheless they make a valid will, namely when they are occupied in campaigns. In the beginning of the Institutes, Code.

units.la: Quid autem si non sunt in castris aut expeditionibus?
units.tr: But what if they are not in camp or on campaign?

units.la: Illis temporibus, per quæ citra expeditionum necessitatem in aliis locis vel suis ædibus degunt: minimè ad vendicandum tale privilegium adjuvantur: sed testari quidem, etsi filiifamiliarum sint, propter militiam conceduntur: iure tamè communi eadem observatione & in eorum testamentis adhibenda, quam in testamentis paganorum proximè exposuimus. §. illis autem inst. cod.
units.tr: In those times during which, apart from the necessity of campaigns, they live in other places or in their own houses, they are by no means helped to claim such a privilege. But they are granted the power to make a will on account of military service, even if they are sons under paternal power; yet under the common law the same observance that we have just set out for the wills of civilians is to be employed also in their wills. Institutes, Code, the section "Illis autem".

units.la: Possuntne mutus & surdus testamen- tum facere?
units.tr: Can a mute and deaf man make a testament?

units.la: Quinimò & mutus & surdus miles testamentum facere potest. §. quinimò. inst. cod.
units.tr: Indeed, even a mute and deaf soldier can make a testament. Institutes, Code, the section "Quinimo".

units.la: QUIS EST DUODECIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWELFTH TITLE?

units.la: Quibus non est permissum facere testa- mentum. <bl>Welchen nicht zugelassen</bl> <bl>ist testament zu machen.</bl>
units.tr: Those to whom it is not permitted to make a will. <bl>Welchen nicht zugelassen</bl> <bl>ist testament zu machen.</bl> Note: the German glosses in the bl lines are reproduced as printed, since they are not Latin.

units.la: Num omnibus licet facere testamentum?
units.tr: Is it permitted to everyone to make a will?

units.la: NON tamen omnibus licét facere testamentum. Statim enim ij, qui alieno juri subjecti sunt, testamenti faciendi jus non habent. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Not, however, is it permitted to everyone to make a will. For first, those who are subject to another's authority do not have the right to make a will. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Qui præterea non possunt facere testamentum?
units.tr: Who else cannot make a will?

units.la: Præterea testamentum facere non possunt impuberes: quia nullum eorum animi judicium est. Item furiosi: quia mente carent. §. præterea. inst. eod.
units.tr: Further, minors below the age of puberty cannot make a will, because none of them has the judgement of mind. Likewise madmen, because they lack reason. §. Præterea, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Item prodigus, cui bonorum suorum administratio interdicta est, testamentum facere non potest. §. item prodigus. inst. eod.
units.tr: Likewise a prodigal, whose administration of his goods has been forbidden, cannot make a will. §. Item prodigus, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Item surdus & mutus non semper testamentum facere possunt. Utriq; autem de eo surdo loquimur, qui omnino non exaudit. Nam & mutus is intelligitur, qui eloqui nihil potest, non qui tarde loquitur. §. item surdus. inst. eod.
units.tr: Likewise a deaf man and a mute man cannot always make a will. We speak of a deaf man only in the case of one who does not hear at all; for a mute man is understood to be one who cannot utter anything at all, not one who speaks slowly. §. Item surdus, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Cæcus autem non potest facere testamentum, inquit Imperator, nisi per observationem, quam lex Divi Justini patris nostri introduxit. §. cæcus autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: But a blind man cannot make a will, says the Emperor, except by the formality which the law of the Divine Justin, our father, introduced. §. Cæcus autem, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Ejus, qui apud hostes est, testamentum, quod ibi fecit, non valet quamvis redierit. §. final. inst. eod.
units.tr: The will of a man who is among the enemy is not valid, what he made there, even if he has returned. §. Final, Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS tertius Titulus?
units.tr: What is the Tenth, Third Title?

units.la: De exhæredatione liberorum. <bl>Von ent-</bl> <bl>erbung der kinder.</bl>
units.tr: On the disinheriting of children.

units.la: H
units.tr: H

units.la: Quomodo liberi sunt exhaeredandi?
units.tr: How are children to be disinherited?

units.la: QUi filium in potestate habet, curare debet, ut eum haeredem instituat vel exhaeredem eum nominatim faciat, alioqui si eum silentio praeterierit inutiliter testabitur. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: Whoever has a son in his power must take care either to make him heir or to disinherit him by name. Otherwise, if he passes him over in silence, his will is ineffective.

units.la: Suntne & posthumi nominatim exh- aeredandi?
units.tr: Must posthumous children also be disinherited by name?

units.la: Posthumi quoq; liberi, vel haeredes instituii debet, vel exhaeredari. §. posthumi. inst. cod.
units.tr: Posthumous children too must either be instituted heirs or be disinherited.

units.la: Quid dicis de nepotibus?
units.tr: What do you say about grandchildren?

units.la: Nepotem neptemve ex filio necesse est vel haeredem instituere, vel exhaeredare. §. posthumorum. inst. cod.
units.tr: A grandson or granddaughter born of a son must either be instituted heir or be disinherited.

units.la: Quid dicis de emancipatis liberis?
units.tr: What do you say about emancipated children?

units.la: Emancipatos liberos jure civili neq; haeredes instituere neque exhaeredare necesse est: quia non sunt sui haeredes. §. emancipatos. inst. cod.
units.tr: Under civil law, emancipated children need be neither instituted heirs nor disinherited, because they are not "their own heirs."

units.la: Quid dicis de adoptivis liberis?
units.tr: What do you say about adopted children?

units.la: Adoptivi liberi quandiu sunt in potestate patris adoptivi, ejusdem juris habentur, cujus sunt justis nuptiis quaesiti: Itaq; haeredes instituendi vel exhaeredandi sunt secundum ea, quae de naturalibus exposuimus. §. adoptivi. inst. cod.
units.tr: As long as adopted children remain in the power of the adoptive father, they are regarded as having the same standing as those born in lawful marriage. Therefore they are to be instituted heirs or disinherited in the same way as we have explained for natural children.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS quartus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the fourth title of the tenth?

units.la: De haeredibus instituendis. Von Erben einsetzen.
units.tr: On appointing heirs.

units.la: Quinam possunt haeredes instituí?
units.tr: Who may be instituted heirs?

units.la: HAeredes instituere permissum est tam liberos homines, quam servos: Et tam proprios, quam alienos. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: It is permitted to institute heirs both free men and slaves, and both one's own and others'. Inst. (beginning).

units.la: Cogitúrne servus proprius institutus hæ- reditatem adire?
units.tr: Is a slave of one's own, instituted heir, compelled to enter the inheritance?

units.la: Servus a Domino suo hæres institutus, siquidem in eadem causa manserit: fit ex testamento liber hæresque ei necessarius. Si vero a vivo testatore manumissus fuerit, suo arbitrio adire hereditatem potest: quia non fit hæres necessarius. §. servus autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: A slave instituted heir by his master, provided he remains in the same condition, is made free by the will and becomes a necessary heir to him. But if he is manumitted by the testator while still alive, he may enter the inheritance at his own discretion, because he does not become a necessary heir. Inst., the paragraph on the slave.

units.la: Possúntne plures, quàm unus hæres institui?
units.tr: Can more than one heir be instituted?

units.la: Et unum hominem, & plures usque in infinitum, quot quis hæredes velit, facere licet. §. & unum, instit. eod.
units.tr: One may appoint one person or several, even an unlimited number, as many heirs as one wishes. Inst., the paragraph on "one."

units.la: In quot partes dividitur hæreditas?
units.tr: Into how many parts is an inheritance divided?

units.la: Hæreditas plærunque dividitur in duodecim uncias, quæ assis appellatione continentur. Habent autem & hæ partes propria nomina ab uncia usque ad assem, hæc: Sextans, quadrans, triens, quincunx, semis, septunx, bes, dodrans, dextans, deunx. Non autem utique semper duodecim uncias esse oportet. Nam tot unciæ assem efficiunt, quot testator voluerit. §. 5. inst. eod.
units.tr: An inheritance is usually divided into twelve ounces, which together make up the name of the as. These parts also have their own names, from the ounce up to the as: the sixth, the quarter, the third, the five-twelfths, the half, the seven-twelfths, the two-thirds, the three-quarters, the five-sixths, and the eleven-twelfths. But it is not always necessary that there be twelve ounces, for the number of ounces that make up the as is as many as the testator wishes. Inst., paragraph 5.

units.la: Estne semper partium distributio ne- cessaria?
units.tr: Is the division into parts always necessary?

units.la: Si plures instituantur hæredes: ita demum in hoc casu partium distributio necessaria est, si nolit testator eos ex æquis partibus hæredes esse. Satis enim constat, nullis partibus nominatim, ex æquis partibus eos hæredes esse. §. si plures. inst. eod.
units.tr: If several heirs are instituted, then division into parts is necessary in this case only if the testator does not wish them to be heirs in equal shares. For it is well established that, where no parts are named, they are heirs in equal shares. Inst., the paragraph on "if several."

units.la: Si pars aliqua vacet, nec tamen quisquam sine parte sit hæres institutus, quid juris?
units.tr: If some part is vacant, yet no one has been instituted without a part, what is the law?

units.la: Constat vacantem partem singulis tacitè pro hæreditaria parte accedere, & perinde haberi, ac si ex tertiis partibus hæredes scripti essent: Et ex diverbo, si plures hæredes scripti in portionibus sint: tacitè singulis decrescere. §.videamus.inst.cod.
units.tr: It is established that a vacant part accrues tacitly to each of the heirs in proportion to his share of the inheritance, and they are regarded as if they had been named heirs in thirds; and conversely, if several heirs are named in fixed shares, the share of each tacitly diminishes. Inst., "let us see."

units.la: Quid habet is qui sine parte insti- tutus est?
units.tr: What does one who was instituted without a part receive?

units.la: Si plures unciæ, quàm duodecim distributæ sint: is, qui sine parte institutus est, quod dupondio deest habebit § & si plures.inst.cod.
units.tr: If more than twelve ounces are distributed, the person instituted without a part will have what is lacking from the dupondius. Inst., the paragraph "and if more."

units.la: Dupondium autem appellatur, si as dupletur & in viginti quatuor uncias deducatur. Tripondium dicitur quando as in triginta sex uncias dividitur. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: The dupondius is called so when the as is doubled and reduced to twenty-four ounces. The tripondius is so called when the as is divided into thirty-six ounces. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Qualiter hæres institui potest?
units.tr: In what way can an heir be instituted?

units.la: Hæres & purè & sub conditione institui potest: Ex certo tempore, aut ad certum tempus non potest. §.hæres.inst.cod.
units.tr: An heir can be instituted either purely or under a condition; he cannot be instituted from a certain time or until a certain time. Inst., the paragraph "heir."

units.la: Impossibilis conditio in institutionibus & legatis, nec nō in fideicommissis & libertatibus, pro non scripta habetur. §.impossibilis.inst.cod.
units.tr: An impossible condition in institutions and legacies, and likewise in trusts and manumissions, is regarded as not written. Inst., the paragraph "impossible."

units.la: Potestne quis instituere hæredes, quos nunquam vidit?
units.tr: Can someone institute as heirs persons whom he has never seen?

units.la: Ii, quos nunquam testator vidit, hæredes institui possunt: veluti si fratris filios peregrinantes, ignoras qui essent, hæredes instituerit: Ignorantia enim testantis inutilem institutionem non facit. §.final.instit.cod.
units.tr: Those whom the testator never saw can be instituted heirs: for example, if he appointed as heirs the sons of his brother, who were travelling abroad, and whom he did not know; for the testator's ignorance does not make the institution invalid. Inst., final paragraph.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS quintus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the fifth title of the tenth?

units.la: De vulgari substitutione. <bl>Von gemei-</bl> <bl>ner nach erbsatzung[?].</bl>
units.tr: On common (vulgar) substitution. <bl>On the substitution of heirs in general.</bl>

units.la: Quonam pacto consulitur testatori, si forte hæ- res aut hæredes plures testamentum recusarent?
units.tr: In what way is provision made for the testator if one or more heirs should refuse the will?

units.la: TUm potest in testamento suo plures gradus hæredum facere: utputa, si ille hæres non erit, ille hæres esto: Et deinceps, in quantum velit testator: ut novissimo loco in subsidium vel servum necessarium hæredem instituere possit in princ.inst.eod.
units.tr: Then the testator may make several degrees of heirs in his will: for example, "if this man will not be heir, let that man be heir"; and so on, as far as the testator wishes; so that in the last place he may appoint a necessary slave as heir in reserve (Inst. eod., princ.).

units.la: Possuntne uni hæredi plures substitui?
units.tr: Can several heirs be substituted for one heir?

units.la: Plures in unius locum possunt substitui,vel unus in plurium,vel singuli in singulorū, vel invicem ipsi, qui hæredes instituti sunt.§. Et plures. inst.eod.
units.tr: Several persons may be substituted in the place of one, or one in the place of several, or each in the place of each, or the instituted heirs may be substituted for one another (Inst. eod., §. Et plures).

units.la: Quam partem habituru̅s est is,qui substitutur?
units.tr: What share will the person who is substituted have?

units.la: Etsi ex disparibus partibus hæredes scriptos invicem substituerit, & nullam mentionem in substitutione partium habuerit: eas videtur, in substitutione partes dedisse, quas in institutione expressit.§. etsi ex.inst.eod.
units.tr: Even if he has substituted heirs appointed in unequal shares for one another, and has made no mention of shares in the substitution, he is held to have given in the substitution the shares which he expressed in the institution (Inst. eod., §. etsi ex).

units.la: QVIS EST DECIMVS sextus Titulus? De pupillari substitutione. <bl>Von der Wai-</bl> <bl>sen vnd minderjärigen nach</bl> <bl>erbfassung.</bl>
units.tr: WHO IS THE SIXTH TITLE OF THE TENTH BOOK? On pupillary substitution. Of substitution of orphans and minors in inheritance.

units.la: Quomodo quis liberis suis impuberibus substituere possit?
units.tr: How may someone substitute heirs for his children who are below puberty?

units.la: LIberis suis impuberibus, quos in potestate quis habet, non solum ita, ut supra diximus, substituere potest, id est, ut si hæredes ei non extiterint, alius sit eis hæres: sed eo amplius, ut si hæredes ei extiterint, & adhuc impuberes mortui fuerint, sit eis aliquis hæres. in princ.inst.eod. Moribus institutum est, ut quum ejus ætatis filij sint,in qua ipsi sibi testamentum facere non possunt: parentes eis faciant.in princip.eod.
units.tr: A person may substitute heirs for his children below puberty, whom he holds in his power, not only in the way we said above, that is, so that if they do not become his heirs, another shall be their heir; but further, so that if they have become his heirs and have died while still below puberty, some other heir shall be theirs. Custom has established that, since the children are of an age at which they cannot make a will for themselves, their parents make one for them.

units.la: Potestne quis mente captis liberis, licet puberibus, substituere?
units.tr: Can someone substitute heirs for children who are out of their mind, even though they have reached puberty?

units.la: Prospectum est,ut si qui mente captos habeant filios,vel nepotes,vel pronepotes cujuscunq; sexus vel gradus,liceat eis,& si puberes sint,ad exemplum pupillaris substitutionis, certas personas substituere: sin autem resipuerint, eandem substitutionem infirmari.§.qua ratione.inst.eod.
units.tr: Provision has been made that if anyone has children, or grandchildren, or great-grandchildren of either sex or any degree who are out of their mind, it is permitted for them, even if they have reached puberty, to substitute certain persons on the model of pupillary substitution; but if they recover their senses, that same substitution is invalidated.

units.la: Potestne quis liberis testamentum facere, licet sibi non faciat?
units.tr: Can someone make a will for his children without making one for himself?

units.la: Liberis suis testamentum nemo facere potest, nisi & sibi faciat. Nam pupillare testamentum,pars & sequela est paterni testamenti: adeo ut si patris testamentum non valeat: nec filij quidem valebit.§. Liberis,inst.eod.
units.tr: No one can make a will for his children unless he also makes one for himself. For a pupillary will is a part and consequence of the father's will, so that if the father's will is not valid, neither will the son's be valid.

units.la: Quamdiu licet pupillis substituere?
units.tr: How long is it permitted to substitute heirs for minors?

units.la: Masculo usque ad quatuordecim annos substitui potest: fœminæ usq; ad duodecim annos. Et si hoc tempus excesserint, substitutio evanescit.§.masculo.inst.eod.
units.tr: A male may be substituted up to the age of fourteen; a female up to the age of twelve. And if they pass this age, the substitution lapses.

units.la: QVIS EST DECIMVS septimus Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SEVENTEENTH TITLE?

units.la: Quibus modis testamenta infirmentur. Auff welche weise die testament vn- fresstig werden. Quamdiu testamentum valet?
units.tr: In what ways wills are invalidated. How long does a will remain valid?

units.la: Testamentum jure factum usque eo valet, donec rumpatur, irritumve fiat. Rumpitur autem testamentum, cum in eodem statu manente testatore, ipsius testamenti jus vitiatur. in princ.inst.cod.
units.tr: A will validly made remains valid until it is broken or made void. A will is broken when, while the testator remains in the same condition, the validity of the will itself is impaired.

units.la: Quot modis id accidit?
units.tr: In how many ways does this happen?

units.la: Tribus: Primò, si quis post factum testamentum adoptaverit sibi filium pei Imperatorem, cum, qui est sui juris: aut per praetorem secundum Imperatoris constitutionem, cum, qui in potestate parentis fuerit: testamentum ejus rumpitur, quasi agnatione sui haeredis. §.rumpitur.inst.cod.
units.tr: In three ways. First, if someone, after making a will, adopts a son for himself by imperial rescript (if he is sui iuris), or through the praetor according to the imperial constitution (if the adopted son was under a parent's power), his will is broken, as if by the agnation of a sui heres.

units.la: Secundò, posteriore quoq; testamento, quod jure perfectum est, superius rumpitur. §. posteriore. instit.cod.
units.tr: Second, an earlier will is also broken by a later will that is validly completed.

units.la: Tertiò, alio autem modo testamenta jure facta infirmantur: veluti cum is, qui fecit testamentum, capite deminutus sit. §. alio. inst.cod.
units.tr: Third, validly made wills are invalidated in another way: for example, when the person who made the will suffers a loss of status (capitis deminutio).

units.la: Infirmatur etiam testamentum, quando testator dicit se nolle superius valere?
units.tr: Is a will also invalidated when the testator says that he does not wish the earlier one to stand?

units.la: Ex hoc solo non potest infirmari testamentū quod postea testator id noluerit valere: usq; adeo, ut & si quis post factum prius testamentum posterius faceie[?] coeperit. §.ex.eo.inst.cod.
units.tr: A will cannot be invalidated merely because the testator afterwards did not wish it to stand; indeed, even if someone has begun to make a later will after making an earlier one, that alone does not break the first.

units.la: Potestne quis litis causa, aut alioqui contra leges, principem instituere?
units.tr: Can someone institute the prince as heir for the sake of a lawsuit, or otherwise against the laws?

units.la: Non potest: licet enim (inquiunt principes) legibus soluti simus, attamen legibus vivimus. §.final, inst.cod.
units.tr: He cannot. For although (as the princes themselves say) we are released from the laws, nevertheless we live under the laws.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS octavus Titulus? De inofficioso testamento. <bl>Von einem</bl> <bl>unbedachtsam testament.</bl>
units.tr: THE EIGHTH TITLE OF THE TENTH BOOK? Concerning the undutiful testament.

units.la: Cur introducta est querela de inofficioso testamento?
units.tr: Why was the complaint concerning the undutiful testament introduced?

units.la: Quia plerunq; parentes, sine causa liberos suos exheredant, vel omittunt: introductum est, ut de inofficioso testamento agere possint liberi, qui querūtur, aut iniquè se exheredatos, aut iniquè praeteritos: hoc colore, quasi non sanae mentis fuerint cum testamentum ordinarent. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Because parents often disinherit or pass over their children without cause, it was introduced so that children who complain that they have been disinherited or passed over unjustly may bring an action concerning the undutiful testament, on the pretext that the testator was not of sound mind when he made the will. (Beginning of the Institutes, same title.)

units.la: Quibus competit inofficiosi querela?
units.tr: To whom is the complaint of undutifulness available?

units.la: Non liberis tantum permissum est testamentum parentum inofficiosum accusare, verum etiam liberorum parentibus. §. non autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: Not only children are permitted to accuse a parent's testament of being undutiful, but parents may also accuse the testament of their children. (§ non autem, Institutes, same title.)

units.la: Possúntne omnes liberi de inofficioso te- stamento queri?
units.tr: Can all children complain of an undutiful testament?

units.la: Tam naturales liberi, quàm adoptati, ita demum de inofficioso testamento agere possunt, si nullo alio jure ad defuncti bona venire possint. Posthumi quoque, qui nullo alio jure venire possunt, de inofficioso agere possunt. §. tam autem. inst eod.
units.tr: Natural children, as well as adopted ones, may bring an action concerning an undutiful testament only if they cannot obtain the goods of the deceased by any other right. Posthumous children too, who cannot come to the estate by any other right, may bring an action concerning an undutiful testament. (§ tam autem, Institutes, same title.)

units.la: Quomodo haec sunt accipienda?
units.tr: How are these things to be understood?

units.la: Haec ita accipienda sunt, si nihil eis penitus à testatoribus testamento relictum est: sin verò quantacunque pars hereditatis vel res eis fuerit relicta: de inofficioso querela quiescente, id quod eis deest, usque ad quartam legitimae partis repleatur. §. sed haec, instit.eod.
units.tr: They are to be understood thus: if nothing at all has been left to the children by the testators in the will. But if any part whatever of the inheritance, or any thing at all, has been left to them, the complaint of undutifulness lapses, and what is lacking to them is made up to the fourth part of the legitimate portion. (§ sed haec, Institutes, same title.)

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS nonus Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE NINETEENTH TITLE?

units.la: De hæredum qualitate & differentia. Von mancherley art/vnd vnterscheid der Erben.
units.tr: On the quality and difference of heirs. On the various kinds and distinctions of heirs.

units.la: Quotuplices sunt hæredes?
units.tr: How many kinds of heirs are there?

units.la: Triplices: Hæredes enim aut necessarij dicuntur, aut sui & necessarij, aut extranei. in princip. instit.eod.
units.tr: There are three kinds: heirs are either necessary, or own and necessary, or outside heirs. At the beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Necessarius quis est?
units.tr: What is a necessary heir?

units.la: Necessarius hæres est servus heres institutus: idcoque sic appellatur, quia sive velit, sive nolit, omnino post mortem testatoris protinus liber & necessarius hæres fit. §. necessarius. inst.eod.
units.tr: A necessary heir is a slave instituted as heir. He is so called because, whether he wishes it or not, he becomes at once, on the testator's death, free and a necessary heir. Institutes, same title, section "necessarius".

units.la: Qui sunt sui & necessarij?
units.tr: Who are own and necessary heirs?

units.la: Sui & necessarij hæredes sunt, veluti filius, filia, nepos, neptisve ex filio, & deinceps cæteri liberi, qui in potestate morientis modo fuerint. §. sui autem. instit.eod.
units.tr: Own and necessary heirs are, for example, a son, a daughter, a grandson, a granddaughter through a son, and the other children who were under the power of the deceased at the time of death. Institutes, same title, section "sui autem".

units.la: Sui hæredes ideo appellantur, quia domestici heredes sunt, & vivo quoq; patre quodammodo domini existimantur. §. sed sui. inst.eod.
units.tr: They are called own heirs because they are heirs of the household, and even while the father is alive they are in a way regarded as masters. Institutes, same title, section "sed sui".

units.la: Qui sunt extranei?
units.tr: Who are outside heirs?

units.la: Cæteri, qui testatoris juri subjecti non sunt, extranei hæredes appellantur. Itaque liberi quoq; nostri, qui in potestate nostra non sunt, hæredes à nobis instituti, extranei hæredes nobis videntur. Qua de causa, & qui hæredes à matre instituuntur, eodem numero sunt: quia fœminæ in potestate liberos non habent. §. cæteri. inst.eod.
units.tr: All others who are not subject to the testator's authority are called outside heirs. Thus our children also, who are not under our power, when instituted heirs by us, seem to us to be outside heirs. For this reason, those who are instituted heirs by their mother belong to the same class, because women do not have children under their power. Institutes, same title, section "cæteri".

units.la: Quid in extraneis hæredibus observatur?
units.tr: What is observed concerning outside heirs?

units.la: In extraneis hæredibus illud observatur, ut sit cum eis testamenti factio: sive hæredes ipsi instituantur, sive hi, qui in potestate eorum sunt. §. in extraneis. inst.eod.
units.tr: With outside heirs this is observed: that they must have testamentary capacity, whether they are themselves instituted heirs or those who are under their power are. Institutes, same title, section "in extraneis".

units.la: Quis habet testamenti factionem?
units.tr: Who has testamentary capacity?
