units.la: Testamenti factionem non solum is habere videtur, qui testamentum facere potest: sed etiam qui ex alieno testamento vel ipse capere potest vel alij ad[?] quirere,licet non possit facere testamentum. Et ideo furiosus,& mutus,& posthumus, & infans, & filiusfamilias, & servus alienus testamenti factionem habere dicuntur. Licet enim testamentum facere non possint, attamen ex testamento vel sibi, vel alij adquirere possunt. §. in extraneis. veif. testamenti autem.inst cod.
units.tr: Testamentary capacity is held to belong not only to one who can make a will, but also to one who can either take something himself from another's will or let others acquire it, even though he cannot make a will himself. Therefore the madman, the mute, the posthumous child, the infant, the son under his father's power, and another's slave are said to have testamentary capacity. For although they cannot make a will, they can acquire something from a will, either for themselves or for others. Institutes, same title, sections "in extraneis" and "testamenti autem".

units.la: Possúntne extranei hæredes cogi ut ad- eant hæreditatem?
units.tr: Can outside heirs be compelled to enter upon the inheritance?

units.la: Extraneis[?] hæredibus deliberandi potestas est de adeunda hæreditate, vel non adeunda. §. extraneis. instit.cod.
units.tr: Outside heirs have the power of deliberation about whether to enter upon the inheritance or not. Institutes, same title, section "extraneis".

units.la: Quomodo extraneus hæreditatem pos- sit adire?
units.tr: How can an outside heir enter upon the inheritance?

units.la: Si rebus hæreditariis tanquam hæres utatur, vel vendendo res hæreditarias, vel prædia colendo,locandóve, & quoquo modo voluntatem suam declaret, vel re, vel verbo de adeunda hæreditate. §. item extraneus.inst.cod.
units.tr: If he uses the goods of the inheritance as heir, either by selling the goods of the inheritance or by cultivating or letting out the estates, and in whatever way he declares his will to accept the inheritance, by deed or by word. Institutes, same title, section "item extraneus".

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTIETH TITLE?

units.la: De legatis. <bl>Von bescheidenen gütern.</bl>
units.tr: On legacies.

units.la: Nónne pars juris de legatis extra proposi- tam materiam videtur?
units.tr: Is not part of the law on legacies outside the proposed subject?

units.la: IMò: Nam loquimur de iis juris figuris, quibus per universitatem res adquiruntur: sed cum omninò de testamentis, & de hæredibus, qui in testamento instituuntur, loquuti sumus: non sine causa sequenti loco potest hæc juris materia tractari. in princ.instit.cod.
units.tr: No. For we are speaking of those legal figures by which things are acquired through a universal succession. Since we have spoken at length about wills and about heirs instituted in a will, this subject of law can, not without reason, be treated in the next place. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid est legatum?
units.tr: What is a legacy?

units.la: <bl>Legatum,ein bescheiden gut/est</bl> donatio quædam à defuna defuncto relicta, ab hærede præstanda. §. legatum. instit. eod.
units.tr: A legacy (<bl>ein bescheiden gut</bl>) is a gift left by the deceased, to be paid by the heir. Institutes, same title, the section on legacies.

units.la: Quot erant olim genera legator- um?
units.tr: How many kinds of legacies were there formerly?

units.la: Olim quidem erant legatorum genera quatuor: per vindicationem (quando testator dicebat: vindico tibi talem rem) per damnationem (quando testator dicebat hæredi, damnatus esto Titio dare centum) sinendi modo (quando testator dicebat: sine & permitte Titium habere illum equum) per præceptionem, (quando testator dicebat, præcipito illam domum, vel habeas illam domum præ cæteris hæredibus.) Vide Schneidewinum.
units.tr: Formerly there were four kinds of legacies: (1) by vindication, when the testator said, "I vindicate such a thing to you"; (2) by condemnation, when the testator said to the heir, "Let Titius be condemned to give one hundred"; (3) by the mode of permission, when the testator said, "Allow and permit Titius to have that horse"; (4) by preception, when the testator said, "I give preference to that house," or "Let you have that house before the other heirs." See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid constitutio Justiniani disposuit?
units.tr: What did the constitution of Justinian provide?

units.la: Ut omnibus legatis una sit natura, & quibuscunque verbis aliquid relictum sit, liceat legatariis id persequi non solum per actiones personales, sed etiam per in rem: & per hypothecariam. <bl>nicht allein durch</bl> <bl>persönliche Klagen / sondern auch durch Klagen auff</bl> <bl>die güter vnd vnderpfande.</bl> §. sed olim. inst. eod.
units.tr: That all legacies should have one nature, and that, whatever words had been used to leave something, the legatees might pursue it not only by personal actions but also by actions in rem, and by the hypothecary action (<bl>not only by personal actions, but also by actions against the goods and the pledges</bl>). Institutes, same title, the section "but formerly."

units.la: Quæ res legari possunt?
units.tr: What things can be bequeathed?

units.la: Non solum autem testatoris vel hæredis res, sed etiam aliena legari potest: ita, ut hæres cogatur redimere eam & præstare: vel si non potest eam redimere, æstimationem ejus dare. <bl>Der Erbe sol das frömb-de</bl> <bl>bescheiden gut lösen vnnd bezalen: oder so er das</bl> <bl>nicht lösen kan / so sol er den werth darfür geben.</bl> §. non solum. inst. eod.
units.tr: Not only the testator's own things or the heir's, but also another's property may be bequeathed, so that the heir is compelled to buy it and deliver it; or, if he cannot buy it, to give its value (<bl>the heir shall redeem and pay the bequeathed goods of another; or if he cannot redeem them, he shall give their worth</bl>). Institutes, same title, the section "not only."

units.la: Potestne res, quæ non est, legari?
units.tr: Can a thing that does not exist be bequeathed?

units.la: Ea quaque res, quæ in rerum natura non est, si modo futura est, recte legatur: veluti fructus, qui in illo fundo nati erunt. §. ea quoque. inst. eod.
units.tr: Also a thing which is not yet in existence may validly be bequeathed, provided that it will exist in future: for example, the fruits which will be born on that farm. Institutes, same title, the section "that also."

units.la: Valetne res legata quasi aliena?
units.tr: Is a thing bequeathed as if it belonged to another valid?

units.la: Si quis rem suam quasi alienam legaverit: valet legatum. Nam plus valet quod in veritate est,quàm in opinione.§.si quis.inst.eod.
units.tr: If someone bequeaths his own thing as though it were another's, the legacy is valid. For what is true has more force than what is believed. Institutes, same title, the section "if someone."

units.la: Potestne maritus uxori dotem legare?
units.tr: Can a husband bequeath a dowry to his wife?

units.la: Si uxori maritus dotem legaverit, valet legatum: quia plenius est legatum, quàm de dote actio.§.sed si uxori.inst.eod.
units.tr: If a husband bequeaths a dowry to his wife, the legacy is valid, because the legacy is fuller than the action on the dowry. Institutes, same title, the section "but if to a wife."

units.la: Quid dicis de grege legato?
units.tr: What do you say about a bequeathed flock?

units.la: Si grex legatus fuerit: & postea ad unam ovem pervenerit: quo superfuerit, vindicari potest.
units.tr: If a flock is bequeathed, and afterwards has been reduced to a single sheep, the remaining sheep can be claimed by vindication.

units.la: Grege autem legato, etiam eas oves, quæ post testamentum factum gregi adjiciuntur, legato cedere Julianus ait.§.si grex.inst.eod.
units.tr: Julian says that when a flock is bequeathed, the sheep which are added to the flock after the will was made also pass to the legacy. Institutes, same title, the section "if a flock."

units.la: Quid dicis de ædibus legatis?
units.tr: What do you say about a bequeathed house?

units.la: Ædibus denique legatis, columnas & marmora, quæ post testamentum factum adjecta sunt, legato dicimus cedere.§.ædibus.inst.eod.
units.tr: Finally, we say that when a house is bequeathed, the columns and marble added after the will was made also pass to the legacy. Institutes, same title, the section "a house."

units.la: Quales res possunt legari?
units.tr: What kinds of things can be bequeathed?

units.la: Tàm corporales res legari possunt, quàm incorporales.§.tam autem. inst.eod.
units.tr: Corporeal things may be bequeathed, and incorporeal things as well. Institutes, same title, the section "but also."

units.la: Quibus potest legari?
units.tr: To whom can a legacy be left?

units.la: Legari illis solum potest, cum quibus testamenti factio est. Incertis verò personis neq; legata,neq; fideicommissa olim relinqui concessum erat.§.legari.inst.eod.
units.tr: A legacy can be left only to those with whom there is the capacity to make a will. Formerly it was not permitted to leave either legacies or trust bequests to uncertain persons. Institutes, same title, the section "legacies."

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS primus Titulus? De ademptione legatorum. <bl>Von entz-</bl> <bl>iehung der bescheiden güter.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTY-FIRST TITLE? On the revocation of legacies. <bl>On the withdrawal of bequeathed goods.</bl>

units.la: Quid est ademptio Legatorum?
units.tr: What is the revocation of legacies?

units.la: EST nihil aliud quàm relictorum, per contrariam voluntatem, propter poenitentiâ testatoris, puta sive conditionalis revocatio, inquit Schneidevvin.
units.tr: It is nothing other than the withdrawal of what has been bequeathed, by a contrary will, on account of the testator's repentance; that is, a conditional revocation, as Schneidewin says.

units.la: Quomos[?]
units.tr: Quomos[?]

units.la: Quomodo possunt legata adimi vel transferri?
units.tr: How can legacies be revoked or transferred?

units.la: Ademptio legatorum (sive eodem testamento adimantur, sive codicillis) firma est. Transferri quoq; legatum ab alio ad alium potest: sive in eodem testamento, sive in codicillis hoc fecerit quis. § .transferri.inst.cod.
units.tr: The revocation of legacies (whether they are withdrawn in the same will or by codicils) is valid. A legacy may also be transferred from one person to another, whether someone does this in the same will or in codicils. § transferri, Inst. de codicillis.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS secundus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the twenty-second Title?

units.la: De Lege Falcidia. <bl>Vom Gesetz Falcidia.</bl> Poteratne olim testator totum patrimon- ium per legata erog- are?
units.tr: On the Falcidian Law. Could a testator in former times dispose of his whole estate through legacies?

units.la: OLim lege duodecim tabularum libera erat legandi potestas, ut liceret vel totum patrimonium legatis erogare in princ.inst.eod.
units.tr: Formerly, under the law of the Twelve Tables, the power of bequeathing was unrestricted, so that one could even give away the whole estate in legacies.

units.la: Quid cavetur Lege Falcidia?
units.tr: What does the Falcidian Law provide?

units.la: Novissimè lata est lex Falcidia, qua cavetur, ne plus legare liceat, quàm dodrantem totorum bonorum, id est, ut sive unus hæres institutus sit, sive plures, apud eū eōsve pars quarta remaneat. in prin.inst.eod.
units.tr: The Falcidian Law was passed most recently, and it provides that one may not bequeath more than three quarters of the whole estate: that is, whether one heir or several is appointed, a quarter remains with him or them.

units.la: Diminutio patrimonii post mortem testa- toris contingens, ad quos pertinet?
units.tr: To whom does a diminution of the estate occurring after the testator's death pertain?

units.la: Si testator septuaginta quinq; aureos legaverit, & ante aditam hæreditatem in tantum decreverint bona (incendiis forte, aut naufragiis, aut morte servorum) ut non amplius, quàm septuaginta quinq; aureorum substantia vel etiam minus relinquatur: solida legata debentur. Nec ea res damnosa est hæredi, cui liberum est non adire hæreditatem: quæ res efficit,ut sit necesse legatariis, ne destituto testamento nihil consequantur, cum hærede in portione pacisci. §.quantitas.inst.eod.
units.tr: If a testator bequeathed seventy-five gold coins, and before the inheritance is entered upon the goods diminish (through fires perhaps, or shipwrecks, or the death of slaves) so that no more than the value of seventy-five gold coins, or even less, is left, the legacies are owed in full. Nor is this harmful to the heir, who is free not to enter upon the inheritance. This makes it necessary for the legatees, lest they gain nothing if the will falls through, to come to terms with the heir over a share.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS tertius Titulus? De fideicommissariis hæreditatibus, & ad Senatusconsultum Trebellianum. Von erbschafften auß trewem befelch zu ent-richten/und vom Rathsgebott Trebelliano.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTY-THIRD TITLE? On fideicommissary inheritances, and on the Senatus-consultum Trebellianum. <bl>On inheritances to be handed over under a trustful request, and on the Trebellian decree of the council.</bl>

units.la: Ecquid fideicommissa semper firma fuerunt?
units.tr: Were fideicommissa always valid?

units.la: SCiendum est omnia fideicommissa primis temporibus infirma fuisse: quia nemo invitus cogebatur præstare id, de quo rogatus erat. §. sciendum. inst. eod.
units.tr: It must be noted that all fideicommissa were invalid in the earliest times, because no one was compelled against his will to perform what he had been asked to do. Inst. eod., §. sciendum.

units.la: Quid opus est in fideicommissis?
units.tr: What is required for fideicommissa?

units.la: In primis sciendum est, opus esse, ut aliquis recto jure testamento hæres instituatur: ejusq; fidei committatur, ut eam hæreditatem alij restituat: alioqui inutile est testamentum in quo nemo hæres instituitur.§.in primis inst.eod.
units.tr: First of all it must be noted that it is required that someone be instituted heir by a valid testament, and be entrusted with a request to hand that inheritance over to another; otherwise a testament in which no one is instituted heir is useless. Inst. eod., §. in primis.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS tertius Titulus? De singulis rebus per fideicommissum relictis. Von besondern und einzeln gütern/so durch vertrewlichen befehle nachgelassen sein.
units.tr: THE TWENTY-THIRD TITLE: On individual things left by fideicommissum. Of particular and single goods left by way of trust instructions.

units.la: Quæ res per fideicommissum relinquuntur?
units.tr: What things are left by fideicommissum?

units.la: Potest quis etiam singulas res per fideicommissum relinquere: veluti, fundum, argentum, hominem, vestem, & pecuniam numeratam. in princ. inst.cod.
units.tr: One may also leave single things by fideicommissum, for example a farm, silver, a slave, a garment, and counted money.

units.la: Potestne & libertas per fideicommissum dari?
units.tr: Can liberty also be given by fideicommissum?

units.la: Libertas quoque servo per fideicommissum dari potest. §. libertas. inst. eod.
units.tr: Liberty can also be given to a slave by fideicommissum.

units.la: Quæ verba fideicommissorum in usu habentur?
units.tr: Which words of fideicommissa are commonly used?

units.la: Verba fideicommissorum hæc maximè in usu habentur: peto, rogo, volo, mando, fidei tuæ committo: quæ perinde singula firma sunt, atq; si omnia in unum congesta essent. §. final. inst. eod.
units.tr: The words most commonly used in fideicommissa are these: I ask, I request, I wish, I command, I commit to your trust. Each of these is binding in the same way as if all were gathered into one.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS quintus Titulus? De codicillis. <bl>Von schlechten testamenten.</bl>
units.tr: THE TWENTY-FIFTH TITLE: On codicils. Of informal wills.

units.la: Quid est Codicillus?
units.tr: What is a codicil?

units.la: Codicillus est ultima voluntas minus solennis, & absq; hæredis institutione, de eo quod quis post mortem suam fieri vult, coram quinq; testibus declarata. Codicillus autem sic se habet ad testamentum, sicut scapha se habet ad navem. Licet enim scapha nō sit navis magna, tamē est navis: Ita codicillus etiamsi non sit testamentum, tamen ejus naturam habet, & testatio mentis ipsius defuncti dicitur. Et concordat Titulus in. ff. de jur. codicil. & in C. de codicillis. Vide Schneidewin.
units.tr: A codicil is a less solemn last will, without institution of an heir, declaring what someone wishes to be done after his death, made before five witnesses. A codicil stands to a testament as a skiff stands to a ship. For although a skiff is not a large ship, it is still a ship; so a codicil, even if it is not a testament, has its nature and is called a declaration of the dead man's own mind. The title in the Digest on the law of codicils agrees, and so does the title in the Code on codicils. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quis primus codicillos introduxit?
units.tr: Who first introduced codicils?

units.la: Ante Augusti tempora cōstat codicillorum jus in usu non fuisse: sed primus Lucius Lentulus, ex cujus persona etiam fideicommissa esse cœperunt, codicillos introduxit. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: It is established that before the time of Augustus the law of codicils was not in use; but Lucius Lentulus, from whose person fideicommissa also began to be made, first introduced codicils.

units.la: Quando potest quis codicillos facere?
units.tr: When can someone make codicils?

units.la: Non tantum testamento facto potest quis codicillos facere: sed & intestatus quis decedens fideicommittere codicillis potest. § non tantum. inst. eod.
units.tr: Someone may make codicils not only when a testament has been made; a person dying intestate can also entrust fideicommissa by codicils.

units.la: Potestne hæreditas in codicillis dari vel adimi?
units.tr: Can an inheritance be given or taken away by codicils?

units.la: Codicillis hæreditas neque dari, neque adimi potest: ne confundatur jus testamentorum & codicillorum. Et ideo nec exhæredatio scribi. § codicillis. inst. eod.
units.tr: An inheritance can be neither given nor taken away by codicils, so that the law of testaments and of codicils is not confused. For the same reason, neither can disinheritance be written in them.

units.la: Quid ergo fieri potest in codicillis?
units.tr: What then can be done by codicils?

units.la: Per fideicommissum hæreditas codicillis jure relinquitur. § final. inst. eod. Licet enim directò in eis hæreditas dari non possit: tamen fideicommissa universalia & particularia rectè in eis relinquuntur, inquit Schneidevvinus.
units.tr: By fideicommissum an inheritance is rightly left by codicils. For although an inheritance cannot be given directly in them, universal and particular fideicommissa can rightly be left in them, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Hactenus Tituli secundi libri Institutionum breviter enarrati fuere.
units.tr: Thus far the titles of the second book of the Institutes have been briefly explained.

units.la: QUOT SUNT TITULI IN TER- tio libro Institutionum?
units.tr: HOW MANY TITLES ARE THERE IN THE THIRD BOOK OF THE INSTITUTES?

units.la: Triginta.
units.tr: Thirty.

units.la: QUIS EST PRIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIRST TITLE?

units.la: De hæreditatibus, quæ ab intestato deferuntur. <bl>Von Erbschafften / welche ohn Testament gegeben werden.</bl>
units.tr: On inheritances that pass by intestacy. On inheritances that are given without a will.

units.la: Quæ est continuatio hujus tituli ad præcedentes?
units.tr: What is the continuation of this title from the preceding ones?

units.la: IN præcedentibus titulis de hæreditatibus, quæ ex testamento ad vos pertinent, dictum est: Restat ut dicamus de hæreditatibus quæ ab intestato deferuntur.
units.tr: In the preceding titles, concerning the inheritances that come to you by will, we have spoken. It remains for us to speak of the inheritances that pass by intestacy.

units.la: Quis dicitur intestatus discedere?
units.tr: Who is said to die intestate?

units.la: Intestatus decedit, qui aut omnino testamentum non facit: aut non jure fecit: aut id quod fecerat, ruptum, irritúmve factum est, aut si ex eo nemo hæres extiterit. in princip. inst. eod.
units.tr: A person dies intestate who either makes no will at all, or does not make one lawfully, or whose will has been broken or annulled, or if no heir has come forth under it. Institutes, beginning of the same title.

units.la: Præfertúrne successio ex testamento suc- cessioni ab intestato?
units.tr: Does succession by will take precedence over succession by intestacy?

units.la: Præfertur: Quamdiu enim potest ex testamento adiri hæreditas, ab intestato non defertur. l. quamdiu.ff.de adquirend.vel omittend. hæredit.
units.tr: It does. For as long as the inheritance can be entered upon under a will, it does not pass by intestacy. Law "quamdiu", Digest, on acquiring or omitting inheritances.

units.la: Quibus primum ab intestato hæredi- tas defertur?
units.tr: To whom is the inheritance first passed on intestacy?

units.la: Intestatorum hęreditates[?] ex lege duodecim tabularum, primum ad suos hæredes pertinent. §.intestatorum.inst.cod.
units.tr: Under the law of the Twelve Tables, the inheritances of those who die intestate first belong to their own heirs. Section "intestatorum", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Qui sunt sui hæredes?
units.tr: Who are the own heirs?

units.la: Sui hæredes existimantur, ut suprà diximus, qui in potestate morientis fuerint, veluti filius, filiáve, nepos neptísve ex filio, pronepos proneptísve. Nec interest, utrū naturales sint liberi, an adoptivi. Quibus cōnumerari necesse est eos, qui ex legitimis quidem nuptiis vel matrimoniis non sunt progeniti, curiis tamen civitatum dati secundum Divalium Constitutionum, quæ[?] super his positæ sunt, tenorem, hæredum suorū jura nanciscūtur. §.sui autem. inst.cod.
units.tr: Own heirs are considered, as we said above, those who were in the power of the dying person, such as a son or daughter, a grandson or granddaughter through a son, a great-grandson or great-granddaughter. It makes no difference whether the children are natural or adopted. To these must be added those who were not born of lawful marriages or matrimony but were given to the curiae of the cities according to the terms of the imperial constitutions laid down on these matters; they acquire the rights of own heirs. Section "sui autem", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Possúntne & ignorantes sui hære- des fieri?
units.tr: Can those who are ignorant also become own heirs?

units.la: Sui hæredes fiunt etiam ignorantes, & licèt furiosi sint, hæredes possunt existere. §.sui autem hæredes fiunt.inst.cod.
units.tr: Own heirs become so even when they are ignorant, and although they may be insane, they can still be heirs. Section "sui autem heredes fiunt", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quomodo filius filiáve, & ex altero filio nepos neptísve succedunt?
units.tr: How do a son or daughter, and a grandson or granddaughter through another son, succeed?

units.la: Cum filius filiáve,& ex altero filio nepos neptísve existunt, pariter ad hæreditatem avi vocantur: nec qui gradu proximior, ulteriorem excludit: æquum enim esse videtur, nepotes, neptesq; in patris sui locum succedere.§.cum filius.inst.eod.
units.tr: When a son or daughter and a grandson or granddaughter through another son both exist, they are called equally to the grandfather's inheritance. Nor does the nearer in degree exclude the more remote, for it seems fair that the grandchildren should succeed in the place of their father. Section "cum filius", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid juris habent emancipati liberi?
units.tr: What rights do emancipated children have?

units.la: Emancipati liberi, jure civili nihil juris habent: neque enim sui hæredes sunt, qui in potestate parentis esse desierunt: neque ullo alio jure per legem duodecim tabularum vocantur: sed prætor naturali æquitate motus, dat eis bonorum possessionem, Unde Liberi, perinde ac si in potestate parentis tempore mortis fuissent: sive soli sint, sive cum suis hæredibus concurrant.§ emancipati.inst.eod.
units.tr: Emancipated children have no right under civil law. For they are not own heirs, since they have ceased to be in the parent's power, and they are not called by any other right under the Twelve Tables. But the praetor, moved by natural equity, gives them possession of the goods (whence they are called "liberi"), just as if they had been in the parent's power at the time of death, whether they are alone or share with own heirs. Section "emancipati", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Estne nepotis & pronepotis nomen commune?
units.tr: Is "grandson" and "great-grandson" a common name?

units.la: Nepotis & pronepotis nomen commune est utrisque, tàm qui ex masculis, quàm qui ex fœminis descendunt.§.item vetustas.inst. eod.
units.tr: The names "nepos" and "pronepos" are common to both, whether they descend through males or through females. Section "item vetustas", Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid Justinianus fieri iussit?
units.tr: What did Justinian order to be done?

units.la: Quemadmodum inter filios & nepotes ex filio antiquitas statuit, non in capita, sed in stirpes dividi hæreditatem, <bl>daß die erbschafft nicht in die häupter/</bl> <bl>sondern in die stamme getheilet werde/ sagt Doctor</bl> <bl>Goblerus</bl>: Similiter Justinianus inter filios & nepotes ex filia, distributionem fieri jussit, vel inter omnes nepotes & neptes, & inter pronepotes & proneptes,& alias deinceps personas: utraque progenies, matris vel patris,aviæ vel avi portionem sine ulla deminutione consequatur: ut si forte unus vel duo ex una parte,ex altera tres aut quatuor extent: unus aut duo dimidiam, alteri tres aut quatuor alteram dimidiam hæreditatis habeant.§.final.instit.cod.
units.tr: Just as ancient law determined between sons and grandsons through a son that the inheritance is divided not by heads but by stocks, "that the inheritance is not divided by heads but by stocks, says Doctor Goblerus": similarly, Justinian ordered that the distribution be made between sons and grandsons through a daughter, or among all grandsons and granddaughters, and among great-grandsons and great-granddaughters, and other persons in turn; each line, whether of mother or father, grandmother or grandfather, should obtain its share without any reduction. So if perhaps one or two are on one side and three or four on the other, the one or two should have half of the inheritance and the three or four the other half. Section "final", Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST SECUNDUS Titulus?
units.tr: Which is the second title?

units.la: De legitima agnatorum successione. Von erbung der schwertmagen.
units.tr: On the lawful succession of agnates. On the inheritance of the sword-kin (Von erbung der schwertmagen).

units.la: Ad quos pertinet hereditas suis non extantibus?
units.tr: To whom does an inheritance pass when there are no heirs of the body?

units.la: SI nemo suus haeres, vel eorum, quos inter suos haeredes praetor, vel constitutiones vocant, exstat, qui successionem quoquo modo amplectatur: tunc ex lege duodecim tabularum ad agnatum proximum pertinet hereditas. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: If no heir of the body (suus haeres), or of those whom the praetor or the constitutions call heirs among the family, is present to take up the succession in any way, then by the law of the Twelve Tables the inheritance passes to the nearest agnate. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Datürne omnibus agnatis simul hæ- reditas?
units.tr: Does the inheritance go to all agnates at once?

units.la: Non omnibus simul agnatis dat lex hæreditatem: sed iis, qui tunc proximiores gradu sunt, cum certum esse coeperit aliquem intestatum decessisse. §. sunt autem. inst. cod.
units.tr: The law does not give the inheritance to all agnates together, but to those who are nearer in degree at the time when it has begun to be certain that someone has died intestate. §. Moreover, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quem vocat lex, si plures sunt gradus agnatorum?
units.tr: Whom does the law call, if there are several degrees of agnates?

units.la: Si plures sint gradus agnatorum: aperte lex duodecim tabularum proximum vocat. Itaque, si, verbi gratia, sint defuncti frater, & alterius fratris filius, aut patruus: frater potior habetur, <bl>hat den Vorzug.</bl> Et quanvis singulari numero usa lex duodecim tabularum, proximum vocet: tamen dubium non est, quin, si plures sint ejusdem gradus, omnes admittantur. §. si plures. inst. cod.
units.tr: If there are several degrees of agnates, the law of the Twelve Tables clearly calls the nearest. Thus, for example, if the deceased left a brother and the son of another brother, or a paternal uncle, the brother is regarded as preferable (<bl>hat den Vorzug</bl>). And although the law of the Twelve Tables uses the singular and calls "the nearest," there is no doubt that if there are several of the same degree, all are admitted. §. If several. Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE THIRD TITLE?

units.la: De Senatusconsulto Tertulliano. Von dem Rathsgebott Tertylliano.
units.tr: On the Tertullian Senatus-consult. (On the Tertullian Senatus-consult, in German: concerning the Tertullian decree of the Senate.)

units.la: Quid est Senatusconsultum Ter- tyllianum?
units.tr: What is the Tertullian Senatus-consult?

units.la: EST jus, quo plenissime de tristi successione matri non etiam aviae deferenda cautum est: ut ingenua trium liberorum jus habens, libertina quatuor ad bona filiorum filiarumve admittatur intestato mortuorum. §. postea autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: It is a law by which provision is most fully made that the succession is to be deferred to the mother, and not also to the grandmother, so that a freeborn woman who has the right of three children, or a freedwoman with four, is admitted to the goods of her children, sons or daughters, who die intestate. §. postea autem. inst. eod.

units.la: Repellitúrne hodie mater, nisi certum li- berorum numerum peperit?
units.tr: Is a mother excluded today, unless she has borne a certain number of children?

units.la: Matri, inquit Imperator, subveniendum esse existimavimus: respicientes ad naturam, & puerperium, & periculum, & saepe mortem ex hoc casu matribus illatam: Ideoque impium esse credidimus, casum fortuitum in ejus admitti detrimentum. Si enim ingenua ter, vel libertina quater peperit, immerito defraudabatur successione suorum liberorum: quid enim peccavit, si non plures, sed paucos peperit? Et dedimus jus legitimum plenum matribus, sive ingenuis sive libertinis. §. sed nos. inst. eod.
units.tr: The Emperor says: "We have judged that the mother must be helped, having regard to nature, to childbirth, to the danger, and to the death that often befalls mothers from this cause. We have therefore believed it wrong that a chance event should be allowed to work to her detriment. For if a freeborn woman has borne three children, or a freedwoman four, it would be undeserved for her to be cheated of the succession to her children. For what fault has she committed if she has borne not many but few? And we have given full legal right to mothers, whether freeborn or freedwomen." §. sed nos. inst. eod.

units.la: Admittiturne mater ad bona vulgò quaesitis?
units.tr: Is a mother admitted to the goods of children born out of wedlock?

units.la: Licet vulgò quaesitus sit filius filiave: potest tamen ad bona ejus mater ex Tertylliano senatusconsulto admitti. §. final. inst. eod.
units.tr: Although the son or daughter was born out of wedlock, the mother may nevertheless be admitted to their goods under the Tertullian senatus-consult. §. final. inst. eod.

units.la: QUIS EST QUARTUS Titulus? De Senatusconsulto Orphitiano. <bl>Von</bl> <bl>dem Orphicianischen Raths-</bl> <bl>gebott.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FOURTH TITLE? On the Orphitian Senatus-consult. (On the Orphitian decree of the Senate.)

units.la: Quid est Senatusconsultum Orphitianum?
units.tr: What is the Orphitian Senatus-consult?

units.la: EST jus, quo liberi ad bona matrum intestatarum admittuntur.in princ.inst eod.
units.tr: It is a law by which children are admitted to the goods of their mothers who die intestate. in princ.inst eod.

units.la: Vocantúrne ex hoc Senatusconsulto nepotes & neptes ad aviæ successionem?
units.tr: Are grandsons and granddaughters called to the grandmother's succession under this Senatus-consult?

units.la: Ad similitudinem filiorum filiarumq; & nepotes & neptes vocantur.§.sed cùm.inst.eod.
units.tr: By analogy with sons and daughters, grandsons and granddaughters are also called. §.sed cùm.inst.eod.

units.la: Quid dicis de vulgò quæsitis?
units.tr: What do you say about children born out of wedlock?

units.la: Sciendum est etiam illos liberos, qui vulgò quæsiti sunt, <bl>von gemeinen</bl> <bl>weibern geboren</bl> / ad matris hæreditatem ex hoc Senatusconsulto admitti.§.novissimè.inst.eod.
units.tr: It must also be known that those children who were born out of wedlock, born of common women, are admitted to their mother's inheritance under this Senatus-consult. §.novissimè.inst.eod.

units.la: QUIS EST QUINTUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIFTH TITLE?

units.la: De successione cognatorum, <bl>Von er-</bl> <bl>bung der spilmagen.</bl>
units.tr: On the succession of cognates, <bl>On the</bl> <bl>inheritance of the kinsfolk by blood.</bl>

units.la: Ad quos pertinet hæreditas suis & agnatis non existentibus?
units.tr: To whom does the inheritance pass when there are no heirs of the body and no agnates?

units.la: Post suos hæredes, eosq; quos inter suos hæredes prætor & constitutiones vocant, & post legitimos, quo numero sunt agnati, & hi, quos in locum agnatorum tàm supradicta Senatusconsulta, quàm nostra erexit constitutio, proximos cognatos prætor vocat,inquit Imperator, in princ.inst.eod.
units.tr: After the heirs of the body, namely those whom the praetor and the imperial constitutions call among the heirs of the household, and after the legitimate heirs, among whom are the agnates, and those whom the aforesaid senatusconsults as well as our constitution have set in the place of agnates, the praetor calls the nearest cognates, says the Emperor at the beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Ad quos secundò pertinet hæreditas suis & agna- tis non existentibus?
units.tr: To whom does the inheritance pass secondly when there are no heirs of the body and no agnates?

units.la: Eos etiam, qui per fœminini sexus personas ex transverso cognatione junguntur, tertio gradu proximitatis nomine prætor ad successionem vocat.§. eos. inst. eod.
units.tr: The praetor also calls to the succession, by the name of the third degree of proximity, those who are joined by cognation across the line through persons of the female sex. Institutes, same title, §. eos.

units.la: Quid dicis de liberis adoptivis?
units.tr: What do you say of adopted children?

units.la: Liberi quoq;, qui in adoptiva familia sunt ad naturalium parentum hæreditatem hoc eodem gradu vocantur.§.liberi quoq;.inst.cod.
units.tr: Children also who are in an adoptive family are called to the inheritance of their natural parents in this same degree. Institutes, same title, §. liberi quoque.

units.la: Quid dicis de vulgò quæsitis?
units.tr: What do you say of those born out of wedlock?

units.la: Vulgò quæsitos, nullos habere agnatos, manifestum est: quum agnatio à patre fit, cognatio à matre: hi autem nullum patrem habere intelliguntur.§.vulgò.inst.cod.
units.tr: It is clear that those born out of wedlock have no agnates, since agnation comes from the father and cognation from the mother; but such persons are understood to have no father.  Institutes, same title, §. vulgo.

units.la: QUIS EST SEXTUS Titulus? De gradibus cognationum. Von den graden der Sipschafft/ oder blut- freundtschafft.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SIXTH Title? On the degrees of kinship. Of the degrees of kinship, or blood-relationship.

units.la: Quomodo numeratur cognatio?
units.tr: How is kinship counted?

units.la: IN primis admonendi sumus, cognationem aliam supra numerari, aliam infra, aliam ex transverso, quæ etiam a latere dicitur. Superior cognatio est parentum, Inferior liberorum, Ex transverso fratrum sororumve & eorum, qui quæve ex his generantur. in princip.cod.
units.tr: FIRST we must note that kinship is counted in three ways: upward, downward, and across, which is also called collateral. Upward kinship is that of parents, downward that of children, and across that of brothers and sisters and those who are born of them. (Cod. tit. de gradibus, beginning.)

units.la: Quot gradus numerantur in hoc titulo?
units.tr: How many degrees are counted in this title?

units.la: Sex: primo gradu est supra, pater, mater, <bl>im[?] ersten</bl> <bl>grad oberfich ist Vatter / Mutter:</bl> Infra filius, filia, <bl>underfich/Sohn/Tochter.</bl>
units.tr: Six. In the first degree upward are father and mother (in German: in the first degree upward are father and mother); downward are son and daughter (downward: son, daughter).

units.la: Secundo gradu supra avus, avia, <bl>grofvatter grof-</bl> <bl>muter:</bl> Infra, nepos, neptis, <bl>findes[?] john/findes tocht-</bl> <bl>er:</bl> Ex transverso frater, soror, <bl>bruder/schwester.</bl>
units.tr: In the second degree upward are grandfather and grandmother (grandfather, grandmother); downward, grandson and granddaughter (grandson, granddaughter); across, brother and sister (brother, sister).

units.la: Tertio gradu supra proavus, proavia, <bl>der ander</bl> <bl>grosvatter / die ander grosmutter:</bl> Infra proneps, proneptis, <bl>ander findes john / ander findes tochter:</bl> Ex transverso fratris sororisq; filius, filia, & convenienter patruus, Des Vatters bruder / amita, Des Vatters schwester / avunculus, Der mutter bruder / matertera, Der mutter schwester.
units.tr: In the third degree upward are great-grandfather and great-grandmother (the second grandfather, the second grandmother); downward, great-grandson and great-granddaughter (the second grandson, the second granddaughter); across, the son and daughter of a brother or sister, and likewise the paternal uncle (the father's brother), the amita (the father's sister), the maternal uncle (the mother's brother), and the matertera (the mother's sister).

units.la: Quarto gradu supra abavus, abavia, D' dritte großvatter / Die dritte großmutter: Infra abnepos, abneptis, Der dritte Kindes sohn / Die dritte Kindes tochter: Ex transverso fratris sororisque nepos neptisve: Et convenienter patruus magnus, Des großvatters bruder / amita magna, Des großvatters schwester: Item avunculus magnus, Der großmutter bruder / matertera magna, Der großmutter schwester. Qui ex duobus fratribus progenerantur, proprie fratres patrueles vocantur: qui ex duabus sororibus progenerantur proprie consobrini dicuntur. Si autem ex duobus fratribus filiae nascuntur, sorores patrueles appellantur: qui ex fratre & sorore progenerantur, amitini proprie dicuntur, vulgo etiam consobrini.
units.tr: In the fourth degree upward are the abavus and abavia (the third grandfather, the third grandmother); downward, the abnepos and abneptis (the third grandson, the third granddaughter); across, the nepos and neptis of a brother or sister; and likewise the patruus magnus (the grandfather's brother), the amita magna (the grandfather's sister), and also the avunculus magnus (the grandmother's brother), and the matertera magna (the grandmother's sister). Those born of two brothers are properly called patrueles fratres (cousins-german on the father's side); those born of two sisters are properly called consobrini. If daughters are born of two brothers, they are called sorores patrueles; those born of a brother and a sister are properly called amitini, and commonly also consobrini.

units.la: Quinto gradu supra atavus, atavia, Der vierdte großvater / Die vierdte großmutter: Infra atnepos, atneptis, Der vierdte Kindes sohn / Die vierdte Kindes tochter. Ex transverso fratris sororisque pronepos, proneptis: Et convenienter propatruus, proamita, Des andern großvatters bruder / Des andern großvatters schwester / & proavunculus, promatertera, Der andern großmutter bruder / Der andern großmutter schwester.
units.tr: In the fifth degree upward are the atavus and atavia (the fourth grandfather, the fourth grandmother); downward, the atnepos and atneptis (the fourth grandson, the fourth granddaughter). Across, the pronepos and proneptis of a brother or sister; and likewise the propatruus and proamita (the brother and sister of the second grandfather), and the proavunculus and promatertera (the brother and sister of the second grandmother).

units.la: Sexto gradu supra tritavus, tritavia, Der fünffte großvatter / Die fünffte großmutter: Infra trinepos, trineptis, Der fünffte Kindes sohn / Die fünffte Kindes tochter: Ex transverso fratris sororisq; abnepos, abneptis: & convenienter abpatruus, abamita, Des dritten großvatters bruder / Des dritten großvatters schwester / abavunculus, abmatertera, Der dritten großmutter bruder / Der dritten großmutter schwester. §. 1.2.3.4.5.6. inst. eod.
units.tr: In the sixth degree upward are the tritavus and tritavia (the fifth grandfather, the fifth grandmother); downward, the trinepos and trineptis (the fifth grandson, the fifth granddaughter); across, the abnepos and abneptis of a brother or sister; and likewise the abpatruus and abamita (the brother and sister of the third grandfather), and the abavunculus and abmatertera (the brother and sister of the third grandmother). (§§ 1–6, Inst., same title.)

units.la: Quid est Arbor consanguinitatis?
units.tr: What is a tree of consanguinity?

units.la: Est series, quae indicat personas ab uno stipite ortas, quomodo inter se distet & se invicem attingant. Secundum Schneidevvinum in prin. inst. de nuptiis. Estq; duplex: civilis aut canonica. Civilis, proprie gradus complectitur, & ad tutelas & ad successiones pertinet: Canonica vero lineis utitur in computatione, & matrimonia tantum respicit.
units.tr: It is a series which shows the persons descended from one stock, how far they are distant from one another and how they touch each other (according to Schneidewin, at the beginning of the Institutes, on marriages). It is twofold: civil or canonical. The civil tree properly embraces degrees and pertains both to guardianships and to successions; the canonical tree, however, uses lines in its reckoning and regards only marriages.

units.la: Quid est gradus?
units.tr: What is a degree?

units.la: Gradus est intervallum, quo agnoscitur, quae persona stipiti sit propior, vel ab eode remotius distet. Dicitur autem stipes illa persona, a qua caeterae personae, de quarum conjunctione quaeritur, originem ducunt.
units.tr: A degree is the interval by which we recognise which person is nearer to the stock, or stands farther away from it. The stock is that person from whom the other persons, whose relationship is in question, derive their origin.

units.la: Quid est Linea?
units.tr: What is a line?

units.la: Linea est personarum ab eodem stipite descendentium collectio, gradus continens & cognationes distinguens. Estque triplex: Ascendentium, Descendentium & Collateralium. <bl>Der verwandten</bl> <bl>vbersich/vnterfich/vnd von den seiten.</bl>
units.tr: A line is a collection of persons descending from the same stock, containing degrees and distinguishing kindreds. It is threefold: of ascendants, of descendants, and of collaterals. (Of relatives upward, downward, and from the sides.)

units.la: Quotuplex est linea Collateralium?
units.tr: How many kinds of line of collaterals are there?

units.la: Duplex: Aequalis aut Inaequalis. Linea aequalis est aequa graduum distantia a communi stipite: Linea vero inaequalis est qua persona aliam in gradu praecedit.
units.tr: Two: equal or unequal. An equal line is one in which the persons are at an equal distance of degrees from the common stock; an unequal line is one in which one person precedes another in degree.

units.la: Quid discriminis est inter Arborem Civi- lem & Canonicam?
units.tr: What is the difference between the civil and the canonical tree?

units.la: In numeratione graduum nulla est differetia, quo ad ascendentes & descendentes, inter jus civile & canonicum. Nam de utroq; jure in linea ascendentium & descendentium tot sunt gradus, quot sunt personae, una dempta, videlicet dempto stipite, a quo suputatio initium habet: ut Abraham, filius Thare, primum gradum constituit: Isaac, nepos Thare, seeundum: Jacob, pronepos, tertium: Iofeph adnepos, quartum: Ephraim, atnepos, quintum. Nuptiæ autem inter ascendentes & descendentes in infinitum sunt prohibitæ.
units.tr: In the counting of degrees there is no difference between civil and canonical law as regards ascendants and descendants. For under either law, in the line of ascendants and descendants there are as many degrees as there are persons, one excepted, namely the stock from which the reckoning has its beginning: thus Abraham, son of Terah, constitutes the first degree; Isaac, grandson of Terah, the second; Jacob, great-grandson, the third; Joseph, the great-great-grandson, the fourth; Ephraim, the atnepos, the fifth. Marriages between ascendants and descendants are forbidden without limit.

units.la: Sed quoad Collaterales, valde differunt jus civile & canonicum. Nam de jure civili in linea Collaterali æquali vel inæquali tot sunt gradus, quot sunt perfonæ stipite dempto. De jure autem Canonico fequentes observentur Regulæ.
units.tr: But as regards collaterals, civil and canonical law differ greatly. For under civil law, in the collateral line, equal or unequal, there are as many degrees as there are persons, the stock excepted. Under canon law, however, the following rules are observed.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Quoto gradu altera persona in linea æquali collateralium distat à communi stipite, eodem gradu inter fe distant: ut, Acacus Peleus | Telamon Achilles | Ajax.
units.tr: In a straight line of collaterals, the persons who are equally distant from their common stock are distant from each other by the same degree: for example, Acacus, Peleus, Telamon, Achilles, Ajax.

units.la: Achilles distat à stipite fecundo gradu: Ergo Achilles & Ajax inter fe, fecundo gradu distant, per hanc primam Regulam. Nunc autem prohibitum est matrimonium inter collaterales ufq; ad quartum gradum inclusive, id est, ut quartus gradus includatur, & non licet tibi ducere uxorem, quæ tibi in quarto gradu consanguinitatis est conjuncta, inquit Schneidewinus.
units.tr: Achilles is distant from the stock by the second degree; therefore Achilles and Ajax are distant from each other by the second degree, by this first rule. Now, marriage is forbidden between collaterals up to the fourth degree inclusive, that is, so that the fourth degree is included, and you may not take as wife a woman who is joined to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Quoto gradu lineæ inæqualis collateralium, remotior distat à stipite, eodem gradu à fe quoque distant: ut, Thare Abraham | Nachor Ifaac | Bathuel Rebecca.
units.tr: In a line of collaterals that is unequal, the one who is more remote from the stock is distant from the other by the same degree: for example, Terah, Abraham, Nahor, Isaac, Bethuel, Rebekah.

units.la: Rebecca distat tertio gradu à stipite, ideo & ab Ifaac distat tertio gradu, per hanc fecundam Regulam
units.tr: Rebekah is distant from the stock by the third degree, and so she is distant from Isaac by the third degree, by this second rule.

units.la: Quid est affinitas?
units.tr: What is affinity?

units.la: Affinitas secundum canones dicitur personarum proximitas ex quocunque coitu proveniens. Secundum leges vero est proximitas personarum ex justi[?] nuptiis proveniens. l. non facile. §. Sciendum. ff.de[?] gradibus & adfinib. & nominib. eor.
units.tr: According to the canons, affinity is said to be the kinship of persons arising from any sexual union. According to the civil laws, however, it is the kinship of persons arising from lawful marriage. l. non facile. §. Sciendum. ff. de gradibus et adfinibus et nominibus eorum.

units.la: Dic Regulas de Affinitate.
units.tr: Give the Rules on Affinity.

units.la: Prima Regula?
units.tr: First Rule?

units.la: Persona addita personæ per carnis copulam mutat genus attinentiæ, & non gradum: ut, Ego & frater meus sumus consanguinei in primo gradu consanguinitatis, frater ducit uxorem Annam, quæ est persona addita personæ, scilicet fratris mei, per matrimonialem cōjunctionem, & mutat genus attinentiæ, id est, alio genere mihi conjuncta est quàm frater meus.
units.tr: A person added to a person through the bond of the flesh changes the kind of relationship, and not the degree. For example, I and my brother are blood relations in the first degree of consanguinity. My brother takes as his wife Anna, who is a person added to a person, namely to my brother, through the marital union, and she changes the kind of relationship: that is, she is joined to me by a different kind of tie than my brother is.

units.la: Secunda Regula?
units.tr: Second Rule?

units.la: Affinitas tantum contrahitur inter maritum & consanguineos uxoris, & econtrà: inter consanguineos autem mariti & uxoris nulla est affinitas impediens matrimonium. Unde duo fratres possunt ducere duas sorores.
units.tr: Affinity is contracted only between a husband and the blood relations of his wife, and conversely between a wife and the blood relations of her husband. Between the blood relations of the husband and those of the wife there is no affinity that impedes marriage. Hence two brothers may marry two sisters.

units.la: Tertia Regula?
units.tr: Third Rule?

units.la: Consanguinei uxoris quoto gradu sunt ipsi uxori jure consanguinitatis, eodem gradu sunt ipsi marito jure affinitatis, & contrà: ut, Frater meus de jure canonico est mihi in primo gradu consanguinitatis: ita eodem gradu est mihi ipsius uxor, nempe primo gradu affinitatis.
units.tr: The blood relations of a wife stand to the wife herself in whatever degree of consanguinity, by right of blood, and they stand to the husband in the same degree by right of affinity, and conversely. For example, my brother is related to me in the first degree of consanguinity by canon law; in the same way his wife is related to me in the same degree, namely the first degree of affinity.

units.la: Quarta Regula?
units.tr: Fourth Rule?

units.la: Sicut matrimonium inter consanguineos ascendentes & descendentes ratione consanguinitatis in infinitum prohibitum est: ita etiam inter affines ascendentes & descendentes perpetua est conjugii prohibitio, ratione affinitatis.l.non facil.§.hos ita-que.ff.de gradib.
units.tr: Just as marriage between blood relations in the ascending and descending line is forbidden without limit, on account of consanguinity, so too the prohibition of marriage between relations by affinity in the ascending and descending line is perpetual, on account of affinity. See the law "Non facile", the paragraph "Hos itaque", Digest, on degrees.

units.la: Quinta Regula.
units.tr: Fifth Rule.

units.la: Sicut de jure canonico inter consanguineos usq; ad quartum gradum consanguinitatis inclusive matrimonium prohibetur, ita quoq; inter affines. Vide Schneidewinum super Inst. de Nuptiis.
units.tr: Just as by canon law marriage is forbidden between blood relations up to and including the fourth degree of consanguinity, so too it is forbidden between relations by affinity. See Schneidewin on the Institutes, on Marriages.

units.la: QUIS EST SEPTIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: What is the Seventh Title?

units.la: De servili cognatione. Von leibeigener knechtlicher Sippschafft. Quid dicit Imperator de servili suc- cessione?
units.tr: On servile kinship. Of serf-born kinship (German: Von leibeigener knechtlicher Sippschafft). What does the Emperor say about servile succession?

units.la: Concessimus, inquit, ut si quis in servili constitutus consortio, liberum vel liberos habuerit, sive ex libera, sive ex servilis cōditionis muliere: vel contra serva mulier ex libero vel servo habuerit liberos cujuscunq; sexus: Et ad libertatem his pervenientibus, ij, qui ex servili ventre nati sunt, libertatem meruerint, vel dum mulieres liberae erant, ipsi in servitute eos habuerint, & postea ad libertatem pervenerint: ut hi omnes ad successionem patris vel matris veniant, patronatus jure in hac parte sopito. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: We have granted, he says, that if anyone who is placed in servile condition has a free child or children, whether by a free woman or by a woman of servile condition; or conversely, if a female slave has children by a free man or by a slave, of either sex; and when these have attained liberty, those who were born of a servile womb have earned their freedom, or, while their mothers were free, the parents kept them in servitude and afterwards they attained liberty: then all of these shall come to the succession of father or mother, the right of patronage being set aside in this respect. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Estne pronepos defuncti potior, quàm de- functi frater aut pater?
units.tr: Is a great-grandson of the deceased preferred to a brother or father of the deceased?

units.la: Cùm prima causa sit suorum haeredum, & eorum, quos inter suos haeredes enumeravimus: apparet pronepotem & abnepotem defuncti potiorem esse, quàm fratrem aut patrem matremq; defuncti, inquit Imperator, §. repetitis. inst. cod.
units.tr: Since the first cause belongs to the deceased's own heirs, and to those whom we have listed among his own heirs, it is clear that a grandson's son and a great-grandson of the deceased are preferred to the deceased's brother or to his father and mother, says the Emperor, §. repetitis, Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST OCTAVUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHICH IS THE EIGHTH TITLE?

units.la: De successione libertorum. <bl>Von erbung</bl> <bl>der freygelassen knechte.</bl>
units.tr: On the succession of freedmen. <bl>On inheritance</bl> <bl>of freed slaves.</bl>

units.la: Quando vocabat lex patronum ad hæreditatem liberti?
units.tr: When did the law call the patron to the inheritance of the freedman?

units.la: ITA demum lex duodecim tabularum ad hæreditatem liberti vocabat patronum, si intestatus mortuus esset libertus, hærede suo nullo relicto in prin.inst.cod.
units.tr: THE law of the Twelve Tables called the patron to the inheritance of a freedman only in this case: if the freedman died intestate, leaving no heir of his own (in the principle of the Institutes and the Code).

units.la: Quid Justiniani constitutio definivit?
units.tr: What did the constitution of Justinian determine?

units.la: Ut si libertus vel libera minores centenariis sint, id est, minus centum aureis habeant substantiam, nullum locum habeat patronus in eorum successione: si tamen testamentum fecerint. Sin autem intestati decesserint, nullo liberorum relicto: tunc patronatus jus (quod erat ex lege duodecim tabularum) integrum Justiniani constitutio reservavit.
units.tr: That if a freedman, male or female, is under a hundred gold pieces, that is, holds property of less than one hundred aurei, the patron has no place in their succession, provided they have made a will. But if they die intestate, leaving no children, then the constitution of Justinian preserved the right of patronage (which came from the Law of the Twelve Tables) intact.

units.la: Si vero testamentum quidem fecerint, patronos autem aut patronas praeterierint: tunc ex Imperatoris constitutione per bonorum possessionem contra tabulas, non dimidiam, (ut antea) sed tertiam partem bonorum liberti consequantur. §.sed nostra. inst.cod.
units.tr: But if they have indeed made a will, yet have passed over their patrons or patronesses, then by the Emperor's constitution, through the possession of goods against the tablets, they obtain not half of the freedman's goods (as before) but a third part. (In the section "but our constitution," Institutes, same title.)

units.la: QUIS EST NONUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE NINTH Title?

units.la: De assignatione libertorum. <bl>Von zueignung</bl> <bl>der freygelassen knechte.</bl>
units.tr: On the assignment of freedmen. <bl>On the assignment</bl> <bl>of freed slaves.</bl>

units.la: Ad quos pertinent bona libertorum?
units.tr: To whom do the goods of freedmen pertain?

units.la: SEnatus censuit, ut quamvis ad omnes patroni liberos, qui ejusdem gradus sunt, æqualiter bona libertorum pertineant: tamen liceret parenti, uni ex liberis assignare libertum, ut post mortem ejus solus is patronus habeatur, cui assignatus est. in princ. instit. eod.
units.tr: The Senate decreed that although the goods of a freedman pertain equally to all the patron's children who are of the same degree, nevertheless it is permitted for a parent to assign a freedman to one of the children, so that after the parent's death that child alone is regarded as the patron to whom he has been assigned.

units.la: Quid est assignare libertum?
units.tr: What is it to assign a freedman?

units.la: Est nihil aliud, quàm si patronus plures habens liberos, testificatur & declarat, quem ex suis liberis velit esse patronum liberti, & habere jus patronatus l.adsignare.197.ff.de verbor.signif.
units.tr: It is nothing other than when a patron who has several children bears witness and declares which of his children he wishes to be the patron of the freedman, and to have the right of patronage.

units.la: Si quis filium, cui adsignavit, emancipa- verit, quid juris?
units.tr: If someone emancipates the son to whom he assigned him, what is the law?

units.la: Quaerebatur, si cum, cui assignavit, postea emancipaverit: num evanescat adsignatio? sed placuit evanescere, quod & Juliano & aliis plerisq; visum est. §.datur.inst.eod.
units.tr: It was asked whether, if the parent afterwards emancipated the child to whom he had assigned the freedman, the assignment lapses. But it was settled that it lapses, as Julian and most others also thought.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS Titulus? De bonorum possessionibus. Von be- sitzung der güter.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TENTH Title? On possessions of goods. On the possession of goods.

units.la: Hactenus de successionibus juris civilis, Nunc de prætoriis seu bonorum possessione.
units.tr: So far on the successions of civil law; now on the praetorian succession, or bonorum possessio.

units.la: Quid est bonorum possessio?
units.tr: What is bonorum possessio?

units.la: Bonorum possessio est jus persequendi retinendiq; patrimonii, sive rei, quę cujusq; , cùm moritur, fuit. l.bona autem.§.bonorum igitur.ff.eodem.
units.tr: Bonorum possessio is the right of pursuing and holding the estate, or the property, which belonged to a person when he died. l. bona autem. §. bonorum igitur. ff. eodem.

units.la: Quid discriminis inter bonorum possessio- nem & hæreditatem?
units.tr: What is the difference between bonorum possessio and hereditas?

units.la: Bonorum possessio in effectu nihil aliud est quàm hæreditas, quæ dicitur successio in universum jus quod defunctus tempore mortis habuit. l. hæreditas.62. ff. de regul. jur. Nisi quòd hæreditas est juris civilis: Bonorum possessio vero de jure prætorio indu&ta.
units.tr: In effect, bonorum possessio is nothing other than hereditas, which is called succession to the whole right that the deceased had at the time of death. l. hereditas. 62. ff. de regul. jur. Except that hereditas belongs to civil law, whereas bonorum possessio was introduced by praetorian law.

units.la: Consistit autem bonorum possessio in mero jure, estq; nomen juris, quod denotat beneficium prætoris concessum in successionibus ad consequendum patrimonium defuncti: possessio vero bonorum, licet sit juris, prout in intellectu consistit, plurimum tamen facti habet, & consistit in facto. l. deniq;.19 ff. ex quib. cauf.major. viginti quinq; annis in integrum restituantur.
units.tr: Bonorum possessio consists in pure law, and it is a term of law, which denotes the benefit granted by the praetor in successions for obtaining the estate of the deceased. But the possession of goods, although it belongs to law as far as its concept goes, nevertheless has a great deal of fact in it and consists in fact. l. denique. 19. ff. ex quib. caus. major. viginti quinque annis in integrum restituantur.

units.la: Quare jus bonorum possessionis introd- uctum est?
units.tr: Why was the right of bonorum possessio introduced?

units.la: Jus bonorum possessionis introductum est à prætore emendandi veteris juris gratia. Aliquando tamen neq; emendandi, neq; impugnandi veteris juris, sed magis confirmandi gratia prætor pollicetur bonorum possessionem. in princ.inst.eod.
units.tr: The right of bonorum possessio was introduced by the praetor for the sake of amending the old law. Sometimes, however, the praetor grants bonorum possessio not for amending or overturning the old law, but rather for confirming it. in princ. inst. eod.

units.la: Fiúntne hæredes, quos solus præ- tor vocat?
units.tr: Do those become heirs whom the praetor alone calls?

units.la: Quos solus vocat prætor ad hæreditatem, hæredes quidem ipso jure non fiunt. Nam prætor hæredem facere non potest: per legem enim tantum, vel similem juris constitutionem hæredes fiunt, veluti per Senatusconsulta, & constitutiones principales: sed cum eis prætor dat bonorum possessionem, loco hæredum constituuntur, & vocantur bonorum possessores. §. Quos autem. inst.eod.
units.tr: Those whom the praetor alone calls to the inheritance do not indeed become heirs by the law itself. For the praetor cannot make an heir: heirs are made only by a law or a similar constitution of law, such as senatus-consults and imperial constitutions. But when the praetor gives them bonorum possessio, they are placed in the position of heirs and are called bonorum possessores. §. Quos autem. inst. eod.

units.la: Quotuplex est bonorum possessio?
units.tr: How many kinds of bonorum possessio are there?

units.la: Duplex alia ex testamento: Eaq; vicissim duplex: una, quæ præteritis liberis datur, vocaturq; Contra tabulas: altera, quam omnibus jure scriptis hæredibus prætor pollicetur: Ideoq; vocatur Secundum tabulas. Alia bonorum possessio est ab intestato, cujus octo sunt species: prima, quæ suis hæredibus, & iis, qui ex edicto prætoris inter suos hæredes connumerantur, datur, vocatur Unde Liberi.
units.tr: There are two kinds from a will, and these in turn are of two sorts: one, which is given to children who were passed over, and is called contra tabulas; the other, which the praetor promises to all heirs written in the will, and therefore is called secundum tabulas. The other bonorum possessio is from intestacy, of which there are eight kinds. The first, which is given to heirs of the household and to those who by the praetor's edict are counted among the heirs of the family, is called unde liberi.

units.la: Secunda datur legitimis hæredibus, & vocatur Unde legitimi.
units.tr: The second is given to legitimate heirs and is called unde legitimi.

units.la: Tertia datur decem personis, & vocatur Unde decem personæ. Sunt autem decem personæ hæ: pater, mater, avus, avia, tàm paterni, quàm materni: Item filius, filia, nepos, neptis, tàm ex filio, quàm ex filia: frater, soror, consanguinei, vel uterini.
units.tr: The third is given to ten persons and is called unde decem personae. The ten persons are these: father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, both paternal and maternal; likewise son, daughter, grandson, granddaughter, both through a son and through a daughter; brother, sister, consanguine or uterine relatives.

units.la: Quarta, cognatis proximis, & vocatur, Unde cognati. Quinta, tanquam ex familia.
units.tr: The fourth is to the nearest kindred, and is called unde cognati. The fifth is as if from the family.

units.la: Sexta, patrono patronæq;, liberisq; eorum, & parentibus, datur.
units.tr: The sixth is given to the patron and patroness, their children, and their parents.

units.la: Septima, viro & uxori datur.
units.tr: The seventh is given to husband and wife.

units.la: Octava cognatis manumissoris. §. sunt autem. instit. eod.
units.tr: The eighth is to the kinsfolk of the manumitter. §. sunt autem. instit. eod.

units.la: Et hæ bonorum possessiones dicuntur Ordinariæ, quòd fundatæ sint in certa & expressa parte edicti prætoris. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: And these bonorum possessiones are called ordinary, because they are founded on a certain and express part of the praetor's edict. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quot sunt autem hodie ordinariæ bono- rum possessiones?
units.tr: How many ordinary bonorum possessiones are there today?

units.la: Sex: Bonorum possessio contra tabulas, de qua Titulus in ff. & C. de bonor. possess. contra tab. Et datur liberis in testamento præteritis, & iniustè exhæredatis, contra voluntatem paternam, & principaliter inducta est propter liberos emancipatos.
units.tr: Six: the bonorum possessio contra tabulas, on which there is a title in the Digest and the Code, de bonorum possessione contra tabulas. It is given to children who were passed over in the will and unjustly disinherited, against the father's wish, and was introduced chiefly on account of emancipated children.

units.la: Bonorum possessio secundum tabulas, quæ scilicet datur secundum dispositionem seu voluntatem testatoris in tabulis expressam, his qui in testamento instituti & substituti sunt hæredes. l. æquissimum, §. defertur. ff de bonor. possess. secund. tab.
units.tr: The bonorum possessio secundum tabulas, which is given, that is, according to the disposition or will of the testator expressed in the tabulae, to those who are instituted and substituted as heirs in the will. l. aequissimum, §. defertur. ff. de bonor. possess. secund. tab.

units.la: Hæ duæ bonorum possessiones dantur ex testamento: sequentes quatuor ab intestato.
units.tr: These two bonorum possessiones are given from a will; the following four from intestacy.

units.la: Bonorum possessio, unde liberi, quæ principaliter induĉta est propter filios emancipatos, qui lege duodecim tabularum ad successionem paternam ab intestato non admittebantur. §. emancipati. supra de hæreditatib. quæ ab intest. deferuntur. Ideo prætor eis hanc bonorum possessionem concessit, per quam patri succedunt.
units.tr: The bonorum possessio unde liberi, which was introduced chiefly on account of emancipated sons, who were not admitted to succession to their father on intestacy by the law of the Twelve Tables. §. emancipati. supra de hereditatibus quae ab intestato deferuntur. Therefore the praetor granted them this bonorum possessio, by which they succeed to their father.

units.la: Bonorum possessio, unde legitimi, per quam agnati vocantur etiam de jure prætorio ad successionem defuncti. Et hoc casu jus prætorium adjuvit legem duodecim tabularum.
units.tr: The bonorum possessio unde legitimi, by which agnates are called to the succession of the deceased, also by praetorian law. And in this case praetorian law supported the law of the Twelve Tables.

units.la: Bonorum possessio, unde cognati, & in hoc prætor correxit jus legis duodecim tabularum, quo, deficientibus agnatis, cognati prorsus excludebantur à successione per fiscū: sed prætor exclusō fisco, non extantibus agnatis, tertio loco cognatos ad successionem vocavit, de quo titulus in ff. & C. unde cognati.
units.tr: The bonorum possessio unde cognati, in which the praetor corrected the law of the Twelve Tables, under which, when agnates failed, cognates were wholly excluded from succession in favour of the treasury. But the praetor, with the treasury excluded, when agnates were not present, called cognates to the succession in the third place. On this there is a title in the Digest and the Code, unde cognati.

units.la: Bonorum possessio, unde vir & uxor, per quam deficientibus consanguineis, agnatis & cognatis, vir ad successionem uxoris vocatur, & cōtrā, exclusō fisco. De quo titulus in ff. & C. unde vir & uxor.
units.tr: The bonorum possessio unde vir et uxor, by which, when blood relations, agnates and cognates fail, the husband is called to the succession of his wife, and conversely, the treasury being excluded. On this there is a title in the Digest and the Code, unde vir et uxor.

units.la: Quid est Extraordinaria bonorum possessio?
units.tr: What is extraordinary possession of goods?

units.la: Quæ non habet certam sedem, sed est vaga & nona stabilita certa parte edicti, & aliquando ex testamento, aliquando ab intestato datur. Exempli gratia: Cæsar promulgat legem, quod, si studiosus in aliqua Academia testatus vel intestatus decedat sine consanguineis, Rector vel senior Doctor in Academia ei per bonorum possessionem succedat. Hoc casu est extraordinaria bonorum possessio.
units.tr: It is that which does not have a fixed seat, but is vague and given by a new rule established apart from the fixed part of the edict, and sometimes from a will, sometimes without one (ab intestato). For example: the Emperor promulgates a law that if a student in some Academy dies, whether testate or intestate, without relatives, the Rector or a senior Doctor in the Academy shall succeed him by possession of goods. In this case there is extraordinary possession of goods.

units.la: Quæ habentur pro jure civili & jure prætorio?
units.tr: What things are held to belong to civil law and to praetorian law?

units.la: Omnia statuta condita ab illis qui non recognofcunt superiorem, habentur pro legibus civilibus: sed statuta à Marchionibus, Ducibus & aliis, qui superiorem recognoscunt, habentur pro jure prætorio, inquit Schneidevvinus.
units.tr: All statutes enacted by those who acknowledge no superior are held to be civil laws; but statutes made by Marquises, Dukes and others who acknowledge a superior are held to be praetorian law, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Intra quod tempus bonorum possessio est agnoscenda?
units.tr: Within what time must possession of goods be claimed?

units.la: Prætor liberis & parentibus, tàm naturalibus, quã adoptivis in petenda bonorum possessione, anni spatium: cæteris autem agnatis vel cognatis centum dierum dedit. §. cùm igitur. inst. cod.
units.tr: The praetor gave a period of one year to children and parents, both natural and adoptive, in seeking possession of goods; but to the other agnates or cognates, a period of a hundred days. Inst. de bonorum possessione, §. cum igitur.

units.la: Hactenus de modo acquirendi per successionem diximus: sequitur modus acquirendi per arrogationem.
units.tr: So far we have spoken of the manner of acquiring by succession; there follows the manner of acquiring by arrogation.

units.la: QUIS EST UNDECIMUS Titulus? De acquisitione per arrogationem. Von bekommung der güter durch annem-mung an kindesstat.
units.tr: What is the eleventh title? On acquisition by adrogation. On acquiring goods by being taken into the status of a child.

units.la: Quid hodie arrogatori adquiritur?
units.tr: What is acquired today by the adrogator?

units.la: NIhil aliud, nisi tantummodò ususfructus tàm naturalibus parentibus, quàm adoptivis per filios familiarum adquiritur in iis rebus, quę extrinsecus filiis obveniunt, Domino eis integro servato.
units.tr: Nothing else, except merely the usufruct, which is acquired both for natural parents and for adoptive parents through the sons of the household, in those things that come to the sons from outside, the ownership remaining wholly with the sons.

units.la: Mortuo autem filio arrogato in adoptiva familia, etiam dominū rerum ejus ad arrogatorē pertransit: nisi supersint aliæ personæ, quæ patrem in iis, quæ adquiri possunt, antecedant. §. Nunc autem. inst. cod.
units.tr: But when a son adrogated into the adoptive family dies, the ownership of his property also passes to the adrogator, unless there survive other persons who take precedence over the father in those things that can be acquired. §. Nunc autem. inst. cod.

units.la: QUIS EST DUODECI- MUS Titulus? De eo cui libertatis causa bona addicûntur, Von dem/ welchem vmb freyheit willen/ güter zugeeignet werden
units.tr: Which is the twelfth title? Concerning the one to whom goods are assigned for the sake of freedom; of him to whom property is granted on account of liberty (German heading: "Von dem, welchem umb Freyheit willen, Güter zugeeignet werden")

units.la: Accessitne novus casus succedendi?
units.tr: Has a new case of succession arisen?

units.la: Accessit novus casus successionis ex constitutione Divi Marci.in princip.inst.cod. Nam quando quis decessit condito testamento, in quo servis suis reliquit libertatem directam, vel fideicommissariam. Et heres institutus in testamento non voluit adire hereditatem,quia metuit ne[?] alienum, quo defunctus fuit oneratus: tum propter tuendas & conservandas libertates, quae alias nemine adeunte hereditatem perirent.l. testamento.ff.de manumiss.testament.per Constitutionem Divi Marci statutum est, ut quilibet extraneus, & etiam ipsi servi, quibus libertas relicta est,vel etiam fiscus, a judice petere possent sibi addici bona defuncti, quae heres institutus non voluit adire, ut ita servi libertatem relictam consequerentur.Schneidewinus hic.
units.tr: A new case of succession has arisen under the constitution of the divine Marcus, at the beginning of the Institutes of the Code. For when someone has died leaving a will, in which he bequeathed to his slaves freedom, either directly or by trust (fideicommissum), and the heir instituted in the will has been unwilling to enter upon the inheritance, because he fears the debt with which the deceased was burdened, then, for the sake of protecting and preserving those freedoms which would otherwise perish if no one entered upon the inheritance (l. testamento, ff. de manumissis testamento), it was established by the constitution of the divine Marcus that any outsider, and even the slaves themselves to whom freedom was left, or even the treasury (fiscus), could petition a judge that the goods of the deceased which the instituted heir did not wish to enter upon be assigned to them, so that the slaves might thus obtain the freedom left to them. See Schneidewin here.

units.la: Quare haec Constitutio introducta est?
units.tr: Why was this constitution introduced?

units.la: Haec constitutio libertatum tuendarum causa introducta est. Ergo si libertates nullae sunt datae: cessat haec constitutio.§.haec.inst.cod.
units.tr: This constitution was introduced for the sake of protecting freedoms. Therefore, if no freedoms have been given, this constitution does not apply (§ haec, Inst. Cod.).

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS tertius Titulus?
units.tr: What is the thirteenth title?

units.la: De successionibus sublatis, quae fiebant per bonorum venditiones, & ex SC. Clau- diano. <bl>Von abgeschafften Erbnemmungen, welche geschahen durch</bl> <bl>verkauffungen der güter, und aus dem Claudianischen Rahtsgebott.</bl>
units.tr: On the abolished successions which were made through sales of goods, and from the Claudian senatus consultum. <bl>On abolished inheritance-takings, which occurred through sales of goods, and from the Claudian decree of the council.</bl>

units.la: Quid erat modus olim succedendi per bo- norum venditiones?
units.tr: What was the former manner of succeeding through sales of goods?

units.la: Erat, quando debitor in solutione cessabat, & solenniter contra eum proponebatur actio :ipse Vero si non comparebat, sed fiebat contumax: tunc propter ejus contumaciam creditor in omnibus bonis debitori, tanquam mortuo succedebat, & licebat ei vendere ista bona. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: It was when a debtor was slow to pay and an action was solemnly brought against him. If he did not appear but became contumacious, then, on account of his contumacy, the creditor succeeded to all the debtor's goods as though he were dead, and was allowed to sell those goods. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid erat modus olim succedendi ex SC. Claudiano?
units.tr: What was the former manner of succeeding under the Claudian senatus consultum?

units.la: Erat, quando libera mulier, capta amore servi alieni, cui denunciabatur per Dominum servi, ne servo commisceretur, & admonebatur per Judicem, nec ipsa acquiesceret post trinam denuntiationem: cum omnibus bonis addicebatur Domino servi, ita ut mulier libertatem amitteret: & universa ejus bona per universitatem Domino servi adquireretur. Schneidevvinus hic. Hi modi per Imperatorem sublati & correcti sunt.
units.tr: It was when a free woman, captivated by love of another's slave, was warned by the slave's master not to have intercourse with the slave, and was admonished by the judge, but did not desist after three warnings. Then, together with all her goods, she was adjudged to the master of the slave, so that the woman lost her liberty and the master of the slave acquired all her property as a whole. See Schneidewin here. These procedures were abolished and corrected by the Emperor.

units.la: QUOT SUNT HODIE GRADUS ab intestato succedendi?
units.tr: How many degrees of succession ab intestato are there today?

units.la: Quinq; : Primus descendentium, Secundus ascendentium, Tertius collateralium, Quartus viri & uxoris, Quintus fisci. Studiosi adolescentes videant Schneidevvinum & Analysin Dialecticam Institutionum Argentorati excusam, ex quibus sequentia fere desumpsimus.
units.tr: Five: the first is of descendants, the second of ascendants, the third of collateral relatives, the fourth of husband and wife, and the fifth of the fisc. Keen young students should consult Schneidewin and the Dialectical Analysis of the Institutes printed at Strasbourg, from which we have drawn the following points more or less.

units.la: Quid dicis de primo gradu?
units.tr: What do you say about the first degree?

units.la: Ad successionem ab intestato vocantur descendentes, exclusis aliis ascendentibus & collateralibus.
units.tr: Descendants are called to succession ab intestato, with the other ascendants and collaterals excluded.

units.la: Quinam intelliguntur appellatione descendentium?
units.tr: Who are understood by the term descendants?

units.la: Non tantum liberi, sive masculi sive foeminae, tam sui haeredes quam emancipati: sed etiam nepotes in infinitum, & posthumi. l. liberorum [?]220. ff. de verborum signif.
units.tr: Not only children, whether sons or daughters, both those under their father's power and those emancipated, but also grandchildren to infinity, and posthumous children. l. liberorum [?]220. ff. de verborum signif.

units.la: Quot species liberorum vulgò nu- merantur?
units.tr: How many kinds of children are commonly counted?

units.la: Sex: prima species naturalium & legitimorum simul, secunda naturaliù tantùm, tertia legitimorum tantùm, quarta spuriorum seu vulgò quæsitorum, quinta incestuosorum & ex damnato coitu susceptorum, sexta spiritualium.
units.tr: Six: the first kind is those both natural and legitimate; the second is natural only; the third is legitimate only; the fourth is spurious, or born out of wedlock; the fifth is incestuous and those born of a condemned union; the sixth is spiritual.

units.la: Qui sunt liberi naturales & legiti- mi simul?
units.tr: Who are children both natural and legitimate?
