units.la: Qui ex justis nuptiis, seu legitimo matrimonio nati sunt l. filium definimus. ff.de his qui sunt sui vel alien.jur.Vulgò <bl>Ehelicheꝫ gebohne Kinder</bl> [?]. Inter hosce liberos refert Schneidewinus per subsequens matrimonium legitimatos.
units.tr: Those born of lawful marriage, or of a legitimate wedlock: l. filium definimus. ff. de his qui sunt sui vel alien. jur. Commonly called children born in wedlock. Among these children Schneidewin includes those legitimated by a subsequent marriage.

units.la: De horum successione sequentes ob- servandæ sunt Regulæ.
units.tr: The following rules are to be observed concerning the succession of these children.

units.la: Prima Regula?
units.tr: First Rule?

units.la: Liberi naturales & legitimi tàm masculi, quàm fœminæ, sive in patria potestate existentes, sive emancipati, hodie præferuntur omnibus aliis: Et suis ascendentibus æqualiter succedunt in capita. Authen. in successio̅n. C. de suis & legitimis liberis.
units.tr: Natural and legitimate children, both sons and daughters, whether they are in their father's power or emancipated, are today preferred to all others; and they succeed equally with their ascendants per capita. Authen. in successionem. C. de suis et legitimis liberis.

units.la: Obiter autem observandum, quòd successio in capita dicitur fieri, quando hæreditas secundùm numerum personarum, quibus defertur, dividitur in viriles seu æquales portiones, ut ibi tot sint partes, quot capita vel personæ, & unus tantùm habeat, quantum alter.
units.tr: It should be noted in passing that succession is said to take place per capita when the inheritance is divided, according to the number of persons to whom it passes, into equal or individual shares, so that there are as many parts as heads or persons, and each has as much as another.

units.la: In stirpes verò fit divisio hæreditatis in portiones inæquales, quando plures succedunt in locum alterius, qui eam tantùm partem accipiunt, quam is, in cujus locum succedunt accepisset, & non numerantur succedentium personæ sive capita: sed unius tan-tùm tům stirpis habetur ratio, cujus jure nituntur, qui succedunt, etsi plures sunt.
units.tr: But division takes place per stirpes, into unequal portions, when several succeed in the place of another, and they receive only that share which the person in whose place they succeed would have received; the number of persons succeeding is not counted, but account is taken only of the one stock from whose right those who succeed derive their claim, even if there are several of them.

units.la: Deinde observandum quòd liberi parétibus succedunt indistinctè, sive sint filij, sive filiæ. Nam inter filios & filias bona intestatorum parentum pro virilibus portionibus æquo jure dividi oportere, explorati juris est. l. inter filios. C. familiæ herciscundæ. Quod est verum in successione bonorum allodialiũ, non autem feudalium: quia fœminæ in feudis regulariter non succedunt. §.hoc autem F. de his qui seudum dare possunt.
units.tr: Next, it should be noted that children succeed their parents without distinction, whether they are sons or daughters. For it is established law that the goods of parents who die intestate must be divided equally among sons and daughters in equal shares. l. inter filios. C. familiae herciscundae. This holds true for the succession to allodial goods, but not to feudal ones, because women do not regularly succeed to fiefs. §. hoc autem F. de his qui feudum dare possunt.

units.la: Secunda Regula
units.tr: Second Rule

units.la: Nepotes ex filio vel filia præmortua, assumunt locum sui patris vel matris, & succedunt avo cum filiis ipsius in stirpem, id est, tantam de hæreditate avi accipiunt partem, quotcunq; fuerint, quantam parens eorum, si viveret, accepisset. l. nepotes. C. de suis & legitimis liberis.
units.tr: Grandchildren by a son or daughter who has died before, take the place of their father or mother, and they succeed their grandfather together with his children, per stirpes; that is, whatever their number, they receive from the grandfather's inheritance as much as their parent would have received had he or she been alive. l. nepotes. C. de suis et legitimis liberis.

units.la: Idem de pronepotibus tàm ex filio, quàm ex filia natis, & de aliis descendentibus, qui concurrunt cum filiis ascendentium, sentiendum est. cap.i.verf. Nam in usu. Auth. de hæredit. ab intestat. venientib.
units.tr: The same is to be understood of great-grandchildren born both of a son and of a daughter, and of other descendants who concur with the children of ascendants. cap. i. verf. Nam in usu. Auth. de hereditatibus ab intestato venientibus.

units.la: Tertia Regula
units.tr: Third Rule

units.la: Soli ac numero diversi nepotes vel pronepotes sive ex filiis sive filiabus procreati, succedunt avo suo vel proavo in stirpes l.2. C. de suis & legitimis liber. & d.cap.i.verf. in hoc enim ordine gradum quæri no[?] lumus. Authent. de hæred. ab intest. venientib.
units.tr: Grandchildren or great-grandchildren, alone and of different numbers, born either of sons or of daughters, succeed their grandfather or great-grandfather per stirpes. l. 2. C. de suis et legitimis liber. and d. cap. i. verf. in hoc enim ordine gradum quaeri nolumus. Authent. de hered. ab intest. venientib.

units.la: Quarta Regula
units.tr: Fourth Rule

units.la: In descendentibus collatio profectitiorum bonorum regulariter locum habet, nisi à defuncto aliter expressè sit dispositum. Quare liberi quibus ante ab ascendentibus est collatum, volentes in illorum defunctorum hæreditate cum aliis simul succedere, tenentur prius illud conferre. l. ut liberis. C. de collationib. Sumptus autem studiosorum nō conferuntur si filius studiosus nulla alia habuerit bona propria, & longo tempore in scholis ex consensu & patientia parentis vixerit: quia tunc pater per hanc suam patientiam videtur se obligasse ad hujusmodi sumptus filij, quò is sua studia cū aliqua laude absolvere posset. l. quæ pater. ff. familiæ Herciscundæ. & l. i. §. sed an id. ff. de collation. bonor. Non solus, inquit ibi Ulpianus, oneretur is, qui dignitatem meruit: sed commune sit omnium hæredum onus hoc debitum.
units.tr: Among descendants, collation of goods derived from the ascendants ordinarily applies, unless the deceased has expressly ordered otherwise. Therefore children to whom something was previously given by their ascendants, if they wish to succeed together with the others in the inheritance of those who have died, are bound first to bring that into collation. l. ut liberis. C. de collationibus. However, the expenses of students are not collated, if a student son had no other property of his own and has lived for a long time at school with his father's consent and forbearance; for then the father is seen by this forbearance to have bound himself to pay such expenses for his son, so that he might complete his studies with some credit. l. quae pater. ff. familiae herciscundae. and l. i. §. sed an id. ff. de collationibus bonorum. "Not only," says Ulpian there, "should he bear the burden who has earned the distinction, but this debt should be a common burden of all the heirs."

units.la: Qui dicuntur liberi naturales tantum?
units.tr: Who are said to be children merely natural?

units.la: Qui extra legitimum matrimonium ex viro uno unaq; concubina, in domo retenta & uxoris loco habita, nati sunt. Vulgò <bl>Basthart tinder</bl>[?]. Et hi aut patri naturali succedere volunt, aut matri.
units.tr: Those born outside legitimate marriage, of one man and one concubine kept in the house and treated as a wife. Commonly called bastard children. And these either wish to succeed their natural father, or their mother.

units.la: In utroq; casu sequentes observen- tur Regulæ. Prima Regula.
units.tr: In either case the following rules are observed. First rule.

units.la: Liberi naturales tantum succedunt suo patri naturali ab intestato, non habenti vel alios naturales & legitimos simul, vel etiam conjugem legitimam, in duabꝰ unciis, hoc est, in sexta hæreditatis parte, quæ habebunt una cum matre, quotquot fuerint liberi, & mater unius filij portionem accipit. cap. 12. discretis. verf. si quis autem defunctus. Auth. quib. mod. natural. efficiantur sui. Hoc tamen fallit, si pater plures habuerit concubinas. Nam tum in odium effusæ concupiscentiæ hujusmodi liberi nō possunt succedere patri suo naturali. d. cap. discretis. verf. si vero effusa.
units.tr: Natural children alone succeed their natural father intestate, when he leaves no other natural and legitimate children together with them, and no legitimate spouse either. They take in two ounces, that is, in the sixth part of the inheritance, which they share with their mother, however many children there are; and the mother receives the portion of one child. cap. 12. discretis. verf. si quis autem defunctus. Auth. quib. mod. natural. efficiantur sui. This rule has one exception: if the father had several concubines. For then, in hatred of such unrestrained lust, children of this kind cannot succeed their natural father. d. cap. discretis. verf. si vero effusa.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second rule.

units.la: Si vero extiterint legitimi & naturales simul, aut uxor legitima, liberi naturales tantum, omnino ab hæredihæreditate paterna excluduntur, & in nihilo succedunt: sunt tamen à legitimis alendi pro facultatum modo, juxta arbitrium boni viri. d. cap. discretis. verf.si quis autem. Authent.quib.modis natural.effici.fui.
units.tr: But if there are legitimate and natural children together, or a legitimate wife, then natural children alone are wholly excluded from the paternal inheritance and succeed to nothing. Nevertheless, they are to be supported by the legitimate heirs in proportion to the means available, at the discretion of a good man. d. cap. discretis. verf. si quis autem. Authent. quib. modis natural. effici. sui.

units.la: Tertia Regula.
units.tr: Third rule.

units.la: Nepotes aut pronepotes avo suo naturali ab intestato nullo modo succedere queunt. l.final. C.de naturalib.liberis.
units.tr: Grandchildren or great-grandchildren can in no way succeed intestate to their natural grandfather. l. final. C. de naturalib. liberis.

units.la: Quarta Regula.
units.tr: Fourth rule.

units.la: Matri illustri & omnibus aliis ascendentibus in linea foemina non solùm liberi naturales tantùm, sed etiam nepotes & pronepotes cum aliis liberis & legitimis simul æqualiter succedunt: liberi quidem in capita, nepotes verò in stirpem. l. si qua illustris. §. final. C. ad SC. Orphitian.
units.tr: To an illustrious mother and to all other ascendants in the female line, not only natural children but also grandchildren and great-grandchildren succeed equally, together with other natural and legitimate children: the children indeed per capita, but the grandchildren per stirpes. l. si qua illustris. §. final. C. ad SC. Orphitian.

units.la: Qui liberi dicuntur legitimi tantùm?
units.tr: Who are called legitimate children only?

units.la: Quibus non natura, sed lex ipsa jus filiationis per adoptionem vel arrogationem attribuit. Vulgò an<bl>genommen Finder</bl>. De horum successione sequentes observentur Regulæ.
units.tr: Those to whom the law itself, not nature, grants the status of child by adoption or arrogation. Vulgarly, "adopted-in" children (Finder). The following rules are observed concerning their succession.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First rule.

units.la: Liberi adoptati ab extraneo & permanentes in tali adoptione usq; ad mortem adoptantis, æqualiter cum aliis liberis naturalibus & legitimis simul ab intestato succedunt, tàm adoptati, quàm parenti suo naturali. l. cum in odoptivis. §. sed ne articulum. C. de adoptionibus.
units.tr: Children adopted from outside, and remaining in such adoption until the death of the adopter, succeed intestate equally with the other natural and legitimate children together, both to the adopter and to their natural parent. l. cum in adoptivis. §. sed ne articulum. C. de adoptionibus.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second rule.

units.la: Nullis autem naturalibus & legitimis superstitibus, liberi legitimi soli succedùt patri adoptivo, nulla emancipatione facta, exclusis etiam defuncti parentibus: sed ad successionem Agnatorū & Cognatorum ipsius defuncti nequaquam admittuntur. l. cum in adoptivis. §. sed ne. verf. & ideo sancimus. C. de adoptionibus.
units.tr: But when there are no natural and legitimate survivors, legitimate children alone succeed the adoptive father, no emancipation having taken place; the parents of the deceased are excluded too. Yet they are in no way admitted to the succession of the agnates and cognates of the deceased. l. cum in adoptivis. §. sed ne. verf. & ideo sancimus. C. de adoptionibus.

units.la: Tertia Regula?
units.tr: Third rule?

units.la: Filiusfamilias adoptatus ab ascendente, hoc est, ab avo vel paterno vel materno definit esse in patris sui potestate, & soli adoptanti instar filij naturalis & legitimi simul succedit, durante adhuc adoptione. l. cum in adoptivis. in princip. verf. si vero pater. C. de adoptionibus.
units.tr: A son under power adopted by an ascendant, that is, by a grandfather, either paternal or maternal, ceases to be in the power of his father and succeeds only the adopter, together with the natural and legitimate children, while the adoption still lasts. l. cum in adoptivis. in princip. verf. si vero pater. C. de adoptionibus.

units.la: Quarta Regula?
units.tr: Fourth rule?

units.la: Arrogatus transiens non solum in familiam, sed etiam in potestate arrogatoris, patris licet extranei, non facta emancipatione, tam in iis bonis quae ad cum attulit, quam in aliis ipsius arrogantis propriis, & ab intestato, & ex testamento, tanquam filius naturalis & legitimus simul, eidem succedit. d. l. cum in Adoptivis. §. final. C. de adoptionib. l. si adrogator. ff. eod.
units.tr: An arrogated person, passing not only into the family but also into the power of the arrogator, even though he is a stranger to the father, with no emancipation having been made, succeeds that same man, as a natural and legitimate son together with the others, both intestate and by testament, both in the goods he brought with him and in the other property of the arrogator himself. d. l. cum in Adoptivis. §. final. C. de adoptionib. l. si adrogator. ff. eod.

units.la: Qui dicuntur Spurij?
units.tr: Who are called spurious?

units.la: Primo, nati ex libera & servo: secundo, qui patre demonstrare non possunt, vel qui possunt quidem, sed eum habent, quem habere non licet. l. vulgo concepti. ff. de statu homin. Tertio, spurij magis proprie dicuntur nati extra matrimonium & concubinatum ex soluto & soluta, ut sunt filij publicarum meretricum, qui vulgo quaesiti appellantur, hurensinter. De horum successione sequentes observetur regulae.
units.tr: First, those born of a free woman and a slave; second, those who cannot show their father, or who can, but have one whom it is not lawful for them to have. l. vulgo concepti. ff. de statu homin. Third, spurious children are more properly those born outside marriage and concubinage, of an unmarried man and an unmarried woman, such as the children of public prostitutes, who are commonly called "sought after" (quaesiti), or bastards (hurenkinder). The following rules are observed concerning their succession.

units.la: Prima Regula?
units.tr: First rule?

units.la: Spurius propter patris sui incertitudinem prorsus destituitur successione hereditatis paternae aut aliorum per lineam paternam ascendentium. l. si spurius. ff. unde cognati.
units.tr: A spurious child, because his father is uncertain, is wholly deprived of succession to the paternal inheritance or to that of other ascendants in the paternal line. l. si spurius. ff. unde cognati.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second rule.

units.la: Spurius ad successionem illustris matris non admittitur, sive ex testamento, sive ab intestato, si alij liberi naturales & legitimi simul extiterint. l. si qua illustris. C. ad. S C. Orphitianum.
units.tr: A spurious child is not admitted to the succession of an illustrious mother, whether by testament or intestate, if other natural and legitimate children are living at the same time. l. si qua illustris. C. ad. S C. Orphitianum.

units.la: Tertia Regula.
units.tr: Third rule.

units.la: Nullis vero liberis naturalibus & legitimis extantibus soli spurij superstites, tam ex testamento quàm ab intestato matri illustri etiam, aviæ & aliis ascendentibus in linea fœminea succedere possunt. §. novissimè. inst. de SC. Orphitiano. l. hac parte. & l. Modestinus. ff. unde cognati.
units.tr: But when there are no natural and legitimate children living, and only spurious children survive, they can succeed an illustrious mother, whether by testament or intestate, as also a grandmother and other ascendants in the female line. §. novissime. inst. de SC. Orphitiano. l. hac parte. & l. Modestinus. ff. unde cognati.

units.la: Qui sunt ex damnato coitu suscepti?
units.tr: Who are those born of a condemned union?

units.la: Incestuosi, Nefarij, & Adulterini. Et de his omnibus traditur unica saltem Regula.
units.tr: Incestuous, nefarious, and adulterine children. And for all of these only a single rule is given.

units.la: Regula.
units.tr: Rule.

units.la: Ex damnato coitu suscepti neq; patri, neq; matri succedunt: sed prorsus ab omni successione excluduntur. Cap. si quid autem. §. eos enim. Auth. quibus modis natural. filij efficiuntur legitimi.
units.tr: Those born of a condemned union succeed neither to their father nor to their mother, but are wholly excluded from every succession. Cap. si quid autem. §. eos enim. Auth. quibus modis naturales filii efficiuntur legitimi.

units.la: Qui appellantur liberi spirituales?
units.tr: Who are called spiritual children?

units.la: Illi, quos ex sacro fonte levavimus. Et hi in nihilo succedunt parentibus suis spiritualibus: quia hoc non reperitur jure cautum. Si autem non cum lege agimus, erubescimus. Cap. consideremus. Auth. de trient. femiss.
units.tr: Those whom we have lifted from the holy font. And these succeed in nothing to their spiritual parents, because no right on this point is found in the law. If we are not arguing from the law itself, we are ashamed. Cap. consideremus. Auth. de trient. femiss.

units.la: Affinitas & compaternitas impediunt quidem matrimonia, nullum tamen jus succedendi tribuunt. Schwägerschafft vnd Gevatterschafft hindern wol am ehelichen leben: fürdern aber nicht um erbe.
units.tr: Kinship by marriage and godparentage do indeed hinder marriages, but they confer no right of inheritance. Kinship by marriage and godparentage certainly hinder married life, but they do not advance anyone's claim to an inheritance.

units.la: Primus gradus ab intestato succedendi hactenus fuit:
units.tr: The first degree of succession ab intestato has hitherto been:

units.la: Quid dicis de secundo gradu?
units.tr: What do you say of the second degree?

units.la: Liberis & omnibus descendentibus extinctis, proximum locum in successione parentes ascendentes obtinent. cap.2.Authent. de hæredib.ab intestato venientibus.
units.tr: When the children and all descendants are gone, the parents, as ascendants, hold the next place in the succession. Cap. 2. Authent. de haeredib. ab intestato venientibus.

units.la: Quinam intelliguntur appellatione parentum?
units.tr: Who are understood under the name of parents?

units.la: Avus, avia, proavus,proavia,utriusq; sexus in infinitum.l.quiq;.§.parentem. ff.de in jus vocando.
units.tr: Grandfather, grandmother, great-grandfather, great-grandmother, of either sex, to infinity. L. quiq. §. parentem. ff. de in jus vocando.

units.la: Sequentes Regulę de parentibus naturalib. & legitimis simul, circa successionem descendentium sunt ob- servandæ.
units.tr: The following rules concerning natural and legitimate parents together are to be observed with regard to the succession of descendants.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Pater & mater soli superstites hodie æqualiter possunt succedere filio mortuo, sive sit masculus, sive fœmina, tàm in patria potestate existens, quàm emancipatus, non solum in castrensi peculio, vel quasi, sed etiam in adventitiis per filium ab aliquo extra neo acquisitis. Auth.defuncto C.ad SC.Tertyllianū.
units.tr: Today the father and mother, if they alone survive, can succeed equally to a dead son or daughter, whether the child be male or female, whether still under paternal power or emancipated; and this holds not only for the camp property or its equivalent, but also for property acquired by the child from anyone outside the family. Auth. defuncto C. ad SC. Tertyllianum.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Sed in bonis adventitiis acquisitis ex linea materna,mater regulariter patri,sicut in acquisitis ex linea paterna,pater matri in successione filij defuncti præ-ferri solet. Secundum Bartolum in Authent.Itaq;.C. communia de successionib.
units.tr: But in property acquired from the maternal line, the mother is ordinarily preferred to the father, just as, in property acquired from the paternal line, the father is usually preferred to the mother in the succession of the dead child. According to Bartolus, on Authent. Itaque. C. communia de successionibus.

units.la: Tertia Regula.
units.tr: Third Rule.

units.la: Similiter quoq; de aliis ascendentibus solis judicandum est, inter quos bona defuncti æqualiter in duas portiones utrinq; dividuntur, ita ut unam partem paterni, alteram vero materni sortiantur. In bonis tamen ex una linea acquisitis, succedunt ascendentes illius lineæ tantùm.d. Authen defuncto. C.ad SC.Tertyllianum.
units.tr: The same judgment is to be made of the other ascendants when they alone survive: the goods of the deceased are divided equally into two portions, on each side, so that the paternal and the maternal relatives each take one part. Yet in goods acquired from one line, only the ascendants of that line succeed. Authent. defuncto, as above, C. ad SC. Tertyllianum.

units.la: Si vero ascendentes dispares fuerint in gradu, proximior eorum excludit remotiorem.d. Authent.defuncto. verf. salva gradus sui prærogativa. C. ad SC. Tertyllianum.
units.tr: But if the ascendants are unequal in degree, the nearer excludes the more remote. Authent. defuncto, as above, verse salva gradus sui praerogativa. C. ad SC. Tertyllianum.

units.la: Quarta Regula.
units.tr: Fourth Rule.

units.la: Quando sunt plures ascendentes in secundo vel tertio gradu disparis numeri, qui tamen defuncto sunt in pari gradu: tum hæreditas dividitur in duas partes: unam habebunt ascendentes ex linea paterna, & aliam parentes ex linea materna: sive sit unus vel plures, dict. Auth. defuncto.
units.tr: When there are several ascendants in the second or third degree of an odd number, who nonetheless stand in equal degree to the deceased, then the inheritance is divided into two parts: the ascendants of the paternal line will have one, and the parents of the maternal line the other, whether there be one or several. Said Authent. defuncto.

units.la: Quinta Regula.
units.tr: Fifth Rule.

units.la: Sed si cum parentibus aut aliis ascendentibus, simul concurrat fratres & sorores ipsi defuncto utrinque conjuncti, successio inter eos æqualiter fit in capita. d. Authen. defuncto. verf. sed si cum parentibus. C. ad. SC. Tertyllian.
units.tr: But if brothers and sisters who are joined to the deceased on both sides come together with the parents or other ascendants, the succession among them is made equally per capita. Said Authent. defuncto, verse sed si cum parentibus. C. ad SC. Tertyllian.

units.la: Olim Fratrum filii cum parentibus & fratribus defuncti non succedebant: Hodie vero liberi sororis vel fratris utrinq; conjuncti præmortui, cu ascendentibus, & fratribus ipsius defuncti ad successionem patrui admittuntur in stirpes. in princip. Authent. ut fratrum filii succedant.
units.tr: Formerly the children of brothers did not succeed together with the parents and brothers of the deceased; but today the children of a brother or sister, joined on both sides and dead before, are admitted per stirpes, along with the ascendants and brothers of the deceased, to the succession of their uncle. In princip. Authent. ut fratrum filii succedant.

units.la: Hoc autem privilegium ad nepotes vel pronepotes fratris utrinque conjuncti præmortui non extenditur: quia ultra fratrum filios repræsentatio in Collateralibus locum non habet. Authent. post fratres. cum ibi notatis. C. de legitim. hæredib.
units.tr: This privilege, however, does not extend to the grandchildren or great-grandchildren of a brother joined on both sides who has died before; for representation among collateral relatives does not go beyond the children of brothers. Authent. post fratres, with the notes there. C. de legitim. haeredib.

units.la: De jure vero Saxonico, defuncto sine liberis, succedunt soli pater & mater, exclusis defuncti fratribus & sororibus, etiam utrinque conjunctis, inquit Schneidewinus. Unde sicut pater & mater fratres defuncti excludunt, ita & avus, avia, proavus sive paternus sive maternus, fratribus utrinque conjunctis defuncto præferuntur: Et ita quotidie pronuntiatur, ut est sententia Scabin. Lipsensiũ post <bl>weichbild.</bl> Sub Rubric. <bl>Gros eltern sind näher</bl> <bl>Erben zunemmen / dann schwester oder brüder.</bl> Vide Schneidcvvinum[?].
units.tr: By Saxon law, however, if the deceased leaves no children, only the father and mother succeed, the brothers and sisters of the deceased being excluded, even those joined on both sides, as Schneidewin says. Hence, just as the father and mother exclude the brothers of the deceased, so too the grandfather, grandmother, great-grandfather or great-grandmother, whether on the paternal or maternal side, are preferred to brothers and sisters joined on both sides. And this is pronounced daily, as is the opinion of the Lipsian scabini after the Weichbild, under the rubric: Grandparents are nearer heirs than sister or brother. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Sequentes Regulae de parentum natu- ralium successione sunt ob- servandae.
units.tr: The following rules concerning the succession of natural parents are to be observed.

units.la: Prima Regula
units.tr: First Rule

units.la: Pater naturalis tantum, solus existens, filio naturali extincto, succedit in duabus unciis, hoc est, sexta parte hereditatis. Authen. licet. §. ab intestato. C. de naturalibus liber.
units.tr: A natural father, if he alone survives, succeeds to two ounces, that is, a sixth part of the inheritance, when his natural son has died without children. Authen. licet. §. ab intestato. C. de naturalibus liberis.

units.la: Secunda Regula
units.tr: Second Rule

units.la: Mater vero & alij ascendentes lineae maternae, eidem filio defuncto æque succedere possunt, ac si ex legitimo matrimonio natus esset. §. final. inst. de SC. Tertyllian. & l. si spuriis. ff. unde cognati.
units.tr: The mother, and the other ascendants of the maternal line, can succeed to the same deceased child just as if he had been born of a lawful marriage. §. final. Inst. de SC. Tertyllian. and l. si spuriis. ff. unde cognati.

units.la: Sequentes Regulae de successione le- gitimorum parentum tan- tum sunt obser- vandae.
units.tr: The following rules concerning the succession of lawful parents alone are to be observed.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Facta adoptione ab extraneo, filio defuncto, pater naturalis patri adoptivo in ejus hæreditatis successione præfertur: sed defuncto adoptato ab ascendente, adoptivus pater excluso, naturali, eidem succedit. l. cum in adoptivis. §. sed ne articulum. C. de adoptionibus.
units.tr: When an adoption has been made by a stranger and the adopted son has died, the natural father is preferred to the adoptive father in the succession to the inheritance. But if the adopted son has died having been adopted by an ascendant, the natural father, to the exclusion of the adoptive father, succeeds to him. Law "cum in adoptivis", §. "sed ne articulum", Code, on adoptions.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Pater arrogante solo superstite post obitum filij arrogati, tota ejus hæreditas ad eundem solum devolvitur: sed si vixerit adhuc arrogati pater natura-lis, lis, is patri arrogato in defuncti filii successione præfertur: Sin vero cum Arrogatore patre, extincto naturali, concurrant fratres & sorores utrinque conjuncti ipsi defuncto, inter illos omnes fit successio in capita. Gloss super verbis, Aliæ personæ. §. mortuo. instit. de adquisit. per adrogat.
units.tr: If the adrogating father survives alone after the death of the adrogated son, his whole inheritance passes to him alone. But if the natural father of the adrogated son is still alive, he is preferred to the adrogating father in the succession to the dead son. But if, with the adrogating father, the natural father being dead, brothers and sisters related on both sides to the deceased himself come together, the succession among all of them is by heads. Gloss on the words "Aliae personae", §. "mortuo", Institutes, on acquisition through adrogation.

units.la: Sequentes Regulæ de successione pa- rentum spuriorum sunt ob- servandæ.
units.tr: The following rules on the succession of spurious parents are to be observed.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Pater filio spurio nulla in re succedit, cum is plane sit incertus. l. si spurius. ff. unde cognati.
units.tr: A father succeeds to his spurious son in nothing, since the latter is plainly of uncertain father. Law "si spurius", Digest, "unde cognati".

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Mater vero, licet sit illustris, aliosque naturales & legitimos simul habeat, nihilominus filio suo spurio mortuo ab intestato succedere potest. §. final. & ibi Angel. inst. de SC. Tertyllian. Verum Accursius in d. §. final. diversum tenet, sed male. Unde a Doctoribus communiter reprehenditur, inquit Schneidewyn[?].
units.tr: A mother, however, although she is of noble rank and has other natural and legitimate children at the same time, may nevertheless succeed to her spurious son intestate when he has died. §. "final", and there Angelus, Institutes, on the Senatusconsultum Tertullianum. But Accursius, in the said §. "final", holds the contrary, but wrongly. Hence he is commonly criticised by the teachers, says Schneidewin[?].

units.la: De successione parentum, ex damnato coitu susceptorum, hæc tenenda est Regula.
units.tr: On the succession of parents to children born of a condemned union, this rule is to be held.

units.la: Neque pater, neque mater, nec ulli alii ascendentes liberis ex damnato coitu susceptis succedere possunt. Authen. ex complexu. C. de incest. & inutilib. nuptiis.
units.tr: Neither father, nor mother, nor any other ascendants can succeed to children born of a condemned union. Authentic "ex complexu", Code, on incest and invalid marriages.

units.la: De successione parentum spiritualium hæc notanda est Regula.
units.tr: On the succession of spiritual parents this rule is to be noted.

units.la: Sicut filii spirituales non succedunt parentibus spiritualibus: ita econtra, Parentes spirituales, non succedunt filiis spiritualibns.
units.tr: Just as spiritual children do not succeed to spiritual parents, so conversely spiritual parents do not succeed to spiritual children.

units.la: Secundus gradus ab intestato succedendi breviter expositus est.
units.tr: The second degree of succession intestate has been briefly set out.

units.la: Quid dicis de tertio Gradu?
units.tr: What do you say of the third degree?

units.la: Quando quis moritur non reliquis neque descendentibus, neque ascendentibus, tum Collaterales, à lege ad successionem defuncti, ab intestato, secundum gradus prærogativam vocantur. Authen: cessante. C. de legitim. hæredib.
units.tr: When someone dies leaving neither descendants nor ascendants, then collateral relatives are called by law to the succession of the deceased intestate, according to the priority of degree. Authentic "cessante", Code, on lawful heirs.

units.la: Quinam intelliguntur appellatione Collateralium?
units.tr: Who are understood by the term collaterals?

units.la: Non solùm fratres & sorores, & omnes alii sanguine juncti extransverso, sive sint propioris, sive ulterioris gradus in linea paterna, ad quam Agnati: aut materna, ad quam Cognati referuntur. §. 1. instit: de gradib. cognat.
units.tr: Not only brothers and sisters, but all others joined by blood across the line, whether of nearer or more remote degree, on the paternal line, to which the Agnates belong, or on the maternal line, to which the Cognates belong. §. 1, Institutes, on degrees of kinship.

units.la: Quot differentiæ inter fratres & sorores recensentur?
units.tr: How many differences are reckoned between brothers and sisters?

units.la: Tres. Alii enim Germani dicuntur, qui ex uno patre & una matre prognati sunt, & hi alias utrinque conjuncti vocantur, <bl>Brüder von vollet[?] geburt.</bl> Alii Consanguinei, qui unum eundemque quidem habuerunt patrem, sed diversas matres: Alii vero uterini, quibus una est mater, sed non unus idemque pater.
units.tr: Three. For some are called full (german) siblings, who were born of one father and one mother; these are otherwise called brothers related on both sides, "brothers of full birth". Others are half-blood (consanguine), who indeed had one and the same father but different mothers. And others are uterine, to whom there is one mother but not one and the same father.

units.la: Sequentes Regulæ sunt de collateralium naturalium & legitimorum simul successione obser- vandæ.
units.tr: The following rules are to be observed concerning the simultaneous succession of natural and legitimate collateral relatives.

units.la: Prima Regula.
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Fratres & sorores utrinque conjuncti, sive sint legitimi & naturales simul, sive legitimati per subsequens matrimonium, exclusis fratribus aut sororibus ex uno latere conjunctis, defuncto fratri aut sorori succedut in bonis tàm paternis, quàm maternis & aliunde quæsitis æqualiter sive in capita. Authent. cessante C. de legitim. hæred. cap. si igitur defunctus. Authent. de hæredib. ab intestato venientib.
units.tr: Brothers and sisters related on both sides, whether they are legitimate and natural at the same time, or legitimated by a later marriage, succeed the deceased brother or sister equally, per capita, in the paternal and maternal goods alike and in goods acquired from elsewhere, to the exclusion of brothers or sisters related on one side only. Authent. cessante C. de legitim. hæred. cap. si igitur defunctus. Authent. de hæredib. ab intestato venientib.

units.la: Secunda Regula.
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Fratres consanguinei, fratri suo consanguineo defuncto pariter succedunt, exclusis uterinis, quod ad adquisitionem bonorum paternorum attinet. l. de emancipatis. § cum enim &. C .de legitim. hæredib. Fratres vero uterini, quoad bona materna, in successione sui defuncti fratris uterini, præferuntur consanguineis fratribus. d. §. cum enim &. Sed in bonis aliunde acquisitis, ipsi defuncto fratres consanguinei & uterini æqualiter succedunt. Authent. Itaque. C. communia de successionib.
units.tr: Consanguine brothers succeed equally to their deceased consanguine brother, with uterine brothers excluded, so far as the acquisition of paternal goods is concerned. l. de emancipatis. § cum enim &. C. de legitim. hæredib. Uterine brothers, however, are preferred to consanguine brothers in the succession to their deceased uterine brother as regards maternal goods. d. §. cum enim &. But in goods acquired from elsewhere, consanguine and uterine brothers succeed the deceased equally. Authent. Itaque. C. communia de successionib.

units.la: Tertia Regula.
units.tr: Third Rule.

units.la: Filij prædefuncti fratris utrinq; conjuncti, admittuntur ad successionem defuncti, cum fratribus & sororibus ipsi defuncto utrinque junctis, in stirpes. Authent. cessante. C. de legitim. hæredib. Dissentit ab hac Regula jus Saxonicum, quod fratres & sorores utrinq; conjunctos defuncto, præfert fratris prædefuncti filiis. Vide Schneidewin.
units.tr: The children of a brother who has predeceased, related on both sides, are admitted to the succession of the deceased together with the brothers and sisters who are related to the deceased on both sides, per stirpes. Authent. cessante. C. de legitim. hæredib. The Saxon law dissents from this rule, since it prefers the brothers and sisters related on both sides to the deceased over the children of a predeceased brother. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quarta Regula.
units.tr: Fourth Rule.

units.la: Filij prædefuncti fratris ipsi defuncto utrinq; conjuncti, excludunt ab ea successione fratres ex uno latere tantum, propter jus repræsentationis. d. Auth. cessante. Variat & hic jus Saxonicum à jure civili. Nam de jure Saxonico præmortuorum fratrum filij, & fratres & sorores ex uno latere tantum, æqualiter succedunt defuncto in capita.
units.tr: The children of a predeceased brother, related on both sides to the deceased, exclude from that succession brothers related on one side only, by right of representation. d. Auth. cessante. Here too the Saxon law differs from the civil law. For by Saxon law the children of predeceased brothers succeed the deceased equally per capita together with brothers and sisters related on one side only.

units.la: Quinta Regula.
units.tr: Fifth Rule.

units.la: Filij fratris excludunt defuncti patruos, vel similes personas, in successione propter jus repræsentationis. Auth. post fratres autem. C. de legit. hæredib.
units.tr: The children of a brother exclude the uncles of the deceased, or persons in a similar position, from the succession, by right of representation. Authent. post fratres autem. C. de legit. hæredib.

units.la: Sexta Regula.
units.tr: Sixth Rule.

units.la: Filij aut filiæ, ex pluribus fratribus aut sororibus n[?]ati,natæve,quamvis numero inæquales sint, patruo tamen defuncto, non in stirpes (ut quidam veterum voluerunt) sed in capita succedunt. Secundum Baldum & Salycetum in d.Auth. cessante. Et per Constitutionem Caroli Quinti Imperatoris in Comitiis Spirensibus, Anno 1529. promulgatam.Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: Sons or daughters born of several brothers or sisters, although unequal in number, succeed to the deceased uncle not per stirpes (as some of the ancients wished) but per capita. So according to Baldus and Salicetus on the said Authent. cessante. And by the constitution of Emperor Charles V, promulgated at the Diet of Speyer in the year 1529. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Septima Regula[?]
units.tr: Seventh Rule.

units.la: Post fratres fratrumq; filios, vocantur ad successionem reliqui collaterales, quicunq; in gradu sunt proximiores, remotioribus exclusis: ita quòd infallibiliter semper prior in gradu, sit potior in successione, & pares in gradu, pariter admittantur in capita, secundum numerum personarum, non in stirpes. Authen. post fratres.la.2. C. de legitimis hæredibus. Obseruandum, quòd semper in computatione graduum descendentes ex fratre ex altero tantum latere sint remotiores, quàm descendentes à fatre[?], ex utroq; parente conjuncti, inquit Schneidevvinus.
units.tr: After brothers and the children of brothers, the remaining collateral relatives are called to the succession, whoever are nearer in degree, the more remote being excluded; so that the one who is prior in degree is always without fail preferred in succession, and those equal in degree are admitted equally per capita, according to the number of persons, not per stirpes. Authent. post fratres. l. 2. C. de legitimis hæredibus. It is to be observed that in the computation of degrees, descendants from a brother related through one parent only are always more remote than descendants of a brother related through both parents, says Schneidewin.

units.la: Sequentes Regulæ de Collateralium naturalium tantum succes- sione observen- tur.
units.tr: The following rules are to be observed concerning the succession of natural collateral relatives only.

units.la: Prima Regula[?]
units.tr: First Rule.

units.la: Fratres naturales tantùm, paterna origine conjuncti, sibi invicem non succedunt: quia nulla inter eos agnatio, vel cognatio de jure intercedit. §. vulgò quæsitos. inst. de successione cognator.
units.tr: Natural brothers related only through the father cannot succeed one another, because by law there is no agnation or cognation between them. §. vulgò quæsitos. inst. de successione cognator.

units.la: Secunda Regula[?]
units.tr: Second Rule.

units.la: Fratres naturales tantùm, respectu maternæ lineæ conjuncti sibi invicem succedere queunt. l.1. & l. sipurius.ff. unde cognati. constituta, incipit locatio & conductio esse. §. final. inst.cod.
units.tr: Natural brothers, joined to one another only through the maternal line, can succeed one another. Law 1 and the law "sipurius", Digest, "unde cognati"; the constitution beginning "locatio et conductio" ... Institutes, final paragraph, Code.

units.la: Hactenus dictum est de obligationibus, quæ ex contractu oriuntur: sequuntur obligationes, quæ quasi ex contractu nascuntur.
units.tr: So much has been said about obligations which arise from contract; there follow obligations which arise as if from contract.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS octavus Titulus? De obligationibus, quæ quasi ex contractu nascuntur. <bl>Von verpflichtungen/</bl> <bl>welche erwachsen auß handlungen/die</bl> <bl>sich einem contract vergleichen.</bl>
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TWENTY-EIGHTH TITLE? On obligations which arise as if from contract. On obligations which arise from acts resembling a contract.

units.la: Quæ obligationes oriuntur ex quasi contractu?
units.tr: Which obligations arise from quasi-contract?

units.la: SEx: Negotiorum gestio, cùm quis negotia abscentis gesserit: ultrò citroq; inter eos nascuntur actiones, quæ appellantur negotiorum gestorum: sed Domino quidem rei gestæ adversus eum, qui gessit, directa competit actio: Negotiorum autem gestori contraria. §. igitur cùm. inst eod.
units.tr: Management of another's affairs: when someone has managed the affairs of an absent person, actions arise between them in both directions, called actions for managed affairs. The principal has a direct action against the one who managed the business, and the manager has a contrary action against the principal. §. igitur cùm. Inst. eod.

units.la: Tutelæ administratio: ut, Tutores, qui tutelæ judicio tenentur, non proprie ex contractu obligati esse intelliguntur (nullum enim negotium inter tutorem & pupillum contrahitur) sed quia sanè non ex maleficio tenentur, quasi ex contractu teneri videntur. §. tutores. inst eod.
units.tr: Administration of guardianship: guardians, who are liable under the guardianship action, are not understood to be bound strictly by contract, since no contract is made between guardian and ward. But because they are not bound by delict, they are seen to be bound as if by contract. §. tutores. Inst. eod.

units.la: Rerum communio: ut, si inter aliquos communis res sit sine societate: veluti quòd pariter eis legata donatáve esset: & alter eorum alteri ideo teneatur communi dividundo judicio, quòd solus fructus ex ea re perceperit: quasi ex contractu teneri videtur. §. item si inter. inst. cod. Hæreditatis communio: ut, quando aliquis cohæredi familiæ hercisCundæ judicio obligatus est. §. idem juris, inst. cod.
units.tr: Joint ownership of things: for example, if a thing is held in common by certain persons without a partnership, as when it was left or given to them equally, and one of them is liable to the other under the action for dividing a common thing because he alone has taken the profit from it, he is seen to be bound as if by contract. §. item si inter. Inst. cod. Joint inheritance: for example, when someone is bound to a co-heir by the action for dividing an estate. §. idem juris, Inst. cod.

units.la: Hæreditatis aditio: ut hæres legatorum nomine non proprie ex contractu obligatus intelligitur: & tamen quia ex maleficio non est obligatus: quasi ex contractu debere intelligitur. §. hæres. inst. cod.
units.tr: Acceptance of an inheritance: the heir is not properly understood to be bound by contract on account of the legacies, yet because he is not bound by delict, he is understood to owe as if by contract. §. hæres. Inst. cod.

units.la: Solutio indebiti: ut, is, cui quis per errorem non debitum solvit, quasi ex contractu debere intelligitur. §. item is cui. inst. cod.
units.tr: Payment of what is not owed: one to whom someone pays by mistake what is not owed is understood to owe as if by contract. §. item is cui. Inst. cod.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS nonus Titulus? Per quas personas nobis obligatio adqui- ritur. Durch was personen wir verpflichtung bekommen.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE twenty-ninth Title? By what persons an obligation is acquired for us. By what persons an obligation is acquired.

units.la: Per quas personas adquiritur obligatio?
units.tr: By what persons is obligation acquired?

units.la: ADquiritur nobis non solum per nosmetipsos, sed per eas quoq; personas, quæ in nostra potestate sunt, veluti per servos & filios nostros. in princ. instit. cod.
units.tr: An obligation is acquired for us not only through ourselves but also through those persons who are in our power, such as our slaves and sons. in princ. Inst. cod.

units.la: Item per liberos homines & alienos servos, quos bona fide possidemus, adquiritur nobis: sed tantum ex duabus causis, id est, si quid ex operis suis, vel ex re nostra adquirant. §. item per. inst. cod.
units.tr: Likewise it is acquired for us through free men and other people's slaves whom we possess in good faith, but only on two grounds: namely, if they acquire something by their own work or by means of our property. §. item per. Inst. cod.

units.la: QUIS EST TRICESI- MUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE THIRTIETH Title?

units.la: Quibus modis tollitur obligatio. <bl>Jn was massen verpflichtung aufs-</bl> <bl>gehaben wirt.</bl>
units.tr: In what ways an obligation is removed. In what manner an obligation is ended.

units.la: Recita modos obligationis tollendae?
units.tr: State the ways of removing an obligation.

units.la: Primò, tollitur omnis obligatio solutione ejus quod debetur: vel si quis consentiente creditore, aliud pro alio solverit. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: First, every obligation is removed by payment of what is owed, or if someone, with the creditor's consent, pays something else in place of what was owed. in princ. Inst. eod.

units.la: Secundò, per acceptilationem (<bl>Durch ein quittantz</bl>) tollitur obligatio. Est autem acceptilatio, imaginaria solutio. §. item per. inst. eod.
units.tr: Second, an obligation is removed by acceptilation (by a receipt). Acceptilation is an imaginary payment. §. item per. Inst. eod.

units.la: Tertiò, novatione tollitur obligatio: veluti si id, quod tibi Sejus debebat, à Titio dari stipulatus sis. Nam interventu novę personę, nova nascitur obligatio, & prima tollitur, translata in posteriorem. §. praeterea. inst. eod.
units.tr: Third, an obligation is removed by novation: for example, if you have stipulated that what Seius owed you be given by Titius. For by the intervention of a new person a new obligation arises, and the first is removed, transferred to the later one. §. praeterea. Inst. eod.

units.la: Quartò, obligationes, quę consensu contrahuntur, contraria voluntate dissolvuntur. §. final. inst. eod.
units.tr: Fourth, obligations contracted by consent are dissolved by a contrary will. §. final. Inst. eod.

units.la: Hactenus tituli Tertij libri Institutionum breviter enarrati fuêre.
units.tr: Thus the titles of the third book of the Institutes have been briefly explained.

units.la: QUOT SUNT TITULI IN Quarto Libro Institutionum?
units.tr: HOW MANY TITLES ARE THERE IN THE Fourth Book of the Institutes?

units.la: Octodecim.
units.tr: Eighteen.

units.la: QUIS EST PRIMUS Titulus? De obligationibus, quae ex delicto na- scuntur. Von verpflichtungen, welche auß Malefiz oder vbelthaten erwachsen.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIRST Title? On obligations which arise from delict. On obligations which arise from crimes or wrongdoing.

units.la: Quae est continuatio hujus Rubricae ad praecedentes?
units.tr: What is the connection of this rubric with the preceding ones?

units.la: Quum sit expositum superiore libro de obligationibus ex contractu, & quasi ex contractu: sequitur ut de obligationibus ex maleficio, & quasi ex maleficio dispiciamus. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Since obligations from contract and quasi-contract were set out in the previous book, it follows that we should examine obligations from delict and quasi-delict. in princ. Inst. eod.

units.la: Obligationes ex delicto unde nascuntur?
units.tr: Whence do obligations from delict arise?

units.la: Omnes ex re nascuntur, id est, ex ipso maleficio, veluti ex furto, rapina, dāno, injuria, in prin.inst.cod.
units.tr: All arise from a thing, that is, from the wrong itself, as from theft, robbery, damage and injury. in prin. Inst. cod.

units.la: Quid est furtum?
units.tr: What is theft?

units.la: Furtum (ein <bl>Diebstal</bl>) est contrectatio fraudulosa, lucri faciendi gratia, vel ipsius rei, vel etiam usus ejus possessionisve, quod lege naturali prohibitum est admittere.§ furtum est.inst.cod.
units.tr: Theft (a Diebstal) is the fraudulent handling of a thing, for the sake of gain, whether of the thing itself or even of its use or possession, which natural law forbids. §. furtum est. Inst. cod.

units.la: Quot sunt furtorum genera?
units.tr: How many kinds of theft are there?

units.la: Duo: Manifestum, & non manifestum.§.furtorum autem.inst.cod.
units.tr: Two: manifest and non-manifest. §. furtorum autem. Inst. cod.

units.la: Quid est manifestus fur?
units.tr: What is a manifest thief?

units.la: Manifestus fur nec solum is est, qui in ipso furto deprehenditur, sed etiam is, qui in eo loco deprehenditur, quo furtum fit: veluti qui in domo furtum facit & nondum egressus janua, deprehensus fuerit. Sed si pertulit quo destinavit, tametsi non deprehendatur cum re furtiva, non est manifestus fur. Nec manifestū furtum quid sit, ex iis quæ diximus intelligitur.§. furtorum autem.inst.cod.
units.tr: A manifest thief is not only the one who is caught in the very act of theft, but also one who is caught in the place where the theft is committed, as one who commits theft in a house and is caught before he has gone out through the door. But if he has carried the goods to where he intended, even though he is not caught with the stolen property, he is not a manifest thief. Nor is it clear from what we have said what manifest theft is. §. furtorum autem. Inst. cod.

units.la: Quæ est pœna furti?
units.tr: What is the penalty for theft?

units.la: Pœna manifesti furti, quadrupli est tam ex servi, quam ex liberi persona: Nec manifesti, dupli.§.pœna.inst.cod.
units.tr: The penalty for manifest theft is fourfold, whether the thief is a slave or a free person; for non-manifest theft it is twofold. §. pœna. Inst. eod.

units.la: Jure tamen novissimo, & recepta Germaniæ consuetudine, fures, si quinq; aureos Ungaricos furati, laqueo suspenduntur: sin minus, scopis excoriantur: quod licet quidam improbent, frustra tamen nituntur: quotiescunq; enim, multis grassantibus, exemplo opus est, pœnæ augeri possunt, ut unius pœnæ metus possit esse multorum, ut dicitur in l.1. C.ad.l. Juliam repetundar. Et expressus textus est in §.si quis quinq;. C.F.de pace tenenda, & ejus violatorib.fures esse laqueo suspendendos. Inquit enim imperator Fredericus: si quis quinque solidos valens, aut plus fuerit furatus, laqueo suspendatur: sin minus scopis & forpice excorietur & tundatur (vel ut Gothofredus in margine habet, tondeatur.)
units.tr: Under the most recent law, however, and the custom received in Germany, thieves who have stolen five Hungarian gold coins are hanged from a noose; otherwise they are flogged with birch brooms. Some disapprove of this, but they strive in vain. For whenever many are running wild, an example is needed, and penalties may be increased so that the fear of one punishment may restrain many, as is said in l. 1. C. ad l. Juliam repetundarum. There is also an express text in §. si quis quinque. C. F. de pace tenenda, et ejus violatoribus, that thieves are to be hanged from a noose. For the emperor Frederick says: "If anyone has stolen five solidi in value or more, let him be hanged from a noose; otherwise let him be flayed with brooms and tongs and beaten" (or, as Gothofredus has in the margin, "shorn").

units.la: Ad quem spectat res furtiva fure deprehenso?
units.tr: To whom does stolen property belong once the thief has been caught?

units.la: Ad dominum, cui res subtracta est. Argum. l. si. ca-ptivus. ff. de captivis & de postliminio. Ubi deciditur quod expulsis hostibus ex agris, quos ceperant, dominia agrorū ad priores dominos redeant & non publicentur. Per quem textum reprobāda videtur consuetudo, qua fiscus rem furtivam retinet: Nihil enim Dominus rei admisit. Nō igitur debet propter delictum furis re sua privari. l. sancimus. C. de poenis, ubi dicitur, peccata suos teneant authores: nec ulterius progrediatur metus, quam reperiatur delictum.
units.tr: To the owner from whom it was taken. Argument from l. si captivus, ff. de captivis et de postliminio, where it is decided that when the enemy has been driven out, the ownership of the fields they had seized returns to the former owners and is not confiscated. By this text the custom by which the treasury keeps stolen property seems to be rejected: for the owner has committed no offence. Therefore he ought not to be deprived of his property on account of the thief's crime. l. sancimus. C. de poenis, where it is said that sins hold their own authors, and that fear should not go further than the offence found.

units.la: De jure Saxonico judex rem furtivam servat per annum & diem, & domino intra illud tempus petēti eam restituit: si vero intra annum & diem non venerit, judex rem furtivam in usum proprium vertit. Schneidevvinus hic.
units.tr: By Saxon law the judge keeps stolen property for a year and a day, and restores it to the owner if he seeks it within that time. If the owner does not come within a year and a day, the judge puts the stolen property to his own use. Schneidewinus here.

units.la: Quomodo fit furtum?
units.tr: How is theft committed?

units.la: Furtum fit, non solum cum quis intercipiendi causa rem alienam amovet: sed generaliter cum quis alienam rem invito Domino contrectat. Itaque sive creditoris pignore, sive is, apud quem res deposita est, ea re utatur: sive is, qui rem utendam accepit, in alium usum eam transferat, quam cujus gratia ei data est, furtum committit. Placuit tamen eos, qui rebus commodatis aliter uterentur, quam utendas acceperint, ita furtum committere: si se intelligant, id invito domino facere: cumq; si intellexisset nō permissurum. At si permissurum credant, extra crimen videri, optima sane distinctione: quia furtum sine affectu furandi non committatur. §. furtum autem. & §. placuit. inst. eod.
units.tr: Theft is committed not only when someone removes another's property for the sake of appropriating it, but generally whenever someone handles another's property against the owner's will. Therefore, whether a creditor makes use of a pledge, or the one with whom goods have been deposited uses them, or the one who has received a thing for use transfers it to another use than that for which it was given to him, he commits theft. It has nevertheless been held that those who use lent goods otherwise than they received them to use commit theft in this way: if they understand that they are doing so against the owner's will, and especially if he would not have permitted it had he known. But if they believe he would permit it, they are seen to be outside the crime, a very sound distinction, since theft is not committed without the intention of stealing. §. furtum autem. and §. placuit. Inst. eod.

units.la: Tenetúrne furti, præstans opem & consilium ad committendum furtum?
units.tr: Is one liable for theft who gives help and counsel in committing it?

units.la: Interdum quoq; furti tenetur, qui ipse furtum nō fecit : qualis est is, cujus ope & consilio furtum factum est.§.interdum.inst.eod.
units.tr: Sometimes a person is also liable for theft who did not commit the theft himself, such as one by whose help and counsel the theft was done. §. interdum. Inst. eod.

units.la: Si filij & servi in patria vel dominica potestate exi- stentes, surripiant res aliquas patri vel domino, committúntne furtum?
units.tr: If sons and slaves who are under paternal or lordly power take some goods from their father or master, do they commit theft?

units.la: Hi, qui in parentum vel dominorū potestate sunt, si rem eis surripiunt, furtum faciunt, & res in furtivâ causam cadit.§.hi qui.inst.eod.
units.tr: Those who are under the power of parents or masters, if they take something from them, commit theft, and the property falls under the charge of theft. §. hi qui. Inst. eod.

units.la: Cui competit furti Actio?
units.tr: To whom does the action for theft belong?

units.la: Furti actio ei competit, cujus interest rem salvam esse, licèt Dominus non sit.§.furti autem.inst.eod.
units.tr: The action for theft belongs to the one whose interest it is that the property be safe, even if he is not the owner. §. furti autem. Inst. eod.

units.la: Facitne furtum impubes rem alienam amovendo?
units.tr: Does a minor commit theft by removing another's property?

units.la: In summa sciendum est, quæsitum esse, an impubes rem alienam amovendo, furtum faciat? Et placuit, quia furtum ex affectu furandi consistit, ita demum obligari eo crimine impuberem, si proximus pubertati sit, & ob id intelligat se delinquere.§.in summa. inst.eod.
units.tr: In sum, it should be known that the question has been raised whether a minor who removes another's property commits theft. And it has been held that, since theft consists in the intention of stealing, a minor is bound by that crime only if he is close to puberty and therefore understands that he is doing wrong. §. in summa. Inst. eod.

units.la: QVIS EST SECVNDVS Titulus? De vi bonorum raptorum. Von gewalt der genommenen güter.
units.tr: What is the second title? On the force of goods seized. Concerning violence over goods taken away.

units.la: Tenetúrne furti, qui res alienas rapit?
units.tr: Is one liable for theft who seizes another's property?

units.la: QVi res alienas rapit, tenetur quidē furti (quis enim magis alienam rem invito Domino contrectat, quam qui vi rapit? ideoque rectè dictum est eum improbū furem esse) sed tamen propriā actione ejus delicti nomine prætor introduxit, quæ appellatur vi bonorum raptorum: Et est intra annum quadrupli, post annum simpli. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: Whoever seizes another's property is indeed liable for theft (for who handles another's property more against the owner's will than one who seizes it by force? Hence it is rightly said that he is a wicked thief). Nevertheless, the praetor introduced a special action on account of this wrong, which is called the action for goods seized by force; it lies for quadruple within a year, and for simple damages after a year. Institutes, beginning, same title.

units.la: Quando competit Actio?
units.tr: When does the action lie?

units.la: Si dolo malo quis rapuerit. Nam qui aliquo errore ductus, rem suam esse existimans, & imprudens juris, eo animo rapuerit, quasi domino liceat etiam per vim rem suam auferre à possessoribus, absolvi debet. §. ita tamen inst. cod.
units.tr: When someone has seized by evil intent. For one who, led by some mistake, thinking the thing to be his own, and ignorant of the law, seized it with the intention that, as though it were lawful for the owner to take back his own property by force from its possessors, ought to be acquitted. Institutes, §. "ita tamen", same title.

units.la: Quid Divalibus Constitutionibus prospectum est?
units.tr: What has been provided by the imperial constitutions?

units.la: Ut nemini liceat vi rapere vel rem mobilem, vel se moventem, licet suam eandem rem existimet: sed si quis contra statuta principum fecerit, rei quidem suæ dominio cadat: sin autem aliena res sit, post restitutionem ejus, etiam æstimationem ejusdem rei præstet. §. ita tamen. inst. cod.
units.tr: That no one may lawfully seize by force either a movable thing or one that moves itself, even if he believes the thing to be his own; but if anyone acts against the enactments of the emperors, he indeed forfeits ownership of his own thing, but if the thing belongs to another, he must, after its restitution, also make good its value. Institutes, §. "ita tamen", same title.

units.la: QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE THIRD TITLE?

units.la: De Lege Aquilia. Vom Gesetz Aquilia. Quid constituitur per legem Aquiliam?
units.tr: On the Lex Aquilia. On the Aquilian Law. What is established by the Lex Aquilia?

units.la: Damni injuriæ actio constituitur per legem Aquiliam: cujus primo capite cautum est, ut si quis alienum hominem, alienámve quadrupedem, quæ pecudum numero sit, injuria occiderit: quanti ea res in eo anno plurimi fuerit, tantum domino dare damnetur. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: The action for wrongful damage is established by the Lex Aquilia. Its first chapter provides that if anyone wrongfully kills another's man or another's four-footed animal of the kind that belongs to the herd, he is condemned to give the owner as much as the thing was worth at its highest in that year. In the beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quis intelligitur injuria occidere?
units.tr: Who is understood to kill wrongfully?

units.la: Injuria occidere intelligitur, qui nullo jure occidit. Itaq; qui latronem insidiatorem occiderit, non tenetur, utiq; si aliter periculum effugere nō potest. §. injuria autem. inst. cod. Ac ne is quidē hac lege tenetur, qui casu occidit, si modo culpa ejus nulla inveniatur §. ac ne is. inst.cod.
units.tr: One is understood to kill wrongfully who kills without any right. Therefore, one who kills a robber or an ambusher is not liable, especially if he cannot otherwise escape the danger. Institutes, same title, the section on wrongful killing. Nor is even he liable under this law who kills by chance, provided that no fault of his is found. Institutes, same title, the section "and not even he".

units.la: Tenetúrne miles, si exercendo se in campo servum alicujus prætereuntem occiderit?
units.tr: Is a soldier liable, if while exercising himself in a field he kills a passing slave of someone?

units.la: Si id à milite in eo campo, ubi solitum est exercitari, admissum est, nulla culpa eius intelligitur. Si-alius tale quid admiserit, culpæ reus est. Idem juris est de milite, si in alio loco, quàm qui ad exercitandū militib. destinatus est, id admiserit. §. itaq;. inst.cod.
units.tr: If this was done by a soldier in that field where it is customary to drill, no fault is understood in him. If someone else had done such a thing, he is liable for fault. The same law holds for a soldier if he did it in a place other than the one assigned for training soldiers. Institutes, same title, the section "therefore".

units.la: Tenetúrne putator, si putando arbores, ramo dejecto, servum alicujus præte- reuntem occiderit?
units.tr: Is a pruner liable, if while pruning trees he knocks down a branch and kills a passing slave of someone?

units.la: Si propè viam publicam aut vicinalem id factum est, neq; proclamavit, ut casus evitari posset: culpæ reus est: sed si proclamavit, nec ille curavit præcavere, extra culpam est putator. §. item si. inst.eod.
units.tr: If the thing was done near a public or local road, and he did not call out so that the accident could be avoided, he is liable for fault. But if he called out and the other did not take care to guard himself, the pruner is free from fault. Institutes, same title, the section "likewise if".

units.la: Tenetúrne medicus secans servum, & cura- tionem derelinquens?
units.tr: Is a physician liable, who cuts a slave and abandons the treatment?

units.la: Si medicus, qui servum tuum secuit, dereliquerit curationem ejus, & ob id mortuus fuerit servus: culpæ reus erit. Imperitia quoq; culpæ adnumeratur: veluti si medicus ideo servum tuum occiderit, quia male eum secuit, aut perperam ei medicamentum dederit. §. praterea. inst.eod.
units.tr: If a physician who cut your slave abandons his treatment, and the slave dies because of it, he will be liable for fault. Lack of skill is also counted as fault, as when a physician kills your slave because he cut him badly, or gave him the wrong medicine. Institutes, same title, the section "moreover".

units.la: Quid dicis de imperitia & infirmitate mu- lionis aut equo vectii? [?]
units.tr: What do you say about the inexperience and weakness of a muleteer or of a rider on a horse? [?]

units.la: Impetu mularum, quas mulio propter imperitiā retinere non potuit, si servus tuus oppressus fuerit, culpæ reus est mulio. Sed si & propter infirmitatem eas retinere non potuerit, cùm alius firmior eas retinere potuisset, æquè culpa tenetur. Eadem placuerunt de eo quoq;, qui cum equo vehereatur, impetum ejus aut propter infirmitatem, aut propter imperitiam suam retinere non potuerit.§. impetu.inst.cod.
units.tr: If your slave is crushed by the rush of mules which the muleteer could not restrain because of his inexperience, the muleteer is liable for fault. But if he also could not restrain them because of his weakness, when another stronger man could have restrained them, he is equally held liable for fault. The same rule was laid down also for one who is carried on a horse, if he could not restrain its rush, either because of his weakness or because of his inexperience. Institutes, same title, the section "the rush".

units.la: Quot actiones damno dato competunt?
units.tr: How many actions for damage done are available?

units.la: Tres:Directa, utilis, & in factum. Directa quę competit ex mente & verbis legis duodecim tabularum: Utilis, quę non expresse constat ex verbis legis duodecim tabularum, sed per JC ex interpretatione introducta est: Actio in factum, est inventa a prętore, in subsidium legis Aquiliæ in casibus, qui lege Aquilia non comprehenduntur. Schneidcvvin[?].hic.
units.tr: Three: (1) the direct action, (2) the useful action, and (3) the action on the case. The direct action is available from the intention and words of the law of the Twelve Tables. The useful action is not expressly contained in the words of the law of the Twelve Tables, but was introduced by the jurists through interpretation. The action on the case was devised by the praetor, in support of the Lex Aquilia, in cases which are not covered by the Lex Aquilia. Schneidewin[?] here.

units.la: QUIS EST QUARTUS Titulus? De injuriis. <bl>Von injurien vnnd schmache.</bl>
units.tr: WHICH IS THE FOURTH TITLE? Of injuries. Of injuries and insults.

units.la: Quid est injuria?
units.tr: What is injury?

units.la: GEneraliter injuria dicitur omne, quod non jure fit: specialiter, alias contumelia, quæ a contemnendo dicta est, alias culpa, alias iniquitas & injustitia. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: In general, injury means anything done contrary to law. In a narrower sense it is sometimes insult, a word derived from contempt; sometimes fault; sometimes wrong and injustice. In the beginning of the Institutes, same book.

units.la: Quibus modis fit injuria?
units.tr: In what ways is injury committed?

units.la: Injuria committitur non solum cum quis pugnapulsatus, aut fustibus cæsus vel etiam verberatus erit: sed & si cui convicium factum fuerit, sive cujus bona quasi debitoris, qui nihil deberet, possessa fuerint ab eo, qui intelligebat nihil eum sibi debere: vel si quis ad infamiam alicujus libellum, aut carmen, aut historiam scripserit, composuerit, ediderit, dolove malo fecerit, quo quid eorum fieret. §. injuria autem. inst. cod.
units.tr: Injury is committed not only when someone is struck with a fist, beaten with clubs, or even whipped. It is also committed when someone is subjected to abuse, or when another's goods are seized as though he were a debtor, although he owes nothing and the seizer knew that he owed nothing. It is likewise committed when someone writes, composes, or publishes a pamphlet, poem, or history to another's disgrace, or does anything with malicious intent to bring about any of these. §. Injury moreover, Institutes, same book.

units.la: Quæ est pœna injuriarum?
units.tr: What is the penalty for injuries?

units.la: Pœna injuriarum ex lege duodecim tabularum propter membrum quidem ruptum talio erat: propter os vero fractum nummariæ pœnæ erant constitutæ.§ pœna autem.inst.eod.
units.tr: Under the Law of the Twelve Tables, the penalty for injuries was retaliation in kind for a broken limb, but for a broken bone fixed monetary penalties. §. The penalty moreover, Institutes, same place.

units.la: De Jure Saxonico quando criminaliter actio injuriarum instituta est, in effectu ita distinguitur: aut agitur pro gravi & atroci injuria reali, aut pro injuria verbali vel reali levi. Primo casu, quando vulnera ex dolo inflicta sunt, & criminaliter pro iis vindicandis agitur, punitur reus in amputatione unius manus, qua delictum perpetratum est: Secundo casu, ab accusatione criminali injuriarum verbalium, reus potest se redimere, solvendo triginta solidos[?], sive civiliter sive criminaliter actum fuerit. Schneidevvin. hic.
units.tr: As to Saxon law, when the action for injury is brought criminally, it is in effect distinguished thus: either it is brought for a grave and atrocious real injury, or for a verbal injury or a slight real one. In the first case, when wounds have been inflicted deliberately and the matter is pursued criminally to avenge them, the guilty party is punished by the amputation of the hand with which the wrong was committed. In the second case, the defendant may buy himself out of a criminal accusation of verbal injuries by paying thirty solidi, whether the matter is brought civilly or criminally. Schneidewin, here.

units.la: Mynsingerus autem Centur. 2.obseivat[?].98. inquit: formula agendi de injuriis admodum in frequenti apud nos est usu,ut is,qui passus est injuriam,ad revocationem injuriosorum verborum & restitutionem famæ læsæ agat.
units.tr: Mynsinger, however, in Centuria 2, observation 98, says: the form of action concerning injuries is very frequently used among us, namely that the one who has suffered the injury sues for the retraction of the injurious words and the restoration of his damaged reputation.

units.la: Quomodo æstimatur atrox injuria?
units.tr: How is an atrocious injury assessed?

units.la: Vel ex facto: veluti si quis ab alio vulneratus sit, vel fustibus cæsus. Vel ex loco: veluti si cui in Theatro vel[?] in foro vel conspectu prætoris injuria facta sit. Vel ex persona: veluti si magistratus injuriam passus fuerit. Nonnunquam & locus vulneris atrocem injuriam facit, veluti si in oculo quis percussus fuerit.§ Atrox.inst.cod.
units.tr: Either by the deed: for example, if someone has been wounded by another or beaten with clubs. Or by the place: for example, if an injury has been done to someone in the theatre, in the forum, or in the sight of the praetor. Or by the person: for example, if a magistrate has suffered the injury. Sometimes the location of the wound also makes the injury atrocious, for example if someone has been struck in the eye. §. Atrocious, Institutes, same book.

units.la: Quomodo possumus agere de injuria?
units.tr: How can we bring an action for injury?

units.la: In summa sciendum est, de omni injuria eum, qui passus est, posse vel criminaliter agere, vel civiliter. Criminaliter agitur, quando affectus injuria petit injuriantem puniri in corpore vel agit ad pœnam pecuniariam Fisco inferendam: Civiliter agitur, quando actor petit poenam sibi adjudicari: daturque actio in tantum, in quantum injuriatus eam astimaverit: ut cùm dicit in libello se malle tot vel tot aureos amittere, quàm ejusmodi injuria affici, secundum Mynsing. hic. Et Andreà Gaill. observat. 65. lib. 1.
units.tr: In sum, it must be understood that for any injury the one who has suffered it may proceed either criminally or civilly. Proceedings are criminal when the injured party seeks that the wrongdoer be punished in his body, or sues for a pecuniary penalty to be paid to the treasury. Proceedings are civil when the plaintiff asks that a penalty be awarded to him, and the action is granted for as much as the injured party has assessed it at, as when he states in the libel that he would rather lose such and such a number of gold coins than suffer such an injury; according to Mynsinger here, and Andreas Gail, Observation 65, Book 1.

units.la: QUIS EST QUINTUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE FIFTH TITLE?

units.la: <bl>De obligationibus quae quasi ex delicto</bl> <bl>nascuntur. Von verpflichtungen, welche als auß Malefiz vnd vbelthat erwachsen.</bl>
units.tr: On obligations which arise as if from a delict. Von verpflichtungen, welche als auß Malefiz vnd vbelthat erwachsen. (On obligations which arise as if from wrongdoing. On obligations that arise as from a crime and misdeed.)

units.la: Quot modis obligationes ex quasi delicto nascuntur?
units.tr: How many ways do obligations arise as if from a delict?

units.la: Quatuor: primo, si judex litem suam fecerit: non proprie ex maleficio obligatus videtur: sed quia neq; ex maleficio, neq; ex contractu obligatus est, & utiq; peccasse aliquid intelligitur, licet per imprudentiam: ideo videtur quasi ex maleficio teneri, & in quantum de ea re aequum religioni judicantis videbitur, poenam sustinebit. in prin.inst eod.
units.tr: Four: first, if a judge has made the case his own: he is not strictly seen as bound from a wrongdoing, but because he is bound neither from a wrongdoing nor from a contract, and yet is understood to have done something wrong, though through carelessness, he is therefore held as if bound from a wrongdoing, and he will undergo a penalty to the extent that it seems fair to the judge's conscience concerning that matter. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Secudo,is,ex cujus coenaculo, vel proprio ipsius, vel conducto, vel in quo gratis habitat, dejectum effusumve aliquid est, ita ut alicui noceret, quasi ex maleficio obligatus intelligitur. §.item is.ex.inst eod.
units.tr: Second, the person from whose upper room something has been thrown or poured out, whether it is his own, rented, or where he lives free of charge, so that it harms someone, is understood to be bound as if from a wrongdoing. Institutes, same title, §. item is.

units.la: Tertio,is quasi ex maleficio obligatur, qui ea parte, qua vulgò iter fieri solet, id positum aut suspensum habet, quod potest (si ceciderit) alicui nocere, §.1. verf.cui similis.inst.eod.
units.tr: Third, the person is bound as if from a wrongdoing who has placed or hung something in that part where people commonly pass, which could (if it fell) harm someone. Institutes, same title, §. 1, verse "cui similis."

units.la: Quarto, exercitor navis aut cauponae aut stabuli de dolo aut furto, quod in navi aut caupona ut stabulo factum erit, quasi ex maleficio teneri videtur, si modo ipsius nullum est maleficium, sed alicujus co.ü[?], quorum opera navem aut cauponam aut stabulum exercet.§.final.inst.cod.
units.tr: Fourth, the master of a ship, or of an inn or stable, is held as if bound from a wrongdoing for a fraud or theft committed in the ship, inn or stable, provided that it was not his own wrongdoing but that of some of those whose work he uses to run the ship, inn or stable. Final §, Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST SEXTUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE SIXTH TITLE?

units.la: De actionibus. Von rechtlichen forderungen oder klagen.
units.tr: On actions. On legal claims or suits.

units.la: Unde sumi potest continuatio huius Ti- tuli ad praecedentes?
units.tr: From what can the continuation of this title to the preceding ones be drawn?

units.la: EX.§. finali supr. de jur. N. G. & C. Ubi Imperator posuit generalem quandam divisionem juris, q; omne jus, quo utimur, vel ad personas, vel res, vel actiones pertineat. Absoluto igitur tractatu personarum & rerum, nunc tertiam partem, tanquam sinalem, de Actionibus subjicit.
units.tr: From the final paragraph (§ final) of the Title above, on law (de iure) of persons, things and actions: there the Emperor laid down a general division of law, namely that all law we use pertains either to persons, to things, or to actions. Having therefore completed the treatment of persons and things, he now adds, as a final third part, the treatment of Actions.

units.la: Quid igitur est Actio?
units.tr: What, then, is an action?

units.la: Actio nihil aliud est, quàm jus persequendi in judicio, quod sibi debetur.in princ.inst.cod.
units.tr: An action is nothing other than the right of pursuing in court what is owed to oneself.

units.la: Omnium autem actionum quibus inter aliquos apud judices, arbitrósve, de quacunque re quaeritur, summa divisio in duo genera deducitur; aut enim in rem sunt, aut in personam. Namq; agit unusquisque aut cum eo, qui ei obligatus est, vel ex contractu vel ex maleficio: quo casu proditae sunt actiones in personam, per quas intendit adversarium ei dare aut facere oportere, & aliis quibusdam modis. Aut cum eo agit, qui nullo jure ei obligatus est, movet tamen alicui de aliqua re controversiam: quo casu proditae actiones in rem sunt: veluti si rem corporalem possideat quis, quam Titius suã esse affirmet: possessor autem dominum ejus se esse dicat. Nam si Titius suã esse intendat: in rem actio est.§.omniû.inst.cod. Sunt praeterea Actiones aut Civiles, aut Praetoriae. Civiles sunt, quae vel ex lege duodecim tabularum, vel plebiscitis, vel scriptis seu responsis prudentum vel constitutionibus principum producuntur: praetoriae sunt, quae in defectum civilium actionum, aut a praetore, aut ab aedilibus curulibus fuerunt introductae. Praetoriae autem Actiones tripliciter intelliguntur: primo inventione seu origine: Secundo extensione: Tertio approbatione. Nunc breviter ex Schneidecvvino & libello, qui inscribitur, Analysis Dialectica Institutionum, Actionum definitiones seu descriptiones enarrabimus.
units.tr: The chief division of all actions, by which anyone seeks something from another before judges or arbitrators, is reduced to two kinds: for actions are either in rem or in personam. For each person sues either the one who is bound to him, whether by contract or by wrongdoing; in which case actions in personam are provided, by which the plaintiff claims that the opponent ought to give or do something to him, and so on. Or he sues one who is bound to him by no right, yet raises a dispute with him over some matter; in which case actions in rem are provided. For example, if someone possesses a corporeal thing which Titius affirms to be his own, while the possessor says that he himself is its owner: if Titius claims that it is his, the action is in rem. Moreover, actions are either civil or praetorian. Civil actions are those introduced by the Law of the Twelve Tables, by plebiscites, by writings or opinions of the jurists, or by imperial constitutions; praetorian actions are those introduced, in default of civil actions, either by the praetor or by the curule aediles. Praetorian actions are understood in three ways: first by their invention or origin, secondly by their extension, thirdly by their approval.
