Now we shall briefly set out the definitions or descriptions of actions from Schneidewin and from the little book entitled Analysis Dialectica Institutionum.

units.la: Quid est rei vendicatio?
units.tr: What is the vindication of a thing?

units.la: Est actio realis, domino directo vel utili contra possessorem, vel quasi, ad quandam rem corporalem competens, qua declaratio dominij illius rei, & restitutio una cum fructibus pendentibus & extantibus petitur. l.action. genera.ff.de actionib.& oblig.
units.tr: It is a real action, belonging to the direct or indirect owner against the possessor, or against one quasi-possessor, concerning a certain corporeal thing, by which a declaration of ownership of that thing is sought, together with its restitution along with the fruits both hanging and still extant.

units.la: Vendicare enim propria significatione est appropriare, id est, suum esse dicere, proprietatis affirmatione, [illegible, ~8 letters] Schneidecvvin. hic.
units.tr: For to vindicate, in its proper sense, is to appropriate, that is, to say that a thing is one's own, by affirming ownership, [illegible, ~8 letters] Schneidewin, here.

units.la: Quid est Actio confessoria?
units.tr: What is the confessory action?

units.la: Est actio in rem competens alicui ratione juris, vel servitutis sibi debitae, vel fundo suo, vel quasi suo, contra impedientem, ad declarationem juris sui. Et dicitur cōfessoria, quia Actor eam proponendo confitetur, & asserit sibi jus in re competere, nec refert, sive verbis affirmativis, sive negativis proponatur. Vide Schneidecvvinum.
units.tr: It is an action in rem belonging to someone by reason of a right, either of a servitude owed to him or to his land, or to what is quasi his, against one who hinders him, for the declaration of his right. It is called confessory because the plaintiff, by bringing it, confesses and asserts that a right in the thing belongs to him; and it makes no difference whether it is framed in affirmative or in negative words. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid est Actio negatoria?
units.tr: What is the negatory action?

units.la: Est actio in rem, competens alicui ratione rei suae, vel quasi liberę, respectu adversarij, contra utentem aliqua servitute in illa re ad pronuntiandum, adversario non esse jus utendi tali servitute.
units.tr: It is an action in rem belonging to someone by reason of his thing, or of what is quasi free, against an opponent who uses some servitude over that thing, to declare that the opponent has no right to use such a servitude.

units.la: Quid est publiciana Actio?
units.tr: What is the Publician action?

units.la: Est actio prætoria realis, qua petimus id, quod non bis ex iusta causa à non domino bona fide traditum est, & nondum usucaptum. Nam pone, quòd ad te ex titulo donationis, vel alia quacunq; causa habili ad transferendum dominium, pervenerit equus quidam, quia forte in itinere, dum ires[?] Noribergam, emisti, à quodam extraneo tibi incognito, quem credebas esse dominum, qui tamen in rei veritate non erat, si postea casu amittas possessionem istius equi, antequam illum usucapias, non competit tibi rei vendicatio contra possessorem. Nam ad hoc, ut rei vendicatio competat, requiritur à patre Actoris dominium. l. in rem. ff. de rei vendicat. Sed tu non es dominus. Ergo non competit tibi rei vendicatio. Minor probatur ex eo, quia venditor non dominus, non potuit in te transferre dominium, quod ipse non habuit. l. nemo plus juris. ff. de diverf. Reg. jur. Sed tantum transtulit in te usucapiendi conditionem, quam usucapionem nondum complevisti. Igitur de jure civili, nulla tibi datur actio ad equuum vendicandum & recuperandum. Sed quia inconveniens erat, quòd habes bonam fidem, & justum titulum, actione reali ad recuperandam rem destituerentur: prætor seu judex (qui æquitate ante oculos habere debet. l. quod si Ephesi. ff. de eo quod cert. loc. dar. oport.) benignitate motus, introduxit hanc actionem publicianam, quæ datur ei, qui bona fide & justo titulo à non domino habet rem, quam nondum usucepit, ad eam vendicandam, si forte casu eam amisit. Vide Tit. ff. de publician. in rem Action.
units.tr: It is a praetorian real action, by which we claim that thing which was delivered in good faith, on a just cause, by one who was not the owner, and which has not yet been acquired by usucapion. For suppose that a certain horse came into your hands by a title of gift, or by any other cause suitable for transferring ownership, and that you bought it, perhaps on a journey to Nuremberg, from some stranger unknown to you, whom you believed to be the owner, though in truth he was not; if afterwards by chance you lose possession of that horse before you acquire it by usucapion, the vindication of the thing against the possessor is not available to you. For in order that vindication be available, ownership on the part of the plaintiff's predecessor is required (D. 6.1.) But you are not the owner. Therefore the vindication of the thing is not available to you. The minor premise is proved from the fact that a seller who is not the owner could not transfer to you an ownership which he did not himself have (D. 50.17.). But he transferred to you only the condition of acquiring by usucapion, which you have not yet completed. Therefore by civil law no action is granted to you for claiming and recovering the horse. But since it was unfitting that you, who have good faith and a just title, should be left without a real action for recovering the thing, the praetor or judge (who ought to keep equity before his eyes) was moved by kindness and introduced this Publician action, which is granted to one who has the thing in good faith and by a just title from a non-owner, and which he has not yet acquired by usucapion, for vindicating it, if by chance he has lost it. See the title in the Digest on the Publician action.

units.la: Quid est Actio rescissoria?
units.tr: What is the rescissory action?

units.la: Est actio prætoria, qua rescissa usucapione, agitur ad rem à possessore usucaptam, quasi nunquam usucapta fit. Complectitur autem duo remedia: scilicet Judicium rescindens, quod est officium judicis nobile, per quod datur restitutio in integrum, remoto obstaculo usucapionis completæ in alterius absentia: Et judicium rescissorium, quod competit rescisso obstaculo per remedium rescindens, cum scilicet via aperta est, & impedimentum usucapionis remotum, ut is, qui læsus fuit, possit jam priorem actione intentare, & rem suam petere, ac si nunquam fuisset usucapta. Exempli gratia: Titius emit meum Codicem a Sempronio bona fide, & per traditionem accepit, postea cum proficisceretur causa studiorum in Italiam, abfuit per triennium, & ita usucapionem complevit, ac Codicem meum usucepit (de jure enim civili res mobiles triennio præscribuntur. l. unica. C. de usucap. transformanda. De Jure vero Saxonico, anno, in jar vnnd tag/ Das ist/ in einem ganzen jar/ sechs wochen/vnd drey tage) postea cum revertitur, volo Codicem meum per rei vendicationem ab eo petere, sed quia obstat mihi exceptio præscriptionis, directò hoc facere nō possum. Quæritur igitur, qualiter mihi succurratur, ne amittam Codicem meum, quem propter absentiam Titij vendicare non potui. Et quia iustissima causa est restitutionis, deciditur quod debeam adire judicem, & narrare qualiter Titius studiorum causa fuerit absens, & Codicem meu usuceperit: Et implorare ipsius officium, ut restituat me in integrum, & rescindat illam usucapionem a Titio in absentia completam, qua rescissa, recuperro pristinam actionem, & potero jam a Titio vendicare Codicem, ac si eum non usucepissem. Illa restitutio in integrum, quo rescinditur usucapio, appellatur remedium rescindens: Actio vero, quæ concessa restitutione, & rescisso obstaculo usucapionis mihi competit, rescissoria dicitur. Schneidewinus[?] hic.
units.tr: It is a praetorian action by which, once usucapion has been rescinded, one sues for a thing usucapted by its possessor, as if it had never been usucapted. It comprises two remedies. The first is the rescinding judgment, the noble office of the judge, by which restitution in integrum is granted and the obstacle of a usucapion completed in the absence of the other party is removed. The second is the rescissory judgment, which belongs to the party restored once the obstacle has been rescinded by the rescinding remedy, that is, when the way is open and the impediment of usucapion has been removed, so that the injured party may now bring the former action and claim his property as if it had never been usucapted. For example: Titius bought my codex from Sempronius in good faith and received it by delivery. Afterwards, when he set out for Italy for the sake of his studies, he was away for three years, and so he completed the usucapion and acquired my codex by usucapion (for under the civil law movable things are prescribed after three years, see the single law C. de usucapione transformanda. Under the Saxon law, however, it is a year, "in Jar und Tag", that is, one whole year, six weeks and three days). Later, when he returns, I wish to claim my codex from him by the action for recovery of property, but because the plea of prescription stands in my way, I cannot do this directly. The question therefore is how I may be helped, so that I do not lose my codex, which I could not claim because of Titius's absence. And since the cause of restitution is most just, it is decided that I ought to approach the judge, tell him how Titius was absent for the sake of his studies and acquired my codex, and implore his office to restore me to my former position and rescind that usucapion completed by Titius in his absence. Once this is rescinded, I recover my former action and can now claim the codex from Titius as if I had never allowed him to usucapt it. The restitution in integrum by which the usucapion is rescinded is called the rescinding remedy; the action which, once restitution is granted and the obstacle of usucapion removed, belongs to me is called the rescissory action. Schneidewin[?] on this point.

units.la: Quid est Actio revocatoria?
units.tr: What is the revocatory action?

units.la: Est actio praetoria realis, competens creditori contra eum, qui sciens & particeps fraudis accepit bona à debitore in fraudem creditoris alienata. Refertur aut ideo inter reales praetorias actiones, quia magnâ cognationem cum publiciana & rescissoria habet.
units.tr: It is a real praetorian action, belonging to a creditor against one who, knowing of and party to the fraud, has received goods from a debtor that were alienated to the creditor's prejudice. It is ranked among the real praetorian actions because it has a close kinship with the publician and the rescissory action.

units.la: Et comprehendit sub se tanquàm sex species: Actionem Paulianam, quae competit creditori ad bona corporalia, mobilia vel immobilia, in fraudem creditoris alienata: Actionem in factum, quae ad bona incorporalia in fraudem creditorum alienata datur: Actionem Favianam: quae datur patrono, in cujus fraudem libertus aliquid inter vivos alienavit, per quam revocat res alienatas, ut legitimam portionem in successione liberti, quae hodie tertia est, consequatur: Actionem Calvisianam, quae indifferenter tam patrono in bonis liberti, quam creditori in bonis debitoris competit: Actionem utilem Favianam, quae datur impuberi arrogato ad consequendâ quartam: Edictû fraudatorium, quod locum habet cùm quis non rem suam, sed alienam in alterius fraudem alienaverit, ut patet in exemplo tutoris alienantis res pupilli. l. si pupilli debitor. ibi Gloss. & Bartol. ff. de solutionibus. Vide Schneidevvinum.
units.tr: It comprehends under itself, as it were, six kinds: the Pauline action, which belongs to a creditor against corporeal goods, movable or immovable, alienated to the creditor's prejudice; the action in factum, which is given against incorporeal goods alienated to the prejudice of creditors; the Favian action, which is given to a patron against whose fraud a freedman has alienated something inter vivos, by which he revokes the alienated things so that he may obtain the legitimate portion in the freedman's succession, which today is one third; the Calvisian action, which belongs indifferently to the patron against the freedman's goods and to the creditor against the debtor's goods; the useful Favian action, which is given to an arrogated minor for obtaining the fourth; and the fraudulent edict, which applies when someone has alienated not his own thing but another's, to the prejudice of another, as is clear in the example of a guardian alienating the property of his ward (see the law si pupilli debitor, with the Gloss and Bartolus there, ff. de solutionibus). See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid est Actio Serviana?
units.tr: What is the Serviana action?

units.la: Est actio praetoria realis, qua locator agit ad res, quae à conductore in rem locatam, ut perpetuò, id est, quamdiu durat tempus locationis, illic essent, invectae & illatae: Et locatori pro pensione, deterioratione rei tacitè obligatae sunt, & à quocunq; possessore quasi pignus avocat, & donec ei integrè satisfiat, retinet.
units.tr: It is a real praetorian action by which a landlord sues for the things which the tenant has brought in and placed on the leased property, so that they remain there continually, that is, for as long as the lease lasts; and they are tacitly bound to the landlord for the rent and against damage to the property. He recovers them from any possessor as if they were a pledge, and retains them until he is fully satisfied.

units.la: Quid est Actio quasi Serviana, seu hypothecaria?
units.tr: What is the quasi-Serviana, or hypothecary, action?

units.la: Est actio praetoria realis, quae competit creditori contra possidentem rem, quæ ei expressè in specie, vel generaliter & tacitè obligata est, ad consequendā ejus rei possessionem, ad hoc, ut eam retinere vel alienare possit, si à debitore non fuerit redempta.
units.tr: It is a real praetorian action which belongs to a creditor against the possessor of a thing that has been expressly pledged to him specifically, or generally and tacitly, to obtain possession of that thing, so that he may retain or alienate it, if it has not been redeemed by the debtor.

units.la: Quid differt hæc actio à Serviana & pignoratitia?
units.tr: How does this action differ from the Serviana and the pignoratitia?

units.la: Serviana pro tacito pignore tantùm locatori datur: Hypothecaria verò cuivis creditori, cui res expressè est pignorata, competit.
units.tr: The Serviana is granted only to a landlord, on account of a tacit pledge; the hypothecary action, on the other hand, belongs to any creditor to whom a thing has been expressly pledged.

units.la: Pignoratitia actio est personalis, quæ actualem traditionem desiderat, & personam creditoris, non autem tertij cujusdam possessoris insequitur: Sed Hypothecaria seu quasi Serviana est realis, quæ etiam sine traditione ex solo consensu partium producitur, ad consequendam rei oppignoratæ possessionem. l. pignoris. C. de pignoribus & hypothecis. l. final. C. de distractione pignor.
units.tr: The pignoratitia action is personal: it requires actual delivery and pursues the person of the creditor, not of some third possessor. But the hypothecary or quasi-Serviana action is real: it is brought even without delivery, from the consent of the parties alone, to obtain possession of the pledged thing (see the law pignoris, C. de pignoribus et hypothecis; and the final law, C. de distractione pignorum).

units.la: Quid est Actio de constituta pecunia?
units.tr: What is the Action on a Promise of Payment (de constituta pecunia)?

units.la: Est actio prætoria personalis, qua agimus contra eum, qui per nudum pactum constituit se soluturum id, quod prius ipse, vel alius quidam ex nudo pacto, vel quacunq; causa debebat. De hac actione est T.tulus in ff. & C. de constitut. pecun.
units.tr: It is a praetorian personal action, by which we sue against one who, by a bare agreement, promises to pay what he himself, or some other person, owed from a bare agreement or from any cause whatever. On this action see the title in the Digest and the Code, de constituta pecunia.

units.la: Exemplo autem sic poterit illustrari: Ego per nudum pactum promisi tibi decem, certum est quòd de jure civili non competat actio contra me, ad illa decem l. juris gentium. §. sed cum nulla. ff. de pactis. Si postea ex intervallo iterum per nudum pactum tibi eadem decem promittam, & constituam me soluturum, Actione de constituta pecunia contra me experiri poteris, ut solvam.
units.tr: It can be illustrated by an example. Suppose I promised you ten by a bare agreement. It is certain that under the civil law no action lies against me for those ten (law juris gentium, §. sed cum nulla, Digest de pactis). If afterwards, at some interval, I again promise you the same ten by a bare agreement and undertake to pay them, you may bring the Action on a Promise of Payment against me, to make me pay.

units.la: Quid est Actio de peculio?
units.tr: What is the Action concerning the Peculium?

units.la: Est actio prætoria personalis, qua petimus à patre vel domino, ut solvat pro filio vivente, vel servo, nobis ex contractu obligato, quatenus est in peculio. Est autem hæc actio a prętore introducta. §.actiones autem. inst. de Actionib. De jure enim civili pater ex filij contractu, & econtrà, nec naturaliter, nec civiliter obligatur, ut per Titul. C. ne filius pro patre.
units.tr: It is a praetorian personal action, by which we seek from a father or master that he pay, on behalf of a living son or slave who has bound himself to us by contract, to the extent of the peculium. This action was introduced by the praetor (§. actiones autem, Institutes de actionibus). For under the civil law a father is not bound, either naturally or civilly, by his son's contract, nor the reverse, as the title in the Code ne filius pro patre shows.

units.la: Sed prætor consideravit, quòd pater (idem de domino & servo intelligendum est) habens filium industrium, & ad negotiationes idoneum, dat ei aliquando pusillam aliquam pecuniarum substantiam, qua negotietur, & quia ejus occasione sæpe multum æris alieni filius conflat, æquum visum fuit prætori ne contrahentes cum filiofamilias deciperentur, ut pater ex contractu filij teneatur, & convenirí possit ex præsumpta voluntate, propter concessionem peculij. Sed quia illa voluntas non est simplex & absoluta, sed certa & limitata, respectu illius quantitatis concessæ in peculium. Prætor adjecit moderationem & induxit, quòd & pater & Dominus non teneantur simpliciter & in solidum, sed eatenus, quatenus illa voluntas se extendit, & sic peculiotenus tantum, id est, non ultra vires peculij.
units.tr: But the praetor considered that when a father (the same must be understood of a master and slave) has a son who is diligent and fit for business, he sometimes gives him a small sum of money to trade with; and because the son often runs up a large debt on that occasion, it seemed fair to the praetor that those contracting with a son under power should not be deceived. Therefore the father is held liable on his son's contract and may be sued, on the presumed will of the father, by reason of the grant of the peculium. But since that will is not simple and absolute, but definite and limited to the amount granted as peculium, the praetor added a restriction and provided that neither father nor master is liable simply and for the whole, but only so far as that will extends, that is, only up to the value of the peculium and not beyond its resources.

units.la: Quid est Actio in factum ex juramento præstito?
units.tr: What is the Action in factum arising from an oath taken?

units.la: Est actio prætoria personalis, qua agit is, qui, postulante adversario suo, in continenti juravit aliquid sibi deberi, vel reum res suas possidere ad præstandum id super quo antea actor juravit sibi deberi, vel rem suam esse. Juramentum autem litis decisivum dupliciter præstari potest, formiter & informiter. Formiter juratur, quando cum causa adjecta, vel cum expressione contractus juratur: Informiter vero juratur, quando nulla causa seu nomine contractus, expresse juratum est, sibi aliquid deberi. Ex juramentis formiter aut informiter præstitis tres actiones oriuntur. Nam ex juramento formiter præstito nascuntur duæ: Una in factum ex juramento: Altera utilis ex contractu. Ex informi vero juramento tantum Actio in factum juratoria producitur.
units.tr: It is a praetorian personal action, by which one sues who, at his opponent's demand, has immediately sworn that something is owed to him, or that the defendant possesses his goods, in order to make good what the plaintiff had sworn was owed to him, or that the thing was his. An oath decisive of a lawsuit may be taken in two ways, formally and informally. It is taken formally when it is sworn with a cause added, or with the contract expressly named; it is taken informally when it is sworn expressly that something is owed to him without any cause or name of contract being given. Three actions arise from oaths taken formally or informally. For from an oath taken formally two arise: one, the action in factum from the oath, the other, the equitable action from the contract. From an informal oath only the action in factum on the oath is produced.

units.la: Quid est pœnalis Actio?
units.tr: What is a penal action?

units.la: Est per quam non petitur res, tanquam principale debitum, sed tanquam pœna. Et licet pœna etiam sit res, cum rei vocabulum sit latissimum. l. rei appellat. ff. de verbor. signif. Tamen est res incidens, & non principaliter in negotio versatur, sed ex quodam eventu & accidenti petitur.
units.tr: It is one by which the thing is not sought as the principal debt, but as a penalty. And although a penalty is also a thing, since the word "thing" is very broad (law rei appellatione, Digest de verborum significatione), it is nevertheless an incidental thing, and does not lie at the heart of the transaction, but is sought from some event or accident.

units.la: Quid est Actio Albi corrupti?
units.tr: What is the Action concerning the corrupted White Board (Album corruptum)?

units.la: Est actio prætoria, pœnalis, quæ dicitur Actio in factum ex edicto prætoris de albo corrupto descendens. Estq; popularis, competens cuilibet de populo, contra eum qui id, quod in albo prætoris propositum est, per se, vel per alium, dolo malo corrupit, vel amovit, ad pœnam quinquaginta aureorum. Fuit Album, murus seu paries dealbatus vel tabula dealbata, in qua jura & præcepta prætoris generalia & specialia scribebantur, & publicè proponebantur ac pro curia & palatio affigebātur, ut quilibet ea videre & legere posset. Vide Schneidewin.
units.tr: It is a praetorian penal action, called the Action in factum arising from the praetor's edict on the corrupted white board. It is also popular, available to any member of the public, against one who, by malicious deceit, himself or through another, has corrupted or removed what was posted on the praetor's board, for a penalty of fifty gold pieces. The album was a whitened wall or panel or a whitened tablet on which the general and special laws and edicts of the praetor were written, publicly displayed and fixed up before the court-house and palace, so that anyone could see and read them. See Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid est Actio in jus vocandi?
units.tr: What is the Action for summoning to court (in jus vocandi)?

units.la: Est actio pœnalis prætoria, per quam filius aut libertus, qui patrem patronumve sine prætoris venia in jus vocavit, pœna quinquaginta aureorum damnatur. l. penultim. ff. de in jus vocando.
units.tr: It is a praetorian penal action, by which a son or freedman who summoned his father or patron to court without the praetor's permission is condemned to a penalty of fifty gold pieces (law penultima, Digest de in jus vocando).

units.la: Quid est actio de in jus vocato vi exempto?
units.tr: What is the action concerning one who forcibly rescued a summoned person?

units.la: Est actio prætoria pœnalis, qua cum eo agitur, qui in jus vocatum vi exemit, dolóve malo eximendum curavit, ut quanti ea res ab actore æstimatur, damnetur. l. 1. & l. 5. ff. ne quis eum, qui in jus vocabitur, vi eximat. Eximendi autem verbum generale est. Nam eximere est quoquo modo auferre: utputa si quis morâ fecerit, quo minus aliquis in jus veniret, ut actionis dies exiret, vel res tempore amitteretur. l. sed eximendi. ff. eod.
units.tr: It is a praetorian penal action, brought against one who forcibly rescued a person summoned to court, or maliciously with deceit took care that he should be rescued, so that he is condemned to the value that the plaintiff puts on the matter (laws 1 and 5, Digest ne quis eum, qui in jus vocabitur, vi eximat). The word eximere is general: for to rescue is to remove in any manner whatever; for example, if someone caused a delay so that a person would not come to court, so that the day for the action passed, or the thing was lost through lapse of time (law sed eximendi, Digest, same title).

units.la: Quid sunt Actiones præjudiciales?
units.tr: What are prejudicial actions?

units.la: Sunt actiones in quibus agitur de statu alicujus personæ. Et sunt tres actiones præjudiciales: quarum prima est civilis, non prætoria, & in ea quæritur an quis sit servus vel liber, de hac loquitur Tit. in. ff. & C. de liberal. cauf.
units.tr: They are actions in which the status of some person is contested. There are three prejudicial actions. The first is civil, not praetorian, and in it the question is whether someone is a slave or free; on this see the title in the Digest and the Code, de liberali causa.

units.la: Secunda dicitur de ingenuitate, qua scilicet quæritur an quis sit libertus vel ingenuus.
units.tr: The second is called the action concerning freeborn status (de ingenuitate), in which the question is whether someone is a freedman or a freeborn person.

units.la: Tertia de partu agnoscendo dicitur, qua quæritur, an quis sit filius vel non, de qua Tit. in. ff. de liber. agnoscendis. Posteriores duæ actiones sunt prætoriæ. Dicuntur autem ideo præjudiciales, quia omnes aliæ quæstiones silent & quiescunt, donec declaretur, an aliquis sit servus, libertus vel filius, ita quod præjudicent aliis quæstionibus, quæ non possunt intentari, si verum est, quod per præjudicialem petitur.
units.tr: The third is called the action for acknowledging a child (de partu agnoscendo), in which the question is whether someone is a son or not; on this see the title in the Digest, de liberis agnoscendis. The latter two actions are praetorian. They are called prejudicial because all other questions stand silent and rest until it is declared whether someone is a slave, a freedman or a son; thus they prejudge other questions, which cannot be brought if what is sought by the prejudicial action is true.

units.la: Quid est Condictio furtiva?
units.tr: What is the action for condiction of theft?

units.la: Est actio personalis, quæ ex delicto oritur, & rei persecutoria est: Non enim pœnam furti, sed ipsam rem furtivam persequitur, ita quod si res extet, condicatur cum omni interesse. l. 3. ff. de condictio. furtiva.
units.tr: It is a personal action, arising from a delict, and it is a real action for recovery: it does not pursue the penalty for theft but the stolen thing itself, so that if the thing still exists it is reclaimed together with all its value to the claimant. Digest, de condictione furtiva, law 3.

units.la: Quid est Actio mutui?
units.tr: What is the action on a loan (actio mutui)?

units.la: Est Actio personalis, qua petimus res nostras, quas alicui mutuo dedimus, in eodem genere nobis reddendas. Datur autem ad hoc, ut debitor rem mutuatam restituat, non quidem in specie seu individuo (quotiescunq; enim hoc agitur, ut idem corpus, quod traditur, restituatur, non mutuum contrahitur, sed cadit in aliam speciem contractus, & erit aut commodatum, depositum vel pignus. l. 2. in princip. ff. de rebus credit. si certum petetur), sed in eodem genere, ut pecunia pro pecunia, vinum pro vino. Vide Mynsinger. & Schneidevvin.
units.tr: It is a personal action by which we claim our goods, which we have lent to someone, to be returned to us in the same kind. It is given so that the debtor may restore the thing lent, not indeed in its specific individual form (for whenever it is sought that the very same body which was handed over be returned, a loan is not contracted, but the matter falls under another kind of contract, and it will be either a commodatum, a deposit or a pledge; Digest, de rebus creditis, law 2, beginning, if a specific thing is demanded), but in the same kind, as money for money, wine for wine. See Mynsinger and Schneidewin.

units.la: Quid est Actio commodati directa?
units.tr: What is the direct action of commodatum?

units.la: Est actio personalis, qua persequimur: primò, ut commodatarius rem ipsam commodatam restituat in specie: Deinde, si res commodata sit reddita[?] deterior, ut praestetur, quod interest commodantis, secundum Mynsingerum.Vide Tit.in ff.commodati.
units.tr: It is a personal action by which we pursue: first, that the borrower restore the very thing lent in its specific form; then, if the thing lent has been returned in worse condition, that there be paid what the lender's interest requires, according to Mynsinger. See the title in the Digest, de commodato.

units.la: Quid est Actio commodati contraria?
units.tr: What is the contrary action of commodatum?

units.la: Est actio personalis, qua persequimur: primò, ut solvatur, quanti interest commodatarij, rem commodatam ante expletum usum fuisse ablatam: Deinde impensas majores, & necessariò in re cōmodata factas. l. in commodato. §. sicut. ff. commodati vel contrà. l. in rebus. §. possunt. ff. eod.
units.tr: It is a personal action by which we pursue: first, that there be paid to the borrower the value of his interest, because the thing lent was taken from him before the use was finished; then the greater expenses necessarily incurred on the thing lent. Digest, de commodato, law on the commodatum, paragraph "sicut"; or conversely, law "in rebus", paragraph "possunt", under the same title.

units.la: Quid est Actio depositi directa?
units.tr: What is the direct action of deposit?

units.la: Est actio personalis, qua deponens agit adversus eum, apud quem res deposita est, ut eandem rem sibi restituat.
units.tr: It is a personal action by which the depositor sues the one with whom the thing was deposited, that he restore that same thing to him.

units.la: Quid est Actio depositi contraria?
units.tr: What is the contrary action of deposit?

units.la: Est qua depositarius adversus eum, qui rem deposuit, agit, ut quicquid in re deposita tuenda & asservanda bona fide impenderit, refundat. Vid. Tit. in ff. depositi vel contrà.
units.tr: It is the action by which the depositary sues the one who made the deposit, that he repay whatever he has spent in good faith on protecting and keeping the deposited thing. See the title in the Digest, de depositi vel contra.

units.la: Quid est Actio furti?
units.tr: What is the action for theft?

units.la: Est actio merè poenalis, quae vel jure praetorio vel civili competit, ad persequendam poenam, sive quadrupli, si furtum manifestum sit: sive dupli, si non manifestum. Caeterum quanquam haec dupli & quadrupli poena pecuniaria, in fures à jure civili olim in usum recepta est, Fredericus tamen Imperator ejus nominis primus constituit, ut fures laqueo suspenderentur. §. ultim. in C. F. de pace tenend. & ejus violatoribus.
units.tr: It is a purely penal action, which lies either by praetorian or by civil law, for pursuing a penalty of fourfold if the theft is manifest, or twofold if it is not manifest. Yet although this penalty of double and fourfold in money was once received into common use against thieves by the civil law, the Emperor Frederick, the first of that name, nevertheless ordained that thieves be hanged by the noose, and their violators likewise. Last paragraph, Code, Frederick, on keeping the peace and against its violators.

units.la: Quid est Actio vi bonorum raptorum?
units.tr: What is the action for goods taken by force?

units.la: Est actio praetoria, per quam ab eo, qui rem violenta manu eripuit, quadruplum intra annum exigitur: post annum vero simplum duntaxat. l. 4. §. idcirco illud. ff. de vi bonor. raptor. In quadruplo autem & rei persecutio inst, ita ut poena tripli fit: unde & haec actio mixta dicitur, quia tam poenae, quam rei persecutoria est.
units.tr: It is a praetorian action, by which, from the one who seized the property by violent hand, fourfold is exacted within a year; but after a year only the single amount. Digest, de vi bonorum raptorum, law 4, paragraph "idcirco illud". In the fourfold, however, there is also a pursuit of the thing itself, so that the penalty becomes threefold; whence this action is also called mixed, because it is both penal and a real action for recovery.

units.la: Quid est Actio legis Aquiliae?
units.tr: What is the action under the Lex Aquilia?

units.la: Est actio civilis in personam, quae datur domino adversus eum, qui damnum injuria dedit, vel saltem causam damni praestitit, ut quanti plurimi res vel anno proximo, vel triginta diebus proximis, fuerit, tanti damnetur. Vide Tit. in ff. ad leg. Aquil.
units.tr: It is a civil action in personam, given to the owner against the one who has caused damage by wrong, or at least furnished the cause of the damage, so that he be condemned to pay as much as the thing was worth at its highest value in the year just past or in the thirty days just past. See the title in the Digest, ad legem Aquiliam.

units.la: Estq; duplex: Directa & Utilis. Directa in eum datur, qui praecipue suo corpore vel manibus suis damnum dedit: Utilis vero in eum competit, qui aliquo medio damni causam praestitit.
units.tr: It is twofold: direct and useful. The direct action lies against the one who caused the damage chiefly by his own body or hands; the useful action lies against the one who furnished the cause of the damage by some intermediary means.

units.la: Quid est Actio ex testamento pro legato Vene- rabilibus locus relicto?
units.tr: What is the action on a testament for a legacy left to the venerable place (Church)?

units.la: Est actio personalis, in duplum competens adversus eum, qui negat ex haereditate, quam ipse adivit, Ecclesiae quid legatum esse: vel fatetur, & sine causa differt illius legati solutionem.
units.tr: It is a personal action, lying for double against the one who, having taken up the inheritance, denies that anything is owed to the Church from it as a legacy, or admits it but without cause delays payment of that legacy.

units.la: Etiamsi autem actio ex testamento regulariter rem tantum legatam, vel per fideicommissum relictam complectatur, sitq; rei tantum persecutoria, & in simplum detur: tamen si quis rem Ecclesiae vel aliis piis scholarum vel pauperum locis in testamento relictam tantisper tradere differt, donec in jus vocetur, tunc mixta est: & in duplum datur, quia & rem ipsam, vel pecuniam & aliud tantundem pro poena dare ac solvere condemnandus est. §. item mista. inst. de Actionibus. Vide Mynsingerum.
units.tr: Although the action arising from a testament ordinarily embraces only the thing bequeathed, or left by fideicommissum, and is merely a real action for recovery, given for single value, nevertheless if someone delays handing over to the Church, or to schools or other pious places or places for the poor, a thing left in a testament, until he is summoned to court, then it becomes mixed, and is given for double, because he is condemned to give and pay both the thing itself, or money, and an equal amount besides as a penalty. Institutes, de actionibus, paragraph "item mista". See Mynsinger.

units.la: Quid est Actio familiae herciscundae?
units.tr: What is the action for dividing an inheritance among heirs (actio familiae herciscundae)?

units.la: Est actio personalis, mixtam causam habens, & adversus haeredem competit, qui sine justa causa cohaeredi negat divisionem rerum haereditariarum de sui natura divisibilium, quas pro indiviso possident, ut dividat, praestetque interesse. Vide Tit.in ff.familiae herciscundae.
units.tr: It is a personal action with a mixed cause. It lies against an heir who, without just cause, refuses to a co-heir the division of the inherited goods, which by their nature are divisible but are held undivided, so that he divides them and makes good the interest involved. See the title in the Digest on the action for dividing a family inheritance.

units.la: Quid est Actio communi dividundo?
units.tr: What is the action for dividing common property (actio communi dividundo)?

units.la: Est actio mixta, quę competit inter eos, qui ex qua cunq; causa habet res aliquas communes, & eas pro indiviso possident, ut per officium judicis dividantur. Vide Tit. in ff. communi dividundo.
units.tr: It is a mixed action, which lies between those who hold some goods in common, from whatever cause, and possess them undivided, so that they may be divided through the office of a judge. See the title in the Digest on the action for dividing common property.

units.la: Quid est Actio finium regundorum?
units.tr: What is the action for determining boundaries (actio finium regundorum)?

units.la: Est actio mixta, illis competens, qui habent praedia rustica confinia adversus vicinum possessorem, ad constitutionem novorum terminorum, vel reparationem antiquorum, & ad praestandum interesse. Vide Mynsingerum.
units.tr: It is a mixed action, available to those who hold rural estates bordering one another, against the neighbouring possessor, for the establishment of new boundary markers or the restoration of old ones, and for making good the interest involved. See Mynsinger.

units.la: Qui est Actio servi corrupti?
units.tr: What is the action for a corrupted slave (actio servi corrupti)?

units.la: Est actio personalis, quae datur ad duplum, contra eum qui servi alterius animum dolo malo persuadedo corrupit, ut deterior fieret. §. item servi. instit. de actionib. l. 1. ff. de servo corrupto.
units.tr: It is a personal action, given for double damages, against one who by deceit and wicked intent persuades another's slave to change his mind, so that he becomes worse. Institutes, the section "item servi", on actions; Digest, law 1, on a corrupted slave.

units.la: Quid est Actio in factum contra ca- lumniatores?
units.tr: What is the action in factum against false accusers (actio in factum contra calumniatores)?

units.la: Est actio personalis, quae proprie in eum datur, qui pecuniam accepit, ut innocenti alicui in judicio per calumniam negotium faceret, hoc est, calumnioso judicio vexaret, vel qui alteri per calumniam pecuniam dedit, ne sibi negotium fieret, intra annum in quadruplum, post annum vero in simplum ejus pecuniae, quam accepit. l. 1. ff. de calumniatoribus.
units.tr: It is a personal action, given properly against one who has accepted money in order to harass an innocent person in a lawsuit through false accusation, that is, to vex him with a malicious prosecution; or against one who, through false accusation, has given money to another so that a case would not be brought against him. It lies for fourfold the money received if brought within a year, and after a year for the simple amount of that money. Digest, law 1, on false accusers.

units.la: Quid est Condictio ex lege contra mi- nistros publicos?
units.tr: What is the condictio against public officials (condictio ex lege contra ministros publicos)?

units.la: Est actio personalis, quæ datur contra executores magistratuum, seu publicos nuntios, qui plus debito exigunt à litigantibus ratione sportularum[?].
units.tr: It is a personal action, given against the executors of magistrates, or public messengers, who demand from litigants more than is owed by way of fees (sportulae).

units.la: Differt autem ab actione tripli, quia ea condictio datur reo contra actorem plus debito petentem in libello: condictio vero de qua hic dicitur competit parti gravatæ ab ipsis executoribus ad quadruplum.
units.tr: It differs, however, from the action for the triple amount, because that condictio is granted to the defendant against a plaintiff who sues in his writ for more than is owed, whereas the condictio of which we speak here belongs to the injured party against the executors themselves, for fourfold damages.

units.la: Quid est Actio quod metus causa?
units.tr: What is the action quod metus causa?

units.la: Est actio prætoria personalis in rem scripta, per quam is, cui res per vim vel metum, in constantem virum cadentem, extorta est, intra annum quadruplum, vel post annum simplum, ab eo qui rem extortam possidet, consequitur. l.1.ff. quod metus causa gestum erit.
units.tr: It is a praetorian personal action, framed on a thing, by which one from whom property has been extorted by force or by fear falling upon a steadfast man recovers, within a year, fourfold, or after a year, the simple amount, from the person who holds the extorted property. Digest, law 1, on what was done through fear.

units.la: Quid est Actio empti?
units.tr: What is the action of purchase (actio empti)?

units.la: Est actio in personam bonæ fidei civilis, quæ datur emptori contra venditorem pro re empta, cujus pretium exolvit, consequenda. Vide Titul.in ff. de actionib. empti & venditi.
units.tr: It is a personal action in good faith of the civil law, which is granted to the buyer against the seller, to be pursued for goods bought, the price of which he has paid. See the title in the Digest on the actions of buying and selling.

units.la: Complectitur autem hæc actio & tres alias sub se actiones. Primo actionem de Evictione, qua agitur contra venditorem, qui rei venditæ dominus non fuit, ut evictionem emptori de re vendita præstet. Vide Tit.in ff. de Evictionib. Est autem Evictio, ut Hotomannus inquit, ejus rei quam Adversarius legitimo jure acquisierat, per Judicem recuperatio.
units.tr: This action also embraces three other actions under it. First, the action on eviction, by which one sues a seller who was not the owner of the goods sold, so that the seller makes good to the buyer the eviction from the goods sold. See the title in the Digest on evictions. Eviction, as Hotman says, is the recovery, by a judge, of a thing that an adversary had acquired by lawful right.

units.la: Secundo Redhibitoriam actionem, qua emptor intra sex menses ad rescindendum contractum agere potest, si res vendita latens aliquod vitium in se habeat.l.ex empto. §. redhibitionem. ff. de actionib. empti & venditi.
units.tr: Second, the redhibitory action, by which a buyer may sue within six months to rescind the contract, if the goods sold have some hidden defect. Digest, law "ex empto", section "redhibitionem", on the actions of buying and selling.

units.la: Tertio actionem præscriptis verbis, qua compellendus est venditor ad implenda pacta actioni adjecta. Vide Mynsinger. in §. rei persequendæ. num. 65. Titulo noftio[?].
units.tr: Third, the action on the terms stated, by which the seller is compelled to fulfil the agreements attached to the sale. See Mynsinger on the section "rei persequendae", number 65, and in this title.

units.la: Quid est Actio venditi?
units.tr: What is the action of sale (actio venditi)?

units.la: Est actio bonæ fidei civilis, qua venditor utitur adversus emptorem, ut justum pretium pro re vendita consequatur. l. Julianus. §. ex vendit. ff. de Actionib. empti & venditi.
units.tr: It is an action in good faith of the civil law, by which the seller proceeds against the buyer, so as to obtain a just price for the goods sold. Digest, law "Julianus", section "ex vendito", on the actions of buying and selling.

units.la: Quid est Actio locati?
units.tr: What is the action of letting (actio locati)?

units.la: Est actio personalis bonæ fidei civilis, quæ locatori adversus conductorem competit, pro repetenda annua pensione rei locatæ. Vide Tit. in. ff. locati & conducti.
units.tr: It is a personal action in good faith of the civil law, which lies to the lessor against the lessee, for recovering the yearly rent of the thing let. See the title in the Digest on letting and hiring.

units.la: Quid est Actio conducti?
units.tr: What is the action of hiring (actio conducti)?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonæ fidei in personam, per quam is, qui vel rem utendam, vel opus faciendum conduxit, sive recepit, ut vel re sarta tecta utatur, vel operis perfecti mercedem consequatur, & leges conventionis servantur, postulat. l. ex conducto. ff. locati & conducti.
units.tr: It is a civil action in good faith, in personam, by which one who has hired either a thing to be used or a work to be done, or has undertaken it, demands that either he may use the thing kept in repair, or obtain the wages of the completed work, and that the terms of the agreement be observed. Digest, law "ex conducto", on letting and hiring.

units.la: Quid est Actio negotiorum gestorum?
units.tr: What is the action for business done (actio negotiorum gestorum)?

units.la: Est actio prætoria bonæ fidei personalis, ex quasi contractu proveniens, qua, qui alterius negotium sine mandato ac sponte sua gessit, quicquid con nomine illi vel abest vel abfuturum est, a domino repetit: vicissimque illi actus sui rationem probare, & si quid vel non, ut oportuerit, gesserit, vel ex his negotiis qd[?] setinuerit[?], præstare cogitur. l. 2. ff. de negot. gest.
units.tr: It is a praetorian personal action in good faith, arising from a quasi-contract, by which one who has managed another's business without mandate and on his own initiative recovers from the owner whatever he has spent or will have to spend on that account; and in turn the manager is obliged to render an account of his conduct to the owner and to make good whatever he has not managed as he ought, or whatever he has retained from those affairs. Digest, law 2, on business done.

units.la: Quid est Actio mandati?
units.tr: What is the action of mandate?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonæ fidei personalis, qua vel mandator contra eum, cui mandavit, ob non perfectum vel intempestive renunciatum mandatum: vel contra mandatarius adversus mandatorem ad repetendos & consequendos sumptus & expensas in rem mandatam factos, agit.l. si mandavero, & l. si alicui. ff. mandati vel contrà.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, personal, by which either the mandator sues the one to whom he gave the mandate, on account of a mandate not carried out or announced too late; or the mandatary sues the mandator, to recover and obtain the costs and expenses incurred in carrying out the mandate. See the laws "si mandavero" and "si alicui", Digest, under mandate, or against.

units.la: Quid est Actio pro socio?
units.tr: What is the action on partnership?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonae fidei in personam, per quam ii, qui non fortuna sed voluntate res communes habent, ad perficiendam vel dirimendam societatem aut ad alias praestationes juxta societatis conventionem agere possunt. Vide Tit. in ff. pro socio.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, in personam, by which those who hold common goods not by chance but by choice may bring suit to bring about or dissolve the partnership, or to obtain other performances according to the terms of the partnership agreement. See the title in the Digest on partnership.

units.la: Quid est Actio tutelae?
units.tr: What is the action of guardianship?

units.la: Est actio civilis & praetoria bonae fidei in personam, ex quasi contractu proveniens, quae datur vel adulto adversus tutorem, ut finita tutela reddat rationes, vel contrà, tutori adversus suum pupillum, ad consequendum id, quod in eius res, administrationis ratione utiliter impendit. l. 1. ff. de tutel.
units.tr: It is a civil and praetorian action of good faith, in personam, arising from a quasi-contract, which is granted either to a person who has come of age against the guardian, so that once the guardianship has ended he may render accounts; or the reverse, to the guardian against his ward, to recover what he has usefully spent on the ward's property in the course of administration. Digest, law 1, on guardianship.

units.la: Quid est Actio pignoratitia?
units.tr: What is the action for pledge?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonae fidei in personam, quae competit debitori adversus suum creditorem ad repetendum pignus conventionale satisfactione praecedente: vel contrà, creditori adversus debitorem, qui pignus pro debito non sufficiens dedit, aut si aliquid impensarum necessariarum in rem pignori datam fecit. Vide Tit. in ff. de pignoratit. action.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, in personam, which belongs to a debtor against his creditor to recover a contractual pledge, after satisfaction has been made first; or the reverse, to a creditor against a debtor who gave a pledge insufficient for the debt, or if the creditor has made some necessary outlay on the thing pledged. See the title in the Digest on the action for pledge.

units.la: Quid est Actio praescriptis verbis quae de aestimato propo- nitur?
units.tr: What is the action "praescriptis verbis" proposed concerning an appraised thing?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonae fidei in personam, ei competens, qui rem aliquam alteri certa aestimatione, aut vendendam aut utendam dedit, ita ut ipsi rem eandem aestimationemve ejus restituat. l. 1. ff. de aestimatoria action.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, in personam, belonging to one who has given something to another, for sale or for use, at a fixed valuation, on the understanding that the other will return the same thing or its value. Digest, law 1, on the appraisal action.

units.la: Quid est Actio praescriptis verbis ex permutatione?
units.tr: What is the action "praescriptis verbis" arising from exchange?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonae fidei in personam, ei competens, qui rem suam animo permutandi alteri dedit, ut ipse aliam rem in specie ab eo ex permutatione recipiat. l. rebus. C. de rerum permutat. l. naturalis. ff. de praescriptis verbis.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, in personam, belonging to one who has given his own thing to another with intent to exchange, so that he himself receives from that person another specific thing by way of exchange. Code, law "rebus", on the exchange of things; Digest, law "naturalis", on the praescriptis verbis actions.

units.la: Quid est hereditatis petitio?
units.tr: What is the petition for inheritance?

units.la: Est actio civilis, bonæ fidei mixta, in qua actor petit, se hæredem declarari, vel in totum, vel pro parte, & rem sine titulo possidentem, ut res hæreditarias cum fructibus perceptis restituat, condemnari. l. sed etsi lege. ff. de petition. hæreditat.
units.tr: It is a civil action, mixed in good faith, in which the plaintiff asks to be declared heir, either wholly or in part, and seeks that the person possessing the inheritance property without title be condemned to restore the inheritance property together with the fruits received. Digest, law "sed etsi lege", on the petition for inheritance.

units.la: Petitio hæreditatis, etsi in rem actio sit, habet tamen præstationes quasdam personales: utputa eorum, quæ à debitoribus sunt exacta :. item pretiorū, d.l. sed etsi. 25. §. petitio. ff. eod.
units.tr: The petition for inheritance, although it is an action in rem, nevertheless contains certain personal claims, for example for those things which have been collected from debtors; likewise for prices. Law "sed etsi", and Digest 25, §"petitio", under the same title.

units.la: Quid est actio ex stipulatu pro dote peten- da vel repetenda?
units.tr: What is the action on stipulation for claiming or recovering a dowry?

units.la: Est actio civilis bonæ fidei in personam, quæ datur marito constante adhuc matrimonio, ad consequendam dotem in matrimonij contractu sibi promissam: vel uxori ad eandem repetendam, vel matrimonio adhuc durante ob mariti incidentem inopiam, vel facta dissolutione matrimonij sive per mortem sive per divortium.
units.tr: It is a civil action of good faith, in personam, which is granted to a husband while the marriage still continues, to obtain the dowry promised to him in the marriage contract; or to a wife to recover the same, either while the marriage still endures because of the husband's unforeseen poverty, or once the marriage has been dissolved, whether by death or by divorce.

units.la: Quid est Actio arbitraria?
units.tr: What is the arbitrary action?

units.la: Est actio ex arbitrio judicis pendens, in qua nisi arbitrio judicis is, cum quo agitur, actori satisfaciat: veluti rem restituat, vel exhibeat, vel solvat, vel ex noxali causa servum dedat, condemnatur.
units.tr: It is an action depending on the discretion of the judge, in which the defendant is condemned, unless by the judge's discretion he satisfies the plaintiff: for example by restoring or producing the thing, or paying, or surrendering a slave by way of noxal action.

units.la: Quid est Actio de dolo malo?
units.tr: What is the action for fraud?

units.la: Est actio prætori arbitraria & subsidiaria personalis, quæ datur adversus decipientem dolo malo, ut deceptus seu circumventus consequatur id, quod dolosum pervenit, & in quo damno affectus est. l. 1. & l. a:bitrio[?].ff. de dolo malo.
units.tr: It is a praetorian, arbitrary and subsidiary personal action, which is granted against one who deceives by fraud, so that the person deceived or circumvented may recover what came to the deceiver by fraud and the loss by which he was harmed. Digest, law 1 and law "arbitrio", on fraud.

units.la: Quid est actio de eo quod certo loco dari oportet?
units.tr: What is the action concerning what ought to be given in a certain place?

units.la: Est actio stricti juris arbitraria, adversus eum competens, qui certo loco sese soluturum obligans promissioni non satisfecit, sed in mora solvendi constitutus, ad id quod Actoris interest judicis arbitrio condemnatur. Vide Tit. in. ff. de eo quod certo loco dari oportet.
units.tr: It is an arbitrary action of strict law, belonging against one who, having bound himself to pay at a certain place, has not fulfilled the promise, but, being in default of payment, is condemned, at the judge's discretion, to pay what the plaintiff's interest requires. See the title in the Digest on what ought to be given in a certain place.

units.la: Quid est Actio ad exhibendum?
units.tr: What is the action for production?

units.la: Est actio personalis arbitraria, in rem scripta, & aliarum realium actionum præparatoria, quæ cuilibet interesse pecuniarium prætendenti datur, adversus quemcunq;, qui copiam exhibendi habet, ut rem mobilem publice exhibeat, seu in modico coram Judice ostendat, quo sibi experiundi potestas seu facultas sit. Vide Tit. in ff. ad exhibend.
units.tr: It is a personal arbitrary action, written in rem, and preparatory to the other real actions, which is granted to anyone claiming a pecuniary interest against whoever has the power of producing, so that he publicly produces a movable thing, or displays it briefly before a judge, so that he may have the power or opportunity of bringing suit. See the title in the Digest on the action for production.

units.la: Est autem interesse damnum emergens, & lucrum cessans. <bl>Ein angehender schabe[?] / unnd auffhörender nutz.</bl>
units.tr: Interest, however, is the loss that arises and the gain that is lost. <bl>Ein angehender schabe / unnd auffhörender nutz.</bl>

units.la: Quomodo fit cessio bonorum?
units.tr: How is a cession of goods made?

units.la: Cum debitor profitetur, se velle cedere omnibus bonis & fortunis suis, (<bl>er</bl> <bl>wölle von aller seiner habe</bl> <bl>vnd gut abtretten</bl>) sive in judicio, sive extra judicium, coram, aut per nuncium, vel per epistolam. l. final. ff. de cession. bonor.
units.tr: When a debtor declares that he wishes to cede all his goods and property (he wishes to give up all his substance and possessions), whether in court or outside of court, in person, or through a messenger, or by letter. Dig. final, de cessione bonorum.

units.la: Is qui bonis cessit, si quid postea adquisierit: inquantum facere potest convenitur. l. 4. ff. eod.
units.tr: A person who has ceded his goods, if he afterwards acquires anything, is sued only to the extent that he is able to pay. Dig. 4, same title.

units.la: Sed qui bonis suis cessit, si modicum aliquid post bona sua vendita adquisivit: iterum bona ejus non veneunt. Unde ergo modum hunc æstimabimus? utrum ex quantitate ejus, quod adquisitum est, an vero ex qualitate? & putem, ex quantitate id æstimā[?] dum esse ejus, quod quæsiit: dummodo illud sciamus, si quid misericordiæ causa ei fuerit relictum, uta menstruum vel annuum alimentorum nomine, non oportere propter hoc, bona ejus iterato venundari: nec enim fraudandus est alimentis quotidianis.l.6.ff.eod.
units.tr: But if a person who has ceded his goods has acquired some small thing after his goods were sold, his goods are not sold again on that account. By what measure, then, shall we judge this limit? By the amount of what has been acquired, or rather by its quality? I think it should be judged by the amount of what he has gained, provided we know this: if something has been left to him out of charity, for example a monthly or yearly allowance for maintenance, his goods must not for that reason be sold again, for he must not be deprived of his daily sustenance. Dig. 6, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST SEPTIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: TITLE VII: WHAT IS IT?

units.la: Quod cum eo, qui in aliena potestate est, negotium gestum esse dicitur. Was mit dem/so in eines andern gewalt ist/ gehandelt ist. Quot actiones oriuntur ex aliena contractu?
units.tr: That a transaction was made with one who is under another's power. How many actions arise from a contract made with another's agent?

units.la: Quinq,: prima,si jussu domini cum servo negotium gestum erit:in solidum Praetor adversus Dominum Actionem pollicetur.§.si igitur.inst.eod.
units.tr: There are five. The first: if a transaction is made with a slave by the command of his master, the Praetor grants an action against the master for the full amount. §. si igitur. Inst. eod.

units.la: Secunda Exercitoria locum habet, cum quis servum suum magistrum navi praeposuerit,& quid cum eo ejus rei gratia,cui praepositus erit, contractum fuerit.§. eadem ratione.inst.eod.
units.tr: The second, the exercitoria, applies when someone places his slave as master over a ship, and any contract is made with that slave for the purpose of the business for which he was placed in charge. §. eadem ratione. inst. eod.

units.la: Tertia Institoria locum habet, cum quis tabernae forte,aut cuilibet negotiationi servum suum praepofuerit, & quid cum eo ejus rei causa, cui praepositus erit contractum fuerit.§. eadem ration.verf.institoria.inst.eod.
units.tr: The third, the institoria, applies when someone places his slave over a shop or any other business, and any contract is made with that slave for the purpose of the business for which he was placed in charge. §. eadem ratione, verb. institoria. inst. eod.

units.la: Quarta Tributoria, si servus in peculiari merce sciente domino negotietur , & quid cum eo ejus rei causa contractum erit: ita praetor jus dicit,ut quicquid in his mercibus erit , quoq; inde receptum erit id inter dominum , si quid ei debetur,& caeteros creditores pro rata portione distribuatur. §. introduxit.inst.eod. Quinta actio introducta est de peculio, deque eo, quod in rem domini versum erit. §. praeterea. institut. eod.
units.tr: The fourth, the tributoria: if a slave trades with his peculium of goods with the master's knowledge, and a contract is made with him for the purpose of that business, the praetor rules that whatever is in those goods, and whatever is recovered from them, is to be distributed pro rata between the master, if anything is owed to him, and the other creditors. §. introduxit. inst. eod. The fifth action was introduced concerning the peculium, and concerning that which has been turned to the master's advantage. §. praeterea. institut. eod.

units.la: QUIS EST OCTAVUS Titulus? De noxalibus actionibus. Von flagen[?] erl- ittener beschädi-ung halben.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE EIGHTH Title? On noxal actions. <bl>Concerning damage done by a slave's wrongdoing.</bl>

units.la: Quid proditum est ex maleficiis servorum?
units.tr: What has been laid down concerning the wrongful acts of slaves?

units.la: EX maleficiis servorum: veluti si furtum fecerint; aut bona rapuerint, aut damnum dederint, aut injuriam commiserint: noxales actiones proditae sunt, quibus domino damnato permittitur, aut litis aestimationem sufferre, aut ipsum hominem noxae dedere, <bl>den menschen selbs für den schaden zur straff</bl> <bl>heimgeben.</bl> in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Concerning the wrongful acts of slaves: for example, if they have committed theft, or seized goods, or caused loss, or done injury, noxal actions have been provided, by which the owner, once condemned, is permitted either to pay the assessed value of the suit or to surrender the man himself in compensation for the harm, <bl>to hand over the person himself as punishment for the damage.</bl> At the beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid est Noxa?
units.tr: What is a noxa?

units.la: Noxa est ipsum corpus quod nocuit: id est, servus: Noxia ipsum maleficium, veluti furtum, damnum, rapina, injuria. §. noxa autem. inst. eo.
units.tr: A noxa is the body itself which did the harm, that is, the slave; a noxia is the wrongful act itself, such as theft, damage, robbery, injury. Institutes, same title, the section on noxa.

units.la: Sequiturne noxalis actio caput?
units.tr: Does a noxal action follow the person?

units.la: Omnis noxalis actio caput sequitur. Nam si servus tuus noxam commiserit: quamdiu in tua potestate sit, tecum est Actio: si autem in alterius potestatem pervenerit: cum illo incipit actio esse. §. omnis autem. inst. eod.
units.tr: Every noxal action follows the person. For if your slave has committed a noxa, then as long as he is in your power, the action lies against you; but if he has passed into another's power, the action begins to lie against that person. Institutes, same title, the section on every action.

units.la: QUIS EST NONUS Titulus? Si quadrupes pauperiem fecisse dicatur, So ein vierfüssiges thier schaden gethan hat.
units.tr: WHAT IS THE NINTH TITLE? If a quadruped is said to have done damage (pauperies), <bl>So ein vierfüssiges thier schaden</bl> <bl>gethan hat.</bl> Note: the bl-tagged German lines are part of the source and are reproduced as printed.

units.la: Quid Animalium nomine proditum est?
units.tr: What has been handed down under the name of animals?

units.la: ANimalium nomine, quae ratione carent, si qua lascivia, aut pavore, aut feritate pauperiem secerint: Noxalis actio lege duodecim tabularum prodita est. Quae animalia si noxae dedantur, proficiunt reo ad liberationem. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Under the name of animals, which lack reason, if they have caused damage through any playfulness, fear, or savagery, the noxal action was handed down by the Law of the Twelve Tables. If such animals are surrendered as noxa, they benefit the defendant by way of release. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quid est pauperies?
units.tr: What is pauperies?

units.la: Pauperies est damnum sine injuria facientis datum. Nec enim potest animal injuriam fecisse dici, quod sensu caret. in princ. verf. pauperies. inst. eod.
units.tr: Pauperies is damage given without injury on the part of the one causing it. For an animal cannot be said to have committed an injury, since it lacks sense. Beginning, under the word pauperies, Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quidnam ædilitio edicto prohibetur?
units.tr: What is prohibited by the edict of the aediles?

units.la: Sciendum est ædilitio edicto prohiberi nos canes, verrem, aprum, ursum, leonem ibi habere, quà vulgo iter fit.[?] §. cæterum. inst. eod.
units.tr: It must be understood that by the edict of the aediles we are forbidden to keep dogs, a boar, a wild boar, a bear, or a lion there, where the public road runs. Further, Institutes, same title.

units.la: QU- IS EST DECIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE TENTH TITLE?

units.la: De iis, per quos agere possumus. <bl>Von</bl> <bl>denen durch welche wir klagen vnd rechtlich</bl> <bl>handlen mögen.</bl> Cujus nomine agere possumus?
units.tr: On those through whom we can act. On those through whom we may sue and proceed legally. In whose name can we act?

units.la: ADmonendi sumus agere posse quemlibet hominem, aut suo nomine, aut alieno. Alieno, veluti procuratorio, tutorio, in princ. inst. eo.
units.tr: We must note that anyone may act, either in his own name or in another's. In another's name, as a procurator or a guardian, at the beginning of the same title in the Institutes.

units.la: Quomodo constituitur procurator?
units.tr: How is a procurator appointed?

units.la: Procurator (ein[?] [illegible, ~8 letters]) neque certis verbis, neque praesente semper adversario, imo plerunque eo ignorante constituitur: cuicunque enim permissum est rem tuam agere, aut defendere: is tuus procurator intelligitur. §. procurator. inst. eod.
units.tr: A procurator is appointed neither with fixed words nor always with the opponent present; indeed, for the most part he is appointed with the opponent unaware. For whoever has been permitted to act or defend your affair is understood to be your procurator. §. procurator, Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST UNDECIMUS Titulus?
units.tr: WHAT IS THE ELEVENTH TITLE?

units.la: De satisdationibus. Von bürgschaff- ten zu recht. Quid dicis de satisdatione secundum Jus Novum?
units.tr: On satisdations. On sureties according to law. What do you say about satisdation according to the New Law?

units.la: Sive quis in rem actione convenitur, sive personali suo nomine: nullam satisdationem pro litis aestimatione dare compellitur: sed pro sua tantum persona, quod in judicio permaneat usq; ad terminum, vel committitur suae promissioni cum jurejurando (quam juratoriam cautionem vocant, welches man einen geschwornen Vorstand oder Versicherung[?] nennet) vel nudam promissionem, vel satisdationem pro qualitate personae suae dare compellitur. §. sed hodie. inst. cod.
units.tr: If someone is sued in a real action, or in a personal action in his own name, he is not compelled to give any satisfactory security (satisdatio) in proportion to the estimated value of the suit; he is required only to give security for his own person, that he remain in court until the end of the case, or he is entrusted to his own promise with an oath (which they call a juratory caution, what one calls a sworn guarantee or assurance[?]), or a bare promise, or is compelled to give satisdation in proportion to the quality of his person. §. sed hodie. Inst., same title.

units.la: QUIS EST DUODECI- MUS Titulus?
units.tr: What is the twelfth title?

units.la: De perpetuis & temporalibus actioni- bus, & quae ad haeredes, & in haeredes transeunt. Von ewigen vnnd zeitlichen klagen / vnnd welche auff die erben beyd- erseits des klägers vnd beklagten kommen. Quot sunt perpetuae Actiones?
units.tr: On perpetual and temporal actions, and which pass to heirs and against heirs. On perpetual and temporal actions, and which pass to the heirs of plaintiff and defendant. How many perpetual actions are there?

units.la: Quae ex lege, senatusve consultis, sive ex saeri[?] constitutionibus proficiscuntur. in prin inst. cod. Quae vero ex propria praetoris jurisdictione pendent, plerunque intra annum vivunt.in prin.inst.eod.
units.tr: Those that arise from statute, from senatorial decrees, or from imperial constitutions. (Institutes, beginning.) But those that depend on the praetor's own jurisdiction generally last for a year. (Institutes, beginning, same place.)

units.la: Dantúrne omnes actiones contra hæredes?
units.tr: Are all actions given against heirs?

units.la: Non omnes actiones quæ in aliquem aut ipso jure competunt, aut à prætore dantur: & in hæredem æqué competunt, aut dari solent: Est enim certissima juris Regula, ex maleficiis pœnales actiones in hæredem rei non competere, veluti furti, vi bonorum raptorum, injuriarum, damni, injuriæ. §. non autem. inst.cod.
units.tr: Not every action that lies against someone, either by law itself or granted by the praetor, equally lies against his heir or is customarily granted against him. For it is a most certain rule of law that penal actions arising from wrongful acts do not lie against the heir of the wrongdoer, as for theft, for goods taken by force, for insult, and for damage done by injury. (Institutes, same title, the section beginning "non autem.")

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS tertius Titulus?
units.tr: What is the thirteenth title?

units.la: De exceptionibus. <bl>Von außzügen/gegenwehr/ oder einreden.</bl>
units.tr: On exceptions: concerning objections, defences, or pleas in bar.

units.la: Quare comparatæ sunt exceptiones.
units.tr: Why exceptions were devised.

units.la: Comparatæ sunt exceptiones defendendorum eorum gratia, cum quibus agitur: sæpe enim accidit, ut licet ipsa persecutio, qua actor experitur, justa sit: tamen iniqua sit adversus eum cum quo agitur. Verbi gratia, si metu coactus, aut dolo inductus, aut errore lapsus, stipulanti Titio promisisti, quod nō debueras promittere, palam est, jure civili te obligatum esse: Et actio, qua intenditur dare oportere, efficax est: sed iniquum est te condemnari: Ideoque datur tibi exceptio, quod metus causa, aut doli mali, aut in factum composita ad impugnandam actionē. in princ. inst.cod.
units.tr: Exceptions were devised for the defence of those against whom an action is brought. For it often happens that, although the very suit by which the plaintiff proceeds is just, it is nevertheless unjust against the person it is brought against. For example, if you were compelled by fear, or induced by fraud, or led astray by error, and promised Titius when he stipulated what you ought not to have promised, it is plain that civil law binds you, and the action by which he claims that you must give is effective. But it is unjust that you be condemned. Therefore an exception is given to you, namely that it was done through fear, or through wicked fraud, or an exception framed on the facts, to oppose the action. Inst., beginning, cod.

units.la: Quæ est prima exceptionum divisio?
units.tr: What is the first division of exceptions?

units.la: Exceptionum quædam ex legibus, vel ex iis, quæ legis vicem obtinent, vel ex ipsius prætoris jurisdictione substantiâ capiunt. §. quarũ quædam. inst.cod.
units.tr: Some exceptions take their force from laws, or from those things which hold the place of law, and others from the praetor's own jurisdiction. Inst., §. quarundam, cod.

units.la: Quæ est secunda divisio?
units.tr: What is the second division?

units.la: Exceptiones aliæ perpetuæ & peremptoriæ sunt, aliae temporales & dilatoriae.§. appellatur. inst. eod.
units.tr: Some exceptions are perpetual and peremptory, others temporary and dilatory. Inst., §. appellatur, same place.

units.la: Perpetuae & peremptoriae, (<bl>ewige vnd verstörliche</bl> <bl>gegenwehre</bl>) aut quae semper agentibus obstant, & semper rem, de qua agitur, perimunt: qualis est exceptio doli mali, & quod metus causa factum est.§. perpetuae. inst. eod.
units.tr: Perpetual and peremptory defences (eternal and destructive defences) are those which always stand in the way of the plaintiff and always destroy the matter in dispute. Such is the exception of wicked fraud, and that of an act done through fear. Inst., §. perpetuae, same place.

units.la: Temporales & dilatoriae, (<bl>zeitliche vnd verzugliche</bl> <bl>gegenwehre</bl>) sunt quae ad tempus nocent, & temporis dilationem tribuunt.§. temporales. inst. eod. Qualis est Declinatoria fori, <bl>wenn der beklagte einem</bl> <bl>gericht nicht vnterworffen / noch vor demselben zu</bl> <bl>antworten schuldig:</bl> Exceptio contra Judicem, <bl>wenn</bl> <bl>der Richter dem kläger gefreundet/vnd dem beklagten</bl> <bl>feind ist:</bl> Exceptio contra Actorem, <bl>wenn der</bl> <bl>kläger im bann oder in der acht/ oder meyneidig ist.</bl> Vide <bl>Heinrich Knaustens Gewrʒeugk gerichtlicher</bl> <bl>Ordenung.</bl>
units.tr: Temporary and dilatory defences (temporal and delaying defences) are those which harm only for a time and grant a postponement. Such is the declinatory exception, when the defendant is not subject to the court and is not obliged to answer before it; the exception against the judge, when the judge is a friend of the plaintiff and an enemy of the defendant; the exception against the plaintiff, when the plaintiff is under ban, outlawed, or perjured. See Heinrich Knaust's guide to court procedure. Inst., §. temporales, same place.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS quartus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the fourth title?

units.la: De replicationibus. <bl>Von replicken oder gegenrede.</bl>
units.tr: On replications. Von replicken oder gegenrede.

units.la: Quid dicit Imperator de replicationibus?
units.tr: What does the Emperor say about replications?

units.la: INterdum evenit, inquit, ut exceptio, quae prima facie justa videtur, tamen iniquè noceat, quod cum accidit, alia allegatione opus est, adjuvandi Actoris gratia, quae Replicatio vocatur, quia per eam replicatur, atque resolvitur jus exceptionis.in princip. instit. eod.
units.tr: Sometimes it happens, he says, that an exception which seems just at first sight nevertheless harms unjustly. When this occurs, another pleading is needed, to assist the plaintiff; it is called the Replication, because by it the right of the exception is replied to and dissolved. Institutes, at the beginning of the same title.

units.la: Rursus interdum evenit, ut Replicatio, quae prima facie justa est, iniquè noceat: quod cum accidit, alia allegatione opus est, adjuvandi rei gratia, quae Duplicatio vocatur. Et si rursus ea prima facie justa videavideatur, sed propter aliquam causam Actori iniquè noceat: rursus alia allegatione opus est, quà actor adjuvetur: quæ dicitur Triplicatio. §. 1. & 2. inst. cod.
units.tr: Again, sometimes it happens that a Replication, which seems just at first sight, harms unjustly. When this occurs, another pleading is needed, to assist the defendant; this is called the Duplication. And if again that pleading seems just at first sight, but for some reason harms the plaintiff unjustly, then yet another pleading is needed, by which the plaintiff is assisted; this is called the Triplication. Institutes, §§ 1 and 2, of the same title.

units.la: QUIS EST VICESIMUS quintus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the twenty-fifth title?

units.la: De interdictis. <bl>Von richterlichen verbotten</bl> <bl>und verbotten.</bl>
units.tr: On interdicts. <bl>On judicial prohibitions</bl> <bl>and forbiddings.</bl>

units.la: Quid erant interdicta?
units.tr: What were interdicts?

units.la: Erant interdicta formæ atq; conceptiones verborum quibus prætor aut jubebat aliquid fieri, aut fieri prohibebat: quod tunc maximè fiebat, cùm de possessione, aut quasi possessione inter aliquos contendebatur. in princ. inst. eod.
units.tr: Interdicts were formulas and wordings of words by which the praetor either ordered something to be done or forbade it to be done; this happened especially when a dispute arose concerning possession, or quasi-possession, between certain parties. Init. Inst. same title.

units.la: Quæ est summa divis- io interdictorum?
units.tr: What is the chief division of interdicts?

units.la: Summa divisio interdictorum hæc est: quòd aut prohibitoria sunt, aut restitutoria, aut exhibitoria.
units.tr: The chief division of interdicts is this: that they are either prohibitory, or restitutory, or exhibitory.

units.la: Prohibitoria (<bl>verbietliche</bl>) sunt quibus prætor vetat aliquid fieri.
units.tr: Prohibitory (<bl>verbietliche</bl>) interdicts are those by which the praetor forbids something to be done.

units.la: Restitutoria (<bl>die widergebliche</bl>) sunt, quibus restitui aliquid jubet.
units.tr: Restitutory (<bl>die widergebliche</bl>) interdicts are those by which he orders something to be restored.

units.la: Exhibitoria (<bl>die herausgebliche</bl>) sunt, per quæ jubet exhiberi. §. summa. inst. eod.
units.tr: Exhibitory (<bl>die herausgebliche</bl>) interdicts are those by which he orders something to be produced. §. summa. Inst. same title.

units.la: Quæ est secunda divisio?
units.tr: What is the second division?

units.la: Secunda divisio interdictorum hæc est, quòd quædam adipiscendæ possessionis causa comparata sunt; quædam retinendæ, quædā recuperandæ. §. sequens. inst. eod.
units.tr: The second division of interdicts is this: some are framed for the purpose of obtaining possession, others for retaining it, others for recovering it. §. following. Inst. same title.

units.la: Quæ est tertia divisio?
units.tr: What is the third division?

units.la: Tertia divisio interdictorum hæc est, quòd aut simplicia sunt, aut duplicia. Simplicia sunt, veluti in quibus alter Actor, alter Reus est: Qualia sunt omnia restitutoria, aut exhibitoria. Duplicia sunt veluti, Uti possidetis interdictum, <bl>wie|h: besitzt:</bl> & Utrubi, <bl>beiderseits.</bl> Ideo autem duplicia vocantur, quia par utriusque litigatoris in his conditio est, nec quisquam præcipuè Reus vel Actor intelligitur: sed unusquisque tàm Rei quàm Actoris partes sustinet. §. tertia. inst. cod.
units.tr: The third division of interdicts is this: they are either simple or double. Simple interdicts are those in which one party is plaintiff and the other defendant, as with all restitutory or exhibitory interdicts. Double interdicts are, for example, the interdict Uti possidetis, <bl>as you possess</bl>, and Utrubi, <bl>on both sides</bl>. They are called double because in these the condition of each litigant is equal, and neither is specifically understood as defendant or plaintiff; each sustains the part of both defendant and plaintiff. §. tertia. Inst. same title.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS sextus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the sixth title of the tenth book?

units.la: De poena temerè litigantium. <bl>Von straffe deᵣer, welche muthwilliger</bl> <bl>weise einen gerichtlichen krieg anfangen.</bl>
units.tr: On the punishment of those who litigate rashly. <bl>On the punishment of those who wantonly begin a lawsuit.</bl> <bl>[German, not translated]</bl>

units.la: Quomodo temeritas litigantium coercetur?
units.tr: How is the rashness of litigants restrained?

units.la: Temeritas tàm agëtium, quàm eorum, cum quibus agitur, modò pecuniaria poena, modò juris jurandi religione, modò infamiæ metu coercetur. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: The rashness both of those who bring suit and of those against whom suit is brought is restrained sometimes by a monetary penalty, sometimes by the obligation of an oath, sometimes by fear of infamy. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: Quibus defertur jusjurandum?
units.tr: To whom is the oath deferred?

units.la: Jusjurandum omnibus qui conveniuntur, ex constitutione Imperatoris defertur. Nam Reus non aliter allegationibus utitur, nisi prius juraverit, quòd putans se bona instantia uti, ad cōtradicēdum pervenit. Item Actoris quoq; calumnia coercetur. Nam etiam actor pro calumnia jurare cogitur ex Imperatoris constitutione. §. Ecce enim. inst. cod.
units.tr: The oath is deferred to all who are sued, by constitution of the Emperor.
