For the defendant may not use his pleas unless he has first sworn that, believing he has a good cause, he has come to contradict. Likewise the calumny of the plaintiff is also restrained. For the plaintiff too is compelled to swear against calumny, by constitution of the Emperor. Section "Ecce enim", Institutes, same title.

units.la: QUIS EST DECIMUS septimus Titulus?
units.tr: What is the seventeenth title?

units.la: De officio Iudicis. <bl>Von des</bl> <bl>Richters Ampt.</bl>
units.tr: On the office of the judge. <bl>Von des</bl> <bl>Richters Ampt.</bl>

units.la: Quid debet Judex observare?
units.tr: What ought a judge to observe?

units.la: INprimis illud observare debet Judex, ne aliter judicet, quàm legibus aut constitutionibus, aut moribus proditum est. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: First of all, a judge ought to observe this: that he must not judge otherwise than has been handed down by the laws, the imperial constitutions, or custom. Beginning of the Institutes, same title.

units.la: QVIS EST DECIMVS octavus Titulus? De publicis Iudiciis. <bl>[?]Von peinlichen</bl> <bl>Halsgerichten.</bl>
units.tr: What is the eighteenth title? On public judgments. Of capital criminal courts.

units.la: Quid dicit Imperator de publicis Iudiciis?
units.tr: What does the Emperor say about public judgments?

units.la: PUblica judicia neq; per actiones ordinantur, neque omninò quicquam simile habent, cum cæteris judiciis, de quibus dictum est: magnaq; diversitas eorum est, & in instituendo, & in exercendo. in princ. inst. cod.
units.tr: Public judgments are not conducted by actions, and they have nothing at all like the other judgments discussed earlier. There is great difference between them both in how they are instituted and in how they are carried out.

units.la: Quare dicta sunt publica?
units.tr: Why are they called public?

units.la: Publica dicta sunt, quòd cuivis ex populo executio eorum plærunq; datur. §. publica. inst. cod.
units.tr: They are called public because the carrying out of them is generally granted to any one of the people.

units.la: Quotuplicia sunt publica judicia?
units.tr: How many kinds of public judgments are there?

units.la: Publicorum judiciorum quædam capitalia sunt, quædam non capitalia. Capitalia dicimus, quæ ultimo supplicio afficiunt homines, vel etiam aquæ & ignis interdictione, vel deportatione, vel metallo.
units.tr: Some public judgments are capital and some are not. We call those capital which subject people to the ultimate punishment, or even to banishment from water and fire, or to deportation, or to the mines.

units.la: Cætera, si quam infamiam irrogant cum damno pecuniario: hæc publica quidem sunt, non tamen capitalia. §. publicorum. inst. cod.
units.tr: The rest, if they impose some infamy together with a pecuniary loss, are public but not capital.

units.la: Quæ sunt publica judicia?
units.tr: What are the public judgments?

units.la: Publica judicia hæc sunt: Lex Julia Majestatis, quæ in eos, qui contra Imperatorem, vel Rempublicam aliquid moliti sunt, suum vigorem extendit. §. 3. inst. cod. Item lex Julia de adulteriis coercendis, quæ non solum temeratores alienarum nuptiarum gladio punit, sed & eos, qui cum masculis nefandam libidinem exercere audent.§.4.inst.eod.
units.tr: The public judgments are these: the Julian law of majesty, which extends its force against those who have attempted anything against the Emperor or the commonwealth. Likewise the Julian law on the restraint of adulteries, which punishes with the sword not only those who violate other men's marriages but also those who dare to practise unspeakable lust with males.

units.la: Item Lex Cornelia de sicariis, quae homicidas ultore ferro persequitur, vel eos, qui hominis occidendi causa cum telo ambulant.§.5.inst. eod.
units.tr: Likewise the Cornelian law on assassins, which pursues murderers with avenging steel, and those who walk about with a weapon for the purpose of killing a man.

units.la: Lex Pompeja de parricidiis, qua cautum est, ut parricida neque gladio, neque ignibus, neque ulli alij solenni[?] poenae subjiciatur, sed insutus culeo cum cane, & gallo gallinaceo, & vipera, & simia, & inter eas feraes angustias comprehensus (secundum quod regionis qualitas tulerit) vel in vicinum mare, vel in amnem projiciatur: ut omnium elementorum usu vivus carere incipiat, & ei coelum superstiti, & terra mortuo auferatur.§.6.inst.eod.& l.unica, C.de his qui parentes vel liberos occiderunt.
units.tr: The Pompeian law on parricides, by which it is provided that a parricide is subjected neither to the sword, nor to fire, nor to any other customary punishment, but is sewn into a sack with a dog, a rooster, a viper and an ape, and shut up among these in a wild, narrow space (according to what the nature of the region allows), and is thrown either into the nearby sea or into a river, so that, while alive, he begins to lose the use of all the elements, and heaven is taken from him while he survives and earth from him when he is dead. See also the single law of the Code, On those who have killed their parents or children.

units.la: Lex Cornelia de falsis, quae etiam testamentaria vocatur, poenam irrogat ei, qui testamentum falsum scripserit, signaverit, recitaverit, subjecerit: vel signū adulterinum fecerit, sculpserit, expresserit sciens dolo malo.§.7.inst.eod.
units.tr: The Cornelian law on forgeries, which is also called the testamentary law, imposes a penalty on one who knowingly and with evil intent has written, sealed, read out or inserted a false will, or who has made, carved or impressed a counterfeit seal.

units.la: Lex Julia de vi publica seu privata adversus eos exoritur, qui vim vel armatam, vel sine armis commiserint.§.8.inst.eod.
units.tr: The Julian law on public or private violence is directed against those who have committed violence, whether armed or without arms.

units.la: Lex Julia peculatus eos punit, qui publicam pecuniam, vel rem sacram, vel religiosam furati fuerint. §.9.inst.eod.
units.tr: The Julian law on embezzlement punishes those who have stolen public money, or a sacred or religious object.

units.la: Lex Flavia de plagiariis, quae interdum capitis poenam ex sacris Constitutionibus irrogat, interdum leviorem.§.10.inst.eod.
units.tr: The Flavian law on kidnapping, which sometimes imposes the penalty of death under the sacred constitutions and sometimes a lighter one.

units.la: Sunt praeterea publica judicia, Lex Julia de ambitu, Lex Julia repetundarum, & Lex Julia de Annona, & Lex Julia de residuis.§.11.inst.eod.
units.tr: There are also these public judgments: the Julian law on canvassing for office, the Julian law on extortion, the Julian law on the grain supply, and the Julian law on residues.

units.la: Hactenus quatuor libri Institutionum iuris breviter traditi sunt.
units.tr: Thus far the four books of the Institutes of Law have been briefly set out.

units.la: DE PROCESSU Iudiciario.
units.tr: ON THE JUDICIAL PROCESS.

units.la: Quid est Judicium?
units.tr: What is a judgment?

units.la: Iudicium & legitima controversiae judicialis, quae est inter Actorem (<bl>dem klåger</bl>) & Reum (<bl>dem bek-</bl> <bl>lagten</bl>) apud Judicem disceptatio & dijudicatio, ut publica authoritate lites sopiantur, inquit Vvesenbecius in paratitlis. C. de judicijs.
units.tr: Judgment is the lawful settling, by a judge, of a judicial dispute between the plaintiff (the one who brings the suit, "dem Kläger") and the defendant (the one who is sued, "dem Beklagten"), so that by public authority the quarrel may be brought to an end. So Wesenbeck defines it in his Paratitla, on the Code, de iudiciis.

units.la: Quotuplices sunt Judices?
units.tr: How many kinds of judges are there?

units.la: Quintuplices: Ordinarij <bl>ordenliche</bl> / qui à Papa, ut sunt Episcopi vel Ecclesiastici magistratus: vel ab Imperatore, ut sunt seculares principes: vel à lege: vel Universitate ordinariam seu legitimam jurisdictionem habent (<bl>Gerichtszwang haben.</bl>)
units.tr: There are five kinds. Ordinary judges (the "ordentliche" ones) are those who hold ordinary or lawful jurisdiction (the power to hold court, "Gerichtszwang") from the Pope, such as bishops or ecclesiastical magistrates; from the emperor, such as secular princes; from the law itself; or from a university.

units.la: Delegati, <bl>nachgesetzte richter oder befelchshaber</bl> / quibus ab ordinario Judice una vel pluries causae cognoscendae & terminandae committuntur: ut Vicarij in spiritualibus & secularibus, qui appellantur, Officiales, Sigilliferi, Commissarij, Vicedomini.
units.tr: Delegated judges (the "nachgesetzten Richter" or commissioned officers) are those to whom the ordinary judge commits the hearing and determining of one or more cases. Examples are the vicars in spiritual and secular matters, called officials, sigillifers, commissaries, and vice-domini.

units.la: Subdelegati, <bl>den nachgesetzten vnderseßte</bl> / sunt, qui permittente ordinario judice, à delegatis constituuntur.
units.tr: Subdelegated judges (the "untergeordneten" ones) are those who, with the permission of the ordinary judge, are appointed by the delegated judges.

units.la: Arbitri juris (<bl>schiedsrichter</bl>) dicuntur qui ex necessitate à jure vel statuto electi sunt, & assimilantur delegatis sicut eis lex tribuat jurisdictionem delegatam, illam scilicet, quam Judex recusatus habuit.
units.tr: Arbiters of law (arbitrators, "Schiedsrichter") are those who are chosen by law or statute out of necessity. They are treated like delegated judges, since the law grants them delegated jurisdiction, namely the same that the judge who was challenged had.

units.la: Arbitri Compromissarij, <bl>willkürliche schiedsrichter</bl> / sunt in quos voluntarie & non necessitate juris à partibus est compromissum, & eliguntur à partibus ut judices, conceditur que eis à partibus voluntarie potestas super causa pronuntiandi.
units.tr: Compromissary arbiters (arbitrators by agreement, "willkürliche Schiedsrichter") are those to whom the parties voluntarily submit a dispute by compromise, not from any necessity of law. They are chosen by the parties as judges, and the parties voluntarily grant them power to pronounce on the case.

units.la: Qui autem Arbitratores appellantur sunt proxenetæ, <bl>vnte ihå Dler / Die Die jachen nach jrem besten verstande für sich</bl> <bl>handeln / ohn form des gerichts,</bl> Vide Schneidevvinum in §. omnium. inst. de Actione,
units.tr: Those who are called arbitrators in the looser sense are go-betweens, who handle matters according to their own best judgment, without the form of a court. See Schneidewin on the paragraph omnium, Institutes, de actionibus.

units.la: Quotnam in judiciario processu sunt con- siderranda?
units.tr: How many things must be considered in the judicial process?

units.la: Duo: Instantia & Executio.
units.tr: Two: the instance and the execution.

units.la: Quotuplex est Instantia?
units.tr: How many kinds of instance are there?

units.la: Duplex: Prima aut Secunda.
units.tr: Two: the first or the second.

units.la: Quot sunt termini judiciales?
units.tr: How many judicial steps are there?

units.la: Decem: Primo Actor judicem competentem adit, cujus jurisdictioni Reus est subjectus, & Reum citari petit.
units.tr: Ten. First, the plaintiff approaches the competent judge, under whose jurisdiction the defendant is, and asks that the defendant be summoned.

units.la: Secundo, Reo comparente Actor vel ejus nomine Procurator libellum Judici & Adversario exhibet. Libellus <bl>(ein Klag in schrifft verfasset)</bl> est brevis & ordinata scriptura, claram continens, & judici & parti demonstrans intentionem Actoris vel Accusatoris. Dicitur brevis, quia verborum prolixitas à jure respuitur. l. ampliorem. §. in refutatoriis. C. de appellationib. Et ideo vulgo in Libellis dici solet: <bl>Es er-</bl> <bl>scheinet N. vnd sagt furtlich / &c.</bl> Vide Schneidevvinum. §. omnium. 98. inst. de Actionib.
units.tr: Second, when the defendant appears, the plaintiff, or a proctor in his name, presents a libel (a written complaint, "eine Klage in Schrift verfasst") to the judge and to the opponent. A libel is a short and orderly writing, which contains the claim clearly and makes the intention of the plaintiff or accuser plain to the judge and the party. It is called short because the law rejects wordiness. See the law ampliorem, the paragraph in refutatoriis, Code, de appellationibus. For this reason the common form in libels is: "N. appears and states, unlawfully, etc." See Schneidewin on the paragraph omnium, 98, Institutes, de actionibus.

units.la: Tertio, Reus dilationes petit ad deliberandum contenderene, an liti cedere velit.
units.tr: Third, the defendant asks for delay, so that he may deliberate whether he will contest the matter or yield to the suit.

units.la: Quarto, cum Reus contendendum putat, initio exceptiones opponit, vel declinatorias fori, vel dilatorias: sequuntur Replicationes, Duplicationes.
units.tr: Fourth, when the defendant thinks he must contest, he at the outset raises exceptions, either declinatory exceptions to the jurisdiction of the court or dilatory ones. These are followed by replications and duplications.

units.la: Quinto, cum Reus tandem respondere iussus est, utrinque à partibus satisfdatur, se usque ad finem in lite permansuros.
units.tr: Fifth, when the defendant is at last ordered to answer, each party gives security to the other that they will remain in the suit to the end.

units.la: Sexto, Reus litem contestatur, affirmando aut negando intentionem libelli Actoris. <bl>Die Kriegsbefes-</bl> <bl>tigung aber ist gleich einer Kriegsordnung / als wenn</bl> <bl>wenn die feinde gegen einander zu Felde ziehen/ vnd</bl> <bl>einer dem andern ein schlacht verkündiget/ so ist der</bl> <bl>krieg daselbst befestiget/sagt Doctor Knauffinus.</bl>
units.tr: Sixth, the defendant joins issue (litem contestatur), by affirming or denying the intention of the plaintiff's libel. "The declaration of war is like a battle order: when enemies take the field against each other and one announces battle to the other, then the war is established there," says Doctor Knauff.

units.la: Septimo,post litem contestatam partes utrinque jusjurandum calumniae praestant. <bl>Der Kläger für ge-</bl> <bl>fehrde ist das der Kläger schwere/ er wisse nichts an-</bl> <bl>ders/dann daß er ein gute sache habe: Der Beklagte</bl> <bl>aber / Er schütze vnnd verfechte sich / in einer guten sach.</bl>
units.tr: Seventh, after the issue is joined, each party takes an oath against calumny. The plaintiff swears in good faith that he knows nothing except that he has a good cause; the defendant swears that he defends and maintains himself in a good cause.

units.la: Octavo,Actor petitionem suam Articulis comprehensam(qui positionales appellantur) medio jurejurando offert. His Reus medio itidem jurejurando, <bl>per verbum,glaubt wahr/oder nit wahr sein/respon-</bl> <bl>det:</bl> Et defensionales articulos incontinenti, vel ex intervallo,responsionibus adjungit.
units.tr: Eighth, the plaintiff offers his petition, set out in articles (called positional articles), under oath. The defendant replies to these, likewise under oath, saying "I believe it true" or "I believe it not true." He adds defensive articles to his replies, either at once or after an interval.

units.la: Nono, Actori terminus constituitur ad Articulos per Reum negatos probandum testibus vel instrumentis. Reus autem Interrogatoria (<bl>fragstücken</bl>) addere potest singulis articulis Actoris, de quibus testes simul audiantur. Deinde publicantur attestationes utraque parte praesente vel in contumaciam Absentis: Et terminus ad excipiendum contra Attestationes & replicandum denuò datur.
units.tr: Ninth, a time limit is set for the plaintiff to prove the articles denied by the defendant, by witnesses or documents. The defendant may add questions (interrogatories, "Fragstücke") to each of the plaintiff's articles, so that the witnesses may be heard on both at once. Then the testimonies are published, with either party present, or with the absent party in contumacy. A further period is given for objecting to the testimonies and for replying.

units.la: Decimo,his peractis,concluditur in causa. Atque haec de terminis judicialibus ante sententiam.
units.tr: Tenth, when these steps are complete, the case is concluded. So much for the judicial steps before sentence.

units.la: Quid est Sententia?
units.tr: What is a sentence?

units.la: <bl>Sententia, ein Urtheil / est</bl> nihil aliud,quàm pronunciatio Judicis. Estq; duplex:Interlocutoria, aut Definitiva.
units.tr: A sentence (a judgment, "ein Urtheil") is nothing other than the pronouncement of the judge. It is of two kinds: interlocutory or definitive.

units.la: Interlocutoria sententia, <bl>ein Zwischenurtheil/est</bl> quae fertur inter principium causae, & finem, non super principali negotio,sed super incidentibus & emergentibus quaestionibus, puta super dilatione danda, de persona procuratoris admittenda, probatione imponenda,& similibus.
units.tr: An interlocutory sentence (an interim judgment, "ein Zwischenurtheil") is one given between the beginning and the end of a case, not on the main matter but on incidental and emerging questions, such as granting a delay, admitting a proctor, or imposing proof, and the like.

units.la: Sententia vero definitiva,<bl>ein Endurtheil</bl>/est quæ principalem definit quæstionem, & imponit finem negotio principali, quod fit vel condemnatione vel absolutione. Atq; hæc (de prima Instantia: Sequitur appellatio,unde oritur secunda Instantia.
units.tr: A definitive sentence (a final judgment, "ein Endurtheil") is one that decides the principal question and puts an end to the main business, and this is done either by condemnation or by absolution. So much for the first instance. Appeal follows, from which the second instance arises.

units.la: Quid est Appellatio?
units.tr: What is an appeal?

units.la: Appellatio, <bl>ein beruffung zum höhern Richter</bl>/est ab audientia minoris judicis, ad majorem, propter gravamen illatum, provocatio.Nam si sententia iniqua condemnato videtur, appellare ab interlocutoria per scriptum potest: A definitiva vero vel viva voce, vel ex intervallo decem dierum in scriptis.Judex Apostolos <bl>(abfertigs brieffe)</bl> ad superiorem judicem appellanti impertit.
units.tr: An appeal (a calling upon a higher judge) is an appeal (provocatio) from the hearing of a lesser judge to a greater one, on account of a grievance inflicted. For if a sentence seems unjust to the condemned party, he may appeal from an interlocutory sentence in writing; but from a definitive sentence he may appeal either by word of mouth or in writing within an interval of ten days. The judge grants the appellant letters dimissory (dispatch letters) to the superior judge.

units.la: Si intra illud tempus non appellatur, Sententia in rem judicatam transit, <bl>(gehet Das Urtheil in seine</bl> <bl>Kraffi[?])</bl> & petente parte pro qua pronunciatum est a Judice Executioni satisfieri debet. <bl>Es soll die</bl> execution <bl>vnd vollziehung darauff folgen.</bl>
units.tr: If no appeal is lodged within that time, the sentence passes into a judgment that has been adjudged (res judicata), and, at the request of the party in whose favour it was pronounced, execution must be carried out by the judge. Execution and enforcement shall follow upon it.

units.la: ¶ His cognitis, studiosus adolescens Corpus Juris legat, ut Imperat. monet. §. sin. Inst. de pub. Jud.
units.tr: ¶ With these things understood, the studious young man should read the Corpus Juris, as the Emperor advises in §. sin. Inst. de pub. Jud.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: Series Characterum.
units.tr: Series of Characters.
